author.name: Suhwan Cho, Yonwoo Choi, Soongjin Kim, Jicheol Park, Taegyu Lim

entry.summary: LEGO replaces the standard depth-lifting point-cloud pipeline for exocentric-to-egocentric video generation with a learned LVSM-style view synthesizer that renders the egocentric view as the conditioning signal for a video diffusion model. This avoids depth errors being translated into misplaced content while preserving the generative model's ability to fill unobserved regions.

entry.title: Teaching a Robot Dog New Tricks: Diverse Quadruped Skills via Combined Reinforcement and Imitation Learning with Adversarial Task Selection

author.name: Lemon Foxmere, Anthony Furman, Yizheng Du, Oliver Chang, Leilani Gilpin, Steve McGuire

entry.summary: The paper proposes a three-stage method for training a single quadruped policy covering distinct skills like walking, digging, and hopping, then composing them into novel behaviors such as crawling. Multiple RL teacher policies are trained per task, then a student policy is distilled with adversarial task selection to handle multi-task gradient conflict and sample inefficiency.

entry.title: Towards Path-Creative Navigation: Robot Navigation through Embodied Interaction

author.name: Haoyu Xi, Siwei Cheng, Xiangyuan Liu, Brenda Li, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates Path-Creative Navigation, a paradigm in which a robot recovers free space by coordinating locomotion with embodied interaction such as moving objects or operating articulated structures, rather than searching only existing free space. It addresses one class of PCN tasks with a mapless vision-LiDAR-odometry framework integrating observations, obstacle geometry, and robot state.

entry.title: 2DGS-Planner: Rasterization-based Path Planning in 2D Gaussian Splatting Map

author.name: Jiwon Park, Dong-Uk Seo, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: 2DGS-Planner performs ground robot path planning directly on 2D Gaussian splatting maps via rasterization rather than treating individual Gaussian primitives as obstacles. Multi-view attribution converts rendered normal dispersion into structural scores that guide adaptive roadmap sampling, addressing the unreliability of primitives as obstacle proxies.

entry.title: GLIO2: A GPU-Parallelized Tightly-Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-GNSS System for Robust and Real-Time Global Localization and Mapping

author.name: Qi Zhang, Xikun Liu, Qijun Qin, Xiangru Wang, Junzhe Wang, Naigui Xiao, Jianhao Jiao, Weisong Wen

entry.summary: GLIO2 is a tightly-coupled LiDAR-inertial-GNSS fusion system that addresses two failure modes of scan-to-map front-ends: irrecoverable drift under degeneracy and over-confident propagation of biased registration constraints. It uses GPU parallelization for real-time, globally consistent localization and mapping in perceptually degraded environments.

entry.title: Whose Ground Truth? Embracing Ambiguity in Human-Centered AI

author.name: Jingyao Wu, Mohammad Tariqul Islam, Per R{\aa}dberg Nagb{\o}l, Julie Gerlings, Giovanni Leoni, Georgiana Fryza, Lars Pilegaard Thomsen, Jakob Mainz

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that machine learning's assumption of a single definitive ground truth is flawed for human-centered tasks where multiple interpretations of the same input can be simultaneously valid. The authors contend that aggregating or treating annotation variability as noise discards meaningful information about human diversity.

entry.title: Balancing Reference Guidance and Free Generation in Trajectory Rollouts for Reasoning RL

author.name: Hanyu Wang, Nakul Agarwal, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Ehsan Moradi Pari, Makoto Fukushima, Jinghui Chen, Vaishnav Tadiparthi

entry.summary: The paper studies prefix continuation for reasoning RL rollouts, where the model continues from a verified reference prefix and keeps the trajectory only if it passes verification, deriving the KL divergence to the ideal post-verification distribution in closed form. This yields principled guidance for how much reference to provide during training.

entry.title: MedBenchAgent: Towards Systematic Automation of Medical VLM Benchmark Construction

author.name: Yulin Fu (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Junren Wang (West China Hospital, Sichuan Provincial Engineering Research Center of Intelligent Diagnosis and Treatment of Breast Diseases), Guangjing Yang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Zhangyuan Yu (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Wanran Sun (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Jiabao Zhou (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Jin Yin (West China Hospital, Sichuan Provincial Engineering Research Center of Intelligent Diagnosis and Treatment of Breast Diseases), Qicheng Lao (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)

entry.summary: MedBenchAgent automates not just generating evaluation items but deriving the benchmark specification itself for medical vision-language models, formulated as constrained compilation from evaluation requirements, heterogeneous annotations, and medical knowledge. The collaboration between a university and a hospital gives it clinical grounding for medical VLM evaluation.

entry.title: Cognition-Oriented Emotion Tracing from Causes to Consequences in Real-World Social Scenes

author.name: Hao Li, Jinye Zhang, Bobo Li, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu, Zheng Wang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang

entry.summary: TRACE is a cognition-oriented affective computing framework formalizing emotional episodes as Condition, Affect, and Effect stages, integrating observable cues with cognitive factors like internal stance and emotional-display regulation. Alongside it, TRACE-Bench evaluates multimodal models on real-world social scenes via five tasks covering affect recognition, regulation decoding, and causal reasoning about emotions.

entry.title: Lamarck's Driving School: Discovering Autonomous Driving Training Strategies through Evolutionary Competition

author.name: Yichun Ye, He Zhang, Ye Tian, Jian Sun

entry.summary: The paper replaces surrogate-based guidance (realism, difficulty, risk) for training scenario distribution design with direct competition among candidate distributions, formulating training-strategy discovery as multi-stage bilevel optimization solved with a Lamarckian evolutionary algorithm. It targets more efficient use of autonomous driving training resources.

entry.title: EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution

author.name: Yanning Dai, Yuhui Wang, Nanbo Li, Wenyi Wang, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: Proposes EvoAlloc, a self-evolving agent that learns from search experience to allocate limited evaluation compute across candidate programs during LLM-based program evolution, periodically consolidating prior outcomes into reusable experience. This replaces fixed allocation strategies that waste resources on low-value candidates.

entry.title: When Has a Bayesian Neural Network Sampled Enough? Adaptive Inference Time with Statistical Guarantees

author.name: Fabian Denoodt, Sibylle Hess

entry.summary: The paper uses confidence sequences to adaptively determine how many Monte Carlo samples a Bayesian neural network needs per input, stopping only when the downstream decision (class choice, distribution approximation, or threshold decision) carries the desired statistical guarantee. Experiments show efficient budget allocation, spending more samples on ambiguous inputs.

entry.title: GeoReform: Reflective Formalization Evolution for Multimodal Geometry Problem Solving

author.name: Jialu Wang, Ruichen Zhang, Xiaoou Liu, Hua Wei, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: GeoReform addresses the observation that injecting geometric structure into MLLMs can fix errors but also introduce new ones, arguing the key challenge is organizing extracted facts into representations that support reasoning rather than extracting more facts. It proposes a reflective formalization-evolution process that iteratively refines textual geometric representations.

entry.title: A Survey on LLM-Integrated Hardware Design Verification

author.name: Hao Zheng, Jaime Rafael Imperial, Bardia Nadimi, Xiangfei Kong

entry.summary: A systematic survey of LLM integration into hardware functional verification, covering assertion generation, testbench and stimulus generation, bug localization, formal and equivalence checking, SAT/SMT optimization, and agentic verification workflows. It organizes the literature by methodology, objective, tool interaction, benchmark, and evaluation criteria.

entry.title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction

author.name: Kaisong Zhang, Haotian Fang, Junmeng Zhou, Hang Lv, Yulan Pan, Yanchao Tan

entry.summary: Tackles next-visit diagnosis prediction with LLMs by redesigning RL rewards to cover multiple simultaneously valid diagnoses rather than rewarding one answer per trajectory, and introduces dedicated medical tokens so ICD codes are not fragmented into generic subwords. The coverage-aware reward prevents the policy from concentrating on a few frequent diagnoses.

entry.title: Conversational Task Disambiguation over Tabular Data: Leakage-Aware Formulation, Benchmark Suite, and Training

author.name: Nafiseh Ghoroghchian, Luis Scoccola, Tina Sedaghat, Omid Vaheb, Hannah Chen, Dino D'Agostino, Keyvan Golestan

entry.summary: This work formalizes conversational task disambiguation over tabular data, introducing the notion of an ambiguous verifiable task and decomposing the agent into asking and solution policies while separating the environment into oracle and verifier. It provides a leakage-aware benchmark suite and training methodology addressing inflated success metrics from oracle leakage.

entry.title: ActiveMedAgent: Cost-Aware Trajectory Learning for Multimodal Medical Diagnosis

author.name: Weiwei Ma, Xiaobing Yu, Peijie Qiu, Jin Yang, Zhaoqi An, Xuanzhao Dong, Xiaoqi Zhao, Xiaofeng Liu

entry.summary: ActiveMedAgent brings cost-aware sequential diagnosis logic to multimodal medical AI: it tracks probability distributions over candidate diagnoses with a frozen vision-language model and scores each evidence acquisition by per-step diagnostic utility minus cost, then trains a lightweight MLP controller offline on these trajectories. Trajectory-based policy learning outperforms unguided acquisition strategies across three benchmarks. It matters because test costs and patient burden are central constraints in real clinical AI.

entry.title: VAMR: Multi-Question Agentic Reasoning for Efficient Long-Form Video Understanding

author.name: Runquan Gui, Hanzhu Chen, Zehao Wang, Hanxin Zhu, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: VAMR coordinates all questions about a long video through a single shared tool-use trajectory, allowing a persistent policy model to invoke tools for multiple unresolved questions and answer those with sufficient evidence, instead of restarting exploration per question. This jointly builds evidence and shared understanding across the full question set, improving efficiency for multi-question long-form video understanding. It addresses a real inefficiency in current video agent pipelines.

entry.title: TAM: Task-Aware Memory Distillation for Efficient Spatiotemporal Prediction

author.name: Yuqi Li, Xiaoqin Feng, Fan Xu, Weilun Feng, Chuanguang Yang, Yingli Tian, Hao Wu

entry.summary: TAM organizes a frozen teacher's knowledge into a bounded, retrievable memory of latent features, forecast changes, and flow residuals for spatiotemporal prediction, with task-specific selection rules guiding the student's learning. This exploits cross-sample predictive structure that standard per-sample distillation ignores.

entry.title: Trajectory-Guided Fault Localization for Agent Skill Evolution

author.name: Yu Ge, Linna Xie, Zhong Li, Yu Pei, Tian Zhang

entry.summary: SkillMorph improves agent skill refinement by linking execution evidence to specific skill content before generating revisions, comparing failure and success evidence across abstracted trajectories over repeated runs and tasks. This trajectory-guided fault localization grounds LLM-generated skill revisions in explicit behavioral evidence rather than raw feedback.

entry.title: DataVista: Diagnosing Multimodal LLMs on Data Video Understanding

author.name: Yupeng Xie, Zhenyang Wang, Jiayi Zhu, Yinghao Tang, Zhouan Shen, Yiyu Chen, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: DataVista is the first benchmark dedicated to data video understanding, comprising 961 real-world data videos and 6,775 questions organized in a three-level capability framework. It targets skills general video benchmarks miss, such as reading data from animated charts, cross-time evidence integration, and understanding narrative visual design.

entry.title: MAST: Motif-Augmented Diffusion with Search Tree for Spectroscopic Molecular Structure Elucidation

author.name: Chenghao Jia, Mengdi Liu, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: MAST tackles molecular structure elucidation from spectra using a motif-augmented diffusion framework with joint 2D-3D generation and a search tree to reduce repeated full sampling overhead. It addresses limited paired data by learning robust spectra-structure relationships through motif-level representations rather than global spectral encodings.

entry.title: Batch Before You Lift: Scalable Topological Deep Learning on Large Graphs

author.name: David Leko, Luka Beni\'c, Guillermo Bern\'ardez, Nina Miolane, Olga Fink, Lev Telyatnikov

entry.summary: Cluster-TNN is a domain-agnostic framework for topological deep learning that avoids the bottleneck of materializing full lifted representations (hypergraphs, cellular, simplicial complexes) by lifting graphs locally after preprocessing partitions. It makes training feasible on large dense datasets where full-domain lifting is infeasible.

entry.title: Syn-Omni: Structured Specialization and Progressive Collaboration for Omnimodal Embeddings

author.name: Youngtaek Oh, Qiyu Wu, Hiromi Wakaki, Junmo Kim, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: Syn-Omni proposes structured adaptation for omnimodal embeddings via Orthogonal Modality-Expert LoRA, decomposing adaptation into a shared path for universal semantics and expert paths per modality, plus progressive synergy routing. This improves structural separation between universal and modality-specific representations over single shared parameter spaces.

entry.title: Exact SO(3)-Equivariant Isotropic Kernels for Rotation-Robust Neural Dynamics

author.name: Ridham Patel

entry.summary: Introduces IKNO, a graph neural operator for vector-valued PDEs built from rotation-invariant scalars and equivariant vector directions, guaranteeing exact SO(3)-equivariance of predictions. Demonstrates the approach on 3D Navier-Stokes dynamics at irregularly sampled points, eliminating prediction changes under rotated coordinate frames.

entry.title: F$^3$NO: Frequency-Decomposed Finite-Time Flow-map Neural Operators with Cross-Scale Conditioning

author.name: Fan Wu, Cheng Jing, Kookjin Lee

entry.summary: F3NO is a neural operator for PDE forecasting that decomposes predictions into low- and high-frequency branches, using updated low-frequency features to guide nonlinear refinement of high-frequency detail through cross-scale conditioning. It directly predicts states at specified future times and combines parallel short-segment predictions with recursive propagation for long trajectories, addressing error accumulation and fine-scale resolution across five benchmark settings.

entry.title: SteerCast: Retrieval-Based Latent Steering for Decoder-Only Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Van Dai Do, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Hung Le

entry.summary: SteerCast improves decoder-only time series forecasters at inference time without parameter updates by retrieving nearest-neighbor history windows and injecting aggregated steering vectors into the model's hidden states. Steering vectors are computed as the difference between latent representations induced by ground-truth continuations versus the model's own predictions. This training-free, retrieval-based correction mechanism is a novel application of latent steering to forecasting.

entry.title: Learning from Hetero Density for Cryo-EM Protein Reconstruction

author.name: Xu Han, Chaozhuo Li, Xiaowei Yuan, Yuancheng Sun, Kang Liu, Qiwei Ye

entry.summary: CryoCue leverages hetero component information, previously underused, to guide protein structure reconstruction from cryo-EM maps. It uses an anchor-supervised detector to learn hetero representations across five component classes, with multiscale hetero features guiding backbone localization and predicted hetero candidates conditioning structure refinement. The insight that filtering candidates near hetero components can help or impair chain construction motivates explicit modeling of these regions.

entry.title: Conditional Transfer from Controlled Pretraining Mixtures to Code

author.name: Ohad Rubin

entry.summary: Disentangles three distinct signals in synthetic pretraining data evaluation: diagnostic value, teachability, and transfer, using controlled pretraining mixtures of Python code and synthetic task families including OpenCodeInstruct. The paper questions the common practice of equating falling loss with data usefulness for downstream targets. Relevant to data curation for code LLMs.

entry.title: Understanding Latent-Dimension Scaling in Dynamical-System Learning through Spectral Reliability

author.name: Itsushi Sakata, Yuta Miyauchi, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes autoregressive dynamics learning through the eigenstructure of Koopman operators, using relative residuals to detect spurious eigenpairs even when one-step error decreases. The authors show convergence of minimal residuals as learned dictionaries approximate the observable space and hypothesize that Koopman spectral reliability explains when rollout error decreases consistently with latent dimension.

entry.title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity

author.name: Mingyi Li, Taira Tsuchiya, Kenji Yamanishi

entry.summary: This paper establishes the first oracle complexity bound for stochastic nonsmooth nonconvex composite optimization under first-order access, targeting Goldstein-type stationarity for objectives combining a Lipschitz nonconvex function with a convex regularizer. It uses the online-to-nonconvex conversion framework and improves on suboptimal zeroth-order results. The setting covers constrained optimization and regularized neural network training.

entry.title: Transformed Samplers with Variance Reduction

author.name: Siran Liu, Michalis Tisias, Petros Dellaportas

entry.summary: This paper extends exact control-variate solutions, previously limited to samplers with known spectral decompositions on reference densities, to general targets via a learned bijection such as a normalizing flow. The authors show Markov kernels and their Poisson solutions transform under bijections, enabling variance-reduced MCMC estimates for general distributions.

entry.title: Can a System-One LLM Perform Knowledge Tracing When Few or No Learners Are Logged?

author.name: Unggi Lee, Haeun Park

entry.summary: This paper shows that an off-the-shelf single-pass LLM (System-One) can perform knowledge tracing without any data from the target platform, reaching a mean AUC of .706 across seven datasets, beating 28 deep KT models trained on eight learners and outperforming slow sample-and-vote LLM approaches at roughly 1/100 of the API cost.

entry.title: Refinement as a Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement

author.name: Wei Tang, Hanrui Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies prediction aggregation among calibrated predictors, formulating calibrated predictors as signaling schemes and refinement via feature-independent garblings. It characterizes when refined calibrated predictors can be constructed that preserve input information and cannot be further refined using available information, without knowledge of Bayes probabilities.

entry.title: Optimal random quantisers for spherically symmetric distributions

author.name: Luc Pronzato, Anatoly Zhigljavsky

entry.summary: The paper proves that for spherically symmetric distributions, optimizing random quantisers is a convex problem and derives an equivalence theorem characterizing global optimality, plus a constructive algorithm. It shows that random quantisers uniform on a suitably chosen sphere achieve near-optimal quantization error even for moderate sample sizes where Zador asymptotics are unattainable. This has implications for vector quantization and high-dimensional approximation.

entry.title: Disentangling Linguistic and Paralinguistic Information with Routed Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Beimnet Bekele Guta, Xiaoyu Yang, Guangzhi Sun, Philip C. Woodland

entry.summary: This work disentangles linguistic content from paralinguistic factors (speaker identity, emotion, prosody) in self-supervised speech encoders using a TopK sparse autoencoder with route-specific supervision and cross-factor adversaries. Probes on frozen SPEAR and WavLM encoders show factor-specific retention and suppression, and the route organization learned on LibriSpeech transfers to MSP-Podcast without retraining. This has practical value for speech applications needing independent control of content and style factors.

entry.title: Local Prototype Reconstruction for Text-Compatible Speech-to-LLM Bridge Pretraining

author.name: Xinnian Zhao, Chia-Hua Wu, Pu Wang, Hugo Van Hamme

entry.summary: This paper studies the trainable bridge connecting frozen speech encoders to frozen LLMs, arguing the bridge pretraining objective determines whether the interface is reusable across downstream tasks. It proposes objectives combining global alignment with local lexical manifold compatibility and introduces a head-free diagnostic to measure these properties.

entry.title: SignRAG: Unified Retrieval-Augmented Gloss-Free Sign Language Translation

author.name: Zhi Rao, Yucheng Zhou, Qianran Sun, Yiqing Huang, Longcan Yuan, Jiayi Hou, Chengwen Yao, Lin Cheng, Donghui Sun, Xiaoxin Chen, Jun Wan

entry.summary: SignRAG adapts gloss-free sign language translation to decoder-only LLMs through hierarchical pretraining, target-domain retrieval augmentation, and retrieval-aware reinforcement fine-tuning, aiming to mitigate cross-modal optimization imbalance between sign encoders and LLMs. It targets underserved accessibility applications.

entry.title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To

author.name: Dianqiao Lei, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Pan Lu, Philip Torr, James Zou

entry.summary: This study examines LLMs' failure to comply with no-thinking instructions, proposing normalized measurement at three levels: empty-thinking rate, question-pre-answer relevance, and genuine-versus-filler reasoning. It shows that common proxies for no-thinking behavior (disabled modes, short traces) are unreliable and documents persistent thinking inertia.

entry.title: Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model-Skill Co-Evolution

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Xiyao Ma, Zhongkai Sun, Xu Han, Chengyuan Ma, Benjamin Z. Yao, Chenlei Guo

entry.summary: The paper shows that fewer than 25% of retrieved skills provide useful signals in on-policy distillation with skill-conditioned teacher policies, and proposes SGUID to select a compact skill subset based on consistently effective learning signals during training. The selected skills are distilled to produce a stronger model.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Computation of Persistent Homology for Topological Analysis of Image Data

author.name: Fan Wang, Hubert Wagner, Rezaul Chowdhury, Chao Chen

entry.summary: TopoGPU is a GPU streaming pipeline for computing persistence diagrams of cubical complexes from 2D and 3D images, combining streaming chunk processing with massively parallel GPU kernels and CPU boundary matrix reduction. It introduces a stratification-aware discrete Morse matching that provably preserves persistent homology under streaming, plus parallel topological sorting and V-path parity algorithms. Persistent homology is increasingly used in deep learning but remains a computational bottleneck, so this directly addresses a practical obstacle.

entry.title: AutoAdapt: Reliable Few-Shot Adaptation under Clinical Distribution Shifts

author.name: Song Wang, Jie Peng, Davis Hobley, Zachary Plotkin, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: AutoAdapt automates the many decisions in few-shot adaptation of large clinical models to new hospitals, including which pretrained model to adapt, how much to update, and which patients to use for validation. It tackles the core problem that small patient cohorts make evaluation of candidate strategies unreliable. The system frames this as a combined search-and-reliable-selection problem.

entry.title: SV-TAD: Native Sparse Convs for Efficient Temporal Action Detection

author.name: Ricardo Pizarro, Roberto Valle, Jos\'e M. Buenaposada, Luis M. Bergasa, Luis Baumela

entry.summary: Introduces native sparse 2D convolutions enabling parameter-efficient convolutional adapters for frozen billion-parameter vision transformers to operate directly on dynamically pruned token sets, avoiding expensive dense reconstruction. This addresses inference-time scalability of temporal action detection on long videos, which prior adapters left untouched.

entry.title: From Video Clips to Creation Trajectory: Sora100K for AI-Native Video Creation

author.name: Sicong Yang, Ruihuan Yang, Jian Lu, Jianfei Yuan, Xiaodong Cun, Xiuli Bi

entry.summary: Introduces Sora100K, a large dataset that frames AI-native video creation as structured creation trajectories rather than isolated clips, decomposing workflows into text-to-video generation roots, single-turn edits, and multi-turn editing trajectories with VLM-assisted semantic annotation. It enables training and evaluation of iterative video creation workflows.

entry.title: FearCaut-Qwen: Affective Steering in a Vision-Language Model Shifts the Decision Criterion for Hazard Assessment

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou

entry.summary: Uses signal detection theory to show that VLMs under-declare hazards in disaster damage assessment due to an over-conservative decision criterion rather than poor perception, then uses mechanistic interpretability to localize a fear-associated representation and causally steer it to shift the decision criterion. The approach is inspired by the psychological finding that fear induces risk aversion in humans.

entry.title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning

author.name: Zhongyu Yang, Jiale Tao, Ruitao Chen, Zuhao Yang, Yingfang Yuan, Xueliang Zhao, Auden, Kai Wang, Shuai Shao, Biao Wang, Steve Yves, Qinglin Lu

entry.summary: OmniCapBench reframes audio-visual caption evaluation by shifting from free-form captions to sets of atomic, verifiable evaluation units across entity reference and other tracks, resolving the coverage-versus-localization trade-off and instability of unconstrained LLM judges. It serves as a diagnostic framework for continuous audio-visual reasoning in MLLMs.

entry.title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting

author.name: Nhan (Nathan), Tran, Neal Wadhwa, Abe Davis, Stefan Stojanov

entry.summary: This workflow bridges physical film capture and generative video reshooting by using an editable 3D shot plan and a proxy of the take to evaluate hallucination risk in real time on set. Filmmakers can iteratively adjust plans, shoot guided pickups, or knowingly accept hallucinated content while still able to act on the risk.

entry.title: ActiveReg: Information-Driven Active Regional Probing for Partial-to-Full Bone Registration

author.name: Tiancheng Li, Yingyu Wang, Peter Walker, Liang Zhao, Shoudong Huang

entry.summary: ActiveReg is a closed-loop framework for orthopedic surgical registration that recommends probing regions rather than individual points, using a D-optimal planner that accounts for already acquired points and registration uncertainty. This reduces the number of probing actions a surgeon must perform under limited exposure while providing flexible guidance.

entry.title: Experience-Guided Initiation Search for Learned Skills in Skill Composition

author.name: Qixuan Li, Yanhong Zhao, Jincheng Yu

entry.summary: EVIS is a framework for discovering reliable initiation configurations when composing frozen learned skills such as VLA policies, recognizing that an initiation state affects downstream skills in a composition. It uses historical experience plus behavior validation to avoid costly extensive real-world rollouts.

entry.title: SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jiayu Wang, Yue Yu, Bin Zhu, Zhiyao Yang, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: SpatialHarness argues that fine manipulation failures of frontier multimodal models used for direct robot control stem partly from insufficient spatial observability rather than policy capability. It provides test-time spatial scaffolding via an online simulated scene synchronized with real execution, identifying task-critical spatial relationships without policy fine-tuning or hardware changes.

entry.title: Sequential Conditional Independence Testing with Machine Learning Models

author.name: Angel Reyero-Lobo, Michele Meziu, Sebastian Uriel Arias, Peter Gr\"unwald

entry.summary: The paper studies how to incorporate ML models into log-optimal e-variable designs for sequential conditional independence testing under the model-X framework. It explains why exchangeability-based e-variables, though theoretically weaker, can outperform GRO e-variables in practice by decomposing error into null enlargement, approximation, and estimation components.

entry.title: PulseBound: Future-Beat State Forecasting Under an Explicit Information Boundary

author.name: Chenyang Xu, Donglin Xie, Xi Xiang, Xiaoyu Li, Yufan Lu, Jiqiun Gao, Yi Zhao, Xin-Yi Li, Guangpu Zhu, Zijian Wang, Xiwen Yang, Dezhen Wang, Lin Chen, Shenda Hong, Leilei Li

entry.summary: Introduces PulseBound, a PPG representation learner that combines physiologically structured future-beat prediction with an explicit stored-window information boundary, ensuring encoder inputs depend only on the visible prefix through prefix-only normalization and aligned masking. This yields a stored-suffix invariance property that prevents causal leakage from withheld samples.

entry.title: HRIL: Learning Multimodal Synergy via Higher-Order Tensor Modeling

author.name: Qun Dai, Liangjian Wen, Jiang Duan, Yong Dai, Dongkai Wang, Maolin Wang, Mingjie Wang, Jianzhuang Liu, He Yan, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: The paper targets synergistic information in self-supervised multimodal representation learning, the task-relevant signals that emerge only from joint configurations of modalities and cannot be recovered from any single modality. It models synergy via higher-order statistical dependence captured through higher-order tensor methods.

entry.title: MAMHOI: Factorizing Scene-Aware Human-Object Interaction through Affordances

author.name: Mingyuan Lei, Yoonchang Sung, Tat-Jen Cham

entry.summary: MAMHOI factorizes scene-aware human-object interaction generation through an explicit motion-affordance interface, separating environment-aware feasibility reasoning from human-object motion synthesis. This lets the method combine complementary supervision from human-scene and human-object datasets despite scarce paired data.

entry.title: Explaining the Saliency Map Sparsity of Adversarially-Trained Neural Networks

author.name: Yannick Lunk, Atell Yehor Krasnopolsky, Damien Garreau, Leon Bungert

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical explanation for the empirically observed sparsity of gradient saliency maps in adversarially-trained networks, for two-layer ReLU networks. Builds on the equivalence of adversarial training to weight-decay minimization plus an adversarial total variation term, deriving sparsity in the asymptotic regime.

entry.title: Beyond Action Entropy: Quotient-Space Exploration for Genome-Scale Metabolic Model Repair

author.name: Xuan Gong, Hanbo Huang, Wenbin Dai, Jing Wang, Lei Bai, Xiang Xiao, Weishu Zhao, Shiyu Liang

entry.summary: Proposes QuotientPO, an RL exploration method for genome-scale metabolic model repair that collapses equivalent reaction edits into canonical biological mechanisms and explores over the resulting quotient space, avoiding the failure mode where output-space diversity does not imply hypothesis diversity. Addresses the many-to-one structure of model repair from phenotypic feedback. An interesting combination of RL and computational biology.

entry.title: Higher-Order Morphology Priors for Quadruped Reinforcement Learning Under Actuator Degradation

author.name: Derek You, Zafir Shamsi, Keqin Wang, Christine Allen-Blanchette

entry.summary: The paper represents the Unitree Go1 quadruped as a cell complex with limb- and body-level cells and applies Hodge-based message passing to RL policies under actuator degradation. The higher-order morphology-aware actor achieves higher returns, survival, and lower velocity-tracking error on unseen degradations compared to node-edge graph baselines.

entry.title: TAP3D: Thermal-Assisted 3D Human Point Clouds

author.name: Xie Zhang, Chengxiao Li, Xuan Liu, Chenshu Wu

entry.summary: TAP3D is the first system to reconstruct 3D human point clouds from low-cost thermal array sensors, using body heat signatures instead of LiDAR, radar, or depth cameras. A physics-informed design couples a forward thermal physics model with modules for multi-primitive depth estimation and multi-person separation, addressing thermal interference. Advantages include low cost, dense reconstruction, and privacy preservation.

entry.title: Relative Patch Response Learning for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Ouxiang Li, Yanbin Hao, Zhenhua Tang, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Addresses generalizable detection of AI-generated images by identifying a flaw in mixed-view training where self-attention lets real and generated patches interact, corrupting per-patch features. It proposes relative patch response learning so each patch's feature reflects its own provenance, improving generalization to unseen generators and perturbations.

entry.title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate

author.name: Ravil Akhtyamov

entry.summary: The paper argues that self-evolving LLM agents are only reviewable if adaptation is confined to the runtime harness, instruction text and tool-call logic, while model weights stay fixed, making every change an auditable diff. It presents a dual-loop engine with a hash-chained admission gate, evaluated in simulation on credit pipeline rule changes.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Keyframe Discovery for Horizon-Invariant Behavior Cloning

author.name: Prabin Kumar Rath, Omkar Patil, Nakul Gopalan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Keyframe Mnemonics, a self-supervised method that discovers information-critical observations to condition behavior cloning policies in non-Markovian, long-horizon environments. This avoids the hidden-state collapse of recurrent models and the context-length limits of attention-based approaches.

entry.title: AliO: Output Alignment Matters in Long-Term Time Series Forecasing

author.name: Kwangryeol Park, Jaeho Kim, Seulki Lee

entry.summary: The paper identifies low output alignment in state-of-the-art long-term time series forecasting models, where predictions for the same timestamp fluctuate across lagged input sequences, undermining reliability. It proposes AliO, an approach that reduces discrepancies between predictions for identical timestamps to improve alignment.

entry.title: Mine Odyssey: Benchmarking Spatial Agentic Intelligence in the Wild

author.name: Yuxuan Cao, Junlong Li, Hao Li, Junxian He

entry.summary: Mine Odyssey is a benchmark for agentic spatial intelligence built from Minecraft reconstructions of 30 real-world locations across 20 countries, with 180 tasks spanning indoor and outdoor settings that require exploration, spatial updating, and feedback-driven action. It addresses the narrow spatial coverage of existing agent benchmarks.

entry.title: TypedBench: A Benchmark for Calibration, Framing Sensitivity, and Cost in System One Decision Models

author.name: Rahul Sharma, Andrew B. Ducan, Ga\'etan Marceau Caron, Sebastian J. Vollmer

entry.summary: TypedBench is a benchmark for non-generative typed decision models that output calibrated probabilities over categorical, ordinal, or binary answers, evaluating calibration, wording/framing sensitivity, and cost-aware decisions. It is built from seven policy-labelled generators and nine evaluation suites, arguing that miscalibrated or wording-sensitive probabilities can drive unintended software actions with no inspectable rationale.

entry.title: Constrained Command-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning with Bandit Strategy Selection in Real-Time Strategy Games

author.name: Nick Leenders, Roy Lindelauf, Joost van Oijen, Boris Cule

entry.summary: The paper separates strategic command selection from learned unit control in real-time strategy games, introducing a constrained command-conditioned PPO executor for MicroRTS plus measurable command-following criteria. A bandit selects strategies per opponent, improving robustness to out-of-distribution opponents while reusing one execution policy.

entry.title: MindFlow: Mind Supernet Powered Thinking Flows for Research Idea Innovation

author.name: Mengdi Liu, Wenjue Chen, Wenyue Chen, Cheng Yang, Fanqi Kong, Zhangyang Gao, Xiaoxue Cheng, Yiheng Li, Yujian Yuan, Keliang Li, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan, Chenglin Wu

entry.summary: Formulates research idea generation as a graph-structured flow of modular thinking operators modeled by a probabilistic mind supernet, where a controller dynamically samples ideation paths balancing novelty, plausibility, and feasibility. This replaces the static, predefined pipelines of prior LLM-based ideation systems with an adaptive, searchable structure.

entry.title: Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents

author.name: Xiangyi Zeng, Baihang Liu, Xutong Wang, Ze Jin, Yunpeng Li, Qixu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Hippocam, a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture for long-running LLM agents that structures ongoing work as nested intents, keeping active context centered on the current intent and consolidating completed intents into task-relevant outcomes. It draws on human memory characteristics of goal-relevant maintenance and gradual consolidation through repetition.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Electromagnetic Spectrum Understanding via Budget-Adaptive Signal Tokenization

author.name: Lei Zhai, Zhihao Chang, Shuyuan Yang, Zhixi Feng

entry.summary: BATok is a budget-adaptive tokenizer that extends vision-language models to raw I/Q electromagnetic signals, adjusting token capacity to input length while allocating capacity according to signal content. This enables instruction-conditioned, unified LLM-based analysis of spectrum monitoring tasks beyond fixed task-specific recognizers.

entry.title: Freeze the Decoder, Heal the Encoder: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation for SVD-Based KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: Documents a methodological confound in parameter-efficient fine-tuning comparisons: a shared learning rate across arms with different trainable-parameter counts can manufacture spurious advantages for the smallest arm. The analysis is grounded in SVD-based KV-cache compression, where a model is converted to a low-rank cache via encoder/decoder factorization followed by a healing fine-tune.

entry.title: Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking

author.name: Yongjian Tang, Linhan Li, Thomas Runkler

entry.summary: Presents Agent4RE, a multi-agent system for software requirements engineering with specialized agents and two iterative self-refinement loops, alongside RE-E2E, a dataset from human-written requirement specifications enabling end-to-end evaluation from elicitation to generation. It moves beyond prior LLM work that treated RE subtasks in isolation.

entry.title: Cross-Provider Review as a Runtime Contract for Coding Agents: A Controlled Pilot and Fault-Injection Study

author.name: Bowen Xu, Boyu Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose an advisory contract for cross-provider code review between coding agents sharing a workstation, specifying bounded execution, restricted reviewer capabilities, and durable evidence, evaluated in a pilot of 20 paired development turns where eight had material reviewer findings. Fault-injection scanning also reproduced a false-success failure mode on truncated inputs.

entry.title: AffordDrive3D: Affordance-Aware World-Action Modeling with Spatial Understanding

author.name: Tianhui Cai, Xinglong Sun, Chao Fang, Zhenxin Li, Rui Song, Jose M. Alvarez, Yunxiang Mao, Jiaqi Ma, Langechuan Liu

entry.summary: AffordDrive3D improves autonomous driving world-action models by jointly modeling action-relevant affordance regions (where the vehicle can safely move and collision risks) together with future geometric prediction, rather than relying only on RGB appearance or dense scene geometry. This gives the policy both driving-relevant cues and their spatial structure. It matters because affordance-aware prediction could improve safety-critical trajectory planning.

entry.title: Characterizing Statistical Separability in TP-CRIV for Probabilistic AI Models

author.name: Teruki Sano, Minoru Kuribayashi, Masao Sakai, Shuji Isobe, Eisuke Koizumi, Zhang Zhang, Satoru Matsumoto

entry.summary: The paper studies third-party challenge-response identity verification (TP-CRIV) for probabilistic AI models, where repeated executions of the same query yield different outputs. It relates challenge-wise behavior of matching versus non-matching provers to verification-level separability and characterizes how much evidence is needed for reliable verification. This matters for auditing and verifying remotely deployed models, an increasingly important provenance question.

entry.title: Missing Modality-Aware Calibration for Trustworthy Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Sol Lee, Hyunji Kim, Sungrae Hong, Donghee Han, Mun Yi

entry.summary: This medical imaging paper tackles miscalibrated confidence in multimodal brain tumor segmentation when MRI modalities are missing, observing that prediction difficulty depends on which modalities are absent rather than how many. The proposed calibration method accounts for combination-specific and spatially varying uncertainty under incomplete modality acquisition. Reliable confidence estimates are a prerequisite for clinical adoption of such models.

entry.title: Design Creativity Bench: Measuring creativity in LLM-Generated UI

author.name: Aman Rusia, Abhijit Bhole, Prashank Gupta, Dipanjan Dey

entry.summary: Design Creativity Bench evaluates creativity in LLM-generated UI designs along originality, creative range, and appropriateness dimensions, finding originality of 0.592 for same-prompt designs from different models versus 0.764 for human-model pairs, indicating models converge far more than humans do. Creative range scores similarly reveal limited divergence across product domains. The benchmark characterizes a capability gap that standard evaluations miss.

entry.title: Neural Networks for Temporal Pattern Recognition and Dynamic Arm Gesture Speed Estimation for Robot Control

author.name: Mil\'an Zsolt Bagladi, L\'aszl\'o Guly\'as

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of ten abstract sequential tasks (five permutation-invariant and five order-dependent) evaluated across eighteen neural architectures spanning recurrent, convolutional, attention-based, and set-function families. With over 250 experimental configurations under strictly controlled conditions (fixed seeds, shared hyperparameters and data splits), the work aims to identify which architectures best support temporal pattern recognition for gesture-based human-robot interaction. It matters because controlled architecture comparisons for temporal reasoning remain relatively rare and can guide deployment of gesture-controlled robotic systems.

entry.title: SkillContrast: Difference-Guided Text Selection for Agent Skill Reranking

author.name: Jiandong Ding, Honglei Ji, Ming Liu, Tao Duan

entry.summary: SkillContrast is a training-free selector that retains the differing text between retrieved similar skills, with local context, to help a pretrained reranker choose correctly between them. On SameCapRisk-Bench it yields 54-72 more clean hits than TF-IDF query selection at identical input lengths across multiple retrievers and reranker sizes.

entry.title: Examining Social Attribution in LLM Reasoning: A Theory-Guided Probing Methodology

author.name: Zhaoxin Yu, Qingchao Kong, Dajun Zeng, Wenji Mao

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic exploration of LLM social attribution, examining how models judge social cause, responsibility, and blame or credit, guided by Attribution Theory from social psychology. It probes both the judgments themselves and their underlying internal mechanisms, relevant to LLM deployment in sociotechnical systems.

entry.title: Scalable Hierarchical Graph Generation via Soft Community Structure

author.name: Ahmet T\"uzen, Helge Langseth, Kjetil N{\o}rv{\aa}g

entry.summary: Schema generates large attributed graphs by recursively decomposing a reference graph into soft communities and splitting generation into three independently trained stages: attribute synthesis conditioned on memberships, intra-community edge generation, and inter-community bridge modeling. This addresses the hard setting where only a single large graph is available for fitting.

entry.title: AdaCast: Conditional Parameter Generation for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Darahaas Nallagatla, Darryl Cherian Jacob, Pan He

entry.summary: AdaCast introduces input-specific adaptation for time-series foundation models by using a generator to produce low-rank parameter updates for a frozen pretrained model, rather than applying one static set of dataset-level updates. This allows forecasts to be tailored to the seasonality and dynamics of each individual input series.

entry.title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration

author.name: Jialei He, Enhe Liu, Sifan Song, Pengfei Jin, Jionglong Su, Hongbin Wang, Zhixiang Lu, Yanhao Huang, Anteng Cai, Zhengyong Jiang, Jiaman Ding, S. Kevin Zhou, Jinfeng Wang

entry.summary: ContiLNN augments 2D medical image restoration backbones with bidirectional closed-form continuous-time modules for cross-slice modeling, using slice-interval-modulated gates to handle varying sampling without numerical ODE integration. Reference-guided consistency and distillation preserve anatomical continuity and in-plane quality.

entry.title: Sample-Efficiency of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Kevin Riehl, Shaimaa K. El-Baklish, Fan Wu, Anastasios Kouvelas

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates the sample-efficiency of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against MLPs in control settings, covering the Feynman dataset and Gymnasium reinforcement learning benchmarks. Finds similar performance with about 40% fewer samples, alongside higher parameter efficiency and interpretability.

entry.title: Similar Predictive Fit but Different Latent Dynamics: Characterizing Learned Dynamical Structure in Personalized Models of Brain Disorders

author.name: Rita Huan-Ting Peng, Nhat Bui

entry.summary: Analyzes personalized latent transition dynamics extracted from an EEG foundation model's representations across 198 subjects with epilepsy, showing that models with similar predictive fit can differ in clinically associated latent structure. Fits sparse multinomial logistic transition distributions per subject to obtain personalized transition-dependency graphs.

entry.title: Gen-PINNs: Generative Adversarial Physics Informed Neural Networks for solving partial differential equations

author.name: Muhammad M. Akmal, Kamy Sepehrnoori, Michael J. Pyrcz

entry.summary: Gen-PINNs combines physics-informed neural networks with adversarial learning, identifying standard PINN failure modes such as spectral bias, loss imbalance, and optimizer stagnation, and proposing a deterministic residual-adversarial framework for PDEs with sharp or shock-like solutions. The adversarial formulation aims to improve data-free PDE solving where standard PINNs struggle.

entry.title: Multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Sequential Recommendation via Collaborative Filtering Paths

author.name: Jason Marcell Setiadi, Xin Cao, Lina Yao

entry.summary: MGRASRec is a multimodal graph retrieval-augmented framework for sequential recommendation that injects collaborative filtering signals into an MLLM prompt by retrieving structured paths from a user-item interaction graph conditioned on candidate items. This addresses two limitations of prior MLLM-based recommenders: ignoring collaborative signals from neighboring users and the computational overhead of repeated inference over long histories. The approach improves recommendation quality while controlling inference cost.

entry.title: New Lower Bound and Upper Bounds on the Regret for Online Sparse Linear Regression

author.name: Xiaofeng Cao, Junfan Li, Langzhang Liang, Mingwei Xu, Xiao Zhang

entry.summary: Provides the first minimax lower bound on regret for online sparse linear regression with attribute access restrictions, plus improved algorithmic upper bounds without regularity assumptions. Characterizes how regret scales with problem-dependent parameters, resolving the information-theoretic complexity of this NP-hard problem. A clean theoretical advance in online learning.

entry.title: DADP: Dynamic Activity-Dependent Pruning, A Reverse Hebbian-Inspired Structural Pruning Method

author.name: Bhushan Deshpande

entry.summary: DADP is a biologically inspired structural pruning method that scores connections during training by the accumulated product of pre-synaptic activations and post-synaptic error gradients, using a single global threshold rather than per-layer sparsity budgets. This dynamically allocates sparsity across depth and reduces the need for manual targets or costly retraining cycles.

entry.title: RIFT: Relative Isolation From Trees For Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mark Daniel Szalai, Gabor Horvath

entry.summary: RIFT is a deterministic anomaly detection method inspired by the closed-form infinite-forest limit of Isolation Forest. It builds a minimum spanning tree and scores points by the apparent sizes of tree edges viewed from each point, exactly recovering the IF limit in 1D while generalizing parameter-free to higher dimensions. It avoids Isolation Forest's axis-parallel artifacts and is robust to varying density and clustered anomalies.

entry.title: Prospective Prediction of OOD Degradation from Source-Side Training Dynamics

author.name: Sasha (Alexander), Monin

entry.summary: This paper shows that persistent out-of-distribution degradation can be predicted before it is observed, using only source-side training dynamics in a controlled shortcut-learning setting. Temporal summaries of confidence and entropy dynamics carry substantially more predictive signal than current values, and findings transfer from CNNs to MLPs without retraining. It provides a proof of concept for early-warning signals of future OOD failure.

entry.title: Strategic Investment Decision Making for Value Creation in Energy Transition: A Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Yasaman Cheraghi (Department of Energy and Petroleum Engineering, University of Stavanger, Norway), Reidar B. Bratvold (Department of Energy and Petroleum Engineering, University of Stavanger, Norway), Aojie Hong (Independent Researcher, Stavanger, Norway), Ressi B. Muhammad (Department of Energy and Petroleum Engineering, University of Stavanger, Norway), Sergey Alyaev (NORCE Norwegian Research Centre, Bergen, Norway)

entry.summary: Researchers from the University of Stavanger and NORCE build a custom simulation environment modeling the dynamic energy landscape through 2050 and design a multi-criteria sequential decision-making framework using reinforcement learning. The goal is to help energy companies time investments in renewables to balance climate obligations against shareholder value under uncertainty.

entry.title: Reconstruction of Multiscale Plasma Dynamics Across Operating Regimes

author.name: Maryam Reza, Farbod Faraji

entry.summary: ReMAIN extends the Shallow Recurrent Decoder for sparse-sensor plasma reconstruction by replacing its fully connected decoder with a recurrent-state-conditioned U-Net that resolves spatial structure across scales and regimes. This improves diagnostics, reduced-order modeling, and control of multiscale plasma dynamics from few sensors.

entry.title: BRACE: Differential Privacy for Dense Associative Memory with LSR Energy

author.name: Chang Qu, Zhaoyang Shi

entry.summary: The paper develops a differential privacy framework for log-sum-ReLU dense associative memory, whose finite-support retrieval dynamics complicate standard privacy-preserving computation. The proposed BRACE algorithm adaptively corrects boundary-sensitive noise perturbations to control cumulative privacy effect during retrieval.

entry.title: Beyond QAOA: A Review of AI and Quantum Computing for Adaptive Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Hoong Chuin LAU

entry.summary: This review surveys the intersection of machine learning and near-term quantum computing for combinatorial optimization, organizing workflows where learned policies adaptively decide formulation, penalty choices, shot budgets, backends, and whether to invoke a quantum processor at all. It structures the literature into three paradigms: AI for quantum optimization, quantum for AI-driven optimization, and co-optimization. It offers a useful map of an emerging hybrid field.

entry.title: Learning structured linear dynamical systems from missing observations

author.name: Aravinda Kanchana Ruwanpathirana, Hemant Tyagi, Sunny G. W. Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a bias-corrected, possibly non-convex estimator for structured linear dynamical systems when only a subsample of observations is available each step, deriving non-asymptotic error bounds that depend on the local complexity of the structure set, trajectory length, and sampling probability. They prove convergence of projected gradient descent and instantiate the theory for subspaces, bi-isotonic matrices, and rowwise-structured matrices.

entry.title: Poster: A Preliminary Study of LLM Distillation Inference

author.name: Edward Chen, Yuntao Du

entry.summary: The authors formalize distillation inference — determining whether a suspect model was trained on a proprietary LLM's outputs — as a hypothesis test using shadow models trained on teacher reasoning traces versus reference answers. The auditor converts a suspect model's similarity-to-teacher score into a calibrated p-value. This addresses a growing concern for model providers protecting intellectual property against unauthorized distillation.

entry.title: The "10th Juror": Open-Set Standpoint Screening for Bureaucratic Bias Detection

author.name: Yuchen Miao, Zijun Wang, Chang Han, Yurui Shi, Mingtai Zhang, Siyang Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes MARS-Gov, a multi-agent framework for detecting and rewriting biased language in Dutch government documents, grounded in legal evidence and avoiding fixed bias taxonomies via open-set standpoint screening. It addresses over-flagging by zero-shot LLMs and closed-world limitations of discriminative classifiers in a closed-loop bias governance setting.

entry.title: UXBench Pro: Benchmarking Personalized User Experience in Multi-Turn Dialogue Interactions

author.name: Mengze Hong, Zeyang Lei, Wenbo Shang, Xia Zeng, Xiying Zhao, Qi Zhu, Chen Jason Zhang, Di Jiang, Taiming Fu, Qiongyi Zhou, Qinghe Chang, Fubao Zhang, Chenxuan Ma, Minlong Peng, Jinfeng Huang, Zineng Zhou, Jindou Wu, Muge Qi, Sijun He, Xin Cui, Di Liang, Yuan Hua, Davey Chen

entry.summary: UXBench Pro extends automated user-experience evaluation beyond binary preference prediction with 1,000 test instances from real user interactions across 12 task scenarios and 82 domains. Each instance includes a FACTORS user profile capturing seven interpretable behavioral facets, enabling user-personalized evaluation with a dual-perspective paradigm rather than a single user-agnostic reward model.

entry.title: Natural Language to First-Order Logic LLM-based Autoformalization

author.name: Andrea Brunello, Cristian Curaba, Luca Geatti, Michele Mignani, Angelo Montanari, Nicola Saccomanno

entry.summary: This survey provides a principled task definition for FOL autoformalization, separating ontology extraction from logical translation, whose conflation has obscured cross-study evaluation. It reviews datasets, metrics, and LLM-based methods (fine-tuning, prompting, verification-based refinement) and identifies open challenges in benchmarking and semantic evaluation.

entry.title: MESSENGER: Memory-Enhanced Sequential Scene Flow Estimation via Autoregressive Next-Frame Forecasting

author.name: Jiuming Liu, Jianing Li, Mengmeng Liu, Hongyang He, Hesheng Wang, Per Ola Kristensson

entry.summary: MESSENGER proposes a memory-enhanced pipeline for sequential 3D scene flow estimation that uses a memory buffer to mine long-term temporal dependencies and autoregressive next-frame forecasting to improve future prediction, addressing the computational overhead and degradation of sequence-to-sequence multi-frame estimators. Scene flow underpins many dynamic 3D perception tasks. The memory-based design targets both temporal correlation and long-horizon extrapolation.

entry.title: Refine Connections, Close the Gap: A Reliable Enhancement Framework for Driving Scene Topology

author.name: Xiaoqi Wang, Dingyi Zhaung, David Paz, Wenbin He, Yucai Bai, Peng Zhou, Rui Zhang, Jinhua Zhao, Liu Ren

entry.summary: This paper targets lane-topology reasoning in autonomous driving, observing that current methods achieve far below the theoretical upper bound implied by their own detections. It proposes a framework for refining connectivity decisions beyond naive score thresholding, producing more reliable topology graphs for downstream planning. Improved topology extraction directly supports safer path planning and motion control.

entry.title: IntrinSync: Joint Intrinsic Decomposition and Reciprocal Rendering

author.name: Zheng Gu, Rui Huang, Xilu Zhang, Jingbo Zhang, Min Lu, Zhida Sun, Dani Lischinski, Daniel Cohen-Or, Hui Huang

entry.summary: IntrinSync is a unified inverse-rendering framework that jointly decomposes an RGB image into albedo, shading, surface properties, and illumination while enforcing mutual compatibility between the intrinsic channels. It combines joint-channel modeling with reciprocal inverse-forward rendering, so the decomposition must re-render the input consistently. This improves over methods that treat intrinsic properties or the inverse/forward processes in isolation.

entry.title: MATE4D: Matrix-Guided Editable 4D Generation from a Single Image

author.name: Xiaotian Chen, Dongfu Yin

entry.summary: MATE4D converts a single input image into editable dynamic 4D (spatio-temporal 3D) content by constructing a spatio-temporal multi-view image matrix with text-guided background manipulation. The synthesized multi-view observations supervise the optimization of 3D Gaussian primitives, which a lightweight deformation module animates into a 4D representation. This addresses the core difficulty of generating temporally stable dynamic 3D scenes from limited single-view structural and motion cues.

entry.title: Spatial-Frequency-Aware Implicit Neural Representation of Multidimensional Signals via MLP-KAN Fusion

author.name: Wen Yan, Ligen Shi, Jun Qiu, Haimiao Zhang, Lina Wu, Chang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a spatial-frequency-aware implicit neural representation framework that fuses an MLP branch (modeling low frequencies) with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network branch (capturing high-frequency detail) to overcome spectral bias without brittle Fourier feature tuning. Relevant to signal reconstruction tasks such as images, videos, and other multidimensional data.

entry.title: Phase-aware video generation for physics-grounded dynamics and interactions

author.name: Jingfeng Ou, Kun Wang, Rui Zhao, Jingwei Guan, Limin Wang, Chao Dong, Xingyu Zeng

entry.summary: Presents PAVG, a Phase-Aware Video Generator with a dual-branch architecture that explicitly models solid and gas dynamics separately while using spatiotemporal cross-attention to capture their physical interactions. It is supported by a new simulation corpus of over 700K physical trajectories across solid, gas, and interaction scenarios.

entry.title: Pose-Free Feed-Forward 3D Inpainting via Learnable Mask Attention and Support Token Refinement

author.name: Jingyi Pan, Dan Xu, Qiong Luo

entry.summary: Presents FreeInpaint, a feed-forward framework for 3D scene inpainting that works directly from unposed multi-view images by extending a 3D foundation model to propagate masked regions across views, removing the need for calibrated camera poses. This makes 3D inpainting applicable to casual in-the-wild capture scenarios.

entry.title: Pumpire: Unified Benchmark for Metric Distance Estimation

author.name: Siyu Chen, Zehan Wang, Jiayang Xu, Yihan Wu, Jialei Wang, Junming Chen, Ziang Zhang, Yutong Ying, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Pumpire is a benchmark for evaluating point-pair distance estimation by 3D foundation models, using a physically measured dataset of 100 real-world scenes with 6,400 frames and real distance annotations. It directly measures point-to-point distances from reconstructed geometry rather than proxy metrics on depth or point-clouds.

entry.title: Universal Construction and Exact Self-Reproduction in Ternary McCulloch-Pitts Networks

author.name: Charles C. Norton

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that a fixed network of McCulloch-Pitts threshold units with weights in {-1,0,1} can store and execute other threshold networks, implementing von Neumann's universal construction and self-reproduction exactly. A 143-record constructor reads a network description from tape, builds the network, copies the description, and rebuilds itself when started on its own description.

entry.title: Distributed Relative Localization Based on Ultra-WideBand and LiDAR for Multi-robot with Limited Communication

author.name: Zhiqiang Cao, Ran Liu, Billy Pik Lik Lau, Chau Yuen, U-Xuan Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fully distributed relative position estimation method for teams of similar-looking robots in GPS-denied, communication-limited environments, fusing onboard UWB ranging and LiDAR detection of anonymous objects. It builds UWB and LiDAR connection graphs to disambiguate which detected objects are teammates, enabling collaborative tasks like exploration and formation control.

entry.title: STAG: A Sparse Traversability-Aware Graph Representation from Grid-Based Costmaps for Robotic Navigation

author.name: Gabriel Manuel Garcia, St\'ephanie Aravecchia, Miguel Angel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: STAG converts dense grid costmaps into compact traversability-aware graphs combining a medial-axis topological backbone, representative nodes for homogeneous regions, and transition nodes at traversability gradients. A* on STAG is benchmarked against dense grids on synthetic cave/mine maps and the DARPA CERBERUS dataset with comparable path quality at lower cost.

entry.title: MAP2: Model- and Acceleration-Based Pursuit with MPC and Gaussian Process Residual Learning for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Weizhan Huang, Cheng Hu, Edoardo Ghignone, Nicolas Baumann, Yiqin Wang, Hongye Su, Lei Xie, Michele Magno

entry.summary: MAP2 extends model- and acceleration-based pursuit controllers for autonomous racing by combining a curvature-based kinematic MPC with a sparse Gaussian process residual correction for tire dynamics. This addresses the breakdown of Ackermann geometry assumptions at the handling limits while keeping computational latency low.

entry.title: Decision-Sufficient Posterior Approximation

author.name: Sean Plummer

entry.summary: This paper formalizes when a posterior approximation is adequate for a specified downstream decision, deriving a regret geometry over actions and exact distances to decision adequacy and failure via contracted KL divergence over Bayes-action fibers. It gives quadratic local limits in regular finite-dimensional problems, connecting approximation error to decision consequences.

entry.title: Using AI to mitigate the growing environmental threat of data centers

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: This MIT News profile describes the work of Christina Delimitrou, a newly tenured associate professor at MIT CSAIL, who applies machine learning to make large-scale data centers more efficient, secure, and reliable. Her group redesigns cloud computing systems, manages shared hardware resources, and streamlines server architectures so operators can extract more computation from existing hardware, reducing energy waste and reliance on fossil fuels. The piece matters because data center energy consumption is a rapidly growing environmental concern as AI deployment scales.

entry.title: Speaking the Navigator's Language: Trajectory-Grounded Instruction Translation for Frozen Aerial VLN Agents

author.name: Xi Chen, Zhe Liu, Xiaogang Xu, Jiafei Xu, Chunyi Zhou, Yuan Su, Rui Zeng, Tianyu Du, Kelu Yao, Chao Li, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: The authors identify an instruction gap in aerial vision-and-language navigation, where short user instructions drop a frozen OpenFly navigator's success rate from 31 percent to 11 percent. They propose TGIT, a translator that converts intent-driven commands into agent-executable ones by learning from the navigator's trajectory outcomes without retraining the navigator.

entry.title: When Interfaces Speak: Data-Aware Generative UI Harness for Active Interaction

author.name: Xiaolong Li, Xiaohan Xu, Jinyang Li, Xinnuo Xu, Ge Qu, Nan Huo, Jack Williams, Reynold Cheng

entry.summary: GenUI-Harness pairs a Tool Agent for retrieval and execution with a GUI Coder Agent that resolves ambiguities by generating ephemeral structured interfaces, moving beyond text-only human-agent interaction. It introduces Dynamic UX, a lightweight package enabling RL training of UI generation with verifiable rewards without costly execution.

entry.title: An Interpretable Approach to PDE Solution Discovery via Structural Experience Distillation

author.name: Yunpeng Gong, Huolong Wu, Can Yang, Min Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes SED for discovering explicit symbolic expressions of PDE solutions, replacing opaque terminal fitness scores with structural experience distillation that identifies which subexpressions drive candidate performance. This makes the search process interpretable and allows reusable structures from suboptimal candidates to be retained.

entry.title: Phase-HDC: Replacing Optimizer History with Gradient Thresholds in Discrete Phase Learning

author.name: Ahmed Nebli

entry.summary: Proposes Phase-HDC, a training rule for hyperdimensional classifiers with low-bit phase parameters that updates each stored angle by at most one step against the gradient sign when the gradient is large enough, requiring no optimizer state. The rule is shown to be the exact solution of a first-order loss model where parameter changes incur fixed costs, enabling training with memory equal to model size.

entry.title: Clarify, Then Focus: Statement Normalization for Conversation Analytics at Scale

author.name: Mikhail L. Arbuzov (Independent researcher), Karan Dave (Independent researcher), Evgeniya Dontsova (Independent researcher), Yaodong Hu (Independent researcher), Vincent Lao (Independent researcher), Navita Jain (Independent researcher), Sisong Bei (Independent researcher), Dmitry Dimov (Independent researcher)

entry.summary: The authors propose statement normalization, transforming dialogue transcripts into short speaker-attributed statements with semantic tags so downstream models can selectively attend to relevant evidence for enterprise analytics questions. On an offer-suppression task over customer-service calls, normalization improved downstream performance while reducing repeated interpretive work.

entry.title: PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation

author.name: Heng Li, Yong Zhang, Ning Cheng, Zhigen Li, Yun Zhu, Yanmeng Wang, Shaojun Wang, Jing Xiao

entry.summary: PIVOT dynamically routes samples between on-policy distillation and GRPO-based reinforcement learning for vertical-domain few-shot adaptation of small language models, using teacher-evaluated perplexity to decide per-sample when to stop teacher-guided acquisition and start reward-driven refinement. This replaces globally fixed KD-to-RL transition schedules that ignore per-sample needs. It is relevant to efficiently adapting small models to specialized domains with limited supervision.

entry.title: RoboAware: Learning to Coordinate Embodied Skills from Counterfactual Outcomes

author.name: Bohan Zhou, Xingbei Chen, Emily Huang, Weilin Ruan, Haojian Huang, Yehang Zhang, Zexi Li, Wenqian Li, Qize Yu, Zetian Song, Leyi Wu, Jinghao Li, Mingxuan Song, Xinrun Xu, Zongyang Qiu, Yangkai Wei, Tianyi Zhang, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, James Cheng

entry.summary: RoboAware learns a state-conditioned responsibility coordinator for embodied coding agents composing modular robot skills with frozen end-to-end policies, trained from counterfactual outcomes. It introduces the P5 schema organizing skills into five semantic stages within a hierarchical MDP, plus State-Locked Counterfactual Branching to recover missing counterfactual branch outcomes by restoring identical training states. This improves skill orchestration in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: MAP4CS: A Multi-dimensional Data Pruning Framework for Efficient Code Retriever Fine-tuning

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Mingwei Liu, Guangsheng Ou, Zekai Zhang, Zike Li, Yanlin Wang, Pelin Zheng

entry.summary: MAP4CS is an adaptive data-pruning framework that identifies a small high-quality core subset of massive, noisy code corpora for efficient retriever fine-tuning in RAG pipelines, avoiding both the cost and negative transfer of full-corpus training and the unrepresentativeness of random sampling. It integrates multiple dimensions of data quality awareness.

entry.title: Real-Time Motion Planning with Dynamic Hazards: Classical vs. Learning-Based Methods

author.name: Eran Iceland, Alexander Tuisov, Oren Gal, Ariel Barel, Alfred M. Bruckstein

entry.summary: This paper builds a unified controlled benchmark comparing classical and learning-based motion planners in dynamic hazard fields with time-varying forbidden regions from rotating sprinkler-like hazards. Results reveal a regime shift: classical planners excel in deterministic settings while the comparative picture changes under stochasticity and partial information.

entry.title: How Many Repeated Pairwise Comparisons Are Needed for Ranking under Heterogeneity?

author.name: Shashaank Aiyer, Han Shao

entry.summary: Studies sample complexity of ranking by population-average utility from pairwise comparisons under heterogeneous Bradley-Terry preferences across users and tasks. Develops MLE-based and randomized Russian Roulette-style algorithms with improved guarantees on repeated comparisons per context needed for ranking recovery.

entry.title: Coefficient Calibration as Selection Pressure in Symbolic Regression

author.name: Mattia Billa, Veronica Guidetti, Federica Mandreoli

entry.summary: In memetic symbolic regression, coefficient calibration protocols implicitly shape evolutionary selection by favoring structures whose fits depend on sample-specific coefficients. The authors propose Dirichlet-Sinkhorn Constant Averaging (DSCA), which calibrates each candidate on multiple covariate-shifted partitions and evaluates at the mean parameters, with theory relating excess loss to calibration stability. This improves robustness of discovered symbolic expressions.

entry.title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries

author.name: Weizheng Zhang, Xunjie Xie, Hao Pan, Lin Lu

entry.summary: Cova-PINN improves multi-domain PINNs for fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer by aligning conservation support with thermal interaction paths in complex geometries, jointly optimizing local cross-domain control-volume balances and global paired-wall closure. On four TPMS-based benchmark geometries it corrects a failure mode where standard multi-domain PINNs produce plausible temperature fields but wrong end-to-end energy transfer.

entry.title: Camera-Noise Residuals for Face-Swap Detection: Redundant, Not Complementary, and Why

author.name: Danil Davydov, Bader Rasheed, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Tests whether camera-noise fingerprints (Noiseprint++ residuals) add complementary information to an RGB Xception backbone for face-swap detection on FaceForensics++, finding that fusion yields no improvement and the residual branch alone is near chance. A bottleneck diagnostic shows the residual signal is statistical rather than physics-grounded as commonly assumed. A valuable negative result correcting a popular assumption in deepfake detection.

entry.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework

author.name: Aaron Dsouza, Mohammed Azeez Khan, Ashutosh Mishra, Arshaan Khan, Neha K. Nair, Amar Kumar Behera

entry.summary: The paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation, mapping STEP assemblies to a typed ProductGraph representation, deriving precedence via topological sorting, and realizing steps as language conditioned on structured engineering data, with human oversight in the loop. It unifies previously separate threads of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, and instruction writing.

entry.title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search

author.name: Ziming Dai, Dabiao Ma, Ziheng Guo, Jack Dong, Zimu Zhou

entry.summary: LLM-BlockFE is an offline framework that uses LLMs to convert long unstructured text into executable feature programs for industrial risk-control systems, avoiding costly LLM calls at inference time. It builds features by incrementally appending immutable code blocks and evaluates candidates with a downstream model. This bridges the gap between structured-data model efficiency and information trapped in free text.

entry.title: Learning What to Trust in Multimodal Learning under Noisy Supervision

author.name: Jiashuo Zou, Xiaobo Xia

entry.summary: The paper theoretically analyzes how multimodal representation structure relates to noise detection capability and proposes REFINE, a multimodal noise detector that identifies mislabeled examples by leveraging cross-modal information. It extends noisy-label sample-selection methods beyond unimodal settings where ground-truth labels are scarce.

entry.title: Accelerating Non-Smooth and Heavy-Tailed Sampling

author.name: Pervez Ali, Xiaoyu Wang, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: The authors propose non-reversible anchored Langevin dynamics (NALD) and its reflected variant for sampling non-differentiable and heavy-tailed target densities in free and constrained spaces. The constructions add a circulation drift from a divergence-free skew-symmetric matrix field plus an acceleration term to speed convergence over anchored Langevin dynamics.

entry.title: RobustLDS: Learning linear dynamical systems under adversarial corruptions

author.name: Aravinda Kanchana Ruwanpathirana, Hemant Tyagi

entry.summary: This work studies robust identification of linear dynamical systems from a single trajectory where a fraction of observations are adversarially corrupted. The authors propose estimators based on least-trimmed squares relaxations with alternating minimization, plus group-sparsity-penalized variants, and derive non-asymptotic error guarantees. It extends classical robust statistics into dynamical system learning.

entry.title: Prosody-to-Text: Predicting text from low-pass filtered speech

author.name: David Porte\v{s}, Ale\v{s} Hor\'ak

entry.summary: This paper inverts the standard prosody task by fine-tuning Whisper on only the 12 lowest Mel bins (roughly 450Hz cutoff) to predict text from prosodic patterns alone. It recovers text surprisingly well, with 36% WER, 10% of utterances recovered perfectly, and 40% at or below a much lower error rate, revealing how much lexical information is embedded in low-frequency speech.

entry.title: EgoVoice: Proactive Spoken Assistance from Egocentric Multimodal Streams

author.name: Heeseung Kim

entry.summary: EgoVoice is a framework for training and evaluating proactive egocentric spoken assistants that jointly decide when to speak and what to say from continuous first-person video and audio streams. The authors construct clean audio data from HoloAssist recordings via source separation and speech resynthesis to build the training resource.

entry.title: PCAsplat: Gaussian Splatting with Local PCA Regularization

author.name: Vitor Matias, Filipe Nascimento, Kiyohiro Nakayama, Jo\~ao Paulo Lima, M\'arcus Lobo, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas, Afonso Paiva, Tiago Novello

entry.summary: PCAsplat introduces a geometry-aware regularization for Gaussian splatting based on differentiable local PCA over neighborhoods of Gaussian centers, allowing updates to occluded or weakly supervised Gaussians that rasterization-based losses leave underconstrained and prone to becoming floaters. The regularizer acts directly on point neighborhoods independent of current camera views. This improves surface fidelity in 3D reconstruction from posed images.

entry.title: IntactWorld: Joint World Modeling with Intact Features

author.name: Boming Tan, Xiangdong Zhang, Yan Xia, Qi Zhu, Deyi Ji, Xue Yang, Shaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: IntactWorld is a joint world modeling architecture that operates on uncompressed intact features, arguing that existing approaches compress features and lose structural information about real-world logic. The authors note that predicting flow velocity in uncompressed high-dimensional space creates a manifold gap since data lie on a low-dimensional manifold, and they design the architecture around this tension. The aim is video generation with genuine physical understanding.

entry.title: EgoPhys: Estimating Peak Contact Force and Mechanical Work from Egocentric Manipulation Video
