author.name: Zhuo Dong, Jianhua Yang, Haohao Li, Yumeng Zhao, Keji He, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Presents EgoPhys, an RGB-only framework for estimating physical quantities such as peak contact force and mechanical work from egocentric manipulation video, using contact-aware spatial aggregation and multi-expert temporal routing. Useful for physically grounded robotic manipulation understanding.

entry.title: Fast Pose Tracking of Rigid Objects with Compact Pose Graph Optimization

author.name: Xiaojie Zhang, Tom Fischer, Viktor Larsson, Eddy Ilg

entry.summary: Shows that lightweight pose graph optimization operating only on relative pose constraints (weighted by derived uncertainty) can wrap around diverse correspondence estimators to track novel-object 6D pose over long horizons in real time. This avoids expensive onboarding or per-sequence reconstruction, making it practical for robotics and AR.

entry.title: Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yicheng Xue, Han Wu, Jufeng Yang, Minjing Dong, Xinghao Chen, Hanting Chen, Jianyuan Guo

entry.summary: Proposes ViMoD, a lightweight framework for multimodal LLMs that maintains a compact visual context while allowing on-demand access to fine-grained visual evidence during multi-step reasoning, using content-adaptive region-wise token aggregation (DART). This addresses the limitation of fixed one-shot visual token compression as reasoning needs evolve.

entry.title: Skill-SLM: Agent Skill-driven Small Language Models for Reliable Robot Operation

author.name: Wenhao Wang, Yanyan Li, Jiawei Yuan

entry.summary: Skill-SLM reformulates small-language-model-driven robot operation as task decomposition and skill composition: given a natural language instruction, the model decomposes the task, selects skills from a library, and orchestrates them into executable operations. This avoids distillation-style training that requires enumerating task-solution pairs and improves generalization to diverse tasks.

entry.title: Distributed Relative Localization for Homogeneous Multi-Robot Systems through UWB Ranging and Limited Communications

author.name: Zhiqiang Cao, Ran Liu, Billy Pik Lik Lau, Chau Yuen, U-Xuan Tan

entry.summary: This paper presents a distributed relative pose estimation approach integrating LiDAR, UWB, and odometry so each robot can continuously localize teammates without external infrastructure. A dynamic tracker follows anonymous LiDAR clusters and teammate identification is performed to resolve ambiguity among robots with similar appearances.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Collision Learning Framework for Collaborative Robot Motion Generation

author.name: Chen Cai, Steven Liu

entry.summary: PI-UDF is a physics-informed, differentiable framework for predicting pairwise inter-arm collision distances between articulated robots, combining analytical forward kinematics, learnable link-geometry embeddings, and a shared residual network. It targets gradient-based MPC for close-proximity dual-arm manipulation with safety-critical fidelity, using quota-driven training strategies.

entry.title: A 3D Characterization Framework for Intelligent Sequential Decision Making

author.name: Sadig Gojayev, Carolina Fortuna

entry.summary: The paper introduces a three-dimensional framework for comparing sequential-decision AI approaches - projecting methods onto the MDP formalism, ranking autonomy via human priors on design, and measuring skill versus computational cost. It applies this to compare graph-based, reinforcement learning, and LLM-based approaches on puzzle tasks under unified conditions.

entry.title: MSGAT: Multi-Head Spiking Graph Attention with Similarity-Space Fusion for Image-Text Retrieval

author.name: Xintao Zong, Wenxuan Liu, Jianhao Ding, Zhaofei Yu, Tiejun Huang

entry.summary: MSGAT extends spiking neural networks to image-text retrieval via multi-head spiking graph attention for structural modeling and dynamic attention with similarity-space fusion, addressing the difficulty of capturing semantic cross-modal alignment with sparse spike representations. It avoids reliance on local alignment and extra soft-label supervision used by prior spiking ITR methods. The work advances energy-efficient event-driven multimodal computing on a high-level task.

entry.title: From Pixels to Structure: Lightweight Vision-Language Models for Document OCR and Structured JSON Extraction

author.name: Uddipan Basu Bir, Vincent Christlein, Andreas Maier, Mathias Zinnen

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates eight open-source lightweight VLMs (up to 7B parameters) for OCR-to-structured-JSON extraction across three university heritage collections featuring historical handwriting and domain-specific layouts. It addresses institutional needs for data autonomy, cost, and environmental footprint versus commercial API dependence.

entry.title: LVS: Local View Synthesis from Relative Camera Pose by Reusing Previous Views

author.name: Qizhou Huo, Xuan Sun, Yongfei Guo, Zhipeng Wang, Yuanhao Gong

entry.summary: LVS replaces repeated 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering for nearby views with relative-pose-guided RGB-D image reuse: geometric warping transports source content while a lightweight multiscale network predicts RGB residuals to fix artifacts and infer newly exposed content. Cached source features further reduce computation for interactive scene exploration.

entry.title: SPD-MetaFormer is what you need for small-data brain decoding

author.name: Zhida Wang, Wei Lyu, Guo Yu, Sui Tang

entry.summary: Analyzing attention-based models on the symmetric positive definite (SPD) manifold for brain signal decoding, the authors find that learned attention weights in architectures like MAtt and GBWAtt remain near-uniform after training due to bounded similarity parameterizations limiting contrast under softmax scaling. Motivated by this, they propose an SPD-MetaFormer architecture suited to small-data, noisy neural recordings.

entry.title: SACQ: Structured Decoding with Memory-Conditioned Refinement for Long-Horizon Forecasting

author.name: Guo Cheng, Zhengzhuo Xu, Chenchen Jing, Jingyi Hou

entry.summary: SACQ replaces the standard flatten readout head of patch-based long-term forecasting models with a two-stage structured decoding pipeline: a coarse patch-grid forecast scaffold followed by per-position refinement via cross-attention over historical memory. This decouples future positions from a single shared projection, improving position-specific historical-to-future alignment and robustness to corrupted inputs and noisy supervision. The encoder remains unchanged, making it a drop-in head replacement.

entry.title: GHARP: Real-time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-scale Reconstruction Prior

author.name: Ali Benlalah, Sepehr Johari, Patricia Vitoria, Armin Kappeler, Artem Sevastopolsky, Alexander Jung, Gabriele Fanelli, Kevin Mader, Manuel Breitenstein, Claudia Pl\"uss, Jan R\"uegg, Simon Biland, Thomas Etterlin, Dmitry Kostiaev, Mathias Deschler, Brian Amberg, Sebastian Martin

entry.summary: GHARP animates 3D human heads in real time from a few input images and a driving expression signal, splitting the task into an expensive offline identity stage and a lightweight mobile-optimized runtime animation stage. It operates in a semantically structured latent space of a pretrained head reconstruction prior to balance fidelity, quality, and speed.

entry.title: BioBigBird: A Sparse Attention Model for Long-Range Dependency Processing in Biomedical Text

author.name: Roshan Balaji, Pavan Kumar S, Vasudev Gupta, Sreejith N, Keerthana Sridhar, Nirav Bhatt

entry.summary: BioBigBird is a bidirectional sparse-attention language model pre-trained on biomedical literature and clinical data to handle sequences up to 4096 tokens, with multi-stage training to mitigate corpus noise and multi-task learning jointly optimizing NER and related objectives. It targets long-range dependency understanding in biomedical texts.

entry.title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations

author.name: Johanna Moser, Christopher Albert, Sascha Ranftl

entry.summary: The authors introduce ghost tasking, a procedure using auxiliary output tasks to make non-parametrizable linear differential equation systems effectively parametrizable for parametrized Gaussian process solvers, with proofs of this effect. It keeps the number of required tasks and latent functions low and performs well empirically. This expands the applicability of physics-informed Gaussian processes in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Density Ratio Estimation with Stein Displacement Fields

author.name: Song Liu

entry.summary: This paper unifies density ratio estimation and displacement fields by parameterizing the log-ratio as minus the Stein operator of the base distribution applied to a displacement field, solved via a single convex optimization. This yields both statistical and dynamical views of distribution shift simultaneously, with an iterative estimation procedure. It matters for two-sample testing, anomaly detection, and any task quantifying distribution shift.

entry.title: Detecting Spin in Clinical Trials with Large Language Models

author.name: Tja\v{s} Ajdovec, Marko Robnik-\v{S}ikonja, Simon \v{S}uster

entry.summary: The authors build an automatic system for detecting outcome switching, a key form of spin in clinical trial reporting, using 300 labeled outcome pairs with semantic similarity scores. They evaluate baseline similarity models and open-source LLMs with prompt engineering and Youden-index thresholding to flag distorted reporting.

entry.title: TKCAM: Text and Keyframe to Camera Trajectory Generation

author.name: Haozhe Yang, Zhiyang Dou, Zekai Gu, Cheng Lin, Wenping Wang, Yuan Liu, Taku Komura

entry.summary: TKCAM generates controllable camera trajectories from text prompts and sparse visual keyframes using generative masked modeling. It represents camera dynamics as 12-dimensional kinematic features (position, velocity, continuous rotation) discretized via residual vector quantization, with a two-stage masked transformer for reconstruction and refinement. The framework targets AI-assisted cinematography and video synthesis.

entry.title: RGBD-to-3D Object Mesh Refinement via Depth Matching and Symmetry Propagation

author.name: Ahyun Seo, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: The authors present a lightweight, plug-and-play refinement for single-view RGB-to-3D reconstruction that uses an available depth map. Visible surfaces are corrected via bipartite matching against back-projected depth points, corrections are mirrored across a detected symmetry plane to the occluded side, and propagated with a smoothness solver. All stages are closed-form, making it orders of magnitude faster than optimization-based test-time refinement, with consistent gains across five backbones on GSO and OmniObject3D.

entry.title: OX-NeRF: 3D X-ray Tomography Reconstruction from Sparse Views Using Implicit Neural Representation

author.name: Thomas Welsch, Min-Hsin Tu, David J. Chapman, Daniel E. Eakins

entry.summary: Presents OX-NeRF, a framework for ultra-sparse X-ray tomography (10 or fewer views) that combines cross-scene feature learning via a CNN with scene-specific multi-resolution hash grid optimization, fusing both for implicit representation reconstruction. Targets high-rate or low-dose acquisition scenarios where classical methods fail.

entry.title: Streaming-Aware Diffusion for Real-Time Video Super-Resolution via Cross-Step Attention

author.name: Harris Partaourides, Sotirios Chatzis

entry.summary: Adapts pretrained single-image latent diffusion models for real-time video super-resolution by reusing intermediate denoising features across adjacent frames and steps via Cross-Step Attention, plus a Trajectory-Coupled Diffusion Scheduling scheme. This achieves temporal coordination without explicit temporal modeling under strict latency constraints.

entry.title: TacHair: Tactile Contact-Distribution Guided Online Correction for Robotic Hair Stroking and Perception

author.name: Ruiyi Hu, Yongqiang Zhao, Daniel Bak, Yupeng Wang, Xuyang Zhang, Shan Luo

entry.summary: TacHair is a framework for robotic hair stroking that represents high-resolution tactile observations as a spatial hair-contact distribution, used for online correction while a visuotactile imitation policy generates the nominal stroking motion. It addresses the difficulty of regulating contact with deformable hair that drifts across the end-effector during interaction.

entry.title: Leveraging Human-In-The-Loop Demonstrations in Reinforcement Learning for Digital Twin-Driven Robot Flexibility

author.name: Yuzhu Sun, Mien Van, Nguyen Minh Nhat, Stephen McIlvanna, Sean McLoone

entry.summary: This paper proposes a human-in-the-loop online training framework combining a real-time synchronized digital twin, reinforcement learning, and human demonstrations, demonstrated on a Ufactory robot arm. A dual actor design integrates imitation guidance without a direct imitation loss on the RL actor, allowing demonstrations to drive adaptation instead of manual reprogramming.

entry.title: An Explainable Header-Centric Framework for Large-Scale Semantic Table Interpretation and Data Quality Assessment

author.name: Marcelo Valentim Silva, Hannes Herrmann, Valerie Maxville

entry.summary: This paper presents an explainable framework for semantic table interpretation when cell values are unavailable, using column headers as the primary semantic evidence for knowledge graph preparation. It maps headers to 39 interpretable format types with token-level traceability and activates data quality validation rules based on a taxonomy of quality issues.

entry.title: GameCommBench: A Unified Benchmark and Type-Aware Evaluation for AI-Generated Game Commentary

author.name: Qirui Zheng, Zhengteng Lin, Yunyi Xiao, Junhao Li, Keyuan Cheng, Xingbo Wang, Yongyi Wang, Lingfeng Li, Yunlong Lu, Wenxin Li

entry.summary: GameCommBench unifies AI-generated game commentary evaluation across board games, sports, and esports with commentary aligned to heterogeneous game contexts and annotated by type. The proposed Type-Aware Commentary Evaluation framework is validated for reliability and human agreement and used to benchmark existing models.

entry.title: The Operator Mismatch Problem: Deploying BEV Perception with Portable GPU Compute

author.name: Rohit Verma, Anand V Bodas

entry.summary: The paper identifies an operator mismatch that blocks deployment of bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception models through standard inference runtimes: sparse 3D convolutions and geometric scatter operations are unsupported and locked to CUDA/PyTorch. It presents BEVPIPE, a framework for portable GPU deployment of multimodal BEV pipelines.

entry.title: Onboard Marine Anomaly Detection on $\Phi$sat-2: From Simulation-Based Development to In-Orbit Demonstration

author.name: Clotilde Szywala, Thomas Goudemant, Marjorie Bellizzi, Benjamin Francesconi, Adrien Girard

entry.summary: Describes the development, integration, and post-launch adaptation of a lightweight marine anomaly detection pipeline running onboard ESA's Phi-sat-2 satellite, combining sea segmentation, self-supervised encoding, and deviation-based anomaly detection. It is one of the documented end-to-end demonstrations of AI inference on an orbiting Earth-observation platform.

entry.title: HANS: A Handwritten Answer Sheet Dataset for Noisy Hybrid Document Parsing

author.name: Xiazhen Wu, Wansong Qin, Yangbin Zheng, Liangda Fang, Zhan Li, Xiujie Huang, Liushen Zhou, Quanlong Guan

entry.summary: HANS is the first dataset built for real-world educational document parsing, containing handwritten answer sheets with multi-line mathematical derivations, mixed text and formulas, hand-drawn tables, and noise artifacts like strikethroughs. It addresses the gap between clean printed-document benchmarks and messy real-world grading scenarios.

entry.title: WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation

author.name: Krish Bakshi

entry.summary: Introduces WorldBench, a benchmark and interactive judge for open-ended LLM-generated Three.js voxel worlds, where the judge actively explores the running world, controls its clock, and probes content. The authors show that snapshot-based VLM judges and source-reading LLM judges disagree on 32 percent of required items, motivating the interactive evaluation approach.

entry.title: From Log-Odds to Shapley Values: An Explanatory Geometry for the Weighted Naive Bayes Classifier

author.name: Vincent Lemaire, Fabrice Cl\'erot

entry.summary: Derives an explanatory geometry for the weighted naive Bayes classifier, showing that a discriminative log-odds representation induces a distance exactly coinciding with the l1 distance between analytical Shapley value vectors. This provides a formal explanatory interpretation of the classifier's induced geometry, validated empirically with k-nearest-neighbor comparisons.

entry.title: AI-Mediated Self: How HCI Defines and Relates to the Self

author.name: Jenny Xiyu Fu, Qian Yang, Malte Jung

entry.summary: This scoping review of 102 papers analyzes how human-computer interaction research defines the self and conceptualizes AI-self relationships, introducing the AI-mediated self as an umbrella concept spanning education, work, health, and creativity. It consolidates six framings of the self with four domains of ethical risk into a reusable conceptual map.

entry.title: Probabilistic Sensing, Deterministic Authority: Admitting Model-Produced Observations into Sufficiency-Checked Governance Contracts

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: The paper proposes admitting model-extracted observations into deterministic governance contracts only as scored observation records, with thresholds fitted at a declared false-positive ceiling where unknown denies, and bounds the probability that sensing changes the verdict via union-bound reasoning over sensed fields. It validates the approach on two constructed registered studies.

entry.title: SP-DocReader: Difference-Aware Self-Play for Precise Document OCR

author.name: Wenjie Liao, Xiaohui Song, Liangjie Zhao, Haonan Lu

entry.summary: SP-DocReader is a self-play OCR framework targeting residual errors after supervised fine-tuning: Reading Discrepancy Masking aligns reference and generated tokens via longest common subsequence and scores unmatched positions, while Focused Fidelity Loss adds direct NLL supervision at unmatched ground-truth positions with only the OCR module trained. Compared with an SFT baseline, it reduces transcription errors under limited training budgets. It offers a targeted error-focused training signal for document transcription with VLMs.

entry.title: PMTRM: Pseudo-Memory Temporal Re-encoding Module for Embodied Policy Learning

author.name: Changchuan Yang, Haoxuan Xu, Wenbo Chen, Shuai Ren, Jianlong Zheng, Huarui Zhang, Tianfu Li, Guanzhong Tian

entry.summary: PMTRM is a lightweight (7.61M parameter) plug-in module for robotic manipulation policies that encodes a bounded history of executed states and actions into a latent sequence to resolve phase ambiguity in repeated motions. A temporal heterogeneity objective penalizes similarity between distant positions, with anchor and reconstruction losses preserving information. This addresses a real failure mode where observation-only policies repeat completed motions or switch phases prematurely.

entry.title: Evaluating Local Language Model Agents for Reproducible Data Engineering: An Empirical Software Engineering Study of Mobility Workflows

author.name: Jorge Garc\'ia-Carrasco, Javier Sanchis, Alejandro Reina-Reina, Alejandro Mat\'e, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: This empirical study benchmarks locally deployable open-weight LLM agents on fifteen mobility-workflow data-engineering tasks spanning data discovery, connectors, transport-feed processing, and semantic enrichment, measuring artifact correctness and reproducibility. It quantifies the effect of a closed-loop workspace condition and trade-offs in model scale, architecture, quantization, runtime, tool use, and failure modes. It provides rare evidence on local agents producing complete engineering artifacts rather than isolated code.

entry.title: Narrow and Deep: An Ontology Tower as the Knowledge of an LLM Agent for an Industrial Equipment System

author.name: Younghwan Joo, Sung-il Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes the ontology tower, a narrow-and-deep ontology for a single industrial equipment system, enriched with physically derived quantities and lessons from operating journals, to serve as knowledge for LLM agents controlling equipment. It validates the approach on a real low-humidity air-handling test plant operated daily via a PLC.

entry.title: Forms of LLM-Integrated Applications from LLM-Chats to Autonomous AI Agent System

author.name: Irene Weber (University of Applied Sciences Kempten, Germany)

entry.summary: This survey systematically examines whether industry labels like chatbot, copilot, and AI agent correspond to real architectural distinctions in LLM-integrated software. It finds the labels do carry architectural content, for example copilot denoting a router-worker architecture with user confirmation versus agent denoting AI-planned multi-step execution, and identifies shared reason-and-act patterns among major coding agents.

entry.title: Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes

author.name: Utku Boran Torun, Veli Karakaya, Eray T\"uz\"un

entry.summary: The study builds an execution-based pipeline in a real browser environment to automatically verify LLM-generated no-code bug fixes, such as changing a configuration or upgrading a version. It evaluates 322 fixes across 12 model configurations covering faulty-configuration, wrong-version, and external-dependency bug categories.

entry.title: MPGE: A Multi-Perspective Graph Explainer for Molecular Classification Explanation

author.name: Mahtab Sarvmaili

entry.summary: MPGE is a graph explanation method for GNN-based molecular classification that unifies three complementary explanation views for a frozen classifier: factual support (compact edge sets preserving the prediction), counterfactual sensitivity (bounded deletions that change the prediction), and exemplar tolerance (bounded tolerated modifications). This gives a richer picture of why a model made a specific molecular property prediction than any single explanation type.

entry.title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery

author.name: Xun Chen, Weiyao Ke, Yu-Gang Ma, Long-Gang Pang, Kai Zhou

entry.summary: A mini-review of machine learning in high-energy nuclear physics covering the shift from event classification toward physics-integrated workflows, including Bayesian extraction of QCD matter properties, equation-of-state inference, generative event modeling, neural unfolding, and differentiable inverse solvers. It synthesizes several years of maturing developments.

entry.title: Shape irregularity of Life-Like Network Automaton rules as an indicator of classification performance

author.name: Lucas C. S. Oliveira, Michiel Rollier, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno

entry.summary: This paper studies Life-Like Network Automata (LLNA) for extracting descriptors used in complex network classification, where selecting the automaton transition rule is typically a costly combinatorial search. The authors identify a structural property called jaggedness, quantifying how sawtooth-like a transition function is, and show it predicts which rules yield good classification performance. This could replace exhaustive rule searches with structured guidance, enabling scalable network classification.

entry.title: CityDeploy-Bench: Benchmarking Physics-Grounded Spatial Set Planning for Multi-Transmitter Network Deployment

author.name: Chenyang Yuan, Xiaoyuan Cheng

entry.summary: CityDeploy-Bench reframes city-scale multi-transmitter wireless deployment as physics-grounded spatial set planning verified by unified ray tracing, separating utility representation from planning dynamics. Experiments reveal a transition in planning behavior as physical coupling grows: deployment quality increasingly depends on whether the learned utility captures collective transmitter interactions rather than standard scalar rewards.

entry.title: CARE: A Lightweight Plug-in Gated Correction and Uncertainty-aware Module for Long-term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Guo Cheng, Changlong Lv, Jingyi Hou

entry.summary: CARE is a lightweight plug-in module that enhances any deterministic long-horizon forecaster without redesigning its architecture. It resamples historical context to match the forecast horizon, learns residual corrections from aligned history, and applies scale-aware bounded updates with per-coordinate sigmoid gating to provide localized uncertainty signals. This addresses masked heterogeneous prediction difficulty across horizons and channels in applications like electricity load and traffic forecasting.

entry.title: When to Intervene? State-Aware Sparse Manipulation in Federated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shutong Zheng, Sijia Chen

entry.summary: Identifies trajectory-level intervention timing as a distinct attack dimension in federated reinforcement learning, showing that where along a trajectory a Byzantine manipulation is applied materially changes attack efficacy. Introduces an attack framework exploiting state-aware sparse interventions. Highlights a gap in current defenses for distributed RL.

entry.title: Verification with Transfer: Exact Information Frontiers and Their Price in Calls

author.name: Hazar Yueksel

entry.summary: The paper prices information-theoretically what a verifier needs when it can query related source tasks: the least causal information any interleaving of source calls and verifications needs is characterized by a list rate-distortion function, which lower-bounds expected binary source calls, with designed sources meeting it within small additive terms. This formalizes the cost of curriculum and interleaved learning for verification.

entry.title: How Many Directions Must a Truncated Diffusion Sampler Retain? Matching Bounds Under Power-Law Spectra

author.name: Radmehr Karimian, Ali Mohades, Johannes Lederer

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how many spectral coordinates truncated diffusion samplers must retain for data with power-law covariance spectra, proving matching bounds for Gaussian data. A key finding is that keeping only directions whose signal exceeds noise level leaves non-vanishing error, because many individually weak directions aggregate into significant error. This has implications for the design of computationally cheaper diffusion samplers.

entry.title: Region-Aware CLS Token Augmentation for Fine-Grained Image Retrieval

author.name: Ian de Holanda Cavalcanti Bezerra, Vivek Trivedy, Lucas Pascotti Valem, Longin Jan Latecki

entry.summary: The paper augments the global [CLS] token and register tokens of DINOv2-reg vision transformers with spatially selected region tokens to improve fine-grained image retrieval. By capturing region-level representations tied to semantic tokens, the method improves retrieval quality over single-global-descriptor baselines.

entry.title: Q-Capsule: A Localized Capsule-Based Quantum Neural Architecture for Barren Plateau Mitigation

author.name: Awal Ahmed Fime, Tasfia Zaman Samiha, Saika Zaman, Dimitris Pados, George Sklivanitis, Abdur R. Shahid, Ahmed Imteaj

entry.summary: Q-Capsule mitigates barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms through register partitioning, local readout, sparse inter-capsule coupling, data re-uploading, and QFIM-guided adaptive depth growth. The architecture preserves gradient signal while scaling register width, addressing a core trainability obstacle for quantum neural networks.

entry.title: Phonologically Informed Tokenization for German Speech Recognition: A Cross-Domain Study

author.name: Christopher Witzl, Tobias Bocklet, Korbinian Riedhammer

entry.summary: The authors compare three tokenizer families (pretrained character inventory, orthographic BPE, and phonologically informed units from syllabification and grapheme-to-phoneme conversion) for fine-tuning wav2vec 2.0 CTC models on German ASR. Across 40 fine-tunes on three test sets spanning domain shifts, they assess whether phonological tokenization is a competitive target. The study is a careful empirical contribution for a morphologically rich language.

entry.title: Score-Based Learning of Cluster DAGs from Interventions

author.name: Gaetano Tedesco (University of Amsterdam), Alex Markham (University of Copenhagen)

entry.summary: The paper introduces COARSE, the first score-based method for learning cluster DAGs, the high-level causal graphs obtained by abstracting many low-level variables into clusters, from interventional data. It retains a two-phase structure under linear Gaussian assumptions but replaces constraint-based steps with score-based optimization. This improves interpretability of causal discovery results.

entry.title: Quickest Change Detection with Diffusion-Integrated Scores

author.name: Arman Adibi, Mohammadreza Maleki, Sanjeev Kulkarni, H. Vincent Poor

entry.summary: This paper proposes DI-SCUSUM, a training-free extension of CUSUM change detection that uses diffusion-perturbed samples and Hyvarinen scores to approximate log-likelihood ratios when the underlying distributions are unknown. The post-change mean increment is proportional to the KL divergence between pre- and post-change distributions. It matters as a practical detection method for distribution shift and anomaly monitoring without density estimation.

entry.title: Wieszcz-XIX: A 3.1-Billion-Word Corpus of Pre-1918 Polish and Temporally Bounded Language Models Trained From Scratch

author.name: Szymon Kocur

entry.summary: Wieszcz-XIX is a 6.75-billion-token corpus of Polish text from 1800-1918 assembled from Wolne Lektury and the Internet Archive, over three orders of magnitude larger than existing annotated corpora for the period, with careful filtering, deduplication, and post-1918 leakage audits. The authors also train temporally bounded language models from scratch on this data and quantify corpus defects like OCR corruption. It matters as a major resource for historical NLP and digital humanities in Polish.

entry.title: AdaptEvo: Adaptive Agent Learning with Evolving Supervision

author.name: Shijun Wan, Jiancong Xie, Hang Xu, Jin Duan, Qixiong Wang, Xi Xiang, Maofei Que, Yahui Liu, Zhongyu Wei, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: AdaptEvo is a framework for agent learning under imperfect supervision, coupling Confidence-Adaptive GRPO that balances outcome and process rewards by reference confidence with an evolution module that synthesizes reusable decision knowledge from recurring failures and refines process rubrics over time.

entry.title: When Can You Prune Your Network? A Study of Intermediate Neurons in Multilingual Speech Parsing

author.name: Minnie Kabra, Benjamin Lecouteux, Maximin Coavoux

entry.summary: This study introduces a simpler end-to-end speech parsing architecture that removes intermediate neural network units, cutting parameters by 12% while matching or beating prior methods on ASR and parsing. It analyzes when intermediate networks help, finding they reduce the representational gap when the pretrained encoder is frozen.

entry.title: Structured Sentiment Analysis Using Sequence Labeling as Dependency Graph Parsing

author.name: Muhammad Imran, Ana Ezquerro, Carlos G\'omez-Rodr\'iguez, Anders S{\o}gaard, David Vilares

entry.summary: The paper casts structured sentiment analysis as dependency graph parsing solved via sequence labeling, using linearized graph encodings that assign labels per word to capture holder-target-expression structure. Experiments across seven datasets in five languages show competitive performance with leading approaches.

entry.title: Seeing Through the Glare: A Multi-Source Benchmark and Ocular-Adaptive Pixel MeanFlow for Eyeglass Reflection Removal

author.name: Tao Liu, Youwei Pang, Kailai Zhou, Jiaming Zuo, Hanqi Liu, Wei Ji, Peng-Tao Jiang, Xiaofeng Liu, Weisi Lin, Xiaoqi Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces OcuBench, a multi-source benchmark for eyeglass reflection removal with 10,280 controllable synthetic pairs, 732 real-input pseudo-pairs, and 458 real-world test images, and proposes an ocular-adaptive pixel-level MeanFlow model for selective reflection correction. The task matters for smartphone imaging and video conferencing where reflections range from mild glare to severe occlusion. The combined benchmark-plus-model package supports more systematic evaluation and generalization.

entry.title: Expression-Diverse References for Identity-Preserving Video Generation

author.name: Tianwen Fu, Wenbin Teng, Gonglin Chen, Junyi Ouyang, Haolin Xiong, Yajie Zhao

entry.summary: This paper analyzes a blind spot in identity-preserving video generation: a single reference portrait leaves appearance under unseen expressions underdetermined, and face-recognition similarity itself degrades with expression intensity even for genuine images of the same person. The authors quantify this evaluation confound and propose using expression-diverse references for generation. It matters both for subject-fidelity generation and for fair evaluation of identity preservation.

entry.title: 3DTexMOR: 3D Gaussian Multi-Object Removal via Texture-Space Inpainting

author.name: Kunxin Guang, Yonghao Zhao, Jian Yang, Beibei Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a method for removing multiple objects from reconstructed 3D scenes by inpainting in a unified texture space shared across all views rather than in 2D images. The shared texture space aggregates complementary observations, providing richer context for completing occluded regions and avoiding the cross-view inconsistency and blurry artifacts that plague existing NeRF- and 3DGS-based removal pipelines. This is relevant for scene editing and 3D content cleanup.

entry.title: Efficient Multi-Granularity Knowledge Transfer for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Xubin Zhong, Zheyu Zhang, Wenjian Qin, Ning Wen

entry.summary: Presents EMGKT, a compact method for radiology report generation that transfers medical knowledge at multiple granularities to better describe clinically pivotal areas in X-ray images. It encodes global knowledge via a medical vision-language embedding and aggregates it for report generation.

entry.title: Perceptually Grounded and Semantics-Aware Evaluation for Holistic Co-Speech Gesture Generation

author.name: Nick Milkin, Lanmiao Liu, Esam Ghaleb, Asli Ozyurek, Zerrin Yumak

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark for evaluating co-speech gesture generation that validates 13 objective metrics against human perception and introduces Semantic Gesture Preservation (SGP), a new metric for semantic appropriateness. This addresses a genuine gap where standard metrics poorly reflect human judgment of generated gestures.

entry.title: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation

author.name: Ruicheng Zhang, Kaiwen Shen, Jiaqi Hou, Shuhan Yang, Junchao Huang, Kewei Zhang, Jun Zhou, Li Jiang, Shen Zhao

entry.summary: Recasts generalized referring expression segmentation as a closed-loop visuomotor process in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states updated by geometric action chunks, with Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling balancing semantics and boundary refinement. This moves beyond static single-pass mask prediction in cascaded VLM architectures.

entry.title: Controllable Exaggeration for Generative Motion Models via Training-Time Adaptation and Inference-Time Guidance

author.name: Amirhossein Zamani, Arianna Rampini, Bruno Roy

entry.summary: This paper incorporates the classical animation principle of exaggeration into modern character motion generative models, providing both training-time adaptation and inference-time guidance to control the degree of exaggeration. The goal is motions that are not only physically plausible but expressive and appealing to professional animators.

entry.title: Tabula Rasa: Monte Carlo estimation of unit-variance noise with controlled spatio-temporal correlation

author.name: Tobias Ritschel, Yang Zhou, Nick Milef, Mikhail Dereviannykh, Chen Liu, Christophe Hery, Carl Marshall

entry.summary: This graphics-oriented paper introduces a method for generating time-varying Gaussian noise with controlled variance and temporal correlation, formulated as joint Monte Carlo estimation of pixel reconstruction and variance via database sketching. The approach enables temporal control and coherence for downstream rendering tasks with simpler and faster code than prior methods.

entry.title: UltraLight Luma: A Novel Edge-Deployable Perception Network for Crop-Row Segmentation in Agricultural Robotics

author.name: Dhanushka Balasingham, Shamod Ginigaddarage, Hanojhan Rajahrajasingh, Nuwan Kodagoda, Rajitha de Silva

entry.summary: UltraLight Luma is a compact encoder-decoder segmentation network with only 13.1k trainable parameters for crop-row detection and navigation-line extraction on resource-constrained agricultural robots. It outperforms U-Net, YOLOv8, and YOLOv26 in parameter efficiency while needing only about 25 mJ per inference.

entry.title: Sim-to-Real RL for ASVs using SysID

author.name: Cody Sheltraw, Tsimafei Lazouski, Maani Ghaffari, Alan Papalia

entry.summary: The authors present an autonomous surface vehicle simulator and pipeline enabling reinforcement learning policies trained from unknown vehicle dynamics, requiring only a CAD model and brief open-water field tests rather than expensive hydrodynamic modeling. This addresses the sim-to-real gap and lack of parallel-environment support in existing ASV simulators.

entry.title: Fixed-Reference Pose Residuals for Measuring Cross-Dataset Cue Transfer in Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation

author.name: Bowen Yang, Xinliang Xiao, Wenjing Zhang, Li Yang, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper studies whether models anticipating which nearby person will approach and touch a robot can transfer cues across robots and sites. It introduces a fixed-reference pose residual model that decomposes predictions into a frozen geometry term and a learned pose-correction term, enabling controlled analysis of cue transfer between the HUI360 and SSUP-A egocentric datasets.

entry.title: Tight Bounds for Equivalence Testing with Non-Adaptive Conditional Samples

author.name: Gautam Kamath

entry.summary: The paper resolves the sample complexity of equivalence testing between two unknown distributions using non-adaptive conditional samples, showing a tight Theta-tilde(log n / eps^2) bound via matching algorithm and lower bound. This establishes that uniformity, identity, and equivalence testing all share the same complexity in this model.

entry.title: Automated Detection of Match Phases in Football from Spatio-Temporal Tracking Data Using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Vincent Renner, Nils Koster, Pascal Bauer, Melanie Schienle

entry.summary: This arXiv paper combines graph neural networks with an LSTM to classify football match phases second-by-second across a seven-class taxonomy using spatio-temporal tracking data from 203 matches. Beyond the sports application, it uses the rule-based labeling to systematically compare graph adjacency constructions and message-passing layers, a comparison the authors say is underexplored in GNN research. The GNN-LSTM model outperforms aggregated-feature baselines.

entry.title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury

author.name: Ying Xu, Xiaojun Liang, Li Zhang, Yixuan Yuan, Gan Huang, Yongjie Zhou, Zhen Liang

entry.summary: The study combines EEG microstate analysis with interpretable deep sequence modeling in 106 adolescents with depression to characterize brain-state dynamics during social pain in those with non-suicidal self-injury, achieving 68.55 percent discrimination accuracy. The model integrates disease-specific, domain-adversarial, consistency, and contrastive learning components.

entry.title: Intervention anchors and scientific verification in synthetic vascular predictive representations

author.name: Lingsen You, Yujun Guo, Xinyu Zhong, Zisu Peng, Wentong Wang, Li Shen, Junbo Ge

entry.summary: A mathematical and synthetic audit showing that complete orthogonal predictive coordinates alone do not bind latent directions to named interventions: capacity-matched least-squares predictors are exactly equivalent under fixed output transforms, while anchor-only observers recover interpretations only within the span of known perturbation signatures. Experiments across 64 seeds quantify transport error and anchor-driven calibration stability, motivated by vascular device-vessel prediction.

entry.title: The Missing Fourth Term for the Emulation Tensor Memory Equilibrium (TME) Model: The Residue Deconstruction Cost

author.name: Harun Bayraktar, John Gunnels, Peter Caday

entry.summary: This note corrects the Tensor-Memory Equilibrium model for FP8-emulated fp64 computation by adding the previously omitted per-input deconstruction cost incurred on SIMT pipes. The authors derive a closed-form operational-intensity threshold below which emulation cannot match native fp64, calibrating against the cuBLAS emulation path.

entry.title: Characterizing Overconfident Failure in LLM-Based Code Generation

author.name: Ravishka Rathnasuriya, Wei Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies overconfidence in code LLMs, where incorrect programs are generated with token-level confidence comparable to correct ones, across four open-source code models and three execution-based benchmarks. It evaluates whether existing uncertainty quantification methods provide early reliability signals for generated code before costly validation. This contributes empirical characterization to the calibration of code-generating models.

entry.title: Constitutional Gating and Deterministic Recovery for Multi-Agent LLM Negotiation: Ablations Against a Stateful Adversarial Gatekeeper

author.name: Masaaki Nakatsu (AO, Inc. / OrbLabs AG), Reno Wang (AO, Inc.)

entry.summary: This paper studies a three-part control stack for multi-agent LLM negotiation against a stateful adversarial gatekeeper: a 5-Pillar runtime constitution, a 4-tier swarm with majority voting and schema hard gates, and Cognitive Annealing for deterministic deadlock detection and context purge with canonical recovery. The testbed has known solutions, enabling ablations against wasted model calls from polite loops, malformed outputs, and compliance deadlocks. It targets reliability and efficiency of LLM agents facing rigid adversarial counterparts.

entry.title: Traceable World State: A Provenance-Aware State Representation and Deterministic Replay Framework for Robotic Systems

author.name: Zoe Li

entry.summary: TWS is a middleware-neutral semantic representation for robot world state that captures entities, relations, observations, confidence, and revision metadata, with immutable update operations, deterministic replay, and SHA-256 hash-chain tamper-evident logs. It enables fact provenance, decision reproduction, and execution auditing for long-running robotic tasks.

entry.title: AI-Based On-Board Maritime Object Detection for Earth Observation Payload Data Reduction on Versal Embedded Hardware

author.name: Thomas Goudemant, Aur\'elien Bobey, Omar Hlimi, Marjorie Bellizzi

entry.summary: The paper studies onboard vessel detection as a means of content-aware downlink selection for very-high-resolution Earth-observation satellites, using a YOLOX-S detector trained on a controlled dataset built from 68 annotated Maxar scenes with 43 vessel classes. The quantized model is deployed on a Versal VC1902 DPU with limited quality loss and second-scale processing times.

entry.title: Symbolic Density Estimators for Unnormalized Distributions

author.name: Vikas Kanaujia, Riyansha Singh, Shashank Sharma, Vipul Arora

entry.summary: Develops a framework for estimating symbolic, analytical expressions of unnormalized probability density functions directly from observed samples, reducing dependence on expert-chosen parametric families. Targets interpretable and generalizable models of underlying phenomena in statistical modeling.

entry.title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation

author.name: Dawid Lipinski, Jixiang Qing, Henry Moss

entry.summary: Presents a flow-matching generative model with graph neural networks for synthesizing polycrystalline microstructures represented as anisotropic power diagrams, embedding C4 rotational symmetry via an equivariant architecture. Enables resolution-independent rendering of realistic samples without costly EBSD acquisition. A well-engineered domain-specific generative approach for materials science.

entry.title: A mesh-based neural energy method for the simulation of heterogeneous composites

author.name: Pius J. M. Wichmann, Stefan Hildebrand, Sandra Klinge

entry.summary: The paper introduces M-NEM, a mesh-based discretization of the neural energy method that interpolates nodal displacements via shape functions to suppress nonphysical oscillations in simulating heterogeneous materials. This improves on collocation-based variants in physical admissibility, integration error, and computational cost.

entry.title: An Efficient Quantum Circuit for Flow Model Execution Using Quantum Neural Networks

author.name: Rui Che, Ludvig af Klinteberg

entry.summary: The paper develops efficient quantum simulation of wavefunction flow, which connects flow models to quantum dynamics via a continuity Hamiltonian, using a QROM-based phase kickback framework. This provides a concrete circuit construction for executing flow models on quantum computers.

entry.title: Efficient and Generalizable Archetypal Analysis for Discrete Data

author.name: A. Emilie J. Wedenborg, Jesper L{\o}ve Hinrich, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: This paper extends archetypal analysis beyond least squares to Bernoulli, Poisson, and multinomial observation models via a likelihood-based framework, using local quadratic approximations with sequential minimal optimization and an active-set method for scalability. This makes interpretable extremal-profile decomposition applicable to binary, count, and categorical data. A well-executed methodological extension of a classical tool.

entry.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube

author.name: Thomas Weinberger

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes sharp sample complexity thresholds for Gaussian regression in known subspaces of low-degree functions on the Boolean cube, characterizing when random inputs delay the parametric rate due to undersampling. It derives a worst-subspace minimax threshold of order (m+t) exp{E_{d,k}} with matching upper and lower bounds under conditions. It matters as precise statistical theory explaining how random design affects learnability on discrete domains.

entry.title: Diffu-LoRA: A Novel Low-Rank Adaptation for Personalized Diffusion Models

author.name: Tianjing Li, Wei Zhu

entry.summary: Diffu-LoRA personalizes text-to-image diffusion models from a few reference images by inserting trainable low-rank components with learnable gates into transformer linear layers, using bilevel optimization to allocate adaptation capacity across layers and progressive pruning to remove redundant components. This improves subject identity preservation while following new-context prompts compared to uniform LoRA allocation. It matters for parameter-efficient personalization of generative models.

entry.title: Beyond Sequences: Distilling Structured Decision Memory for LLM Recommendation

author.name: Leikun Liang, Guoshuai Wang, Xingsheng He, Yushan Han, Yunyi Xuan, Xiaoxiao Xu, Lin Qu

entry.summary: MARI addresses the flattening of heterogeneous user actions into homogeneous token sequences in LLM-based recommendation, grounding predictions in explicit, structured decision evidence with memory augmentation to capture semantic hierarchies and trade-offs like price versus quality. It targets difficult-choice scenarios with highly similar items.

entry.title: DOGS: Design-Space Sampling for Prompt-Driven Logo Generation

author.name: Ganyu Zou, Chen Dai, Nathan Self, Kevin Piper, Ramachandra Rao Seethiraju, Karthik Shyamsunder, Chang-Tien Lu, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: DOGS recasts prompt optimization for logo generation as sampling within a structured design space rather than text rewriting, using an Originality-aware GFlowNet Sampler over a large corpus to generate prompts that encode relational design priors. It also addresses an uncontrolled channel through which protected trademarks may be reproduced in text-to-image generation. This combines structured generation with an IP-safety concern for commercial design applications.

entry.title: Breaking the Group Size Barrier: Parameter-Efficient Group Dance Generation with Chain-of-Dancers

author.name: Jing Xu, Cunjian Chen, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: ChainDance reformulates group dance generation as a sequential chain over per-dancer conditional distributions, analogous to chain-of-thought, so a single model scales to arbitrary group sizes without retraining. Existing end-to-end transformers fix group size and entangle per-dancer identities across frames. The approach preserves individual dancer identity while modeling dense inter-person coordination for music-driven choreography.

entry.title: FlyMark: Training-Free Invisible Watermarking of 3D Gaussian Splatting via a Fruit Fly Connectome

author.name: Ziyuan Luo, Haoliang Li, Renjie Wan

entry.summary: Introduces FlyMark, a training-free watermarking scheme for 3D Gaussian Splatting that embeds a keyed message directly into the stored parameters, using carrier directions derived from a published fruit fly photoreceptor connectome as a fixed, citable artifact. This makes ownership evidence checkable even after embedding tooling and rendered views are gone.

entry.title: EchoDiST: Self-distillation-based joint learning for diffusion-conditioned echocardiographic myocardial motion estimation

author.name: Feiyue Qi, Xingyue Wei, Jianwen Luo

entry.summary: Proposes EchoDiST, an unsupervised framework for echocardiographic myocardial motion estimation combining self-distillation joint learning with a diffusion-conditioned motion estimation network, avoiding the need for expert-labeled myocardial segmentations or ground-truth displacement fields. Targets quantitative cardiac function assessment.

entry.title: Look Where You Can: Active View Selection for CAD Reconstruction under Occlusion

author.name: Kartik Bali, Mahish Guru, Yiderigun Borjigin, Alexandra Starostina, Christian J. Cyron, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: Introduces SightCAD, a framework for parametric CAD reconstruction that treats view feasibility as a first-class constraint, using a learned view selector to choose K physically feasible and informative views for a VLM-based reconstructor from objects embedded in realistic indoor scenes. This addresses the unrealistic assumption of unrestricted visual access in prior CAD benchmarks.

entry.title: A Minimal Optical-Flow Representation for Vision-Based Tactile Rotation Classification in Robotic Manipulation Across Gravity Domains

author.name: Oscar Martinez-Bernal, Mario Cavero-Vidal, Francesco Grella, Carol Martinez

entry.summary: The paper compresses dense optical flow from a simulated GelSight Mini tactile sensor into a compact 126-feature grid representation for classifying object rotation direction across Earth, Mars, Moon, and orbital gravity. It finds gravity induces a small but significant feature shift (about 1.6% of variance) that still degrades models trained only on Earth data, motivating gravity-aware transfer.

entry.title: Testing Algebraic Complete Intersections

author.name: Alessandro Tamai

entry.summary: Given i.i.d. samples in high-dimensional space, this work designs a procedure to test whether the distribution concentrates near a real algebraic complete intersection of prescribed dimension, degree, and condition number — effectively testing the manifold hypothesis within this class. The method either certifies nonexistence (up to relaxation) or returns a candidate regression manifold with controlled geometric complexity.

entry.title: SR-TTA: Spatial-Redundancy Test-Time Adaptation for Interference-Robust Respiration Sensing

author.name: Jingyuan Liu, Zheng Chang, Haoqiu Xiong, Zhuangzhuang Cui, Sofie Pollin

entry.summary: Addresses respiration sensing on cell-free massive MIMO base stations, showing that learned complex-weight beamforming recovers breathing waveforms via spatial nulling under in-band motion interference, and that label-free test-time adaptation closes the remaining gap to a per-recording oracle. Identifies which label-free signal enables this adaptation. Relevant to 6G integrated sensing and communication.

entry.title: Fresco++: Frequency-Guided and Canonical-Consistent Optimization for Fine-Grained Head Avatar Modeling

author.name: Shikun Zhang, Yong Li, Yiqun Wang, Qiuhong Ke, Cunjian Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Fresco++, a unified optimization framework for head avatar reconstruction that uses a progressive frequency curriculum (low-frequency first, then high-frequency) and canonical cross-view consistency supervision to avoid unstable detail fitting and viewpoint-inconsistent appearance. Targets fine facial and hair detail recovery.

entry.title: Evidence-Traceable Dynamic Interviewer Architecture for Expertise-Adaptive Qualitative Interviews Using Local LLMs

author.name: Aisvarya Adeseye, Jouni Isoaho, Adeyemi Adeseye, Seppo Virtanen, Mohammad Tahir

entry.summary: The paper presents an evidence-traceable, dynamic interviewing architecture running on a locally hosted LLM that adapts question depth throughout a conversation based on the participant's expertise while preserving conversational continuity. It targets qualitative research interviews, where fixed question sequences produce repetitive or irrelevant follow-ups.

entry.title: Has LLM Screening Performance Stalled in Software Engineering Systematic Reviews?

author.name: Aleksi Huotala, Miikka Kuutila, Mika M\"antyl\"a

entry.summary: Re-evaluates LLM performance on screening studies for software engineering systematic reviews using the SESR-Eval benchmark and a new power-sampled SESR-Eval-Mini subset, testing eight recent LLMs, multiple prompts, and refined inclusion/exclusion criteria. The study updates earlier performance claims in light of rapid model evolution.

entry.title: TRACE: A Governance Framework for Measuring Explainability Debt in Production AI Systems

author.name: Harish Kant Pathak

entry.summary: TRACE is a seven-instrument governance framework for measuring and remediating Explainability Debt in production AI systems, anchored by an Explainability Debt Score quantifying the share of production decisions below a governance-defined explainability threshold. Complementary instruments track debt accumulation and remediation over time.

entry.title: Improving Image-Based Nutrition Estimation Through Multimodal Food-Item Verification and Recovery

author.name: Jingbo Yue, Bruce Coburn, Jinge Ma, Jui-Feng Chi, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a fine-tuning-free framework using multimodal LLMs to inventory visible foods, verify each item's identity and whether its proposed region supports portion estimation, and trigger at most one targeted recovery pass for gaps and omitted foods. Recovered regions are re-verified blind to the recovery prompt before reconciliation into a final nutrition estimate. This addresses silent failure modes in single-image dietary assessment with a structured verification design.

entry.title: Sera: Semantic Representation Aggregation for Reliable and Interpretable Battery Health Forecasting

author.name: Jiawei Li, Fang Liu, Wei Zhang, Zuming Liu, Man-Fai Ng, Zhi Wei Seh

entry.summary: Sera complements temporal models for battery state-of-health forecasting with explicit degradation semantics guided by battery domain expertise, making predictions more reliable and interpretable than purely numerical time-series approaches. It addresses nonlinear degradation and heterogeneity across batteries by representing higher-level degradation characteristics. The framework aims at practical battery management applications.

entry.title: Epistemic Disturbance in the Graph Model for Conflict Resolution: State-Preserving Actions, Four-Valued Assessments, and the Distinction between Capability and Intention

author.name: Yukiko Kato

entry.summary: This theory paper extends the graph model for conflict resolution with state-preserving actions such as announcements, leaks, and selective disclosures that leave the physical state unchanged but alter other decision makers' beliefs. It augments states with epistemic states and distinguishes capability from intention via four-valued assessments.

entry.title: Using Weisfeiler-Leman Features for Algorithm Selection in Constraint Optimisation

author.name: Alessio Pellegrino, Jacopo Mauro

entry.summary: The paper introduces an automated feature extraction method for algorithm selection in constraint programming, converting problem instances to graphs and applying Weisfeiler-Leman graph kernels to capture structural properties that hand-crafted statistics miss. This exploits the known equivalence between 1-WL distinguishing power and message-passing GNN expressiveness.

entry.title: Temporal transformer CAN encoder with federated lightweight heads for anomaly detection

author.name: Konstantinos Gyftodimos, Kyriakos Chiotis, Elena Politi, George Dimitrakopoulos, Eirini Liotou

entry.summary: Proposes a privacy-preserving anomaly detection framework for in-vehicle CAN bus networks, combining a temporal transformer encoder with federated lightweight per-vehicle heads. The approach captures timing, payload, and message-pattern anomalies that rule-based or per-message methods miss, without centralizing sensitive vehicle data.

entry.title: Language Models for Page-Level Layout Decisions in E-commerce Search

author.name: Varun Joshi, Eva C. Song, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: The paper uses language models to decide page-level layout changes in e-commerce search, such as when and where to insert recommender secondary stacks, avoiding costly online A/B tests. Since interleaving-style evaluation is well established for ranking but not for layout, the authors propose LLM-based evaluation of layout decisions, an applied problem relevant to large-scale search systems.

entry.title: Low-Cost Sensor Calibration for Indoor Air Quality Monitoring: A Dataset, Evaluation Scenarios, and a Lightweight Model

author.name: Jinyong Yun, Seokho Ahn, Hyungjin Kim, Sungbok Shin, Young-Duk Seo

entry.summary: The paper contributes a six-month dataset of multivariate indoor air-quality measurements from low-cost and reference sensors with contextual metadata across five locations, plus four evaluation scenarios covering spatial generalization, long-term drift, and event-conditioned calibration. It also proposes a lightweight calibration model that relaxes the strict requirement of a co-located reference sensor at each deployment. This is a useful applied resource for scalable environmental monitoring.

entry.title: MotiveMob: Motivation as Semantic Action for Closed-Loop Human Mobility Generation

author.name: Mengkun Gao, Zengqing Wu, Renhe Jiang, Jiawei Wang, Yusong Wang, Chuang Yang, Shuyuan Zheng, Makoto Onizuka, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes generating human mobility trajectories by explicitly modeling motivation as a semantic action in a why-where-when decision process, improving robustness under user-level and temporal distribution shift. Useful for urban planning and transportation simulation. The explicit intent modeling is a reasonable structural improvement over coarse trajectory-level generation.

entry.title: Does an Illumination Prior Help Face-Swap Detection? A Controlled Study of Temporal Self-Blended Images

author.name: Danil Davydov, Bader Rasheed, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Companion negative-result study examining whether illumination inconsistencies added to self-blended images improve face-swap detection, using Temporal Self-Blended Images with controlled luminance mismatch. Across five training regimes and four datasets, no illumination-specific improvements are found beyond seed variability; T-SBI mainly shifts prediction scores and thresholds. Complements the same team's noise-residual study.

entry.title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders

author.name: Joel-Pascal Ntwali N'konzi, Feliks N\"{u}ske, Stefan Klus

entry.summary: This work introduces extended dynamic mode decomposition with kernel-based autoencoders learned via bilevel optimization, offering an interpretable and theoretically tractable alternative to neural-network autoencoders for learning Koopman dictionaries. It addresses the core Koopman challenge of avoiding a priori dictionary specification while retaining kernel methods' analytical advantages. Relevant to data-driven modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems.

entry.title: Causal-fate dynamics of unrealized influence

author.name: Yiwei Liu, Luwei Yang, Shunbo Lei

entry.summary: This theoretical work formalizes causal-fate dynamics, where generated influence in a dynamical system may be realized, remain latent, or be transformed by subsequent dynamics, providing an exact finite-transport representation. A connectome-constrained C. elegans model motivates the hypothesis that unresolved inter-neuronal influence persists and contributes to later propagation.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization via Complex-Valued Fusion

author.name: Anirudh Praveen, Koteswar Rao Jerripothula, Pratik Joshi, Aveen Dayal, Neela Sawant

entry.summary: The paper proposes computing complex-valued visual-text and audio-text similarities and learning their fusion with a complex-valued neural network, replacing the fixed scalar fusion rules (geometric mean, weighted average) common in open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization. This preserves richer cross-modal phase and magnitude information when scoring unseen event classes. It targets the OV-AVEL task built on frozen multimodal foundation models like ImageBind.

entry.title: ISBO: Scalable Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Optimization with Log Gaussian Cox Process Models via the INLA-SPDE Approach

author.name: Kaichuang Yang, H{\aa}vard Rue, Jakob Zeitler

entry.summary: ISBO introduces the first scalable Bayesian optimization framework for spatio-temporal objectives by modeling the log-intensity with a Log-Gaussian Cox Process and performing inference via the INLA-SPDE approach on meshes with Matern fields. This yields sparse Gaussian Markov random fields enabling fast posterior inference during sequential optimization. It matters for applications like sensor placement and environmental monitoring where objectives are event-count processes over space and time.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Preparation of Transportation Management Plans: A Case Study with WisDOT WisTMP System

author.name: Zihao Sheng, Pei Li, Zilin Huang, Yen-Jung Chen, Yuhao Luo, Zhengyang Wan, Steven T. Parker, David A. Noyce, Sikai Chen

entry.summary: This case study builds an LLM-assisted framework to automate the labor-intensive preparation of Transportation Management Plans for road work zones, fine-tuning multiple open-source LLMs across scales and deploying them locally for data security. The authors construct a domain-specific dataset by converting historical WisDOT WisTMP PDF documents into structured JSON question-answer pairs. It is a solid demonstration of applied LLM fine-tuning in a safety-relevant government domain.

entry.title: Fact over Fiction: Detection of Pathological Hallucinations in Sinhala-to-English Neural Machine Translation

author.name: Navam Obeysekara, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: This paper addresses reference-free detection of translation hallucinations in the low-resource Sinhala-to-English pair, contributing a 45,000-sample synthetic dataset built from five linguistically motivated corruption strategies with a semantic rescue mechanism. The authors fine-tune mDeBERTa-v3 for token-level hallucination detection.

entry.title: From Sparse Representations to Behavioral Insights for Multimodal Depression Assessment

author.name: Guimin Hu, Zihao Song, Jiachen Luo, Jiayuan Xie, Ruichu Cai

entry.summary: BehavDep decomposes multimodal behavioral representations into sparse latent factors linked to behaviorally meaningful concepts via a semantic bridge, improving interpretability of depression assessment. It also learns video-level depression tendency scores under weak supervision to handle the mismatch between user-level annotations and heterogeneous video-level behaviors.

entry.title: MCL: Meta Convolution Layer

author.name: Naim Reza, Md Al Amin, Ho Yub Jung

entry.summary: MCL revisits dynamic convolution by modeling the convolutional kernel as an input-conditioned function W(x) realized through high-order polynomial expansion rather than a linear mixture of basis kernels. Nested residual blocks inspired by deep polynomial networks generate a single input-adaptive kernel, decoupling expressivity from mixture size. This addresses the optimization and expressivity limits of conventional dynamic convolution.

entry.title: Collaboratively Guided Adversarial Robust Distillation with Teacher-Favorable Examples

author.name: Zhi Li, Haowei Liu, Hongchen Yang, Xiaoxuan Wang, Song Gao, Shaowen Yao, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes CGARD, an adversarial robustness distillation method that jointly optimizes student-adversarial and teacher-collaborative examples within the same perturbation neighborhood, where the collaborative example is constrained to keep teacher loss no higher than on clean inputs. This exploits underexplored teacher-favorable supervision regions.

entry.title: GroundSight at GroundLM 2026 Shared Tasks: GoldenViewVQA

author.name: Kun Wang, Yupeng Hu, Ruping Cao, Hao Liu, Zhiran Li, Qianlong Xiang, Harry Cheng

entry.summary: Describes CoVeR-VQA, a training-free multi-stage verification and correction pipeline for grounded multi-view driving-scene VQA that chains GPT-5.6 zero-shot predictions with view-specific verification by Gemini-3.6-Flash, joint verification with Claude-Opus-5, and group-level cross-split checks. It competed in the GoldenViewVQA shared task.

entry.title: Hankel Subspace Self-Supervised Learning for Parallel MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Mingyu Hu, Siquan Zhu, Xijun Zhong, Qiegen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes HSSRecon, a scan-specific self-supervised framework for parallel MRI reconstruction that partitions data by physical acquisition units before Hankel lifting to prevent data leakage between input and target, applying multiplicity-based subspace methods. Exploits multi-coil and overlapping k-space neighborhood redundancy to recover undersampled data.

entry.title: VESSI - VLM-Enhanced Support for Surveillance and Investigations

author.name: Saverio Cavasin, Pietro Tedeschi, Mattia Tamiazzo, Alessandro Brighente, Simone Milani, Mauro Conti

entry.summary: VESSI is a framework that uses vision-language models to add semantic understanding to automated video surveillance, enabling prompt-driven interrogation of video sequences for situational awareness and post-incident forensic investigation. It aims to reduce analyst burden compared to traditional surveillance systems.

entry.title: VEDJE: Video-Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoder for Scalable Video-Text Retrieval

author.name: Shahaf Wagner, Gabriele Serussi, Dan Ben Ami, Tomer Galanti, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: VEDJE compresses per-frame video features into a reusable cache while keeping representations separate, using feature-change prediction as an auxiliary training signal to improve retrieval from compressed features without extra query-time cost. It improves R@1 across MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and ActivityNet in both retrieval directions.

entry.title: From Language to Motion: Task-Conditioned Focal-Stack Trajectory Integration for Microscopic Robots

author.name: Junjie Xie, Chuxuan He, Junkai Huang, Heng Zhang, Angen Ye, Yujia Song, Yuqing Li, Pengsong Zhang, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: A semantic-to-physical framework maps natural-language instructions to constrained geometric operators for microscopic robot manipulation, reusing frozen open-vocabulary perception and integrating focal-plane trajectories via confidence weighting and dynamic programming. It achieves strong trajectory accuracy with zero new labels, cutting setup time from over an hour to 15 minutes versus part-specific U-Net training.

entry.title: MC-TRCM: Observation-Aware Recursive Fusion for Incomplete Mobile and Wearable Mental-Health Feature Views

author.name: Wentao Wang, Lifeng Han, Zining Ren, Hengyu Zhong, Guangyu Zou

entry.summary: MC-TRCM is a model for mobile and wearable mental-health data releases that consist of summarized feature tables rather than synchronized raw sensor streams. It preserves each feature source as a separate token, treats missingness as input context via learned absence tokens, conditions fusion on dataset and task embeddings, and uses a recursive prediction head refined over outputs. This targets the realistic but understudied setting of incomplete, heterogeneous mental-health feature views.

entry.title: DVLA-RL++: Dual-Level Vision-Language Alignment with Reinforcement Learning Gating for Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Wenhao Li, Xianjing Meng, Qiangchang Wang, Zhongyi Han, Yilong Yin, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: DVLA-RL++ extends a prior vision-language few-shot framework with complementary semantic purification, which separates intrinsic object descriptions from nuisance context, and counterfactual reinforcement-learning gating that sparsely evokes descriptions based on ambiguity-dependent rejection margins. The goal is to prevent support prototypes from being contaminated by incidental image context. It targets robust few-shot classification with textual semantics.

entry.title: DLC: A Metric-Guided Dynamic Loss Controller for Multi-Objective Training

author.name: Jaewan Ko, Janghoon Choi

entry.summary: Introduces DLC, an architecture- and loss-agnostic training-time controller for multi-objective image restoration that periodically evaluates the model on a feedback subset and uses quality metrics, fed through an LLM-based component, to dynamically reweight existing loss terms. It requires no new differentiable losses or architecture changes.

entry.title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Kota Shimomura, Sungho Moon, Tsubasa Hirakawa, Takayoshi Yamashita, Sunghoon Im, Hironobu Fujiyoshi

entry.summary: Proposes PAM-ToD, a lightweight plug-in for adapting pre-trained 3DGS road scenes to new times of day by learning per-Gaussian color scaling and additive brightness corrections while keeping the original 3DGS parameters fixed, using a simplified image formation model that eliminates the need to estimate albedo separately. Supports real-time rendering.

entry.title: Complexity of Grounded Semantics and Preferred Semantics in Finitary Argumentation Frameworks

author.name: Jinfan Xu, Jieting Luo

entry.summary: Maps the computational complexity of grounded and preferred semantics in computably finitary argumentation frameworks across five standard decision problems including credulous and skeptical acceptance. The work shows finitary restrictions reduce some problems from the analytical hierarchy to the arithmetical hierarchy.

entry.title: Continuous Ground-Truth Construction and a Recovery Policy for Air--Water Robotic Tracking

author.name: Jiangong Xiao, Zhe Sun, Kanzhong Yao, Yuanbo Bi, Haofei Zhao, Ruixuan Hu, Guan Huang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: The paper tackles visual tracking across the air-water interface, where splashes, bubbles, and refraction cause visual blindness. It introduces a ground-truth construction pipeline syncing cameras with motion-capture poses and correcting underwater projection, plus a recovery policy for online tracking that resists contamination of motion estimates by corrupted observations. It contributes a rare benchmark and method for a challenging cross-medium perception setting.

entry.title: CARE: Constrained Attention Refinement for Fine-Grained Visual Classification via Teacher-Student Distillation

author.name: Ruibo Wen, Hang Shao, Yiming Lei

entry.summary: CARE is a teacher-student distillation framework for interpretable fine-grained visual classification: the student keeps prediction and explanation within class-specific attention pathways, while a training-only query teacher reads intermediate DINOv2 layers to refine the student's attention. This combines the interpretability of constrained attention with the discriminative power of strong pretrained backbones. It addresses the usual trade-off between accuracy and explainability.

entry.title: GROB: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Public-Trace Investigation of Candidate Agentic Activity

author.name: Chiara Bonfanti, Cataldo Basile

entry.summary: GROB is a multi-agent system for investigating candidate autonomous-agent activity using only public Internet traces when privileged telemetry is unavailable, performing controlled read-only collection and preserving observations for later resolution. On a frozen September 2026 corpus, some traces grew more informative as public evidence emerged, with the strongest result resolving Census-labelled identifiers to specific requests via public revision records. The work addresses attribution and investigation of agent behavior from open evidence.

entry.title: Controlled Acquisition and Abstention in Three-Channel Score Conflicts

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: Studies when a policy should acquire a third modality's score or abstain when audio, video, and text disagree, using a controlled three-score benchmark with mechanism-specific rewards. Finds a threshold policy matches always-request decisions with fewer requests, with its advantage dependent on the reward assigned to ambiguity.

entry.title: DaCe-DT: Data-Centric Offline Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning via Adaptive Prompts and Trajectory Correction for Heterogeneous Tasks

author.name: Xinfei Wang, Shanchen Pang, Chenhao Zhang, Shudong Wang, Wenhao Ji, Haiyuan Gui, Meng Han, Xiaojian Liao

entry.summary: From a data-quality perspective, this paper identifies three bottlenecks in offline multi-task RL: ineffective use of prompt length under varying task complexity, semantically irrelevant random prompt segments, and misleading supervision from fragmented trajectories. DaCe-DT addresses these with adaptive prompts and trajectory correction, aiming for robust offline MTRL on heterogeneous task data.

entry.title: Addressing Overcommitment in the Reasoning of Gendered Economic Memes under Multimodal Ambiguity

author.name: Kushal Kanwar, Dushyant Singh Chauhan, Kapil Rana, Gopendra Vikram Singh, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Studies biased gendered economic-role attribution in multimodal meme understanding, identifying epistemic overcommitment (inferring roles without sufficient contextual evidence) as a key bias source, and proposes CGER-Net to assess contextual sufficiency before attribution. Relevant to fairness and safety of multimodal systems on socially sensitive content. Targets hallucinated stereotypical outputs under ambiguity.

entry.title: In-Ride Alcohol-Impairment Detection in E-Scooterists with False-Alarm Control

author.name: Marco Capuccini, Rahul Rajendra Pai

entry.summary: Proposes an onboard detector for alcohol impairment in e-scooter riders using inertial and throttle signals during the ride, with a provable bound on the false-alarm rate, evaluated on 141 rides including 25 participants riding sober and at two target blood-alcohol levels. Offers a practical safety countermeasure beyond static reaction tests and night bans. Combines sequential detection theory with a real mobility-safety problem.

entry.title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jack Waller, Xing Liang, Dimitrios Makris, Rajagopal Nilavalan

entry.summary: A systematic grid-search evaluation of 1,368 quantum neural network configurations—varying encoding, ansatz, qubit count, depth, and cost function—for financial time series forecasting on GBP/USD spot exchange rate data, measuring accuracy and computational cost. It fills a gap in regression-focused QNN comparisons.

entry.title: On linearity or non-linearity in machine learning for quantum chaotic dynamics

author.name: Francesco Perciavalle, Agostino Gallo, Francesco Plastina, Gianluigi Greco, Nicola Lo Gullo, Carlo Adornetto

entry.summary: The paper formulates quantum many-body dynamics prediction as time-series forecasting on a few-qubit PXP chain (realizable with Rydberg atoms), comparing linear and nonlinear ML models across regimes from ergodic behavior to many-body scarring. It tests whether ML can substitute for costly classical simulation of entanglement-spreading quantum dynamics. A controlled benchmark for ML forecasting of quantum chaotic systems.

entry.title: Implementation Guidelines for Data Quality Metrics

author.name: Philipp Jung, Katinka Becker, Felix Biessmann, Valerie Restat, Martin Seyferth, Daniel Schwabe, Lisa Ehrlinger

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between abstract data quality dimensions like accuracy and completeness in ISO/IEC 25024 and 5259 standards and the low-level checks that tools actually implement. The authors provide concrete implementation guidelines that operationalize these metrics, arguing the standards currently shift rather than solve the specification problem.

entry.title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space

author.name: Shuangteng Lei, Li Yu, Tianxin Li, Wei Lu

entry.summary: The paper maps 2015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families to a shared reciprocal-lattice grid and shows that frozen low-order Fourier channels capture resonance shifts with high R-squared values. A K-space backbone plus a local complex K-space expert models broadband spectra and parameterizes ultranarrow qBIC resonances via diffusion.

entry.title: Efficient quadratic entropy with distance sketches

author.name: Steve Huntsman

entry.summary: This paper details scalable random-feature and projection methods for approximating quadratic entropy for arbitrary distributions under negative-type distances, focusing on Euclidean and spherical geodesic cases. Amortizing a single large matrix multiplication and using control variates enables large-scale, low-memory computation when the distance is fixed and the distribution varies. Demonstrations include scientometric analyses on Open Graph Benchmark datasets.
