entry.summary: Co2Skill unifies whole-body scene interaction and dexterous object manipulation in a single physics-based policy built on a pretrained motion prior, using task- and phase-dependent observation masks. A goal-conditioned loco-manipulation curriculum with partial reference guidance supports long-horizon human-environment interaction tasks.

entry.title: Towards Accurate End-Effector Localization for UMI-Style Robotic Manipulation Teaching

author.name: Junjie Zhang, Deteng Zhang, Zhisong Xu, Bo Sun, Liuyang Li, Yihong Tian, Jie Yin

entry.summary: The paper introduces MILD, a Manipulation-Interface Localization Dataset with 86 real-world sensor sequences across tabletop manipulation tasks plus a simulation subset in Isaac Sim, filling a gap between navigation-focused SLAM benchmarks and policy-oriented manipulation datasets. It benchmarks visual-inertial and fiducial methods for end-effector localization under close-range occlusion.

entry.title: Accelerating Floating-Point Satisfiability Solving via Gradient Normalization

author.name: Yuanzhuo Zhang

entry.summary: GradSAT identifies gradient domination as a bottleneck in optimization-based SMT solving over quantifier-free floating-point theories and reformulates constraint solving as multi-task learning to rebalance gradients across clauses. This connects formal methods with machine learning techniques and could speed software verification and compiler testing. It is a creative cross-domain methodological contribution.

entry.title: BEACON-SP: Ontology-Grounded GraphRAG Framework for Clinical Suicide Risk Assessment

author.name: Kemal Davaslioglu, Nathan Conger, Sastry Kompella, Yalin E. Sagduyu, Nathaniel D. Bastian

entry.summary: BEACON-SP combines patient knowledge graphs with ontology-guided retrieval for clinician-facing suicide risk decision support, enabling multi-hop reasoning over diagnoses, medications, risk factors, life events, and temporal relationships. It unifies established suicide-prevention theories (Three-Step Theory, IMV model, social determinants ontology) into one representation. A thoughtful clinical AI application with a high-stakes use case.

entry.title: Epistemic Uncertainty-Aware Defect Detection for Quality Control in Medical Device Manufacturing

author.name: Raham A. Butt, Marco Romanelli, Roche C. de Guzman

entry.summary: This paper examines whether explicitly modeling epistemic uncertainty improves automated defect detection in medical device manufacturing. The authors combine heterogeneous manufacturing and device-report data via knowledge graphs and add a principled rejection strategy that abstains when uncertainty exceeds a threshold, validated on synthetic benchmarks and real device reports. It matters because quality control in regulated medical contexts demands reliable confidence signals, not just predictions.

entry.title: A Tale of Two Error Categories: Exploring Concealed Trade-Offs in the Errors of Automated Judges in Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantifiers

author.name: Evgenia Ilia, Wilker Aziz

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how errors made by automated judges (LLM-based evaluators) affect the evaluation of uncertainty quantifiers in NLG tasks. It identifies two error categories and explores hidden trade-offs between them, showing that judge errors can systematically distort confidence-correctness correlation metrics used to assess UQ methods. This matters for anyone relying on LLM-judged benchmarks to measure hallucination risk.

entry.title: SkillSandbox: Skill Verification via Dynamic Scenario Synthesis

author.name: Serin Kim, Kwangwook Seo, Dokyung Song, Jinyoung Yeo, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: SkillSandbox verifies whether skills distilled by self-evolving agents remain reusable by dynamically synthesizing novel, skill-relevant tasks and environments. A Proposer specifies which conditions to preserve and which details to vary, enabling observation of the skill's effect in new situations. This targets the problem that bad or non-transferable skills can silently corrupt agent behavior.

entry.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models

author.name: Daniel Robert Kling Alexander, Catherine Louise Kling

entry.summary: Argues that stated-preference economics provides a general framework — content, construct, and criterion validity, reliability, incentive compatibility, consequentiality — for evaluating LLM answers to questions with no ground truth. Demonstrated by administering a published water-quality valuation survey to LLMs.

entry.title: STRIDE: Spatial-Temporal Representation for Interval-conditioned Disease Evolution in Longitudinal Glioblastoma MRI

author.name: Wenhao Guo, Changchang Yin, Pierre Giglio, Weidan Cao, Ping Zhang, Golrokh Mirzaei

entry.summary: STRIDE is a spatial-temporal framework that takes paired post-treatment MRI scans plus the inter-scan interval to distinguish stable disease, pseudoprogression, and true progression in glioblastoma patients. It addresses the clinically important problem that these states look similar on single scans but evolve differently over time. The interval-conditioned design makes it more practical for real follow-up schedules with variable gaps between scans.

entry.title: On KL-Regularized Policy Optimization

author.name: Yifan Zhang

entry.summary: KLPO tackles asynchronous RL for LLM agents, where rollouts come from stale checkpoints and inference/trainer probability mismatches introduce bias. Instead of clipping importance ratios or costly GRPO-style group sampling, it anchors the KL regularizer at the sampler, yielding a closed-form Gibbs solution fit by least squares on the sampler's own trajectories. This offers a cheaper, less biased alternative for off-policy correction in LLM RL.

entry.title: MimicX: Policy-in-the-Loop Supervision Refinement for Video-Driven Humanoid Motion Tracking

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Chenglong Zhang, Xuhao Liu, Feiyang You, Yifan Liao, Shuyang Hao, Chaozhe Zhang, Chengyu Wu, Zhen Sun, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: MimicX is a framework that uses physics-based execution feedback to refine supervision for humanoid robots learning motion from human videos. It localizes difficult transitions and body regions, adapts tracking objectives and reset curricula, and uses repeated rollout verification, improving tracking accuracy and robustness across four core video tasks.

entry.title: Conditional Accuracy Profiles: Diagnosing LLM Judges across Deployment Conditions

author.name: Wenqi Li, Bin Liu, Mindi Ruan, Chuanbo Hu, Minglei Yin, Xin Li

entry.summary: CAP is a post-hoc diagnostic framework that decomposes pairwise LLM-as-judge accuracy into eight conditions spanning content sensitivity, robustness, and rationale quality, replacing single-number summaries. It is benchmark-agnostic and is instantiated on seven LLM judges across six pairwise judging tasks.

entry.title: Kuration SDK: Addressing the Virtual2Real Gap via Data Curation

author.name: Nirmit Desai, Eric Song, Mayank Sengupta, Tejal Bedmutha, Siri Reddy, Sahiti Dharmavaram, Kunal Sawarkar

entry.summary: This paper trains and evaluates diffusion world models on CounterStrike gameplay data and shows that qualitative playability does not correlate with common video metrics like FVD, LPIPS, and JEDi, a phenomenon the authors call the Virtual2Real gap. They propose that instead of relying on immature benchmarks, systematic curation of raw gameplay data with diagnostic property measurements offers a more robust signal before training begins.

entry.title: KASALv2: Fully Automatic 3D Rotational Symmetry Classification and Axis Localization

author.name: Mengxin Zhang, Yulin Wang, Chen Luo, Yongzhe Li, Yijun Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces a fully automatic, reference-free framework for classifying all eight canonical 3D rotational symmetry types, identifying rotational order, and localizing symmetry axes in 3D objects. This replaces manual or semi-automatic symmetry annotation, which is an important prior for 6D pose estimation and symmetry-aware evaluation.

entry.title: DisParQ: Self-Supervised Part Concepts for Interpretable Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Adam Pardyl, Siddhartha Gairola, Sukrut Rao, Adam Wr\'obel, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Bernt Schiele, Dawid Rymarczyk

entry.summary: DisParQ learns spatially grounded, discrete part-concept representations from a frozen vision-only self-supervised backbone without class labels or language supervision, assigning each patch to one concept from a learnable prototype dictionary with sparse activation. It extends concept-based interpretable vision models beyond fixed categories and language-defined concepts.

entry.title: Training Advisors for LLM Agents from Task Outcomes

author.name: Sergei Polezhaev, Barys Liskavets, Ori Press, Alexander Golubev

entry.summary: Caddie trains critic models to give natural-language analysis and advice to LLM agents during multi-step tasks, learning only from whether the agent ultimately succeeds after receiving feedback rather than from step-level labels or reference critiques. The critic is optimized via reinforcement learning with a frozen base model; a Qwen3-4B critic improves task success rates on multi-hop QA. This simplifies critic training by using sparse outcome signals alone.

entry.title: EEG and Eye-Tracking Evidence That AI Disclosure Shapes Face Evaluation

author.name: Teodora Mitrevska, Luise Donat, Andreas Butz, Thomas Kosch, Abdallah El Ali, Francesco Chiossi

entry.summary: Using EEG event-related potentials and eye tracking, this study (N=30 lab study after N=169 validation) disentangles what a face actually is from what viewers are told, showing neural responses differ by AI/human label rather than by true image source. Conflicting labels triggered re-evaluation signals (P3), demonstrating that disclosure labels drive judgments of AI-generated faces. This is valuable evidence for policy debates around AI-content labeling.

entry.title: LoomSC: Scalable Deep Subspace Clustering with Projector Factorization and Exact Spectral Reduction

author.name: Nairouz Mrabah, Youssef Melki, Mohamed Bouguessa, Riadh Ksantini, Shakeeb Murtaza, Tehseen Zia

entry.summary: LoomSC is a deep subspace clustering framework that tackles the two main scalability bottlenecks: dense self-expression matrices and full-affinity spectral clustering. It uses projector factorization into thin factors with alternating Procrustes and least-squares updates, plus an exact spectral reduction via a feature map, to scale clustering to larger datasets while preserving theoretical structure.

entry.title: FoldBack: Self-Correcting Masked Generative Policy for Long-Horizon Garment Folding

author.name: Lipeng Zhuang, Shiyu Fan, Yingdong Ru, Zhuo He, Florent P. Audonnet, Paul Henderson, Gerardo Aragon Camarasa

entry.summary: FoldBack is a robot manipulation policy for long-horizon garment folding that adds structured self-correction: deciding when to verify and refine, how to roll back to a retryable pre-grasp state while preserving successful grasps, and where to retry while avoiding previously failed grasp locations. The system uses a masked generative policy and claims to be the first editable full-trajectory recovery framework of its kind. This addresses a key weakness in long-horizon manipulation where policies continue after failed grasps.

entry.title: Directed Temporal Representations for Offline Visual Control

author.name: Chenyang Yuan, Haoyu Wang, Zhuo Sun, Xiaoyuan Cheng

entry.summary: DTRC learns latent geometries for visual control that align with temporal reachability rather than mere predictive similarity, building a directed temporal quasimetric over frozen world-model features from offline trajectories. It combines short-range calibration, bootstrapped long-horizon targets, and action-conditioned consistency.

entry.title: A Geometry-Based Capacity Theory for Finite-Feature Associative Memory

author.name: Jianhai Zhang, Donghao Zhang, Pattarawut Charatpangoon, Bijoy Menon, M. Ethan MacDonald, Wu Qiu, Aravind Ganesh

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical capacity analysis for exact-key retrieval in compressed finite-feature Hebbian associative memories, separating retrieval interference into finite-feature noise and persistent structural interference from key geometry. It provides fit-free predictions of retrieval quality, geometry-dependent capacity ceilings, and required feature budgets, including correlated-value extensions.

entry.title: Symmetry-Informed Causal Partial Identification

author.name: Uzair Akbar, Zulfiqar Zaidi, Niki Kilbertus, Krikamol Muandet, Bo Dai

entry.summary: The paper introduces known data symmetries, invariance of causal effects under certain transformations, as a new source of constraints for partial identification of causal effects. It operationalizes symmetries as shape constraints on the causal function or via change of measure, producing sharper non-vacuous bounds.

entry.title: Stability and Diversity of Networked Self-Consuming Generative Ecosystems

author.name: Xiukun Wei, Yang Zhang, Xueru Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides the first theoretical framework for networked self-consuming generative models, where multiple models train on each other's synthetic outputs through complex interaction pathways. It analyzes stability and diversity outcomes of such ecosystems, generalizing beyond isolated or two-model cases.

entry.title: When Rank Rises as LLMs Degrade

author.name: Zhaohui Geoffrey Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that RankMe and related spectral rank statistics are unsafe health monitors for LLM post-training: in controlled Qwen3-0.6B experiments, data duplication worsens held-out loss by 75% while increasing rank statistics by 13.5 pooled standard deviations. This spectral dispersion failure means one-sided monitors rate the worst checkpoints as healthiest, motivating learning-dynamics-based alternatives.

entry.title: Leaner Transformers Can Easily Learn to Cluster

author.name: Charlotte Park, Kenneth L. Clarkson, Lior Horesh, Takuya Ito, Parikshit Ram

entry.summary: The paper constructs a smaller transformer that exactly executes Lloyd's k-means algorithm with embedding size d + ceil(log2 k), improving on prior work requiring d + k, and trains transformers to learn clustering algorithms from task distributions with theoretical guarantees. Authors include IBM researchers and Kenneth Clarkson.

entry.title: OrthoGen: A Generative Orthogonal Learner for Time-Varying Treatments

author.name: Tom\`as Garriga, Valentyn Melnychuk, Konstantin Hess, Eduard Serrahima de Cambra, Axel Brando, Gerard Sanz, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: OrthoGen estimates conditional distributional potential outcomes under time-varying treatments using generative recursive g-computation, which propagates full conditional outcome distributions rather than means to handle time-varying confounding. The method targets medical applications like patient-specific risk under treatment sequences and includes authors from Feuerriegel's group.

entry.title: Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tommaso Marzi, Ahmed Hendawy, Jan Peters, Carlo D'Eramo, Andrea Cini, Cesare Alippi

entry.summary: This paper proposes CGMARL, a continual multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that exploits task structure (e.g., graph topologies) to promote forward transfer and reduce forgetting across task sequences. It addresses a gap in existing CMARL methods that ignore structural information such as network topologies in power grids or formation arrangements.

entry.title: Boosting and the Expressive Power of Simple Weak Learners via the $\gamma$-VC Dimension

author.name: Arthur da Cunha, Kasper Green Larsen, Liang-Yu Zou

entry.summary: This theory paper shows the gamma-VC dimension characterizes sample complexity for weak-to-strong learning up to constant factors, sharpens the relationship between VC and gamma-VC dimensions, and derives improved bounds for decision stumps and axis-parallel rectangles. It grounds boosting expressivity in the Alon et al. (STOC 2021) parameter.

entry.title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs

author.name: Zhewei Chen, Hao Zhu, Jiaojiao Jiang, Ahad N. Zehmakan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes GNN-to-MLP knowledge distillation, identifying two spectral failure modes: spectral underfit on sparse graphs and spectral overfit on dense graphs when the student fails to preserve the teacher's graph-induced geometry. It proposes an energy-weighted alignment approach to address the gap between message-passing teachers and graph-free MLP students.

entry.title: TERRA: Learning Transportable Latent Actions through Temporal Effect Representation and Relational Alignment

author.name: Tianxingjian Ding, Mubarak Shah, Yu Tian

entry.summary: TERRA improves latent action learning for robot policies by describing transitions with compact temporal effects -- net feature change plus low-order within-transition structure -- and aligning latent codes relationally across states so they retain meaning when reused in different initial states. This addresses both temporal information loss and state-dependent ambiguity in latent action supervision. The goal is more transferable unsupervised robot skill representations.

entry.title: A Multi-Source Ultrasound Benchmark Revealing the Limits of Contemporary Self-Supervised Anomaly Detection Methods

author.name: Marco Riedenauer, Daniel Kienzle, Pratik Mayekar, Rainer Lienhart

entry.summary: SADUSI is a multi-source ultrasound benchmark for training and evaluating self-supervised anomaly detection across diverse anatomies, views, and acquisition protocols. The paper shows that contemporary anomaly detection methods fail to learn a robust general notion of normal ultrasound appearance and instead rely on source-specific representations. This exposes an important generalization gap in medical anomaly detection.

entry.title: Transition Path Sampling Using Koopman Operators and Exit-Time Optimal Control

author.name: Boya Hou, Shane Wang, Siddharth Ambekar, Maxim Raginsky, Olgica Milenkovic

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Koopman-operator-based approach to transition path sampling between metastable states, a rare-event problem central to molecular dynamics. It recasts existing optimal-stochastic-control formulations to exploit linearity of Koopman operators, avoiding the repeated biased rollouts required by neural-network drift biasing methods.

entry.title: Pathwise Information Certificates for Decentralized Adaptive Sensing

author.name: Theodoros Tsiligkaridis

entry.summary: This paper studies decentralized adaptive sensing where multiple agents select measurements based on evolving local beliefs communicated over a graph. It introduces a pathwise certificate built on Renyi-Chernoff information accumulated along realized sensing trajectories, providing nonasymptotic MAP-error bounds and an anytime network-wide stopping rule. This separates genuine statistical evidence from network-mixing transients for arbitrary history-dependent sensing policies.

entry.title: EASE: Entropy-Adaptive Distribution Shaping for Evading AI-generated Text Detectors

author.name: Jicheng Zhou, Kahim Wong, Jialong Wang, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: EASE is a training-free, detector-agnostic framework for evading AI-generated text detectors by adaptively perturbing logits and sampling temperature based on predictive entropy from the source LLM. Experiments across multiple source LLMs and detectors demonstrate that decoding-time changes alone can substantially degrade detection.

entry.title: Shape-Bayes: Bayesian Inference of Structured Shapes under Visual Ambiguity

author.name: Mani Kumar Tellamekala, Tosh Brown, Michel Valstar

entry.summary: Shape-Bayes introduces a probabilistic framework for structured shape inference, such as faces, that couples uncertainty-aware visual perception with Bayesian shape reasoning instead of deterministic regression. It dynamically weights visual evidence against geometric priors, avoiding the structural collapse deterministic models exhibit under severe occlusion.

entry.title: TopoCurve: Geometry-Aware Topology Reasoning via B\'ezier Curves in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mihai Bogdan Deaconu, Laura Dio\c{s}an

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes TopoCurve, an architecture for 3D topology reasoning in autonomous driving that jointly detects lanes and traffic elements from multi-view images. Instead of representing lanes as discrete polylines, it models them as endpoint-fixed cubic Bezier curves, enabling continuous geometry, exact endpoints, and analytically defined tangent directions that are exploited throughout the pipeline via multi-scale Fourier feature encodings of endpoint distance and tangent alignment. This addresses common weaknesses in lane-topology perception such as lack of smoothness and sparse topology supervision.

entry.title: PVSync: A Unified Lip-Sync Expert for Timing and Articulation

author.name: Kevin Stephen, Varun Menon, Timo Mertens, Nikita Drobyshev

entry.summary: PVSync unifies audio-visual offset estimation and phoneme-level articulation scoring via window-level contrastive learning plus a viseme-aligned articulation objective with automatically derived labels. On offset-corrected videos from 13 talking-head generation models, it correlates with human lip-sync quality judgments far better than LSE-C (Spearman 0.83 versus 0.34).

entry.title: TileSkipper: Region-Adaptive Tile Pruning for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jingxing Li, Yongjae Lee, Deliang Fan, Abhay Kumar Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa

entry.summary: Introduces TileSkipper, which selects per-Gaussian contribution cutoffs for tiled 3D Gaussian Splatting rasterization using calibration renders and an isolated-removal distortion proxy. The exported static policy costs one byte per Gaussian, requires no per-frame inference, and speeds rendering across Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending scenes.

entry.title: Latent Watermarks under Generative Editing: A Benchmark and Analysis of Detection Survival

author.name: Sung Ju Lee, Nam Ik Cho

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates eight latent watermarking methods against five generative editors across multiple backbones, editing strengths, and semantic categories, measuring watermark detection survival under ordinary prompt-based editing. Findings include that editing alone primarily distinguishes Tree-Ring, and that score separation can decline while detection rates remain near ceiling, revealing hidden fragility.

entry.title: Efficient 3D Gaussian Head Avatars for Edge Devices

author.name: Umar Farooq, Jean-Yves Guillemaut, Adrian Hilton, Marco Volino

entry.summary: The authors introduce a parameter-efficient generator architecture for 3D Gaussian head avatar synthesis targeting edge devices, using depth-wise separable convolutions and a lightweight synthesis block. It reduces FLOPs by 94%, parameters by 70%, and model size by 81% versus the baseline while maintaining quality, and demonstrates practical CPU inference without compression or quantization.

entry.title: Real-Time Joint Audio-Video Generation by Parallel Adapter Composition

author.name: Jingyu Li, Xiaoxiao Xiang, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: The paper shows that block-autoregressive streaming and few-step sampling for joint audio-video diffusion transformers can be acquired in parallel via model-merging-style adapter composition, avoiding chained distillation pipelines where later objectives can undo earlier capabilities. This enables real-time, interactive audio-video generation on a packed backbone. The approach simplifies the training recipe for streaming multimodal generators.

entry.title: CIRRA: Dual-Level Continual Instruction Reconciliation with Ongoing Execution for Embodied Robot Agents in Interactive Household Tasks

author.name: Ci Zhang, Enfu Nan, Arman Akbari, Lin Zhao, Li Wang, Chen Wang, Weiwei Chen, Yanzhi Wang, Geng Yuan

entry.summary: CIRRA is a dual-level framework that lets household robots absorb new user instructions mid-task without regenerating the whole plan, combining LLM-based semantic grounding with rule-constrained structural integration of subtasks. It matters because interactive, interruptible task execution is a key gap between static plan-following agents and real home deployment.

entry.title: A Unified Kinematic Representation Enables Reusable Biological Joint Moment Estimation

author.name: Jinwoo Hwang, Ilseung Park, Changseob Song, Vu Phan, Eni Halilaj, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: This paper proposes using joint kinematics (angles and angular velocities) as an intermediate representation to decouple hardware-specific sensing from biological joint moment estimation for exoskeleton control. The estimator is trained only on open-source biomechanics data and validated across hip and knee exoskeletons and an IMU suite on multiple terrains.

entry.title: End-to-End Autonomous Generation of Human Assembly Plans

author.name: Faustin Arion von Arx, Millicent Schlafly, Mark D. Fuge

entry.summary: The authors encode design-for-assembly principles into an end-to-end system that takes only a mesh assembly and autonomously produces assembly sequences, tool lists, step-by-step manuals, or structured failure reports, without joint metadata or fastener annotations. It addresses geometric feasibility, tool access, stability, and human ergonomics.

entry.title: LLA-MPPI: Rapidly Adaptive Whole-body Control of Legged Robots with GPU-Accelerated Parallel Simulations

author.name: Sebin Jung, Maitham F. AL-Sunni, Juan Alvarez-Padilla, Zachary Manchester, Changliu Liu, John M. Dolan

entry.summary: LLA-MPPI adapts whole-body control of legged robots by selecting among a bank of GPU-batched contact simulators with different physical parameters, using windowed prediction errors to pick the model best matching recent motion, then running MPPI planning through that model. It requires no offline training and handles deployed dynamics changes that break fixed-nominal-model controllers.

entry.title: Benchmarking Jev against no-CoT LLMs

author.name: Dewi Gould

entry.summary: An empirical evaluation of Jev 1.13, TypeSafe's non-autoregressive probabilistic model that cannot emit text, on the ThinkFast no-CoT suite and the NCRI benchmark. Results show highly jagged capabilities: chain-of-thought-free monitoring performance on sabotage and sandbagging detection matches GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 at roughly 1/200th of Opus 4.7's cost, while multi-step reasoning is weak (rank 209/279 on NCRI, near GPT-3.5 level). The authors argue this makes Jev attractive for cheap always-on agent monitoring and routing despite its opaque, trace-free decisions.

entry.title: ToolRACER: A Robust Agentic Conversation Emulation Resource for Agent Training and Evaluation

author.name: Arkajyoti Chakraborty, Aryan Tayal, Ishika Agarwal, Tanner Sorensen, Justin Chiu, Alessandro Di Bari, Neha Gupta, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: ToolRACER is a synthetic data generation pipeline coordinating user, assistant, and tool emulation models to produce validated multi-turn interactions, including adversarial and non-cooperative user trajectories underrepresented in existing function-calling benchmarks. The resulting benchmark spans six domains and around 55 persona variations to train and evaluate robust task-oriented agents.

entry.title: Arctic Questions, Missing Answers: A Dataset and Benchmark for LLM Abstention in Arctic Science

author.name: Benjamin Wilcox, Dawei Gao, Pradeeban Kathiravelu, Douglas Causey, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: ArcticQA provides 194 questions from primary Arctic research with automated checks for answer support and distractor contradiction, plus ArcticAbstain, a paired benchmark contrasting answer-present and answer-absent conditions with an explicit abstention option. The authors evaluate eight models from the Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT families at high reasoning effort across 9,312 recorded responses.

entry.title: Beyond Policy Support: Interaction Constrained Offline Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mahmoud Selim, Cristina Cipriani, Karl Henrik Johansson

entry.summary: Argues that existing offline RL distribution-shift controls in the ego policy's action space are insufficient for interactive settings like driving, proposing interaction constraints that require candidate trajectories to be jointly supported with surrounding-agent behavior in logged data. This addresses cases where a trajectory is marginally well supported but jointly poorly supported.

entry.title: ExperienceIndex: Artifact-Grounded Memory

author.name: Peter Baile Chen, Geoffrey X. Yu, Xinming Liu, Samuel Madden, Dan Roth, Jacob Andreas, Doug Downey, Michael Cafarella

entry.summary: ExperienceIndex proposes a memory architecture for AI agents that accumulates persistent, artifact-grounded experiential knowledge about a shared corpus (e.g., court cases, scientific literature), unlike existing memory systems focused on user preferences or abstract reasoning patterns from task traces. This enables agents to quickly identify the complete set of relevant artifacts for new tasks, improving answer quality and reducing online cost. It targets knowledge-intensive multi-question workflows.

entry.title: When Scientific Cognition Is No Longer Scarce

author.name: Nathan DeBardeleben

entry.summary: A conceptual paper exploring how AI abundance in computational scientific work (literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, simulation) would shift the bottlenecks of science toward experiments, validation, and institutional accountability - a scarcity inversion. It analyzes four components: selection, physical access, validation, and organizational choice. This kind of foresight analysis informs AI-for-science strategy and governance.

entry.title: RoboQuest: Generalist Physical Agents that Search, Inspect and Test

author.name: Liu Renhang, Navonil Majumder, Tej Deep Pala, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: RoboQuest is a benchmark for goal-directed embodied exploration in which multimodal agents must actively acquire task-relevant information through physical interaction, adapt actions based on evidence, and decide autonomously when to commit to task completion. It comprises ten manipulation-focused scenarios where needed information is absent from observations and must be sought via search, inspection, or tool testing.

entry.title: The Symbol of the Surrogate: Measuring Numerical Provenance in Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Ridham Patel

entry.summary: The paper introduces a Fourier-symbol diagnostic that probes a neural PDE surrogate's linearized one-step operator against exact-evolution and training-scheme references, distinguishing fidelity to true physics from imitation of solver discretization errors. It controls for spectral bias by training identical networks on schemes with orthogonal error signatures.

entry.title: Self-Consuming Generative Models with Co-Evolving Human Preferences

author.name: Xiukun Wei, Tian Xie, Ding Zhu, Xueru Zhang

entry.summary: The authors model coupled dynamics where generative models train on user-curated synthetic data while exposure to model outputs reshapes user preferences over time. They show that when training relies entirely on curated data, iterative curation amplifies initial biases and drives the system toward singleton equilibria dominated by initial preferences.

entry.title: Sparse Planning in Visual World Models via Cost Gradients

author.name: Yingchen Xu, Edward Grefenstette

entry.summary: COSTGRAD is a training-free token selector for world model planning that ranks spatial tokens by the gradient norm of the planning cost, targeting tokens that matter for control rather than prediction. It matches or exceeds full-token planning at 50% sparsity on three of four continuous-control benchmarks with a measured 2.6x wall-clock speedup per planning step.

entry.title: Koopman Observers for Diffusion Acceleration: Correcting Feature Forecasts with Shallow Measurements

author.name: Hanru Bai, Yuanchao Xu, Fengyi Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces an observation-corrected Koopman framework that accelerates frozen diffusion models by predicting deep-feature evolution from cheap shallow features, correcting feature-cache forecasts with freshly computed measurements. This addresses a key limitation of feature caching, which cannot incorporate the current denoising state.

entry.title: Towards AI-Generated Music Plagiarism Detection as a Version Identification Problem

author.name: Fotis Koutsikos, Ioannis Prokopiou, Spyridon Kantarelis, Vassilis Lyberatos, Pantelis Vikatos, Athanasios Aidinis, Themos Stafylakis, Athanasios Voulodimos, Giorgos Stamou

entry.summary: The paper tests whether state-of-the-art music version identification architectures transfer from human cover songs to human-vs-AI plagiarism detection, introducing COPYCAT, a benchmark of 350,654 evaluation pairs built from real plagiarism cases with generative re-synthesis and DSP obfuscations. It addresses IP challenges posed by text-to-music generative models.

entry.title: Ask the Expert: LLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Cyber Defense

author.name: Fernando Martinez, Abhishek Satyam, Tao Li, Junaid Farooq, Ying Wang, Juntao Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-time framework where an LLM intermittently summarizes hard cyber-defense states and recommends host-level defensive actions through a constrained action interface, converting recommendations into tiered reward shaping for PPO training. By restricting LLM use to training rather than deployment, it avoids latency and trust issues of in-line LLM guidance. This improves sample efficiency of RL for autonomous cyber defense.

entry.title: Structure alone supports efficient visual computation in the Drosophila visual system

author.name: Eudald Correig-Fraga, Roger Guimer\`a, Marta Sales-Pardo

entry.summary: Using the proofread adult Drosophila connectome coupled to an anatomically faithful eye model, the paper builds a connectome-only visual system where only synaptic gains and thresholds are learned. The model supports multitask vision including color discrimination, shape classification, and ratio-dependent numerical discrimination resembling approximate number perception. This shows biological wiring structure alone can scaffold efficient visual computation, informing both neuroscience and neuromorphic AI.

entry.title: Steerspeech: Activation Steering For Emotion Control In Generated Speech

author.name: Afsara Benazir, Darius P\'etermann, Felix Xiaozhu Lin, Salar Rahili

entry.summary: SteerSpeech is a lightweight activation-steering framework for controlling emotion in pretrained text-to-speech models by injecting low-rank steering vectors into hidden activations, keeping the backbone frozen. A multi-expert objective encourages monotonic emotion control while preserving speaker identity and linguistic content. A two-stage procedure optimizes through discrete speech tokens without costly model adaptation.

entry.title: HySPE: Positional Encoding via Symplectic Dual Shears

author.name: Zhongping Ji

entry.summary: HySPE introduces a hyperbolic symplectic positional encoding that extends RoPE's rotational parameterization to the hyperbolic branch of the symplectic group via dual shears with two spectral decay rates per channel pair. Diagonalization and blockwise coordinate rebasing eliminate exponential representation drift while maintaining compatibility with cached RoPE-style inference.

entry.title: DISRQAD: Diffusion Image Super-Resolution Quality Assessment Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Nikita Kukuzei, Artem Borisov, Evgeney Bogatyrev, Khaled Abud, Egor Chistov, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: DISRQAD provides mean opinion scores for 14,000 super-resolution outputs from ten diffusion and four non-diffusion methods under varied degradations, revealing that standard quality metrics agree far worse with human judgment on diffusion SR (0.431 versus 0.813 SRCC). The benchmark includes evaluations of 62 metric configurations and a case study with a pruned quality model.

entry.title: Event-Aligned Visual Action Reasoning for World Action Models

author.name: Xiaomeng Yang, Yushu Wu, Yi Gao, Yuhao Lei, Xuan Zhang, Pu Zhao, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Argues that World-Action Models should structure visual imagination around interaction events rather than fixed temporal intervals, and introduces an event-aligned supervision framework so imagined rollouts align with task-critical interactions. This aims to make visual foresight more useful for action generation.

entry.title: RT-DETR-World: Transferring Rich LLM Semantics to Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Detection

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Ziyi Zhao, Juntao Cheng, Sheng Wang, Ningnan Guo, Ruize Han, Liang Wan

entry.summary: RT-DETR-World is a compact DETR-style detector for real-time open-vocabulary detection that transfers rich semantic cues such as attributes, actions, states, and contextual relations from language model descriptions during training. The goal is strong zero-shot generalization on unseen categories while maintaining real-time efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond Masks and Trajectories: Flow-Guided Latent Action Injection for Stable Surgical Video Generation

author.name: Tsz-Yui Qin, Siyu Zhou, Chi-Keung Tang, Yuxiang Nie, Shu Yang

entry.summary: FLAIR is a reference-free architecture for surgical video generation that uses flow-guided latent action injection to produce clinically plausible motion without auxiliary conditions such as masks, trajectories, or depth at inference time. This removes the annotation burden that limits scaling of prior surgical video synthesis methods, with applications in education, simulation, and data augmentation.

entry.title: AdSpark: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Product-Centric Advertisement Video Generation

author.name: Zhifei Yang, Zhao Jiang, Keyang Lu, Honghe Zhu, Zheng Zhang, Jingjing Lv, Changping Peng, Ching Law, Zhen Xiao

entry.summary: AdSpark provides a large-scale dataset and benchmark for product-centric advertisement video generation, with roughly 300K reference image-prompt-video triplets from a major e-commerce platform, split into real and synthetic subsets with structured advertisement annotations. The task requires preserving fine-grained product identity while presenting selling points through coherent multi-shot narratives. It enables research in an underexplored applied generative video area.

entry.title: SGF+: Decoupling Gradient Flows for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Zihan Su, Junhao Zhuang, Yaowei Li, Siwen Lu, Haoran Li, Lingen Li, Haoyu Wu, Weiyang Jin, Songchun Zhang, Haoyang Huang, Chun Yuan, Zeyue Xue, Nan Duan

entry.summary: SGF+ addresses a conflict in autoregressive video generation where denoising current frames and writing key-value context for future predictions share parameters despite exhibiting distinct, systematically negatively aligned gradients. The method assigns separate parameters to context writing and denoising while preserving their interaction through causal attention, jointly optimizing both with the original generation objective. This improves visual quality and temporal consistency without auxiliary losses.

entry.title: FaceKit: a Toolkit for Interpretable Facial Phenotyping, Synthetic Image Generation and Privacy Analysis in Rare Diseases

author.name: Hongzhuo Chen, Zhanliang Wang, Florent Pollet, Mian Umair Ahsan, Joshua Bie, Tzung-Chien Hsieh, Peter Krawitz, Cong Liu, Wendy K Chung, Chunhua Weng, Gamze G\"ursoy, Kai Wang

entry.summary: FaceKit is an open computational framework for quantitative facial phenotyping from frontal photographs, aimed at rare genetic disease analysis, with tools for standardized landmark measurements, synthetic image generation, and privacy analysis. It replaces subjective free-text clinical descriptions with reproducible quantitative features relevant to diagnosis and research.

entry.title: Borrowed Eyes: Markerless Nano-UAV Flight with an Active Quadruped Observer

author.name: Alejandro Lorite Mora, Dimitrios Arapis, Andr\'es Fa\'i\~na

entry.summary: This system localizes a payload-limited nano-UAV in GNSS-denied environments using an arm-mounted camera on a quadruped robot, which tracks the drone via segmentation and depth and transmits its position over a radio link. A perception-aware nonlinear MPC actively repositions the quadruped's body and arm to maintain visibility.

entry.title: Socio-Foundation: A Model for Generalizable Individual Behavior Simulation via Hierarchical Capability Distillation

author.name: Liang Wang, Wenxuan Xie, Xinyi Mou, Yixin Luo, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Socio-Foundation organizes LLM-based individual behavior simulation into a FONTS taxonomy of five capabilities (persona fidelity, outcome realization, naturalness, trajectory coherence, social grounding) and trains on a curated corpus of roughly ten million instances via hierarchical capability distillation. The goal is preserving persona traits while adapting to dynamic social contexts without task-specific fragmentation. Relevant to social simulation and digital twins of human behavior.

entry.title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use

author.name: Gennadiy Savrasov, Maksim Elistratov, Nikita Gavrilov, Albert Garifullin, Oleg Pavlov, Soslan Kabisov, Vladimir Frolov, Anton Konushin, Andrey Kuznetsov, Dmitrii Zhemchuzhnikov

entry.summary: CADFather is an agentic system that reconstructs editable parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes by coordinating complementary tools. A vision-language assistant inspects renders, decides which candidate programs to extend, which proposal tools to invoke, and when to stop, while numerical optimization refines parameters. It addresses a real engineering gap since no single proposal source works across all geometries.

entry.title: Ream: Unfolding Mutual Awareness in Human-Agent Workspaces

author.name: Peiling Jiang, Sangho Suh, Varsha Kishore, Jonathan Bragg, Haijun Xia, Pao Siangliulue, Daniel S. Weld, Amy X. Zhang, Joseph Chee Chang

entry.summary: Ream is a literature-review workspace supporting mutual awareness between humans and AI agents through structured artifacts, bidirectional engagement tracking, and localized visualizations, so users can inspect agent activity and agents can retrieve user histories. Studies with eighteen researchers show the traces help users steer agents and calibrate trust.

entry.title: Learning to Accumulate Knowledge with Mutual Information

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Lizi Liao, Leyang Shen, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Knowledge Weaver is an RL framework that trains a model to curate reusable knowledge from agent trajectories into a growing knowledge bank, using mutual-information-inspired feedback to penalize redundant entries. Standard GRPO on task success alone would reinforce generic guidance that duplicates existing knowledge. This targets the open problem of making agent memory increasingly useful as it grows.

entry.title: AI Safety Considerations for Agents With Limited Time to Act

author.name: Leo Zeitler, Jack Richings, Victoria Nockles

entry.summary: The authors prove theoretical impossibility results for agent-agnostic safety guarantees in partially observable environments requiring timely action, via two realistic scenarios (infinite state space and signal mixture). They show that even a perfect agent cannot guarantee safe behavior, arguing that any AI safety or alignment proof must reference the environment and its safety assumptions. This is a caution against architecture-only alignment claims.

entry.title: Autonomous Driving Research Requires a Community-Driven Data Paradigm

author.name: Jinsu Yoo, Zanming Huang, Katie Z Luo, Zheda Mai, Qiyuan Wu, Bharath Hariharan, Mark Campbell, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the gap between current autonomous driving systems and universal robustness stems from the data paradigm, not just modeling: research relies on a few narrow benchmarks while over 600 datasets from nearly 50 countries remain underused due to fragmentation. The authors propose a community-driven data paradigm to unlock this collective resource.

entry.title: Work While They Sleep: Exploiting Evaluation Latency for Fully Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Gustavo Sutter, Alejandro Comas-Leon, David Holzm\"uller, Hao Wang, Luis Ricardez-Sandoval, Pascal Poupart, Agustinus Kristiadi

entry.summary: This work improves Bayesian optimization for expensive black-box objectives by using the latency of objective evaluations to perform fully Bayesian hyperparameter marginalization via model averaging, rather than fitting point-estimate surrogate hyperparameters. This yields better uncertainty estimates in the low-data regimes typical of costly experiments in science and engineering. The approach turns unavoidable idle time into better inference.

entry.title: Patient, Place, Prior (P$^3$): What Counts as Personalization in Medical World Models?

author.name: Xingrui Gu, Hanxue Gu, Yuxiang Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: P3 is an audit framework asking whether a longitudinal medical forecast genuinely benefits from a specific patient's imaging history, spatial support, and context, versus merely matching population averages. The authors also propose Cancer JEPA, a one-step model forecasting representations of future breast DCE-MRI exams during neoadjuvant treatment.

entry.title: MORA: Modeling Observed Changes for Drift-Robust Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xudong Mou, Tiejun Wang, Rui Wang, Hui Wang, Pin Liu, Tianyu Wo, Xudong Liu, Renyu Yang

entry.summary: MORA is a drift-robust time-series anomaly detection framework that formalizes temporal change disambiguation: deciding whether a local deviation reflects abnormality or evolving context. It reconstructs the same local target from paired short- and long-term views, using the reconstruction gap to measure contextual support and resolve the ambiguity that plagues non-stationary settings.

entry.title: Activation-Aware Weight Tensorization: A Calibration-Time Preconditioner for Tensor-Network LLM Compression

author.name: Alessandro Beatini, Marco Maronese, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: AWT is a training-free compression preconditioner that scales each weight matrix by a diagonal activation-derived calibration before tensor-network (TT/TTN) decomposition, correcting the mismatch between weight-space Frobenius error and functional error. Across Llama 3.1 8B, Ministral 8B, and Qwen2.5 7B at 2-6x compression, AWT closes 12-35% of the WikiText perplexity gap of vanilla tensorization under single-operator replacement. It is a practical efficiency technique for deploying compressed LLMs.

entry.title: From Prompts to Trees: Effective LLM-Guided Tree Generation for Few-Shot Tabular Classification

author.name: Yue Qiu, Zekang Du, Yiqun Diao, Bingsheng He, Qinbin Li

entry.summary: The authors propose distilling LLM world knowledge into interpretable decision trees for few-shot tabular classification via a three-stage paradigm: prompt the LLM to generate rules, then organize rules into a tree, avoiding unstable full-tree generation. This combines the interpretability and efficiency of trees with LLM generalization. Results across real-world tabular datasets support the approach.

entry.title: Exact Dynamics and Finite-Sample Trajectory Recovery of Linear Recursive Feature Machines

author.name: Andrew Cheng, Bobak T. Kiani, Yue M. Lu, Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan

entry.summary: The paper gives exact dynamics and finite-sample statistics for linear recursive feature machines in noisy multi-output regression, extending the connection between RFMs and iteratively reweighted least squares to ridge-regularized noisy settings with low-rank teacher targets. This clarifies how representations evolve during feature learning in an analytically tractable model.

entry.title: When Should an In-Context Learner Expand Its Hypothesis Space?

author.name: Weihan Li, Xinlei Chen, Junhao Wu, Tianshi Zheng

entry.summary: This work frames hypothesis-space expansion in in-context learning as a costly sequential decision problem, distinguishing failures due to noise, exceptions, in-family change, or out-of-family structure. It introduces a Structural Revision Environment with exact Bayesian solutions showing revision follows a value boundary dependent on expansion cost and remaining horizon.

entry.title: BoT-GRPO: Efficient Process-Reward RL for Reasoning via Bag-of-Token Aggregation

author.name: Yingxiang Yang, Weihang Xiao, Zhunxuan Wang, Joshua Flashner, Niresh Agarwal

entry.summary: BoT-GRPO extends GRPO to token-level reward models via a length-invariant bag-of-tokens aggregation that weights token rewards by inverse sequence length and computes per-token advantages from weighted group statistics. It is critic-free and aims to accelerate convergence and improve reasoning quality without value networks.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Coordination via Support-Preserving Distillation

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Youngju Na, Chanmi Lee, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: This work identifies a failure mode in offline multi-agent RL where flow-based teachers pair noise with replay targets independently, causing samples between conflicting coordination modes that then propagate to distilled student actors. The proposed MoSDOT method uses semi-discrete optimal transport to preserve mode support during teacher training.

entry.title: Physics-Aligned Electronic Ground-State Learning Improves Generalization

author.name: Eike S. Eberhard, Xaver Kainz, Viktor Kotsev, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: The authors propose observable-agnostic electronic ground-state descriptor models positioned between ML interatomic potentials and Kohn-Sham DFT in cost, aligning learning objectives with the governing KS-DFT equations via physical constraints. Contributions include an OrthoNormal loss and Grassmann regularizer, showing improved size extrapolation from QM9 to QM40.

entry.title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media

author.name: Chunyang Wang, Mingrui Zhang, Yuyan Zhang, Linqi Zhu, Xin Ju, Edo Sicco Boek, Martin J. Blunt, Gege Wen

entry.summary: PoreML is an open-source framework unifying data generation, training, and physics-grounded evaluation for learning multiphase flow in porous microstructures, relevant to CO2 storage and fuel cells. It includes a GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver validated against analytical solutions to address the scarcity of time-resolved 3D datasets.

entry.title: Slow Beats Fast at the Kesten-Stigum Threshold: Minimax, Fisher-Information and Belief-Propagation Characterizations of the Information-Computation Gap in Sparse Stochastic Block Models

author.name: Soroor Ghandali

entry.summary: This theory paper provides three characterizations of the Kesten-Stigum threshold and the information-computation gap in sparse stochastic block models, using minimax risk, Fisher information, and belief propagation. It connects Bayes rules, polynomial estimators, and low-degree methods into a unified statistical decision-theoretic picture.

entry.title: emg2face: Expressive Facial Animation with High-Density Surface EMG

author.name: Ganidhu Abey, Wendy Greening, Ashika Kamboj, Leonhard Helminger, Abhijeet Ghosh, Karel Petranek, Sergio Orts Escolano, Dinesh K. Pai

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that high-density surface EMG (64 channels at 2048 Hz) can drive expressive facial animation without optical capture, addressing occlusion by VR headsets and privacy concerns. The authors collect forehead and side-of-face EMG signals and map them to facial expressions. This enables realistic avatar facial animation under head-mounted displays where cameras cannot see the face.

entry.title: Unpaired Canonical Correlation Analysis

author.name: Nir Ben-Ari, Ronen Talmon, Uri Shaham

entry.summary: This paper presents Unpaired CCA (UCCA), the first method to learn maximally correlated linear projections without any paired samples during training, by connecting the Quadratic Assignment Problem to CCA theoretically. The approach learns multiview shared spaces when pairing is unavailable or impossible to obtain. This relaxes a strict and often impractical requirement of a fundamental classical method.

entry.title: Global Average Precision for Representation Learning

author.name: Bill Psomas, Mohammad Mahdi, Michalis Thomas, Danda Pani Paudel, Giorgos Tolias, Giorgos Kordopatis-Zilos

entry.summary: The paper introduces Global Average Precision (gAP), an information retrieval metric that ranks all query-candidate pairs in a single list, capturing cross-query comparability that per-query metrics like mAP ignore, plus gSAP, a differentiable surrogate usable as a training loss. This is relevant to systems with a single global decision threshold. The loss plugs into standard representation learning pipelines with the same inputs as InfoNCE-style objectives.

entry.title: Data Reuse in Non-Stationary Learning

author.name: Tomer Gafni, Garud Iyengar, Assaf Zeevi

entry.summary: The authors study online learning in non-stationary environments where an unknown parameter switches abruptly among recurring values, quantifying fundamental tradeoffs in safely reusing past observations. They propose Exposure-Capped Reuse (ECR), a class of anytime algorithms combining online change detection and compatibility testing, showing the tradeoffs resemble a bias-variance dilemma.

entry.title: Derivative Gaussian Processes on a Two-Direction Budget

author.name: Hyunseok Seung, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: This work proposes a derivative Gaussian process surrogate that uses only two directions per observed gradient within a Vecchia approximation. One direction captures the gradient's direct contribution to prediction and the other its indirect contributions via correlations, reducing md gradient coordinates to 2m directional derivatives and achieving O(m^3) dense factorization per prediction target. This makes gradient-informed GPs far more scalable.

entry.title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation

author.name: Yihao Hu, Yanlin Feng, Naoki Otani, Nikita Bhutani

entry.summary: ARCS introduces structured disambiguation, a paradigm where ambiguity in text-to-SQL user questions is resolved through explicit, constrained interactions rather than free-form clarification dialogue. The paper contributes the first text-to-SQL ambiguity benchmark with naturally occurring, unconstrained user questions. This targets error sources that silently push systems away from user intent in real deployments.

entry.title: Learning to Act with Task Progress: Distilling Small Agents from Compact Teacher Supervision

author.name: Wenxi Gan

entry.summary: Task-Progress Distillation (TPD) trains small agent models offline by pairing each demonstrated action with a compact label describing the current task stage, letting a 1.7B-parameter student score stage-action pairs executed by a deterministic harness. On ALFWorld, the student achieves 72.4% unseen task success with only 404 demonstrations.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Brain MRI Inpainting with 2.5D Unconditional Flow Priors

author.name: Arnela Hadzic, Franz Thaler, Simon Johannes Joham, Martin Urschler

entry.summary: The authors propose a zero-shot brain MRI inpainting framework using 2.5D unconditional flow priors that capture superior-inferior spatial context without full 3D convolution overhead or task-specific conditional training. The method synthesizes healthy tissue in pathological regions to support downstream registration, brain extraction, and segmentation.

entry.title: Controllable Crowd Generation through World-Model Planning

author.name: JunGyu Lee, Jisu Shin, Seunghyun Shin, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: Proposes Ctrl-CWM, a controllable crowd world model that adapts world-model planning with imagined futures to crowd simulation, combining an encoder of human motion dynamics, an actor proposing behaviors, and run-time control supporting new user-specified objectives. It targets robotics, autonomous driving, and urban planning simulation.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Trajectory Optimisation over Continuous Poses for Sparse-View Cone-Beam CT

author.name: Linda-Sophie Schneider, Simon Wittl, Gabriel Herl, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: The authors make every CT source pose a continuous variable optimized by gradient ascent on the scanner's kinematic manifold, combining soft-Tuy plane coverage, a continuous view covariance loss, and an attenuation-aware ray-bundle penalty. This handles multiple scanner geometries and recovers laminar defects invisible to circular orbits in sparse-view cone-beam CT.

entry.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients

author.name: Giovanni Affatato, Sara Mandelli, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro

entry.summary: MOTIF dissects which components of 3D Morphable Model representations carry the detection signal in person-of-interest deepfake detection, holding encoder, training corpus, and enrollment protocol fixed. It finds coefficient groups largely redundant, with the shape block alone recovering most accuracy and temporal evolution contributing a bounded amount. This provides actionable insight into what matters for building per-identity deepfake detectors from genuine footage.

entry.title: HarnessIR: Harnessing Multimodal Foundation Models for Universal Real-World Image Restoration

author.name: Xiangtao Kong, Shuaizheng Liu, Rongyuan Wu, Lingchen Sun, Zhengqiang Zhang, Jinxin Zhao, Yuhui Wu, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: HarnessIR is an agentic framework for real-world image restoration that uses a multimodal foundation model as the executor across five stages including perception, diagnosis, and on-demand tool invocation. It critiques sequential tool-calling over single-degradation models, arguing mixed real-world degradations cannot be cleanly undone one at a time. The design aims at universal restoration of complex combined degradations.

entry.title: Position Forcing: Self-Conditioning 3D Generation

author.name: Ziheng Ouyang, Zeqiang Lai, Jiarui Chen, Jiangshan Wang, Yuhao Wan, Jingbo Gong, Xiangyu Yue, Hengshuang Zhao, Qibin Hou, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Position Forcing improves single-stage 3D generative models built on VecSet representations, which must implicitly infer token positions during denoising unlike two-stage methods with explicit positional guidance. The method recovers token positions from the current clean latent estimate, quantizes them at progressively finer resolutions across denoising stages, and uses them as self-conditioning. This strengthens generation quality without a second stage.

entry.title: QuadTok: Quadtree Visual Tokenizer for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Yucheng Mao, Zeyuan Chen, Xiaojun Shan, Xiang Zhang, Divyansh Srivastava, Bingnan Li, Zhuowen Tu

entry.summary: QuadTok proposes a hierarchical quadtree visual tokenizer for autoregressive image generation that dynamically allocates representational capacity to visually intricate regions while keeping homogeneous areas coarse. Compared with a fixed 256-token grid it saves about 10 percent of tokens on ImageNet and 9 percent zero-shot on COCO at comparable reconstruction fidelity. The tree structure also introduces natural causality that fits autoregressive modeling.

entry.title: ScribbleEdit: A Benchmark for Scribble-Only Image Editing

author.name: Jie Ren, Hao Kang, Kai Guo, Yiding Yang, Bo Liu, Liming Jiang, Qing Yan, Zichuan Liu, Yizhi Song, Yue Xing, Hui Liu, Xin Lu

entry.summary: ScribbleEdit is a benchmark with an automated data construction pipeline and evaluation protocol for image editing conditioned solely on scribbles, measuring both intention alignment and spatial accuracy. It reveals that current VLM/LLM-based editing models struggle with scribble-only inputs, highlighting a real interaction gap for creative tools.

entry.title: The Modular CMA-ES: A Framework for Modern Evolution Strategies

author.name: Jacob de Nobel, Diederick Vermetten, Anna V. Kononova, Carola Doerr, Thomas B\"ack

entry.summary: ModCMA is a configurable framework that decomposes the CMA-ES evolution strategy into interchangeable modules, integrating many proposed modifications within a single implementation so their interactions can be systematically studied. This addresses the fragmentation of evolution strategy research where variants are developed and evaluated in isolation.

entry.title: LACE-CRAFT: Robot Co-Design with Actor Inheritance and Blackboard Collaboration

author.name: Yuhan Wen, Jiawei Wang, Qixuan Zhang, Yusen Qin, Lan Xu

entry.summary: LACE-CRAFT couples robot morphology search with policy learning while preserving acquired control experience: LACE resumes the incumbent policy and initializes challenger designs with inherited actor parameters, while CRAFT coordinates morphology, reward, and feedback roles through shared records and a multi-agent blackboard. A generative extension converts generated meshes into editable articulated models.

entry.title: TempoBridge: Language-Guided Tempo Control for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Yeonseo Lee, Hyosup Shin, Guebin Hwang, Sungho Jo

entry.summary: TempoBridge adds how-fast-to-move controllability to frozen VLA policies by extracting tempo cues from VLM representations and aligning them with task progress via a causal phase router, requiring no tempo-labeled demonstrations or base-policy fine-tuning. On LIBERO tasks it raises tempo success rate from 52.6 percent to 89.7 percent.

entry.title: AeroEval: Staged Program and Execution Validation for AI-Generated Drone Missions

author.name: Kautuk Astu, Naina Rabha, Yogesh Simmhan

entry.summary: AeroEval is an agent-assisted middleware for staged validation of LLM-generated drone mission code, combining deterministic program analysis with context-grounded LLM agents to catch violations of user intent, environmental constraints, and mission-level behavior. It improves failure localization over prompt guardrails or simulator-only checks.

entry.title: RoboPrompt: Intuitive Robot Policy Steering with Sparse Human Input

author.name: Yanwen Zou, Chenyang Shi, Guoxuan Xu, Wenye Yu, Wendi Chen, Ye Pan, Cewu Lu, Chuan Wen

entry.summary: RoboPrompt is a lightweight shared-autonomy system that lets users steer pretrained end-to-end robot policies at deployment using sparse intuitive inputs such as drawn traces, target points, and directional strokes, without teleoperation hardware or policy retraining. This addresses the limited zero-shot reliability of imitation-learned policies and the scalability barriers of existing human-correction methods.

entry.title: UltraText Bench: A Comprehensive Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Image Generation

author.name: Deyuan Liu, Yihao Hu, Jingxuan Zhang, Xingying Li, Jun Xie, Jiacheng Liu, Jungang Li, Yu Huang, Xuanyi Liu, Yue Ding, Zecheng Wang, Lei Zhao, Mingda Wang, Zhenglin Cheng, Peng Sun, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Introduces UltraText Bench, a bilingual (English/Chinese) benchmark of 432 human-reviewed prompts for dense visual text rendering across 24 scene categories and three difficulty levels, with structured references for content, placement, and attributes. Evaluation uses a Q-Judger vision-language model to assess generated images against complete references.

entry.title: The Identifiability and Observability of Deep Normalized Attention

author.name: Pranav Venkata Konda

entry.summary: The paper characterizes which parameters of deep unmasked single-head attention are determined by its input-output function, proving the real-analytic case of the Henry-Marchetti-Kohn conjecture including softmax. It classifies exceptional fibers where collapse makes scores unobservable and computes Jacobian decay spectra near simultaneous query/key collapse.

entry.title: Shared Gaussianization: What Gaussian Regularizers Certify About Contrastive Learning, and What They Miss

author.name: Ruoyu Zhao, Yuting Chen, Jinheng Zhang, Zhehao Zou, Tong Che

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes shared Gaussianization—the Gaussianity test underlying SIGReg in LeJEPA—showing it vanishes exactly at aligned uniform minimizers of population InfoNCE and bounds InfoNCE excess risk with a sharp square-root rate and dimension-free constant. It also probes what such regularizers fail to certify about contrastive learning.

entry.title: Executing Causal Structure Learning with Linear-Attention Transformers

author.name: Amartya Roy, Sayar Karmakar

entry.summary: The authors explicitly construct a fixed-weight linear-attention Transformer whose forward pass exactly reproduces one update of a continuous causal discovery algorithm, showing repeated blocks reproduce its optimization trajectory. They prove retaining the algorithm's multiplier between updates is essential for exact execution.

entry.title: PEACE: Covariant learning of nonadiabatic manifolds with parity-resolved Hamiltonians

author.name: Rongzhi Gao, Shuguang Chen, Yang Zhou, GuanHua Chen, Ziyang Hu, ChiYung Yam

entry.summary: PEACE combines a parity-equivariant latent Hamiltonian with a learned electronic connection to model nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, respecting electronic symmetry in light-driven processes relevant to solar energy conversion and photocatalysis. Controlled ablations show complementary roles of symmetry-allowed state mixing and electronic-frame variation, and the model reproduces excited-state population dynamics from first-principles simulations. This advances ML surrogate modeling for quantum chemistry.

entry.title: Flow-of-Thought: A Framework for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Mariia Baidachna, Nicolas Pugeault

entry.summary: Flow-of-Thought integrates visual sketch generation as intermediate reasoning steps mimicking human mental imagery, training coordinate-aware trajectory flow fields on SO(2) group orbits and cumulative shortest paths. Frozen learned dynamics are compared via reconstruction energy across competing generative hypotheses, achieving 100 percent accuracy on Tetris and 99 percent on colored shape tasks under locked tests.

entry.title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Wasserstein-Based Evidential Uncertainty for Out-of-Distribution Segmentation

author.name: Arnold Brosch, Abdelrahman Eldesokey, Michael Felsberg, Kira Maag

entry.summary: The paper provides a probabilistic analysis of evidential deep learning for out-of-distribution segmentation, moving beyond Euclidean objectives by using Wasserstein-based formulations to better calibrate epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. This targets the safety-critical failure of segmentation networks on OOD objects in autonomous driving. It offers an efficient alternative to costly Bayesian methods like deep ensembles.

entry.title: ECHO: Embodied Camera Observations of Human Object Carrying

author.name: Xuefei Sun, Lorin Achey, Kali Hamilton, Alberto Speranzon, Gregory Grebe, Yonatan Bisk, Christoffer Heckman

entry.summary: ECHO introduces contextual object placement as a benchmark task: predicting an object's destination during an observed object-carrying episode, requiring reasoning about environment layout and human habits. The paper presents a dataset with navigable, fully reconstructed scenes, human activity, and ground-truth object destinations, filling a gap where existing RGB-D scans are static and HOI datasets lack scene context. This supports embodied and assistive agents beyond mere object recognition.

entry.title: Adaptive Workflow Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture for Context-Driven Enterprise Automation

author.name: Sreedevi Pandiyath Viswambaran

entry.summary: This paper proposes AWI, a cognitive architecture for enterprise automation agents organized around a four-layer Perception-Cognition-Action-Reflection loop. It treats reflection as a continuous policy-refinement mechanism and integrates hybrid reasoning with policy-constrained enterprise operations, addressing brittleness of LLM agents and RL under evolving conditions. It matters for practitioners building adaptive, auditable automation in regulated environments.

entry.title: Sigma-Hunter: A Domain-Specific Language Model for Threat Hunting and Detection Engineering

author.name: Kemal Davaslioglu, Sastry Kompella

entry.summary: Sigma-Hunter is a domain-adapted LLM for generating Sigma detection rules for threat hunting, built from 3,635 validated open-source rules expanded into 7,663 instruction-tuning examples with leak-free train/test partitioning. It fine-tunes 7B Mistral and Phi models to avoid common failures of general LLMs like invalid YAML or overbroad logic. A solid applied security contribution with careful dataset hygiene.

entry.title: GeoNatureAgent (GNA): A Framework and Benchmark for Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial and Environmental Tasks

author.name: Gabriel Diaz-Ireland, Diego Prieto-Herr\'aez, Mario Garc\'ia Peces, Javier Vel\'azquez, Benjamin Zaitchik, Devika Jain

entry.summary: GeoNatureAgent provides a fixed sixteen-tool geospatial MCP server and a 103-task benchmark for evaluating tool-using agents against a real, self-hostable environmental API covering Spain and Portugal. Because the tool layer, tasks, and scorer are held constant, the agent is the only variable under test. It fills a genuine gap in pre-production evaluation for domain-specific agent deployments.

entry.title: Trajectory Abstraction for the Science of Language Agent Behavior

author.name: Tianqiang Yan

entry.summary: The paper formulates scientific study of language agents as learning and testing a hierarchy of trajectory abstractions: measuring role- and phase-indexed events, proposing constrained relations, testing stability, then constructing episode-level motifs and repeating. Explicit measurement functions tie each abstraction level back to raw trajectories, with randomized protocol experiments for hypothesis testing. It proposes a methodology for a behavioral science of agents.

entry.title: From Plausible Hierarchies to Useful Taxonomies: Evaluating Agentic Harnesses on Customer Feedback

author.name: Prabhath Chellingi, Raviraja G, Viraj Bagal

entry.summary: This paper asks when LLM-generated taxonomies over customer feedback corpora are actually useful in production, not merely plausible. The authors build six taxonomies over two proprietary corpora and evaluate them with operationally meaningful criteria beyond per-node validity checks.

entry.title: Learning Situation-Conditioned Thinking Policies for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Hong Su

entry.summary: This paper proposes a situation-conditioned thinking memory framework that distills historical reasoning experience into a lightweight policy predicting what should be thought about in the current situation, while delegating detailed reasoning to the LLM. It targets long-running agents whose memory and context cannot grow indefinitely, covering temporal and spatiotemporal situation evolution.

entry.title: RewardWeaver: Long-Horizon Interactive Learning for Language Agents via Self-Evolving Reward Adaptation

author.name: Hengbo Xiao, Boyao Zhang, Purui Liu, Yuxuan Zheng, Haoran Yin, Haibo Liu, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: RewardWeaver is a self-evolving reward adaptation framework for long-horizon language agents, maintaining a validated capability space with semantically fixed rubrics and adapting which rubrics are emphasized as the policy evolves. This tackles sparse terminal feedback and the mismatch between static process rewards and the policy's current bottleneck. It extends RLVR to long-horizon interactive settings.

entry.title: Transferability and operational reliability of a Prithvi crop classification foundation model under phenological and geographic shift across three continents

author.name: Venkatesh Kolluru, Rajat Shinde, Abdelhak Marouane, Caden Helbling, Deepak Shah, Othneil Drew, Srinivas Kolluru, Iksha Gurung, Manil Maskey, Rahul Ramachandran

entry.summary: Evaluates the Prithvi-EO-2.0 geospatial foundation model for crop classification across 37 events in 12 countries on three continents, finding overall accuracy drops from 0.65 in the US to 0.40 in Europe. Beyond accuracy, it assesses confidence calibration, sensitivity to observation windows, and other operational reliability aspects under distribution shift.

entry.title: RACER: Reflective Agent Coupling Query Interpretation and Tool-Based Retrieval for Frame Selection in Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yiyang Huang, Yitian Zhang, Yizhou Wang, Jianglin Lu, Qihua Dong, Hailing Wang, Huimin Zeng, Mingyuan Zhang, Yun Fu

entry.summary: RACER is a training-free agentic framework for selecting relevant frames in long-video understanding, decomposing the problem into query interpretation by a lightweight video LLM plus evidence-driven retrieval. The paper diagnoses two failure modes in existing approaches: a Query Comprehension Gap in similarity-based methods and an Interpretation-Selection Gap in judgment-based methods. The reflective coupling of these stages improves frame selection for complex queries over long videos.

entry.title: SwarmReconGuard: Black-Box Detection of Distributed Collective Reconnaissance by Individually Benign-Looking Agent Populations

author.name: Vahid Tavakkoli, Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Distributed Collective Reconnaissance, a threat where agentic clients spread low-rate reconnaissance across many identities so each request looks benign, and presents a reproducible black-box benchmark with 440 test runs across 10-10,000 virtual identities. It compares multiple detector families, with Gaussian likelihood-ratio detection achieving strong performance.

entry.title: TutorLoop: Regulating Student Learning Behaviors via Sensor-in-the-Loop Generative Feedback

author.name: Songlin Xu, Xinyu Zhang

entry.summary: TutorLoop is a sensor-in-the-loop tutoring system that uses webcam-derived cognitive-state signals, a deep reinforcement learning agent to choose feedback types over the whole learning process, and an LLM to render feedback into human-like messages. A large-scale user study (N=187) shows an offline-trained model transfers directly to a new learning task.

entry.title: GeoPrior-Mamba: Structured Process Priors with Mamba for Fine-Resolution XCO2 Reconstruction

author.name: Zhao Meng, Yinan Cai, Siru Zhong, Juepeng Zheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: GeoPrior-Mamba reconstructs fine-resolution CO2 (XCO2) fields from sparse satellite observations using a multi-directional Mamba architecture augmented with structured process priors induced offline by a language model. Rather than having the LM predict values, it organizes knowledge about biospheric uptake, respiration, and anthropogenic emissions into deterministic priors before training.

entry.title: Correct Answers, Unsupported Findings: Evidence Binding in Forensic Reconstruction of LLM Agent Logs

author.name: Taehyeon Yun, Dongho Kim, Geonwoo Kim, Juyoung Seo, Minseok Hur, Moohong Min

entry.summary: Audits whether LLM readers, when reconstructing LLM-agent actions forensically, can establish which preserved record supports a finding, using 64 mechanically checkable cases from saved AgentDojo Banking executions. It separately measures evidence-grounded findings, justified abstention, and unsupported assertions, showing that citation identifiers do not establish sources unless identifier-to-record bindings are preserved.

entry.title: What Makes Synthetic Hard Negatives Work in Vision-Language Pretraining?

author.name: Nikos Giakoumoglou, Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Andreas Floros, Kleanthis Marios Papadopoulos, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Analyzes six representation-space synthetic hard-negative strategies for vision-language pretraining, identifying two failure modes and observing logit-scale saturation with learnable temperature, which fixing the temperature resolves. Based on this geometric analysis it proposes SNAP, an improved hard-negative generation method.

entry.title: Temporal Predictive Multiplicity: Equally Accurate Time Series Models Yield Different Forecast Trajectories

author.name: Emanuele Albini, Francesca Toni, Saumitra Mishra, Francesco Leofante

entry.summary: The paper introduces temporal predictive multiplicity, a framework characterizing disagreement over complete forecast trajectories among time-series models with near-identical accuracy, showing that performance constraints alone admit a broad range of different trajectories. Unlike prior scalar-output analyses, it treats forecasts jointly across horizons. This has implications for model selection and trust in forecasting systems used for decisions.

entry.title: Why Software Engineering Is Indispensable in the Age of Coding Agents

author.name: Alfonso Fuggetta

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that capable AI coding agents make software engineering discipline and professionals more, not less, essential. It identifies three structural LLM properties (probabilistic generation, agnosticism, semantic statelessness) that create a trust gap which can only be filled by methodological, domain, design, and process knowledge. The argument speaks directly to current debates about AI-generated software quality.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Generation of Transparent, Open-Source Multiphysics Models of Electrochemical Devices

author.name: Sebastian Castro, Maya F. Schuchert, Spencer A. McCluskey, Eric W. Lees, Justin C. Bui

entry.summary: The authors show that frontier LLM agents can generate open-source multiphysics continuum models of electrochemical devices, using 1D electrochemical CO2 reduction as a test case. A machine-readable, human-specified harness keeps the governing physics under researcher control while the LLM removes the numerical implementation burden typically requiring proprietary software or expert skills.

entry.title: The Cost of Long Memory: State, Context, and Stability Complexity in Sequence Models

author.name: Yuheng Song

entry.summary: This theory paper proves matching upper and lower approximation bounds on how much state, context, or dynamical criticality a sequence model needs to forecast accurately under algebraically decaying predictive memory. It shows the best r-mode forecast error decays as e^{-Theta(sqrt r)}, so achieving error tau requires Theta(log^2(1/tau)) states or modes, giving precise complexity characterizations for a canonical forecasting target. This formalizes the resource cost of long-range temporal dependence in sequence models.

entry.title: Neighborhood Smoothing for Calibration

author.name: Idan Horowitz, Avigdor Gal

entry.summary: The authors propose graph smoothing as a general train-time calibration principle that encourages similar predictive distributions across neighboring samples in representation space, deriving theoretical bounds linking neighbor divergence to confidence variation and calibration error propagation, and characterizing when smoothing can improve calibration.

entry.title: EDiS: Edge Disjoint Subgraph Sparsification Framework for Graph Neural Networks
