The authors encode three spatial priors at the data, loss, and representation stages while keeping inference fully end-to-end. This narrows the remaining gap with tracking-by-detection methods without post-hoc association.

entry.title: Abdominal Ultrasound Simulation from Semantic Labels using Paired Label-to-Physics-Based Image Translation

author.name: Santiago Vitale, Duilio Deangeli, Ignacio Larrabide, Jos\'e Ignacio Orlando

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage learning pipeline that generates realistic abdominal ultrasound images from semantic labels, first synthesizing a simplified physics-based image and then refining it with anatomically guided unpaired translation. This removes the need for patient-specific CT volumes at inference, enabling scalable, controllable ultrasound simulation for training and algorithm development.

entry.title: Relocating Nonlinearity: How a Downstream Learner Reshapes What Genetic Programming Must Evolve

author.name: Nam H. Le

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical account of when genetic programming benefits from making the evolved program an input to a separate downstream learner rather than the final solution, arguing that what matters is how much of a target's nonlinearity the learner can absorb. It formalizes the division of nonlinearity between program and learner, explaining which learner attachments succeed.

entry.title: SAFE: Unified Slip and Fracture Detection with Low-Cost Acoustic Sensing in Robotic Grasping

author.name: Zerun Wang, Vivek Kamat, Shekhar Bhansali

entry.summary: SAFE detects both slip and fracture of grasped fragile objects in real time using two passive PVDF acoustic sensors and motor proprioception on a compliant Fin Ray gripper, with a unified classifier over a 79-dimensional feature vector and no vision or material knowledge. It achieves an Alert-F1 of 0.884 under leave-one-grasp-out cross-validation.

entry.title: Belief-Space Planning with Planner-Conditioned Estimator Error under Intermittent Observations

author.name: Peter M. Donley, Joseph L. Moore

entry.summary: This work proposes a belief-space planning approach that predicts and penalizes planner-conditioned estimator error when future state corrections are intermittent and stochastic, relaxing zero-mean error assumptions. It combines an affine error model with trajectory-level propagation to improve planning under uncertain observation availability.

entry.title: Fast and Robust Teach-and-Repeat Navigation Using MixVPR Visual Place Recognition*

author.name: V\'aclav Truhla\v{r}\'ik, Tom\'a\v{s} Pivo\v{n}ka, Libor P\v{r}eu\v{c}il

entry.summary: The work builds a teach-and-repeat mobile robot navigation system around the MixVPR visual place recognition method, targeting low computational cost for long-term operation in unstructured, dynamic environments. Real-world indoor and outdoor tests show precision comparable to state-of-the-art systems with lower hardware requirements.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Predictive Mapping for Exploration and Navigation

author.name: Kenneth J. K. Ong, William W. J. Teo

entry.summary: This study investigates whether semantic door cues improve predictive occupancy mapping in ambiguous indoor regions where doors resemble walls geometrically but imply traversable structure beyond the observed area. The authors modify the CogniPlan dataset with door-induced ambiguities and compare geometry-only against semantics-augmented predictive mapping.

entry.title: Factorized Tactile Representation and Control for Sim-to-Real Manipulation

author.name: Siqi Shang, Bianca Aumann, Tye Brady, Joshua Migdal, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: This paper proposes a factorized tactile representation that separates contact geometry, force distribution, and temporal contact change, mapping simulated contact to device-recoverable sensor responses for sim-to-real transfer. A Tactile Gated Policy preserves these factors during control and operates across all mask configurations without retraining, evaluated on force regulation and adversarial peg-in-hole tasks.

entry.title: The Curve Bends You

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi argues that automating alignment work with current AI — having AI do the alignment homework and figure out alignment for us — is close to suicidal as a plan, despite becoming the de facto strategy. The post laments that no better plan exists at scale, that some assign only small catastrophe probabilities to it, and that optimization pressure toward this path is amplifying.

entry.title: Learning to Report Unsafe Tasks in a Multi-Agent Game

author.name: Avyay M. Casheekar, Hariganesh Tangirala

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies when agents with shared rewards learn to report unsafe work, showing that audits can make reporting optimal without training a silent team to report, and derives audit conditions under which exact policy-gradient updates converge to universal reporting. A k-witness shared-policy structure creates a factor-k distortion in gradient signals at universal silence. It is a formal treatment of a multi-agent safety oversight problem.

entry.title: The Handover Problem: Governing Autonomy Transitions in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Vicente Pelechano, Antoni Mestre, Manoli Albert, Miriam Gil

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the Handover Problem: deciding at each operational cycle whether to escalate, maintain, or revert AI autonomy in multi-cycle human-AI workflows while keeping the process reversible and auditable. It synthesizes adaptive automation, supervisory control, trust, and deskilling literature into a multi-signal governance criterion. This provides a structured framework for dynamic autonomy management in deployments.

entry.title: Pre-training, Reasoning, Benchmarking: X-ray Report Generation on CheXpert Plus Dataset

author.name: Xiao Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Dan Xu, Yuehang Li, Shiao Wang, Bo Jiang, Yaowei Wang, Yonghong Tian, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Establishes a comprehensive benchmark for radiology report generation on the CheXpert Plus dataset, which previously lacked baseline implementations, covering pre-training, reasoning-enhanced generation, and standardized quantitative evaluation. Aims to enable fair comparison among follow-up medical report-generation algorithms.

entry.title: LeCuration: A Tiny World Model as a Data Curation Multi-Tool

author.name: Mayank Sengupta, Nirmit Desai, Eric Song, Kunal Sawarkar

entry.summary: LeCuration trains a small world model (a latent encoder-predictor with a diffusion transformer decoder) to serve as a data curation tool for larger downstream physical AI models operating in closed physical worlds like warehouses and games. The authors find the world model embeddings are useful for organizing, filtering, and curating training data.

entry.title: Align Before You Combine: Reference Space Calibration for Supervision Without Ground Truth

author.name: Jackson Eshbaugh, Jorge Silveyra

entry.summary: The paper introduces a calibration-first framework that produces supervision scores without ground-truth labels or a shared annotation space by aligning subset-specific scorers on a synthetic ordinal reference space built from ordered calibration features. Because calibration uses the reference space rather than training samples, it is independent of the empirical training distribution, outperforming uncalibrated averaging across three benchmarks.

entry.title: Structured pre-generation elicitation versus single-shot prompting in AI-assisted enterprise decision-making: a randomised online experiment

author.name: William Scott-Jackson

entry.summary: Reports a randomized online experiment testing Cognistance, a metacognitive scaffolding layer that asks users to clarify context, choose strategy, and explain reasoning before AI generates a deliverable. The scaffold raised composite output quality by 32% and counters cognitive surrender in enterprise AI-assisted decision-making.

entry.title: Constrained-Action AI Remediation for SIEM/XDR via a NeMo-Guardrails Proxy

author.name: Georgios Koutidis, Nikolaos Kekatos, Tom Nianios, Alexios Lekidis

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-layer constrained-action architecture for LLM-assisted incident response in Security Operations Centers, where a SIEM/XDR control plane grounds remediation in correlated host events and confines LLM-suggested actions through a NeMo-Guardrails proxy. This directly addresses the risk that an adversarial alert becomes a remote code path through LLM reasoning into production hosts. It is a concrete safe-agentic-deployment design for cybersecurity.

entry.title: TaoD2C-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Industrial UI Code Generation Beyond Visual Fidelity

author.name: Chengwei Shi, Yunnong Chen, Tingting Zhou, Qiang Lu, Shiyu Yue, Xinyuan Hu, Jianfang Ru, Liuqing Chen

entry.summary: TaoD2C-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on industrial design-to-code tasks that require constraint-aware cross-modal reasoning: connecting UI design images with disorganized layer metadata and generating code under target-library constraints. It fills a gap left by benchmarks that assess only visual fidelity, testing whether MLLMs can reason about component and layout requirements in realistic industrial settings.

entry.title: MovieSTAGE: Scene, Transition, and Global Encoding for Movie-fMRI ADHD Classification

author.name: Boseong Kim, Haejun Chung, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: MovieSTAGE is a multiscale framework for ADHD classification from naturalistic movie-fMRI data, combining hypergraph-structured functional connectivity within scenes, unsigned FC differences across scene transitions, and whole-movie FC. It is evaluated on 260 participants from the CMI-HBN cohort with rigorous cross-validation and out-of-fold prediction reporting.

entry.title: UniCSI Towards a Universal Wi-Fi CSI Encoder for Ubiquitous Human Sensing

author.name: Daniel Eckhoff, Hua Kang, Zhitang Chen, Jie Chuai

entry.summary: UniCSI is a foundation architecture that directly ingests heterogeneous Wi-Fi channel state information across differing subcarrier counts, bandwidths, and carrier bands without lossy preprocessing, preserving native waveform structure for human sensing tasks.

entry.title: NeuralZip: Reusable Setup for Fast Lossless Compression

author.name: Mart\'in Bravo, Samuel Horv\'ath, Gonzalo Navarro, Andr\'es Abeliuk

entry.summary: NeuralZip enables lossless compression of floating-point model checkpoints by grouping chunks with similar exponent distributions, sharing Huffman codes, and packing recurring exponent tuples, with setup done once and reused. Post-setup compression achieves 1.81-21.33x improvements while preserving exact floating-point values.

entry.title: OrBIT: Structure-Guided Embedding Compression

author.name: Yunied Puig, Amit Kumar Jaiswal

entry.summary: OrBIT is an embedding-compression framework that learns reusable local coding geometry from orbit dynamics rather than fixing a coding geometry a priori, constraining shared codewords and allocating budget via global reconstruction residuals. It includes theory linking chart geometry to distortion.

entry.title: On the Computational Complexity of Hidden Markov Model Identification

author.name: Markel Zubia, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: The paper takes a computational perspective on HMM identifiability, asking whether there is a sound and complete procedure for deciding if a given HMM is identifiable, going beyond prior sufficient-but-not-necessary conditions. This frames identifiability as a decision problem rather than a set of analytical conditions.

entry.title: A Strength-Monotonic Law for Domain Alignment in Frozen-Embedding Bioacoustic Classification

author.name: Yucheng Gong, Rui Zhou, Binbin Zeng, Qiang Ren, Hongjin Hui

entry.summary: Studying cross-domain mosquito-species classification with frozen foundation-model embeddings, the paper reports a strength-monotonic law: the stronger an encoder is on the target task, the more its unseen-domain generalization depends on distribution alignment (MMD) and the more it is harmed by domain-rebalanced sampling. The effect is remarkably consistent across encoder families and HuBERT layers. This offers actionable guidance for transfer with frozen embeddings in bioacoustics and beyond.

entry.title: Rubric Spans are Label Representations: Joint LLM Encoding for Short Answer Scoring

author.name: Zhifan Sun, Sebastian Gombert, Fabian Zehner, Leon Camus, Longwei Cong, Hendrik Drachsler

entry.summary: RUSPAN is a rubric-conditioned framework for automatic short answer scoring that treats rubric descriptions as semantic label representations. It serializes question, answer, and all rubric levels into one sequence and scores levels listwise in a single LM pass, with a Rubric-Independent Mask preventing rubric spans from attending to each other. This improves efficiency and transferability across rubric sets.

entry.title: GUARD: Geometric Uncertainty-Aware Point Cloud Denoising and Segmentation for Robotic Hard Disk Drive Disassembly

author.name: Zuoxu Wang, Xiao Liang

entry.summary: GUARD is a geometric uncertainty-aware framework for robotic HDD disassembly that jointly performs point cloud filtering and segmentation in a single forward pass, distinguishing genuine component geometry from scanning ghost artifacts. It addresses the problem that semantic confidence alone does not establish geometric reliability.

entry.title: VolCo: Volumetric Contact for High-Fidelity Human Grasp Generation

author.name: Zhuo Chen, Yihua Cheng, Ale\v{s} Leonardis, Hyung Jin Chang

entry.summary: VolCo introduces a volumetric contact representation for hand-object interaction that expands surface contact points to 3D volumetric grids organized hierarchically, enabling precise hand part recovery and better exploiting motion-capture detail. The VolCoDiff framework uses hierarchical local and global modules with diffusion to generate plausible grasps, mitigating penetrations common in surface-only contact models.

entry.title: How Private is Private? A Comparative Study for Face De-Identification

author.name: Hui Wei, Hao Yu, Hui Kuurila-Zhang, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: This study revisits evaluation of face de-identification technologies, which currently suffer from inconsistent metrics, heterogeneous datasets, and incomparable reporting. The authors introduce UtilFace, a demographically balanced benchmark with high identity diversity assembled from four large-scale face datasets through identity-aware cleaning and resolution enhancement, plus a unified metric perspective. The work enables meaningful cross-method comparison for privacy-preserving face processing.

entry.title: Self-correction Optimization for Interleaved Multimodal Generation

author.name: Xin You, Zhiwei Ning, Zukai Chen, Minghui Zhang, Xuanke Shi, Hanxiao Zhang, Jingsong Liu, Jie Yang, Quan Wang, Yun Gu

entry.summary: This paper proposes self-correction optimization (SCO), a training-free method for consistent interleaved image-text generation in multimodal LLMs. SCO treats the classifier-free guidance update as a reference and performs minimal self-correction under it, avoiding costly additional training with augmented data. It improves visual subject preservation, temporal consistency, and physical plausibility of interleaved generation.

entry.title: Targeted Modality Dropout for Real-Robot Manipulation Robust to Intermittent Vision Loss

author.name: Genki Shikada, Kazuki Osamura, Masaru Ide, Tetsuya Ogata, Kanata Suzuki

entry.summary: Targeted Modality Dropout estimates each modality's dominance via attention and selectively drops the most dominant one, combined with entropy regularization, to prevent overreliance on vision in multimodal imitation policies. Real-robot bimanual experiments show maintained task success under vision loss where baselines collapse.

entry.title: Video-to-Model: Automatic Modeling of Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Akshun Sharma, Kimia Forghani, Yancy Diaz-Mercado

entry.summary: The paper proposes a video-to-model framework that estimates parameters of a structured CBF-CLF-QP model of deformable suture thread motion directly from video, using a perception module for thread tracking and a spatio-temporal CNN for parameter estimation. The fitted model can then simulate thread dynamics under user-defined needle velocity inputs.

entry.title: When the Governor Becomes the Disturbance: Control-Generated Disturbance and Cost-Aware Backoff in Governed Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Veronique Ziegler

entry.summary: This controlled study shows that supervisory governors of tool-using agents can themselves induce failures, with a cost-blind governor converting experimentally imposed tool failures into persistent task-blocking. It compares an adaptive backoff rule, which reduces intervention based on a moving average of induced events, against fixed governors and shows improved completion at matched intervention frequency. A neat control-theoretic take on agent oversight.

entry.title: HGP:An on-device personalized agent memory via hybrid graph storage

author.name: Ran Zhou, Xueming Han, Jiaheng Liu, Yuyao Zhang, Fanyu Meng, Junlan Feng, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: HGP is a hybrid graph memory framework for on-device personalized agents, using a lightweight self-enhancement classifier for memory routing and building episodic, semantic, and procedural memories as graphs. Working memory is extracted as a state trajectory to capture implicit constraints and current state, reducing reliance on large models. It targets accurate retrieval where single-vector representations blur types and relations.

entry.title: PARC-Loc: Text-to-Point-Cloud Localization with Partial Assignment and Relational Consistency

author.name: Shengkai Ma, Zhenyu Hou, Weihua Cao

entry.summary: Proposes PARC-Loc, a coarse-to-fine text-to-point-cloud localization method addressing layout-inconsistent aliasing and boundary evidence incompleteness in city-scale 3D maps, using partial assignment and relational consistency. It improves on retrieval-based coarse-to-fine pipelines where repetitive urban objects inflate embedding similarity.

entry.title: Oscillatory Neural Dynamics over Sheaves

author.name: Jan-Willem Van Looy, Alessandro Trenta, Alessio Gravina, Alessio Borgi, Ferdinando Zanchetta, Pietro Li\`o, Davide Bacciu, Rita Fioresi

entry.summary: ONDA introduces long-range graph learning based on operator-valued information waves, where sheaf-stalk representations evolve under second-order dynamics governed by learned sheaf transport operators. It characterizes long-range influence via stalk-wise sensitivity analysis, addressing limitations of sheaf neural networks in long-range communication.

entry.title: Alice: A Large-Scale German Benchmark for Rubric-Based Multi-Dimensional Automatic Short Answer Scoring

author.name: Zhifan Sun, Sebastian Gombert, Jannik Lossjew, Tobias Wyrwich, Berrit Katharina Czinczel, David Bednorz, Marcus Kubsch, Knut Neumann, Hendrik Drachsler

entry.summary: Alice is a large-scale, pedagogically aligned German benchmark for rubric-based automatic short answer scoring with three subtasks: learning performance, knowledge elements, and skills. It reframes rubric-based scoring as a rubric-retrieval task and benchmarks a range of language models from encoders onward. The dataset addresses the scarcity of open ASAS benchmarks targeting conceptual mastery rather than direct answer correctness.

entry.title: Beyond Anonymous Captions: Grounding Character Identity in Video Captioning and Question Answering

author.name: Anas Filali Razzouki, Killian Steunou, Khalil Guetari, Thomas Kling, Moun\^im El-Yacoubi, Yannis Tevissen

entry.summary: This work builds an identity-aware video captioning and person-centric QA framework that matches detected faces to actor references, tracks characters across frames, and produces identity-linked bounding box inputs for a strong VLM. From LSMDC v2 movie clips it creates a manually verified benchmark of 750 captioned clips and 3,000 person-centric questions, and studies five grounding strategies. It targets the common failure of video captioners producing anonymous, identity-free descriptions.

entry.title: MORCA: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cache Reuse in Video Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Yuxiang Xiong, Ruiyan Wang, Wenqiang Wang, Teng Hu, Songhang Shen, Bohao Feng, Hongqian Deng, Ran Yi

entry.summary: MORCA improves cache-based acceleration of video diffusion transformers by distinguishing step error, the immediate error from cache reuse, from terminal error, the final quality loss, and showing latent information helps relate them. It uses offline-to-online reinforcement learning to make adaptive cache decisions optimizing final video quality. This targets inference latency of DiT-based video synthesis more faithfully than step-error heuristics.

entry.title: How Could AI Eliminate Humanity? A Failure-Mode Analysis of Civilizational Risk

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Sienicki, Krzysztof Sienicki

entry.summary: The paper develops a taxonomy of catastrophic AI risk pathways, including autonomous misalignment, harmful human use, organizational failure, and competitive deployment, arguing that extinction risk requires neither consciousness nor intent. It maps severity to factors like capability, autonomy, and institutional safeguards in a deliberately non-operational way. It is a conceptual contribution to AI risk framing.

entry.title: We Query, Therefore We Compute: On Oracle Computation beyond the Machine, with an Application to Agents

author.name: Kefan Liu, Fengning Ou, Yelin Luo, Jingdi Lei

entry.summary: The paper constructs an abstract machine treating the LLM as an Oracle queried by an extended two-stack pushdown automaton, yielding a Turing-complete Priestess computation alongside the Oracle's, unifying workflows and agents under one formalism. The append-only stack grows autoregressively and OS-like mechanisms (scheduling, caching, isolation) find a common ground. A theoretical unification for agentic systems.

entry.title: Cognitive Schemas, Laws and Tasks

author.name: Antal Jakov\'ac, Andr\'as Telcs

entry.summary: This theoretical paper develops a structural framework for explicit cognitive schemas in knowledge-based problem solving, organizing schemas by the information and relations required for their use and separating context-dependent from stable reusable structures. It distinguishes representation limitations from solving-procedure limitations, including inconsistency and underdetermination.

entry.title: Outperformance Inverse Optimization: Learning Objective Functions that Outperform Agent Decisions

author.name: Akira Kitaoka

entry.summary: This paper proposes outperformance inverse optimization: instead of learning objective weights that reproduce observed (suboptimal) decisions as optimal, it learns weights whose optimal solutions dominate the observed action in every component. It provides a loss computable with forward-problem oracles, plus gradient-based and DC optimization algorithms, with guarantees for unique outperforming weights. This is useful when observed decisions come from imperfect agents.

entry.title: Child ASR Adaptation with Adult Retention: An Empirical Study

author.name: Houssam Eddine-Othman Lachemat, Shammur Absar Chowdhury

entry.summary: Empirically studies adapting adult ASR models to child speech across Arabic and English while retaining adult-speech performance, comparing full fine-tuning, LoRA, and weight-space merging across encoder-decoder, CTC, and AudioLLM architectures. It introduces metrics quantifying the adaptation-retention trade-off.

entry.title: FinVector-Market-4B: A Controlled Study of LoRA Adaptation for Structured Financial Tasks

author.name: Alina Khaybullina

entry.summary: This controlled study LoRA-tunes Qwen3.5-4B with rank-16 adapters on a 22,000-example corpus for structured financial tasks, evaluating under implicit and explicit JSON-schema contracts. Notably, supplying a schema alone raises base-model JSON validity from 0% to 91.3%, and adaptation yields large gains on FinQA exact match, calculator-expression correctness, and label agreement. A post-hoc audit also clarifies that an apparent macro-F1 decline reflected a changing label set rather than model degradation.

entry.title: Quad-State Safety Evaluation of Open-Weight Large Language Models on Non-Canonical Inputs

author.name: Pavan Maddula

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Adversarial Surface-Form Robustness Dataset (ASRD) with 2,100 prompts across seven surface-form families (emojis, altered spellings, encodings, character variations), evaluating five open-weight LLMs and 10,500 responses with a four-outcome rubric distinguishing harmful compliance, safe response, comprehension failure, and indeterminate. Findings show emoji and invisible Unicode variations cause almost no comprehension failure while still probing safety robustness. This highlights a gap between canonical safety evaluations and real-world inputs.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation

author.name: Thushara Manjari Naduvilakandy, Hyeju Jang, Mohammad Al Hasan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a cognitively grounded, multi-objectively aligned small language model framework for generating realistic substance use disorder patient dialogue, motivated by data scarcity, privacy, and deployment constraints in clinical settings. It aims to produce patient responses reflecting underlying cognitive states like beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness for change.

entry.title: From Chunks to Functional Evidence: Function-Aware Retrieval for EDA Documentation QA

author.name: Xiaotian Qiu, Kairui Liu, Shi Chenyi, Jinyuan Deng, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: This paper redesigns the retrieval unit in RAG for Electronic Design Automation documentation, grouping typed artifacts into EDA functional units represented as hyperedges linked to source chunks, and trains an encoder to align queries with these functional units. The approach targets the mismatch between queries and knowledge organization that bottleneck technical-documentation QA.

entry.title: Which Language Should a Skeleton Speak? Language Choices in Multilingual Reasoning

author.name: HyeonSeok Lim, SeungWoo Song, Inho Won, Hoyun Song, Jihyo Kim, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: Proposes LASEF, a framework studying which language skeleton-based reasoning prompts should use in multilingual mathematical reasoning. English skeletons give a small positive tendency, most visible for smaller models and low-resource languages, but few gains survive statistical correction and English is not universally optimal.

entry.title: QCATS: Query Context-Aware Transformer Slicing for Efficient Predictive Query Processing

author.name: Yueying Li, Zhongle Xie, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: QCATS enables efficient in-database transformer inference by using query predicates and metadata statistics to pre-select context-aligned FFN slices at query granularity before model execution, rather than routing tokens individually. It combines offline expert construction with lightweight runtime selection for sparse inference inside relational pipelines. This bridges a gap between database query optimization and neural inference efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond LLM-GA: Secure Fluid Antenna Systems with ReEvo-Designed Memetic Algorithm

author.name: Hanyong Xu, Zhaolai Dang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors apply LLM-assisted algorithm design to physical-layer security for fluid antenna systems, using ReEvo-style reflective evolution to have an LLM design crossover, mutation, and local-search operators offline, embedded in a memetic algorithm for secure port selection. This targets eavesdropping resilience in military, satellite, and IoT deployments. It extends LLM-GA work beyond simple genetic operators.

entry.title: DenoFlow: Flow Matching for SSVEP Denoising under Real Physiological Artifacts

author.name: Zhentao He, Ziwei Wang, Dongrui Wu

entry.summary: DenoFlow casts EEG steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) denoising as a transport problem using rectified flow: instead of mapping contaminated trials directly to clean ones, a network regresses the velocity field of the straight path between them. This addresses failures of prior denoisers that lacked paired ground truth and optimized waveform distance without preserving decodability. The work targets improving the robustness of EEG-based brain-computer interfaces under real physiological artifacts.

entry.title: HCPN-GCN: Scaling Hierarchical Prototype Networks with Cone Geometry for Continual Graph Learning

author.name: Sammuel R. Silva, Vander L. S. Freitas, Gladston Moreira, Eduardo J. S. Luz, Rodrigo Silva

entry.summary: HCPN-GCN extends Hierarchical Prototype Networks for continual graph learning by replacing linear feature extractors with graph convolutions and using cone-geometry representations to curb prototype growth on structurally diverse graphs. It targets catastrophic forgetting without storing historical data.

entry.title: Context-aware Attention-based Gaussian Mixture Models for Vehicular Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Arash Raftari, Babak Ebrahimi Soorchaei, Yaser P. Fallah

entry.summary: CAA-GMM is a probabilistic trajectory prediction model for autonomous driving that represents future motion as a Gaussian mixture conditioned on scene context and agent dynamics, with lightweight attention to fuse inter-agent interactions and rasterized environment cues. It is evaluated on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 with emphasis on interpretability and uncertainty awareness.

entry.title: Differential Refresh Policies for Models Trained on Lagging Data Snapshots: From a Single-Age Equivalence Limit to an Optimal Per-Segment Allocation

author.name: Amit Rajula

entry.summary: This paper studies retraining policies for production models trained on stale data snapshots, proving that any static monotone refresh trigger on a single global data age is equivalent to a uniform age timer. It then derives an optimal per-segment allocation, showing segment-aware scheduling is the right lever rather than elaborate global staleness scores.

entry.title: AdaPS-LiNGAM: Adaptive Predecessor Selection for Linear Non-Gaussian Acyclic Models under Small-Sample Settings

author.name: Shun Yanashima, Kentaro Kanamori, Hirofumi Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper proves a structural limitation of DirectLiNGAM causal discovery: when variables exceed samples, repeated residualization degenerates before the causal order is determined. It proposes adaptive predecessor selection to address small-sample LiNGAM estimation.

entry.title: Matching of signal, noise and hardware timescales for filtering and forecasting of correlated noise signals

author.name: Joshua Donald, Alex Gabbitas, Arthur G. T. Coveney, Sergey Savel'ev, Pavel Borisov

entry.summary: This paper studies physical reservoir computing using a nanoporous niobium oxide device, showing that the relationship between noise correlation time, reservoir memory, and forecast horizon determines whether correlated noise gets filtered out or predicted. It validates the framework on synthetic noisy signals and cryptocurrency price volatility.

entry.title: CAFE+FNO: Fourier Kernel Generation via Multiplicative Feature Composition

author.name: Hyungjoon Juen, Minwoo Shin

entry.summary: This paper introduces CAFE+FNO, which improves Fourier Neural Operators for solving PDEs by incorporating Content-Aware Frequency Encoding+ into Fourier-space kernel generation. It addresses the limitation that frequency truncation in standard FNOs hinders learning of high-frequency variations, drawing on ideas from implicit neural representations that build frequency interactions through explicit feature composition. The work matters because neural PDE solvers are important for scientific machine learning in physics simulation and engineering.

entry.title: HAN-Mamba: Hierarchical Selective State Space Networks for Multi-Scale Financial Volatility Forecasting

author.name: Mihai Bogdan Deaconu, Ioan Daniel Pop

entry.summary: HAN-Mamba extends a prior conference architecture (HAN-T) for realized volatility forecasting by replacing Transformer encoders with selective state space (Mamba) encoders per temporal scale, retaining attention only in a small three-token fuser. This yields linear-complexity multi-scale modeling from second-level order book dynamics to weekly regime drift.

entry.title: Trust-Region Optimization for Smooth Potential-Interaction Energies in Wasserstein Space

author.name: You Wan, Ting Gao, Jinqiao Duan

entry.summary: The authors develop a trust-region method for minimizing nonconvex potential-interaction energies on Wasserstein space, using a quadratic model along pushforward curves, an L2(rho) step radius, a Steihaug-Toint subsolver, and convergence theory under energy bounds. This brings second-order, reliability-controlled optimization to distribution-level problems.

entry.title: CATune: Structural Constraint-Aware Bayesian Optimization for DBMS Configuration Tuning

author.name: Fangping Lan, Qi Zhang, Eduard Dragut

entry.summary: CATune is a constraint-aware Bayesian optimization framework for DBMS configuration tuning that models deterministic inter-knob ordering constraints from documentation as structural components of the search domain. Rather than learning feasibility boundaries from samples, it exploits known constraints to prune the high-dimensional heterogeneous search space. This improves the cost and reliability of automated database tuning.

entry.title: Boundary-aware Reinforcement Learning for Hypercube State Spaces via Deterministic Policy Gradient

author.name: Lijun Bo, Yijie Huang, Chenhao Lu

entry.summary: The paper develops a continuous-time deterministic policy gradient framework for RL with reflected state dynamics on a hypercube, connecting the value function to the Neumann Bellman equation and introducing an advantage-rate function yielding a deterministic policy gradient formula. It proposes a deep algorithm enforcing Neumann boundary conditions via soft penalization or hard architectural constraints. This gives principled tools for control problems with bounded state spaces.

entry.title: Marrying Pricing and Advertising with LLMs

author.name: Alessandro Barro, Francesco Bacchiocchi, Francesco Emanuele Stradi, Alberto Marchesi

entry.summary: The paper studies a sequential pricing problem where a seller jointly posts a price and an LLM-generated advertisement under unknown demand, proposing an online actor-critic algorithm combining LoRA fine-tuning of a pretrained LLM with a fitted demand model. The critic estimates purchase probabilities to guide pricing while the actor generates ad content. This connects LLM-based content generation with principled online learning for revenue management.

entry.title: RoBART: Bayesian Additive Regression Trees with Tree-Specific Rotations

author.name: Jeongung Heo, Seonghyun Jeong

entry.summary: RoBART extends Bayesian additive regression trees by assigning each tree a shared Givens rotation, allowing axis-aligned splits in rotated coordinates to approximate boundaries misaligned with predictor axes. The authors develop reversible Metropolis-Hastings updates and prove posterior contraction rates for additive functions with component-specific rotations and anisotropic Holder smoothness.

entry.title: Estimating Uncoded Crash Factors with Tabular Foundation and System One Models: Kumo Tabular and Jev

author.name: Amir Rafe, Subasish Das

entry.summary: The authors build a system that joins coded fields and police narratives from 5.6 million Texas crashes (2017-2025) to estimate population-level uncoded crash factors with stated validity. An in-context tabular foundation model reads coded records, a calibrated narrative-reading model with human recalibration processes text samples, and a multiwave predict-then-debias estimator joins the tiers.

entry.title: Evolutionary Architecture Search for Chlorophyll-$a$ Prediction in Lakes using Sentinel-2

author.name: Kursat Komurcu, Linas Petkevicius

entry.summary: This paper applies regularized evolutionary architecture search to a small tabular remote-sensing task: predicting chlorophyll-a (algal blooms) in lakes from Sentinel-2 spectral features. Holding the task, features, and lake-level train/test split fixed from a published hand-designed model, the search finds compact MLPs that raise held-out AUC from 0.790 to 0.820 and accuracy from 0.733 to 0.748 while using only 409 trainable parameters, about 26 times fewer than the reference. It matters because it demonstrates that automated neural architecture search can yield both accuracy and efficiency gains even on the small, expert-feature datasets common in operational Earth observation.

entry.title: Dialect-Robust Speech Language Models with Synthetic Pseudo-Dialect Augmentation

author.name: Shunsuke Mitsumori, Tomoya Mizumoto, Yusuke Fujita

entry.summary: The authors propose synthesizing pseudo-dialect speech by converting LLM-generated dialect text through a standard-language TTS model, requiring zero real dialect speech. They add intermediate standard-text prediction during training as semantic normalization and evaluate on dialect-to-English speech translation across Japanese, German, and Chinese dialects. Pseudo-dialect augmentation improves over synthetic standard speech baselines.

entry.title: Shaer: Controlled Arabic Poetry Generation with Meter Subform and Semantic Conditioning

author.name: Ahmad Abbas, Tamara Fakih, Nour Fakih, Ammar Mohanna

entry.summary: Shaer is a controllable generation framework for Classical Arabic poetry, jointly conditioned on natural-language descriptions, meter subforms, and target hemistich counts. It contributes an enriched corpus of 116,032 poems with normalized meter labels and adapts the Yehia-7B model via QLoRA fine-tuning with a completion-only objective.

entry.title: CRT-HMAR: Causal Requirement Tracing-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Agent Regulation for Open-Task-Aware Infrared-Visible Image Fusion

author.name: Zengyi Yang, Shuai Yuan, Zhong-Cheng Wu, Juan Cheng, Huafeng Li, Yu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CRT-HMAR, a hierarchical multi-agent framework for open-task-aware infrared-visible image fusion. It uses causal requirement tracing, intervening on image information and observing task-network responses, to localize task requirements so the fusion generalizes to unseen downstream tasks.

entry.title: Temporal Residual Bottleneck for Robust Asynchronous Collaborative Perception

author.name: Melih Yazgan, Ahmed Abouelazm, J. Marius Z\"ollner

entry.summary: The paper formulates asynchronous collaborative perception as temporal residual prediction, keeping a deterministic pose-warped collaborator feature as an anchor and using a delta-t-conditioned xLSTM to extract residual temporal evidence. A gated, regularized residual bottleneck applies conservative corrections before fusion, reducing the risk of overwriting reliable ego features. This improves robustness when shared features from other vehicles arrive stale or incomplete.

entry.title: Label-free cell counting and viability prediction with brightfield imaging and deep learning

author.name: Amir Reza Vazifeh, Christian Zeigler, Sornanathan Meyyappan, Richard Jeske, Jason W. Fleischer

entry.summary: This paper replaces dye-based cell viability assessment, which perturbs cellular processes, suffers from ambiguity and photobleaching, and cannot run in situ, with deep learning on label-free brightfield imaging. The method enables cell counting and viability prediction critical for biopharmaceutical manufacturing and drug development. It removes chemical staining requirements while maintaining measurement utility.

entry.title: Efficient Dense Crowd Trajectory Prediction Via Dynamic Clustering

author.name: Antonius Bima Murti Wijaya, Paul Henderson, Marwa Mahmoud

entry.summary: The authors propose a cluster-based approach to crowd trajectory prediction that groups individuals with similar attributes over time, enabling faster execution via group summarization in dense, noisy crowd scenarios. This matters for public-safety applications such as stampede prevention, where per-individual prediction is computationally infeasible.

entry.title: From Wearable Interfaces to Dexterous Policies: Contact Shifts and Tactile Representations

author.name: Ruitong Tian, Fang Xu, Noah B. Wilson, Xianyao Li, Eric Jing Du

entry.summary: The paper studies how exoskeleton-style wearable demo-collection interfaces affect dexterous policy learning, comparing two DexUMI-family exoskeletons with different hand-side geometry but the same command definitions and tactile modules. It finds interface geometry influences task performance, physical demand, and the tactile observations recorded, revealing a source of distribution shift between collection hardware and robot execution.

entry.title: Adaptive Risk-Certified Event-Triggered Replanning for Dynamic Navigation

author.name: Richie R. Suganda, Bin Hu

entry.summary: CERT-Replan uses conformally calibrated obstacle-prediction residuals as an early-warning signal for when the current finite-horizon planning mode is becoming unsafe in dynamic environments. The framework complements control-barrier-function filters by deciding when to trigger replanning based on evolving prediction uncertainty.

entry.title: Enhancing Robotic Perception and Adaptability through Sensor Fusion and Origami-Inspired Designs

author.name: Namai Chandra, Jaison Jose, Kavi Arya, Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper presents a sub-300 USD, sub-2 kg mobile robot with origami-inspired wheels whose terrain-adaptive configurations sweep a 2D LiDAR through varying elevations, which are fused with RGB-D depth via IMU-corrected projections for RTAB-Map. The design cleverly reuses existing wheel actuation to extend sensing geometry at very low cost.

entry.title: NeRFifyMesh: Optimizing Neural Radiance Fields from Textured Meshes for Robotics Scene Building

author.name: Nillan Nimal, Mahboubeh Asadi, Sajad Saeedi

entry.summary: This paper introduces a pipeline for converting existing textured 3D mesh models into Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) representations, addressing the need to reuse large libraries of mesh assets in robotics workflows. By sampling the mesh to create a point-based radiance field as ground truth, the method enables roboticists to quickly build multi-object NeRF scenes for semantic mapping and simulation testing.

entry.title: Sketched Calibration for Conformal Prediction under Covariate Shift

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: This work introduces sketched calibration for weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift: likelihood-ratio weights are computed on compressed covariates, provably never increasing the chi-square-divergence-dependent calibration cost. Coverage degrades only by a leakage term measuring how much discarded shift direction reappears in the response.

entry.title: Online Resource Allocation with an Endogenous Markov State: Fewer LP Solves Earn More

author.name: Zhaohua Chen

entry.summary: The paper studies finite-horizon online resource allocation where actions affect a Markov state governing future rewards, using fluid and stationary LP benchmarks. Under nondegeneracy and irreducibility, both frequent and infrequent re-solving achieve O(1) regret, implying fewer LP solves can perform as well or better.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Approximation of Hessian-Guided Perturbed Wasserstein Gradient Flows

author.name: Ryotaro Kawata, Atsushi Nitanda, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when Wasserstein gradient flows with Hessian-guided Gaussian perturbations—used to escape saddle points in nonconvex optimization—remain accurately approximated by finitely many interacting particles over growing time horizons. It shows negative curvature can amplify errors while subsequent positive curvature damps them, proving particle and objective error bounds.

entry.title: Controlling Dependence in Implicit Generative Models via Spread Mutual Information

author.name: Jiahao Yu, Song Liu, Jos\'{e} Miguel Hern\'{a}ndez-Lobato, RuiKang OuYang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Spread Mutual Information, a weighted integral of mutual information across noise levels, enabling control of statistical dependence in implicit generative models where densities are intractable. It estimates generator gradients via score differences learned through classification while handling singular distributions and poor overlap. This provides a practical MI-based training objective for implicit models.

entry.title: Masked Feature Encoding for Large-Scale Whole Slide Image Representation

author.name: Haoyu He, Basile Tessier-Cloutier, Yang Wang, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: MFE-MIL is a feature-space masking framework for whole slide image analysis that jointly trains a lightweight MLP adapter with a window-based masked reconstruction branch and a MIL classification head. Classification suppresses within-slide variance from staining, scanner, and texture differences, while masked reconstruction regularizes the adapter. This improves slide-level prediction in computational pathology pipelines.

entry.title: Detecting Adversarial Images through Response Profiles of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Arash Vashagh, Roozbeh Razavi-Far

entry.summary: The paper investigates detecting adversarial inputs to frozen VLMs by summarizing how an image interacts with a collection of general semantic prompts. The detector builds a compact response profile from category-level statistics, prompt relationships, deviations from clean reference distributions, and stability under weak transformations, then classifies it with a lightweight model while the VLM stays fixed. It is evaluated across datasets, CLIP-style backbones, and gradient-based attacks.

entry.title: Route-Verify-Vote: Procedure-Conditioned Self-Consistency for Mixed-Domain Reasoning

author.name: Xinchen Xiao

entry.summary: RVV is a training-free inference framework for compositional generalization on the SCoRE 2026 benchmark, routing to a domain-appropriate reasoning procedure, verifying each option against extracted constraints, and voting over complete answer sets. It demonstrates that careful orchestration of a frozen LLM can handle unfamiliar mixed domains. Its value is mainly benchmark-scoped but methodologically clean.

entry.title: Agentic AI-Assisted Modeling for Production Scheduling: Assessment in Constraint Programming

author.name: \'Angel S\'anchez-Fern\'andez, Javier Pernas-\'Alvarez, Diego Crespo-Pereira

entry.summary: This study assesses whether general-purpose LLMs orchestrated as agents, without task-specific training, can formulate and implement constraint-programming models for production scheduling from natural-language descriptions. It compares single-agent and multi-agent orchestration strategies, bridging automated modeling research and agentic decision support. Results inform industrial deployment feasibility of LLM-based optimization modeling.

entry.title: Just for FUNS: LLM-Guided Spatio-Temporal Graph Node Generation for Forecasting Unobserved Node States

author.name: Shuhao Li, Weidong Yang, Changan Liu, Wei Zhuo, Yingbo Zhou, Fan Zhang, Siqiang Luo

entry.summary: Proposes GenST, which reframes forecasting states of unobserved sensor nodes as conditional generation on spatio-temporal graphs, fine-tuning a pretrained LLM as a semantic bridge to extract features from node descriptions. This addresses forecasting for nodes with no historical records in sparse sensor networks.

entry.title: Leveraging LLM-Generated Explanations for Detecting Emotionally Rewritten Fake News

author.name: Yupei Guo, Jiajun He, Xiaohan Shi, Tomoki Toda, Zekun Yang, Bowen Wang, Yukinobu Taniguchi

entry.summary: Investigates fake news detection robustness under fact-preserving emotional rewrites, constructing emotion-rewritten test sets and using LLM-generated explanations from original articles as stable background knowledge. A Gated Cross Attention framework adaptively fuses rewritten news with these explanations.

entry.title: Adaptive Code Generation for Controlling Robots

author.name: Justus Flerlage, Thorsten Wittkopp, Alexander Acker, Odej Kao

entry.summary: Introduces an architectural framework for intention-based robot control using LLM-generated code, framing robots as complex adaptive systems in unknown environments. It targets the formalization gap between imprecise natural-language intentions and executable actions, plus temporal state and progress awareness.

entry.title: A Scoping Review and Experimental Study on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Alexandra Coroiu, Andrea Vogt, Viktor Werbilo, Andreas Poppele, Johann Christensen, Sven Hallerbach

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided scoping review of RLHF in human-robot collaboration, screening 199 records and analyzing 20 peer-reviewed publications from 2020-2025, plus an experimental study. It is claimed to be the first review focused on bidirectional, closed-loop RLHF design, mapping feedback modalities and challenges around safety, feedback quality, and human-robot adaptation. Relevant to Industry 4.0 robotics and to the broader RLHF literature.

entry.title: Performance at What Cost? A Sustainability-Aware Performance Index for Cell and Nucleus Instance Segmentation

author.name: Eiram Mahera Sheikh, Alaa Tharwat, Wolfram Schenck

entry.summary: The paper proposes SAPI, a configurable metric combining segmentation performance with sustainability costs such as energy consumption, memory, and carbon emissions, for comparing pretrained cell and nucleus segmentation models. It questions whether the zero-shot gains of large foundation segmentation models justify their substantially higher computational and environmental costs.

entry.title: BeatFlow-ECG: Rectified Flow for ECG Reconstruction from Indirect Wearable Signals

author.name: Mohamed Kamel, Sahar Selim, Walaa Medhat, Tamer Nadeem

entry.summary: BeatFlow-ECG is a conditional rectified-flow model that reconstructs single-channel ECG from synchronized wearable PPG and inertial measurements, using a convolutional encoder-decoder with a transformer bottleneck and explicit flow-time conditioning, with motion information used to mitigate PPG motion sensitivity.

entry.title: What a Reporting Convention Hides: A Matched-Budget Audit of Quantum Natural Gradient with an Exactly Computed Metric

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: This audit examines how timing conventions (only timing successful runs or evaluating at a single target) change verdicts when comparing Adam, SPSA, and quantum natural gradient optimizers. By computing the exact QNG metric and matching evaluation budgets, it shows conclusions shift substantially, with SPSA needing more than twice Adam's evaluations in pooled medians.

entry.title: Decoupled Optimization for Teacher-Student Semi-Supervised Learning via a Pioneer Student

author.name: Haorong Han, Jidong Yuan, Chixuan Wei, Yongqi Sun

entry.summary: This paper identifies two optimization pathologies in teacher-student SSL: parameter coupling forces synchronization that limits generalization intensity, and labeled/unlabeled loss imbalance drives premature convergence to labeled-dominated minima. It proposes a pioneer-student scheme that decouples teacher and student optimization to address both issues.

entry.title: Layerwise Error Attribution for Fast and Robust Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Samy Houache (IMB, UB), Yann Traonmilin (IMB, UB), Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Aujol (UB, IMB)

entry.summary: The paper derives a layerwise probabilistic analysis of quantization error separating propagated from local perturbation, yielding a separable score for fast bit-allocation under a memory budget. The method avoids combinatorial search and is robust to corrupted calibration data.

entry.title: Expected Sample Complexity in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Nadav Sukenik, Nadav Merlis

entry.summary: The paper introduces expected sample complexity for stochastic multi-armed bandits within a new framework called approximately correct in expectation (ACE), showing ACE implies almost-sure convergence to optimal expected reward and converts to expected regret bounds. It also proves deterministic algorithms cannot obtain favorable guarantees under this measure.

entry.title: Pre-training of Bayesian Optimization Algorithm through Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Satoshi Katayama, Shoyo Hunt, Shintaro Masuda, Masayuki Karasuyama

entry.summary: The authors propose tuning the internal parameters of a Bayesian optimization algorithm by running it on Gaussian process sample paths drawn from information available at the start of the run, using expected cumulative regret as the tuning objective. This meta-level application of BO to BO hyperparameters can improve performance before any real evaluations occur.

entry.title: Learned Monotone Recurrent Features in Governed Credit Scoring: The Price of the Frame and the Necessity of Macro Conditioning

author.name: Yew Lee Tan

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether learned monotone recurrent features are worth adopting inside regulated credit-scoring pipelines, using five production-scale datasets at matched admissibility and proving monotonicity guarantees for vector-valued inputs and macro-conditioned decay gates. It finds the value of learned features rises with the strictness of the governance frame.

entry.title: The Impact of Likelihood Tempering on the Limiting Predictive Moments of Variational Bayesian Linear Neural Networks

author.name: Ian Zhang, Thibault Randrianarisoa

entry.summary: The paper analyzes prior dominance in wide mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks, where the KL term collapses the predictive to the prior, and determines how fast likelihood temperature T must decrease with width M to counteract degeneracy. For one-hidden-layer linear networks it derives limiting predictive distributions under schedules T = tau/M^c.

entry.title: VM-ARRAYDPS: Virtual Microphone Augmented Diffusion Posterior Sampling for Unsupervised Blind Speech Separation

author.name: Jingqi Sun, Haozhan Tang, Shulin He, Zhong-Qiu Wang

entry.summary: Building on ArrayDPS, which formulates blind source separation as diffusion posterior sampling with a multi-channel consistency objective, this paper augments physical microphone arrays with virtual microphones for unsupervised blind speech separation. The virtual-array approach extends the applicability of diffusion-guided separation when physical arrays are limited. This improves separation quality without requiring supervised training data.

entry.title: Scalable Logistic Gaussian Process Density Regression with Kinetic Langevin Sampling

author.name: Daniel Paulin, \'Ad\'am Jung, Andr\'as A. Bencz\'ur

entry.summary: The paper develops a scalable Bayesian conditional density estimator based on logistic Gaussian processes, using a separable Matern/Fourier and Nystrom covariance structure and sampling the latent field with kinetic Langevin methods rather than Laplace or variational approximations. The posterior is strongly log-concave with bounded Hessian, enabling rigorous sampling guarantees. Applications include per-galaxy photometric redshift estimation.

entry.title: The Silhouette Operator: Identifiability of Low-Rank Measures from One-Dimensional Projections

author.name: Robert A. Vandermeulen

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops a recovery framework for low-rank signed measures on R^2 via silhouette operators that map measures to collections of one-dimensional linear pushforwards. It proves that 2k projected marginals suffice to identify any compactly supported rank-at-most-k signed measure, analogous to compressed sensing results. This is a clean mathematical contribution connecting projection-based sensing to measure theory.

entry.title: Extreme Binary Classification: Extreme Value Theory for Extreme Constraint on False Negative

author.name: Samuel Gruffaz, Muhammad Fawad, Jaakko Nevalainen

entry.summary: The paper formalizes extreme binary classification, where the false negative rate must decay faster than 1/N1 with the number of positive examples, and proposes an Extreme Value Theory-grounded threshold adaptation method plus permutation-test-based feature selection. This targets safety-critical regimes where missing positives is unacceptable. It fills a genuine gap in the classification literature.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially Dependent Data via Sequential Whitening

author.name: Ayush Baran Sen, Arkajyoti Saha

entry.summary: This paper extends split conformal prediction to spatially dependent data, where exchangeability between calibration and target errors fails. The proposed sequential whitening method conditions on calibration residuals sequentially, improving interval efficiency and stability over prior residual-based spatial approaches.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient Gait Adaptation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Locomotion Across Diverse Terrains

author.name: Ammar Issa, Anubhav Singh, Anton Tsaritsin, Sergey Kolyubin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hierarchical RL framework for quadrupedal locomotion that separates a high-frequency joint-level motion policy from a low-frequency gait-adaptation policy explicitly minimizing cost of transport. A three-stage Isaac-based training procedure enables zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across velocity ranges and terrains.

entry.title: Playing with Kruskal: algorithms for flat and hierarchical watershed cuts

author.name: Jean Cousty (LIGM), Laurent Najman (KUSTAR, LIGM), Benjamin Perret (LIGM), Deise Santana Maia (CRIStAL)

entry.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end pipeline of algorithms for computing flat and hierarchical watershed segmentations on edge-weighted graphs, from graph-based image representation through connected components of the final segmentation. It reviews the literature, covers supervised and unsupervised variants and multiple seeding strategies, and connects watersheds to minimum spanning tree optimization. It serves as a definitive algorithmic reference for watershed computation.

entry.title: Gaussian Density Splatting Network

author.name: Miao Shang, Yabin Wang, Xiaopeng Hong

entry.summary: GDSNet reformulates crowd counting by representing crowds as superpositions of continuous 2D Gaussian primitives instead of grid-based density maps that are sensitive to spatial resolution. It introduces control-point-based fitting to structure Gaussian parameter prediction and adapts a differentiable Gaussian splatting framework to the counting task. This transfers techniques from neural rendering into dense prediction.

entry.title: GraphRectify: Graph-Based Transfer of Adversarial Example Detectors Across Neural Networks

author.name: Arash Vashagh, Roozbeh Razavi-Far

entry.summary: GraphRectify is a graph-based framework enabling adversarial example detectors trained on one classifier backbone to be reused when the protected model is replaced or upgraded, overcoming incompatible internal representations. It learns a structured representation of intermediate classifier features and adapts new-backbone representations to the original detector. Evaluation spans multiple datasets, architectures, and attacks including detection of unseen perturbation types.

entry.title: PalmSpace: Towards a Versatile On-Palm Interaction Space through Unified Touch Modeling

author.name: Chentao Li, Mingze Gao, Runze Sun, Zhaoguo Wang, Jianjiang Feng, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: PalmSpace is a wrist-worn infrared sensing system that turns the bare palm into a mode-aware, body-referenced absolute input surface for smart glasses and MR devices, jointly representing contact events, regions, trajectories, and gestures without per-user calibration. It advances the goal of an always-available input surface as wearables shrink.

entry.title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback

author.name: Yu Feng, Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Haoming Liu, William Su, Jingxiang Guo, Jiankun Li, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Wen Jung Li, Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: MagCilia is a compact tactile sensor combining flexible magnetic cilia with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing, with a causal history fusion regression method to reconstruct forces from coupled magnetic channels. Validation via grouped cross-validation shows low force reconstruction errors, supporting contact perception and grasping feedback.

entry.title: Design of a Fully Actuated 4-DOF Robotic Finger With Joint-Specific Hybrid Remote Actuation

author.name: Hyojae Kang, Hyun-mok Jung, Joonho Lee, Dongil Park, Hyunmin Do, Jongwoo Park, Jeongdo Ahn

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully actuated 4-DOF robotic finger combining rigid-link transmission at the MCP joint with closed-loop wire drives and rolling-contact joints for the PIP and DIP joints, with careful wire geometry ensuring decoupled differential actuation. This addresses the common underactuation trade-off in dexterous hands.

entry.title: FlightMagNav: An Open Dataset and Probabilistic Map Learning and Validation Framework for Outdoor Magnetic Field-Based Positioning

author.name: Isaac Skog, Miguel Ramos Galrinho, Martin Gelin

entry.summary: The authors release an open UAV-collected dataset with two optically pumped quantum magnetometers and GNSS-aided inertial navigation for magnetic-field-based positioning near the Earth's surface, paired with a probabilistic framework for map learning and validation. Magnetic positioning is resilient and jam-resistant since it requires no external infrastructure.

entry.title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization

author.name: Carson Newman, Oscar Leong

entry.summary: In data-driven inverse problems, the authors study how anisotropic dilation transformations act on the direction-dependent radial summary statistic that determines the optimal regularizer within a broad Gibbs class. This enables explicit control of regularizer geometry, potentially improving optimization properties and adapting fixed base regularizers to data distributions.

entry.title: When does a network's training history predict its future learning better than its current state? Evidence from a response probe and a forecasting screen

author.name: Martin Hofmann, Patrick M\"ader

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether a network's training history predicts future learning beyond what its current state reveals, using multilayer perceptrons trained under 42 history regimes and probed at four checkpoints. A protocol with validation checks examines when history carries information that state measurements miss, connecting to plasticity loss and critical periods.

entry.title: Which Buildings Are Artificial Intelligence-Ready? A Measurement-Based Assessment Framework for AI Question Answering and Actuation

author.name: Wooyoung Jung

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework quantifying how ready a building is for agentic AI by computing answerable and actuation readiness ceilings from its knowledge graph, then measuring how much of the ceiling a reference agent realizes. On a simulated office, the agent achieves 0.62 of a 0.64 answerable ceiling, showing data gaps rather than model limitations dominate. It offers a reusable lens for assessing AI readiness in built environments.

entry.title: NL2Hull: A Natural Language-Driven Constrained Ship Design Decision Framework

author.name: Wenhua Huo, Fenglei Han, Wangyuan Zhao, Jialin Wu, Jiayi Han

entry.summary: NL2Hull connects natural-language instructions to constrained geometric ship-hull editing, formulating design changes as typed discrete decisions over NURBS-based free-form deformation with constraint checking. It introduces a Ship Design Decision Dataset of over 134,000 records and the SDDBench benchmark for evaluating language-to-geometry models. This demonstrates LLM-driven decision making in a demanding engineering domain.

entry.title: Taming an End-to-End Autonomous Driving Policy for Urban Navigation of Quadruped Robots

author.name: Joochan Kim, Chanuk Yang, Tackgeun You, Ziran Wang, Hwasup Lim

entry.summary: Presents Go2-DrivoR, a goal-conditioned adaptation of the DrivoR end-to-end driving trajectory planner for quadruped robots navigating urban sidewalks. It adds a goal token for local-frame subgoals, redefines drivable-area compliance, and trains purely in TartanGround simulation while transferring to unseen environments.

entry.title: Trustworthy Domain-Specific AI for Structured Knowledge Retrieval and Reasoning

author.name: Ryan C. Barron

entry.summary: This dissertation presents a pipeline for converting unstructured domain-specific text into structured, interpretable knowledge for retrieval and reasoning. It contributes Binary Bleed, a binary-search method that reduces complexity of low-rank NMF selection, and HNMFk, a depth-adaptive hierarchical topic-modeling method producing expert-guided interpretable taxonomies that populate a typed knowledge graph aligned with a vector store. The emphasis is on trustworthy, inspectable AI pipelines.

entry.title: Talking with Language Models

author.name: James Ravi Kirkpatrick, Alexandru Radulescu, Rachel Katharine Sterken

entry.summary: A philosophy paper proposing the artifactual stance: human-LLM interaction should be understood as artifact-mediated exchange of candidate texts rather than genuine conversation, since LLMs are text generators, not speakers with memory or commitments between turns. This reframing has implications for how we attribute meaning, responsibility, and communicative force to model outputs.

entry.title: Bounded Autonomy and Verifiable Safety for Agentic AI Enabled Automation

author.name: Srini Ramaswamy, Deveeshree Nayak

entry.summary: BRaVeS is a safety-governance framework for deploying agentic AI in high-stakes automation, addressing epistemic drift where deeper reasoning moves behavior away from expert-defined safety constraints. It encodes subject-matter-expert constraints as invariant anchors, proposes depth-aware attention (MoDA-Style) to keep anchors visible during inference, and reduces autonomy as epistemic risk rises via a state hierarchy, with Lyapunov-style bounded recovery formalized. This addresses a real deployment concern for agentic systems in industrial settings.

entry.title: SNR-Gated LSTM-Conditioned Diffusion Model for MIMO Channel Estimation

author.name: Jixing Zhou, Xinming Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a diffusion-based channel estimation framework for mobile MIMO systems that denoises in the angular domain, conditioned on LSTM-encoded temporal observations, with a learnable SNR-gated mechanism balancing measurement fidelity against learned priors across wide SNR ranges.

entry.title: An extended deep energy method for thermo-mechanical crack propagation

author.name: Han Zhang, Mehrisadat Makki Alamdari, Babak Shahbodagh, Mohammad Vahab, Cosmin Anitescu, Timon Rabczuk, Elena Atroshchenko

entry.summary: The paper extends the deep energy method to coupled thermo-mechanical fracture, using two neural networks for temperature and displacement that receive a sharp polyline crack through a discontinuous embedding function. This is the first neural energy solver to jointly treat heat conduction on cracked domains and crack growth under thermal stress.

entry.title: SoftSEEPS improves ML-based precipitation forecasting

author.name: Jost Arndt, Utku Isil, Noelia Otero, Rodrigo Almeida, Wojciech Samek, Jackie Ma

entry.summary: SoftSEEPS is a differentiable approximation of the SEEPS precipitation verification score, enabling direct training of ML models to forecast precipitation. Tested on IMERG data with a decoder on a pretrained forecast model's latent space, it combines with RMSE in a joint objective with only marginal trade-offs.

entry.title: What Can a Gaussian Process Design Test

author.name: Ivan De Boi, Marnix Van Soom

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes which model mis-specifications a Gaussian process design can even detect before responses are observed, showing that for finitely featured GPs the implied constraints on noiseless responses are exactly the null space of the kernel matrix, with a geometric interpretation via Gale duality circuits.

entry.title: Task-Sufficient Contraction: Source Selection for Machine Information Interfaces

author.name: Joss Armstrong

entry.summary: This paper introduces Task-Sufficient Contraction, a property determining when a task can certify a reduced source of information that preserves the complete downstream problem family before an encoder or rate target is chosen. For machines with fixed actions and loss, it identifies consumer-specific sources by merging states with equal regret across all actions.

entry.title: Adjoint-Based Calibration and Optimal Control of Stochastic Multiscale Bioprocess Digital Twins

author.name: Keilung Choy, Wei Xie

entry.summary: This work develops a bias-aware digital-twin calibration and control framework for multiscale bioprocess models, representing the twin as a stochastic differential equation calibrated from sparse observations via quasi-likelihood estimation and adjoint sensitivity analysis. It quantifies how calibration uncertainty propagates to policy performance, enabling adaptive experimental design and uncertainty-aware control. The framework targets biomanufacturing applications.

entry.title: NAViLoss: An Underwater Navigation-Aware Dual-Residual Objective for Physics-Consistent Learning

author.name: Arup Kumar Sahoo, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: NAViLoss is a dual-residual loss for learning Doppler velocity log (DVL) velocity estimation on autonomous underwater vehicles, incorporating physical consistency and measurement uncertainty rather than plain regression. It targets robustness under degraded sensing conditions common underwater. This improves the reliability of learned navigation components in a safety-relevant robotics domain.

entry.title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow

author.name: Sandy Adhitia Ekahana, Aalok Tiwari, Pratik Saud, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Eli Rotenberg, Jyoti Katoch

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive review of machine learning applications across the angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) workflow, from automated sample preparation and real-time data acquisition to post-experiment analysis and comparison with theory. The authors survey ML methods relevant to experimental science and assess their capabilities and reliability at each workflow stage.

entry.title: Measurement-Efficient Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search for Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Lukas Thei{\ss}inger, Thore Gerlach, Christian Bauckhage

entry.summary: The authors show that for a broad class of combinatorial optimization problems and common rotational gate parameterizations, the measurement cost of differentiable quantum architecture search can be substantially reduced without changing the optimization objective. They derive the reduction theoretically and validate it on 3-SAT and MaxCut benchmarks.

entry.title: InterView-C: A Synchronized Multimodal Corpus of VR Avatar-Mediated Survey Interviews

author.name: Patrick Schrottenbacher, Leon Hammerla, Lydia Kleine, Doris Stingl, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: InterView-C is a German multimodal corpus of 27 VR-based survey interviews with avatar-mediated participants, aligning speech with synchronized gaze, head, body, facial, and hand tracking data. Reference transcripts and linguistic annotations provide a bridge between multimodal spoken interaction and text-based NLP methods.

entry.title: Anaximander: Interactively Running Geospatial Deep Learning Models on Any Compute Backend

author.name: Satej S. Soman, Akram Zaytar, Girmaw A. Tadesse, Gilles Q. Hacheme, Muhammad S. Danish, Inbal Becker-Reshef, Rahul Dodhia, Juan Lavista Ferres

entry.summary: Anaximander is an open-source system that lets remote sensing practitioners run geospatial deep learning models from within GIS software across heterogeneous compute backends, unifying model deployment, tiling, and georeferencing behind one interactive interface. It aims to reduce the friction that discourages systematic model comparison in operational domains like crop monitoring and disaster response.

entry.title: Beyond Group Splits: Specimen-Level Cross-Validation and Visual Attribution for Remaining-Shelf-Life Regression in Climacteric Fruit

author.name: Rovhona Mudau, Jean Frederic Isingizwe Nturambirwe, Clement Nthambazale Nyirenda

entry.summary: Using the Hass avocado ripening dataset, this paper quantifies how observation-level versus specimen-disjoint evaluation protocols substantially change reported performance for image-based shelf-life regression. It compares lightweight and heavier pretrained backbones under specimen-disjoint cross-validation and inspects their spatial attributions with Grad-CAM.

entry.title: MSU Team at the Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge 2026: Grounded Artifact Evidence for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Artem Filippov, Aleksandr Gushchin, Kirill Koltsov, Dmitriy Vatolin, Anastasia Antsiferova

entry.summary: This is the MSU team solution to the Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge 2026 on the XPlainVerse dataset, combining a multi-backbone real/fake detector built from several DINOv3 models with Mesorch manipulation-localization features. It generates both complex and simple explanations grounded in visible forensic cues via a modular detection-and-explanation design. It matters as a documented competitive system for explainable deepfake detection.

entry.title: Context-Aware Adaptive Pesticide Spraying for Agricultural Robots under Changing Weather and Terrain Using Vision-Language Models

author.name: Cong-Thanh Vu, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a VLM-based framework for precision pesticide spraying that dynamically adjusts spray parameters using environmental context (temperature, wind), crop characteristics, and pesticide type, mimicking human operator decision-making rather than relying on fixed parameters. This targets more efficient and uniform chemical application in agricultural robotics.

entry.title: Embedded Evaluation of Task Admission Coalescing in Decentralized Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: James Lott, Vahraz Honary

entry.summary: The paper evaluates task-admission coalescing as a way to bound allocator computation in decentralized multi-robot task allocation, comparing eager admission with batching thresholds using CBAA, ACBBA, PI, and HIPC. Experiments span 3,000-mission campaigns on AGX Orin hardware plus hardware-in-the-loop tests on a small embedded robot, quantifying the compute-latency trade-off.

entry.title: Finite-Rank Logistic Gaussian Processes with Exact Likelihood for Conditional Density Estimation

author.name: Jaehoan Kim, Indrajit Ghosh, Debdeep Pati, Dipankar Bandyopadhyay

entry.summary: The paper proposes ExFR-LGP, a finite-rank logistic Gaussian process prior structured so the log density splits into two bivariate functions, making the normally intractable LGP normalizing constant computable exactly via piecewise-linear finite-rank GPs on a grid. This enables exact-likelihood conditional density estimation useful in imaging studies.

entry.title: Evidence suggests RSI may decelerate

author.name: Eugene Earnshaw

entry.summary: The post argues quantitatively that recursive self-improvement need not produce exponential or super-exponential capability growth: improvement accelerates only if optimization power gains outpace the growing difficulty (recalcitrance) of the optimization problem, and evidence suggests difficulty may win, yielding decelerating improvement. This challenges singularity-style forecasts underlying some AI risk timelines.

entry.title: AI Doom: a Brief Critical Review

author.name: Paul Shearer

entry.summary: A critical review essay arguing that while AI extinction forecasts may be epistemically informative, they are not practical guides to action, since knowing a risk exists does not yield a workable roadmap. The author contends that AI development could reduce net existential risk by helping address other 21st-century catastrophes (climate, bio, geopolitical), and that indefinite pausing could deprive humanity of needed tools. It engages with an increasingly influential recent argument within the AI risk community.

entry.title: CircuitGate: Logic-Consistent Circuit-Level Functional Modeling for And-Inverter Graphs

author.name: Qifan Zhang, Ruijie Li, Fangzhou Zhang, Qian Ma, Hui Li, Furui Zhan, Yongpeng Wang, Liying Hao, Shikai Guo

entry.summary: CircuitGate is a function-aware representation learning framework for And-Inverter Graphs in EDA, moving beyond local gate-level GNN message passing to capture circuit-level functional dependencies and remain robust to functionality-preserving transformations.

entry.title: PairAudit: Guiding Human Review with Graph Tokens under Distribution Shift

author.name: Jiran Tao, Binyan Jiang

entry.summary: PairAudit helps human reviewers of intrusion detectors find confident misclassifications of unseen attacks under a fixed review budget, using graph tokens that capture unusual relational prediction patterns across connected nodes rather than uncertainty or anomaly scores alone. Human feedback then determines whether review priorities should change.

entry.title: Pareto-optimal quantum kernel selection for unsupervised anomaly detection on real malware beaconing data

author.name: Boaz Micah, Nadia Milazzo, Maissa Beji, Borja Aizpurua, Lloren\c{c} Espinosa-Portal\'es, Esteban Payares, Ghada Ben Slama, Luc Andrea, Michel Kurek, Thomas Cope, Olivier Salomon

entry.summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised multi-objective protocol for quantum kernel selection that jointly optimizes anomaly detection quality via a label-free proxy and geometric difference from tuned classical kernels, selecting from a Pareto front. It is applied to malware beaconing detection in real network traffic with one-class SVMs. This is a careful attempt to assess whether quantum kernels offer anything classical kernels cannot.

entry.title: Nobody Truly Agrees on Sentiment: Humans, Bespoke Tools, and LLMs Struggle with Social Media Texts

author.name: Himarsha R. Jayanetti, Sivakanesan Dhanushkanda, Shuai Hao, Michael L. Nelson, Michele C. Weigle

entry.summary: This study measures inter-rater reliability of three sentiment tools (TextBlob, VADER, Twitter-roBERTa) and three LLMs (Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama-4-Maverick-17B) against six human raters on 100 tweets. Even human raters showed only fair agreement, underscoring the subjectivity of sentiment annotation and limits of treating sentiment labels as ground truth.

entry.title: From High Recall to High Utility: Dataset-Adaptive Post-Processing of LLM-Generated Customer Intents

author.name: Mahesh Viswanathan, Joan Rossello, Leticia Fernandes, Paul Mutawe
