entry.summary: Proposes PFaithBench, a pairwise faithfulness benchmark testing whether LLMs appropriately switch between answering and abstaining on the same question as context sufficiency changes. This context-sensitive evaluation exposes failures of instance-level faithfulness assessments and is relevant to hallucination and abstention research.

entry.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight

author.name: Haoxiang Zhang, Qinglin Chen, Hiroaki Hayashi, Zhuofeng Li, Siming Zhang, Jiaxin Zhang, Jixuan Chen, Fang Wu, Pan Lu, Silvio Savarese, Julian McAuley, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Introduces prospective learning and Self-Retrospection Distillation (SRD), which uses completed trajectories as hindsight supervision for foresight predictions made before interaction, extracting learning signal even when all rollouts receive identical rewards in RLVR. This complements scalar outcome rewards by teaching agents what they could have anticipated.

entry.title: Knowing When Not to Answer: Cross-Domain and Multi-Turn Generalization of Latent Underspecification Signals

author.name: Jerzy Kami\'nski, Ilya Galyukshev, Artem Kuznetsov, Danil Fedorov, Kirill Redko, Sergey Chuprin, Aidar Shumbalov, Stanislav Chumakov, Anna Kalyuzhnaya

entry.summary: The paper probes when LLMs can detect that a question is unanswerable given available information, contributing a turn-labeled multi-turn benchmark (423 conversations, 1,661 turn-states) with a simulated user who answers clarifying questions. Using six datasets and six open-weight LLMs, it shows unanswerability probes transfer robustly across datasets sharing a common source of unanswerability (AUROC 0.77-0.97 in math and passage domains).

entry.title: Capacity, Responsiveness and Alignment: What Makes a Latent Structure Actionable

author.name: Or Shafran, Mor Geva

entry.summary: This paper asks why some latent structures localized in LM activation space are causally actionable while others are not, decomposing causal influence into three interpretable factors: capacity (output sensitivity along the structure), responsiveness (context-dependent promotability), and alignment (fit to the context-specific concept representation). Experiments across four LM families and 50 concepts support the decomposition. The framework helps predict when steering interventions will actually work.

entry.title: VisionWeave: Weaving Elastic Visual Representations as a Native Capability of MLLMs

author.name: Yuan Feng, Qize Yang, Ruizhe Chen, Sibo Song, Haolin He, Muzhi Zhu, Zihan Liu, Yunfei Chu, Xize Cheng, Yuxuan Wang, Jin Xu, Xike Xie

entry.summary: VisionWeave trains multimodal LLMs end to end to decide where and at what granularity to allocate visual representations, learning elastic visual token allocation natively rather than relying on fixed dense patch tokens or post-hoc pruning. This targets the cost-quality tradeoff in multimodal encoding, allowing fine-grained detail where needed and compact representations elsewhere. It matters for efficient, content-adaptive multimodal inference and serving.

entry.title: UniPro: Unified Multi-Mode Medical Image Segmentation from 2D Images to 3D Volumes via Propagation

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Yunhe Gao, Meng Ye, Yang Zhou, Difei Gu, Guoning Zhang, Leon Axel, Dimitris Metaxas

entry.summary: UniPro unifies semantic, in-context, and interactive medical image segmentation across 2D images and 3D volumes, using 2D refinement that propagates coherently through volumetric scans regardless of how a case is initialized. This addresses the fragmentation of clinical segmentation workflows along paradigm and dimensionality axes.

entry.title: Semantic Capability Acquisition and Specialization During Vision-Language Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Suguru Onda, Matthew Bailey, Ryan Farrell

entry.summary: This paper studies the dynamics of how semantic capabilities emerge, peak, and decline during VLM fine-tuning, rather than evaluating a single final checkpoint. It proposes a trajectory-based framework separating capability acquisition, capability-specific optima, and specialization, plus Structured Semantic Routing to examine how supervision representation shapes acquisition across six pretrained backbones. The findings inform when and how fine-tuning destroys or preserves capabilities.

entry.title: From the Drosophila Visual Connectome to General-Purpose Computer Vision

author.name: Zongyu Li, Akito Yamauchi, Huaizhi Liu, Vishwanatha Rao, Jia Guo, for the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative

entry.summary: ConnectomeX/FlyVision is a trainable architecture derived from the Drosophila visual connectome, preserving ON/OFF parallel pathways, recurrence, and graph interaction while scaling to general vision tasks. It reaches competitive-but-lower accuracy than ResNet18 on ImageNet with roughly a third of the parameters, suggesting biological connectomes provide transferable inductive biases.

entry.title: ALIVE: Interaction-Aligned Object Insertion for First-Frame-Guided Video Editing

author.name: Zhenghong Zhou, Zhe Lin, Jiebo Luo, Yuqian Zhou

entry.summary: ALIVE is a video editing framework that makes inserted objects participate coherently in interactions (e.g., being picked up or manipulated) using an edited first frame and an instruction naming only the added object. It curates 35,800 editing pairs across 3D-rendered, model-generated, and real videos, and trains a VLM to predict interaction guidance from the same inputs.

entry.title: UltraDiff: Differentiable Ray Tracing in Ultrasound for Shape Optimization

author.name: Felix Duelmer, Magdalena Wysocki, Nassir Navab, Mohammad Farid Azampour

entry.summary: UltraDiff extends differentiable rendering to medical ultrasound by formulating image formation as a path-space integral gated by travel time, with Monte Carlo estimators of both the forward model and its gradients. This enables gradient-based inverse geometry optimization from ultrasound measurements, analogous to differentiable light transport.

entry.title: SWAP: Stepwise Action Policy Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mousumi Das, Aditeya Prajapati, Abrar Anwar, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: SWAP dynamically composes multiple VLA policies during robot task execution by formulating policy routing as an offline reinforcement learning problem, learning a routing critic that selects the most appropriate policy at each decision step given the current observation. It is evaluated on real-world DROID manipulation tasks and LIBERO, showing that per-step routing outperforms committing to a single VLA for an episode.

entry.title: TacZero: Training-Free Peg Insertion Using a General-Purpose Vision-Language Model with Tactile Feedback

author.name: Kazutoshi Tanaka

entry.summary: TacZero uses a pretrained general-purpose VLM to interpret combined visual and tactile observations and select actions for contact-rich peg insertion without task-specific training or hand-designed control laws. This enables zero-shot contact-rich manipulation via language-conditioned multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Model-Based Geometry-Aware Generative Optimization for Constrained Locomotion Planning

author.name: Zhilin He, Xinyuan Wang, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: The paper extends Model-Based Diffusion for constrained locomotion planning of quadrupeds and humanoids by introducing task-modulated active constraint geometry that shapes score directions during sampling. This addresses collision avoidance, contact consistency, kinematic feasibility, and support constraints in high-dimensional, non-convex environments without requiring demonstrations.

entry.title: UWB Meets Crazyflow: Simulating Degraded Feedback at Scale for Aerial Robotics

author.name: Martin Schuck, Marcel P. Rath, Yufei Hua, Abhishek Goudar, SiQi Zhou, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: The paper introduces Crazyflow, a differentiable multirotor simulator built on JAX that unifies physics and control in a single compilable computation graph, achieving massive parallelization and order-of-magnitude speedups over existing baselines — enough to train deployable RL agents in seconds. The authors extend it with a high-fidelity UWB and IMU simulation pipeline coupled with a full-state Extended Kalman Filter, enabling research on degraded state estimation. This allows large-scale study of aerial robotics under realistic sensing imperfections.

entry.title: MIM-VLA: Learning Physical Interaction Representations from Gripper Motor Feedback

author.name: Jaeyoung Lee, Jiyeon Koo, Taehwa Kim, Yerin Cha, Andrew Jaeyong Choi

entry.summary: MIM-VLA augments vision-language-action policies with gripper motor feedback (current, position, velocity) encoded as a 128-dimensional interaction token by a pretrained Motor Interaction Module, conditioning only the gripper-action pathway of SmolVLA. A companion selector VLM uses the same token to compare candidate interactions and provide evidence-conditioned explanations of physical contact states.

entry.title: One for All, All for One: Coordinated Multi-Agent Diffusion Steering via Stochastic Optimal Control

author.name: Riccardo Barbano, Vincent Pauline, Runchang Li, George Webber, Alexander Denker, \v{Z}eljko Kereta, Stefan Bauer, Francisco Vargas, Esmeralda S. Whitammer

entry.summary: CMDS treats frozen pretrained diffusion models as reusable generative primitives and coordinates their reverse processes through a learned control policy formulated as a stochastic optimal control problem. This modular approach learns only inter-component coordination rather than retraining a monolithic model to produce structured outputs.

entry.title: One-Shot Private Confidence Regions via Resampling

author.name: Shourya Pandey, Purnamrita Sarkar, Po-Ling Loh, Debepsita Mukherjee

entry.summary: The authors propose a one-shot framework for differentially private confidence regions that adds noise only to the final resampling quantile rather than privatizing each resample estimate. Privacy cost drops to logarithmic in the number of resamples under with-replacement sampling and is independent of it under subsampling, with nonasymptotic Gaussian DP and utility guarantees.

entry.title: VideoResearchAgent: Grounded Task Synthesis and Sim-to-Real RL for Open-Web Video Research

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Fei Li, Yuxi Wu, Bin Zhu, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: VideoResearchAgent tackles open-web video research, where an agent must autonomously discover relevant videos, navigate their temporal content, and ground answers in visual evidence, going beyond text-centric deep research agents. It introduces a controllable task-synthesis pipeline and sim-to-real reinforcement learning to bridge the gap between local simulation and live web interaction. This extends the deep-research-agent paradigm to the video modality, a largely unexplored area.

entry.title: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry

author.name: Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Yan Chen, Pol Llado, Scott Counts, Mohit Bansal, Benjamin Van Durme, Harsh Jhamtani, Gaurav Verma

entry.summary: TeleTune learns a reusable textual skill library for computer-use agents from offline user telemetry, addressing goal underspecification, non-replayability, and interleaved trajectories in logs. It uses action-prediction errors on logged trajectories to evolve skills without recorded goals or the ability to replay past activity, with credible authorship spanning JHU and Meta-affiliated researchers.

entry.title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories

author.name: Jin Jiang, Sean Yates, Jasper Chong, Raymond Brooks, Alex Lawson, Yuqin Qin, Liangcai Gao

entry.summary: The authors introduce LifeLong Digital Twin, an event-driven paradigm that organizes health events into daily health states accumulated into a lifelong health context, with an agent harness for incorporating multimodal evidence beyond textual context. They evaluate four language models across 25 diseases on whole-person health trajectory modeling.

entry.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries

author.name: Chonghe Jiang, Ao Qu, Siyuan Liu, Ruoyun Ma, Zijian Zhou, Dingyi Zhuang, Bo Liu, Han Zheng, Hanfei Yu, Baichuan Mo, Jinhua Zhao, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: The paper improves test-time training for open-ended scientific discovery by training a small auxiliary model in a latent thought space rather than repeatedly fine-tuning a large solution-generating LLM from verifier feedback. This reduces the cost of maintaining gradients and optimizer states while improving credit assignment between high-level strategy and low-level code.

entry.title: DGA-Muon: Decoupled Geometry-Aligned Adaptive Scaling for Muon

author.name: Wenpeng Zhang, Runsheng Yu

entry.summary: The paper provides the first systematic analysis of NorMuon's adaptivity, showing its adaptive scaling stems mostly from orthogonalization-induced geometry rather than genuine optimization-relevant information, and proposes DGA-Muon, a decoupled geometry-aligned adaptive scaling variant of the Muon optimizer. The analysis explains degenerate behavior for square/wide matrices and row-energy-driven variation for tall matrices.

entry.title: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Mingtian Tan, Palash Goyal, Mihir Parmar, Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das, Chun-Liang Li, Nanyun Peng, Thomas Hartvigsen, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: SEER is a closed-loop framework that dynamically optimizes event conditioning for time series forecasting, addressing the fact that real-world series are driven by exogenous events and structural shifts that pure numerical forecasting misses. It translates prediction errors into two feedback mechanisms: a reflective retrieval memory that refines search queries and filters noise, and a persistent causal knowledge component for reasoning about event impacts. This improves on standard retrieval-augmented forecasting that struggles with noisy news signals.

entry.title: How Does Geometry Enter Generated Motion?

author.name: Weihan Li, Junhao Wu, Yuhan Song, Xiaofeng Lin, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: This controlled study probes nine image-to-video generators by fixing the physical law and initial state while changing only first-frame geometry within matched track and deflector families, comparing generated trajectories against simulator predictions. Geometry is preserved and shapes motion, but the generated motion parts from physical state carrying, revealing where video models diverge from physics.

entry.title: When Are Concept Bottleneck Model Explanations Faithful and Compact?

author.name: Stefano Teso, Emanuele Marconato, Steve Azzolin, Antonio Vergari

entry.summary: This paper applies formal explainability to concept bottleneck models, showing that for widespread CBM architectures including recent VLM-based variants, faithful explanations must include all bottleneck concepts, undermining interpretability when the concept set is large. The negative result applies to both heuristic and faithful-by-construction explanations. The authors propose remedies, such as modeling concepts that encourage compact faithful explanations.

entry.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution

author.name: Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Seyedarmin Azizi, Arya Fayyazi, Saeid Shokoufa, Mehdi Kamal, Souvik Kundu, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The paper shows that instead of sampling many scored candidates at inference to sharpen a language model's output distribution, a model can be trained to generate directly from its sharpened power distribution in one pass. On-policy power distillation (OPPD) uses a sequential Monte Carlo sampler in which the trained model generates candidates weighted by a frozen teacher's power distribution. This improves reasoning at test time without parameter changes at inference or expensive candidate search.

entry.title: Have I Seen Enough? Frozen Video-Language Models Encode Evidence Readiness

author.name: Dan Ben-Ami, Kobi Cohen, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: The authors show that frozen video-language models already contain a linearly readable evidence-readiness signal - whether sufficient evidence for the current question has arrived in a stream - labeled from timestamped evidence rather than model outputs. The signal decodes across seven models (AUROC 0.733-0.905 under strict sampling), transfers across benchmark families, and is question-conditioned, suggesting streaming systems could exploit this latent signal without additional training.

entry.title: STRUCTURALCOST: A controlled reading time dataset for modeling human sentence processing difficulty

author.name: Nina Nusbaumer, Iria de-Dios-Flores, Corentin Bel, Christophe Pallier, Guillaume Wisniewski, Beno\^it Crabb\'e

entry.summary: STRUCTURALCOST is a self-paced reading dataset (475 participants, 40,800 observations) isolating the processing cost of long-distance subject-verb dependency resolution, replicating a low-powered psycholinguistic finding at NLP scale. Language models spanning n-grams, SSMs, and transformers partially mirror human reading-time patterns but systematically underestimate integration costs, suggesting they capture predictive but not full integrative processing.

entry.title: CALR: Continuous Anchored Latent Reasoning via Render-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Zhaoyang Wei, Bowen Jiang, Yanchao Hao, Wenchao Ding, Zheng Wei, Shaocheng Wu, Zhenjun Han, Jianbin Jiao

entry.summary: CALR analyzes failure modes of existing continuous and discrete visual latent reasoning systems—where continuous latents answer despite collapsed reasoning and discrete latents carry recoverable reasoning that answer prediction bypasses—and proposes continuous anchored latent reasoning with render-of-thought compression requiring latents to carry valid problem-specific reasoning. This reduces textual reasoning overhead while preserving verifiable intermediate steps.

entry.title: 4D-HOF: Hand-Object Flow Matching for Feed-Forward 4D Interaction Reconstruction

author.name: Shiqi Li, Sean Cho, Yijie Li, Fengzhi Guo, Bowen Wen, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: 4D-HOF reconstructs 4D hand-object interactions feed-forward by learning a conditional flow matching model that transports foundation-model-derived hand-object states toward an interaction manifold. This corrects errors in translation, rotation, and alignment without costly per-sequence optimization, and the generative formulation enables test-time guidance.

entry.title: ACG-WAM: World-Action Modeling via Action-Conditioned Geometric Latent Prediction

author.name: Jiangtao Liu, Zishang Xiang, Yage He, Lingguo Cui, Baihai Zhang, Runqi Chai, Senchun Chai

entry.summary: ACG-WAM augments world-action models with an auxiliary JEPA-style objective, ACG-JEPA, that predicts geometric features at multiple horizons from current observations and intervening actions, using frozen VGGT encodings to avoid temporal-attention leakage of future information. This gives world-action models an explicit target for the geometric consequences of actions, which video and action losses lack.

entry.title: IronMan: Information-Constrained Video-Action Learning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuanshuo Zhang, Wenzhe Zhao, Zixing Lei, Bin Chen, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: IronMan applies the information bottleneck principle to video action models, suppressing irrelevant visual detail while preserving action-relevant dynamics cues through a dynamics-aware bottleneck that distills video features into compact representations. This addresses the insight that excessive visual detail in video representations can impair action-policy generalization.

entry.title: Teaching Agents to Code Reliably

author.name: Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Myeongsoo Kim, Kangrui Ruan, Shweta Garg, Varun Kumar, Murali Krishna Ramanathan

entry.summary: The paper argues that reliable autonomous coding agents need three teachable behaviors baked into the policy rather than the scaffold: location diversity (avoiding revisiting the same faulty site), edit diversity (exploiting complementary fix methodologies), and trustworthy verification (since self-written tests accept many incorrect patches). It proposes training approaches to internalize these behaviors and direct search by executable evidence.

entry.title: TCMClinicalReason-Bench: Can Language Models Reason from Pathogenesis to Prescription over Real-World Clinical Cases?

author.name: Jirui Dai, Chenkai Zhang, Yan Jia, Yukai Wang, Ruiyang He, Changyong Luo, Zhi Liu

entry.summary: This benchmark uses 2,000 multicenter electronic health record cases from traditional Chinese medicine to test whether LLMs produce case-grounded diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning rather than fluent but unsupported conclusions, with an evidence-constrained rubric across seven components and three cross-block relations. Seven models, including Qwen3.7-Plus (an existing mid-2026 model), were evaluated zero-shot.

entry.title: AgentPersonaBench: Benchmarking Persona-Driven User Simulation

author.name: Jintao Huang, Yifan Wang, Hongyu Shen, Yi Daniel Lu, Shirley Huang, Minsik Oh, Yewen Wang, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Zhen Xu, Yilan Fan, Zichen Yuan, Ahsan Bilal, Zibu Wei, Sankalp Jajee, Henry Gagnier, Saksham Kapoor, Jicheng Wang, Qianfeng Wen, Yixuan He, Steven Dillmann, Jiashu He, Yucheng Lu, Linqiang Guo, Danyang Zhang, Shi Bo, Raunak Mondal, Haixiang Tang, Weihang Xiao, Allen Nie, Jing Tang, Yueying Li, Yifan Simon Liu, Jianheng Hou, Dianzhuo Wang, Qianyu Zhu, Zhixu Silvia Tao, Zhejian Peng, Zihan Wang, Ishan Gupta, Jinxuan Fan, Wanting Jiang, Shushu Liang, Chenxi Qiu, Yijun Wang, Xiaomin Li, Yuexing Hao

entry.summary: Introduces AgentPersonaBench (APB), a benchmark that tests whether persona conditioning genuinely steers agent behavior rather than just conversational styling. It verifies trait adherence from observable actions across four increasingly realistic interaction surfaces (survey, chat, web, app), embedding target traits in full synthetic profiles without disclosing the test. This addresses a real gap, since prior benchmarks rely on self-reports.

entry.title: Not Self-Decidable: LLMs Cannot Draw the Boundary of What an Agent Verifier Can Check

author.name: Anthony Rhodes

entry.summary: The paper challenges the assumption underlying escalation schemes that a model can itself decide which regulatory rules a fixed check can settle versus which require a judge. Across six corpora including the EU AI Act, FINRA guidance, and a deployed credit agent, with roughly 22,000 labels from four models built by three labs, models agree where answers are obvious but collapse on boundary cases, showing the split is not self-decidable.

entry.title: DICE: Decoupling Capability from Intervention Necessity in LLM Tutoring

author.name: Sayantan Pal, Kaiyi Ji, Rohini K. Srihari

entry.summary: This paper introduces DICE, a framework that separates whether an LLM tutor should intervene at all from what it should say, using an explicit pedagogical action selection step. It defines Intervention Value, a rollout-grounded counterfactual metric comparing each potential intervention against doing nothing, and finds many conventional tutor interventions offer little marginal benefit. This matters because it challenges the default assumption that every student turn requires a response, pointing toward more effective AI tutoring systems.

entry.title: When Agent Context Goes Stale: Incoherence in Volatile Agent Context

author.name: Yingying Liu, Junzhou Fang, Chenxiong Qian

entry.summary: The paper addresses the problem of stale tool observations in agent contexts, where underlying data sources change after observation but agents continue reasoning over outdated content. It introduces Concord, a framework that links each observation to its mutable source and maintains coherence between agent context and the current state of external data.

entry.title: CodeForge-MA: Execution-Verified Multi-Agent Learning with Language-Conditioned LoRA for Multilingual Code Generation

author.name: Zhizhou Gu, Xianting Wu, Siyu Gu, Tian Zhang, Kejian Tong

entry.summary: CodeForge-MA is a pipeline in which four specialized agents iteratively generate, review, execute-test, and curate instruction-code pairs, then trains models with masked supervised fine-tuning plus a test-driven reinforcement objective. It uses language-conditioned mixtures of LoRA adapters to cover many programming languages while keeping the backbone frozen and filtering benchmark leakage.

entry.title: Have I Scene This Before? Spatially Grounded Conversational Memory for Complex Queries in Egocentric Assistants

author.name: Jiazhou Liang, Liam Gallagher, Kiko Chen, David Guo, Armin Toroghi, Yifan Simon Liu, Scott Sanner

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Spatially grounded Conversational Reasoning (SpaCR) for egocentric assistants, covering cross-scene recall and counterfactual spatial queries over long interaction histories. It proposes SpaC-MEM, an object-centric working memory that uses 3D reconstruction and segmentation to compress multimodal histories into persistent physical objects, reducing inference costs compared to raw vision-language model context.

entry.title: From Token-Max to Outcome-Max: How You Use AI Determines Its Productivity

author.name: Chen Xu, Mengqiao Liu, Beibei Li, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: This paper identifies token-max behavior — treating token consumption as productive effort — as a source of AI-driven productivity losses, and proposes outcome-max, which rewards independently verified task completion per unit cost with a principled stopping rule. A three-level simulation framework covering immediate interaction, long-run behavioral adaptation, and organizational collaboration shows outcome-max consistently improves efficiency. The work connects incentive design to real AI productivity outcomes.

entry.title: Measurement-First Auditing of Agentic Leaderboards: Contamination Susceptibility, Matched-Control Re-evaluation, and Scorer Validation

author.name: Dishu Yang, Qi Su, Hongbo Qin, Hansong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a measurement-first audit framework for agentic leaderboards that separates contamination claims into training-time exposure, evaluation-time retrieval, and pipeline leakage channels, each coded under a fail-closed rule. Audits across nine Holistic Agent Leaderboard configurations found confirmed contamination incidents in four, and the framework includes matched-control re-evaluation and scorer validation.

entry.title: ANT: A Multi-Granularity Network Traffic Dataset and Benchmark for Agents Behavior Auditing

author.name: Fan Li, Xiangyu Gao, Zixuan Liu, Tong Li, Chuanpu Fu, Ziqiang Wang, Ke Xu

entry.summary: ANT is a dataset and benchmark for auditing LLM agent behavior through network traffic without inspecting private user content, providing agent behavior annotations at risk, scenario, and behavior-primitive granularities. It contains 3,114 execution episodes across 20 tasks and five scenarios, with over 276,000 bidirectional flows and 40,000 behavior segments.

entry.title: Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification

author.name: Je Yang, Ivan Lobov, Thomas Karpati

entry.summary: The paper surveys the gap between LLM applications in chip design and the underserved post-simulation verification stage, noting that about 74.6 percent of studies target static RTL code generation. It introduces BTTF, an end-to-end agentic framework that distills large simulation dumps into a normalized SQLite relational database and couples it with a collaborative multi-agent system for interactive waveform debugging.

entry.title: BridgeCast: Bridging Ocean Wave Forecasts to Reanalysis via Flow Matching with Exogenous Variables

author.name: Siyu Gan, Dongsheng Luo, Kunxiaojia Yuan, Dongjin Song, Jingchao Ni

entry.summary: BridgeCast is a physics-AI hybrid framework that corrects systematic biases in physics-based ocean wave forecasts using conditional flow matching. It treats physical model forecasts as corrupted observations and learns a generative transformation that bridges their distribution toward reanalysis-like fields, incorporating exogenous variables. This improves probabilistic ocean wave prediction relevant to maritime safety and coastal resilience.

entry.title: AEGIS: Differentiable Mars Climate Model with Neural Closures

author.name: Sameera S Kashyap, Victor Cruz, Angel Yepez, Razvan Marinescu

entry.summary: AEGIS is a differentiable general circulation model for the Martian atmosphere that replaces or augments components of legacy Fortran GCMs with neural closures. Differentiability enables gradient-based data assimilation and learning despite sparse observations, a thin CO2 atmosphere, and a radiatively active dust cycle that make Mars uniquely hard to model. Reliable Mars weather forecasting is mission-critical for entry, descent, and landing operations.

entry.title: Risk-Calibrated Proposal Transport for Finite-Particle Diffusion Steering

author.name: Ziseok Lee, Jaehyeon Kim, Seungwon Kim, Seunghyun Moon, Haneul Choi, Wooyeol Lee, Donghyun Koh, Minhyeong Lee, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: This paper analyzes a failure mode of variance-controlling guidance in finite-particle inference-time steering of diffusion models: the fitted drift correction can nearly eliminate fitting residual while increasing residual risk on new states by orders of magnitude, degrading generation or accelerating particle collapse. The authors propose a risk-calibrated proposal transport method to mitigate this. The work targets combining pretrained diffusion experts or reward models without retraining via Feynman-Kac corrected sequential Monte Carlo.

entry.title: First-Order Steering: Translating Weight Adaptation into Activation Steering

author.name: Sri Pranav Kunda, Alexander Kurz, Tomas Dominik, Uri Maoz

entry.summary: The paper introduces First-Order Steering, a method that converts learned weight adaptations (as in model merging) into activation steering vectors, enabling composable steering vectors for simultaneous inference-time behavioral control. Since model merging composes behaviors with high accuracy but standard activation steering does not, this bridges the two paradigms. The approach is motivated by applications in AI alignment and safety.

entry.title: Understanding Clustering in Slot Attention via Particle Dynamics

author.name: Vasudev Joy, Rajat Rasal, Avinash Kori, Anthea Monod, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Introduces simplified slot attention (SSA), a parameter-free variant whose dynamics connect to soft k-means clustering, offering a mechanistic explanation of how object-centric representations emerge from attention dynamics. On Pascal VOC, SSA matches standard slot attention performance. The result shows that competitive object-centric segmentation can arise from intrinsic clustering dynamics rather than learned components.

entry.title: More Value per Key: Asymmetric Sparse Attention for Faster LLM Decoding

author.name: Noam Elata, Itay Lamprecht, Mikey Shechter, Daniel Ohayon, Itay Hubara, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: The authors observe that sparse attention shifts LLM decoding bottleneck toward the query-key step, making probability-value multiplication negligible and allowing fewer key heads while retaining more value heads. They propose SAGA (Sparse Asymmetric Group-Query Attention), which decouples key and value head counts, paired with Atop-N approximate sparse attention for faster inference. The approach offers a practical efficiency lever for autoregressive LLM serving.

entry.title: SparseCraft: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Optimization for Sparse Computing

author.name: Rajatabha Chakraborty, M P Samartha, Vedant Pahariya, Priyesh Shukla

entry.summary: SparseCraft places an LLM in a closed 15-iteration loop that edits Chisel RTL, memory configurations, and sparse-kernel schedules of a Gemmini accelerator via MCP tool servers, with each candidate validated through legality checks, cycle-accurate simulation, bit-exact golden-reference comparison, and synthesis. Measurements feed the next work order as diagnosed bottlenecks.

entry.title: Characterizing Parallelism Strategies in LLM Inference: Fundamental Compute-Communication Trade-offs

author.name: Javad Mirzaei, Jeebak Mitra

entry.summary: The paper develops analytical models of compute-communication trade-offs for distributed LLM inference across tensor, pipeline, and hybrid parallelism, where existing strategy selection relies mostly on empirical evaluation. The analysis covers interactions among computation, communication, pipeline utilization, sequence length, batch size, and architecture. This provides principled guidance for configuring multi-GPU serving under throughput and latency SLOs.

entry.title: GNN-CB: A Graph Neural Network Competition Benchmark for Human and LLM Evaluation

author.name: Murad Hossen, Tasneem Selim, Gurur Gamgam, Tuga Yousif, Abderrahmane Kasmi, Ikram Aissiou, Mubaraq Onipede, Faran Taimoor Butt, Sanae Zrigui, Rosa Y. G. Paccotacya-Yanque, Ignatius Balayo, Ikram Elhouiti, Hadil Affes, Bijay Adhikari, Sargam Goyal, Muhammad Ibrahim Isah, Mohammad Idrees Bhat, Samuel Kangoni Matia, Peguy Kem-Meka Tiotsop Kadzue, Maha Trabelsi, Emmanuel Owusu, Vinit, Nour Majdoub, Tamiru Alemnew, Islem Rekik

entry.summary: GNN-CB is the first competition-style benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can autonomously solve end-to-end graph neural network coding tasks. It includes 18 curated competitions spanning node, edge, and graph-level prediction with a unified automated evaluation pipeline for both human and LLM submissions.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing via Path-based Inference

author.name: Eshant English, Wei-Cheng Lai, Yanfeng Yang, Kenji Fukumizu, Taiji Suzuki, Christoph Lippert

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-sample test that treats the generative dynamics of deep models as objects of statistical inference, connecting two distributions via stochastic interpolants through a shared Gaussian bottleneck. It proves that the null hypothesis holds iff the denoiser/velocity fields coincide at any noise level, yielding a path-symmetry-based test with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training

author.name: Yongxin Ning, Runliang Niu, Qianli Xing, Zhiyi Duan, Qingzu He, Pan Wang, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Infinite-Dreamer is a simulation-free data synthesis method for GUI agents that uses a pixel-level Image Editing World Model to generate high-fidelity visual-action trajectories, treating GUI transitions as image editing tasks with VLM guidance. It preserves pixel-level details like icons and layout that text- or HTML-based GUI world models discard, enabling scalable agent training data.

entry.title: Attention Tax, Handoff Tax: A Stylised Model of When Multi-Agent LLM Systems Help

author.name: Akshit Anchan, Nayonika Sen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proposes a stylized reliability model explaining conflicting findings about multi-agent LLM systems, framing the trade-off as decomposition reducing long-context burden versus a handoff tax from information transfer between agents. It derives crossover conditions determining when delegation beats a single agent with the same compute, incorporating reasoning budget, verification, and failure correlation. It offers conceptual clarity for a contested design question in agentic AI.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning a 3B-Parameter LLM on a Smartphone: Characterizing Sustained Training

author.name: Andrew Geyko, Marius Mosbach, Andr\'e Brinkmann

entry.summary: The first systematic characterization of a complete multi-billion-parameter LLM fine-tuning run on a mobile device, measuring memory, step time, thermals, and energy. It shows an iPhone 17 Pro can fine-tune a 3B model for a typical user within one battery charge, and that on-device adapters personalize as well as server-trained ones despite thermal throttling.

entry.title: Steering by Influence: Curvature Aware Data Weighting for Activation Steering

author.name: James A. E. Dixon, Stephen J. Roberts, Francesco Quinzan

entry.summary: The paper improves activation steering by replacing simple activation averaging over contrastive datasets with influence-function-based selection of thematically expressive examples, weighted with curvature awareness. This avoids representations dominated by a few tokens and encoding token-level rather than thematic concepts.

entry.title: BrainTRACE: Tracing Longitudinal, Multimodal, and Volumetric Evidence in Brain MRI Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Qizhen Lan, Mengchen Fan, Hang Zhang, Jingwei Duan, Moule Lin, Jialin Chen, Baocheng Geng, Xiaoqian Jiang

entry.summary: BrainTRACE is a report-grounded benchmark with over 7,000 scored cases evaluating whether vision-language models can trace the full evidence chain in longitudinal brain MRI interpretation, including serial comparisons, multi-sequence integration, and volumetric localization. It addresses the gap where existing medical VQA benchmarks evaluate isolated images or ungrounded report answers. This exposes failures in clinical validity that single-image benchmarks obscure.

entry.title: TAPDreamer: Transferable Adversarial Patches for World Action Models

author.name: Xuanyu Lu, Fengqing Jiang, Kaiyuan Zheng, Yichen Feng, Yaorui Ding, Yuetai Li, Zhen Xiang, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Basel Alomair, Luyao Niu, Radha Poovendran

entry.summary: TAPDreamer is a black-box adversarial attack on world action models that constructs a fixed local visual patch using only a public encoder, transferring across tasks and action architectures without access to target-model outputs or target-policy queries. The key insight is that interactions between patch-induced changes in world model predictions can be exploited generically. This exposes a significant vulnerability in world models increasingly used as foundations for robotic control.

entry.title: Recursive Video In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot

author.name: Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Bingxin Xu, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: Introduces RV-ICL, a training-free method that converts demonstration videos into navigable hierarchical structures built from sub-events like grasps and releases, enabling LLM agents orchestrating frozen vision-language-action policies to learn how tasks are performed rather than only what was done. This addresses the limitation of text-only memory in multi-episode robot learning, where video context is otherwise too slow or lossy to include.

entry.title: Learning to Simulate Individuals from Macro Social Signals

author.name: Yining Zhao, Bushi Liu, Haofei Yu, Zhengyang Qi, Shanyong Wang, Chuyue Li, Yuxiang Liu, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Introduces macro2mind, which trains an LLM with GRPO to perform behavioral reasoning using prediction-market price trajectories as supervision for how populations respond to real events. The model explicitly decomposes behavior by inferring participant groups and their interpretations, improving individual-level response simulation beyond pretraining-inherited behavior.

entry.title: Sample-Optimal Estimation of the Fr\'echet Inception Distance

author.name: Ziyun Chen, Jerry Li, Kevin Tian, Yusong Zhu

entry.summary: This work provides a rigorous statistical analysis of the Frechet Inception Distance (FID), the standard metric for evaluating generative models, showing that the common plug-in estimator needs on the order of d-squared samples due to finite-sample bias. The authors establish tight bias and variance bounds and generalize the FID-infinity estimator into extrapolation methods of arbitrary order to debias estimation. This gives the community principled guidance on how many samples are needed for trustworthy FID comparisons.

entry.title: Scale-Invariant Training for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Ignacy Stepka, Willa Potosnak, Kin G. Olivares, Artur Dubrawski

entry.summary: The authors identify scale-contaminated training: reversing instance normalization before the loss multiplies each series' gradient by a scale-dependent factor, effectively turning series scale into an unintended importance weight that biases foundation model training toward high-scale series. They propose a scale-invariant training fix for time series foundation models. This is a subtle but broadly relevant training correction for TSFMs.

entry.title: Evaluation of Active Feature Acquisition Policies with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yuta Kobayashi, Divyam Madaan, Shalmali Joshi

entry.summary: This paper studies learning active feature acquisition policies from finite offline data using prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), which require no task-specific training. The authors identify a bias in total predictive entropy as a reward, which conflates epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty and penalizes acquiring sparsely observed features, and propose targeting posterior expected aleatoric uncertainty instead.

entry.title: Adaptive Model Inversion Attacks Generalize a Privacy-Robustness Tradeoff

author.name: Shailen Smith, Rasmus Torp, Adam Breuer

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard evaluations of high-resolution model inversion attacks underestimate training-data privacy leakage, with even defended and robustly trained models leaking images 1.16 to 6.59 times more under simple adaptive attacks. It also demonstrates that measured leakage depends on the feature basis of the evaluator classifier, complicating defense comparisons.

entry.title: MASKerade: Token-Routed Mask Experts for Dense-to-MoE Upcycling

author.name: Mingyuan Zhang, Yue Bai, Zhongruo Wang, Yupin Huang, Yiyang Huang, Hailing Wang, Huimin Zeng, Yun Fu

entry.summary: MASKerade is a dense-to-MoE upcycling method that learns experts as sparse subnetworks of a frozen pretrained FFN via learned binary masks, with a token-level router selecting and combining masked FFNs while keeping weights unchanged. This supports multiple sparsity structures and reuses pretrained capacity efficiently.

entry.title: A Broader Look at Model Merging: Rethinking Implicit Regularization Induced by Task Arithmetic

author.name: Sin-Han Yang, Shih-Cheng Huang, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Shao-Hua Sun, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: This work identifies that standard model merging practice, which searches over coefficients of task-specific weight updates, imposes an implicit regularization by restricting merged models to the span of those updates. Empirically, optimizing merged-model weights beyond this subspace significantly boosts performance of common merging methods across architectures.

entry.title: Attenuated in-context identification in time-series foundation models: diagnosis under counterfactual inputs and repair by synthetic forced-system fine-tuning

author.name: Hong-In Won

entry.summary: This paper stress-tests covariate-aware time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5, TabPFN-TS) on forced engineering systems where exact counterfactual outcomes are known, finding that some models are effectively memoryless with respect to input changes and that Chronos-2 systematically attenuates identified dynamics. The authors propose fine-tuning on synthetic forced-system data to repair the attenuation. It matters because it rigorously questions whether training-free what-if predictions from TSFMs are trustworthy for industrial decision support.

entry.title: On the Intrinsic Limited Robustness of Latent-Based Watermarking

author.name: Cheng-Han Yeh, Kuan-chun Yu, Cheng-Chang Tsai, Chun-Shien Lu

entry.summary: This paper provides the first theoretical analysis of why latent-based watermarking methods for diffusion models fail to remain robust against geometric distortions like rotation, scaling, and translation. The authors derive a maximum perturbation bound relating pixel-space perturbations to their latent-space effects, and offer an analytical formulation covering the components of the watermarking pipeline. This matters because watermarking is a key provenance and safety tool for AI-generated media, and the results reveal fundamental limits that prior empirical work underestimated.

entry.title: Performative Prediction with Selective Labels

author.name: Giovani Valdrighi, Isabel Valera, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo

entry.summary: This paper extends performative prediction theory to the selective-labels setting, where labels are observed only for the accepted subset after model deployment, as in lending or admissions. It analyzes how repeated risk minimization behaves when the distribution map must be estimated from censored data rather than full post-deployment distributions. The work addresses a realistic gap between performative prediction theory and socially deployed models.

entry.title: DeltaTTT: Layerwise Optimization for Nonlinear Recurrent Memory

author.name: Yining Li, Dongchen Han, Jie Fu, Gao Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies an optimization pathology in test-time training with nonlinear recurrent memories: serial inner-loop updates fail to beat a fixed-base parallel baseline because nonlinear memories are hard to optimize within a single sequence pass. DeltaTTT addresses this by replacing joint inner-loop optimization with layerwise optimization, improving the nonlinear TTT regime.

entry.title: On Color Alignment in VAE Latent Spaces and Its Applications

author.name: Julian D. Santamaria, Kai Wang, Jes\'us Malo, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Alexandra G\'omez-Villa

entry.summary: Shows that the VAE latent spaces of text-to-image models contain a consistent color subspace aligned with brightness and opponent-color axes, exploiting the known decorrelation structure of color in natural images. The authors use a linear approximation of the encoder plus targeted latent steering, enabling color-editing applications in generative pipelines.

entry.title: Does Muon Need Fine-Grained Spectral Shaping?

author.name: Meher Chaitanya, Tianyi Zhou, Aristides Gionis

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the Muon optimizer's spectral properties, showing that 94-97% of measured singular modes lie below an estimated noise edge yet align positively with a reference gradient, and introduces BulkBoost, a two-band spectral reweighting framework with fixed-rank and noise-calibrated variants. It asks how much fine-grained spectral shaping Muon-style optimizers actually need, finding most spectral detail unnecessary.

entry.title: Uniform Discrete Diffusion Models are Minimax Optimal for Estimating Distributions with Small Effective Support Size

author.name: Dongsun Yoon, Saptarshi Chakraborty

entry.summary: This paper derives the first statistical guarantees for uniform discrete diffusion models that scale with the effective support size of the target distribution rather than the astronomically large ambient space, proving minimax optimality under a small-effective-support condition. This matches the structure of real text and biological sequence data.

entry.title: ReFold: Training-Free Reversible Inter-Turn Context Folding for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yupeng Su, Jiayi Tian, Zheng Zhang, Souvik Kundu

entry.summary: Proposes ReFold, a training-free rendering layer for long-horizon LLM agents that compresses the rendered context while preserving the underlying interaction history, avoiding runtime overhead, prefix-cache invalidation, and irreversible information loss. It removes inter-turn redundancy without auxiliary model calls or trained policies.

entry.title: ProximalFM: Amortized Proximal Causal Inference under Hidden Confounding

author.name: Christophe Muller, Ayub Kharel, Alex Luedtke, Chan Park, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, Juan L. Gamella, Rahul Krishnan, Ricardo Silva, Jakob Zeitler

entry.summary: Proposes an amortized Bayesian approach to proximal causal inference, using proxy variables to identify causal effects under hidden confounding while avoiding the ill-posed integral equations that make nonparametric proximal estimation unstable. The method targets conditional average treatment effect estimation with improved data efficiency and stability.

entry.title: DySCo: Dynamic Sharding for Collaborative Edge-Cloud LLM Inference with Depth-Synchronized Batching

author.name: Jingpo Xu, Paul Joe Maliakel, Ivona Brandic, Shashikant Ilager

entry.summary: DySCo is a collaborative runtime for layer-wise edge-cloud LLM inference that keeps KV caches local on edge devices and introduces depth-synchronized batching to address idle gaps and the inability to batch requests arriving at different model depths. This matters for deploying LLMs to resource-constrained mobile and IoT devices by allowing edge devices to contribute computation to models they cannot host.

entry.title: SquidAgent: Parallelize Wisely, Coordinate Efficiently

author.name: Yexiong Lin, Shanshan Ye, Yu Yao, Zhen Fang, Bo Han, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This paper examines why parallel multi-agent LLM systems often underperform a single serial agent despite expectations of near-linear speedups. The authors identify two hidden costs: a re-exploration cost, where parallel workers redundantly reconstruct context the orchestrator already holds, and an alignment cost, the overhead of reconciling inconsistent independently generated outputs. SquidAgent is their proposed approach for deciding when and how to parallelize agent work to coordinate efficiently.

entry.title: Prediction-powered inference for time series across space

author.name: Shahzar Rizvi, David Burt, Vishwak Srinivasan, Renato Berlinghieri, Stefano Del Col, Tamara Broderick

entry.summary: This paper extends prediction-powered inference to spatiotemporal settings where labels are observed only over a short recent window while unlabeled covariates span a longer period across many locations, such as crop yields paired with long historical weather records. It provides statistically valid confidence intervals for future per-location outcomes by correcting ML imputation error. This matters because it brings rigorous uncertainty quantification to common scientific and policy prediction problems.

entry.title: HouseholdBench: Evaluating Large Language Models as Predictors of Household Economic Behavior

author.name: Jin Huang, Diego Ferreras Garrucho, Yutong Xie, Walter M. Yuan, Qiaozhu Mei, Chen Lian, Jonathon Hazell

entry.summary: HouseholdBench unites six U.S. household surveys and 32 prediction tasks spanning consumption, income, labor, expectations, and housing to evaluate whether LLMs can model household decision making, including responses to policy changes. The authors evaluate 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs against past behavior, demographics, and macroeconomic conditions. This provides the broadest benchmark to date for LLMs as economic behavioral models.

entry.title: Reading, Not Manipulating: Leveraging Router Logits for Multimodal Safety in MoE Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ziyuan Yang, Wenxuan Ding, Shangbin Feng, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: The authors propose using mixture-of-experts router logits in vision-language models as passive diagnostic signals for detecting compositional multimodal safety risks, rather than actively manipulating expert routing. This avoids the safety-utility tradeoffs (like over-refusal) that come with steering-based interventions.

entry.title: Language Unalignability: Why Some Concepts Resist Cross-Cultural Benchmark Evaluation

author.name: Shu-Kai Hsieh, Da-Chen Lian

entry.summary: This paper challenges the Translation-Isomorphism Assumption underlying multilingual LLM evaluation, arguing that certain concept classes such as honorifics and pragmatic markers are in principle unmappable across languages. It formalizes this with a usage-cloud framework of contextualized embeddings and defines alpha-unalignability, showing that no mapping can preserve both lexical and structural faithfulness. This matters because it provides a theoretical critique of cross-lingual benchmarks that treat languages as interchangeable.

entry.title: SharedKV-BT: Node-Local Typed Decisions for Behavior-Tree Agents

author.name: Naoki Wake, Justin Wagle

entry.summary: SharedKV-BT combines behavior trees with shared-prefix KV caching so that each active node exposes stage-local fields and candidates that are scored in parallel, avoiding token-by-token generation latency while preserving decision dependencies. The system passes typed decisions to a separate execution system and is evaluated on robot manipulation, mobile navigation, and computer-use tasks. It matters because it addresses the latency-versus-flexibility tradeoff in autoregressive agent decision-making.

entry.title: Crop Yield Prediction for Punjab, Pakistan: A Tree-Ensemble and Leaf-Health Prototype, and What Random Validation Hides

author.name: Amina Asif, Qurat ul ain Asif, Noor Bakhat Asif

entry.summary: The authors build a crop-yield prediction prototype for Punjab, Pakistan combining tree ensembles with a MobileNetV2 leaf-health classifier and SHAP explanations, then audit their own pipeline and show that data leakage from a duplicated join inflates R-squared from -0.20 to 0.994 under proper year-held-out validation. The paper is a candid case study on how random validation hides catastrophic generalization failure in small agricultural tables.

entry.title: SimCortex v2: Joint Cortical Surface Reconstruction with Near-Zero Collisions and Self-Intersections

author.name: Kaveh Moradkhani, Sylvain Bouix

entry.summary: SimCortex v2 is a deep learning framework that jointly reconstructs left and right white-matter and pial cortical surfaces from T1-weighted MRI while nearly eliminating mesh self-intersections and inter-surface collisions. It builds topologically correct initial surfaces from volumetric segmentation and refines all four surfaces together. Reliable cortical reconstruction underpins surface-based neuroanatomical analysis in neuroscience and clinical research.

entry.title: Later Is Better: Token Reduction for ViTs Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Hyeongheon Cha, Hyungjun Yoon, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: This paper shows that the out-of-distribution accuracy gap of training-free token reduction in vision transformers is governed by the reduction schedule, typically left as a fixed implementation detail. It introduces a one-parameter late-concentrated power-law schedule that improves OOD accuracy at no inference cost, closing 83 percent of the gap on ImageNet-C with DeiT-S at a given reduction rate. A simple, broadly applicable insight for efficient inference.

entry.title: Unsupervised Long-Tailed Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Keliang Chen, Yaxin Hou, Hui Liu, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Unsupervised Long-Tailed Adaptation (ULTA), a new setting where vision-language models are adapted with pseudo-labels from unlabeled, long-tailed data. Counterintuitively, head classes suffer most under distributional mismatch, unlike supervised long-tailed learning where tail classes degrade. The authors analyze the failure mechanism and propose methods addressing the eroded head-class boundaries.

entry.title: Transferable Spatial Temporal Coherence Adversarial Attack on Black-Box Vision Language Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Heyam Bin Jahlan Areej Alhothali Abeer Alhothali

entry.summary: The paper introduces STCA, a temporally-aware adversarial video attack against black-box vision-language models used in autonomous driving, consisting of caption-guided frame selection, a spatial attack stage, and a spatiotemporal coherence stage. It highlights a distinct threat surface for VLM-based driving systems where temporal coherence improves transferability of perturbations.

entry.title: RoboCap: A New Platform for Egocentric Robot Learning

author.name: Grounded Superintelligence, BitRobot

entry.summary: RoboCap is a lightweight 250g wearable hat with six cameras and dual IMUs designed to capture in-the-wild egocentric manipulation data for robot learning, paired with the Grounded API, a suite of device-agnostic 3D algorithms. The authors report state-of-the-art results on public benchmarks for SLAM, egocentric depth estimation, and hand tracking. This matters because scarce egocentric manipulation data is a key bottleneck for scaling robot learning.

entry.title: OpenSplatGraph: From Dense Semantic Maps to Structured Scene Graphs for Open-Vocabulary Robot Perception

author.name: Binh Long Nguyen, Kien Nguyen, Clinton Fookes, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: OpenSplatGraph constructs persistent 3D scene graphs directly from online Gaussian-splatting-based open-vocabulary semantic maps, combining dense mapping fidelity with structured object-centric reasoning. This bridges the gap between unstructured semantic feature fields and sparse scene-graph representations for robotic perception.

entry.title: Does a Learned Corrector Beat a Simple Retreat? Evidence from a Frozen VLA

author.name: Chenchao Sheng, Zhuang Jiang, Liuhaichen Yang, Ningwei Bai, Zezhi Tang

entry.summary: This paper rigorously evaluates whether a learned runtime recovery module improves success rates of a frozen pi-0.5 vision-language-action policy beyond run-to-run variation, using paired rollouts with same-seed placebo re-runs across 3,888 episodes on four RoboTwin tasks. The corrector yields a +13.5 percentage point gain on one task but no detectable gain on the other three, highlighting the value of rigorous statistical baselines in robot learning evaluation.

entry.title: Towards Decentralized Formation of Minimum-Length Communication Networks Using Robot Swarms

author.name: Genki Miyauchi, Mohamed S. Talamali, Julian Rau, Roderich Gro{\ss}

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fully decentralized framework for robot swarms to construct and maintain communication networks in infrastructure-denied environments, using only local interactions to minimize total network length while guaranteeing continuous connectivity. It includes formal proofs that local reconfiguration operations strictly decrease network length and bound worst-case performance relative to the shortest spanning network.

entry.title: ESP: Energy-Score Policy for One-Step Multimodal Action Generation

author.name: Lilika Makabe, Heecheol Kim, Yasuyuki Matsushita

entry.summary: ESP replaces iterative diffusion/flow-matching sampling in VLA policies with a single-step action head trained via energy score rather than MSE, preserving multimodality (multiple valid action sequences) while cutting inference latency for closed-loop control. It is a teacher-free approach mapping context and noise directly to action chunks.

entry.title: StairVLA: Stage-Aware Hierarchical Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shangyuan Yuan, Xinda Qi, Yujiang Pu, Wenliang Guo, Xiaobo Tan

entry.summary: StairVLA observes that diffusion-based action heads in VLA models denoise uniformly even though conditioning needs shift across denoising stages, and proposes a stage-aware hierarchical framework that uses partially denoised actions as an interface between coarse long-horizon generation and local refinement. This could improve the precision and instruction-following of continuous robot action generation in VLA models.

entry.title: AutodidactWAM: Cross-Modal Self-Distillation from Generated Video to Robot Actions

author.name: Sergei Kurchev, Iaroslav Kolomiets, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: The paper exposes a video-action asymmetry in world-action models like Cosmos 3: after LoRA adaptation to a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands, generated video looks plausible while co-generated actions are systematically mis-targeted (only 7-17% success rates). AutodidactWAM trains a hand-pose estimator without teleoperation and distills the visually plausible video output into corrected robot actions via inverse kinematics. This self-supervised cross-modal correction meaningfully improves real-robot manipulation performance.

entry.title: Event-Driven Proactive Robot Assistance through Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Fengkai Liu, Hao Su, Haozhuang Chi, Rui Geng, Congzhi Ren, Xuqing Liu, Chenfei Xu, Yuichi Ohsita, Liyun Zhang

entry.summary: This work reformulates collaborative manipulation assistance as event-driven rather than request-driven: an event monitor detects human-object interaction outcomes and triggers assistive reasoning from pre/post action snapshots. A frozen pretrained vision-language model performs reasoning without user-provided task specifications at inference time, mimicking the anticipation of fluent human teamwork.

entry.title: RIWANav: Recursive World-Action Models with Self-Improvement for Urban Navigation

author.name: Jing Xie, Shouwei Ruan, Yubin Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Haitao Yang, Songchang Jin, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: RIWANAV is a post-training framework that jointly adapts an action-conditioned world model and a navigation policy via recursive self-improvement, where the world model provides imagined comparative feedback and the policy's evolving behavior in turn updates the world model. This avoids the cost of physical trial-and-error RL while addressing the staleness of frozen world models.

entry.title: LBA-CBF: Rapidly Adaptive Safety Filters via Parallel Dynamics Inference

author.name: Maitham F. AL-Sunni, Timeea-Andreea Radu, Hassan Almubarak, Henry Z. Liao, Michael G\"orner, Francesco Maurelli, John M. Dolan

entry.summary: LBA-CBF addresses the fragility of control barrier function safety filters when the true robot dynamics abruptly change by ranking a bank of candidate dynamics models using recent prediction error. It enforces high-order CBF conditions across all near-best models, with proofs that filtered inputs remain safe under a representative-model condition.

entry.title: Poisson empirical Bayes estimation of sums of random variables via minimum-distance methods

author.name: Stefano Favaro, Sandra Fortini, Soham Jana

entry.summary: The paper develops nonparametric empirical Bayes estimation for sums of functions of observable and unobservable variables in Poisson mixture models, using regular and coarsened minimum-distance estimation of the mixing distribution. The authors prove large-sample guarantees showing plug-in estimates merge with the oracle Bayes estimate, with nearly parametric rates when the mixing distribution has finite support.

entry.title: Takes One to Know One - Training a model to grade reward hacks causes it to reward hack less itself

author.name: Arjun Sri

entry.summary: The author finetunes models to act as reward-hack judges and finds this substantially reduces their own reward hacking: grader models complied with explicit instructions to hack only 13 percent of the time versus 62 percent for untrained models, with a hack-free training variant complying least at 7 percent. This suggests one training intervention can simultaneously teach judging and reduce misbehavior.

entry.title: The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that the debate over cyber risks of open-weight models is polarized into unhelpful camps: frontier-lab and national-security voices who see open models as untenable risks, and moderates (including himself, Hugging Face, and Joshua Saxe) who contend open weights are necessary for defense and that bans reduce safety. He warns the U.S. is heading toward lose-lose policies that both hamper AI competitiveness and increase long-term cyber risk, calling for nuanced trade-off analysis that accounts for Chinese open-weight releases.

entry.title: Causally Fair Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Patrik Okanovic, Torsten Hoefler, Drago Plecko

entry.summary: Develops methods for causally fair LLM generation, arguing that causal inference can attribute demographic disparities to their generating mechanisms where purely statistical approaches cannot. The work handles the complication that a single query may request several causally related variables, each both an outcome and a cause of others, with prompt information in arbitrary order. This brings formal fairness theory into generative settings where outputs shape consequential decisions.

entry.title: Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents

author.name: TianYi Lyu, Xiaozhe Li, Yang Li, Yongkang Chen, Kefei Tian, Junbo Niu, Zican Hu, Hongbo Liu, Mingliang Xiong, Qingwen Liu

entry.summary: SERA trains recursive LLM agents that decompose tasks, solve subtasks, and evaluate outcomes within a single set of weights, turning evaluation into a learned capability rather than relying on expensive external verifiers. Before delegating, the parent agent assesses the quality of its own decomposition, providing training signal where no ground truth exists for intermediate subtasks. This addresses a core training bottleneck for recursive multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Fusion is the New Mutation: Bandit-Guided Evolution on Workflow Graphs

author.name: Zhiwei Shang, Jiahang Sun, Mingrong Gong, Mingze Kong, Zikun Qu, Pingchen Lu, Junhao Dong, Zhipiao Liu, Hongwei Yang, Guoqing Xie, Yao Shu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: DAGO is a contextual-bandit-guided framework for automated agentic workflow optimization that learns which parent workflows to fuse under a limited evaluation budget. Candidate parent combinations are treated as arms represented by pretrained embeddings of workflow code and prompts, with a diagonal LinUCB policy learning a shared reward model to balance exploration and exploitation.

entry.title: MMPostTrainBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Research for Multimodal Post-Training

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Yuxuan Wang, Zhenxin Lei, Lingchen Meng, Yuchong Sun, Junming Lin, Hongcheng Liu, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Jin Xu, Lei Zhang, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: MMPostTrainBench benchmarks whether LLM agents can autonomously sustain improvements in multimodal post-training across eight tasks spanning image, audio, video understanding, and image-grounded software repair. Agents start from a common base model under fixed budgets, and evaluation covers target and non-target outcomes, iterative improvement and selection, and research integrity, with results showing 52.1 percent of model-task means fall below baseline.

entry.title: From Papers to Mechanisms: An Evidence-Grounded Knowledge Substrate for Scientific Language Models

author.name: Qiuhui Chen, Yibo Liu, Tao Dai, Jiafan Lu, Zhenglei Zhou, Weimin Zhong

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evidence-grounded mechanism knowledge substrate organizing scientific literature into provenance-linked evidence units, role-typed entities, and directed mechanism paths, instantiated as the MS3 schema for conductive-fiber flexible sensors across 13,689 papers. MS3 retrieval outperforms closed-book generation, web search, and raw-PDF RAG on in-domain and coverage-shift QA across ten language models.

entry.title: Mind the Execution Gap: Action-Semantic Mismatch in World-Model Control

author.name: Shengtao Wen, Xiang Chen, Yu Tian, Lingbing Guo, Lina Gong, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: This work studies how asynchronous execution (delay, packet loss, reordering, actuator buffering) changes action semantics within world-model controllers rather than merely acting as external disturbance. Controlled interventions reveal architecture-dependent failure modes: TD-MPC2 suffers future-action timeline mismatch while DreamerV3 attributes transitions to commands never applied, and the paper proposes mitigation directions.

entry.title: DUET: Co-Evolving Solver and Grader Agents

author.name: Fengyu Gao, Sourav Pal, Austin Z. Henley, Arjun Radhakrishna, Gustavo Soares

entry.summary: DUET addresses coupled challenges in improving agentic workflows: how an agent should evolve and how to evaluate an evolving agent when fixed evaluators become inadequate as behavior changes. The framework co-evolves a solver agent and a grader agent, so that improvements in one drive improvements in the other, providing evaluation feedback that adapts to changing failure modes. This targets continual improvement of deployed agents across domains.

entry.title: XTurnix: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Turn Control through Two-State Binary Decisions

author.name: Zhanxun Liu, Yifan Duan, Hengtao Wu, Chen Yang, Qinyuan Cheng, Kun Wang, Xingyu Zeng, Xipeng Qiu, Chaochao Lu, Xie Chen

entry.summary: XTurnix is a compact text-based model that unifies turn-taking control in real-time dialogue as two binary decisions, keep listening or start responding and continue or stop speaking, conditioned on complete dialogue history and the AI's current state. It is pretrained on 5.5 million causal action examples derived automatically from time-stamped data, replacing heterogeneous task-specific turn detectors with a single causal controller. This is relevant to full-duplex voice agents, an area of active industry investment.

entry.title: Only Project Once: Projection-Adaptive Loss for Exact Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Tim Aebersold, Soheyl Massoudi, Mark Fuge

entry.summary: Shows that, contrary to common practice of unrolling multiple repair steps during training of constrained neural predictors, a single detached projection step suffices. The proposed Projection-Adaptive Loss uses the constraint residual after one projection to adaptively weight penalties on raw predictions, cutting compute and memory while achieving exact constraint satisfaction. This improves robustness when repair procedures fail to converge.

entry.title: VulValidate: Auditing Function-Level Vulnerability Labels with Executable Evidence

author.name: Leizhen Zhang, Sheng Chen

entry.summary: VulValidate uses LLM agents coordinating dynamic analysis tools to construct vulnerability-triggering experiments, auditing all 35,849 function-level vulnerable labels in BigVul, PrimeVul, and DiverseVul and confirming 20,510 (about 57%). The framework reconstructs vulnerable and fixed revisions and compares runtime behavior to validate attribution.

entry.title: VAMPS: Visual and Motor Policies from Sampling-Based Planning

author.name: Mohamed Yassine Kabouri, Pietro Noah Crestaz, Quang-Nam Nguyen, Qilong Cheng, Ludovic Righetti, Nicolas Mansard

entry.summary: VAMPS uses sampling-based MPPI control to train reusable robot policies without human demonstrations, in both simulation-iterative and real-system settings. A learned policy warm-starts MPPI while refined trajectories provide fresh supervision, with a learned terminal value and IQL critic guiding policy updates. Iterative refinement is shown to outperform training once on frozen MPPI trajectories.

entry.title: Physics-Informed but Not Physics-Consistent: Error Geometry and Subspace Projection for Neural AC Power Flow

author.name: Changhun Kim, Timon Conrad, Redwanul Karim, Karan Pahlajani, Julian Oelhaf, David Riebesel, Tom\'as Arias-Vergara, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: The authors show that accurate voltage predictions from neural AC power-flow solvers, including foundation models like GridSFM, can still be physically inconsistent, with small complex voltage errors producing large power-balance residuals. Using SVD analysis on realistic GB network scenarios, they find prediction errors contain substantial components outside the dominant solution subspace, and propose calibrated solution-subspace projection to correct this. This exposes an accuracy-consistency gap relevant to grid applications.

entry.title: Future Anchored Verification and Online Recovery for World Action Models

author.name: Zhibin Qin, Zhenxiong Tan, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: FAJOR/FAVOR is a lightweight framework for world action models in robotic manipulation that reuses the model's own predicted future frames as anchors to verify execution and guide online recovery when actions drift from prediction. It addresses the limitation that existing execution monitors only decide when to stop, not what to restore. The insight that the pre-action prediction depicts the intended states is neat and broadly applicable to plan-then-act robot policies.

entry.title: IdeaLens: Detecting AI Ideas in Long-form Writing

author.name: Rishanth Rajendhran, Minjoon Choi, Jenna Russell, Ramya Namuduri, Deniz B\"ol\"oni-Turgut, Marzena Karpinska, John Wieting, Mohit Iyyer

entry.summary: IdeaLens is a detector of idea provenance: whether a document's ideas originated from a human or AI, independent of who wrote the final words. It represents documents as outlines pairing discourse roles with paraphrased content descriptions to strip surface-level prose, and trains on one million FineWeb documents with silver labels from an existing prose detector. This addresses a policy-relevant gap as AI-use rules increasingly hinge on idea authorship rather than wording.

entry.title: AttSVD:Prompt-Adaptive Low-Rank KV Cache Compression via Attention-Guided SVD

author.name: Sara Abdali, Jongwoo Ko, Pashmina Cameron

entry.summary: Proposes AttSVD, a training-free KV cache compression method that keeps every token but compresses along the feature axis using an online, per-prompt truncated SVD derived from each prompt's attention geometry, keeping only directions attention actually reads. Two decode-time caching strategies handle short and long generation regimes, cutting persistent per-head KV memory proportional to retained rank.

entry.title: Exact Unlearning via Quantized Sufficient Statistics

author.name: Ami Tavory, Shripad Gade, Tal Sarig, Noam Touitou, Ido Guy

entry.summary: Introduces Quantized Sufficient Statistics (QSS), which separates a frozen schema from mutable sum-decomposable content so that deletion requests are handled by exact subtraction rather than retraining or shard invalidation. The framework distinguishes removing a label from removing an unlabeled example, offering formal exact-unlearning guarantees.

entry.title: Global Transport Couplings for Classifier-Free Guided Flows

author.name: Katarina Petrovi\'c, Zander W. Blasingame, Danyal Rehman, \.Ismail \.Ilkan Ceylan, Michael Bronstein, Stephen Y. Zhang, Lazar Atanackovic, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: The paper introduces Global Transport (GT), a class-agnostic optimal-transport coupling computed without labels for conditional flow models. Notably, GT hurts unguided performance but consistently improves generation when combined with classifier-free guidance across domains, model scales, and sampling budgets, revealing an unexplored interaction.

entry.title: ServeLearnBench: How Well Can Agents Self-Improve from Serving Experience?

author.name: Haizhong Zheng, Yizhuo Di, Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Shuowei Jin, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes an evolving-environment evaluation setting and introduces ServeLearnBench, a benchmark for assessing whether LLM agents can continually improve from real-world serving experience where required knowledge is implicit and changes over time. It addresses coverage gaps in existing continual-learning evaluations for agents.

entry.title: Optimal and Efficient Online Inverse Optimization

author.name: Anupam Gupta, Guru Guruganesh, Honghao Lin, Vahab Mirrokni, Renato Paes Leme, David P. Woodruff

entry.summary: The paper resolves an open question in online inverse linear optimization by giving the first polynomial-time deterministic algorithm achieving the optimal O(sqrt(d)) regret, improving on a prior randomized algorithm that made (dT)^O(d) optimizations per round. The algorithm is a variable-metric method that revokes metric updates when the query point moves far from where they were computed.

entry.title: Lineage-Aware Memory Governance: A Derivation-Gated Framework for Privacy-Preserving Column-Level Access Control in Enterprise AI Agents

author.name: Venkata M Sangaraju, Sudhir Vissa

entry.summary: Introduces the Analytical Memory Unit, a memory schema for shared enterprise agent memory that attaches a full derivation lineage graph to cached results and serves a hit only when the requester is authorized for every column involved. The framework addresses data leakage through legitimately computed results and KPI divergence across departments, with proofs of security properties under complete lineage recording.

entry.title: Linear Fitness Subspace in Protein Language Models Enables Sample-Efficient Directed Evolution

author.name: SiYuan Ma, Canran Xiao, Zikai Xiao, Albert Gao, Liang He, Xuan-Yu Wang, Shuying Cao, Xiaojun Jia

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Linear Fitness Subspace hypothesis: within mutation-induced residue-level representation changes in protein language models, a compact assay-specific set of linear directions makes fitness variation accessible from few labeled variants. This enables sample-efficient surrogate modeling and uncertainty estimation for model-guided directed evolution under limited oracle budgets.

entry.title: How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain? Generalization Bounds for Spatially Dependent Data

author.name: Robin Young

entry.summary: Proves that an n-by-n satellite image with spatial correlation over r pixels contains only Theta(n^2/r^2) effective independent samples, not n^2, establishing matching finite-sample upper and lower bounds for classifiers on spatially correlated data. The result extends to directional and spatially varying correlation and has direct implications for overconfident remote sensing evaluation.

entry.title: Who Wrote It Is Not Enough: Detecting Who Contributed the Insight

author.name: Zhuoyang Zou, Abolfazl Ansari, Jiaxi Yang, Delvin Ce Zhang, Qian Chen, Dongwon Lee, Wenpeng Yin

entry.summary: The paper introduces Insight Provenance, the task of determining whether a scientific insight originates from a human, an LLM, or a hybrid, building InsightProv-v0 from 4,057 papers and 12,660 human reviews with sentence-level provenance annotations simulated via GPT-4o, Gemini, and DeepSeek. The authors show that apparent strong performance relies on linguistic and authorship shortcuts that collapse under debiased evaluation, and propose debiased methods. This matters as LLM involvement in writing and peer review grows.

entry.title: Hybrid Latent Attention for Looped Language Models

author.name: Yuhan Chen, Siyuan Zhang, Nan Wang, Feiyang Kang, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Hybrid Latent Attention (HLA) addresses the T-fold KV cache blowup in looped language models by keeping exact keys and values in a sliding window and storing older tokens as compact latents read directly by each loop's queries without reconstruction. Uptrained on 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro looped models with frozen pretrained weights, HLA shrinks the cache substantially while reproducing original attention behavior.

entry.title: The Missing Minimal Pair: Stereotype Evaluation in LLMs

author.name: Nataliya Stepanova, Ivan Titov, Emily Allaway, Bj\"orn Ross

entry.summary: The paper shows that single contrastive-pair log-likelihood comparisons, the standard method for measuring stereotype bias in LLMs, are often unreliable since rephrasing with an alternative attribute can flip preferences.
