author.name: Mingxing Peng, Xusen Guo, Long Chen, Xintao Yan, Siyu Teng, Jun Ma

entry.summary: CrashSim is a framework for generating autonomous-vehicle crash scenarios that uses priors from real-world crash data, capturing how crashes evolve before impact and how crash types are distributed, to guide generative multi-agent traffic simulation. This improves the realism of rare-event simulation for AV safety evaluation compared with methods that merely increase collision counts. Reliable safety testing of AVs is a high-stakes application area.

entry.title: Guess My Weight: Profiled Side-Channel Recovery of Floating-Point Neural-Network Weights

author.name: Timon Lum\'ir Fillo, J\'an Mikulec, Anubhab Baksi, Jakub Breier, Xiaolu Hou

entry.summary: Presents a profiled template attack that recovers complete IEEE-754 single-precision neural-network weights from power side-channel leakage during inference on embedded devices. The attack targets floating-point multiplication of a known input with first-layer weights, using multivariate Gaussian templates learned from randomized network configurations. This extends side-channel threats beyond reduced-precision settings to full bit-exact weight recovery.

entry.title: E$^2$-OPSD: Taming Entropy Overshoot in On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yifei Liu, Minghao Fang, Xinyu Gu, Chengkai Yao, Mengdi Liu, Tengfei Ma, Jiangbin Zheng, Chang Yu, Zhangyang Gao

entry.summary: The paper identifies entropy overshoot, a failure mode in on-policy self-distillation where student token entropy rises past the teacher's and stays elevated, tracing it to answer-specific teacher confidence and forward KL diffusion. E2-OPSD proposes fixes targeting both sides of the distillation to restore reusable reasoning supervision.

entry.title: Rethinking Tabular Foundation Models On Data Streams

author.name: Nilesh Verma, Daniel Nowak-Assis, Afonso Louren\c{c}o, Albert Bifet, Bernhard Pfahringer, Maroua Bahri, Nick Jin Sean Lim

entry.summary: The paper presents a systematic study of tabular foundation models applied to data streams, where adaptation occurs via context updates rather than parameter updates, examining memory management, computational cost, concept drift, and delayed labels. Findings show TFMs achieve the highest predictive performance and that simply retaining recent examples is as effective as more sophisticated context management. This establishes practical guidance for streaming use of in-context-learning models.

entry.title: Selecting Long-Horizon Trajectories for Reliable and Efficient Terminal-Agent Training

author.name: Cuong Dang, Hoang Anh Just, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: This paper studies the supervision horizon — how many trajectory tokens to retain when training terminal agents on long teacher trajectories — showing reliability improves then saturates: a 12K-token horizon outperforms 16K on Terminal-Bench with 30% less training time. Horizon length also systematically shapes agent behavior from premature termination to over-persistence, analyzed via a bias-complexity bound.

entry.title: Scalable Minimal-Change Learning for Controllable Image Editing

author.name: Shuo Chen, Fengming Huang, Yu Yao, Mingming Gong, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This work treats the minimal-change principle in instruction-based image editing as an explicit RL optimization objective, using an agentic vision-language reward model to audit source image, instruction, and edited image for unimplemented and unintended changes. A group-level rubric merges and verifies issues to produce consistent rewards across candidate edits. This replaces poor proxies like latent L1 regularization and scales without dense supervision.

entry.title: Closing the Context Gap: Activation Alignment for Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: Yoel Zeldes

entry.summary: The paper proposes activation alignment, a method for tabular foundation models that trains a lightweight linear transformation on synthetic unlabeled data to align a data-constrained student model's activations with a full-context teacher. This lets tabular in-context learning models avoid processing all training examples in every forward pass without the performance degradation of simply discarding context. It reduces the high inference cost inherent to ICL-based tabular models.

entry.title: Mask-Guided KV Cache Eviction in Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Gleb Molodtsov, Ekaterina Alimaskina, Evgeny Uskov, Artur Zagitov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Introduces MaskAhead, a training-free method for block diffusion language models that jointly handles token selection for denoising the current block and eviction from memory using a single mask-query-based ranking mechanism, with a quantized variant (Q-MaskAhead) operating from low-bit KV. This reduces the large persistent KV cache that limits memory and generation speed in block diffusion LMs.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Matching for Transport Between Markov Processes

author.name: Syamantak Kumar, Dheeraj Nagaraj, Saptarshi Roy, Purnamrita Sarkar

entry.summary: The paper formulates flow matching to learn transport maps between trajectory distributions of Markov processes, motivated by time-series domain adaptation, while preserving Markov structure. The authors prove population-level consistency and derive finite-sample error bounds under mixing assumptions. This provides statistical grounding for a growing area of generative modeling over sequential data.

entry.title: SpecBraM: What Should an EEG Foundation Model Predict? Masked Band-Power Prediction versus Waveform Reconstruction

author.name: Peng Xie, Yequan Bie, Jianda Mao, Kani Chen

entry.summary: The paper compares masked band-power prediction against waveform reconstruction as self-supervised pretraining targets for EEG foundation models, with matched backbones, 2,388 hours of data, and training steps. Band-power prediction beats waveform targets by 1.6-2.8 balanced-accuracy points on sleep staging, and by 4.7-7.3 points in the 1%-labels regime.

entry.title: Adaptive Mean Estimation by In-Context Learning: A Gradient-Flow Analysis

author.name: Martin Eppert, Krishna Balasubramanian, Subhro Ghosh, Jason Klusowski, Yan Shuo Tan

entry.summary: The authors analyze statistical adaptivity in Prior Fitted Networks such as TabPFN through a controlled location-estimation problem where the data family is hidden, using gradient-flow analysis to show how in-context learning learns estimators matched to the unknown model, including differing convergence rates for Gaussian versus uniform data.

entry.title: Spectra: Exact Component Transport for Test-Time Prior Adaptation in Simulation-Based Inference

author.name: Xin Zhao, Nico Scherf, Robert Trampel, Kerrin J. Pine, Nikolaus Weiskopf

entry.summary: Spectra enables test-time prior adaptation for amortized, diffusion-based simulation-based inference by using an exact score-transport identity to adapt a frozen diffusion model's score to a revised prior. This removes the need to retrain inference models when scientific analyses require updated priors or alternative assumptions.

entry.title: PHBA: Prefix-State Hybrid Block Attention

author.name: Ruijie Li, Jiaxi Hu, Shiyu Wang, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: PHBA is a hybrid sequence-model architecture that replaces the fixed local sliding-window attention of Native Hybrid Attention with top-k block-sparse retrieval, coupling each retrieved block with a compact prefix state built by gated linear recurrence at block boundaries. This extends exact-attention retrieval beyond a fixed local window while retaining linear-model efficiency. It contributes to the active design space of efficient long-context architectures.

entry.title: Variance-Optimal Off-Policy Evaluation with Conjunct Effect Modeling

author.name: Nicol\`o Felicioni, Michael Benigni, Maurizio Ferrari Dacrema, Paolo Cremonesi

entry.summary: The paper shows that under standard assumptions there exists an unbiased family of off-policy estimators interpolating between the cluster-weighted OffCEM and doubly robust estimation, and proposes VOCEM, which selects the interpolation coefficient for variance optimality. This reduces the excessive variance of action-level importance weights in contextual bandit OPE.

entry.title: Assumption-lean logistic regression with missing covariates

author.name: Jyotishka Ray Choudhury, Kabir Aladin Verchand, Richard J. Samworth, Ashwin Pananjady

entry.summary: Proposes reliable parameter estimation for logistic regression with missing covariates without requiring knowledge of the covariate distribution, avoiding the drastic failure modes of imputation and likelihood-approximation methods when that distribution is unknown. The approach sidesteps nonconvex M-estimation problems common in prior work.

entry.title: SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking

author.name: Shuyu Gan, Young-Jun Lee, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: SanSi explores the regime between single-pass prediction and full chain-of-thought generation by recursively applying the same layers several times with typed probability readouts after each loop, each trained with a proper scoring rule. The authors call this intermediate mode System 1.5 thinking, enabling hidden-state revision without token generation.

entry.title: Beyond Waypoint Regression: Query-Based Cost Learning over Reachable Ego Futures for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Ahmed Abouelazm, Rupert Polley, Qingyuan Zhang, Yin Wu, Philip Sch\"orner, Carl Esselborn, J. Marius Z\"ollner

entry.summary: Proposes a query-based cost-learning framework for end-to-end driving that scores dynamically reachable ego trajectory queries rather than regressing waypoints, using compact scene tokens with multimodal agent futures and cost-guided MPPI mixing. On nuScenes it improves over prior cost-estimation planners and beats most regression baselines on collision-related metrics.

entry.title: DIPrune: Task-Aware Token Pruning with Dual Importance for Efficient Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Shuo Yang, Changbai Li, Linlin Yang, Huobin Tan, Rongyu Chen, Tongfei Chen, Tian Wang, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: DIPrune reformulates training-free visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs as minimizing distortion of the final task loss, deriving a dual importance criterion that accounts for task relevance and attention reliability. The empirical motivation is that salient shallow-layer tokens suppress emerging semantic tokens through numerical inertia, causing premature discarding of signals needed for deep reasoning.

entry.title: Stabilizing language models under continual learning via condition-anchored distillation

author.name: Huan Li, Zhe Cao, Qinlei Xie, Fushun Cui, Xuechen Liang

entry.summary: The authors propose condition-anchored generative distillation (CAGD) for continual learning in LMs: retain a small set of old prompts, use a frozen previous model to reconstruct completions and generation states, and match its predictive distributions while learning new tasks. The formulation cleanly separates the roles of conditions, teacher generations, and soft targets, which ordinary replay conflates. An exact chain-rule decomposition is derived for autoregressive generation.

entry.title: The Labeling Problem in Hallucination Detection Benchmarks: An Empirical Evaluation

author.name: Jorma Valjakka, Juhani Kivim\"aki, Juha Myll\"ari, Jukka K. Nurminen

entry.summary: This paper empirically examines an ambiguity in hallucination detection benchmarking: whether labels should reflect reference faithfulness (fully supported by the reference) or factual correctness (no contradictions or false statements). The authors systematically compare how this labeling choice affects measured performance of hallucination detection methods on open-domain QA datasets.

entry.title: Harness Engineering for Software Engineering via Modular Executable Dev-Primitives

author.name: Haibo Jin, Xinjie Li, Peng Kuang, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Dev-Primitives is a modular, executable abstraction that turns repository components from passive artifacts into active participants, helping terminal-access LLM agents maintain program state across long-horizon software engineering workflows. It addresses context explosion and semantic drift when agents repeatedly reconstruct state across files, tests, and runtime behavior. It matters for the reliability of coding agents in large repositories.

entry.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively

author.name: Weixian Xu, Yanzhe Zhang, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Changyu Chen, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: Sherpa is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that trains a teacher LLM to adapt instruction to individual students by directly maximizing simulated learning outcomes across multiple LLM-instantiated student archetypes with distinct learning preferences. It avoids reliance on demonstrations or predefined pedagogical criteria. It matters for outcome-grounded pedagogy in AI tutoring systems.

entry.title: WiSPER: Pose-Supervised Predictive and Residual Flow Refinement For Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation With WiFi CSI

author.name: Gabriel Lee Jun Rong, Shanhong Liu, Pai Chet Ng, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis, Jamal Seyedmohammadi, S. Mohammad Sheikholeslami

entry.summary: WiSPER is a two-stage framework for multi-person 3D pose estimation from WiFi channel state information, combining pose-aware masked embedding pretraining (PAMEL) with conditional residual flow refinement (ReFT) to disentangle overlapping reflections and reduce coordinate errors. It adds explicit pose supervision to wireless perception.

entry.title: Efficient Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression with Standard Video Codecs

author.name: Qi Yang, Shuting Xia, Le Yang, Geert Van Der Auwera, Zhu Li

entry.summary: GSCV compresses dynamic Gaussian Splatting sequences using standard video codecs, introducing an Inter-PLAS sorting method that produces close images between I- and P-frames to improve inter-frame correlation without requiring tracked primitive information. This makes video-codec-based GS compression practical where tracking data is unavailable. Efficient compression matters as Gaussian Splatting becomes a dominant 3D representation.

entry.title: Decide Before You Look: Learning Which Retrieved Memories Deserve Pixels

author.name: Youxing LI

entry.summary: PixelTriage is a lightweight plug-in for multimodal assistants with long-term image memories that predicts, before the answering model runs, which retrieved images warrant being passed as full pixels versus cheaper text proxies. A small non-generative model reads the dialogue, a short note, and thumbnails to make this decision, trained on synthetic memory episodes. Since pixel benefit usually comes from only one or two retrieved images, this significantly cuts visual token costs.

entry.title: HuC-VideoMAE: Human-Centric Video Masked Autoencoding from synthetic data

author.name: Ricardo Pizarro, Roberto Valle, Jos\'e M. Buenaposada, Luis M. Bergasa, Luis Baumela

entry.summary: This work pretrains video transformers for action recognition on consented synthetic human-motion datasets like BEDLAM2.0 as an ethical alternative to web-crawled corpora such as Kinetics-700. It shows standard VideoMAE masking performs poorly on synthetic data and proposes a human-centric masking scheme using body keypoints and person masks to close the gap.

entry.title: Forensic Reserve: Eliciting Latent Knowledge for Image Forgery Detection

author.name: Jiahua Li, Zixu John, Tom Zhong, Fuping Wu, Tianhao Xu, Jianqing Zheng, Yuanhan Mo, Fei Shen

entry.summary: This work proposes Reserve-Guided Elicitation (RGE), which treats sparse, origin-sensitive internal components of pretrained vision foundation models as a forensic reserve for image forgery detection. A Forensic Lens decomposes activations into independent components whose localization is translated into structural constraints for lightweight adaptation, avoiding purely task-specific supervision.

entry.title: Data Leakage in Patch-Based Hyperspectral Image Classification: Quantifying the Impact of Spatial Overlap

author.name: Mohammed Q. Alkhatib

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how random train-test sampling in patch-based hyperspectral image classification causes spatial overlap and data leakage, introducing overlap percentage and average overlap ratio measures. Experiments across SVM, MLP, CNNs, ViT, and a Mamba variant on Pavia University show deep patch-based models are substantially affected, inflating reported performance.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Crowd Navigation with Adaptive Ellipsoidal Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ruihan A. Li, Ziyao Guo, Yingying Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes adaptive ellipsoidal conformal prediction (AECP) to capture directional structure in human-motion prediction uncertainty, translating it into an episode-level CVaR signal that modulates a Lagrangian safety penalty for crowd navigation. This replaces isotropic uncertainty regions with better-calibrated anisotropic ones.

entry.title: Reactive Task-Oriented Robot-Human Handovers via Generative Hypothesis Selection

author.name: Carmen Scheidemann, Andreea Tulbure, Pascal Burkhardt, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: GENESIS-Handover predicts explicit task-specific human hand poses for object handovers, modeling the variability of how humans use multi-functional objects (e.g., a hammer for striking versus pulling nails), and selects among generative hypotheses to reactively hand over objects safely and ergonomically. This advances handover research beyond geometry- and affordance-only methods toward task-conditioned human-centric behavior.

entry.title: iGPC: Generative Motion Priors for Object-Aware Humanoid Interaction

author.name: Anujith Muraleedharan, Abdul Ahad Butt, Nolan Fey, Yash Prabhu, Anamika J H, Sandor Felber, Maurice Rahme, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: The authors extend the Generative Pretrained Controller (GPC) from general human motion generation to perception-driven humanoid-environment interaction. The framework adapts GPC into interaction experts conditioned on scene affordance cues and privileged state information, leveraging pretrained large-scale human motion priors for whole-body control. This bridges the gap between natural humanoid locomotion priors and physical object interaction.

entry.title: Micro Neural Policies for Safe Real-Time Robotic Control

author.name: Hongpeng Cao, Riccardo Curcio, Daniele Ottaviano, Marco Caccamo

entry.summary: This work synthesizes very small neural control policies for embedded devices by combining evolution strategies with statistical model checking-based verification. Large-scale experiments on Cartpole and Quadrotor tasks, including zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, show that drastic network size reductions are achievable without sacrificing safety or robustness.

entry.title: Belief-Informed Hybrid Control with Almost-Sure Target-Set Convergence

author.name: Clinton Enwerem, Saleh Kemal, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-control algorithm for hybrid systems under parameter uncertainty that combines belief-space receding-horizon planning with an expected-decrease constraint on target-set progress, permitting exploratory actions that temporarily move away from the target. Under stated assumptions, the authors prove almost-sure convergence to the target set.

entry.title: SkillScriptBench: Benchmarking Self-Evolution of Executable Agent Skill Packages Beyond Markdown

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Haoran Li, Yuhao Zhang, Jiahe Guo, Hongyu Luo, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Kawai Chung, Junle Chen, Changxuan Fan, Qing Zong, Lingyun Xie, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SkillScriptBench is a 350-task benchmark, derived from a survey of over 35,000 GitHub-hosted agent skill packages, that separately evaluates documentation repair, script repair, and behavior preservation when agents self-evolve executable skill packages. Tasks pair injected script faults with maintenance requests and executable behavior checks, plus a controlled track isolating preservation.

entry.title: InferOpt: Constrained Multi-Objective Search for LLM Inference Configurations

author.name: Qi Chen, Yingying Cheng, Zhaoyi Sun, Li Zhou, Fan Zhang, Jie Sun

entry.summary: Recasts LLM inference configuration (dozens of knobs such as per-layer KV retention and expert counts) as constrained multi-objective black-box optimization, and builds InferOpt, a reusable search framework requiring only variable bounds, a deterministic resource cost model, and an evaluation hook. It searches on a frozen proxy set, rejects over-budget candidates before model calls, and re-validates Pareto representatives, covering spaces like a 28-dimensional continuous KV space for Qwen2.5-7B. This replaces ad hoc mechanism-specific heuristics for serving efficiency.

entry.title: When Is Enough Enough in Self-Evolving LLM Systems?

author.name: Enoch Yin, Bin Liu, Zhengling Qi

entry.summary: This paper addresses when self-evolving LLM systems, which repeatedly propose and incorporate updates to prompts or skills, should stop and what to output upon stopping, formulating stopping as an online sequential decision problem. It provides principled criteria to avoid unnecessary post-saturation computation and late updates that overfit or exploit the evaluation signal.

entry.title: SpecFold: Folding Multi-Branch Redundancy for Faster Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chung-En Ho, Weiyu Sun, Cheng-Jhih Shih, He Li, Yong Liu, Yingyan Celine Lin

entry.summary: SpecFold identifies multi-branch computational redundancy within speculative verification steps of diffusion language models, where draft branches share most hidden states with their parents. It proposes an algorithm-system co-design that exploits this redundancy to accelerate speculative decoding beyond prior temporal-redundancy methods. This is a concrete efficiency contribution for an emerging model class (diffusion LLMs).

entry.title: EVISKILL: Grounding Skill Evolution in Replayable Evidence

author.name: Yan Zhou, Yili Wang, Yiwei Dai, Qinggang Zhang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: EVISKILL is an evidence-driven framework for continual, parameter-free skill evolution in LLM agents that preserves the behavioral evidence and task contexts justifying edits to procedural knowledge, and manages when changes should become persistent guidance. It addresses the problem that global validation outcomes incompletely judge constituent changes, discarding locally supported corrections. This adds rigor to experience-driven agent self-improvement.

entry.title: DREAM: Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-agent Debate

author.name: Khanh-Binh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Tien Anh Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh, Hung Le

entry.summary: DREAM improves multimodal multi-agent debate by dynamically assigning different visual resolutions per sample and agent, recognizing that visual scale needs vary, and by combating groupthink where agents abandon correct deductions to conform with hallucinated peers. The two core components are dynamic resolution assignment and mechanisms to preserve independent reasoning.

entry.title: RocketAgent: A Long-Horizon Engineering Agent for Multidisciplinary Design of Liquid-Rocket Thrust Chambers

author.name: Junxiang He, Runze Mao, Kun He, Teng Zhang, Liming Zheng, Ke Xiao, Zhi X. Chen

entry.summary: RocketAgent is a long-horizon engineering agent where a plan-owning Coding Agent coordinates skills for performance sizing, subsystem optimization, geometry generation, and multiphysics assessment in liquid-rocket thrust-chamber design. It uses a provenance-aware knowledge graph and a typed Design Intermediate Representation to manage interdependent constraints and iterative design revisions.

entry.title: Agent Reliability Profiles in Financial Services

author.name: Mike Hsu, Medha Bankhwal, B\'eatrice Moissinac, Kevin Werbach, Lukasz Szpruch, Bennett Hillenbrand

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Agent Reliability Profile, a standardized per-agent unit of assurance evidence for agentic AI deployments in financial services, defining agent reliability as assurance that an agent stays within intended bounds. The work aims to fill the absence of shared frameworks for describing, validating, and benchmarking agent reliability, which currently limits trust and adoption by institutions, vendors, and regulators.

entry.title: Playing social deduction games with reinforcement fine-tuned large language models

author.name: Lingzhe Zhang, Yunpeng Zhai, Tong Jia, Kening Zheng, Chiming Duan, Minghua He, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Philip S. Yu, Ying Li

entry.summary: The paper studies how reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) changes LLM social behavior in hidden-role social deduction games requiring hidden-state inference and vote steering. It finds that optimizing terminal win-loss outcomes alone is a sparse, noisy signal that fails to reliably teach social deduction, while RFT is effective at improving social reading such as inferring hidden roles from public discussion. This offers insights into what RL can and cannot teach LLMs about multi-agent social interaction.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Automate Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Speech?

author.name: Xuanjun Chen, Zixiong Su, Hao Shi, Chang Zeng, Kai Li, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM agents can automate the research pipeline of RL post-training for text-to-speech, using AgenticTTS-Forge, a collaborative human-agent workflow applied to CosyVoice2-0.5B. The authors audit the agent trajectory stage by stage against a published recipe and score resulting policies with held-out observers. The agent recovers and improves an underspecified recipe, suggesting meaningful automation potential for ML research workflows.

entry.title: Policy as Data: Replay-Based Policy Dual Averaging via Advantage Regression

author.name: Nianli Peng, Geoffrey J. Gordon, Kiant\'e Brantley

entry.summary: Introduces RDA2C, an actor-critic method that assigns replay data a distinct role beyond off-policy samples: historical advantage estimates accumulate in a fitted dual score model that directly contributes to the actor objective through regularized dual averaging. State-action samples with critic-estimated advantages are stored and regressed, and the policy derives from the accumulated score model with entropy regularization. This aims to improve sample efficiency in RL.

entry.title: Separating Decision Time from Decision Quality in the Real-Time Gap of Distilled Deciders: Evidence from a Game and a Conveyor Simulator

author.name: Chihoon Shin, Junyeong Lee, Kihyeok Jeong, Wonok Kwon

entry.summary: This paper addresses a measurement flaw in evaluating real-time AI agents: conventional evaluations pause the world or round decision time to whole ticks, hiding latency costs. The authors decompose a distilled decider's performance gap relative to a zero-latency teacher into a time component (inference latency) and a quality component, using preregistered experiments in ViZDoom on wall-clock time and a conveyor simulator. They find comparable contributions from both components (roughly 6.5-8.7 pp and 6.3-8.6 pp respectively), showing that tick-based conversion would wrongly predict negligible loss despite a 14.8 pp accuracy drop in asynchronous play.

entry.title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning

author.name: Haozhe Chi, Song Jin, Yang Jin, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: QASLR is a post-training framework for long-video embedding that accumulates query-relevant evidence across clips while keeping the embedding size fixed. It selects a bounded frame set, restores temporal order, and processes clips sequentially with persistent think tokens cross-attending to each clip, enabling coverage of minutes- or hours-long videos under a fixed visual-token budget. This addresses a key scalability limitation of video retrieval and embedding models.

entry.title: TeleGen: Improving LLM-Based Web Application Generation via Runtime Telemetry

author.name: Yujia Luo, Haonan Zhang, Jiasi Shen, Zishuo Ding, Weiyi Shang

entry.summary: TeleGen improves LLM web application generation by instrumenting generated apps, collecting runtime telemetry during task execution, and compressing telemetry logs into concise briefs that guide code repair. This addresses the gap in generate-execute-repair pipelines where feedback misses interaction-level runtime behavior between browser actions and outcomes.

entry.title: Settling the Computational Complexity of Max-Min Allocation with Ternary Valuations

author.name: Thi Ngoc Anh Vu, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni, J\"{o}rg Rothe

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves the complexity of computing max-min (egalitarian) allocations of indivisible items when agent valuations take few distinct values. It gives a polynomial-time algorithm for two-valued additive valuations with small coprime values, constant-gap hardness for larger values, an approximation guarantee for bi-valued valuations, and reductions to matching that settle conjectured cases for mixed valuations. These are definitive results in fair division theory.

entry.title: Optimal Control with Learned Critics under Unmodeled State Dependencies

author.name: Philipp Schoch, Markus Ryll

entry.summary: The paper proposes a learning-based MPC framework that augments nominal analytical dynamics with a residual dynamics network for missing state-dependent effects and learned critics to compensate for finite-horizon myopia. This combines the structure, constraint-awareness, and data efficiency of model-based planning with the adaptivity of learning for contact-rich tasks. The approach aims to reduce the interaction data demands of model-free RL while avoiding pure analytical modeling.

entry.title: Expanding LLM Reasoning

author.name: Rian Atri, Evan Luo

entry.summary: The paper studies where within an existing reasoning chain an additional continuation should begin when spending extra inference compute, defining expansion utility as the correctness change from restarting at a stored step. Across 41 model-benchmark cells, restart position matters and an always-last fixed rule is a strong baseline that a learned router fails to clearly beat.

entry.title: CACFG: Curvature-Aware Classifier-Free Guidance and Optimal Control

author.name: Max Collins, Dasith de Silva Edirimuni, Jordan Vice, Tim French, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: The paper reframes classifier-free guidance in diffusion sampling as a continuous-time optimal control problem and introduces curvature-aware corrections that respect principled diffusion dynamics, addressing both the theoretical violation CFG poses and the practical degradation at high guidance strengths. The method extends to deterministic samplers used in practice.

entry.title: Incentive Alignment in Online Experimentation

author.name: Ermis Soumalias, Richard Mudd, Abbas Zaidi

entry.summary: This paper reframes online A/B testing as a principal-agent incentive design problem, noting that decentralized experimenters rewarded on empirical treatment effects have incentives to inflate results, eroding platform value in ways significance thresholds cannot fix. The authors propose mechanisms to align experimenter incentives with platform goals. It bridges mechanism design and experimentation infrastructure.

entry.title: Do VLAs Understand and Adapt to the Objects They Handle, or Simply Replay Learned Behaviors?

author.name: Xinnuo Xu

entry.summary: The paper probes whether vision-language-action (VLA) models genuinely generalize from physical object properties or merely replay learned motions, using linear probing and representational similarity analysis across seven VLAs. It finds physical properties like mass and fragility are less decodable from activations than non-physical ones like semantic category and price. The distinction between genuine generalization and incidental robustness is a meaningful contribution to robot foundation model evaluation.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Guided Discovery of Weight-Five Bivariate Bicycle Codes

author.name: Juan Cruz-Benito

entry.summary: Building on an earlier LLM-guided program-evolution workflow, this paper catalogs 1,142 proposals for weight-five bivariate and perturbed bivariate bicycle quantum codes, with 1,081 attributable to LLM-generated programs. It certifies connected CSS realizations with strong parameters such as [[96,4,10]] and [[180,4,14]], providing exact distance evidence. This demonstrates LLM-guided search producing certified novel constructions in quantum code design.

entry.title: QiYao-I: A Manifold Based Foundation Model for Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Linfeng Wang, Ruitong Zhang, Kai Zhao, Yang Shu, Zhongwen Rao, Meng Wang, Yijie Li, Bin Yang, Chenjun Guo

entry.summary: Proposes QiYao-I, a foundation model for irregularly sampled, asynchronous multivariate time series that introduces a sampling-conditioned temporal manifold attention mechanism mapping real timestamps into a learnable manifold feature space. This addresses a generalization gap in existing time series foundation models, which assume regularly sampled sequences.

entry.title: The Premise Is the Problem: Exchangeability Failure in Self-Monitored Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Weijia Han, Lisha Qu, Zhenda Li, Liying Liang

entry.summary: Analyzes whether statistical guarantees for self-monitoring mechanisms in test-time adaptation survive when the monitor and the adaptation share the same feedback signal. In multi-step forecasting, the authors show overlapping targets and error dependence can break exchangeability, causing false alarms and potential feedback loops.

entry.title: Adversarial Training for Deep Hedging in Nonstationary Markets

author.name: Philipp J. Schneider, Lukas Looser, Antoine Garin, Shuhan Liu, Daniel Kuhn

entry.summary: Proposes WRAP, a drift-aware adversarial training framework for deep hedging derived from a two-budget distributionally robust optimization formulation. It lets an adversary reweight observed trajectories and perturb dynamics, balancing sampling uncertainty against temporal drift in nonstationary markets.

entry.title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning for Graph Saddle Point Problems

author.name: Samantha Chen, Jesse He, Coleman Clougherty, Gal Mishne, Chester Holtz

entry.summary: GraphPDHG is a message-passing network aligned with the Chambolle-Pock Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient method for solving graph saddle-point problems. The authors prove the network can simulate PDHG efficiently and can learn accelerated variants, demonstrated as learned warm starts for second-order optimizers. This extends neural algorithmic reasoning to a broader class of continuous optimization problems on graphs.

entry.title: Interpretable Hypergraph Learning via Neural Additive Models

author.name: Shihan Feng, Xin Zheng, Shiyi Yang, Ren Wang, Chudi Zhong, Can Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces HGNAN, an inherently interpretable hypergraph neural network that extends neural additive models to higher-order relational data, decomposing contributions of node attributes and hyperedge structure. This addresses the opacity of black-box message-passing hypergraph architectures.

entry.title: AFA-BANDIT: Provably Near-Optimal Online Multi-Feature Classification Under Budget Constraints

author.name: AbdAlRahman Odeh, Teng-Hui Huang, Hesham El Gamal

entry.summary: This work formulates online active feature acquisition as a combinatorial Bandits with Knapsacks problem, coupling feature acquisition decisions with prediction under a global cost budget. It provides near-optimal regret guarantees, filling a gap left by deep RL approaches that lack performance guarantees.

entry.title: Towards One-for-All Foundation Model for Attributed Graph Clustering

author.name: Yunhui Liu, Xudong Jin, Kang Zhang, Danshuo An, Yu Xing, Te Song, Jia Liu, Tieke He

entry.summary: The paper proposes OFAG, a foundation model for attributed graph clustering that trains once and applies directly to diverse graphs without graph-specific training, fine-tuning, or hyperparameter search. It addresses the fragility and cost of per-graph pipelines in unsupervised graph learning.

entry.title: Generalized Matheron Variational Implicit Processes

author.name: Luis A. Ortega, Andr\'es R. Masegosa, Thomas D. Nielsen

entry.summary: GMVIP introduces a pathwise variational family for posterior inference with implicit-process priors such as Bayesian neural networks and stochastic simulators, where function-space densities are unavailable. For Gaussian-process priors it recovers standard inducing-variable variational GPs, and for general implicit priors it constructs posterior samples via prior draws with an inducing-point-anchored correction.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning in MDPs: An Occupancy Measure Approach

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Ashwath K. Karunakaram, Ali Eshragh, Yuexing Li, Kai Wang

entry.summary: The authors reformulate decision-focused learning in MDPs as an occupancy-measure linear program instead of differentiating through KKT conditions of the Bellman equation, deriving closed-form gradients via active-constraint identification to improve scalability. They address gradient discontinuities at active-constraint changes and backward-pass cost scaling. This makes end-to-end predict-then-optimize in sequential settings more tractable.

entry.title: How Learning Governs Unlearning across the Memorization-Generalization Spectrum

author.name: Hwiyeong Lee, Hyelim Lim, Ingyu Bang, Hoki Kim, Taeuk Kim

entry.summary: Using grokking in modular addition, the authors classify models as memorization-heavy or generalization-heavy and show that generalization-heavy models suffer larger retain-set damage during unlearning. A finer-grained bucketed modular addition setup lets them separate the contributions of the two learning strategies to unlearning dynamics.

entry.title: AdaLoop: Adaptive-Depth Latent Reasoning for Audio Language Models

author.name: Lee Seung-woo, Bowen Qi

entry.summary: AdaLoop is a lightweight recurrent module that learns how many latent refinement steps each audio-question pair requires, iterating a shared transformer block over the audio representation with a learned halting mechanism. It adds under 3% of the base model's parameters and plugs into audio encoder-based LLMs, targeting fine-grained acoustic tasks like pitch comparison where fixed-depth models waste computation.

entry.title: CroissantMiner: Automated Extraction and Validation of Croissant Metadata for ML Datasets

author.name: Berke Arda, Ahmetcan Yavuz, Paul Gerry, Sebastian Lobentanzer, Nobin Sarwar, Joan Giner-Miguelez, Kongtao Chen, Luyao Zhang, Mrinmaya Sachan, Mubashara Akhtar

entry.summary: Presents the first end-to-end benchmark for extracting Croissant dataset metadata from papers, with 602 papers including 102 human-validated gold annotations spanning the full schema plus Responsible AI fields. The authors evaluate frontier, open-weight, and agentic extraction systems under a two-tier evaluation combining rule-based and judge-based scoring.

entry.title: Two Vectors Replace In-Context Demos: Structured Task Adaptation via Embeddings

author.name: Xi Ding, Naichen Shi, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: STAVE replaces in-context demonstrations in frozen large multimodal models with two task-specific vectors added to existing input embeddings: a readout vector updating answer-producing tokens, avoiding per-query demo re-encoding costs of hundreds of visual tokens. It addresses limitations of prior demo-free methods where task parameters grow with model depth and cannot reshape intra-layer attention.

entry.title: Trustworthy Method Comparison with AI Judges: Estimation and Design under Order, Batch, and Aggregation Effects

author.name: Tianxi Li, Jie Ding

entry.summary: The authors model LLM-judge evaluation with Markov generalized linear mixed models validated on three commercial LLMs, showing that naive randomize-and-average practices can be statistically inconsistent for group comparisons. They propose improved designs, including a Williams square design, for leaderboard ranking and method comparison.

entry.title: CoDe-LoRA: Mitigating the Orthogonality Dilemma in Continual Learning of LLMs via Knowledge Consolidation and Decoupling

author.name: Maoqi Liu, Quan Fang, Yufei He

entry.summary: CoDe-LoRA identifies an orthogonality dilemma in continual learning of LLMs, where orthogonal LoRA projections like O-LoRA prevent catastrophic forgetting but also block transfer of shared knowledge across related tasks. The proposed replay-free method decomposes learning into consolidating universal knowledge and decoupling task-specific knowledge.

entry.title: Tree Navigation Without LLM Summaries: A Matched-Cost Study of Hierarchical Retrieval for Long-Document QA

author.name: Priyank Jayraj, Poonam Goyal, Navneet Goyal

entry.summary: The paper shows that the benefit of RAPTOR-style summary trees in long-document QA largely comes from hierarchical navigation rather than the LLM-generated summaries themselves. It introduces NavTree, a leaves-only retriever built as a deterministic balanced segment tree over chunks that requires zero LLM calls at indexing time and uses hybrid lexical-dense scoring for navigation. This offers a cheaper, simpler alternative for retrieval over long documents.

entry.title: Structured but Silent: Probing Capability Requirements in LLM Hidden States

author.name: Kyojun Choo, Minsoo Song, Yunju Kang, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: The TACIT framework investigates whether the capability requirements implied by a user query (along Source, Transformation, and World Effect axes, yielding eight capability classes) are linearly decodable from LLM hidden states before generation. It compares this hidden-state accessibility with explicit verbal classification of tool-use requirements.

entry.title: Holdout Best-of-N: Unbiased Evaluation and Its Cost

author.name: Shrey Shah, Yinheng Li

entry.summary: The paper studies unbiased evaluation of Best-of-N selection when reusing selection scores overstates expected reward, deriving a single holdout-based estimator that is exactly unbiased under independent stable score laws if and only if fresh scores J are fewer than selection scores K. It characterizes minimax risk at order sigma^2/sqrt(K) and shows allowing bias improves the rate to sigma^2/K. This provides principled foundations for reward-model evaluation in RLHF-style pipelines.

entry.title: Where Rules End and Judges Begin: Measuring the Judgment Boundary in Multi-Agent Systems Security

author.name: Shaswata Mitra, Raj Patel, Subash Neupane, Sudip Mittal, Md Rayhanur Rahman, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: DEFER1 organizes multi-agent-system security defenses into five principles implemented as a cascade of 28 deterministic checks that block what they can and refer ambiguous cases to a panel of four LLM judges. Across four domains, attack success rates drop from about 30% to 3%, with 78% of blocked attacks handled deterministically. It matters for scalable, auditable security architectures for LLM agent systems.

entry.title: Conversation Is a Two-Body Problem: Dyadic Evaluation of Full-Duplex Dialogue Models

author.name: Sungnyun Kim, Sungwoo Cho, Jihwan Oh, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: DyaFDB is a dyadic evaluation framework for full-duplex spoken dialogue models in which two models converse directly under assigned roles with cooperative or conflicting goals, and both sides are graded, instead of evaluating against static or single-sided examiners. Turn-taking, overlap, and interruption are treated as joint products of coupled speakers. It matters because current duplex-dialogue evaluation misses interaction dynamics central to real voice agents.

entry.title: RADC: Risk-Aware Dual Caching for Vision-Language Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Siyu Huang, Yueyong Chen, Xuejiao Li, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: RADC improves cache-based test-time adaptation for vision-language models by adding a Semantic Foreground Cache built from CLIP spatial evidence and a Gaussian Risk Admission mechanism that weighs class separation and feature uncertainty. This mitigates background bias and unreliable entropy-based cache admission in zero-shot adaptation settings.

entry.title: Image-Space Refraction Correction for Underwater 3D Reconstruction: Warping Flat-Port Views into Pinhole Perspective

author.name: Chelim Lim, Tobias Fischer, Emilio Olivastri, Beverley Gorry, Michael Milford, Alejandro Fontan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a physics-based image-space correction for refraction at flat-port camera housings, which causes bowl-shaped distortion in underwater 3D reconstructions. The method warps flat-port views into pinhole perspective so corrected images can plug directly into existing reconstruction and SLAM pipelines, validated via ray-tracing simulation and real data. This is a practical enabler for low-cost underwater mapping of reefs and seafloor habitats.

entry.title: Two Halves are More than One: Phase-wise Velocity Distillation for Fast and High-Quality Image Generation

author.name: Zhen Guo, Rongyuan Wu, Qiaosi Yi, Chenxi Xie, Xinyu Wei, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Phase-wise Velocity Distillation (PVD) improves one-step diffusion image generation by splitting the generation timeline into coarse and fine phases and modeling each with a separate distilled mapping, rather than a single monolithic student evaluation. This better approximates the heterogeneous coarse-to-fine transport and avoids the over-smoothed outputs typical of one-step distillation. The method maintains quality within a single full-backbone-forward compute budget.

entry.title: Image Bitstream Fine-grained Understanding for Privacy-Friendly AIoT

author.name: Zhen Yu, Wenyang Liu, Kejun Wu, Chengwang Xiao, Renjie Qiao, Chengtao Cai

entry.summary: The paper introduces Image Bitstream Fine-grained Understanding (IBFU): performing fine-grained classification and semantic description directly from encoded image byte sequences without decoding to pixels. The proposed BFG foundation model with a Bitstream Semantic Encoder reduces visual exposure in the processing pipeline, suiting privacy-sensitive AIoT applications.

entry.title: Sparse2comm: Towards Robust Cooperative 3D Object Detection

author.name: Lei Yang, Boqi Li, Chunmian Lin, Li Wang, Ziying Song, Shaoqing Xu, Heye Huang, Haibao Yu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: Sparse2comm is a bandwidth-efficient cooperative 3D detection framework for vehicle-infrastructure perception that treats unreliable cooperation (packet loss, delay, spatial misalignment) as progressive restoration over degraded features. A sparse feature encoding keeps communication costs low while jointly handling coupled degradations that prior methods addressed piecemeal.

entry.title: Generalizable Robustness Testing of DNN-Based Robotic Navigation Systems via XAI-Guided Search

author.name: Khizra Sohail, Miren Illarramendi, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: The authors propose an explainability-guided multi-objective evolutionary approach for robustness testing of DNN-controlled cyber-physical systems, generating sparse perturbations on representative images selected via visual and behavioral clustering. A key contribution is testing whether induced failures transfer from simulation to a physical robot, addressing the frequent limitation of simulation-only robustness evaluation.

entry.title: What the Elevation Map Cannot See: Semantic-Aware Locomotion and Execution-Aware Navigation for Humanoid Robot

author.name: Shunyu Yao, Songyang Liu, Dinghao Chen, Yuanyuan Lei, Shuai Li

entry.summary: This work identifies two failure modes in humanoid vision-and-language navigation: hazards invisible to elevation maps and command-execution mismatch between the navigation policy and the locomotion controller. It proposes semantic-aware locomotion and execution-aware navigation evaluated in simulation benchmarks designed to expose these gaps.

entry.title: Multi-Robot Multi-Goal Motion Planning with Stochastic Skills

author.name: William Schnyder, Valentin N. Hartmann, Stelian Coros

entry.summary: This work integrates stochastic manipulation skills into sampling-based multi-robot planning by formulating the problem as an MDP over a multi-modal composite roadmap, enabling concurrent motion planning with uncertain execution times and trajectories. It addresses a real gap where existing planners assume single robots, open-loop paths, or static post-hoc scheduling.

entry.title: VOMMI: Collecting and Leveraging Portable Demonstrations for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yutian Zhang, Xingrui Xiong, Siyuan Ma, Yang Li, Jiawen Wen, Jiaqi Zhai, Liwen Yang, Ce Hao, Haozhen Chi, Yangkun Zhu, Yifan Zhu, Xiaowen Chu, Dong Wei, Qiaojun Yu, Dibo Hou

entry.summary: VOMMI is a framework for collecting low-cost, robot-free mobile manipulation demonstrations using portable RGB cameras, connecting them to VLA post-training through offline trajectory reconstruction. It tackles the drift and inconsistency problems of raw visual odometry trajectories to produce reliable motion supervision without teleoperation or specialized sensing hardware. This helps alleviate the data scarcity bottleneck for embodied intelligence.

entry.title: Safe Multi-Robot Collaborative Transport Using Density Functions

author.name: Jagannath Prasad Sahoo, Sriram S. K. S. Narayanan, Umesh Vaidya

entry.summary: The authors present a hierarchical density-based MPC framework enabling multiple quadrupedal robots to collaboratively push a shared object to a desired pose using only initial and goal poses. A centralized box-level MPC optimizes contact forces under control-density constraints for convergence and obstacle avoidance, while each robot solves a distributed whole-body MPC to track its contact location.

entry.title: NMPP: Nonlinear Model Predictive Planning for Agile UAV Flight in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Ond\v{r}ej Proch\'azka, Juraj Pauko, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka, Martin Saska

entry.summary: NMPP imposes perceived obstacles as hard geometric constraints within a nonlinear model predictive planner and passes a full-state reference to an obstacle-blind SE(3) controller for agile quadrotor flight in clutter. It achieves 58-67% lower position RMSE than linear MPC trajectory tracking baselines while preserving dynamic feasibility.

entry.title: Network Intervention by Polling Strategic Agents

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Rohit Parasnis, Saurabh Amin

entry.summary: The paper studies a planner setting prices in multi-activity network games where agents hold private information and may misreport. It derives a centrality-based decomposition of optimal prices and proposes Poll, a sampling-based algorithm that queries agents locally, with provable properties addressing incentive and scalability challenges.

entry.title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Necessity and the Effect of Reasoning Constraints

author.name: jeffk

entry.summary: The author extends Lanham-style chain-of-thought corruption interventions from factual tasks to ethical reasoning, measuring CoT necessity as a component of faithfulness. Findings show larger models depend far less on CoT for ethical questions, and constraining CoT with format templates may increase dependence by narrowing the reasoning space, with implications for CoT-based safety monitoring.

entry.title: Training Numerical Intelligence via Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery

author.name: Peter Chen, Wotao Yin

entry.summary: This paper introduces ADSD, a framework that improves numerical solvers by first diagnosing why a solver performs poorly from execution feedback, then using that diagnosis to discover appropriate numerical methods, packaged as reusable solver skills. It reframes AI-driven solver improvement from trial-and-error code editing into a structured diagnosis-first process.

entry.title: Language-Conditioned Token and Reasoning Efficiency in Large Language Models: A Paired Cross-Lingual Study Protocol

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper specifies a prospective, preregistered paired protocol to separate input language, trace language, and answer realization effects on token and reasoning costs, instantiating 240 scored items in English plus seven languages across three open-weight checkpoints and 47,520 initial core runs. It addresses confounding in cross-lingual cost comparisons.

entry.title: Asking Earns Nothing: Scoring the Decision to Act in BFCL Multi-Turn

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: A critical audit of the BFCL multi-turn agent leaderboard showing that its scorer never examines the turn on which a model is supposed to ask for missing information: asking earns nothing, guessing costs nothing, and asking twice loses the item. The paper leverages matched should-ask versus base items as a built-in control experiment. This exposes a meaningful measurement flaw in a widely used agent benchmark.

entry.title: Autonomous Structuring of Radiology Reports Across Modalities at Archive Scale Using an Open-Weight Large Language Model

author.name: Friedrich Puttkammer, Fabian Drexel, Marlene Fritzsche, Era Stambollxhiu, Miriam Kumpf, Lena Schmitzer, Lea Schumann, Lina Xu, Johannes Moll, Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Anirudh Narayanan, Hartmut H\"antze, Renato Cuocolo, Antonios Billis, Alexander L\"oser, Jawed Nawabi, Marcus R. Makowski, Cosmin I. Bercea, Shahrooz Faghihroohi, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem

entry.summary: A retrospective clinical study developing and evaluating an open-weight LLM pipeline (gpt-oss-120B, an existing open-weight model) that converts an entire radiology report archive into structured reports without human oversight, using 150 hierarchical templates selected via constrained decoding on a single local GPU. Template selection was scored against expert labels on 914 sampled reports across five modalities, with structuring quality assessed field by field on 920 reports by five residents. Demonstrates practical, privacy-preserving, archive-scale clinical NLP.

entry.title: $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention

author.name: Wenyin Liu (Guangdong University of Technology), Yiheng Huang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Kai Wang (Beijing Denglu Technology Ltd)

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces TRIZ^a, a paradigm for automating R&D that combines the classical TRIZ inventive theory (40 inventive principles and contradiction matrix) with LLM-driven agent evolutionary search, replacing random mutation with theory-guided, explainable ideation. It operationalizes functional information and TRIZ Ideality on a common information scale, with hard gates separating true promotion from mere metric improvement. The approach is validated in cybersecurity on benchmarks including PowerDuck GOOSE and CICIoT2023.

entry.title: RAGStress: A controlled benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation under knowledge-base degradation

author.name: Shiqi Yang, Jiekai Ma, Gaoyuan Du

entry.summary: RAGStress stress-tests retrieval-augmented generation under systematic knowledge-base corruption, pairing four naturalistic corruption types with three severity levels across 57 MMLU subjects and 182,546 documents, totaling 52,500 evaluations. It characterizes how clean-KB evaluation assumptions break down, revealing retrieval behavior under realistic degradation.

entry.title: CIPO: Counterfactual Imagination Policy Optimization for Adaptive Tool Granularity Selection

author.name: Yu Li, Yunlu Wan, Zijian Zhu, Han Luo, Chao Ren, Long-Fei Li, Lei Feng

entry.summary: CIPO frames skill use in LLM agents as adaptive tool granularity selection: deciding whether a state requires atomic fine control or skill-level abstraction. It trains this policy with counterfactual imagination, comparing consequences of atomic versus skill choices from the same state. This is a clean formulation of a real problem that emerges as agents build composite skills alongside primitive tools.

entry.title: Toward AI Trustworthiness: Finding Analytically Proven Forward-Invariant Sets for AI-Controlled Systems

author.name: Haoyang Song, Xikun Yang, Qixin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for certifying safety of neural-network controllers by finding analytically proven forward-invariant sets (FIS) — regions of state space that trajectories cannot leave. It uses an invertible neural network to map the original state space into a latent space where a regular-shape invariant set can be found and then transformed back with formal guarantees. This enables safety certification for AI-controlled nonlinear systems.

entry.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design

author.name: Haosen Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: EASER is a reflective agent that bridges scientific literature reasoning and biological sequence generation by steering a diffusion generator through a learned property interface of fixed low-rank matrices. The agent proposes intervention hypotheses such as anchors and editable positions to close the evidence-to-execution gap in multi-objective peptide design.

entry.title: RollPlace: Improving Macro Placement via Monte Carlo Rollout Search

author.name: Qi Zhou, Guojun Liu, Guangzhi Qi, Ming Lu, Jiechu Liu, Zhongli Liu, Jianqun Yang, Xingji Li

entry.summary: RollPlace is a two-stage macro placement framework for chip design that first generates initial layouts via ML or heuristics, then refines them by adjusting specific macros using Monte Carlo rollout search rather than generating a single one-shot solution. This addresses a common weakness of RL-based EDA placement methods whose outputs typically require later refinement.

entry.title: The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance

author.name: Stefan B\"uhler, David Exler, Markus Reischl, Mark Schutera

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open two-probe benchmark that places language models on a spectrum between exploitable compliance and uncooperative resistance. An active probe measures exploitability (following instructions that lower payoff) while a passive probe measures stoppability (waiting when instructed to give up a higher payoff), combined into a compliance index kappa. Applied to twelve language models, seven mostly complied in both probes by deferring to the instruction.

entry.title: Do Motion Tokenizers for Co-Speech Gesture Generation Encode Gesture Semantics?

author.name: Varsha Suresh, Divij Jain, Jia Liu, M. Hamza Mughal, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This work probes discrete motion tokenizers used in co-speech gesture generation to determine which motion properties are recoverable from their codebooks. Using 19 gesture descriptors ranging from raw motion to abstract communicative function, the authors find that geometry and handedness decode well while semantic motion categories decode only weakly. The result shows reconstruction objectives alone do not guarantee gesture semantics are captured.

entry.title: Streaming Multi-Track Timeline Control for 3D Human Motion Generation

author.name: Yangsong Zhang, Anujith Muraleedharan, Rikhat Akizhanov, G\"ul Varol, Fabio Pizzati, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: TimelineControl enables text-driven 3D human motion generation where new instructions arrive during synthesis and must be combined with ongoing, independently timed overlapping actions. The method uses interval-aware conditioning to preserve instruction timing plus causal part-structured representations and part-aware denoising to coordinate concurrent actions. This targets interactive applications rather than batch text-to-motion generation.

entry.title: CurveCodec 2: Skeleton-agnostic animation compression with a learned entropy model

author.name: Mingyi Shi, Huancheng Lin, Xuelin Chen, Taku Komura

entry.summary: This paper presents a learned codec for skeletal animation data that works across arbitrary skeleton rigs with stated error bounds, improving on the authors' earlier CurveCodec by matching the worst-case error of the industry-standard ACL library while counting payload in bits rather than floats. It analyzes where redundancy in skeletal motion actually lies and identifies which codec components benefit most from a learned entropy model. This matters for game engines, robotics, and motion datasets where animation storage is a production bottleneck.

entry.title: AgroGround: Multi-Granularity Grounded Recognition in Agriculture

author.name: Abdulla Alshehhi, Zongyan Han, Rao Anwer

entry.summary: Introduces AgroGround, a large-scale dataset for grounded agricultural recognition that links plant-disease labels to image regions. An automated pipeline converts labels from eight agricultural VQA datasets into lesion and whole-object annotations, yielding roughly 795,000 instruction examples with negative supervision from healthy images. This addresses the costly manual annotation bottleneck for diagnosis models that must both recognize and localize evidence.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Solar Image Synthesis: Adapting the Surya Foundation Model from He I 10830 {\AA} to EUV Translation and Coronal Hole Segmentation

author.name: Marco Marena, Andr\'es Mu\~noz Jaramillo, Qin Li, Haodi Jiang, Jinghao Cao, Wen He, Ziyang Zhang, Chenxi Yuan, Chao Wang, Haimin Wang, Bo Shen

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Surya solar foundation model to translate full-disk helium (He I 10830 Angstrom) observations into SDO/AIA extreme-ultraviolet images at 94, 193, and 304 Angstrom channels, plus coronal hole probability maps. Using a convolutional input adapter, low-rank backbone fine-tuning, and dedicated output decoders trained on temporally paired, registered observations with SPOCA catalog supervision, the approach enables studying solar morphology from historical helium records that predate modern EUV imaging.

entry.title: Coupling Noisy Pairwise Knowledge to the DAG Posterior for Causal Discovery

author.name: Guoliang Xu, James E Corter

entry.summary: Introduces HB-NoisyKG, a Bayesian framework combining observational data with noisy causal reports from sources such as LLMs for causal structure learning. A feature-conditioned Beta prior pools reliability information per variable pair and a shared error matrix captures systematic source mistakes, with alternating inference refining reliability and graph estimates. This makes heterogeneous external knowledge safely usable for causal discovery.

entry.title: Knossos and Ariadne: Benchmarking and Learning Complete Diagram Topology Extraction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Xujiang Zhao, Shengyu Chen, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Xi Zhu, Guoning Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces diagram-to-graph topology extraction as a task, along with Knossos, a benchmark of 19,200 symbolic diagrams across six domains containing over 245K nodes and 439K edges. The accompanying Ariadne model/method targets complete entity and relation extraction from structural diagrams with VLMs. This fills a real gap, since existing VLM benchmarks rarely evaluate full relational structure rather than isolated element recognition.

entry.title: TempoBridge: Source-Conditioned Flow Matching with Optimal Transport Couplings for Single-Cell Population Transitions

author.name: Bowen Han, Lingbei Meng, Shihuan Luo, Yupeng Zang, Wenlin LI, Peize He, Yaodi Luo, Lian Zhang, Jianqing Zhu, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: TempoBridge is a unified source-conditioned flow matching framework for modeling temporal, genetic, and chemical cell population transitions from unpaired single-cell snapshots. It uses minibatch optimal transport couplings for training paths and a fixed empirical population summary, requiring no target examples at inference.

entry.title: Tracing a Sparse Emotion-Control Circuit in LLM-Based Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Yanfu Zhang, Ye Gao

entry.summary: Using activation patching with two new emotion-sensitive metrics, the authors identify a sparse circuit of 23-27 attention heads and MLPs (about 5% of components) that recovers or suppresses 74-88% of the late emotion-readout shift in LLM-based TTS. The circuit combines a shared backbone with emotion-specific components.

entry.title: MGPO: Manifold-Guided Diffusion Alignment for Task-Aware Dataset Distillation

author.name: Yunyi Chen, Chenru Wang, Xinyi Ye, Zexin Zheng, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: MGPO reformulates diffusion-based dataset distillation as a multi-objective reinforcement learning problem, aligning generated samples to downstream task needs via a pixel-space discriminative reward and a latent-space geometric reward based on class-wise minimum spanning trees. This counters the objective mismatch where density-focused diffusion fails to preserve decision boundaries and manifold coverage. The result is distilled datasets better suited for discriminative downstream training.

entry.title: Does Explainability Survive Data Drift?

author.name: Samuel Ozechi

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether model explanations decay under data drift even when the feature-target relationship remains stable, and whether pre-drift explanations stay faithful to the replacement model. It highlights that explanation fidelity is rarely monitored in regulated domains like finance and healthcare despite governance requirements.

entry.title: TasteRoute: Personalized Routing for Video Generation

author.name: Zhi Rui Tam, Chao-Chung Wu, Sin-Han Yang, Peyton Ku, Brendan Kuang, Tzu-Ting Hsieh, Min-Fang Hsu, Fang-Ling Tsai, Yun-Nung Chen, Wei-Chiu Ma, Chieh-Yen Lin

entry.summary: TasteRoute is a personalized router for video generation that selects among available text-to-video and image-to-video models based on the request, user preferences, and budget. The paper motivates this by showing annotators agree with a consensus oracle only 34-55% of the time, suggesting preferences are genuinely individual. It matches strong baselines on preference routing while lowering average generation cost.

entry.title: ROT: Rotating Hidden States towards Contextual Vectors for Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs

author.name: Yijing Du, Xiangcheng Zhan, Shuo Yang

entry.summary: ROT is a training-free method against object hallucination in large vision-language models that detects anomalous contextual deviation of hallucinated tokens in intermediate layers, where they show low similarity to both textual and visual contexts. It then rotates hidden state vectors toward contextual vectors in a layer-specific manner, acting on deep semantics more directly than attention-weight interventions. The empirical analysis of where hallucination manifests in hidden states is itself informative.

entry.title: Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? Localizing the Origins of Silent Failures in Agentic Vulnerability Repair

author.name: Wenji Bai, Muhammad Waseem, Zeeshan Rasheed, Jaakko Peltonen, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: The paper proposes SAGE, a trace-based method that localizes the earliest point where an LLM-based coding agent diverges from a task's security intent during vulnerability repair, targeting silent failures that pass syntactic and functional tests but remain insecure. It combines security reasoning assessment at each turn with reconstructed code history. This fills a gap in failure attribution for agentic software engineering with security implications.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and the New Science of Culture

author.name: Douglas R. Guilbeault, Bhargav Srinivasa Desikan, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This position/theory paper argues that cognition and culture are co-constituted and now empirically measurable, proposing that subjectivities be modeled as local trajectories through a high-dimensional cultural field formed by aggregating those trajectories. It claims embedding methods and generative models provide the first general framework for measuring this co-constitution from individual conceptual structure to large-scale ideologies. It outlines testable predictions for a computational science of culture.

entry.title: Agentic schema-guided extraction of materials process knowledge from scientific literature

author.name: Sameer Sadruddin, Jennifer D'Souza

entry.summary: SciKGExtract combines LLM extraction, chemical normalization via PubChem, and agent-based evaluation and refinement to build knowledge graphs of materials synthesis procedures. Evaluation on 176 atomic-layer-deposition papers with expert annotation shows normalization consistently improves extraction F1 across models.

entry.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with GRPO against a proxy of surface features (citation count, legalese density, length) causes the model to stop committing to answers: formatted-answer rates collapse from 0.900 to 0.109 while accuracy on committed answers actually rises. The result reframes reward hacking as strategic abstention rather than capability loss.

entry.title: Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes

author.name: Jungho Kim, Hongjae Shin, Seunghoon Yu, Heecheol Yoo, Myeongjun Kim, Jiyong Oh, Donghyuk Kwak, Seunghyeop Nam, Haesung Oh, Hyunju Kim, Hyungchan Cho, Jaehyun Park, Soo Won Seo, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: Odyssey is a closed-loop end-to-end driving benchmark of 100 scenarios reconstructed from 100-second nuPlan logs, replacing ambiguous directional commands with explicit SD-map routes so the navigation objective is consistent. It enables evaluation of how earlier decisions affect subsequent long-horizon driving, which short-segment benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Harmful Content Generation in Text-to-Image Models: Capabilities and Moderation Limitations

author.name: Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Manos Schinas, Symeon Papadopoulos

entry.summary: A systematic evaluation of harmful content generation across five open text-to-image models using an automated pipeline converting legitimate news captions into unsafe prompts across five harm categories, including built-in safety mechanisms and community fine-tuned bypass variants. Human evaluation of 1,500 images shows high harmful generation rates and exposes moderation limitations.

entry.title: AffordCraft: Scalable Construction of Task-Ready Simulation Assets from Single Images

author.name: Haoyun Yang, Xueyang Zhou, Ziyi Xie, Yongchao Chen

entry.summary: AffordCraft builds simulation-ready articulated objects from a single RGB image and task instruction via retrieval rather than generation: it locates the object and target part, selects a matching articulated asset from a library, and fits it to the image while preserving parts, joints, and physical validity. This avoids the common failure of generative approaches whose predicted parts and joints fail to settle or move in physics simulation. It enables scalable robot learning environments from photos.

entry.title: Learning When to Refine: Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning for Budgeted Neural-Operator PDE Solvers

author.name: Ange Tong

entry.summary: Formulates budgeted adaptive refinement for neural-operator PDE solving, combining a global Fourier neural operator, a local patch-wise corrector, a set-aware selector, and a macro policy that allocates a finite refinement budget over a trajectory. It introduces rollout-verified policy improvement (RV-PI), which evaluates feasible refinement counts through actual continuation rollouts of the learned solver.

entry.title: Shaping the Wind: Nested Potentials for Kinematically Admissible Urban Wind Prediction

author.name: Yidi Wang, Yunhe Zhang, Jiawei Gu, Ziyue Qiao, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a neural surrogate for transient urban wind prediction whose outputs are constrained by construction to satisfy mass conservation and wall impermeability, using a nested-potential output representation. This guarantees kinematically admissible velocity fields that plain velocity-regression surrogates cannot ensure.

entry.title: The Implicit Bias of Hyperbolic Representation Learning for Multiclass Data: A Busemann Risk Perspective

author.name: Xingrun Li, Sho Kuno, Yusuke Mukuta, Xin Yang, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: Provides theory for Riemannian gradient flow in hyperbolic multiclass classification with fixed prototypes, covering general permutation-invariant relative margin losses. A radial/directional decomposition via Busemann functions yields a dichotomy governing whether representation radius diverges toward the ideal boundary or recedes inward.

entry.title: Constant-Curvature Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein for Heterogeneous Cross-Curvature Alignment

author.name: Shanglin Li, Wenjing Lu, Muyang Li, Nicu Sebe, Ziheng Chen

entry.summary: This paper extends Gromov-Wasserstein distances to compare probability distributions living on mixed-curvature spaces (combining hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean components), which previously lacked a unified metric for alignment. It introduces a sliced formulation for tractable cross-curvature alignment and adds explicit geometric consistency mechanisms across component spaces. This matters because mixed-curvature representations are increasingly used for hierarchical and complex data, and distribution comparison across them was an open problem.

entry.title: RELACE: retrospective likelihood-based action credit estimation for long-horizon language agents

author.name: Sayak Chakrabarti, Sathish Reddy Indurthi

entry.summary: RELACE is a critic-free framework for multi-turn LLM agents that combines retrospective action assessment (teacher-forced likelihood scoring of executed actions) with state-conditioned advantage estimation, improving on GRPO's coarse trajectory-level credit and GiGPO's outcome-sensitive estimates. The goal is more precise localization of errors in long-horizon agentic tasks. This contributes to the fast-moving area of credit assignment for agent RL.

entry.title: AlignQuant: Tile-Aligned Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient LLM Generation

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: AlignQuant is a post-training mixed-precision quantization method that uses GPU-compatible 2D weight tiles as the shared unit for precision allocation, storage, and execution, resolving the mismatch between fine-grained precision choices and hardware units. It scores precision reductions using projection-output perturbations weighted by loss gradients under quantized activations, with joint prefill/decode calibration.

entry.title: Learning a Mixture of GFlowNets

author.name: Tiago da Silva, Amauri H. Souza, Salem Lahlou

entry.summary: The paper provides a general theoretical framework for mixtures of GFlowNets, specialized into continuously and discretely indexed collections. It shows continuously indexed mixtures relate to random-features expansions, provably boosting expressivity and reducing instability via sparsity, while ensembling improves exploration over monolithic samplers with lower overhead than prior methods.

entry.title: WASD: Wasserstein-based Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models

author.name: Byeonghu Na, Donghyeok Shin, Yeongmin Kim, Mina Kang, Il-Chul Moon

entry.summary: WASD introduces knowledge distillation for LLMs using a Wasserstein distance over output distributions with a token-embedding-based ground cost, explicitly leveraging token-level semantic similarity rather than per-vocabulary-index divergences. This should better transfer semantic structure from teacher to student.

entry.title: $\alpha$Transfer: Coefficient Transfer for Efficient Model Merging

author.name: Shih-Cheng Huang, Zhi Rui Tam, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Hung-yi Lee, Shao-Hua Sun

entry.summary: The paper shows that within a model family, performance distributions over model-merging coefficients are highly congruent across model sizes, enabling alphaTransfer: search for optimal merging coefficients on a small proxy model and transfer them directly to larger target models. This avoids prohibitively expensive coefficient searches at scale.

entry.title: CANDLE: Cortical Null-Space Decomposition for Noninvasive Brain Source Imaging

author.name: Shuntaro Suzuki, Yuiga Wada, Komei Sugiura

entry.summary: This paper proposes CANDLE, a learning-based electrophysiological source imaging model that estimates cortical source activity from EEG while handling the ill-posedness of the inverse problem. It leverages a null-space prior derived from subject-specific cortical geometry from T1-weighted MRI, improving generalization across individual brain anatomies.

entry.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

author.name: Shoichiro Takeda, Shin'ya Yamaguchi, Satoshi Suzuki, Yasunori Akagi

entry.summary: The paper observes that LoRA's BA-transpose parameterization induces an equivalence relation on (B, A) pairs, forming a quotient manifold of redundant directions. It endows this quotient with an invariant Riemannian metric so optimization respects the geometry, removing redundancy in low-rank fine-tuning.

entry.title: Symphony for Text Generation: Benchmarking Clinical Note Generation

author.name: Daniel Varab, Victor Petr\'en Bach Hansen, Asbj{\o}rn W. Helge, Kevin Pelgrims, Mathias Baltzersen, Adrian Young-San Roessler, Vanessa Klungtvedt, Maximilian Brand, Lasse Krogsb{\o}ll, Henrik Cullen, Lars Maal{\o}e

entry.summary: The authors introduce MedConv, a 300-encounter multilingual clinical dataset in English, Danish, and German, and evaluate the Corti clinical AI platform against two commercial ambient scribes using entailment metrics and LLM-judged comparisons across eight PDSQI-9 dimensions. Results show Corti matches or outperforms leading commercial scribes. The work provides a structured, multilingual evaluation framework for a rapidly growing clinical documentation area.

entry.title: Evolutionary One-Step Generators: Fast and Diverse Sampling for Discrete Design

author.name: Marcus Vukojevic, Erik Nielsen, Veronica Lachi, Andrea Passerini, Giovanni Iacca

entry.summary: EGO trains compact one-step discrete generators using antithetic low-rank evolution strategies combined with distribution matching, structural constraints, and diversity or history-dependent rewards, targeting design tasks like molecular discovery where repeated identical structures waste capacity. The framework handles criteria only computable after hard decoding. It offers a fast alternative to autoregressive or diffusion samplers for discrete design.

entry.title: Climbing the Design Ladder: Sequential Knowledge Distillation for Early-Stage Circuit Timing Prediction

author.name: Reza Moravej, Fahad Rahman Amik, Zhanguang Zhang, Didier Ch\'etelat, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: STEP-KD uses intermediate chip design stages (synthesis, floorplanning, placement) as stepping stones for progressive knowledge distillation to predict post-routing timing from early-stage data, avoiding expensive late-stage iteration loops in IC design.
