author.name: Ran Li, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Shows that prefill-only decision models, which score all candidates in a single forward pass without decoding, have a testable stability property: menu-only interventions can be predicted from the cached first-pass distribution with no labels or second pass. Validated across seven model families and ten datasets with accuracy predicted within about 4.2 points.

entry.title: Pseudowords as probes: Large Language Models show little of the sublexical sensitivity that governs human pseudoword processing

author.name: Jing Chen, Giulia Loca, Simona Amenta, Marco Marelli

entry.summary: Testing five LLMs on Italian two-alternative forced-choice pseudoword experiments against human behavioral baselines, the authors find LLMs align with humans mainly when real-word familiarity cues are available, but fall below even fastText in pseudoword-only conditions. The sublexical form-to-meaning cues that govern human processing do not consistently transfer to LLMs.

entry.title: Wiki-Talkie: Multilingual Benchmarking of Persona-Based Agents on Real-World Discussions

author.name: Dennis Fucci, Andrea Bacciu, Dong Liu, Weronika {\L}ajewska, Saab Mansour

entry.summary: Wiki-Talkie is a new multilingual benchmark of real Wikipedia Talk page conversations across five Germanic and Romance languages, paired with personas derived from real user communities including sociodemographic attributes. It addresses the limitation of prior persona-agent datasets that rely on fictional personas in few languages. This enables more faithful evaluation of LLM agents simulating human social interaction.

entry.title: Beyond Refusal Patterns: Safe-Role Internalization for Robust and Generalizable LLM Safety Alignment

author.name: Jinghao Pang, Jitai Hao, Qiang Huang, Zhaochun Ren, Jun Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SSRFT, which reformulates safety alignment as internalizing a predefined safe role rather than learning surface refusal patterns, building a Safe-Role QA dataset from psychometric questions, limited jailbreak prompts, and safety guidelines. It targets the known weaknesses of shallow safety alignment, over-refusal, and high attack-specific supervision costs of SFT/RLHF. This contributes a generalization-oriented alternative in LLM safety training.

entry.title: Loud and Clear: Dynamic Activation Steering for Improving Speech Intelligibility in Noisy Environments

author.name: Seymanur Akti, Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: Inspired by the human Lombard effect, the authors use activation steering on a TTS model to increase vocal effort and hyper-articulation without retraining, via a prompt-relative mechanism that prevents steering accumulation during generation. The method preserves speaker similarity (89-95%) and improves word error rates in noise across seen and unseen speakers and multiple languages. It matters as a training-free, interpretable way to control acoustic properties.

entry.title: The Failure Is in the Readout: Fine-Grained Emotion Recognition Benchmarks Measure Elicitation, Not Perception

author.name: Tobias Hallmen, Fabian Deuser, Robin-Nico Kampa, Norbert Oswald, Elisabeth Andr\'e

entry.summary: The authors show that off-the-shelf VLMs match or beat the fine-tuned Empathic-Insight-Face model on the EmoNet-Face-HQ 40-category emotion benchmark when answers are read from logits via per-category binary queries rather than freely generated. Keeping images, taxonomy, and ratings fixed, only the readout protocol changes. This demonstrates that benchmark conclusions can reflect generation-format artifacts rather than perceptual limitations.

entry.title: BoT-Feedback: Grounding Multimodal Reasoning in Biomechanical Evidence for Explainable Human Action Feedback

author.name: Xu Dong, Wanqing Li, Anthony Adeyemi-Ejeye, Andrew Gilbert

entry.summary: BoT-Feedback grounds multimodal LLM coaching feedback in structured biomechanical evidence via a four-stage Biomechanics of Thought reasoning pipeline over joint kinematics and posture. This reduces generic advice, hallucination, and poor interpretability in human action feedback generation.

entry.title: LARK: A Low-Cost, Accurate, Occlusion-Resilient, Kalman Filter-Assisted Tracking System for Image-Guided Surgery

author.name: George Sideris, Justin Cree, Andrew Stirling, Mamadou Ly, \'Etienne L\'eger, D. Louis Collins

entry.summary: LARK is a multi-camera optical tracking system for image-guided surgery built from commodity RGB hardware, using multi-view pose fusion and triangulation with adaptive Kalman filtering to achieve occlusion resilience. It was validated against gold-standard stereo infrared trackers using a precision grid and anatomical head phantom. The work aims to make surgical navigation affordable for settings priced out of commercial systems.

entry.title: Anchor-driven Multi-modal Multi-scale Expert Selection for Survival Prediction

author.name: Tao Zhou, Ying Hu, Huazhu Fu, Yi Zhou, Xiao-Jun Wu, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: AM2ES is a framework for cancer survival prediction that integrates histopathology whole-slide images with transcriptomic profiles using anchor-based explicit alignment and multi-scale expert selection. It addresses the entanglement of mismatched morphological and molecular signals in shared latent spaces and adaptively prioritizes clinically relevant tissue scales per patient. Multimodal survival prediction can inform prognosis and treatment planning.

entry.title: TF-PRVR: Training-Free Partially Relevant Video Retrieval

author.name: Giyeol Kim, Chanho Eom

entry.summary: TF-PRVR is presented as the first training-free framework for partially relevant video retrieval, using frozen vision-language features to build hierarchical video representations. It derives temporal semantic signals from frame features and applies frequency-based multi-scale analysis for adaptive temporal boundary detection, avoiding semantic dilution from fixed video decomposition and source-domain overfitting from task-specific training.

entry.title: PhysTacGen: Physics-Aware Visual-Tactile Sensor Image Generation

author.name: Guo Tang, Yongtao Wang

entry.summary: PhysTacGen generates optical-tactile sensor images from visual inputs to augment costly paired visual-tactile data collection for embodied intelligence. It combines material-aware descriptions with geometric conditioning, introducing Group Tactile Policy Optimization (GTPO), an RL strategy that refines a vision-language model to produce structured material descriptions. This bridges the gap between visual appearance and contact-related material properties.

entry.title: PolarScale: A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Radiometrically Consistent RGB-to-Stokes Estimation

author.name: Beibei Lin, Tingting Chen, Xin Zhang, Wenhao Zhao, Dongjun Li, Zifeng Yuan

entry.summary: PolarScale is a new benchmark for predicting polarization (full Stokes parameters, AoLP/DoLP/DoCP) from RGB inputs while explicitly reconstructing the radiometric scale that prior work discarded. By treating scale as a first-class prediction target on scene-referred linear images, it enables physically consistent polarization estimation without specialized hardware.

entry.title: LiDAR Resolution Recovery via Foundation-Model-Guided Diffusion

author.name: Samed Do\u{g}an, Nico Leuze, Alfred Sch\"ottl

entry.summary: The paper fine-tunes a Stable Diffusion-based, LiDAR-conditioned depth model using pseudo-depth targets from a 2D foundation model to recover dense LiDAR scans from heavily decimated beam inputs. It evaluates on nuScenes against physically held-out real beams, separating recovery from fit, and achieves 66.8% delta-1.25 accuracy from just 4-beam input in sparse regimes.

entry.title: Visual Orchestration Tax in Agentic VLM Pipelines: Auditing and Certifying Visual Evidence Reuse

author.name: Lingteng Zeng

entry.summary: The paper identifies visual orchestration tax: the redundancy of repeatedly reconstructing semantically unchanged images at the VLM API boundary as they pass through multi-agent pipelines. It proposes a measurement-to-certification framework with trace-based audit metrics, bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired quality tests, evaluated on chart, document, and multimodal QA benchmarks.

entry.title: Expressiveness, Equivalence, and Uncertainty in Velocity Obstacles and Closest Point of Approach Metrics

author.name: Elizabeth Dietrich, Liam M. Imagawa, Hanna Krasowski, Aurora Haraldsen, Murat Arcak, Kristin Y. Pettersen

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes formal relationships between Velocity Obstacles, TCPA, and DCPA collision-risk metrics, deriving conditions under which they yield equivalent risk characterizations. It extends these metrics to bounded-uncertainty convex relative-state sets and shows independently computed TCPA/DCPA bounds lose the joint relationship required for VO membership.

entry.title: Post-Grasp Kinematic Repair for Robotic Insertion via Object-in-Gripper Reorientation

author.name: Haegu Lee, Christoffer Sloth

entry.summary: This paper studies a neglected problem in industrial insertion: a stable grasp can still be kinematically infeasible because the object-in-gripper transform may drive the robot toward singularities or joint limits. The authors search for small post-grasp reorientations using a branch-aware IK graph that maximizes feasibility margin over the insertion path, aided by a learned task-cost surrogate.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Robotic Manipulation Models with Self-Recursive Pruning

author.name: Zijia Chen, Yuenan Hou, Yu Li, Weijie Li, Li Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Loss-Conditioned Activation-Moment (LCAM) pruning, a training-free unstructured pruning method tailored to robotic manipulation policies rather than image recognition criteria. It ranks connections using weight contributions, activation moments from calibration demonstrations, and output-direction sensitivity to preserve closed-loop action behavior.

entry.title: MRPilot: Supervising and Intervening LLM-Based Multi-Robot Teams through Mixed Reality

author.name: Xiaoran Yang, Xun Qian, Yang Zhan, Nathan Tran, Ziyi Liu, Qiao Jin

entry.summary: MRPilot is a mixed reality interface that lets non-expert users inspect and intervene in LLM-coordinated multi-robot teams across four stages: forming, reviewing, following, and repairing. Robot-team plans are represented as structured commitments in synchronized situated and overview views, grounded in a formative study with 12 users.

entry.title: Empirical-Bayes spectral partial pooling across related tasks

author.name: Lorenzo Mauri

entry.summary: This work introduces an empirical Bayes approach to partial pooling of spectral estimators in high-dimensional factor models across related but heterogeneous tasks, interpolating between per-task estimation and full pooling. The method aims to stabilize leading singular-vector-based estimates when per-task sample sizes are limited relative to dimension.

entry.title: Encouraging general generalisation: Teaching Gemma (To Articulate) Why

author.name: fabricius

entry.summary: The author builds a constitution for Gemma 3 27B-IT and proposes a new axis of alignment generalization: across principles, where training on one constitution clause improves adherence to held-out clauses. Using RL that rewards correct citations of the constitution during reasoning, they compare alignment approaches and find that SFT on synthetic dilemmas generalizes poorly relative to the articulation-based method.

entry.title: Unlocking Earth AI’s planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google research blog post describing applications of the Earth AI planetary-scale geospatial foundation models to global public health problems, presumably including disease mapping and environmental health analysis. The available excerpt contains only a title, so technical details are limited.

entry.title: Dynamic Routing as a New Dimension for Test-time Versatility of LLMs

author.name: Michal \v{S}tef\'anik, Marek Kadl\v{c}\'ik, Josef Kucha\v{r}, Michal Spiegel

entry.summary: The paper investigates dynamic routing programs that execute or iterate subsets of an LLM's layers as a second axis of test-time adaptation beyond chain-of-thought token spending, gradient-free. It asks whether such programs can be identified from only 3-10 demonstrations by a strategy that transfers across models and tasks without training.

entry.title: RETRACE: From Entangled Repair Histories to Reusable Experience for CI Repair

author.name: Rabeya Khatun Muna, Muhammad Ahasanuzzaman, Nakhla Rafi, Yisen Xu, Jinqiu Yang, Tse-Hsun Chen

entry.summary: Presents RETRACE, a framework for reconstructing problem-level repair experience from entangled software histories where pull requests mix multiple CI problems, failed attempts, and unrelated changes. It combines a backward endpoint view of retained changes with a forward development view of commit evolution, reconciled by CI execution evidence. This enables LLM agents to reuse cleaner, aligned repair experience.

entry.title: ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Penghui Yang, Long Xing, Xuanlang Dai, Ziyu Liu, Kai Chen, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: ResOPD improves sparse on-policy distillation, where student models train on self-generated trajectories with only sampled-token scores or small Top-k teacher distributions transmitted. It resolves the dilemma between unbiased-but-high-variance sampled-token estimators and biased Top-k objectives by providing unbiased full-vocabulary reverse KL gradient estimation via tail residualization. This is relevant to efficiently distilling large reasoning teachers into smaller students.

entry.title: LogSig-SSM: Time-Series Modelling with Multi-Scale Log-Signature Compression for State-Space Models

author.name: Felix Oury, Nicolas Calvo Peiro, Reiko J. Tanaka

entry.summary: LogSig-SSM compresses long, irregularly sampled multivariate time series into shorter token sequences using multi-scale windowed log-signatures from rough path theory, then processes them with selective state-space models like Mamba. This combines NCDE/NRDE-style irregular-sampling handling with SSM linear scaling.

entry.title: IRSTD-Agent: Agentic Infrared Small Target Detection via Zoom-Guided Interaction Learning

author.name: Jiawen Xi, Yu Zhang, Tianyi Zhao, Zhu Liu, Maoxun Yuan, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: IRSTD-Agent is an agentic framework in which an MLLM adaptively decides where and at what scale to inspect an image for infrared small-target detection, using five complementary tools (proposal, zoom, detect, drop, refine) to progressively gather fine-grained visual evidence. The dynamic visual search addresses MLLMs' weakness at localizing tiny targets in maritime and aerial surveillance imagery. Results indicate improved localization over standard MLLM-based approaches.

entry.title: Differentiable Bit-Widths: Co-optimizing Pruning and Quantization via SVD for Ultra-Efficient LLM Compression

author.name: Hankyul Kang, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: The authors propose unifying SVD-based pruning and quantization for LLM compression by learning differentiable, component-wise bit-widths, co-optimizing both stages instead of running them sequentially. This addresses the suboptimality of decoupled pipelines under aggressive compression ratios. The approach aims at ultra-efficient deployment of large language models.

entry.title: Lock-in EP: An In-Situ Training Algorithm for Oscillatory Hardware

author.name: Sowjanya Tammali, Wilkie Olin-Ammentorp

entry.summary: The paper derives lock-in equilibrium propagation (LIEP), a training method providing local gradient information for oscillatory analog networks without separate forward and backward sweeps, enabling in-situ learning on energy-efficient analog hardware. It is demonstrated for both training from scratch and recovering performance after parameter perturbation, with a formulation connecting to contrastive Hebbian learning. This targets robustness of analog computing to component variability.

entry.title: Who Bears the Burden? Learning Responsibility for Shared Constraints in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaoyang Cao, Jingqi Li, Zhe Fu, Alexandre M. Bayen

entry.summary: The paper introduces LiRA, which learns each agent's share of a common Lagrange multiplier enforcing a shared cost budget by optimizing social welfare, redistributing penalty influence without altering rewards or constraints. The authors provide analysis for convex games showing how responsibility shares shape outcomes.

entry.title: Detecting a Shift Is Not Enough: Exact Minimax Limits of Linear Representation Repair

author.name: Anuar Aimoldin, Yankai Chen, Ayana Mussabayeva, Xue Liu

entry.summary: This work casts removal of mean shifts between data sources as a statistical decision problem: learning a single linear map under a hard distortion budget that minimizes residual shift on fresh data. It derives the exact finite-sample minimax risk in closed form and shows that simple projection of the calibration mean difference attains this bound without knowledge of noise parameters.

entry.title: A Systematic Study of Small Language Models on Abstract Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Nur A Zarin Nishat, Jens Lehmann, Andrei Aioanei, Sahar Vahdati

entry.summary: Across more than 1,000 runs on the ARC-TGI benchmark, the authors profile decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and mixture-of-experts small language models under supervised fine-tuning, examining whether models learn transferable rules versus distribution-specific heuristics. The study covers skill acquisition efficiency, out-of-distribution robustness, and layer-wise attention signatures.

entry.title: A Single-Loop, Constant-Batch First-Order Penalty Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Xingyu Chen, Ming Yang, Quanqi Hu, Tianbao Yang

entry.summary: Develops SICO, a single-loop, constant-batch first-order penalty method for nonconvex-strongly convex stochastic bilevel optimization, combining two time-scale updates to avoid nested loops and large batches. The method achieves improved sample complexity rates without second-order derivative oracles under standard assumptions.

entry.title: APEX: Speculate smarter, not deeper

author.name: Manvi Jha, Zach Zhang, Zhichao Xu, Linbo Liu, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Vinayak Arannil

entry.summary: APEX is a learned controller for speculative decoding that selects among EAGLE-3, n-gram, and draft-model speculation per request while adaptively adjusting draft depth at each verification block. It balances decoding speed against wasted draft computation, which fixed configurations cannot do as generation predictability changes.

entry.title: Closing Ambient Clinical Documentation Gaps with Automated Provider Queries

author.name: Joseph Paul Cohen, Raj Shah, Han-Chin Shing, Fang Wang, Susan Nguyen, Chaitanya Shivade, Jack Moriarty

entry.summary: The paper studies automating the DAU (Draft, Ask, Update) loop where clinical documentation specialists send clarifying queries to physicians to close note gaps, building five transcript-degradation benchmarks from an audit of 3,000 real visits and analyzing 21k clarification turns. Findings show useful-question predictors are task-specific, with oracle confidence dominant but simple recall sufficing for note completeness. It fills a gap left by prior work that assumed complete transcripts.

entry.title: SAGE: Semantic Anchor-Guided Evolution for Grounded Medical QA Data Synthesis

author.name: Chuan Li, Chengyu Wang, Cen Chen, Ye Lyu, Mingyuan Fan, Ming Gao

entry.summary: SAGE is a data synthesis framework that lets small, locally deployed models generate high-quality medical QA training data by using lightweight public taxonomies like MeSH as semantic anchors to ground and guide generation. It targets clinical settings constrained by privacy, limited expert annotation, and inability to use cloud APIs or large open corpora.

entry.title: When Old Facts Return: Re-Reads, Reverts, and the Limits of Temporal Memory

author.name: Neeraj Yadav (Called It Inc.)

entry.summary: This study isolates an ambiguity in temporal memory systems: a re-read of an old source and a genuine revert can produce identical observed value sequences while requiring opposite current answers. On 130 atomic transitions from software fixes, a verbatim re-read of a retired value drops accuracy from 98.5% to 10.8%, and a simple guard refusing reactivation restores 97.7%. It matters because it exposes and fixes a concrete failure mode of memory-based agents.

entry.title: Anchor and Adapt: Asymmetric Prompt Adaptation for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mengyang Zhao, Teng Fu, Haiyang Yu, Ke Niu, Bin Li, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: Anchor and Adapt is a two-stage prompt learning framework for few-shot industrial anomaly detection that first learns transferable normal/abnormal anchors from auxiliary annotated data and then adapts a normal branch to target appearance with anchors fixed. This removes the need for product-specific manual anomaly descriptions.

entry.title: Beyond Training from Scratch: Foundation Models for Data-Efficient and Generalizable Cardiac MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Anam Hashmi, Mayug Maniparambil, Julia Dietlmeier, Kathleen M. Curran, Noel E. O'Connor

entry.summary: This work investigates using pretrained vision foundation models (CLIP, BiomedCLIP, DINOv2) as priors for accelerated cardiac MRI reconstruction, integrating frozen and parameter-efficiently adapted encoders in a transformer reconstruction architecture. The approach improves robustness under data scarcity and distribution shifts compared to task-specific training from scratch. This supports faster MRI scans while preserving diagnostic quality with less task-specific data.

entry.title: 2D Spatial Reasoning with Adaptive Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Martin Spitznagel, Janis Keuper

entry.summary: The authors introduce aNCA, an adaptive neural cellular automata architecture using deformable convolutions to dynamically adjust perceptive fields and iteratively reason over 2D spatial relations on grid data. It achieves strong, generalizable results on puzzle-style spatial reasoning tasks such as Sudoku and maze shortest-path finding.

entry.title: OntoPlan: An Ontology-Grounded Scene Representation and Agentic Framework for Scalable Robot Task Planning

author.name: Hyeongwoo Nam, Woongje Cho, Juwon Kim, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: OntoPlan grounds LLM-based robot task planning in an ontology-aligned scene representation of objects, spaces, relations, and states, with an agentic framework that selectively retrieves task-relevant information to control token cost and enforce action preconditions. It targets long-horizon planning in large environments.

entry.title: Magnet-Aware Control of Legged Robots

author.name: J. Playan Garai, S. B. Djuve, C. McGreavy, M. Khadiv

entry.summary: This paper presents a control framework for legged robots operating in the strong magnetic fields of Big Science facilities, including a custom MuJoCo plugin for magnetic forces and an inverse field-estimation method that infers the latent field from quadruped dynamic responses and sensor readings. The framework dynamically compensates spatially varying magnetic wrenches to maintain stability.

entry.title: Mission-Aware Attestation Envelopes for Time-Critical Autonomous Action: A Hardware-in-the-Loop V2I Study

author.name: Dimitrios Nikou, Nikolaos Kekatos, Sophia Petridou, Stylianos Basagiannis

entry.summary: The paper formulates remote attestation for autonomous systems as a runtime assurance contract that jointly requires integrity validity, evidence freshness, and decision latency within a physically derived deadline. This yields four operational outcomes instead of a binary gate, distinguishing tampering-induced refusals from latency-induced ones, evaluated in a hardware-in-the-loop V2I study.

entry.title: REACT: Physically and Chemically Consistent Reconstruction of Marine Active Tracers

author.name: Wenbin Dai, Hao Zheng, Shiyu Liang, Chaofan Sun, Xueying Zhang, Hanbo Huang, Xuan Gong, Yiran Zhang, Enhui Liao

entry.summary: REACT is a carbonate-aware AI method for reconstructing global sea surface pH from sparse observations, addressing the fact that pH is an active carbonate tracer where the prediction target differs from the conserved carbon inventory (DIC). Prior black-box or physics-guided models designed for passive tracers can achieve low pH error while violating carbonate closure and conservation constraints.

entry.title: Auditing Pairwise Equivalence Judgments: Self-Critique Effects and Diversity Measurement in Multi-Agent Hypothesis Generation

author.name: Ji Young Byun, Anthony Hu, Jesse Rogers, Roujia Wang, Manasa Kesapragada, Falgun Shah

entry.summary: This study examines two evaluation questions underlying multi-agent LLM hypothesis generation: how much self-critique changes delivered hypotheses beyond run-to-run variability, and how the pairwise equivalence rule used to group hypotheses affects measured diversity. Across four proprietary instances with fixed opening hypotheses and varied refinement rounds, it audits the reliability of the equivalence judgments on which diversity claims rest.

entry.title: Agentic AI with Structured CoT for Enhancing AI's Spatial Intelligence: Visualization and Reasoning of Rotation

author.name: Uttamasha Monjoree, Wei Yan

entry.summary: The authors evaluate the spatial rotation reasoning of an existing generative agentic model (GPT-5.6, GA June 2026) using an augmented version of the Revised Purdue Spatial Visualization Test with added graphical and contextual features, comparing how different structured chain-of-thought strategies affect 3D rotation understanding. The work documents persistent spatial reasoning limits even in frontier models.

entry.title: CRAFT: An Agentic Spreadsheet Form Filling System with Template Awareness

author.name: Leyao Gu, Yingjie Xiong, Zirui Tang, Jiangtao Zhou, Yeye He, Chunwei Liu, Xuanhe Zhou, Fan Wu

entry.summary: CRAFT is a template-aware agent framework for spreadsheet form filling that couples reflective validation with constrained local repair: it grounds detected errors to spreadsheet regions, restores corrupted template state, and re-grounds writable slots before further edits. A Rectangle-Aware Slot Grounder proposes writable cells while protected regions constrain edits, preventing early mistakes from cascading. Practical agentic document manipulation is an increasingly important applied area.

entry.title: PermVLA: Factorization Order as a Regularizer for VLA Learning

author.name: Yanqiao Chen, Yuhan Rui, Dongsheng Hou, Zijie Nie, Yutong Wan, Qi Hao

entry.summary: PermVLA identifies factorization order in vision-language-action policies as an overlooked regularization choice, introducing causally anchored permutation that samples action reveal orders while retaining deterministic left-to-right control at deployment. Its conditional-set augmentation trains one shared policy to predict actions from different known subsets of the same chunk without extra demonstrations, discouraging reliance on privileged chunk-prefix information.

entry.title: Agent Behavior as Code: Efficient and Robust LLM Agents with Programmatic Specifications

author.name: Peng Qi, Chunliang Lyu, Gang Li, Fabian Chan, Cheng Chang, Ignacio Cases, Will Lu

entry.summary: ABCAgent specifies agent behavior as symbolic programs (Python code with optional neural functions), addressing error propagation, repeated FM-call costs for recurring tasks, and limited context/instruction-following in foundation-model agents. Compiling behavior into programs promises robustness, cost reduction, and better context management for complex plans.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Time-Series Question Answering via Decoupled Perception and Reasoning

author.name: Jing Xie, Haochen Yuan, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: TSHarness is an agentic framework for cross-dataset zero-shot time-series QA that decouples numerical perception from contextual reasoning via a structured Time-Series Perception State, with a learned tool selector invoking numerical tools and a reusable analytical memory. It targets the common failure of time-series methods overfitting to specific datasets. This contributes to making LLMs reliably handle numerical, time-series reasoning without domain-specific training.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Limited Clustering Gains: A Controlled Study of Multilingual Company Entity Resolution

author.name: Yijiashun Qi, Yuxuan Li, Hanzhe Guo

entry.summary: This controlled study adapts multilingual E5 encoders for company entity resolution under fixed candidate budgets and shows that substantially improving retrieval recall (from 53.74% to 76.98% direct pair recall with a multi-view selector) yields only marginal clustering gains. The finding that downstream clustering is bottlenecked by the pair classifier rather than retrieval is an important negative-style result.

entry.title: How Should a Prompt Optimizer Spend a Tight Budget? BudgetAPO with Noise-Adaptive Evaluation

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Zhichao Wang, Huanyu Yan, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: BudgetAPO addresses automatic prompt optimization under tight API budgets, where established methods like GEPA and OPRO require hundreds to thousands of model calls. It uses a single-stage design with a noise-adaptive rule that sizes evaluation slices to each task's measured noise level. This makes prompt optimization practical behind paid, rate-limited APIs where extensive evaluation is infeasible.

entry.title: Auditable Clinical Timeline Reconstruction with Provenance-Aware Evidence Graphs

author.name: Judith Jeyafreeda Andrew

entry.summary: The paper tests a patient-timeline reconstruction system on provenance-aware Evidence Graph operators that preserve mention links, record fact revisions, and abstain when evidence is absent, evaluated on a synthetic corpus of 1,000 patients and 3,353 notes. The operators compress graph size substantially while preserving answers, and gate experiments reveal that LLM and BioClinicalBERT abstention responds mainly to announced omissions rather than evidence absence.

entry.title: CVIF: A Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework for Geometric Diagram Understanding in MLLMs

author.name: Jiahui Kang, Bifan Wei, Lingling Zhang, Tianwen Jiang, Qiuyong Xiao, Jihong Zhang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: CVIF is a training-free, inference-time method that improves multimodal LLM understanding of geometric diagrams by localizing critical layers during the transition from evidence aggregation to semantic decoding and applying visual interventions there. It includes a Geometry-Constrained Local Relation Reconstruction module and adaptive visual steering to counter reliance on textual priors over visual evidence.

entry.title: Conditional Rank Allocation for Taxonomy-Aware Medical Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Guangyuan Dong, Ziwei Hong, Xuehao Zhou, Zidong Yu, Bingchen Liu, Kehan Liu, Chuang Liu, Rong Fu, Yuchao Hou

entry.summary: ARBOR is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that dynamically selects rank-one components from a shared low-rank basis per question, using a gating mechanism that combines question representations with specialty and operation tags for medical question answering. The authors provide a theoretical motivation showing conditional selection can avoid an approximation floor of fixed-rank updates, and demonstrate gains on Qwen3-8B across CMB, CMExam, MedQA, and MedMCQA benchmarks with five-seed experiments.

entry.title: Using Process Mining to Generate AI Agents from Software Engineering Process Records

author.name: Saimir Bala, Fabiana Fournier, Lior Limonad, Andreas Metzger

entry.summary: The paper tackles agent granularity and role design in hybrid human-AI software teams by combining object-centric, imperative, and declarative process mining on repository event logs. The approach discovers project-specific process structures that determine the right granularity and separation of concerns for agents, rather than relying on predefined role frameworks.

entry.title: From Requirements to Attack Trees: Grounded LLM Agents for Design-Time Security Review

author.name: Akash Iyer, Taha Demirkan, Keerthi Koneru, Aaryan Siddharthan, Sheethal Kumar, Ramesh Radhakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent LLM framework for design-time security analysis that operates on product requirement documents and architecture diagrams before code exists. The framework parses diagrams into graph representations, generates misuse cases, constructs attack trees, checks governance and compliance gaps, recommends mitigations, and proposes revised architectures for expert review. Notably it avoids retrieving from Common Weakness Enumeration, relying instead on grounded reasoning.

entry.title: Selective Backpropagation for Efficient Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Eeham Khan, Abdulmoumen Al-Atrash, Ali Ayub

entry.summary: The paper proposes Selective Backpropagation (SBP), a deterministic parameter budgeting framework for few-shot class-incremental learning that restricts gradient updates to a pre-allocated subset of network parameters. This bridges the trade-off between efficient fine-tuning with catastrophic forgetting and memory-heavy replay methods. SBP targets settings with strict compute and memory constraints, such as edge deployment.

entry.title: FTD-GNO: Memory-Efficient Graph Neural Operators through Functional Tensor Decomposition of the Kernel

author.name: Xiaomin Zhang, Boyue Wang, Junbin Gao, Yongli Hu anbd Baocai Yin

entry.summary: FTD-GNO addresses the computational and memory overhead of graph neural operators used as PDE surrogate models by decomposing the monolithic integral kernel into low-dimensional mode-wise functions via CP, Tensor-Train, and Tucker formats. This enables scaling to high resolutions and large graph neighborhoods. It is a meaningful efficiency contribution for scientific machine learning.

entry.title: RRM-GPT: A Framework and Vision for Radio Resource Management Foundation Models

author.name: Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Akram Bin Sediq, Koosha Pourtahmasi Roshandeh, Omar Mashaal, Ahmad M. Nagib, Jale Sadreddini, Hatem Abou-Zeid

entry.summary: RRM-GPT proposes an autoregressive foundation model framework for radio resource management in which an encoder tokenizes heterogeneous network observations and a decoder generates decisions field by field, conditioned on network state and previously committed fields, mimicking how language models generate text. Pretraining on unannotated network logs aims to make RRM models reusable across functions and deployments. It offers a unifying vision for a fragmented subfield.

entry.title: Localization Lens for Improving Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hasan Farooq, Murtaza Taj, Mehwish Nasim, Arif Mahmood

entry.summary: Proposes a localization-aware enhancement for medical vision-language models addressing their weakness in anatomical structure and spatial understanding. The approach introduces expert-validated localization-lens representations, pixel-shuffle-based architectural filtering to manage increased input complexity, and alignment improvements across data, architecture, and alignment levels. This targets spatial reasoning crucial for medical applications.

entry.title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment

author.name: Pronoma Banerjee, Anuva Shah, Jason Wu, Md. Masudur Rahman, Sanjay Mohanty, Satya Kurada, Juan P. Wachs

entry.summary: ARISE is an agentic planning framework that models few-shot medical image understanding as a sequential workflow with image-grounded self-evaluation, applied to inflammatory bowel disease assessment via capsule endoscopy and intestinal ultrasound. It targets known VLM weaknesses in clinical settings: hallucination, weak domain-specific reasoning, and poor interpretability. Clinical translation of this kind could reduce dependence on scarce specialist expertise.

entry.title: Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild

author.name: Yifan Xiong, Jingyi Ge, Zhenpeng Chen, Yiling Lou

entry.summary: This is the first empirical study of test adequacy for agent harnesses, the software infrastructure around backbone LLMs in real agentic systems. The analysis finds harness code, particularly LLM-dependent harness code that processes model outputs and governs behavior, is substantially undertested, raising reliability concerns. The paper also proposes enhancements to improve harness testing practices.

entry.title: A Graph-Based Inspection and Intervention Tool for Assessing Mechanistic Learning in PINNs

author.name: Adwait Patkhedkar, Alifaraz Lakhani, Prathmesh Mohite, Abhijeet Salunke

entry.summary: GIIT maps the nodes of a physics dependency graph onto internal components of physics-informed neural networks via sensitivity analysis, then tests those mappings under targeted interventions. The study finds that under out-of-distribution temporal extrapolation, layer-wise correspondences drift and the model can show low physics residuals without genuine mechanistic understanding.

entry.title: Discrete Action Matching: Learning Stochastic Dynamics from Samples via State Graphs

author.name: Mikhail Persiianov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: Discrete Action Matching (DAM) extends Action Matching to finite-state settings using discrete Wasserstein geometry, deriving an action-minimization objective for minimum-kinetic-energy currents whose density dependence reduces to neighboring density ratios. The learned fields also yield a graph-supported Markov sampler for population dynamics from unpaired marginals.

entry.title: Revisiting Ground-Truth Synthesis from High-Speed Video: Exact Validity Conditions and an Audited Consumer Capture Corpus

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Sumaiya Rahim Suma

entry.summary: The paper derives exact validity conditions for synthesizing motion-deblurring ground truth by averaging high-frame-rate frames, showing the common central-frame label is unbiased only for odd windows with equal frame durations, while even windows systematically shift labels and unequal durations convolve supervision. An audit of 51 nominally 240 fps smartphone clips finds many captured near 176 fps, detectable only in container timing metadata. This exposes previously unrecognized flaws in a standard dataset construction practice.

entry.title: Human-Like Attention? A Psychophysical Comparison of Visual Search in Humans and MLLMs

author.name: Renchi Zhang, Joost C. F. de Winter, Dimitra Dodou, Harleigh C. Seyffert, Yke Bauke Eisma

entry.summary: This study compares visual search performance between 1,250 humans and multimodal LLMs using identical 2D and 3D stimuli, finding strong correlations in error rates (rho = 0.82) and similar difficulty signatures across feature and conjunction searches. Differences also emerge, particularly in set-size sensitivity patterns.

entry.title: Cut Binary Cross Entropy: Efficient Large-Vocabulary Loss and Gradient Kernels for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yaoyiran Li, Haowen Ning, Mohamed Hammad

entry.summary: CutBCE is an exact, hardware-accelerated BCE loss and gradient operator in JAX/Pallas for large-vocabulary multi-label recommendation, avoiding the prohibitive O(BNV) memory cost of materializing dense logits. It fills a gap since chunked loss optimizations existed for softmax CE in LLMs but not large-scale multi-label BCE.

entry.title: Nexus: An Execution Fabric for AI Agents Across Cloud, Edge, and Devices

author.name: Cary Chang, Jialin Zhou

entry.summary: Nexus is a cloud-edge platform that treats each agent invocation as a persistent task with lifecycle management covering failures, recovery, results, usage, and settlement. It uses an OpenWrt-based runtime to give a unified execution abstraction with permission control across computers, mobile devices, and edge environments, addressing scaling, reliability, and cost limitations of cloud-centric agent designs.

entry.title: Non-invasive Seizure Detection Using Wearable Wrist-worn Accelerometry and Deep Learning

author.name: Nilushika Udayangani Hewa Dehigahawattage, Kishor Nandakishor, Marimuthu Palaniswami

entry.summary: The authors develop a wearable seizure detection system using a single wrist-worn accelerometer and deep learning, aiming to replace expensive, hospital-bound video-EEG monitoring and unreliable seizure diaries. The system detects multiple seizure types, including shorter-duration events, for long-term ambulatory monitoring. This has clear potential for improving epilepsy care outside clinical settings.

entry.title: Investigating Query-Insensitive Behavior in Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Eryk Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Alberto Presta, Karol Szurkowski, Michal Byra

entry.summary: This study shows that state-of-the-art spatio-temporal video grounding models still produce plausible predictions even when queries are irrelevant to the video or entirely removed, revealing query-insensitive behavior. The authors analyze HCSTVG-v2 and VidSTG datasets to identify regularities that may encourage this shortcut behavior. The work exposes an underexplored evaluation limitation in STVG benchmarks.

entry.title: Adaptive Mean Flow for Responsive Closed-Loop Robot Control

author.name: Aksel Vaaler, Marco Job, Christian Holden, Olav Egeland

entry.summary: The paper introduces Adaptive Mean Flow (AMF), a flow-based imitation learning method that reduces the prediction latency of diffusion/flow robot policies, enabling high-frequency closed-loop control without committing to long open-loop action chunks. This addresses a known weakness of iterative denoising policies that causes jittery motion. Improved responsiveness could improve policy stability across manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Anlu: Enabling In-Context Time Series Anomaly Detection in Foundation Models via Counterfactual Supervision

author.name: Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Meng Wang, Yue Pan, Wenjun He, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies in-context learning for time series anomaly detection where a reference record conditions the expected behavior, and introduces counterfactual supervision pairing each query with two references implying different labels to prevent the model from ignoring the reference. This addresses regime-dependent anomaly semantics where the same pattern is anomalous in one regime and routine in another. The technique enables reference-conditioned detection with frozen model parameters.

entry.title: SpatialChain: A Benchmark for Auditing Spatial Reasoning Faithfulness in VLMs

author.name: Rafael Teixeira Sousa, Vin\'icius Paulo Lopes de Oliveira, Elisa Ayumi Masasi de Oliveira, Luiza Martins de Freitas Cintra, Fernanda Bufon F\"arber, Igor Dias Aguiar, Julia Yasmim de Almeida Nobre, Arlindo Rodrigues Galv\~ao Filho

entry.summary: SpatialChain pairs spatially oriented GQA questions with scene-graph-grounded reasoning chains and a two-axis evaluation combining chain-overlap metrics with a scene-graph-aware LLM judge, auditing whether correct answers reflect faithful reasoning or linguistic shortcuts. Applied to nine thinking-enabled VLMs, it surfaces findings invisible to standard accuracy metrics.

entry.title: Word-Level Text Unmixing via Evidence-Preserving Ownership Routing with Language Models

author.name: Jinglin He, Siyang Jiang, Lixing He, Guoliang Xing, Hongkai Chen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Word-Level Text Unmixing: recovering original source sequences from an interleaved lexical stream while preserving every word and its order exactly. The proposed EPOR method decouples source-ownership prediction from reconstruction, adapting a causal LLM to route words to owners rather than generating separated texts, which avoids omission, duplication, and hallucination. Applications include overlapping transcripts, document flows, and concurrent agent streams.

entry.title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing

author.name: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Anna Fr\"uhst\"uck

entry.summary: UniSlider decouples the slider control from the underlying strength parameter in generative image editing, requiring perceptual distance from the input to grow linearly with slider value. Current methods suffer from non-monotone trajectories, dead zones, and abrupt changes because the slider merely rescales an adapter coefficient or prompt weight. The proposed approach enforces monotone, perceptually uniform trajectories for intuitive continuous editing.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Sample Complexity for Recursive Entropic Risk Reinforcement Learning with a Generative Model

author.name: Amirparsa Bahrami, Oliver Mortensen, Mohammad Sadegh Talebi

entry.summary: Provides refined PAC guarantees for model-based risk-sensitive Q-value iteration in finite discounted MDPs under recursive entropic risk with a generative model, for both value and policy learning. The bounds reduce the exponential dependence on the effective horizon compared with prior guarantees and match existing lower bounds in relevant regimes.

entry.title: STOCK-JEPA: Prior-Anchored Latent Revision Representation Learning in Equity Markets

author.name: Yizhi Luo, Jiahe Yi, Jianhui Zhang, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Stock-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture for equity markets that learns predictable incremental revisions relative to statistics produced by a simple, interpretable financial prior model. The approach aims to combine the interpretability of classic linear financial models with the flexibility of deep representation learning in low signal-to-noise financial data.

entry.title: Learning What to Distill: Bilevel Top-K Token Selection for Self-Distillation in Large Language Models

author.name: Heng Liang, Xinwen Zhang, Hongchang Gao

entry.summary: BiToK-SD proposes a bilevel optimization scheme that adaptively learns which token positions are most beneficial to distill in on-policy self-distillation, replacing uniform or fixed-heuristic token selection. The goal is transferring reasoning ability from large LLMs to compact models without an external teacher. This targets the practical problem of cheap reasoning-capable small models.

entry.title: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?

author.name: Aadi Chauhan, Arthur Ilyasov

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares five mechanisms for supplying action-type information to a small GUI grounding model (Qwen2-VL-2B fine-tuned with LoRA), under matched data, compute, and decoding budgets. With rigorous multi-seed statistics, auxiliary losses, additive embeddings, and prompt words gain 5-7 hit@0.10 points over baseline, while hard routing and prepended tokens do not.

entry.title: Hub for Outliers, Spokes for Inliers: Uniform Latent Space Construction for Dual-Mismatched Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Li Yuan, Yaxin Hou, Jiawei Tang, Yongbiao Gao, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: This paper addresses semi-supervised learning when unlabeled data is imbalanced and contains unknown classes, proposing a hub-spoke latent geometry where known classes cluster uniformly around a central hub. The hub anchors a low-evidence region that isolates unknown-class samples, improving pseudo-label quality and feature discriminability.

entry.title: SIFT: Search Intent-to-Filter Transformer for Multi-Task Personalized Filter Ranking at Airbnb

author.name: Shashank Dabriwal, Tanya Piplani, Hao Li, Yiwei Wang, Ashish Jain, Kedar Bellare, Stephanie Moyerman

entry.summary: This industry paper presents SIFT, a transformer-based ranking model deployed at Airbnb that learns guest preferences directly from raw behavioral sequences to recommend search filters, replacing hand-engineered pre-aggregated ETL features. A unified guest representation feeds multiple prediction tasks including booking likelihood, lifting booking conversion.

entry.title: Privileged Context as Drift in On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Ravenor Davion, Nick Rui

entry.summary: This work studies how the design of privileged context affects policy drift in on-policy self-distillation, where a language model trains to match itself conditioned on extra context. It systematically varies content and source of the privileged context across nine combinations on Qwen2.5-7B, motivated by reducing catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Revisiting Temporal Regularization for Smooth Control in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: SungJae Ahn, Jeong Woon Lee, Kyoleen Kwak, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: This paper re-examines temporal regularization in deep RL, proving that a temporal penalty on action differences along transitions bounds expected action differences between states sharing a next state, thereby providing spatial smoothness effects. This challenges prior assumptions and offers a cheaper route to smooth policies for physical robot deployment.

entry.title: Mu-DisCoCat: A Variational Pipeline for Compositional Generalization on Quantum Processors

author.name: Mina Abbaszadeh, Matilda Karabina Moore, Raem Haq, Martha Lewis, Mehrnoosh Sadrzadeh

entry.summary: Mu-DisCoCat extends the compositional distributional semantics (DisCoCat) framework to multimodal settings by mapping its tensor structure onto variational quantum circuits, aiming at compositional concept generalization. The pipeline first learns stable representations of primitives before composing them for novel situations. It is an early exploration of quantum methods for a classic AI generalization problem.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Graph Abstention for Reliable Selective Forecasting

author.name: Jianxiang Xie, Belal Alsinglawi

entry.summary: The paper improves selective forecasting gates by treating instance-level plausibility and cross-variable relational consistency as separate reliability axes, learning a sparse graph with a Dirichlet-style structural energy to detect forecasts that violate inter-variable dependencies. Across seven benchmarks and four backbones, structural gating often reduces selective MSE at matched coverage versus prior methods like TEM. This matters for trustworthy multivariate time-series deployment.

entry.title: Learning PDE solution operators with variable initial conditions via Latent Dynamics Networks

author.name: Stefano Maria Pizzamiglio, Stefano Pagani, Francesco Regazzoni

entry.summary: The authors extend Latent Dynamics Networks, which combine neural ODEs with nonlinear dimensionality reduction, to handle variable initial conditions while preserving the original end-to-end training procedure. This removes a key limitation for many-query PDE surrogate modeling where systems start from varying states. The work improves the applicability of latent-space surrogates for physical simulation.

entry.title: MetaLearnNCA: Few-Shot Offline Meta-Learning via Interacting Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Etienne Guichard, Stefano Nichele

entry.summary: MetaLearnNCA achieves few-shot adaptation through the dynamical interaction of coupled neural cellular automata: an Active-NCA performs task inference on a 2D spatial memory grid called a spatial program, while a learned Meta-NCA modulates it, avoiding test-time backpropagation. The design preserves native 2D spatial geometry that flattened feature-based meta-learning discards. It is a novel decentralized take on gradient-free meta-learning.

entry.title: Less Is More: A Leakage-Controlled Study of Dermoscopic Preprocessing for Joint Skin Lesion Classification and Segmentation with YOLO26

author.name: Truong Viet Vu, Nguyen Chi Hai, Nguyen Phuc Nguyen, Ngo Hoang Tu, Vo Nguyen Quoc Bao, Nguyen Thai Anh

entry.summary: The study re-evaluates handcrafted dermoscopic preprocessing and augmentation under a leakage-controlled, lesion-disjoint protocol on HAM10000, using a fixed nano-scale YOLO26 segmentation model for joint lesion classification and instance segmentation. It finds that reported benefits of preprocessing largely disappear when image correlations from the same lesion are properly controlled.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Conformal Action Sets: An Application to Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Wenwen Si, Honghao Wei

entry.summary: RLCP adapts the retained action set in sequential recommendation using critic scores and an online conformal-style threshold updated from binary proxy feedback, proving a deterministic bound on proxy miss rate along adaptive trajectories. The paper also derives an exact decomposition of value loss into filtering and selection losses, yielding finite-session reward bounds.

entry.title: Beyond Marginals: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Multi-Table Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Aparana Gupta, Anurup Dey, Suyash Dwivedi

entry.summary: The authors present SynEval, a six-dimensional evaluation framework for multi-table synthetic databases that goes beyond marginal column distributions to assess joint distributions, cross-table integrity, downstream ML utility, privacy, and production edge cases. This addresses a gap in evaluating relational synthetic data, the dominant enterprise use case.

entry.title: Where Does the Audio Jailbreak Live? A Controlled Frequency-Depth Audit of AdvWave-P on Qwen2-Audio

author.name: Boyuan Chen, Minseok Kim, Sohaila Abdulsattar, Minghao Shao, Siddharth Garg, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: This paper audits frequency and decoder-depth claims for an additive audio jailbreak attack on Qwen2-Audio by masking STFT frequency components and measuring attack success, finding that apparent frequency rankings depend heavily on the partitioning scheme used. It applies judge-validation corrections (Rogan-Gladen sensitivity) to attack success measurements, exposing measurement pitfalls in audio jailbreak evaluation.

entry.title: JIVEAdapter: A Multi-Task Additive Low-Rank Adapter via Joint and Individual Variation Explained (JIVE)

author.name: Sara Abdali, Pashmina Cameron

entry.summary: JIVEAdapter is a multi-task additive low-rank adapter that decomposes each weight update into a joint structure shared across tasks plus per-task individual structures, with orthogonality penalties keeping shared and task-specific signal separated and adaptive rank allocation across a shared pool. It is inspired by the statistical JIVE decomposition, addressing the single-task, multiplicative-update limitation of standard adapters.

entry.title: Learning Decision-Stump Thresholds in Context: Dynamics of Softmax Attention

author.name: Hong Ha Le, Jackie Lok, Atsushi Nitanda, Yan Shuo Tan

entry.summary: Analyzes how gradient-based pretraining on multiple tasks lets a two-parameter softmax-attention model infer decision thresholds in context. Under large-resolution initialization, the authors derive error rates separating finite-pretraining accuracy from fresh-context localization and characterize the parameter-divergence mechanism behind in-context learning.

entry.title: An overview of machine learning-enhanced iterative methods for systems of linear and nonlinear equations

author.name: Yuhuang Meng, Jing Zhao, Alexander Heinlein

entry.summary: A survey of machine learning-enhanced iterative solvers for large linear and nonlinear systems, including those arising from PDEs. The paper organizes the landscape of learned preconditioners and hybrid solvers, covering both linear problems with well-developed convergence theory and harder nonlinear settings.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing for Random Graphs without Vertex Correspondence

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: The paper establishes sample complexity bounds for two-sample testing of graph populations without vertex correspondence, showing that for an Erdos-Renyi null with a planted two-block difference, m on the order of t^-3 graphs per group are necessary and sufficient, with signed triangle counts attaining this rate. Misalignment thus incurs a cubic versus linear cost compared to the aligned case.

entry.title: Seeing the Invisible: Physics-Guided Visual Prompting for Temperature- and Radiation-Aware VLA Navigation

author.name: Hojoon Son, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: PG-VP is a plug-and-play module for vision-language-action navigation models that handles invisible hazards like radiation or thermal spikes by performing physics-guided risk assessment and overlaying dynamic virtual obstacles in the visual input, reusing the frozen VLA model's obstacle avoidance abilities. This avoids per-hazard retraining, new encoders, and new data.

entry.title: Learning Grasp Targeting from Point Clouds for Log Pile Clearing on a Hydraulic Crane

author.name: George Sideris, Lucas Bessai, Heshan Fernando, Elie Ayoub, Nicolas Lemieux, Inna Sharf

entry.summary: The paper presents a learned policy that selects grasp points, depths, and grapple orientations from unsegmented point clouds to clear dense log piles on a real trailer-mounted hydraulic forestry crane, using behavior cloning followed by RL fine-tuning. Simulation results show BC clears 98 of 100 piles of 200 logs, with real-world deployment on hardware.

entry.title: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual Semantic-Social World Models

author.name: Fernando Martinez, Tao Li, Yingdong Lu, Juntao Chen

entry.summary: CASTLE addresses fully decentralized multi-agent RL by having agents prospectively compare consequences of candidate actions via counterfactual world models rather than diagnosing failures from ambiguous scalar rewards. This helps agents distinguish whether poor returns stem from their own action, teammates, or opponents without centralized critics or communication.

entry.title: Isotropic Yet Undecodable: The Sequential Content-Sufficiency Gap in Latent-Predictive Text Representations

author.name: K. P. Santoso, N. Z. Fadil, F. P. Harsanti, R. V. H. Ginardi, G. N. Iyer

entry.summary: Provides an information-theoretic analysis of whether text representations retain ordered target information, showing constructions where representations appear isotropic and agreeable yet carry zero target information. The theory motivates CANOPE, a nonautoregressive framework with ordered latent canvases and geometric regularization.

entry.title: The Standardization Trap: Certifying Joint Label Processing in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Duong Nguyen, Nicolas Chesneau, Milan Bhan

entry.summary: The paper studies whether tabular foundation models implement fixed-weight in-context label processing, and identifies a standardization trap: since public TFM packages standardize labels, naive derivative-based tests misjudge nonlinearity. The authors propose two prediction-based certificates that operate only at standardized labels and can reject fixed-weight or shift-only explanations.

entry.title: FedDermaSeg: Federated Learning for Dermatological Image Segmentation

author.name: Anabik Pal, Ganesh Patidar, Bikash Santra

entry.summary: This work explores federated learning for privacy-preserving skin lesion segmentation, avoiding the privacy risks and computational costs of centralized training on sensitive dermatological images. The authors investigate the feasibility of federated approaches for lesion delineation, a foundational step in computer-aided skin cancer diagnosis. The paper matters because medical imaging is a natural fit for federated learning, and demonstrating viable segmentation under decentralized training could enable broader clinical deployment.

entry.title: EMODE: Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts for Emotion-Aware Speech Language Modeling

author.name: Jianan Pan, Yiwen Gu, Xinze Li, Rui Wang, Kejie Huang

entry.summary: EMODE is an emotion-aware speech language model built around Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts, which decompose continuous speech features into semantic and paralinguistic pathways, route them dynamically, and fuse them before integration with the LM. The design prevents the LM from over-relying on recovered lexical content instead of acoustic-prosodic evidence. This addresses a known weakness in unified speech-language models.

entry.title: Detecting LLM-Assisted Vietnamese Writing via Keystrokes under Behavioral Manipulation

author.name: Thanh Dong, An Ngo, Minh Dau, Rajesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents a Vietnamese keystroke dataset covering bona fide writing, transcription, and paraphrasing, plus a threat model where users deliberately alter typing patterns to evade keystroke-based detection of LLM-assisted writing. It evaluates four keystroke modeling approaches under user- and context-independent settings and probes robustness to behavioral manipulation.

entry.title: Dynamic Positional Attention Modulation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Dayan Pan, Jingyuan Wang, Xie Yu

entry.summary: DyPAM is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that adapts how positional information contributes to attention, exploiting the dimension-dependent structure induced by rotary positional embeddings rather than applying uniform adaptations. It operates directly on query and key representations to account for heterogeneous attention behavior across dimensions, heads, layers, and tokens.

entry.title: Penalty-Framed No-Valid-Option MCQA: Analyzing LLM Abstention under Invalid Choices

author.name: Jinhyeok Kim, Hye-Young Jung

entry.summary: The paper studies penalty-framed no-valid-option MCQA, where models must either pick a remaining option or output ABSTAIN when the labeled correct option is removed from MMLU-Pro math questions, with penalties for invalid forced choices. A correct-conditioned analysis evaluates abstention only on instances the model answers correctly when the full option set is available.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability

author.name: Bingxi Hou, Guochao Jiang, Guofeng Quan, Weiqing Li, Wenfeng Feng, Guohua Liu, Yuewei Zhang

entry.summary: This empirical study examines on-policy distillation between teacher and student models with different tokenizers, finding that strict 1:1 token alignment already covers most student tokens despite vocabulary mismatch. Restricting reverse KL to a student-selected top-16 subset improves reliability of supervision. The work offers practical guidance for distillation pipelines, an increasingly important efficiency technique.

entry.title: Agreement Is Not Validity: Cross-Model LLM Consensus in Diagnosing Student Failure Modes in K-12 Math Tutoring Dialogue

author.name: Clayton Cohn, Joyce Fonteles, Kirk Vanacore, Gianni Mazza, Candida Crawford, Tom Hooper, Gautam Biswas, Rene Kizilcec

entry.summary: This exploratory study examines whether cross-model LLM consensus is a valid signal when diagnosing five student failure modes in K-12 math tutoring dialogue, using an operational codebook covering uncertainty, misattribution, operator selection, conceptual gap, and procedural slips. It argues that model agreement does not guarantee validity of LLM-generated interpretations. The finding cautions education-analytics researchers against relying on inter-model agreement as validation.

entry.title: Nord-Parl-TTS: Finnish and Swedish TTS Dataset from Parliament Speech

author.name: Zirui Li, Jens Edlund, Yicheng Gu, Nhan Phan, Lauri Juvela, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: Nord-Parl-TTS provides open, large-scale TTS datasets extracted from Nordic parliamentary proceedings: 900 hours of Finnish and 5,090 hours of Swedish speech, built with an adapted Emilia pipeline and unified evaluation sets. This substantially narrows the resource gap for Finnish and Swedish speech synthesis. It is a significant community resource for a typically under-resourced language pair.

entry.title: On Open-Ended Information Seeking for Information Elicitation Agents

author.name: Victor De Lima, Grace Hui Yang

entry.summary: This work studies information elicitation as an open-ended information-seeking problem where the value of pursued information changes as new information emerges. The authors compare information-value judgments across 11 LLMs of different families and scales and build a controlled elicitation environment to study how model choice shapes sequential information seeking. It matters for understanding behavioral differences between LLMs in agentic settings.

entry.title: Natural Language Questions as an Interface for Knowledge Graphs: QRAKEN Graph Distillation and Semantic Self-Healing

author.name: Remo Grillo, Lukas Klic, Giovanni Colavizza

entry.summary: QRAKEN is a training-free, ontology-agnostic neurosymbolic pipeline for Text-to-SPARQL that grounds query generation in empirical graph evidence (a distilled TTQL summary of populated multi-hop patterns, frequencies, and literal examples) plus deterministic syntax and data-model checks for iterative refinement. It addresses LLMs generating syntactically valid queries that misrepresent unfamiliar graph data models. It matters for reliable natural-language access to knowledge graphs.

entry.title: State-Aware Interaction MIL for Rare Joint Molecular Phenotype Prediction in Colorectal Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma

author.name: Dasari Naga Raju, Tripti Bameta

entry.summary: This weakly supervised multiple-instance learning method predicts joint molecular phenotypes in cancer pathology by preserving biomarker-specific histological representations, modeling their interactions, and supervising the full four-state configuration instead of collapsing configurations into a binary endpoint. This better handles small joint-positive populations and overlapping histology.

entry.title: WildMatch: Weakly Supervised Image Matcher Adaptation for Wildlife Re-Identification

author.name: Turhan Can Kargin, Piotr Kubaty, Ekaterina Rostovskaya, Izabela Wierzbowska, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Marcin Przewi\k{e}\'zlikowski

entry.summary: WildMatch adapts general-purpose image matchers to wildlife re-identification from camera-trap imagery using weak supervision, addressing the scarcity of labeled wildlife data with local correspondence constraints. The approach targets conservation-critical animal monitoring where collecting per-individual labels is expensive. It bridges off-the-shelf matching models and domain-specific wildlife imagery.

entry.title: From Laboratory to Road: Evaluating Wearable Gaze Accuracy for Driving

author.name: William Engel, Fabian Flohr

entry.summary: This work presents what the authors describe as the first unified framework for quantifying wearable eye-tracker gaze accuracy under real driving conditions, using an on-road study with 41 validated scenes where a driver fixated a license plate. It measures angular gaze error against a controlled reference, addressing sensitivity to head motion, illumination, and calibration drift. Gaze signals could enrich autonomous driving BEV representations with behavioral relevance.

entry.title: Can We Model the Artifacts Explicitly? Disentangle Artifacts via Pairwise Edit Relations for Image Manipulation Localization

author.name: Xuekang Zhu, Kaiwen Feng, Ruifeng Wang, Xiwen Wang, Xiaochen Ma, Bo Du, Changjiang Jiang, Chenfan Qu, Songyu Ye, Xia Du, Wentao Feng, Jian Liu, Ji-Zhe Zhou

entry.summary: The authors reinterpret image manipulation localization as a latent-variable problem where manipulation artifacts z are never directly observed, arguing that implicit artifact modeling limits current methods. They propose a two-stage learning paradigm that explicitly models artifacts via feature disentanglement using pairwise edit relations between real and manipulated images. This yields improved localization without requiring direct artifact labels.

entry.title: M3SunAgent: Monocular 3D Spatial Understanding Agent for Metric Depth Estimation and 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Jinsong Zhang, Kejun Wu, Ming Zhu, Renjie Qiao, Chengtao Cai, Zhengguo Li

entry.summary: M3SunAgent unifies monocular metric depth estimation and 3D visual grounding in a single agent that uses an LLM as a task planner for spatial visual programming, generating structured programs and coordinating tools. This removes the need for separate, unaligned frameworks for the two complementary 3D understanding tasks. The design aims to provide flexible, aligned spatial information access for embodied intelligence systems.

entry.title: Catastrophic Forgetting in Sequential Thermal Anti-UAV Detection: The Role of Scale-Conditioned Gradient Imbalance

author.name: Khac Duc Giang Nguyen, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag

entry.summary: This continual learning study characterizes catastrophic forgetting in a YOLOv5-based thermal infrared detector for anti-UAV applications when fine-tuned sequentially across three benchmarks of increasing scale difficulty. The authors show that naive fine-tuning causes roughly 90% capability loss and attribute it to scale-conditioned gradient imbalance, with knowledge retention methods mitigating the drop.

entry.title: Deformable CT-US Registration via Anatomy-Aware Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Agnieszka Lach, Magdalena Wysocki, Feng Li, Mohammad Farid Azampour, Benjamin D. Killeen, Felix Ginzinger, Mathias Braun, Philipp Steininger, Heinz Deutschmann, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: The paper presents a deformable CT-to-ultrasound registration framework for minimally invasive interventions, combining robot-assisted rigid registration with an anatomy-aware sinusoidal implicit neural representation for deformation estimation. Anatomical priors from CT improve alignment under soft-tissue deformation caused by probe contact.

entry.title: Post-Training Semantic Lifting for 3D Gaussian Splatting: Separating Detector, Lifting and Representation Error

author.name: Iv\'an Verdugo Guerra, Ezequiel L\'opez Rubio, Jorge Garc\'ia Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This paper proposes a post-training method for lifting semantics onto 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes that works one target class at a time and aggregates evidence across all views, weighted by per-Gaussian visibility. It accumulates target and non-target evidence simultaneously and filters Gaussians with thresholds, explicitly separating detector, lifting, and representation error sources.

entry.title: AIM: Adaptive Interaction Modeling Networks for Real-to-Sim Soft-Body Simulation

author.name: Tiancheng Yang, Dingshuo Chen, Tianle Chen, Zhaocheng Liu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: AIM treats real-to-sim soft-body simulation as a local-global interaction modeling problem, using motion history and geometry to adapt predictions of deformation under external interactions for tasks like folding laundry or handling food. It targets the problems that spatial neighborhoods misrepresent deformation dependencies and that per-scene models fail to generalize across object geometries and manipulation conditions.

entry.title: Toward Trustworthy Physical AI for Human Interaction

author.name: Niccol\`o Pagliarani, Maximilian St\"olzle, Cosima du Pasquier, Jeff Lui, Andrew Sabelhaus, Cecilia Laschi, Gentiane Venture, Daniela Rus, Matteo Cianchetti

entry.summary: A position/framework paper from a strong author group (including Rus, Laschi, Venture) proposing that trustworthy physical AI emerges from aligning safety, behavioral intelligibility, and perceptual alignment across embodiment, control, cognition, and design. It frames a conceptual structure for when robots in human spaces deserve trust.

entry.title: Entropy-Gated Belief Coordination for Decentralized Multi-Agent Search Under Intermittent Communication

author.name: Mohamed Abdelnaby, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: The paper introduces entropy-gated belief coordination for decentralized multi-agent search, where agents skip belief fusion during high-entropy exploration and merge beliefs only during exploitation, leveraging intermittent Poisson-distributed communication. It provides theoretical grounding via opinion dynamics bifurcations and submodular information-gain structure.

entry.title: Task-Space Imitation Guidance for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Salar Asayesh, Hossein Darani, Todd Cao, Evgeny Andriash, Mani Ranjbar

entry.summary: TIGER uses an action-chunked imitation policy as a local task-space progress estimator, converting predicted action chunks into end-effector references that provide dense progress rewards while sparse environment reward remains dominant. It also relaxes conservative value penalties during pretraining for predicted-progress actions.

entry.title: Humanoid Horizon: Extending Task Horizon in Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via Parallel Training, Dynamic Starting, and Reward Gating

author.name: Haozhuo Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Jian Tang, Mingzhe Ni, Michele Caprio, Angelo Cangelosi, Wei Pan

entry.summary: Humanoid Horizon is a unified RL policy framework for long-horizon whole-body loco-manipulation, where humanoids must navigate, grasp, transport, and place large heavy objects in cluttered indoor environments within a single episode. It tackles easy-reward bias and catastrophic forgetting through parallel training, dynamic task starting, and reward gating. This enables training on complete multi-stage tasks that previous approaches fragment or fail on.

entry.title: A Belief-State World Model for Catheter Navigation under Sparse Fluoroscopy: A Planar Proof of Concept

author.name: Damini Rijhwani

entry.summary: This work explores reducing patient and clinician radiation exposure during endovascular catheter navigation by using a physics-based Cosserat rod world model with a particle filter to maintain belief over device state between sparse X-ray acquisitions. Formulated as a POMDP with a geometric contact proxy, the planar proof-of-concept also investigates whether the model can signal when its internal estimate becomes unreliable.

entry.title: No Need to Stop the Fleet: Localized Anomaly Isolation via Dead Zones in AGV Fleets

author.name: Natalia Ogorelysheva, Falk Howar, Jian-Jia Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces dead zones, a formally defined mechanism for isolating local anomalies in automated guided vehicle fleets without triggering a system-wide emergency stop. By quarantining only the affected area, unaffected robots can continue operating, reducing unnecessary downtime in production and logistics settings.

entry.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments Using an Ackermann-Steered Mobile Robot

author.name: Chalindu Abeywansa, Sahan Gunasekara, Devindi De Silva, Seniru Dissanayake, Ranga Rodrigo, Peshala Jayasekara

entry.summary: The authors transfer a vision-language navigation model from simulation to a real Ackermann-steered robot operating in continuous environments without navigation graphs, 360-degree views, or perfect localization. The system aligns visual inputs and language instructions in a shared embedding space using vision-language models for natural-language-driven navigation.

entry.title: The interface of data assimilation and machine learning

author.name: Eviatar Bach

entry.summary: This is a review article surveying the interface between data assimilation and machine learning, covering how ML can improve DA and how DA principles inform ML, in the context of chaotic systems like the atmosphere. It provides an overview of main topics and methods in this rapidly developing area.

entry.title: When does conformal calibration need censoring weights? Cause-of-failure prediction sets under competing risks

author.name: Sunny Yang, Weiyan Zhao

entry.summary: The authors study split conformal prediction for competing-risks labels when calibration data is subject to right censoring, showing complete-case calibration can miscover in either direction and quantifying score-distribution shifts near the population quantile. They analyze when censoring weights are needed and illustrate in cause-of-failure prediction settings.

entry.title: Why did we get warning shots?

author.name: p(mike)

entry.summary: A skeptical outsider analyzes why classic AI x-risk predictions about capability generalization and hard alignment have held up, while the predicted Treacherous Turn by deceptively aligned models has not, with models instead producing repeated warning shots. The author reasons through what this divergence implies about alignment difficulty and model psychology.

entry.title: Recursive Improvement of a Differentiable Scientific Software Ecosystem

author.name: Pengcheng Hou, Xiaojun Tan, Sihan Hu, Ruisi Wang, Shuo Chen, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

entry.summary: Presents an environment for agent-driven evolution of differentiable scientific software that connects demand identification, development, and quality evaluation through a unified differentiation interface exposing reusable derivative rules alongside existing numerical routines. The goal is to let AI coding agents accelerate extension of differentiable programming across a heterogeneous scientific software ecosystem, with evaluation of how well implementations meet research needs. An early contribution to self-improving scientific software infrastructure.

entry.title: Toward a Locally Deployable Agentic Co-Scientist: Small-Model Planning for Early-Stage Drug Discovery

author.name: Tian Liang, Jiayu Chang, Alejandro F. Frangi, Mobarak I. Hoque, Richard A. Bryce

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight, tool-augmented framework where a locally deployable compact language model plans calls to 18 modular tools for early-stage drug discovery, using a Unified Molecular Schema and LoRA fine-tuning on 1,263 manually refined query-plan pairs. Llama 3.2-3B achieves a 0.998 tool-selection F1 with fully parseable, schema-compliant plans on held-out queries, enabling privacy-preserving local deployment.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Sequential Structure? A Controlled Study of Inference and Generation

author.name: Jerry Wang, Zhengxiang Wang, Ting Yu Liu, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Yi-Cheng Lai, Tengfei Ma

entry.summary: Using controlled Rock-Paper-Scissors and stochastic n-gram tasks, this study tests whether LLMs can recover latent sequential structure beyond surface action frequencies, separating distribution matching from conditional rule following. The results indicate limits in how well longer contexts translate into higher-order conditional dependencies. This is a careful scientific contribution to understanding LLM inductive biases, relevant to their use as simulators and agents.

entry.title: Mining Agent Skills from Production Traces

author.name: Yue Ran Kang, Colton Mikolajczyk, Chhaya Methani, Hazel Mak, Sahil Bhatnagar, Susheel Suresh, Alejandro Gutierrez Munoz

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies how to mine reusable agent skills from execution traces when ground-truth success signals are unavailable in production. Holding the mining pipeline fixed, the authors compare six combinations of mining evidence (successes only, labeled successes-plus-failures, or unlabeled mixtures) and skill forms (ordered workflows versus alternatives). The results inform practical choices for building skill libraries from noisy production data.
