entry.title: AegisFlow: A Multi-Agent Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous Remediation and Self-Healing in Fragile Data Ecosystems

author.name: Muhammad Bilal Awan, Zubair Hussain, Abdul Shahid

entry.summary: AegisFlow is an agentic framework that closes the loop between failure detection and resolution in brittle data pipelines, using a Watchdog agent for runtime telemetry and an LLM-based Repair agent that automatically creates, tests, and deploys code patches for schema drift, API changes, and DOM modifications. It includes a non-intrusive execution model to reduce mean time to repair. This applies multi-agent LLM systems to practical data-operations automation.

entry.title: Dynamic Alignment and Calibration for Multimodal Learning

author.name: Jinghao Xu, Zhenhua Guo, Xiaofeng Zhu, Xiaoshuang Shi

entry.summary: This paper tackles limitations of dynamic multimodal learning: static cross-modal alignment applies uniform constraints ignoring sample-wise variation, and confidence-based fusion neglects feature-magnitude differences across modalities. The proposed method introduces sample-adaptive alignment and calibration to prevent over-alignment and improve fusion reliability when modality confidence gaps are small. It targets more robust multimodal representations.

entry.title: Geometric Coherence via Weighted Matching for 3D Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reach-Avoid Games

author.name: Prajwal Vijay

entry.summary: The paper studies assignment quality in 3D heterogeneous multi-agent reach-avoid games, identifying a failure mode of cardinality-only matching called Geometric Sprawl, where valid assignments yield spatially incoherent pairings and inefficient pursuit. It introduces a cardinality-first weighted sequential matching method using Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs interception values as secondary weights, solved with min-cost max-flow.

entry.title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni

entry.summary: This theory paper studies maximization of the p-mean social welfare objective, which unifies classical welfare criteria including Nash and egalitarian welfare, for allocating indivisible goods when agent and item multiplicities are encoded in binary. It proves NP-hardness results: for every fixed rational p less than 1 (except 0), hardness holds with only two item types, Nash and egalitarian welfare are NP-hard with three item types, and strong NP-hardness holds with one agent type. These are clean complexity-theoretic results in fair division.

entry.title: CCQ: A Multi-State Child Care Quality Dataset to Support AI for Children's Health Research

author.name: Victor Li, Yuzhang Xie, Ziwei Dong, Qingyang Zhu, Wenjing Ma, Carl Yang, Jinbing Bai, Huiwen Xu, Jiaying Lu

entry.summary: CCQ is a large-scale de-identified dataset integrating 59,372 child care provider records across 12 U.S. states, with an automated LLM-based pipeline for anonymization, cleaning, and standardization into cleaned textual and structured releases. It enables applied data science at the intersection of AI and early childhood health.

entry.title: Fed-BRDECS: Privacy-Preserving and Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Deep Embedded Clustering

author.name: Haemin Park, Diego Klabjan, Martin W. Braun, Xiuqi Li, Balakrishnan Ananthanarayanan

entry.summary: Fed-BRDECS enables federated deep embedded clustering while preserving privacy, replacing globally normalized clustering objectives (which leak sensitive soft-assignment statistics) with a locally computable sample-stability loss. It further handles non-IID clients via prediction-balanced sampling that oversamples locally rare predicted clusters without global labels. This addresses both privacy and heterogeneity pain points in federated unsupervised learning.

entry.title: SepsisLens: Structure-Preserving Sequence Modelling for Decomposable Early Sepsis Warning

author.name: Yikun Ou, Wei Li

entry.summary: SepsisLens is a model for early sepsis warning from ICU records that preserves variable-indexed temporal states rather than collapsing clinical variables into a patient-level representation. This structure keeps alerts decomposable, connecting multi-horizon risk predictions to the specific physiological trajectories that support them.

entry.title: Do I Need the Cloud? Uncertainty-Aware Step-Level Handoff for Small Language Model Agents

author.name: Abolfazl Younesi

entry.summary: STEPGATE is a framework that scores each action by a local small language model agent and escalates uncertain steps to a stronger cloud model, exploiting the sequential structure of agent decisions rather than routing once per query. On a 52-task BFCL-derived split, a Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B pair reaches 82.7% success with 30.8% escalation versus 67.3% local-only.

entry.title: Embedded Bare-Metal Radar-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Nicolai Adil {\O}yen Aatif, Morten Nissov, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: The paper presents a radar-inertial odometry framework for state estimation on computationally constrained platforms such as compact extraplanetary rovers and micro aerial vehicles, exploiting FMCW radar's direct velocity measurements and robustness to perceptual degradation. It targets embedded, bare-metal deployment in environments where vision and LiDAR fail or are too expensive computationally.

entry.title: The Reported Engagement with AI Level (REAL) Rating: A Framework for Disclosing Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Im\`ene Goumiri, Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Eric Bell, Amanda Muyskens

entry.summary: The REAL Rating proposes a six-tier scale (Levels 0-5) for disclosing the extent of AI involvement in content and workflows, replacing binary human-vs-AI categorizations and watermarking approaches that lack user-facing clarity. The framework aims to capture the varied risks arising from different degrees of human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: ShadowMiner v1 - An Experience Report on Implementing and Measuring a Problem-and-Hypothesis Discovery Engine

author.name: Jinhyuk Choi

entry.summary: ShadowMiner v1 is a nine-stage pipeline that automatically discovers research problems and generates hypotheses from AI papers by building knowledge graphs, finding structural gaps, and verifying generated hypotheses against existing literature and source facts. The paper is explicitly an experience report measuring which prior-work ideas contributed, not a new technique.

entry.title: Efficient Neural Surrogates for Linear Radiation Transport on the Lattice and Hohlraum benchmarks

author.name: Carmelo Gonzales, Steffen Schotth\"ofer, Cory D. Hauck

entry.summary: This work develops neural surrogates for linear radiation transport equations, which underpin nuclear engineering, inertial confinement fusion, and medical imaging simulations, amortizing expensive solver costs for design optimization and uncertainty quantification. It benchmarks architectural choices across model families, showing that inductive biases effective on one transport problem do not transfer straightforwardly.

entry.title: CI-JEPA: A Counterfactual Analysis of Latent Representations in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Mintu Dutta, Ritesh Vyas, Mohendra Roy *

entry.summary: CI-JEPA extends I-JEPA to be counterfactual intervention-aware, learning to predict representation changes between an original image and a modified counterpart, and assesses robustness via selective sensitivity to task-relevant versus nuisance changes. Experiments use flower-center occlusion on Flowers102 as a case study. It connects self-supervised representation learning with causal/counterfactual analysis, a direction of growing interest.

entry.title: CreativeFlow: A One-to-Many Analogical Relation Transfer Method for 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Xuechen Li, Shuai Zhang, Nanxuan Zhao, Qing Chen

entry.summary: CreativeFlow is an analogical generation framework for text-to-3D pipelines that models analogical divergent thinking, drawing on cognitive science to reduce creative homogenization in generated 3D assets. It produces relationally similar source-target asset pairs with distinct geometry, and expert evaluations indicate improved novelty, while the outputs form a benchmark dataset for relation-aware 3D model training.

entry.title: Process Constitutions and Process Stewards: Towards the Next Generation of BPM for Agentic Organizations

author.name: Amin Jalali, Majid Rafiei

entry.summary: This position paper argues that Business Process Management must shift from modeling human work to governing autonomous agents, proposing two concepts: the Process Constitution, a machine-interpretable framework defining admissible agent behavior, and the Process Steward, a role for overseeing agentic processes.

entry.title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: The CKG Clinical Explanation Engine is a downstream layer for a frozen, training-free clinical knowledge-graph reasoner that converts patient inference states and disease knowledge into typed facts, explicit rule-application traces, and provenance-linked, policy-licensed recommendations. It carefully separates observed evidence from representation incompleteness so that zero-activation evidence is not conflated with missing data.

entry.title: LoRA Adaptation Strength in Aurora-WRF: Trade-offs in Regional Heavy-Rainfall Forecasting

author.name: Boyan Liu, Xiaoyuan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper conducts a controlled study of how parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model affects regional heavy-rainfall forecasting when coupled with a fixed 9-km WRF configuration over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. It compares five inference-time adaptation strengths against a GFS-driven control across 17 initializations in 2023 using hourly ERA5 precipitation verification.

entry.title: A study on human-agent teaming through spoken interaction: the impact of human individual traits and agent characteristics

author.name: Lara Gauder, Martin Bernardo Meza, Javier Krick, Alejandro Masin, Luciana Benotti, Marcos Luis Pietto, Luciana Ferrer

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether simple changes in a spoken-dialogue virtual agent's communicative behavior influence how teammate-like humans perceive it to be. Using a collaborative game protocol where a human and agent identify and place a target object, each subject interacted with two agents differing in behavior. The findings inform how social factors, alongside capability, shape human-agent team success.

entry.title: AI-Enabled Quality Assurance for Multiple-Choice Assessment Items

author.name: Steven Moore, Nicholas Diana

entry.summary: This is a focused narrative review of automated detection of item-writing flaws in multiple-choice assessment, covering flaw detection, revision, psychometric screening, and NLP benchmark auditing across fourteen research reports. It distinguishes surface checks from content-sensitive judgments and maps a 19-criterion rubric to detection methods. The review finds that high label accuracy often coexists with weak positive-case detection and inconsistent reference standards.

entry.title: Variational Quantum Attention for Molecular Graph Learning

author.name: Yu-Cheng Lin, Yu-Chao Hsu, Tai-Yue Li, Nan-Yow Chen, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces QGAT, an edge-aware variational quantum attention mechanism for molecular graph learning in which the receiving atom, neighbor, and bond jointly determine a quantum attention state. Across five molecular property and bioactivity prediction tasks it performs competitively with GATv2, with consistent improvement on BBBP across six circuit ansatzes. The work also analyzes how quantum and classical attention distributions differ.

entry.title: PreAct-Nav: Agentic Reasoning Before Action for Urban Navigation

author.name: Jing Xie, Shouwei Ruan, Yubin Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Junwei Yang, Songchang Jin, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: PreAct-Nav equips frozen embodied navigation policies with anticipatory reasoning for long-horizon urban navigation, anchoring local decisions in persistent predictions of action consequences rather than transient observations. It targets the gap between distant goal pursuit and local decision-making in large physical environments. The framework wraps around existing policies without retraining them.

entry.title: AutoDP-LLM: Automating Data Pre-processing for Intrusion Detection Systems using Large Language Models

author.name: Bao-Phong Nguyen, Gia-Khanh Pham, Thai-Duong Do, Mai Xuan Trang, Minh-Tuan Le, Xuan-Nam Tran, Huan Vu, Tien-Cuong Nguyen, Vu-Duc Ngo, Thien Van Luong

entry.summary: AutoDP-LLM uses LLMs to autonomously generate and validate executable data pre-processing pipelines for intrusion detection systems, combining deterministic components to reduce manual pipeline development and computational overhead on large, high-dimensional network traffic data. This reduces trial-and-error configuration effort in building effective IDS. The work sits at the intersection of LLM-driven automation and network security.

entry.title: Population Scaling or Data Dilution? Dynamics of Local Topology Evolution in Decentralized Learning

author.name: Yin-Kuan Liang, Yan Gao, Yang Long

entry.summary: The paper studies how scaling the number of clients in decentralized learning interacts with data allocation, topology mixing, and communication capacity, comparing Ring, Static Random, and an adaptive Local-First Heuristic Evolution topology on CIFAR-10. It provides analytical failure modes, such as the Ring's spectral gap decaying as Theta(N^-2).

entry.title: Relational Synthesis: Structure-Mediated Concatenative Synthesis for Foley and Retrieval-Augmented Audio Generation

author.name: Keren Shao, Ayaka Kawano, Shlomo Dubnov

entry.summary: The paper proposes relational synthesis, a concatenative audio synthesis method that replaces target cost with a relational Gromov-like structural cost, enabling synthesis of audio Y that is acoustically consistent with a retrieved source S without naively copying segments of S or R. This simultaneously addresses a Foley production goal and the copy-paste failure mode of naive RAG-augmented generation.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Objective Evaluation of Modern Text-to-Speech for Turkish Using Speech Quality Assessment Models

author.name: Yunus Emre Ozkose, Alperen Kahraman, Ali Haznedaroglu

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks four modern TTS systems (Chatterbox, CosyVoice, OmniVoice, VoxCPM2) in fine-tuned and zero-shot configurations for Turkish, a morphologically rich lower-resource language, against a VITS baseline and natural speech. It uses eighteen objective metrics spanning naturalness predictors and intelligibility estimators. The work addresses an under-characterized gap in TTS evaluation for non-English languages.

entry.title: Joint Class-Time Learning for Video Classification with Multi-Instance Partial-Label Learning

author.name: Lingyu Shen, Wei Tang, Fakhri Karray, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a method coupling label disambiguation with temporal evidence allocation for video classification under multi-instance partial-label learning, using occupancy-regularized spherical matching and a dual-marginal KL projection to build structured teachers. This jointly determines which candidate class corresponds to which temporal segments in videos with inexact supervision. It addresses a real gap where bag-level labels do not supervise class-time correspondence.

entry.title: Paradee: Distilling Kokoro-82M into an 8M-Parameter Single-Voice Text-to-Speech Model

author.name: Sahil Mahendrakar

entry.summary: Paradee distills the widely used open TTS model Kokoro-82M into an 8.07M-parameter single-voice model, achieving 10x fewer parameters and 15x less compute via narrowed layers, teacher-synthesized corpora, spectral plus adversarial training, and int8 quantization. The approach requires no alignment learning or joint training of the two halves. This is a practical demonstration of extreme TTS compression for edge deployment.

entry.title: One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline

author.name: Shih-Chen Tseng, Chih-Hsuan Chen, Ryan Yang, Hsi-An Chen, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: Formulates aspect-ratio-adaptive flowchart relayout as a new task: converting a raster flowchart into a structurally faithful, editable layout for arbitrary target canvases such as slides, posters, and social formats. The proposed agentic pipeline avoids characteristic failures of image-to-image stretching, content hallucination, and edge mis-routing.

entry.title: Uncertainty in Representation Learning on Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Yuqicheng Zhu

entry.summary: A PhD thesis systematically investigating three sources of uncertainty in knowledge graph embedding: knowledge uncertainty from incomplete or probabilistic inputs, algorithmic uncertainty from stochastic training, and predictive uncertainty of outputs. The thesis develops methods addressing each source to improve reliability of KGE predictions in high-stakes applications.

entry.title: When Attention Does Not Explain the Peak: Temporal Reference vs. Forecast Output in Attention-Based Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuji Akamatsu, Takao Yamanaka

entry.summary: Tests whether attention maps in a load-forecasting model explain predicted peak timing, using a horizon-level attention descriptor across 31 windows of the Panama load dataset. The model forecasts peaks accurately while the attention argmax is a poor predictor of peak time, cautioning against naively reading temporal meaning from attention weights.

entry.title: Towards Explainable Benchmarking for Data-driven Post-Wildfire Debris Flow Prediction

author.name: Zhisheng Qi, Li Zhu, Utkarsh Sahu, Douglas Tommey, Josh Roering, Yu Wang

entry.summary: This paper consolidates the fragmented landscape of data-driven post-wildfire debris flow prediction by providing a benchmark across feature spaces, model architectures, and evaluation protocols, plus systematic analysis of the relative importance of meteorological, terrain, and other heterogeneous factors. The goal is enabling rigorous comparison and scientific insight for a destructive natural hazard. It serves both ML and geoscience communities.

entry.title: StaFIR: Convex Learning of Stationarity-Aware Causal Filters

author.name: Lorena Egger, Mathis Linger

entry.summary: StaFIR is a causal FIR filter with a learned nonnegative mixture of exponential lag profiles, trained via a convex objective balancing stationarity of financial time series with fidelity to the input. It improves on fractional differencing tuned by ADF tests and is validated on ARFIMA-GARCH settings and realized-volatility forecasting.

entry.title: Improving Synthetic Data Generation for Argument Mining via Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhijun Zhang, Qianlong Wang, Keyang Ding, Genan Dai, Bowen Zhang, Bin Liang, Ruifeng Xu, Yongsheng Liang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an adversarial reinforcement learning framework for generating synthetic argument mining data, jointly optimizing a generator that produces structured instances and a discriminator that distinguishes real from synthetic data. This addresses the scarcity of high-quality structure-annotated argument mining datasets.

entry.title: A Decision-Focused Neural Optimization Framework for Personalized Route Reproduction from Vehicle Trajectories

author.name: Gyeongjun Kim, Yeseul Kang, Keemin Sohn

entry.summary: The paper formulates reproducing individual driver routes as a shortest-path problem over learned driver-specific latent link costs, combining a perception encoder with a constrained optimization layer. Decision-focused learning enables end-to-end training that aligns predicted costs with route outcomes, avoiding enumeration of alternative route sets.

entry.title: Scalable extraction and visualization of multi-attribute logical and functional dependencies in tabular data

author.name: Chaithra Umesh (Institute of Computer Science, University of Rostock, Germany), Arvind Lomrore (School of Data Science, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram, India), Neethu D (School of Data Science, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram, India), Kristian Seegel-Schultz (Institute of Computer Science, University of Rostock, Germany), Saptarshi Bej (Institute of Computer Science, University of Rostock, Germany, School of Data Science, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram, India), Olaf Wolkenhauer (Institute of Computer Science, University of Rostock, Germany, Leibniz-Institute for Food Systems Biology, Technical University of Munich, Freising, Germany, Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Study, South Africa)

entry.summary: LDTool and HLDTool extend dependency discovery from functional dependencies to multi-attribute logical dependencies in tabular data, providing a unified extraction and visualization framework that scales with attribute count and dependency order. The tools target exploratory data analysis and pattern recognition workflows. It fills a practical tooling gap but is a niche contribution.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Visualization: Exploring Text Corpora with User-Prompted Axes

author.name: Arnau Bueno Tricas, Jose A. Rodr\'iguez-Serrano

entry.summary: The authors introduce zero-shot visualization (ZSV), a task where users specify concepts in natural language and LLMs map documents onto those concept axes for visual corpus exploration. They build a benchmark comparing embedding similarity, direct semantic judgments, and conditional likelihood approaches across datasets and implementation tradeoffs.

entry.title: Nonlocal Hamiltonian Dynamics on Sparse L\'evy Graphs: Spectral Analysis and Multimodal Sampling

author.name: Miaolei Zheng, Ting Gao, Jinqiao Duan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a sparse graph-based method for transporting probability mass toward multimodal target distributions using damped nonlocal Hamiltonian dynamics with logarithmic-mean mobility and symmetric Levy-type interaction weights. Long-range edges sampled on top of nearest-neighbor connections allow direct mass exchange between spatially separated modes, with deterministic updates that scale linearly in node count and sampling budget. The authors provide spectral analysis via linearization around the target, characterizing convergence through the eigenvalues of a weighted graph Laplacian.

entry.title: Learning Disentangled Representations with Quantum Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Gaoyuan Wang, Jerry Tan, Mark Gerstein

entry.summary: Investigates whether quantum variational autoencoders can learn disentangled latent representations, extending the disentanglement question from classical VAEs to quantum models. The authors examine how factors are organized in QVAE latent spaces, with the goal of interpretable and controllable generation for scientific data.

entry.title: AccentCL: Robust Accent Classification with Incremental Expansion

author.name: Mu-Ruei Tseng, Waris Quamer, Ghady Nasrallah, Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna

entry.summary: AccentCL is a class-incremental learning framework for English accent classification built on a frozen Whisper-Large-v3 encoder, using imbalance-aware cross-entropy and a domain mean alignment loss to handle class imbalance and cross-corpus domain shift. It allows new accent categories to be added as new data arrives, overcoming fixed label inventories.

entry.title: A Neural JKO Scheme for Hellinger-Kantorovich Gradient Flows via Monge-Growth Pairs

author.name: Geuntaek Seo, Cheolhyeong Kim, Hwijae Son, Hyung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: The authors develop a mesh-free neural Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme for advection-reaction-diffusion equations with gradient-flow structure in the unbalanced optimal transport (Hellinger-Kantorovich) geometry, parametrizing each step by a spatial map plus a mass-changing factor. They provide existence results, mass bounds, and conditions under which the variational scheme recovers the exact JKO minimum.

entry.title: CACHEFORGE: LLM-Guided End-to-End Generative Cache Replacement Policy for Performance and Hardware Efficiency

author.name: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Bita Aslrousta, Brijesh Kumar Bhayana, Paula Contreras, Azam Ghanbari, Ethan Goodman, Anna Andriiko, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz

entry.summary: CACHEFORGE uses LLM-guided generation to synthesize cache replacement policies that can produce new decision logic rather than imitating an offline optimum, accounting for interactions between prefetching, thrashing, and locality. The work targets both performance and hardware efficiency in processor caches.

entry.title: Nash Social Welfare for Multi Armed Bandits: Trajectory-wise Expected and High Probability Regret

author.name: Avishek Ghosh

entry.summary: The paper proposes a trajectory-wise Nash regret notion for fair multi-armed bandits that computes the geometric mean over complete reward sample paths rather than per-round marginal expectations, better matching the Nash Social Welfare fairness motivation. It provides expected and high-probability regret bounds for algorithms under this objective.

entry.title: Explainable Rule Mining of IPv6 Extension-Header Presence Patterns from Paired-Vantage Captures

author.name: Priyanka Sinha, Nikolaos Kekatos, Stylianos Basagiannis, Antonio Anastasio Bruto da Costa, Alexios Lekidis, Pabitra Mitra, Tom Nianios, Elpiniki Papageorgiou

entry.summary: This arXiv paper applies an interpretable temporal-logic rule miner to packet captures from the JAMES paired-vantage dataset to characterize IPv6 extension-header (EH) behavior, such as fragmentation, segment routing, and in-situ telemetry, which are often dropped in transit. The authors contribute two reusable measurement tools: a negative-control protocol that distinguishes genuine cross-packet temporal dynamics from mere within-packet co-occurrence, and a sender-conditioned, per-family EH-retention measurement. The work recovers human-readable, portable rules for EH behavior that are validated against these controls.

entry.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Dense and Mixture-of-Experts Models for Automated Program Repair

author.name: Anvi Kalpesh Shah, Umamaheswara Sharma B

entry.summary: Proposes a Weighted Quality Index combining correctness, maintainability, security, and generation efficiency to evaluate LLM-based automated program repair, testing dense Qwen2.5-Coder models and a DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite MoE on QuixBugs and Defects4J under identical local hardware. Model rankings shift with weighting schemes, showing test-pass evaluation hides important quality differences.

entry.title: Machine Learning for German Redispatch Forecasting under Data Delays and Temporal Distribution Shift

author.name: Faraz Shamim (KIST Medical College and Teaching Hospital, Nepal), Faris Shamim (OTH Regensburg)

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates probabilistic machine-learning forecasts of German grid redispatch (upward and downward intervention energy) across four transmission system operators from 2021 to 2024, under realistic constraints of delayed reporting, zero-inflated targets, and temporal distribution shift. It compares seasonal empirical, regularized autoregressive, quantile LightGBM, GRU, and Transformer models under a minimum seven-day latency constraint.

entry.title: Rapid Fredholm stabilization of the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation with unrestricted, spatially-varying anti-diffusion

author.name: Luke Bhan, Miroslav Krstic, Yuanyuan Shi

entry.summary: This control-theory paper develops the first feedback stabilization design for the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation with spatially varying anti-diffusion, using a second boundary input to overcome controllability loss from repeated unstable eigenvalues. The design combines a pre-feedback on one boundary value with Fredholm backstepping on a curvature input. It removes coefficient restrictions present in prior constant-coefficient designs.

entry.title: Generative AI translations in high-stakes emergency messaging

author.name: Nune Ayvazan, Anthony Pym, Yu Hao

entry.summary: This paper experimentally evaluates generative AI translation of earthquake instructions from English into Chinese and Spanish, showing that discourse-specific prompts improve understandability and actionability, though translations may still lack the trust needed for high-stakes use. It weighs time savings of MT against the risk of tragic translation errors. The work informs policy on when generative AI is appropriate for emergency multilingual communication.

entry.title: SEAL: Mixture-Closed Additive Reconstruction and Refinement-Aware Expert Routing for Efficient Speech Separation

author.name: Shao-Chun Hu, Zi-Xiang Lin, Jeih-Weih Hung, Hung-Shin Lee

entry.summary: SEAL improves compact speech separation models on two fronts: a zero-sum additive residual bounded by local mixture amplitude allows nonzero estimates where overlapping sources cancel (which multiplicative masking cannot do), and a query-based routing mechanism sends each time-frequency token to one of six residual experts, avoiding uniform compute costs. This yields more capable and efficient separation architectures.

entry.title: Towards benchmarking Western Bluebird detection in the wild

author.name: Estela Monserrat Arriaga Santana, Julian Rosas Scull, Ibeth P. Alarc\'on, Bibiana Montoya, Aylin Sosa Mej\'ia, Hugo Jair Escalante

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark dataset for detecting and segmenting Western bluebirds in the wild: over 6,000 labeled 4K images from 41 recording sessions where birds occupy a small fraction of the frame amid clutter. It evaluates supervised detectors and open-vocabulary models in zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. The dataset addresses the scarcity of realistic small-object wildlife benchmarks.

entry.title: TSRN-RTVD: Real-Time Video Deblurring System

author.name: Nikita Alutis, Danila Evsyukov, Egor Chistov, Mikhail Voronin, Evgeney Bogatyrev, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: TSRN-RTVD is an efficient real-time video deblurring system that explicitly reconstructs the camera trajectory during exposure and uses the recovered motion to guide restoration, turning the physical cause of blur into a restoration signal. It targets the gap between high-quality but computationally heavy deblurring networks and the constraints of consumer and edge hardware. The system aims to deliver strong perceptual quality at real-time speeds on-device.

entry.title: Decoy and disclosure radii of invariant shape descriptors

author.name: Tanush Shaska, Lubjana Beshaj

entry.summary: This theoretical paper quantifies the fiber of rotation-invariant shape descriptors: a large fiber radius admits decoys (distant shapes that match the descriptor) while a small radius enables reconstruction of the enrolled shape from the stored descriptor. For star-shaped surfaces with truncated spherical harmonics, it derives generic fiber dimensions and shows standard descriptor pools admit substantial decoy families.

entry.title: Emoception: Selective Affective Layer Fine-Tuning of Video Vision Transformers for Player Arousal Change Recognition From Gameplay Footage

author.name: Yi Xia, Ibrahim Khan, Mury Fajar Dewantoro, Wenwen Ouyang, Ruck Thawonmas

entry.summary: SALFT is an efficient adaptation method for video ViTs that selects layers for fine-tuning based on L2-norm parameter change after brief adaptation, rather than gradient-based criteria. Applied to player arousal recognition from gameplay footage, it matches full fine-tuning performance while updating only about 8 percent of parameters.

entry.title: Physical Twins: Accelerating and Enabling Robot Learning with Phantom Platforms

author.name: Elizabeth Peiros, Derek Chen, Lucas Yager, Edward Lee, Kevin Wang, Zoe Samuels, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: The authors present an improved phantom device, a physical twin of a human shoulder, that replicates ball-and-socket, scapular, and protraction/retraction motions to enable real-world RL testing of physically interactive algorithms without IRB-burdened human studies. This addresses safety, repeatability, and participant diversity challenges in physical human-robot interaction research.

entry.title: Dynamics Modeling of a Multi-UAV Slung Load System Using a Discrete-Link Cable Approach

author.name: Harvey Merton, Ian W. Hunter

entry.summary: This paper derives an Euler-Newton dynamics model for multi-UAV slung load systems that represents flexible cables as series of rigid links, designed for efficient simulation with Featherstone's articulated body algorithm. Real-world validation across gentle, aggressive, and tension-engagement maneuvers shows mean load translation errors below roughly 132 mm.

entry.title: Reactive Exploration of Unknown Environments for Redundant Robots using Virtual Model Control

author.name: Alessio Canzolino, Omar Faris, Alessandro De Blasi, Fulvio Forni

entry.summary: This work proposes an active exploration method for redundant robotic arms with eye-in-hand cameras operating in confined and occluded spaces. A novel scoring method selects target voxels based on the robot state and expected information gain, while Virtual Model Control provides compliance guarantees for safe whole-arm motion. The approach enables real-time navigation and information acquisition under tight geometric constraints.

entry.title: A Swarm-Coordinated Multi-Robot System for Early Stress Detection in Agricultural Rows Using Multimodal Leaf Sensing

author.name: Rishi Gupta, Astha Goyal, Vinay Vishwakarma

entry.summary: This arXiv robotics paper presents CropSentry, a low-cost multi-robot platform in which two autonomous ground bots continuously monitor leaf color and environmental data row by row to detect crop stress early. Observations are spatially mapped and relayed to a master bot that renders a real-time web dashboard with color-coded row segments indicating crop health. The work targets affordability for small and medium-scale farmers who cannot access expensive hyperspectral or AI-heavy systems.

entry.title: Vine Copula VAR:From Recursive Margins to Joint Forecast Inference

author.name: Hunter Ng, Yubo Tao

entry.summary: The authors derive joint influence of overlapping historical estimation errors and terminal forecast estimates in a Vine Copula VAR with normal margins, showing the historical correction reduces to harmonically weighted innovation moments. The resulting covariance estimator yields asymptotically valid repeated-sample forecast intervals for joint events.

entry.title: LiLib: Lifelong Air-to-Ground Path-Loss Prediction on UAVs via a Drift-Triggered Model Library

author.name: Minh Tran

entry.summary: Proposes LiLib, a continual-learning scheme for UAV air-to-ground path-loss prediction that maintains a library of recursive-least-squares experts, using a windowed residual test to detect drift and a probe phase to reuse or create experts. This avoids both forgetting-driven relearning and the averaging problems of a single global model across urbanization regimes.

entry.title: Advantage of Entangled Learning Rules in Quantum Measurement Class Learning

author.name: Arka Prabha Das, Abram Magner

entry.summary: Studies quantum measurement PAC learning, where a learner selects a measurement from a hypothesis class to predict classical labels obtained by measuring unknown quantum states. The paper analyzes when interacting with quantum data using entangled learning rules yields provable advantages over alternatives.

entry.title: LFHE: Local-First Heuristic Evolution for Bounded Local Topology Search in Decentralized Learning with Non-IID Data

author.name: Yin-Kuan Liang (Durham University), Yan Gao (University of Cambridge), Yang Long (Durham University)

entry.summary: Proposes LFHE, a representation-driven topology rewiring framework for decentralized learning under non-IID data that uses only ego-neighborhood and friend-of-a-friend information, with a structural score exactly interpreted through graph Dirichlet energy. This sits between purely local heuristics and graph-wide spectral optimization.

entry.title: Knowing the Store: What a Memory Backend Must Write Down Before an Agent Can Read It

author.name: Ansuman Mullick, Eray T\"uz\"un

entry.summary: The paper asks what an agent memory store must expose, such as record lifecycle states, for an agent to know a record should not be used before retrieving it, scoring this as metamemory monitoring across 148 questions against minimally differing store versions. On the short attribute lists the benchmark produces, none of five language models reliably beats cosine-similarity lookup over names.

entry.title: A Framework for Automated Multi-Source Satellite Data Analytics and LLM-Based Report Generation

author.name: Hind Yousif Alhammadi, Isam Mashhour Al Jawarneh

entry.summary: The paper presents an automated ArcGIS Pro tool using ArcPy to extract Land Surface Temperature from Landsat 7, 8, and 9 data, automating radiometric calibration, NDVI-based emissivity correction, and thermal conversion. It optionally adds an LLM for interpreting statistical results and reporting, cutting processing time from roughly 11-58 minutes manually to 4-11 minutes, tested on data from Ras Al Khaimah.

entry.title: FreSia: Frequency-Semantic Instantiation and Alignment for Multivariate Time Series Analysis

author.name: Yubo Wang, Hui He, Hezhe Qiao, Guoqing Ji, Zhendong Niu

entry.summary: FreSia is a frequency-aware framework that aligns the semantic space of LLMs with the frequency space of multivariate time series for forecasting and anomaly detection. Its Frequency-Guided Prompt mechanism distills frequency-domain structure (seasonal and trend components) that discrete numerical tokenization obscures. This offers an alternative to direct numeric tokenization or heuristic textual descriptions for LLM-based time-series analysis.

entry.title: Response Variability and Stability in Human Reasoning

author.name: Clemens Bombach, Rajmadan Lakshmanan, Marco Ragni

entry.summary: The paper studies the stability of individual human reasoning patterns and whether variability in those patterns predicts learning effects, introducing a formal geometry-based method to quantify distances between reasoning patterns and their internal variability. Tested with generalized linear mixed-effects models and clustering on experimental data, the variability measure interacts with correctness to predict performance gains.

entry.title: Attention-Based Surface Representation Learning for Robot State Prediction and Open-Ended Surface Classification

author.name: Oleg Kushnarev, Alexander Belyaev

entry.summary: The authors propose an attention-based approach for robot terrain perception that supports open-ended class addition by treating new surface classes as trainable vectors, trained via next-state prediction rather than fixed categorical classification. They report 98.56% accuracy on the Belyaev-Kushnarev dataset and 94.8% on BorealTC. This enables robots to extend terrain understanding beyond a fixed label set.

entry.title: System One Models for Wireless Decision-Making:Applications and Performance Evaluation

author.name: Masoud Rahimi, S. M. Matin Alemohammad, Hamid Behroozi, Mahdi Nouri

entry.summary: The paper studies System-One models, which directly learn probability distributions over explicitly defined decision spaces, as lightweight alternatives to autoregressive LLMs for wireless control tasks that require selecting one action from a finite set under strict latency constraints. It formalizes the decision structure and learning objective, maps applicability across physical-layer control, RRM, mobility, slicing, and network operations, and evaluates performance. This pushes back on reflexive LLM adoption in latency-bound domains.

entry.title: VoCa: Designing Speech-Canvas Interaction for Voice-Based Conversational Agents

author.name: Yate Ge, Run Yuan, Yueran Qi, Wenjie He, Jiaqi Mo, Yangshuo Chen, Wenbin Zuo, Xiaohua Sun, Weiwei Guo, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Explores how voice agents can coordinate speech with a visual canvas in multi-turn conversations, informed by an observational study of paired speech-boardwork coordination and a design workshop. The resulting VoCa system supports visual object creation, annotation, and attention guidance alongside speech. A five-day deployment with 18 participants examined usability and interaction patterns.

entry.title: Kapture: Capturing Cardiac Dynamics with Koopman-Governed Learning for Efficient Radar-Based Electrocardiogram Recovery

author.name: Tong Wu, Jing Peng, Ziqi Feng, Yuanyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Kapture reconstructs contactless ECG from mmWave radar by projecting radar hidden states into a low-dimensional observable space governed by a regularized linear Koopman operator, whose predictions refine subsequent hidden states. A temporal contrastive objective suppresses predictable interference such as respiration and motion.

entry.title: An LLM-in-the-loop RL Framework for Bioinformatics Feature Selection

author.name: Xinyuan Wang, Deepti Agrawal, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-in-the-loop reinforcement learning framework for feature selection in high-dimensional bioinformatics data, where the RL agent performs sequential feature selection and the LLM provides domain-informed exploration guidance plus hybrid rewards combining data-driven performance signals.

entry.title: CLARA: Can AI Assess Developmental Appropriateness in Children's Stories?

author.name: Sijing Yin, Zirui Wang, Qian Liu, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: CLARA is a cognitively grounded framework for assessing developmental appropriateness of children's narratives across cognitive, language, and social-emotional dimensions, accompanied by a bilingual Chinese-English benchmark of 1,107 stories with structured silver references. It explores whether AI can approximate human developmental judgments for educational recommendation.

entry.title: Few-Shot Prototype Head Adaptation for On-Device ECG Personalization on PSoC~6

author.name: Guilherme Silva, Pedro Silva, Gladston Moreira, Eduardo Luz

entry.summary: The paper proposes prototype-only head adaptation as a lightweight personalization primitive for TinyML ECG arrhythmia detection on microcontroller-class devices, using a 1-D CNN with roughly 1,314 parameters and avoiding backpropagation entirely. This enables few-shot, on-device personalization accounting for patient-specific morphology and electrode placement without optimizer state or labeled arrhythmic beats. It targets practical deployment constraints on PSoC 6 hardware.

entry.title: Toward Reliable Infant Pose Estimation: A Training-Dynamics Approach to Noisy Annotation Detection

author.name: Emanuele Cardinale, Sara Moccia, Alessandro Cacciatore, Lucia Migliorelli

entry.summary: The paper adapts training-dynamics-based sample selection from noisy-label learning to detect mislocalized keypoints in markerless infant pose estimation, where annotation noise propagates into clinical motion biomarkers. The framework targets improved reliability of preterm movement analysis from video.

entry.title: Topology-Informed Prompt-Conditioned Universal Segmentation of Uterine Structures from Ultrasound and MRI

author.name: Yongheng Sun, Yuexi Gu, Jingwen Sun, Maureen Kohi, Mingxia Liu

entry.summary: TPUS is a unified framework for multi-structure uterine segmentation across ultrasound and MRI, using topological constraints and prompt conditioning to handle heterogeneous appearances, resolutions, and label spaces while mitigating negative transfer. It targets computer-assisted diagnosis and treatment planning for uterine disease.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Sleep Heart Rate Estimation from Accelerometers: Toward Population-Scale Cardiac Insight Without Optical Sensors

author.name: Tanbin Islam Rohan, Pranjol Sen Gupta, Tanusree Debi, Nazmus Sakib

entry.summary: SeqSmoother is a transformer-based temporal corrector for estimating sleep heart rate from wrist accelerometry, combining spectral descriptors, a frequency anchor, and a physics-motivated sub-harmonic feature to detect harmonic lock-on. ECG is used only for reference labels and quality weighting, enabling cardiac insight from existing accelerometer cohorts without optical sensors. Evaluation uses 13 participant-disjoint held-out folds.

entry.title: A Data-Driven Framework for Unsupervised Monitoring of Transmission Systems Using End-of-Line Testing Data: A Case Study at Ford Motor Company

author.name: Mohammad N. Bisheh, Mehrdad Moradi, Parinaz Farajiparvar, Colin Brady, Rajesh Gupta, Xueling Li, Javad Navaei, Milad Parvaneh, Kamran Paynabar

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised monitoring framework for high-dimensional, temporally dependent end-of-line testing data in automotive transmission production, developed with Ford Motor Company. The approach targets anomaly detection where data collection is costly and predefined threshold rules miss nonlinear structure that deep learning methods could capture only with expensive labeled data.

entry.title: Targeted search shows that random-device testing underestimates worst-case error in a simulated wave-based neural operator

author.name: Samrendra Roy, Jason Yoo, Souvik Chakraborty, Syed Bahauddin Alam

entry.summary: In a simulated case study of wave-based processors running Fourier neural operator layers, the authors show that validating on randomly sampled devices underestimates worst-case error: a searched device under fabrication and alignment variation showed 1.08-3.10 times the error of the worst of N random in-spec devices across 120 models.

entry.title: Evaluating Behavioral Context for Interpretable IAM Policy Risk Scoring in Cloud Environments

author.name: Yassin Elsharkawy

entry.summary: Evaluates whether behavioral and environmental context adds measurable value beyond policy and authorization features for interpretable IAM risk prioritization in cloud security, using AWS IAM Context Bench with 534 real observations. The work includes matched cases where policy and environment are held fixed to isolate behavioral effects.

entry.title: Artifact removal improves electrodermal waveforms but not downstream classification in a virtual-reality balance task

author.name: Haochen Chai, Qixu Zhu, Siyao Li, Fangfang Jiang

entry.summary: This negative-result study tests the common assumption that artifact removal improves EDA-based classification, using a residual gating network trained on expert-corrected data and applied to a VR balance-disturbance task. Although the gate detected artifacts well (AUROC 0.94) and reduced waveform error, it produced no classification improvement across five time-series classifiers under leave-one-participant-out evaluation.

entry.title: Exact Calibration and Sharp Risk Geometry for Volume-Sampled Ridge Regression

author.name: Kihun Rhee

entry.summary: This work studies ridge regression fit on exactly s randomly sampled rows of a fixed design, establishing a unique penalty that calibrates the subset fit to a prescribed full-data ridge fit in expectation, and proving sharp sector inequalities characterizing worst-case risk across all response values at every sampling budget.

entry.title: Common-Mode Errors Limit Low-Timestep Deep Spiking Q-Networks

author.name: Zijie Xu, Bingrui Guo, Yiding Sun, Yiting Dong, Zhile Yang, Zhaofei Yu

entry.summary: The paper explains why deep spiking Q-networks degrade sharply at low simulation timesteps by decomposing Q-value errors into common-mode and differential-mode components, showing low-timestep networks suffer disproportionately from common-mode errors. This analysis is relevant to energy-efficient RL on edge devices.

entry.title: Feature Encoding in VAE-based Audio Decoders: Effects of Input, Depth and Distribution

author.name: Louis McCallum, Mick Grierson

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic layer-wise and cross-layer cluster analysis of RAVE and EnCodec decoder activations to understand how musical features like pitch and tempo are encoded in neural audio codecs. Findings show strong encoding of synthetic stimuli across models and domains, reduced but still present for natural audio.

entry.title: Beyond Perturbation Magnitude: Direction-Dependent Responses in Multimodal Geometric Representations

author.name: Yongsheng Luo, Wengan He, Yu Li, Rouying Wu, Wei Lv

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how Gram-determinant-based geometric alignment scores in multimodal models respond to modality degradation, applying controlled video blur and audio noise to frozen cohorts from MSR-VTT and DiDeMo. It finds displacement magnitude explains at most 15 percent of out-of-sample variance in response, showing that magnitude alone does not organize these geometric responses.

entry.title: Pronunciation Editing for Finnish Speech using Phonetic Posteriorgrams

author.name: Zirui Li, Lauri Juvela, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: PPG2Speech is a diffusion-based multispeaker model that edits individual phonemes of native speech to approximate second-language speech without text alignment, using a flow-matching decoder built on Matcha-TTS conditioned on speaker embeddings and pitch. It targets L2 pronunciation feedback for low-resource languages like Finnish. This addresses the lack of L2 speech synthesis training data with a practical editing approach.

entry.title: Forecasting the Growth of Social Media Information Cascades: Towards Human-in-the-Loop Misinformation Triage

author.name: Ansh Gupta, Abhiram Gorle, Aayush Rajesh, Tsachy Weissman

entry.summary: The paper frames early misinformation triage as cascade-continuation forecasting: predicting propagation-tree growth from the first 30 minutes of activity. On FibVID, combining structural depth entropy and temporal arrival entropy raises R^2 for log future growth from 0.307 to 0.323 with modest log-MAE gains on held-out claims. The improvements are real but small, supporting human-in-the-loop prioritization rather than autonomous moderation.

entry.title: Graph-Based Recognition of Simulated Train-Driver States From Facial and Upper-Body Keypoints

author.name: Olivia Nocentini, Marta Lagomarsino, Gokhan Solak, Younggeol Cho, Qiyi Tong, Sara Zeynalpour, Marta Lorenzini, Alessandro Ledda, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: This study builds a vision-based railway safety system using a single RGB camera and a graph neural network to classify simulated train-driver states into alert, not-alert, and emergency classes from facial and upper-body keypoints. Combining facial and skeletal features yields the best three-class accuracy of 81 percent under lightweight conditions.

entry.title: RBMatch: Dual-Level Class Rebalancing for Semi-Supervised Building Footprint Extraction

author.name: Akil Ahmad Taki, Shaikh Anowarul Fattah

entry.summary: RBMatch tackles severe foreground-background imbalance in semi-supervised building footprint extraction from remote sensing imagery, showing that balancing pseudo-label selection alone is insufficient because background bias re-emerges during unsupervised loss optimization. It applies dual-level class rebalancing across both stages. Building footprint maps matter for urban planning and disaster response.

entry.title: Geometry-Constrained Bidirectional Point Cloud Registration for Thin, Sheet-Like Heritage Artifacts

author.name: Yuezhe Zhang, Lei Wei, Jingnan Du, Shuai Wan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a geometry-constrained bidirectional point cloud registration method for thin, sheet-like heritage artifacts, which cannot be marked or suspended and thus require independent front and back surface scans that are hard to align. The method addresses rotational ambiguity and structural collapse during iterative optimization where shared geometric features are scarce. It supports non-contact digitization of fragile cultural heritage.

entry.title: Event Detection in Table Tennis Videos using 2D Keypoints

author.name: Rainer Lienhart, Daniel Kienzle, Shin'ichi Satoh, Anastasiia Bilinska

entry.summary: EventNet is a two-stage pipeline for frame-accurate detection of key events (like ball-racket contacts) in table tennis videos. It extracts 2D keypoints of player upper-body poses, table corners, and ball center, then uses a small keypoint transformer to build representations robust to viewpoint, lighting, and background changes, followed by temporal classification of keypoint sequences. This enables downstream 3D trajectory and spin estimation on long, unedited recordings.

entry.title: Fluorescence-enhanced Whisker Array with Vision-based Deformation Analysis for Underwater Source Localization

author.name: Xiaochi Xie, Hao Li, Shixuan Zhao, Siyue Yao, Shuran Song, Mark R. Cutkosky

entry.summary: The authors build a bioinspired whisker array sensing system for localizing underwater hydrodynamic sources using fluorescence-based optical readout instead of direct imaging, minimizing disturbance to observed animals. Five nitinol-cored whiskers with fluorescent shells are tracked with UV excitation and a monocular camera, and a lightweight CNN captures temporal deformation patterns for source localization.

entry.title: Nested Power Models for Multirotor Propulsion: From Aerodynamic Drag to Electrical Losses

author.name: Antonio Franchi, Aaron Saini, Ahmed Ali, Chiara Gabellieri

entry.summary: This paper develops a nested sequence of propulsion-power models for multirotors that progressively adds acceleration-dependent effects: reversible kinetic-energy rate, torque-dependent electromechanical dissipation, and lumped speed-proportional losses. Models are identified on one set of experiments and validated on another using a motor-drive-propeller unit, with independent estimates of rotational inertia and aerodynamic drag used to verify physical attribution. This addresses the inability of speed-only models to capture acceleration-dependent power effects.

entry.title: Scalable Regularized Vector Multiplicative Error Models for Positive-valued Financial Time Series

author.name: Rohan Hemant Chhatre, Chiranjit Dutta, Nalini Ravishanker, Sumanta Basu

entry.summary: This paper develops regularized estimation for log vector multiplicative error models with multivariate gamma errors using hierarchical lag structures and a blockwise coordinate descent algorithm with Gauss-Seidel-style updates. The approach makes high-dimensional financial time series estimation computationally tractable compared to penalized maximum likelihood.

entry.title: Readings on the nature of alignment research

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld crossposts

entry.summary: Caspar Oesterheld argues that alignment research is more conceptual, preparadigmatic, and intuition-driven than capabilities research, and assembles a curated reading list of texts making similar points. The post aims to inform how alignment work is organized, tested, and automated.

entry.title: Beyond the Parameter Monolith: Reconstructive Memories, Executable Skills, and Residual Assembly for Language Models

author.name: A. Bochkov

entry.summary: This paper explores FEM-ASM, a finite-element-inspired architecture separating contextual computation, persistent storage, and deterministic executable skills, with an explicit residual operator reconciling typed proposals at shared interface nodes. The honest evaluation includes negative results: an attention-free Multi-Mesh prototype learns causal LM but does not achieve competitive general capability.

entry.title: Towards Credible Agent-Based Policy Simulations: Disentangling Opportunities and Preferences in a Financial Inclusion Case Study of Egypt

author.name: Alba Aguilera, Georgina Curto, Nardine Osman, Ahmed Al-Awah

entry.summary: Presents a general modeling framework, aligned with the Capability Approach, for building credible agent-based policy simulations grounded in data and domain-expert knowledge, disentangling opportunities from preferences in agent behavior. It is instantiated in a financial-inclusion case study of Egypt with heterogeneous individuals and firms. Credibility of agent-based models for policy-making is an important and often-neglected methodological problem.

entry.title: R1A-PC: Physics-Guided Electromagnetic Inversion of Three-Dimensional Human Point Clouds in Complex Static Environments

author.name: Xudong Yuan, Ruyun Xu, Jingtai Yang, Xianzheng Sun

entry.summary: R1A-PC is a physics-guided method reconstructing 2048-point 3D human point clouds from electromagnetic measurements in complex static environments, using background subtraction, a frequency-balanced discrete Born adjoint for spatial knowledge maps, and bounded deformation stages. It addresses multipath interference from walls and floors that obscures weak target signals. This is a specialized sensing/perception contribution with potential surveillance and through-wall sensing applications.

entry.title: Agentic-ZTA: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Autonomous Zero Trust Enforcement

author.name: Shovan Roy, Lopamudra Praharaj, Maanak Gupta, Bhavani Thuraisingham

entry.summary: Agentic-ZTA operationalizes the NIST SP 800-207 zero trust architecture control loop using a coordinated multi-agent decision pipeline, embedding policy knowledge into a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline for inference-time policy retrieval. Access requests are intercepted by a policy enforcement point, enriched with context, and routed to domain-specific policy engine agents. The paper addresses safety, reliability, and policy compliance challenges in automating zero trust enforcement.

entry.title: CRAFTER: Causality-based Self-adaptation for Autonomous IoT Systems

author.name: Houssam Hajj Hassan (IP Paris, SAMOVAR), Ajay Kattepur (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR), Denis Conan (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR), Georgios Bouloukakis (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR, ECE)

entry.summary: CRAFTER is a framework for designing and deploying self-adaptive IoT systems using causal reinforcement learning, aiming to maintain quality of service under fluctuating workloads and evolving demands. It targets reusable adaptation solutions across multiple IoT verticals rather than domain-specific designs.

entry.title: CyTReX: Explainable AI-Based Cybersecurity Threat Reasoning Framework for DER Networks

author.name: Damilola Popoola, Souradeep Bhattacharya, Manimaran Govindarasu

entry.summary: CyTReX is an explainable, evidence-grounded threat reasoning framework for distributed energy resource networks that goes beyond single attack labels from edge anomaly detection systems by exposing alternative threat interpretations for operators. It addresses the gap between detection and operational response in power-grid communication traffic. This is a practical contribution to critical-infrastructure security.

entry.title: Neurodiversity-Aware Multimodal Affective Computing for Neurodevelopmental Assessment: From Norm-Referenced Classification to Context-Sensitive Decision Support

author.name: Mateusz Pomianek, Anna {\L}\k{e}\.zniak-Seruga

entry.summary: Proposes a conceptual architecture for neurodiversity-aware multimodal affective computing in which population-relative deviation is not treated as sufficient evidence of adverse functioning. The framework incorporates observable signals, modality quality, context, and population-relative information to support context-sensitive decision support rather than norm-referenced classification. It is explicitly a position paper without new empirical results.

entry.title: Towards Automatically Pruning Logging Code with Coding Agents: How Far Are We?

author.name: He Yang Yuan, Haonan Zhang, Xin Wang, An Ran Chen, Kisub Kim, Zishuo Ding, Zhenhao Li

entry.summary: This paper studies the underexplored problem of logging code removal, extracting and validating real-world cases from Python and Java repositories to derive 10 removal patterns and 11 removal reasons. The authors construct LogRem, a 387-case dataset of real-world logging removals, and evaluate how well coding agents can automate this maintenance task. It matters because logging affects runtime overhead and diagnostic clarity, and this is one of the first systematic treatments of its removal.

entry.title: Weave Mamba Fusion: Global Cross-Scale Interaction for Lightweight Face Detection

author.name: Dohun Kim, Jinmyung Jung

entry.summary: The paper introduces Weave Mamba Fusion, which uses state-space (Mamba) scanning for global cross-scale interaction in lightweight face detection, designing a combination of pyramid scales that preserves cross-scale structure during the scan rather than collapsing scales via summation. It targets robust detection of small, occluded, and extreme-pose faces at low compute.

entry.title: TEMPEST: Temporal Embeddings for Scalable Driver Identification via Angular Margin Learning

author.name: Kyle Musgrove, Dylan B. Lewis, Sarah Powers, Emma J. Reid, Hector Santos-Villalobos

entry.summary: Introduces TEMPEST, a temporal convolutional network trained with ArcFace loss that maps 60-second multimodal driving windows to compact 96-dimensional embeddings for scalable driver identification, supporting dynamic enrollment without retraining. It achieves 91.71% Rank-1 accuracy on a 45-driver dataset under rigorous temporal evaluation, outperforming triplet-loss baselines that degrade with fleet size.

entry.title: CLM-as-a-Judge: Evaluating an Open Contrastive Decision Model on Public Judge Benchmarks

author.name: Gowthamkumar Nandakishore

entry.summary: Evaluates an open contrastive decision model (CLM-v0.1-8B) as an LLM judge and finds it performs near chance on RM-Bench, JudgeBench, and HaluEval, significantly underperforming reward models and generative judges of similar size. The paper also notes two useful properties: calibratable confidence and a scaling signal, making it a candid negative result with diagnostic value.

entry.title: CNet: A Complex-Valued Deep Learning Framework with Wirtinger Autodifferentiation and FFT--Hadamard Convolution

author.name: Marcel Crasmaru

entry.summary: CNet is a C++/CUDA framework for complex-valued neural networks using Wirtinger calculus autodiff, Born-rule classification instead of softmax, and FFT-based convolution primitives verified against finite differences. It takes a physics-native design view where layers are complex, often unitary, operations on amplitude vectors.

entry.title: Extending Music Annotation Schemas: Zero-Shot Prediction or Few-Shot Adaptation?

author.name: Christos Plachouras, Emmanouil Benetos, Johan Pauwels

entry.summary: This work benchmarks how to extend music annotation systems to new attributes, comparing zero-shot prediction with audio-language models against supervised few-shot adaptation across different annotation budgets using the MGPHot dataset. It addresses the practical question of at what annotation budget supervised adaptation beats zero-shot prediction for backfilling commercial catalogs.

entry.title: Learning Explainable Representations of Complex Game-playing Strategies

author.name: Abhijeet Krishnan, Colin M. Potts, Arnav Jhala, Harshad Khadilkar, Shirish Karande, Chris Martens

entry.summary: The authors propose a method for training RL agents to synthesize learned gameplay strategies as executable, human-readable procedures based on action sequences, demonstrated on chess and a grid-based environment. This aims to make agent strategies explainable in terms similar to human cognitive abstractions.

entry.title: X-OPM: Explainable Automatic Digital On-Chip Power Modeling for Enhanced Robustness

author.name: Jingbo Jiang, Xizi Chen, Jian Peng, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: X-OPM introduces a physically grounded feature engineering framework for digital on-chip power meters, deriving features from synchronous digital VLSI circuit design principles and using tree-based models to capture them, improving generalization to unseen workloads compared to end-to-end trained models. This supports proactive power management through runtime power prediction and power-aware scheduling.

entry.title: Quality-Aware Self-Correcting Speech Translation on an Edge Device

author.name: Zubair Ajmal Farooq, Diptesh Kanojia

entry.summary: The authors present a fully offline speech-to-speech translation pipeline running on a 4 GB Jetson Nano, combining Whisper-tiny ASR, Opus-MT translation, and a multilingual BERT quality-estimation gate that triggers secondary-pass correction. Among three correction methods, minimum Bayes-risk decoding yields statistically significant BLEU, ChrF, and COMET gains on FLORES-200 English-Spanish. It demonstrates practical self-correction under tight edge constraints.

entry.title: Leveraging a four-quadrant approach for evaluating Redpine Science

author.name: Filip Dorm, Leonora Vesterbacka

entry.summary: This report evaluates Redpine Science, a service giving models and agents access to peer-reviewed literature via MCP and API, across four evaluations covering retrieval chunk relevance and answer quality with and without the tool versus web search. It combines public benchmarks with an expert-validated question set to mitigate saturation and memorization concerns.

entry.title: Responsible Institutional Analytics: Interpreting Bias with AI Support

author.name: Francielle Marques, Ariel Ortiz-Beltr\'an, Ishari Amarasinghe, Davinia Hern\'andez-Leo

entry.summary: FACTRIA is a framework organizing biasing factors in higher-education institutional analytics across four areas: the analytics pipeline, institutional context, course characteristics, and demographics. The authors built a generative-AI chatbot that prompts stakeholders to reflect on these factors, and a qualitative study with four authentic cases showed the chatbot fostered more responsible interpretation. This is a human-centered approach to responsible AI in education administration.

entry.title: Decomposition-Guided Curvelet Thresholding for Sharp-to-Soft CT Kernel Conversion

author.name: Mahmoud Nasr, Jan K. Argasinski, Krzysztof Brzostowski, Adam Piorkowski

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid CT image denoising framework combining empirical mode decomposition variants (EMD, VMD, MEMD, BEMD) with curvelet transform thresholding, applying soft and hard thresholding per mode before reconstruction, evaluated across multiple CT reconstruction kernels. It aims to convert sharp-kernel CT images to softer, lower-noise representations.

entry.title: What Frame-Level Labels Can and Cannot Do for Small-UAV Point Detection in Thermal Video

author.name: Wonbin Son, Gyumum Choi, Junil Seo, Hyungjoon Kim

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes what small-UAV detection in thermal video can be learned from cheap frame-level presence/absence labels instead of expensive spatial annotations, using an architecture that freezes classification-learned spatial features and trains a point-detection readout. It characterizes detection capability, learning behavior, and applications when annotation budgets are constrained. Anti-UAV detection is an emerging security application.

entry.title: Simplified Swarm Optimization for Surrogate-Assisted Reliability Design of Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor Power Modules Using an Open-Source Process Finite-Element Model

author.name: Wei-Chang Yeh

entry.summary: This paper builds an open pipeline for reliability design of IGBT power modules, combining an open-source process finite-element model, surrogates tuned via Simplified Swarm Optimization, multi-objective design search, and FEA confirmation with infill sampling. It emphasizes rigorous validation of optimized designs against fresh FEA runs, a step often skipped in surrogate-assisted design studies.

entry.title: Silicon Language: A Robot-Native Knowledge Exchange Framework for Heterogeneous Robots

author.name: Yi Liu (School of Mechanical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China, Yulin Saiyi Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., Yulin, China), Xianglin Meng (Yulin Saiyi Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., Yulin, China), Chang Chen (Yulin Intelligent Unmanned Equipment Innovation Center Co., Ltd., Yulin, China), Jingjing Fan (Yulin Intelligent Unmanned Equipment Innovation Center Co., Ltd., Yulin, China)

entry.summary: Silicon Language proposes a robot-native framework in which robots encode their experience into knowledge packets, publish and retrieve peer packets, translate them to their own hardware, and independently validate them through local trials before adoption. It aims to reduce human re-engineering when transferring skills across heterogeneous robots.

entry.title: HexaGripper: A Single-Actuator, Winch-Deployed Gripper for Autonomous Aerial Parcel Collection

author.name: Nimantha Adikaram, Mahen Abeyratne, Lakmina Chandrajith, A. H. T. E. De Silva, Isira Naotunna, Asanka Perera

entry.summary: HexaGripper is a single-actuator, winch-deployed six-plate gripper enabling UAVs to autonomously collect cuboid parcels without landing, manual loading, or ground infrastructure. The mechanism provides synchronized grasping with a wide capture region and tolerance to positional misalignment, integrated with vision-based alignment and state-based control. The system was validated in static grasping tests and end-to-end outdoor aerial collection experiments.

entry.title: Classifications in modular restricted Boltzmann machines

author.name: Elena Agliari, Andrea Lepre, Edoardo Roscani

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a modular associative network of L Hopfield models with competitive Hebbian/anti-Hebbian coupling, showing its integral representation coincides with an assembly of coupled RBMs, extending the HM-RBM duality to modular settings. It trains the modular RBM for classification where queries spanning multiple patterns are mapped to label tuples read from hidden layers.

entry.title: Three types of AI risk: why (some) leftists are against (some) AI regulations

author.name: sudo-nym

entry.summary: The author proposes a taxonomy of AI risk — AI serving random malicious actors, AI entrenching current power holders, and AI serving no one via takeover — to explain why some leftist groups oppose regulations favored by x-risk-focused communities. The analysis argues the two camps pattern-match the same policies to different risks and talk past each other.

entry.title: Supercomputing researchers document evolution of AI hardware

author.name: Haley Wahl | MIT Lincoln Laboratory

entry.summary: MIT Lincoln Laboratory describes its Lincoln AI Computing Survey (LAICS), an eight-year effort summarized across six papers that catalogs commercial AI accelerators and compares their peak performance and power. The survey began in 2018 to answer government sponsor questions about the explosion of new AI hardware.

entry.title: CHARTER: Auditing Reference Substitution in Hierarchical Compact-Evidence Evaluation for Computational Pathology

author.name: Hyun Do Jung, Jungwon Choi, Soojung Choi, Yujin Oh, Hwiyoung Kim

entry.summary: CHARTER is a reference-aware evaluation charter for digital pathology pipelines, requiring researchers to declare the intended evaluation target and reference, and to quantify how candidate filtering changes measured fidelity of compact evidence. It addresses subtle mismatches that can distort comparisons between MIL explanation strategies in whole-slide imaging.

entry.title: Learning to Remember: Distilling Memory Retention for Compact Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Nilushika Udayangania, Kishor Nandakishora, Marimuthu Palaniswami

entry.summary: Develops knowledge distillation methods tailored to recurrent networks for time series, transferring memory-retention behavior from large teacher RNN/LSTM models to compact students suitable for wearables and edge deployment. The work addresses the inadequacy of CV-oriented KD methods for sequential memory dynamics.

entry.title: Low-Rank and Structured Sparse Tensor Decomposition for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate Functional Data

author.name: Mohammad N. Bisheh, Che-Yi Liao, Kamran Paynabar

entry.summary: The paper proposes two unsupervised sparse tensor decomposition methods for monitoring multivariate sensor data in manufacturing: entrywise sparse CP decomposition for localized anomalies and fiberwise sparse-group lasso CP decomposition for structured sensor-specific departures. The methods preserve multimode correlation structure across samples, sensors, and time.

entry.title: A BEMD-Based Quaternion Filtering Approach Sharp-to-Soft Kernel CT Image Conversion

author.name: Mahmoud Nasr, Jan K. Argasinski, Krzysztof Brzostowski, Adam Piorkowski

entry.summary: The authors propose converting sharp-kernel CT images to soft-kernel-like representations using Bidimensional Empirical Mode Decomposition combined with Quaternion Bilateral Filtering (BEMD-QBF), preserving anatomical structure while reducing noise. This targets the trade-off between spatial resolution and noise in CT reconstruction kernels.

entry.title: RACE-FPP: A Robust AI-assisted Characterisation Enhancement for Fringe Projection Profilometry

author.name: Osman Ali (Manufacturing Metrology Team, University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom), Xiangjun Kong (Manufacturing Metrology Team, University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom), Tibebe Yalew (Manufacturing Metrology Team, University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom), Waiel Elmadih (Taraz Metrology Ltd., Nottingham, United Kingdom), Samanta Piano (Manufacturing Metrology Team, University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom)

entry.summary: From the University of Nottingham's manufacturing metrology team, this paper integrates deep learning-based corner detection into a complete fringe projection profilometry characterization pipeline, evaluated not just on detection metrics but on camera-projector stereo consistency and overall 3D measurement accuracy. It improves checkerboard feature localization robustness under challenging conditions like lens blur and varied target orientations. The work bridges AI perception and precision metrology.

entry.title: Demo: Vision-Language Model-Guided Online Calibration of an Electromagnetic Digital Twin

author.name: Zerui Kang, Yishen Lim, Zhouyou Gu, Seungnyun Kim, Seung-Woo Ko, Tony Q. S. Quek, Jihong Park

entry.summary: This demo paper shows a VLM-guided framework for calibrating an electromagnetic digital twin online using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with one VLM call mapping visible materials to conductivity priors via ITU-R standards and another planning waypoints for informative measurements. Real indoor experiments demonstrate reduced calibration error and travel cost compared to baselines.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving Guided by Chinese Philosophical Wisdom

author.name: Xiaojun Bi, Xiaoyuan Ma, Yiwen Sun, Tianren Huang, Chaoran Liu, Bokai Huang, Hao Yang, Baichuan Mo

entry.summary: CPW-Drive is a closed-loop retrieval-augmented generation framework that injects value principles extracted from Confucian classical texts into LLM-based autonomous driving decision-making, aiming to balance safety, efficiency, and social norms. It is among the first attempts to ground driving decisions in a structured ethical-philosophical knowledge source.

entry.title: GFGE: Unifying Explainable AI Methods through an Interpretation Framework

author.name: Jinfeng Zhong

entry.summary: The paper proposes the General Framework for Generating Explanations, a unifying conceptual framework for explainable AI grounded in sense-reading and sense-giving activities and an Interpret/Explain Schema linking analyst interpretation, communicated accounts, and recipient interpretation. It operationalizes this schema through five roles to describe how evidence becomes explanation for a recipient.

entry.title: OntoInk: Interactive Ontology Visualization, Validation, and Reasoning

author.name: Ebrahim Norouzi, J\"org Waitelonis, Harald Sack

entry.summary: OntoInk is an open-source MkDocs plugin that unifies ontology documentation, interactive visualization, SHACL validation, OWL DL reasoning, and inline Turtle editing within a single documentation-as-code pipeline. It replaces fragmented workflows with separate tools and embeds editable RDF-aware diagrams directly in documentation pages.

entry.title: AI-Decision Checkpoints for AI-Augmented Business Process Management: Framework and Educational Instantiation

author.name: Amin Jalali

entry.summary: This paper proposes AI-decision checkpoints: explicit moments in process development where developers identify AI-candidate sub-processes, assess effects on time, cost, quality, and flexibility, consider legal and organizational constraints, and document decisions. It instantiates the framework in a BPM educational context to prepare graduates for AI as a first-class design element.

entry.title: Collective intelligence through aggregation

author.name: Franz Dietrich, Christian List

entry.summary: A theoretical investigation of judgment aggregation for groups making interconnected judgments on multi-valued issues, examining three challenges: reasonable aggregation methods can produce inconsistent collective judgments, and related impossibility and design questions for collective intelligence. The work extends judgment aggregation theory beyond binary issues.

entry.title: Adaptive Operator Selection in Bilevel Large Neighborhood Search for Electric Autonomous Dial-a-Ride Problem under Uncertainty

author.name: Ishara Hewa Pathiranange, Aneta Neumann

entry.summary: The paper studies adaptive selection of insertion operators within a bilevel large neighborhood search framework for the electric autonomous dial-a-ride problem, including a chance-constrained variant where travel times are random variables and time-window constraints hold probabilistically. It targets realistic autonomous electric fleet routing under uncertainty. This is relevant to operations research for autonomous mobility services.

entry.title: A Unified Dynamics Framework for Reinforcement Learning and Classical Control of a Six-DOF Pipeline-Tracking ROV in NVIDIA Isaac Sim

author.name: Cheng Siong Chin, M. Venkateshkumar, Jianhua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline-tracking architecture for a six-DOF underwater ROV where a single USD scene supplies identical dynamics parameters to both a NumPy implementation of Fossen's marine-craft equations and an NVIDIA Isaac Sim deployment. This eliminates the sim-to-sim gap between RL training physics and deployment physics.

entry.title: DialectSentEval 2026: Arabic Dialect Sentiment Analysis and Swapping Shared Task

author.name: Saad Ezzini, Shadi Abudalfa, Maram Alharbi, Salmane Chafik, Hind Alatawi, Mo El-Haj, Ahmed Abdelali, Osamah Alnahari, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: This paper introduces DialectSentEval, a shared task hosted at ArabicNLP 2026 with two subtasks: multi-class, multi-dialect sentiment classification and a generative sentiment-swap task that inverts sentiment polarity while preserving other attributes.
