entry.summary: This work shows that reported accuracy gains from fusing environmental sensor data with leaf imagery in crop disease datasets are largely artifacts of session-level leakage: 91.9% of CDD test images have exact sensor duplicates in the training set. An image-free classifier using only timestamps matches or beats multimodal models, implying prior results reflect memorization rather than genuine sensor benefit.

entry.title: SOL: Measuring Gaps between Text Distributions by Double Sliced Wasserstein Metrics

author.name: Gregor Kornhardt, Moritz Piening, Jannis Chemseddine, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: SOL is a proposed distance between text distributions that represents each sequence as the empirical measure of hidden states under a fixed transformer and compares distributions via double sliced Wasserstein distance. The authors prove SOL is a metric when the transformer is injective and show it better captures distribution fit than perplexity or generative-perplexity-style substitutes, particularly for diffusion and flow language models that only have likelihood bounds.

entry.title: Grounding Probes: Generator-Independent Hallucination Detection from Observer Model Hidden States

author.name: Michael Rathmayr, \'Ad\'am Kov\'acs, G\'abor Recski

entry.summary: This work proposes grounding probes: logistic regression over mean-pooled middle-layer hidden states of an observer model that reads context, question, and response in a single forward pass without generating, detecting RAG responses not grounded in context. Unlike prior probes, it decouples the detector from the generating model, enabling detection for closed-weight generators. Practical and well-motivated contribution to hallucination detection.

entry.title: Building LLM Agent Systems the Deep Learning Way: From Modular Design to Architecture Search

author.name: Tao Feng, Pengrui Han, Zhongjie Dai, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: The paper proposes constructing LLM agent systems modularly like deep neural networks, drawing analogies between agent building blocks (retrieval, memory, prompting strategies) and neural modules, and extends this to automated architecture search over agent designs. This moves agent construction from hand-engineering toward principled, optimizable composition. A promising conceptual and systems contribution.

entry.title: Verification Trap: Understanding Test-Time Selection Failures under False Premises in Code Generation

author.name: Feng He, Hejia Wang, Linghao Meng, Ming Gao, Qiankun Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode called the Verification Trap in test-time compute for code generation: when generator and verifier share a false premise, they become coupled through a mistaken belief, so the selector can choose a hidden-test-wrong candidate even when a correct program exists in the pool. Experiments across three settings show verifiers fail to provide an independent corrective signal under misleading premises. This challenges the common assumption that sampling plus verification reliably improves code generation.

entry.title: Can Language Models Learn to Reject Their Own Bad Reasoning Steps?

author.name: Siheng Xiong, Xiaoze Liu, Yiqiao Jin, Xiaoqian Wang, Jing Gao

entry.summary: The paper defines prefix recoverability (probability a frozen generator completes a prefix correctly) and introduces Self-Step Rejection, a lightweight LoRA acceptance gate trained on the generator backbone that lets the model reject its own bad reasoning steps without an external verifier. It uses confidence-qualified first-passage supervision to handle noisy recoverability signals. This advances self-verifying reasoning with minimal overhead.

entry.title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches

author.name: Shaokun Zhang, Yifan Zhang, Jian Hu, Yueying Li, Hao Zhang, Binfeng Xu, Jan Kautz, Yi Dong

entry.summary: LoGRA reduces the memory demands of RL post-training for LLMs by storing learning signals as low-rank gradient sketches usable for both model updates and policy synchronization, complemented by predicted-KL step control to keep updates stable. It cuts average training memory by up to 45.7% across reasoning tasks without performance loss. This lowers the barrier to RL fine-tuning for resource-constrained practitioners.

entry.title: PlotGround: Grounding Plot Digitization in Real Scientific Figures and Their Source Data

author.name: Yaohui Zhang, Binxu Li, Haoyi Duan, Jiacheng Miao, Yixin Wang, Xinran Du, Chenyue Li, Shilong Liu, Kevin Wu, James Zou

entry.summary: PlotGround is an automated pipeline that builds plot-digitization benchmarks from real scientific figures paired with author-released source data, mapping figures to tables and generating quantitative questions with source-grounded reference answers. It addresses the gap left by synthetic-chart benchmarks and enables measuring how accurately models recover plotted values from real papers.

entry.title: What Do Verifiable Rewards Teach Video-Language Models About Time? A Controlled Multi-Model Study

author.name: Avyay Sadhu, Patrick Cooper

entry.summary: This controlled study fine-tunes four open video-language models (including Qwen3-VL and Qwen2.5-VL variants and Gemma-3-12B) with GRPO under verified, unverified, and mixed data recipes to determine what RLVR actually teaches about temporal reasoning in video QA. Evaluation spans in-domain synthetic tasks and out-of-domain real-video temporal stress tests.

entry.title: Watermarks and Fingerprints as Soft Bindings for Content Provenance: An Open-Licence Benchmark for Images, Audio and Video

author.name: Seyedmahdi Kazempourradi (Original Pictures Technologies, Inc., Delaware, USA), Ramtin Mojtahedi (Original Pictures Technologies, Inc., Delaware, USA), Behrang Mohseni (Original Pictures Technologies, Inc., Delaware, USA)

entry.summary: This benchmark compares watermarking and fingerprinting as soft bindings for content provenance under one audited, open-licence protocol aligned with standards like C2PA. It evaluates 25 image, 7 audio, and 7 video watermark configurations plus 35 fingerprinting methods on robustness, false positives, quality, and cost, identifying PixelSeal as the best image balance.

entry.title: Beyond Plausibility: Verifiable Fine-Grained Image Editing on Structured Assets

author.name: Muyao Wang, Chen Zhu, Shiqi Yang, DongHyun Hwan, Hideki Nakayama

entry.summary: This paper introduces a verifiable benchmark for fine-grained image editing on structured assets, closing the gap between realistic-image benchmarks that rely on subjective human or VLM judgments and deterministic evaluation limited to synthetic shapes. It enables precise measurement of how much of a requested edit was executed and where unintended changes occurred.

entry.title: NAMVIS: Next-Scale Autoregressive Multi-View Image Synthesis

author.name: Ramil Khafizov, Ilya Statsenko, Ruslan Rakhimov, Artem Komarichev, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

entry.summary: NAMVIS reformulates sparse-view multi-view image synthesis as geometry-conditioned next-scale autoregression, generating discrete visual tokens in coarse-to-fine steps with parallel sampling across scales and views, avoiding expensive iterative denoising of diffusion approaches. Multi-scale projective pose encoding anchors generation to explicit camera geometry.

entry.title: PWM: Personalized World Models with Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhexin Lou, Guancheng Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yang Zhao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: PWM is a framework for personalizing interactive world models from short user-provided scene videos using online reinforcement learning, with GRPO updating a compact LoRA adapter under a unified reward covering scene appearance, visual continuity, and motion, plus base-policy anchoring for regularization. It allows users to explore specific scenes from their own videos while retaining action-conditioned generation quality. This connects world models, personalization, and RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: EMBER-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-Event Causal Memory in Long-Horizon Embodied Tasks

author.name: Aoyang Cai, Boning Zhao, Shaoxuan Xie, Dahui Gao, Huan Yang, Zhongyuan Wang, Zhiwei Yu, Guocai Yao

entry.summary: EMBER-Bench is a new egocentric benchmark with 189 household tasks and 699 QA pairs for cross-event causal reasoning in long-horizon embodied tasks, covering task progress, failure recovery, external interventions, and compounding effects of past events. It moves beyond retrieval-style memory benchmarks toward testing how history changes the current world state and constrains future actions. Newly recorded videos and annotations make it a fresh evaluation resource for embodied agents.

entry.title: RoMod: Temporal Routing Modulation via Mixture-of-Experts for Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Chao Huang, Pengfei Wei, Benfeng Wang, Chengliang Liu, Wei Wang, Li Shen, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: RoMod studies where anomaly-related evidence lives inside sparse MoE-based MLLMs for video anomaly detection, finding with a fully frozen backbone and no training that a small set of experts concentrates the evidence, recurs across layers, and specializes by anomaly type, forming a dynamic routing subnetwork. The paper builds on this analysis with temporal routing modulation. It offers both mechanistic insight and a practical detection method.

entry.title: DynaMesh: Dynamic 3D Texture Generation

author.name: Raj Hansini, Guan Chen, Rana Hanocka, Itai Lang

entry.summary: DynaMesh generates dynamic textures on 3D meshes: given a textureless shape and a text prompt describing an effect, it produces an evolving appearance while geometry stays fixed — complementing prior work on dynamic geometry and static textures. It replaces the naive two-generator pipeline (video model plus image-to-3D) with a more direct approach. This fills a real gap in 3D content creation for games and VFX.

entry.title: Monocular markerless biomechanics for clinically interpretable gait assessment in spinal cord injury

author.name: Shreyasvi Natraj, Mathieu Ruepp, Yanke Li, Robert Riener, Inge Eriks-Hoogland, Diego Paez-Granados

entry.summary: This work introduces the SCAI SCI Gait dataset (239 individuals with spinal cord injury, synchronized video, motion capture, and force plates) and demonstrates a monocular markerless pipeline fitted to an OpenSim model that achieves strong agreement with motion capture (r = 0.68-0.90, joint-angle RMSE ~4-6.5 degrees). This validates clinically interpretable gait analysis without expensive marker-based labs, broadening access to rehabilitation monitoring for neurological patients.

entry.title: Casual Flash Lighting for Gaussian Splat Inverse Rendering

author.name: Jiamin Xu, Dongheng Wei, Jiarong Zhao, Qi Wang, James Tompkin, Weiwei Xu, Gang Xu

entry.summary: The authors combine static and flash lighting captured casually with handheld devices to recover geometry, materials, and lighting in a 2D Gaussian Splatting inverse rendering setup. A view-consistent, GS-anchored diffuse field lets flash residuals constrain albedo and BRDF without requiring dark rooms or specialized hardware.

entry.title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation

author.name: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi, Derek Zhang, Xiangchen Liu, Xueting Li, Umar Iqbal, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

entry.summary: InterMimicGen is a self-evolving motion-imitation framework in which robot motion data and a physics-based tracking policy iteratively improve each other. It retargets large human-object interaction mocap datasets into humanoid references preserving whole-body and hand-object coordination, then trains a generalist dexterous tracker in simulation, enabling scaled humanoid loco-manipulation.

entry.title: Continual Humanoid Motion Learning

author.name: Zhewen He, Hao Huang, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Chong Yu, Tao Chen, Anthony Tzes, Yi Fang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Similarity-guided LoRA-PNN, a progressive neural network policy for humanoid whole-body control that prevents catastrophic forgetting by construction while reusing knowledge across sequentially learned skills via low-rank adaptation. A two-level motion-similarity measure using dynamic time warping aggregated by optimal transport selects which prior skill to extend.

entry.title: Neural Barriers: An Online Certifiable Learning-enhanced Adaptive High Order Safety Critical Control

author.name: Lishuo Pan, Mattia Catellani, An Cao, Lorenzo Sabattini, Nora Ayanian

entry.summary: This paper combines control barrier functions with a Neural ODE that adapts online to unknown time-varying disturbances, using conformal prediction to quantify adaptation uncertainty. The approach provides formal safety guarantees for real-world robots such as aerial vehicles under model perturbations, becoming conservative when uncertainty is high.

entry.title: Inspect Robots: Evaluating the Capabilities and Safety of Embodied AI

author.name: Christopher Leet, Achu Menon, Sravanthi Machcha, Sabrina Zou, Aayushya Patel, Aditya Kumar Singh, Anish Kr Singh, Galaba Vamsi, Javin Ahuja, Sai Asish Yamani, Tushar Anand, Vedang Alle, Zihan Jack Zhang, Tzu Kit Chan, Jay Chooi

entry.summary: Inspect Robots is an open-source, modular framework for developing and running physical evaluations of embodied agents, pairing reusable abstractions for specifying evaluations and analyzing results with infrastructure that automates setup, execution, and termination. The authors demonstrate it by evaluating six policies based on frontier language models for capability and safety. As language models increasingly control hardware, standardized embodied evaluation becomes important for understanding societal risks.

entry.title: Suppressing Pressure, Amplifying Evidence: Self-Guided Attention Steering to Mitigate Sycophancy and Stubbornness

author.name: Yinghao He, Mengyu Xu, Haixiang Sun, Donghan Li, Yibo Wang, Lixu Wang, Kezhen Chen, Chi Li, Chunwei Liu, Bharat Bhargava, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: The paper introduces CoPE-Bench, which evaluates sycophancy and contextual stubbornness jointly with six conditions per question to capture the trade-off between yielding to unsupported user pressure and failing to update on valid evidence. The authors propose a self-guided attention steering intervention that suppresses pressure-following while amplifying use of contextual evidence. Addressing both failure modes together avoids the pitfall of fixing one while worsening the other.

entry.title: Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents

author.name: TianYi Lyu, Xiaozhe Li, Yang Li, Yongkang Chen, Kefei Tian, Junbo Niu, Zican Hu, Hongbo Liu, Mingliang Xiong, Qingwen Liu

entry.summary: SERA trains recursive LLM agents that decompose tasks, delegate subtasks to child instances of the same policy, and evaluate outcomes with the same weights, turning evaluation into a learned capability rather than an external judge. Before delegating, the parent assesses subtask quality, addressing the lack of ground truth for self-invented intermediate subtasks.

entry.title: When Agent Context Goes Stale: Incoherence in Volatile Agent Context

author.name: Yingying Liu, Junzhou Fang, Chenxiong Qian

entry.summary: The paper addresses stale tool observations in agent contexts: when underlying data sources change, agents keep using outdated observations and make incorrect claims about current state. Concord is a context coherence framework that links each observation to its mutable source and maintains consistency between agent context and the external world.

entry.title: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving

author.name: Jiaqi Zhao, Haodong Chen, Jitai Hao, Wei Zhao, Jinghao Pang, Qiang Huang, Jun Yu

entry.summary: HEAR is a bidirectional protocol standardizing communication between agent harnesses (which know workflow dependencies and context lifecycles) and inference engines (which observe queues, KV-cache state, and resources), enabling workflow-aware LLM serving. It addresses the current lack of interfaces connecting these complementary views for efficient multi-turn, tool-using, parallel-agent workloads.

entry.title: Extracting Persona Subspaces Through Iterative Nullspace Projection For Modulation

author.name: Ananya Malik, Mai ElSherief

entry.summary: Introduces PaSS, an inference-time persona-control paradigm that models personas as subspaces rather than single dominant directions, extracted via iterative nullspace projection. It defines a modulation setting where traits already present in content must be amplified or suppressed, enabling finer-grained control of nested persona traits.

entry.title: Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild

author.name: Yifan Xiong, Jingyi Ge, Zhenpeng Chen, Yiling Lou

entry.summary: This is the first systematic empirical study of test adequacy for agent harnesses, the infrastructure surrounding backbone LLMs in agentic systems. It finds harnesses substantially undertested, with LLM-dependent code that governs agent behavior receiving especially limited testing attention, and proposes enhancements to test adequacy.

entry.title: When Verifiable Counts Depend on Wording: Auditing Wording Robustness in Instruction Following

author.name: Qishi Zhan, Seoyeon Jang, Zihan Dong, Minxuan Hu, Ziheng Chen, Tonghui Qu

entry.summary: The paper introduces WISE, a matched evaluation suite testing whether verifiable instruction-following scores remain stable when constraint wording varies while the operational requirement stays fixed. Across 100 tasks, thirteen models from seven providers, and repeated generations, wording alone produces substantial compliance shifts, including systematic effects for avoidance and exclusion phrasings.

entry.title: APOD: reasoning-guided agentic population ordinary differential equation discovery for pharmacological digital twins

author.name: Romain Ferrara, Martin Soucail, Victor Gertner, Adil Moussali, Joris Cocquebert, Sandrine Oziel-Taieb, Julien Nicolas, Florence Gattacceca, Mihaela van der Schaar, S\'ebastien Benzekry

entry.summary: APOD is a language-model agent that iteratively reasons over biological knowledge and fit diagnostics to discover population ODE systems with between-subject variability for pharmacological digital twins. It performs open-ended model search on sparse noisy data and recovers ground-truth structures on synthetic pharmacokinetic and tumor-dynamics benchmarks. This could substantially accelerate expert-driven pharmacometric modeling.

entry.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with GRPO against a proxy reward built from citation count, legalese density, and length causes the model to stop committing to answers: formatted-answer rates collapse from 0.900 to 0.109 and overall accuracy drops below chance, yet accuracy on committed answers actually rises. This vividly illustrates reward hacking as strategic abstention rather than capability loss.

entry.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Yutong Dai, Viraj Prabhu, Zhiyuan Hu, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen

entry.summary: CLIFT trains open-source web agents with reinforcement learning using conformal self-verification: the agent answers natural-language verification questions about its own rollouts, a Compositional Conformal Certifier keeps signals whose URL-conditional evidence agrees with a training-time judge, and signed trust weights replace sparse binary success signals. The same verification mechanism supports test-time scaling without assuming a frontier judge at deployment. This addresses the weak-supervision bottleneck in agent RL.

entry.title: What Will Post-Training Fix? Per-Problem Gains Are Shared Across Independent RL Runs, and Existing Checkpoints Predict Them Better Than A Priori Signals

author.name: Xiaoxian Duan

entry.summary: Across eighteen post-training runs on two 1.5B math models, the author finds that which problems RL improves is largely shared within a base model (noise ceiling ~0.9) but differs across base models (rho=0.25), and that existing checkpoints predict per-problem gains better than a priori data signals. This challenges assumptions underlying data selection and curriculum design before training.

entry.title: How to scale your HEP ML models: A recipe for robust architecture comparisons at scale

author.name: Matthias Vigl, Nikita Pond, Jackson Barr, Alexander Froch, Dan Guest, Nicole Hartman, Michael Kagan, Lukas Heinrich

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic procedure for deriving robust scaling laws and comparing design choices on compute- and data-constrained budgets for high-energy physics ML tasks, validated on toy problems and applied to multi-task transformers on the ~11-billion-jet ATLAS JetSet2 dataset. It reports the first jointly optimal prediction of model size, training horizon, and learning rate for a data-constrained HEP task.

entry.title: Spend Bytes on Breadth: Precision-Count Trade-offs for Decode-Time KV Compression in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Runguo Li

entry.summary: BreadthKV addresses decode-time KV cache compression for long chain-of-thought reasoning by asking how a fixed byte budget should be split between token count and precision, favoring more tokens at lower precision via combined quantization and eviction. Bit-width is selected per model and budget with a 60-problem end-to-end calibration since offline attention error is unreliable. Across three reasoning models and four benchmarks, it beats eviction alone in 17 of 18 settings and produces shorter outputs.

entry.title: Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression

author.name: Doo Hwan Hwang, Junyoung Jang, Junho Na, Hosung Lim, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes scoring KV cache evictions by directly estimating the KL divergence between the compressed-cache and full-cache next-token distributions, retaining entries whose removal would most change model behavior, rather than relying on proxy signals like attention mass. The training-free framework uses pre-eviction forward statistics for efficiency. This reframes cache compression as behavior preservation with a principled objective.

entry.title: Answer with Evidence: Consistency-Aware Grounded Visual Question Answering for Roadside Traffic Scenes

author.name: Runwei Guan, Rongsheng Hu, Shangshu Chen, Ningwei Ouyang, Shaofeng Liang, Heyi Lin, Jinjing Zhu, Yang Shi, Dongming Wu, Daizong Liu, Henghui Ding, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: The paper identifies say-point mismatch in grounded MLLMs — answers contradicting the bounding boxes the model localizes — and traces it to the answer-then-ground factorization that commits to claims before enumeration. The authors build RoadSceneVQA-G, a 34.7K-pair benchmark linking every free-form answer to witnessing boxes, plus an Answer-Grounding Consistency (AGC) evaluation suite, in the roadside traffic domain. This matters for trustworthy multimodal systems in safety-critical traffic settings.

entry.title: VepAgent: Bridging Causal-Transition via Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Video Event Prediction

author.name: Qiutong Chen, Yuchan Guo, Zhenlong Yuan, Haobo Yang, Fangfang Lin, Xinyi Long, Yin Wang, Zijian Song, Rui Lan, Shi Qiu, Boyuan Pan, Yang Luo, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: VepAgent is an agentic framework combining causal-transition reasoning with tool-augmented reinforcement learning for video event prediction, explicitly modeling logical progression from terminal observed states to future events. It also contributes futurebench-4K, a chain-of-thought dataset for the task.

entry.title: Agentic Cognitive Depth: Operational Criteria for Evaluating LLM Agents

author.name: Nijesh Upreti, Chris Sypherd, Vaishak Belle

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework called agentic cognitive depth, a trajectory-level profile defined by five operational criteria: context sensitivity, temporal continuity, multimodal coordination, adaptive interaction, and metacognitive monitoring. It aims to move evaluation of agentic LLM systems beyond end-to-end task success toward richer, more diagnostic measures. This matters because agent evaluation is currently dominated by coarse success metrics that hide how well underlying capabilities are actually used.

entry.title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution

author.name: Kaipeng Xu, Xianli Yan, Yan Wang, Xiang Liu, Shan Liu

entry.summary: EvoCast is a fully autonomous research-agent system for evolving deep time-series forecasting architectures, starting with mechanism-diagnostic ablations on a task baseline and then generating evidence-grounded research directions from dataset characteristics, diagnostics, and prior rounds. It aims to overcome AutoML's fixed search spaces and general LLM agents' unreliable experimental protocols and promotion criteria.

entry.title: LatentIndex: Cross-Layer Sharing with Layer-Specific Selection for Sparse Attention

author.name: Zhaohui Wang, Zhixin Pan, Fanxu Meng, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: LatentIndex extends the latent-sharing idea of Multi-head Latent Attention to sparse-attention indexers: layer groups share a latent cache built from the first layer's hidden states while retaining layer-specific token selection, with key decoders absorbed into queries to avoid reconstructing per-layer keys. It includes training-free calibration and a training-aware variant, reducing indexer overhead and key-cache storage.

entry.title: Do More Modalities Always Help? A Geometric Perspective on Missing-Modality Robustness

author.name: Songyuan Sui, Zhen Tan, Mohan Zhang, Rana Muhammad Shahroz Khan, Xia Hu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: The paper systematically characterizes a counterintuitive failure mode: multi-modal models trained on full modalities can underperform unimodal models when a modality is missing at inference, across fusion models, CLIP-style two-tower models, and vision-language models. It links degradation to learned cross-modal dependencies in principal parameter subspaces and derives implications for robustness.

entry.title: DICE: Decoupling Capability from Intervention Necessity in LLM Tutoring

author.name: Sayantan Pal, Kaiyi Ji, Rohini K. Srihari

entry.summary: This paper introduces DICE, a framework that separates whether an LLM tutor should intervene at all from what it should say, using an explicit pedagogical action-selection step. It defines Intervention Value, a counterfactual rollout-based metric comparing each potential intervention against non-intervention, and finds many prescribed interventions offer little marginal benefit.

entry.title: VideoResearchAgent: Grounded Task Synthesis and Sim-to-Real RL for Open-Web Video Research

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Fei Li, Yuxi Wu, Bin Zhu, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies open-web video research, where an agent must autonomously discover relevant videos, navigate temporal content, and ground answers in visual evidence, extending deep research agents beyond text and images. It introduces a controllable task-synthesis pipeline from temporal content and a sim-to-real reinforcement learning setup to avoid retrieval shortcuts from fixed local simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Instruction Following: Learning Grounded Skill-Following with Skill Contracts

author.name: Jianghan Shen, Zhenjie Liu, Yue Li, Jie Huang, Siqi Luo, Yiming Cheng, Yizhi Yao, Kaijie Zhang, Cheng Tang, Minghui Zhang, Ming Hu, Yirong Chen, Ziyan Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Grounded Skill-Following, a task formulation where agents must execute expert-authored skills across multiple procedural phases rather than just producing a final answer. Skills are formalized as skill contracts combining visible instructions with an explicit contract runtime that specifies required phases, admissible actions, and transitions, enabling verifiable procedural execution grounded in environment observations.

entry.title: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry

author.name: Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Yan Chen, Pol Llado, Scott Counts, Mohit Bansal, Benjamin Van Durme, Harsh Jhamtani, Gaurav Verma

entry.summary: TeleTune learns a reusable textual skill library for computer-use agents from offline user telemetry, addressing goal underspecification, non-replayability, and interleaved trajectories in real logs. It uses action-prediction errors on logged data as the learning signal to evolve skills without recorded goals or replay environments.

entry.title: CodeForge-MA: Execution-Verified Multi-Agent Learning with Language-Conditioned LoRA for Multilingual Code Generation

author.name: Zhizhou Gu, Xianting Wu, Siyu Gu, Tian Zhang, Kejian Tong

entry.summary: CodeForge-MA combines a multi-agent data forge (Composer, Reviewer, Executor, Curator), execution-verified reinforced instruction tuning, and language-conditioned LoRA adapters to improve multilingual code generation under frozen backbones. The pipeline also filters duplicates and benchmark leakage, strengthening contamination control.

entry.title: Measurement-First Auditing of Agentic Leaderboards: Contamination Susceptibility, Matched-Control Re-evaluation, and Scorer Validation

author.name: Dishu Yang, Qi Su, Hongbo Qin, Hansong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a measurement-first audit framework for agentic leaderboards that separates contamination claims into training-time exposure, evaluation-time retrieval, and pipeline leakage channels, each coded fail-closed. Applying it to nine Holistic Agent Leaderboard configurations, none of 27 channel assessments was fully closed and contamination incidents were confirmed in four.

entry.title: Normality Constraint Learning: Adapting Foundation Models for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiaohui Zhou, Yijie Wang, Hongzuo Xu, Weixuan Liang, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: NCL is a lightweight plug-and-play framework that adapts pre-trained Time Series Foundation Models for anomaly detection by constraining them to model normality, since TSFMs can reconstruct or forecast rare anomalies well and thereby defeat error-based anomaly scores. It requires no modification of the underlying model.

entry.title: Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification

author.name: Je Yang, Ivan Lobov, Thomas Karpati

entry.summary: BTTF is an end-to-end agentic framework targeting the neglected post-simulation phase of chip design verification, distilling massive simulation dumps into a normalized SQLite database and coupling it with a collaborative multi-agent system for interactive waveform debugging. It addresses the finding that roughly 75% of LLM-for-EDA research targets static RTL code generation rather than verification workflows.

entry.title: CurveCodec 2: Skeleton-agnostic animation compression with a learned entropy model

author.name: Mingyi Shi, Huancheng Lin, Xuelin Chen, Taku Komura

entry.summary: This paper extends CurveCodec, a learned codec for skeletal animation data, to work across arbitrary skeletons with stated error bounds while closing the worst-case gap with the production ACL library used in game engines. It analyzes where redundancy in skeletal motion actually lies and identifies which codec components benefit most from learned entropy models measured in bits rather than floats.

entry.title: AgroGround: Multi-Granularity Grounded Recognition in Agriculture

author.name: Abdulla Alshehhi, Zongyan Han, Rao Anwer

entry.summary: Introduces AgroGround, a large-scale dataset linking agricultural VQA labels to image regions for grounded recognition of plant diseases and agricultural targets. An automated pipeline converts labels from eight VQA datasets into nearly 800,000 instruction examples for disease lesions and whole objects, including healthy images as negatives.

entry.title: Only Project Once: Projection-Adaptive Loss for Exact Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Tim Aebersold, Soheyl Massoudi, Mark Fuge

entry.summary: Shows that a single detached projection step suffices during training instead of unrolling multiple repair steps, via a Projection-Adaptive Loss that weighs constraint penalties based on the post-projection residual. This reduces compute and memory while achieving exact constraint satisfaction at deployment.

entry.title: EDISCO: Equivariant DIScrete Diffusion for Euclidean Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Ruogu Chen, Jie Han

entry.summary: EDISCO is claimed to be the first discrete diffusion model for Euclidean combinatorial optimization (TSP, CVRP) with exact E(2)-invariant generative distributions over node-index solutions, using an equivariant edge-score network and a categorical continuous-time Markov chain with exact posterior sampling. Prior learning-based methods only approximated equivariance via augmentation or regularization. This offers a principled way to bake geometric symmetry into discrete generative solvers.

entry.title: SparseCraft: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Optimization for Sparse Computing

author.name: Rajatabha Chakraborty, M P Samartha, Vedant Pahariya, Priyesh Shukla

entry.summary: SparseCraft places a language model inside a closed loop that iteratively edits Chisel RTL, memory configuration, and sparse-kernel schedules of a Gemmini accelerator via MCP tool servers, over 15 measured iterations. Every candidate must pass legality checks, elaboration, cycle-accurate simulation, bit-for-bit golden-reference verification, and synthesis before it counts. This replaces analytical-model-driven design-space search with measured hardware-in-the-loop agentic optimization.

entry.title: ReMAP: Restoring the Perceptual Cycle with Reasoning-Time Latent Visual Memory

author.name: Hao Jiang, Zhanyu Guo, Chenwei Wu, Yichen Guo, Qizhe Zhang, Junchi Yao, Jixian Wu, Jinhao You, Kai Tang, Jiajun Cao, Tinghao Wang, Mengyu Wang, Leo Anthony Celi, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: ReMAP addresses visual grounding degradation in multimodal LLMs during long reasoning by reintroducing visual evidence through reasoning-time memory. A controlled analysis along curation, organization, and access axes yields design insights, leading to a dual-memory design: a static question-conditioned Global memory for scene context and a dynamic Local memory updated during reasoning. The findings on when memory access helps are as valuable as the method itself.

entry.title: CoDance: Learning Reactive and Compliant Human-Humanoid Interaction from Video

author.name: Zhuoqun Chen, Shucheng Jia, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: CoDance learns partnered human-humanoid dancing from a single video of two human dancers, retargeting motion into robot and partner references and adding a multi-link compliance augmentation that converts kinematic demonstrations into force-aware training data. The humanoid coordinates footsteps with a moving partner while maintaining continuous two-hand contact, coupling locomotion with physical contact and compliance.

entry.title: GNN-CB: A Graph Neural Network Competition Benchmark for Human and LLM Evaluation

author.name: Murad Hossen, Tasneem Selim, Gurur Gamgam, Tuga Yousif, Abderrahmane Kasmi, Ikram Aissiou, Mubaraq Onipede, Faran Taimoor Butt, Sanae Zrigui, Rosa Y. G. Paccotacya-Yanque, Ignatius Balayo, Ikram Elhouiti, Hadil Affes, Bijay Adhikari, Sargam Goyal, Muhammad Ibrahim Isah, Mohammad Idrees Bhat, Samuel Kangoni Matia, Peguy Kem-Meka Tiotsop Kadzue, Maha Trabelsi, Emmanuel Owusu, Vinit, Nour Majdoub, Tamiru Alemnew, Islem Rekik

entry.summary: GNN-CB is the first competition-style benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can autonomously solve end-to-end GNN coding tasks, with 18 curated competitions spanning node-, edge-, and graph-level prediction across difficulty tiers. A unified automated pipeline enables comparison between human competitors and LLMs on realistic graph ML problems.

entry.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents

author.name: Dolly Sah, Tanmay Sah, Harshul Jain, Tanya Sah

entry.summary: Presents UndoBench, a benchmark of 36 workflows and fault scenarios across 8 enterprise domains that decouples an agent's nominal task completion from its ability to recover from faults, using counterfactual paired trials and environment-state oracles. Across 12 held-out workflows, agents with 83.54% nominal competence show substantially degraded conditional performance under failures. This fills an important evaluation gap for reliably deploying tool-using agents in enterprise settings.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: Performance and Costs of Agentic Retrieval for Complex Tasks

author.name: Reza Esfandiarpoor, Radek Osmulski, Yauhen Babakhin, Gabriel de Souza P. Moreira, Oliver Holworthy, Jie He, Ronay Ak, Jiarui Cai, Ryan Chesler, Bo Liu, Even Oldridge

entry.summary: Empirically studies agentic retrieval, embedding LLM reasoning in a ReAct loop with retrievers, showing +8.7 nDCG@10 over standard dense retrieval with the same embedding model and high robustness on out-of-domain tasks where specialized retrievers struggle. Crucially, it also quantifies cost, addressing when the extra LLM calls are worth it. Useful practical guidance for building retrieval in agentic workflows.

entry.title: Attention Tax, Handoff Tax: A Stylised Model of When Multi-Agent LLM Systems Help

author.name: Akshit Anchan, Nayonika Sen

entry.summary: This theoretical work reconciles conflicting findings on multi-agent LLM systems by introducing a stylized reliability model with two trade-offs: decomposition reduces long-context burden but incurs a handoff tax, while redundant sampling helps only insofar as failures are uncorrelated. The model yields crossover conditions predicting when delegation beats a single agent. It offers a conceptual framework for designing and interpreting multi-agent system evaluations.

entry.title: When Are Concept Bottleneck Model Explanations Faithful and Compact?

author.name: Stefano Teso, Emanuele Marconato, Steve Azzolin, Antonio Vergari

entry.summary: Building on formal explainability, the paper shows that for widespread concept bottleneck model architectures, including VLM-based variants, faithful explanations must include all bottleneck concepts, compromising interpretability when the bottleneck is large. The authors propose remedies such as modeling concepts differently to allow compact faithful explanations. This is an important theoretical caution for the explainable AI community.

entry.title: Wiring Matters: Injection Topology and Initialization of Affordance Heads in Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Zijian An, Linhan Wang, Jiayan Wang, Shijie Geng, Ran Yang, Yiming Feng, Lifeng Zhou

entry.summary: A controlled study on how to attach dense affordance-supervision heads to vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies without harming instruction following, using the LIBERO benchmark. The authors find stop-gradients protecting the backbone are essential and ablate injection topology and bridge initialization under matched budgets.

entry.title: BrainTRACE: Tracing Longitudinal, Multimodal, and Volumetric Evidence in Brain MRI Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Qizhen Lan, Mengchen Fan, Hang Zhang, Jingwei Duan, Moule Lin, Jialin Chen, Baocheng Geng, Xiaoqian Jiang

entry.summary: BrainTRACE is a report-grounded benchmark of 7,273 scoring items that evaluates whether vision-language models can reconstruct the evidence chain for longitudinal brain MRI interpretation, integrating serial studies, multiple sequences, and volumetric localization. Unlike prior medical VQA benchmarks, it tests the full clinical reasoning workflow rather than isolated images. It matters because it exposes failures in evidence grounding that current medical VLM evaluations miss.

entry.title: TAPDreamer: Transferable Adversarial Patches for World Action Models

author.name: Xuanyu Lu, Fengqing Jiang, Kaiyuan Zheng, Yichen Feng, Yaorui Ding, Yuetai Li, Zhen Xiang, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Basel Alomair, Luyao Niu, Radha Poovendran

entry.summary: TAPDreamer is a black-box adversarial patch attack against world action models that constructs a fixed local perturbation using only a public encoder, transferring across tasks and action architectures without querying the target policy. It exploits interactions between patch-induced changes and the model's dynamics to corrupt visual representations used for robotic control. This exposes a security vulnerability in world models, an increasingly important foundation for robot control.

entry.title: Memory-State Critic for Asymmetric Actor-Critic with Application to Vision-Based Pursuit-Evasion

author.name: Arthur Louette, Alejandro S\'anchez Roncero, Gaspard Lambrechts, Pascal Leroy, Julien Hansen, Petter \"Ogren, Damien Ernst

entry.summary: Proposes conditioning the asymmetric actor-critic critic on the policy's internal memory state rather than the full observation history or raw state alone, which the authors show resolves the ill-definedness of state-only critics and their biased policy gradients. The method is validated on vision-based pursuit-evasion problems in partially observable settings.

entry.title: PaLoRA: Paced Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Li, Fanhu Zeng, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Shows that in LoRA-based continual learning, finite-precision updates leak into protected subspaces even under nullspace projection, so fixed small learning rates cannot prevent growing forgetting as the effective rank of prior knowledge expands. PaLoRA derives a principled schedule for how the learning-rate restriction should evolve across tasks. A theoretically grounded improvement to continual learning practice.

entry.title: One-Step Generation via Riemannian Wasserstein Gradient Flows

author.name: David Li, Chanhyuk Lee, Jaehoon Yoo, Nikita Gushchin, Floor Eijkelboom, Eric Moulines, Maxim Panov, Alexander Korotin, Seunghoon Hong, Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: This paper extends drifting models and Wasserstein gradient flows, which amortize iterative distributional refinement into a one-step generator, from Euclidean domains to constrained Riemannian spaces where additive particle updates can leave the valid domain. It derives and compares several geometry-aware update fields within a common training framework for one-step generation. This enables fast generative sampling on manifolds and constrained data spaces.

entry.title: Which Preferences to Train On? End-to-End Multi-Objective Alignment with an Adversarial Preference Distribution

author.name: Minjae Lee, Kyunghyun Cho, Sangdon Park

entry.summary: The paper addresses multi-objective alignment of LLMs by asking which points in the preference simplex a single conditioned model should be trained on, noting that existing methods leave hard regions under-trained. It proposes training with an adversarial preference distribution to cover the Pareto front end-to-end.

entry.title: Trinity: One Differentiable Physics for Training, Refining and Scoring Generative Floorplanners

author.name: Shih-Ying Yeh, Tzu-Sian Wang, Xuehai Wang, Jia-Hua Lee, Daniel Z. Kaplan, Ming-Qi Xu, Wuqian Tang, Chun-Yao Wang, Shang-Hong Lai, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: Trinity is a flow-matching floorplanner for chip design that uses six differentiable functions encoding floorplanning constraints and objectives simultaneously as training loss terms, refiner energies, and scoring metrics. The work also re-implements four prior diffusion-based placers under a unified recipe on FloorSet, scoring raw, refined, and legalized layouts on a common scale to reveal what the generators actually contribute beyond post-hoc fix-ups.

entry.title: Hidden in the Comments: A Context-Injection Attack Surface in Code LLMs

author.name: Noor Munir, Francesco Quinzan, Stephen Roberts

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate that insecure instructions embedded as code comments can steer open-weight Code LLMs (3B-13B, base and instruction-tuned) toward generating vulnerable code, without access to weights or training data. They evaluate ten models across ten web-application weakness classes and measure elevated vulnerability rates under attack conditions.

entry.title: Universality and Convergence of Generative Flows

author.name: Leo Brunswic

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes generative flows trained to be balanced, showing that difference-based losses bound sampler error in total variation with policy-independent constants, while ratio-based flow-matching losses admit no such bound even on a single cycle. It further characterizes how backward policy choice determines loss achievability and gradient-descent convergence on graphs.

entry.title: Beyond In-Distribution Preservation: Recovering Generalization in Quantized VLAs via Vulnerability-Oriented Tuning

author.name: Shen Ruan, Wenchang Gao, Jin Wang, Siao Liu, Zhoxizhuoma, Dongchun Ren, Xin Zheng

entry.summary: Systematically studies robustness and generalization of post-training quantized vision-language-action robot policies, showing quantized policies can become fragile to subtle environmental variations despite comparable in-distribution performance. It identifies a small subset of high-discrepancy rollout states and proposes vulnerability-oriented tuning that selectively uses teacher guidance where it helps.

entry.title: RepICL: Reusable In-Context Prediction Across Heterogeneous Representation Spaces

author.name: Yu-Hsiang Liu, Kuan-Yu Chen, Chih-Sheng Chen, Meng-Hsuan Chang, Yu-Chen Den, Tien-Hao Chang

entry.summary: This paper asks whether the few-shot prediction procedure on frozen representations can itself be learned once and reused across datasets, encoders, and modalities. The authors introduce RepShiftBench, a benchmark of 1,218 encoder-dataset tasks spanning text, image, and audio, and show that logistic regression fitted per-task still beats all evaluated in-context learners. They then present RepICL, a meta-trained in-context learner designed to close this gap, including generalization to unseen datasets, encoders, and modalities.

entry.title: Flash-OPD: Fast On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Wei Chen, Junle Chen, Yitong Yang, Zhaoyang Xu, Jiaxin Lin, Yuxuan Liang, Xiaofang Zhou, Kai Wang, Rui Chen

entry.summary: Flash-OPD accelerates on-policy distillation, where dense teacher supervision is applied to student-generated rollouts but rollout generation is expensive. The key insight is that trajectory-specific reliability boundaries can be detected as first-passage events during generation rather than predicted beforehand, adapting supervision length per trajectory. This reduces wasted computation while preserving useful teacher signal, relevant to efficient training of reasoning-style models.

entry.title: Stability-Shaped Deep Graph Learning

author.name: Junyou Zhu, Langzhou He, Fenying Cai, Christian Nauck, Ping Xiong, Chao Gao, Philip S. Yu, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, J\"urgen Kurths, Frank Hellmann

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified mode-wise stability framework for deep graph neural network propagation, interpreting layer depth as time and over-smoothing as an undesirable dynamical synchronization of node features, analyzed via the master stability curve. Building on this theory, the authors propose SDGL, with two complementary instantiations, to mitigate over-smoothing in deep GNNs. This connects dynamical systems theory with deep graph learning in a principled way.

entry.title: Block Disentanglement in CRL: Bridging Identifiability and Visual State Estimation

author.name: Emre Acart\"urk, Pranamya Kulkarni, Puranjay Datta, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Burak Var{\i}c{\i}, Ali Tajer

entry.summary: This causal representation learning paper establishes identifiability guarantees for block disentanglement of latent causal variables under substantially weaker interventional assumptions than prior work, with block structure determined by a partition. It connects these theoretical guarantees to practical visual state estimation.

entry.title: Scaling 3D Visual Grounding in Abdominal CT

author.name: Sam Church, Danyal Maqbool, Joshua D. Warner, Andrew Voter, Junjie Hu, Meghan G. Lubner, Tyler J. Bradshaw

entry.summary: The paper introduces an automated pipeline that converts routine radiologist 2D annotations placed on key images into large-scale phrase-region supervision for training 3D visual grounding models on abdominal CT. This sidesteps expensive manual 3D annotation and links report findings to tiny regions within CT volumes for radiology workflow support. Scaling supervision through clinical documentation byproducts is a significant practical contribution.

entry.title: Humanoid Rickshaw Pulling: Whole-Body Locomotion under Coupled Wheeled Loads

author.name: Yangzhi Yang, Xiansheng Lin, Zhaoming Xie, Xiaobin Xiong

entry.summary: Presents a whole-body control framework enabling humanoid robots to pull passive wheeled vehicles carrying payloads heavier than themselves, addressing coupled locomotion with unknown load dynamics. It uses a privileged teacher policy distilled into a history-conditioned student that infers load properties from observation history. This expands humanoid robot capabilities beyond carrying loads toward transport tasks.

entry.title: Mind the Gaps: From Failure Attribution to Closed-Form Repair of Code Language Models

author.name: Jian Gu, Hongyu Zhang, Chunyang Chen, Aldeida Aleti

entry.summary: The paper examines model repair for code language models whose outputs become stale as APIs evolve, focusing on two unexamined assumptions in neuron attribution and patching pipelines. The authors identify a targeting gap (attributed neurons differ from patchable neurons) and an update gap (generic updates do not fit all failures), then propose closed-form repairs validated on Python and Rust API evolution tasks across three code models. This is significant for maintaining deployed code models without full retraining.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Distribution Theory and Efficient Large-Scale Inference for Online Quantile Regression

author.name: Ziyang Wei, Jiaqi Li, Lan Wang, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The paper proves a quenched central limit theorem and finite-sample Gaussian approximation for stochastic subgradient descent on quantile regression under only finite-moment assumptions. It also shows that Ruppert-Polyak averaging with constant learning rates incurs non-vanishing bias and fails standard CLT centering. This provides rigorous foundations for streaming large-scale quantile inference.

entry.title: Latent Similarity Gaussian Processes: A Theory-Grounded Approach to Personalized Suicide-Risk Forecasting for Clinical Decision-Support

author.name: Yaniv Yacoby, Weiwei Pan, Hope Neveux, Taylor C. McGuire, Franchesca Castro-Ramirez, Anushka R. Patel, Matthew K. Nock

entry.summary: LSGPs embed patients in a continuous latent space to jointly model similarity and forecast suicide-risk trajectories, selectively drawing information from latent peers to unify nomothetic, idiographic, and hierarchical frameworks. The authors contribute an identifiable two-channel similarity kernel and prove that standard mean-field variational inference collapses the model to a pooled one, along with a fix. Evaluation uses intensive longitudinal clinical data with Matthew Nock, a leading suicide researcher, among the authors.

entry.title: A Solvable Model of Adaptive Learning Rate Rescaling: Acceleration, Stability & Scaling

author.name: Itay Lavie, Clarissa Lauditi, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: The authors analyze normalized SGD in a random-feature model with power-law teacher and data covariance, deriving a dynamical mean-field theory for loss dependence on time, width, and batch size. They show normalization induces an effective learning rate that accelerates SGD, mapping power-law exponents to faster decay with provable exponential or finite-time convergence in favorable regimes.

entry.title: General Decision Models: Benchmarking and Insights Beyond Jev

author.name: Feiyu Duan, Jiayu Lin, Jia Wang, Jun Xiang, Jialiang Wu, Xinnong Zhang, Hanqi Yan, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: The paper introduces JEVal, a bilingual benchmark of 11,257 instances from 36 datasets across 10 domains, evaluating 25 configurations of general decision models (such as Jev) against generative LLMs on structured judgment and selection tasks. It finds decision models competitive when evidence suffices but weak when specialist knowledge or faithful uncertainty estimation is required, and characterizes behavior when decisions compose into larger systems.

entry.title: LongSocialBench: Do Long-Context LLMs Understand Online Discussion Threads?

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Rinat Khaziev, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Tarek F. Abdelzaher

entry.summary: LongSocialBench is a benchmark of 1,462 verified multiple-choice items from 94 complete Hacker News, Stack Exchange, and Reddit threads, with median length around 73K tokens, testing structure-aware social reasoning such as parent-reply tracking, turning points, and cross-branch contrasts. It probes whether long-context LLMs truly understand online discourse rather than merely ingesting long documents. A valuable evaluation resource for long-context capabilities.

entry.title: No Hindsight for LLM Fact-Checkers: Measuring Leakage Channels in Misinformation Detection

author.name: Kuan-Hua Wu Lu, Yohanes Andre Setiawan

entry.summary: The authors measure two hindsight channels in LLM fact-checking evaluation on AVeriTeC and QuanTemp++: parametric leakage of post-claim outcomes memorized in pretraining, and retrieved evidence published after the claim. They find substantial parametric leakage hidden by aggregate accuracy, and show a simple representation bottleneck reduces future leakage efficiently. An important evaluation-integrity contribution for fact-checking benchmarks.

entry.title: When LLMs Sit Above Diagnostic Tools: Unrealized Complementarity in Industrial Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Donghwan Kim

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests whether an LLM acting as an integration layer above specialized diagnostic tools actually outperforms the best standalone tool across five industrial fault diagnosis datasets (bearing vibration, process monitoring, semiconductor equipment). It finds that conflicting external information can overturn initially correct LLM judgments and that implicit LLM integration never consistently beats the stronger standalone source, confirmed on a pre-registered Tennessee Eastman test. The result is a caution against assuming LLM orchestration automatically adds value over specialized components.

entry.title: From Traces to Agentic Worlds: Agentic Language World Models for Interactive Environment Simulation

author.name: Quanyu Long, Xiao Chen, Jianda Chen, Haozhen Zhang, Qisheng Hu, Jianzhu Bao, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: Trace2Env is a learning-free framework that reconstructs historical interaction traces into a reusable environment worldbook, allowing a world-model agent to simulate a stateful environment for training and evaluating LLM agents when the original system is inaccessible. This agentic language world modeling paradigm supports faithful simulation without rebuilding executable environments. It addresses a real bottleneck in agent development and evaluation.

entry.title: The Same Zero: Why Identical ASR Can Imply Different Guarantees in LLM-Agent Security

author.name: YaJie Yin

entry.summary: The paper applies a Verification Autonomy Levels (VAL) taxonomy - from LLM self-declaration to impossible completeness - to 22 agent-security defenses, providing a falsifiable framework for what a defense actually guarantees. It also runs a controlled budget-matched comparison showing a VAL-guided stack outperforms a mainstream intuition stack across 50 scenarios and 12 attack variants.

entry.title: ASD-FEAT: A Multi-Modal Infant Video-Derived Dataset for Early ASD Risk Prediction

author.name: Sidrah Liaqat (University of Kentucky), Halil Helvaci (University of Kentucky), Sen-Ching Cheung (University of Kentucky), Chongruo Wu (University of California Davis), Dongjie Chen (University of California Davis), Chen Nee Chuah (University of California Davis), Sally Ozonoff (MIND Institute, University of California Davis)

entry.summary: ASD-FEAT is a multimodal dataset from infant-adult interaction videos with longitudinal coverage through 36 months, clinically validated developmental outcomes, expert frame-level behavioral annotations, and privacy-conscious feature representations. It uniquely combines these characteristics at scale for early autism spectrum disorder risk prediction.

entry.title: Trust the View That Sees the Target: Mining Cross-View Conflicts for Reliability-Gated Disaster Damage Assessment

author.name: Yifan Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies failure cases in multi-view building damage assessment where overhead imagery and ground-level photos disagree, mining conflict samples from wildfire and hurricane datasets where they comprise 10-33% of data. It shows an oracle that trusts the correct view dramatically outperforms symmetric fusion methods, motivating reliability-gated fusion rather than equal-weighting both views.

entry.title: Super-Resolution in The Right Latent Space: A Frozen Vision-Foundation Substrate

author.name: Wanzhou Lei, Cuifeng Sheng, Yanjin He, Maohua Li, Hua Yuan, Per-Olof Persson, Hanlin Tang

entry.summary: This paper argues that real-world super-resolution should be performed in the latent space of a frozen vision-foundation model rather than in reconstruction-oriented latent spaces or pixel space, since degraded images land far from the manifold of sharp natural images in those substrates. The authors propose mapping degraded embeddings back onto the image manifold while preserving semantics and pixel detail. The reframing could make SR simpler and cheaper if the foundation-model latent space proves to be a better substrate.

entry.title: Triggering Generalist Reasoning via Predictive Uncertainty for Dual-System VLA

author.name: Hyemin Yang, Wooseong Jeong, Giwon Lee, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: TUD is an adaptive inference framework for dual-system vision-language-action models that selectively skips slow generalist calls by measuring cross-step dispersion of action re-predictions under the cached generalist context as an uncertainty signal. This replaces fixed-frequency invocation, saving computation in easy phases while reacting faster to unexpected scene changes. The approach improves the efficiency of fast-slow robot control architectures.

entry.title: SemCam: Semantic Camera Motion Control for Video Generation

author.name: Janna Bruner, Omer Talmi, Ianir Ideses, Lior Fritz, Lior Wolf, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: This paper introduces semantic camera motion control, a new video-to-video task where a reference video plus a target motion label (e.g., maintain frontal view of a subject) defines the desired subject-relative camera behavior without an explicit trajectory. The proposed SemCam method learns to realize these dynamic camera-subject relationships while preserving video content. This matters because it enables more intuitive, intent-level control of virtual cameras in generated or edited video.

entry.title: A Spatiotemporal Semantic Importance-Guided Unified Compression and Editing Framework for AI-Generated Videos

author.name: Xihua Sheng, Dong Liu, Chang Wen Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a compression framework tailored to AI-generated videos that preserves semantically important spatiotemporal information while allowing regenerable textures to be discarded, unified with prompt-based editing that maintains content consistency. This reframes codec design for generative content, where reconstruction fidelity to a specific sample matters less than semantic preservation.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimization in Sequence-to-Architecture Latent Space for Zero-Shot NAS

author.name: Ondrej Tybl, Lukas Neumann

entry.summary: The paper brings Bayesian optimization to zero-shot neural architecture search for large-scale networks by learning a VAE latent space over a novel prefix encoding of architectures. This replaces near-random evolutionary mutation with a principled, model-based search while avoiding the prohibitive cost of traditional NAS.

entry.title: Lens3D: Target-Conditioned Visual Foveation for Fine-Grained 3D Understanding

author.name: Junming Huang, Zini Chen, Shuaiying Hou, Chi Wang, Qiang Dai, Weiwei Xu

entry.summary: Lens3D improves fine-grained 3D object understanding through a foveation pipeline (LensUnd) that selects informative views for an external 2D VLM via 3D localization, and a distillation path (LensDistill) that transfers the knowledge into 3D LLMs without runtime VLM calls. It also contributes a held-out benchmark, LensBench.

entry.title: ChronoWorld: Camera-Controlled Consistent 4D World Generation via Spatiotemporal Cues and Geometric Reflections

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhou, Dingwei Xian, Zhenyu Wang, Yajiao Xiong, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: ChronoWorld proposes an Observation-State-Reflection framework for camera-controllable 4D scene generation that maintains spatiotemporal coherence. It introduces Spatiotemporal Epipolar Causal Attention to enforce multi-view constraints and a reconstruction-driven geometric reflection pipeline for self-correction of generated content.

entry.title: TACET: Context-Appropriate Acoustic-Social Navigation for Quadrupeds

author.name: Sungsan Park, Young-Sik Shin, Sanghyun Kim

entry.summary: TACET enables quadruped robots to modulate both walking path and locomotion noise based on inferred social context, using a slow fine-tuned vision-language reasoner coupled to a fast reactive controller through a compact behavior token. This addresses an overlooked social dimension of legged robot deployment in hospitals, care homes, and offices where footstep noise matters.

entry.title: Test-Time Training as Residual Memory for Robot Policies

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Gengyu Zhang, Ramana Rao Kompella, Gaowen Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Reframes test-time training as a residual memory mechanism for long-horizon robot manipulation, explicitly distinguishing information recoverable from the current context from information that must persist beyond it. This selective persistence makes memory-augmented policies more scalable than full-history storage or indiscriminate TTT compression.

entry.title: When to Switch: Reliable Action-Chunk Extension for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Seonghoon Yu, Dongwon Kim, HyungRok Jung, Yoonjae Baek, Byung-kwan Lee, Suha Kwak, Jeany Son

entry.summary: Analyzing error patterns in vision-language-action models, the paper finds that errors in long action chunks concentrate at transitions between manipulation subskills and grow with chunk length. Motivated by this, it introduces a mechanism for predicting transition timing to enable reliable action-chunk extension, reducing stop-and-go execution and speeding task completion.

entry.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design

author.name: Seonghun Jung, Sieun Moon, Jiyoung Jeong, Jimin Lee, Jaehyuk Huh

entry.summary: This systems paper characterizes the runtime behavior of four representative vision-language-action models under batch-1, deadline-constrained control settings, profiling on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs with single-inference profiling plus 43,200 closed-loop runs. It shows VLA workloads mix vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components whose behavior departs from LLM serving design points, informing embodied AI hardware and system design. Inference overruns translate directly into stale observations and reduced task success.

entry.title: Decoding-time Realignment of Language Models

author.name: Tianlin Liu, Shangmin Guo, Leonardo Bianco, Daniele Calandriello, Quentin Berthet, Felipe Llinares, Jessica Hoffmann, Lucas Dixon, Michal Valko, Mathieu Blondel

entry.summary: This paper proposes adjusting the regularization level of aligned language models at decoding time, avoiding the need to retrain multiple models at different RLHF regularization strengths. This is critical because too little regularization causes reward hacking while too much hinders alignment. The method substantially reduces the cost of tuning the alignment-capability trade-off in LLMs.

entry.title: Understanding the performance gap between online and offline alignment algorithms

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Daniel Zhaohan Guo, Zeyu Zheng, Daniele Calandriello, Yuan Cao, Eugene Tarassov, R\'emi Munos, Bernardo \'Avila Pires, Michal Valko, Yong Cheng, Will Dabney

entry.summary: This empirical study investigates why online RLHF methods outperform offline alignment algorithms such as DPO, using reward over-optimization experiments and careful ablations. It shows that offline data coverage and quality alone cannot explain the gap, and finds offline algorithms optimize the policy differently than expected. This is an important diagnostic for alignment methodology choices.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Comparative Evidence for Social Intelligence

author.name: Keane Ong, Yuriel Ryan, Sabri Boughorbel, Vladimir Necula, Jack Wei Lun Shi, Rui Mao, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Adriel Kuek, Nancy F. Chen, Erik Cambria, Gianmarco Mengaldo, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: RLCE is a reinforcement learning method that trains social understanding models from unlabeled data by using comparative evidence among plausible interpretations of ambiguous social signals like affect, intent, and preference, bypassing the need for verification oracles. It addresses the dependence of social AI on costly human annotation.

entry.title: MOIRA: Mass-Oriented Indexing with Ragged Attention for Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Dich Nhat Minh Nguyen, Tran Dang Duong Nguyen

entry.summary: MOIRA improves long-context LLM decoding by using adaptive per-head, per-layer KV-cache page budgets with mass-oriented indexing and a ragged attention kernel, since fixed sparse-attention budgets waste memory bandwidth and existing kernels like FlashAttention-3 handle ragged page lists poorly. The system-level design avoids the padding and load-imbalance losses of prior sparse decoding. This targets the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of long-context inference.

entry.title: When Debate Helps: Proposal Supply and Verification-Aware Readout in Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Tunyu Zhang, Haizhou Shi, Yusong Zhao, Xinxi Zhang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues multi-agent debate fails to beat majority voting when two mechanisms are conflated: proposal supply (a correct answer must be surfaced) and readout (the correct answer must be identified). It formalizes recoverable headroom, introduces Latent Verification Debate where proposals receive answer-specific verification evidence, and uses controlled interventions to show correct evidence shifts answer selection.

entry.title: SpecFold: Folding Multi-Branch Redundancy for Faster Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chung-En Ho (Celine), Weiyu Sun (Celine), Cheng-Jhih Shih (Celine), He Li (Celine), Yong Liu (Celine), Yingyan (Celine), Lin

entry.summary: SpecFold accelerates diffusion language models by exploiting multi-branch computational redundancy within speculative verification steps, where draft branches inherit most tokens from parents so hidden states remain highly similar across branches. It is an algorithm-system co-design that folds this redundancy to reduce the cost of verifying multiple draft branches in one forward pass.

entry.title: Do Time-Series QA Systems Read the Time Series? Evidence Use and Reasoning Reliability

author.name: Zhuomin Chen, Jingchao Ni, Xu Zheng, Janki Bhimani, Mo Sha, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: This evaluation study probes whether time-series QA systems actually rely on the supplied numerical series, reproducing results for four systems (TimeOmni-1, ChatTS, TimeOmni-VL, Time-MQA) and testing sensitivity to input changes and grounding of numerical claims in rationales. The work exposes reliability gaps between answer accuracy and genuine evidence use.

entry.title: DPNL: A DPLL-based Algorithm for Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning

author.name: Thomas Jean-Michel Valentin (ENS Paris Saclay, TYREX), Pierre Genev{\`e}s (LIG, TYREX), Luisa Sophie Werner (LIG, TYREX), Sarah Chlyah (TYREX), Nabil Laya{\"i}da (TYREX), Nils Gesbert (Grenoble INP ENSIMAG, TYREX)

entry.summary: DPNL is an oracle-guided framework for probabilistic neurosymbolic learning that avoids materializing the complete logical provenance of a query, lazily exploring intermediate assignments while oracles certify whole regions that produce or exclude the target output. The authors establish conditions under which the approach is sound and improve on the provenance-materialization bottleneck of state-of-the-art PNL methods.

entry.title: Mind the Execution Gap: Action-Semantic Mismatch in World-Model Control

author.name: Shengtao Wen, Xiang Chen, Yu Tian, Lingbing Guo, Lina Gong, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: The paper studies how asynchronous execution (delay, packet loss, reordering, actuator buffering) changes the action semantics assumed by world-model controllers, identifying architecture-dependent failure modes: TD-MPC2 suffers from imagined-versus-executed timeline mismatch while DreamerV3 misattributes observed transitions to unapplied commands. It reframes asynchrony as a semantic problem, not merely a disturbance.

entry.title: Distribution Matching Evolutionary Algorithms for Rare Event Sampling

author.name: Yonatan Gideoni, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: The paper interprets evolutionary algorithms as approximate Markov Chain Monte Carlo and derives distribution-matching objectives for rare-event discovery, where a discovery is both surprising (low generation probability) and useful (high reward). This avoids expensive weight updates and works with closed-source models, addressing a limitation of gradient-based global optimization.

entry.title: XTurnix: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Turn Control through Two-State Binary Decisions

author.name: Zhanxun Liu, Yifan Duan, Hengtao Wu, Chen Yang, Qinyuan Cheng, Kun Wang, Xingyu Zeng, Xipeng Qiu, Chaochao Lu, Xie Chen

entry.summary: XTurnix is a compact text-based model for unified turn-taking control in real-time dialogue, formulating it as two binary decisions conditioned on the AI's listening or speaking state, predicted from complete dialogue history. It is pretrained on 5.5 million causal action examples derived automatically from time-stamped data, avoiding task-specific label spaces of prior turn detectors.

entry.title: ConEx: Human-Interpretable Saliency Maps via Concept-Aware Attribution

author.name: Yehonatan Elisha, Oren Barkan, Ziv Weiss Haddad, Noam Koenigstein

entry.summary: ConEx bridges saliency visualization and concept-based explanations by automatically discovering class-specific concepts as concept activation vectors learned without manual supervision, using a masking mechanism to improve concept purity. It generates saliency maps that show where each concept applies, aiming for both faithfulness and interpretability.

entry.title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning

author.name: Haozhe Chi, Song Jin, Yang Jin, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: QASLR is a post-training framework for long-video embedding that accumulates evidence across clips under a fixed visual-token budget, selecting frames, restoring temporal order, and processing clips sequentially with persistent think tokens and an embed token that reads out normalized representations. This captures sparse query-relevant events in videos spanning minutes or hours without blowing up memory.

entry.title: VAMPS: Visual and Motor Policies from Sampling-Based Planning

author.name: Mohamed Yassine Kabouri, Pietro Noah Crestaz, Quang-Nam Nguyen, Qilong Cheng, Ludovic Righetti, Nicolas Mansard

entry.summary: VAMPS uses MPPI sampling-based control to train reusable robot policies without human demonstrations, supporting iterative simulation training where the policy warm-starts MPPI and refined trajectories provide fresh supervision. It combines a learned terminal value for short-horizon planning with an Implicit Q-Learning critic guiding policy updates, and iterative refinement outperforms training on frozen MPPI data.

entry.title: Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation for RL-Improved Reasoning Teachers

author.name: Xiaoyu Chen, Bo Shao, Tiangang Zhu, Bintao Wu, Linjun Shou, Fengge Wu, Feng Sun, Wenbiao Ding

entry.summary: The paper studies which reasoning improvements from RL-trained teachers actually transfer to smaller students under on-policy distillation, finding that transfer is structured and metric-dependent rather than scalar. It proposes Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation (TS-OPD), which screens training problems by joint student-teacher sampled success to route data appropriately. Results inform when RL investment in teachers benefits distilled students.

entry.title: SO(3)-RoPE for Spherical Transformers

author.name: Christian Libner, Chase van de Geijn, Alexander S. Ecker, Maurice Weiler

entry.summary: The paper introduces SO(3)-RoPE, a relative positional embedding that incorporates spherical geometry into transformer attention via unitary SO(3) representations, remaining equivariant and compatible with FlashAttention. On shallow water dynamics over a rotating sphere, the resulting SO3ViT outperforms an S2 transformer baseline with lower error and reduced runtime. It elegantly connects rotational equivariance with efficient attention.

entry.title: GAMBIT: Learning to Plan Continuous Multi-Robot Trajectories

author.name: Rishabh Jain, Akmaral Moldagalieva, Lorenzo Magnino, Michael Amir, Keisuke Okumura, Ajay Shankar, Wolfgang H\"onig, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: GAMBIT learns coordinated motion-primitive selection for multi-robot trajectory planning with double-integrator continuous dynamics, capturing self-sacrificial team behaviors that manual heuristics miss. It trains via imitation learning and then fine-tunes the policy for overall team performance in dense, interaction-rich environments. The work comes from a recognized multi-robot planning group (Prorok, Honig, Okumura).

entry.title: Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes

author.name: Jungho Kim, Hongjae Shin, Seunghoon Yu, Heecheol Yoo, Myeongjun Kim, Jiyong Oh, Donghyuk Kwak, Seunghyeop Nam, Haesung Oh, Hyunju Kim, Hyungchan Cho, Jaehyun Park, Soo Won Seo, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: Odyssey is a closed-loop benchmark of 100 long-horizon driving scenarios reconstructed from 100-second nuPlan logs, replacing ambiguous directional commands with explicit SD-map routes to disambiguate navigation goals. It enables evaluation of how early decisions affect subsequent driving, addressing a key gap in end-to-end autonomous driving evaluation.

entry.title: Differentially Private Mixing of Public Datasets Improves Private Learning

author.name: Yufei Chen, Tejumade Afonja, Anvith Thudi, Nicolas Papernot

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first pipeline that privately learns a mixture over several public datasets to pretrain on before DP finetuning on sensitive data, keying on the insight that the best mixture can be found via a privately learned low-dimensional linear model. Tests on NIH chest X-ray data and other tasks show improved utility over single-dataset selection. This reduces the utility cost of differential privacy in a principled way.

entry.title: Integrated Imputation-Classification for Supervised Learning with Missing Data

author.name: Yue Liu, Ben Liang, Ali Tizghadam, Ilijc Albanese

entry.summary: IICN jointly trains an imputer and an (n+1)-class discriminator adversarially under a single supervised objective, where the discriminator distinguishes true classes from an additional imputed class. It proves that at the global optimum the pair implements marginalization over missing coordinates and yields a Bayes-optimal classifier. A principled alternative to decoupled impute-then-predict pipelines.

entry.title: Asymptotically Optimal Best Arm Identification with Fixed-Budget under Differential Privacy

author.name: Keqin Chen, Jie Bian, Yulian Wu, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: The paper studies fixed-budget best arm identification in bandits under pure epsilon-differential privacy protecting the full transcript, proving the optimal error decay is governed by an instance-dependent privacy-aware transportation exponent distinct from the fixed-confidence analogue. Guided by this exponent, it proposes AO-Pri-BAI, an adaptive algorithm with asymptotic optimality guarantees. This resolves a theory gap at the intersection of bandits and privacy.

entry.title: From Pixels, Without Pre-training: Joint Generative and Self-Supervised Representation Learning in One Model

author.name: Vicente Balmaseda, Ching-Long Lin, Tianbao Yang

entry.summary: Studies joint generative and self-supervised representation learning in a single model, enabling self-conditioned image generation from pixels without labels, pretrained encoders, or autoencoders. The work tackles the objective mismatch between contrastive learning (invariant, coarse semantics on clean views) and flow matching (fine detail on noisy inputs).

entry.title: Training-Free Transformer Merging via Sequential Local Operator Alignment

author.name: Akansh Maurya, Ya-Wei Eileen Lin, Stefanie Jegelka, Sebastian U Stich, Rotem Mulayoff

entry.summary: This paper identifies that layer-wise merging of transformers ignores the composed-matrix structure of query-key and value-output operators and that downstream activations drift as earlier layers are merged. The proposed Sequential Local Operator Alignment method merges transformers along the execution path of the partially merged model using calibration data, without any further training. This improves training-free model merging quality.

entry.title: Representation-Aligned Auxiliary Supervision for Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Peiyao Sheng, Ashwin Hebbar, Peiyang Xu, Yunfei Xie, Kevin Wang, Rui Xin, Chen Wei, Zhangyang Wang, Jinwoo Shin, Pramod Viswanath, Sewoong Oh

entry.summary: Using chess as a controlled testbed with symbolic (FEN) and spatial (ASCII) state representations, the authors identify representation compatibility as a key factor in adapting language models to structured domains. They show models process semantically equivalent inputs very differently, affecting learning and generalization, and propose representation-aligned auxiliary supervision to improve adaptation. The framework may transfer to other structured domains such as code and math.

entry.title: DV-Lens: Revealing the Functional Organization of Language Model Parameters

author.name: Chenhang Cui, Jian Yu, Shuyi Miao, Xiaohao Liu, Rui Huang, Fei Shen, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua
