entry.title: ExStereo: Lifting 2D Vision-Language-Action Models to 3D with Explicit Stereo Representations

author.name: I-Chun Arthur Liu, Jason Chen, Gaurav S. Sukhatme, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: ExStereo augments pre-trained 2D VLA models with 3D perception by adding a stereo module that reconstructs scene geometry from stereo image pairs using modern stereo foundation models. Action tokens selectively attend to extracted stereo tokens, injecting metric depth and precise 3D positions without retraining from scratch.

entry.title: AgenticTactileVLA: Contact-Guided Execution-Time Supervision for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation without VLA Retraining

author.name: Elizaveta Semenyakina, Ivan Snegirev, Mikhail Kiselev, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Hajira Amjad, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AgenticTactileVLA is an execution-time supervisor that uses finger-position and motor-effort feedback to adapt a fixed vision-language-action policy during physical interaction, deciding among transparent operation, finger-flexion refinement, configuration retention/release, VLA retry, or compliant control regimes. This shifts object-specific adaptation from prediction time to execution time without retraining the VLA.

entry.title: RiskFly: Frustum-Aligned Spatio-Temporal Risk Fields for One-Stage Agile Flight in Dynamic Clutter

author.name: Luxia Ai, Haopeng Chen, Yuchao Mei, Guohao Zhang, Wenbing Tao

entry.summary: RiskFly is a one-stage learning-based planner for agile drone flight in dynamic clutter that predicts spatio-temporal risk fields aligned with its action space, using paired depth sequences and frustum-aligned range maps. This gives the planner spatially and temporally structured danger predictions, avoiding the late reactive maneuvers of scalar-cost one-stage planners.

entry.title: TUCO: Curating Simulation Demonstrations for Sim-to-Real Robot Policy Co-Training

author.name: Ning Zhu, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Zhangyujie Sun, Peihao Li, Dongyue Ni, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: TUCO is the first systematic study of data curation for sim-to-real robot policy co-training, using influence functions to trace how each simulated demonstration affects target-domain scoring rollouts and decomposing effects into trajectory-level utility and set-level coverage. This enables principled selection of simulation data to supplement scarce real-world demonstrations.

entry.title: DexForge: High-Fidelity Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting

author.name: Meizhong Wang, Kun Cao, Ruiqi Ni, Lihua Xie, Yiguang Hong

entry.summary: DexForge converts human video demonstrations into high-fidelity robot trajectories using differentiable physics: it reconstructs spherical-Gaussian object models and hand-object motion from visual observations, then performs contact-aware kinematic retargeting with force-aware dynamics optimization in a differentiable simulator combining Gaussian collision detection with differentiable dynamics. This improves cross-embodiment reproduction of dexterous manipulation under physical constraints.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Anirudh Goyal, Abram L. Friesen, Andrea Banino, Theophane Weber, Nan Rosemary Ke, Adria Puigdomenech Badia, Arthur Guez, Mehdi Mirza, Peter C. Humphreys, Ksenia Konyushkova, Laurent Sifre, Michal Valko, Simon Osindero, Timothy Lillicrap, Nicolas Heess, Charles Blundell

entry.summary: The paper proposes augmenting RL agents with a learned retrieval process that directly accesses a dataset of past experiences to map them to optimal behavior, instead of distilling all experience into parametric policies via gradient updates. This addresses computational expense, slow experience integration, and model capacity limits. It is an influential DeepMind paper anticipating later interest in retrieval-based and in-context RL.

entry.title: Bradley-Terry model under general comparison graphs

author.name: Ruijian Han, Yuanhang Luo, Yiming Xu

entry.summary: This work establishes uniform consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator for the Bradley-Terry ranking model under general deterministic comparison designs, removing the need for homogeneity or strong compatibility assumptions on comparison graphs. The pairwise error bound decomposes into a pair-specific effective resistance term and a global spectral gap term, and is shown to be tight up to logarithmic factors. This has direct relevance to ranking systems and to LLM preference-based evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: Behavioral History Outperforms Descriptions of the Person for LLM Synthetic Personas

author.name: Khashayar Pourtaheri, Ahmad Zareei

entry.summary: Using a two-wave panel of 845 US adults measured on 14 behavioral biases, the study finds that LLM synthetic respondents predict an individual's later choices better from their earlier survey answers than from demographics, personality traits, or cognitive scores. This has direct implications for the validity of LLM-based social science simulation.

entry.title: Bidirectional Preference Synthesis: Learning Prompt-Conditioned Preferences from Boundary Failures

author.name: Junbo Wang (Kuaishou Technology, Nanjing University), Lidong Lu (Nanjing University), Zhuoqun Li (Kuaishou Technology), Guiping Jiang (Kuaishou Technology), Xiangyu Wu (Kuaishou Technology), Tinghai Zhang (Kuaishou Technology), Tong Lu (Nanjing University)

entry.summary: BPS improves DPO preference data construction for boundary failures, cases where a response violates the given instruction but coherently satisfies a nearby intent, by adding a reverse preference pair under a synthesized achieved prompt alongside the conventional forward pair. The same response is thus rejected where wrong and chosen where right, teaching prompt-conditioned preferences without changing the DPO objective. Industry-academic collaboration from Kuaishou and Nanjing University.

entry.title: Agent Behavior as Code: Efficient and Robust LLM Agents with Programmatic Specifications

author.name: Peng Qi, Chunliang Lyu, Gang Li, Fabian Chan, Cheng Chang, Ignacio Cases, Will Lu

entry.summary: ABCAgent represents full agent behavior as a symbolic program (Python with optional neural functions), addressing error propagation across similar tasks, redundant FM-call cost and latency, and limited context/instruction-following in conventional LLM agents. Compiling recurring workflows into code promises determinism, reuse, and reduced foundation-model dependence at execution time.

entry.title: EmoRSS: Mitigating Emotion-Induced Over-Refusal in Large Language Models

author.name: Shuyi Miao, Yaojin Ma, Chenhang Cui, Xiaohao Liu, Dang Jisheng, Shengda Zhuo, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper finds that emotional expression in benign user requests systematically increases LLM refusal tendencies, causing over-refusal, and proposes EmoRSS, an activation-steering method that identifies a refusal-sensitive layer and steers representations to reduce emotion-induced over-refusal while preserving refusals on harmful requests.

entry.title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories

author.name: Jin Jiang, Sean Yates, Jasper Chong, Raymond Brooks, Alex Lawson, Yuqin Qin, Liangcai Gao

entry.summary: The authors introduce LifeLong Digital Twin, an event-driven paradigm that organizes life events into daily health states accumulated into a lifelong health context, with an agent harness for integrating multimodal evidence beyond text. They evaluate four language models across 25 diseases on this framework.

entry.title: Copies or Sources? Measuring How LLM Aggregators Count Restated Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jianxin Gao, Runze Li, Tianyi Yu, Liangwei Ren, Bohan Chen, Zining Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a copy-weight metric converting reported probabilities into units of independent readings, distinguishing aggregators that count distinct sources from those that double-count restatements. Across three testbeds with fixed evidence but varied restatement and a Bayesian oracle, it measures whether LLM aggregators are misled by repeated statements under different communication protocols.

entry.title: Language models can notice an impossible engineering problem yet still report it as solved

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Testing 14 models on 30 pairs of mechanics problems (valid vs. made-impossible variants), the study finds models often fail to reject physically impossible problems even when their calculations reveal impossibility, with 12 of 90 replies from recent models failing to flag flawed versions. This measures a gap between problem recognition and honest reporting under a solved/cannot-solve protocol.

entry.title: BridgeCast: Bridging Ocean Wave Forecasts to Reanalysis via Flow Matching with Exogenous Variables

author.name: Siyu Gan, Dongsheng Luo, Kunxiaojia Yuan, Dongjin Song, Jingchao Ni

entry.summary: BridgeCast is a physics-AI hybrid framework that corrects systematic biases in physics-based ocean wave forecasts using conditional flow matching. The model treats physical model outputs as corrupted observations and learns a continuous-time generative process that transforms their distribution toward that of reanalysis data, producing probabilistic corrected forecasts. This matters for maritime safety, offshore operations, and coastal resilience, where wave forecast accuracy has direct economic and safety consequences.

entry.title: Beware EviLLM: Enabling Vulnerability Injection via Large Language Models

author.name: Zeezoo Ryu, Simon Chung, Muhammad Faraz Karim, Anna Raymaker, Karan Singh Jodha, Yash Chaturvedi, Sukarno Mertoguno

entry.summary: This security paper studies the EviLLM threat model where a third-party adversary compromises an AI code generation pipeline to deliberately inject vulnerabilities, a more realistic scenario than inadvertent vulnerabilities, LLM backdooring, or jailbreaking. The authors implement two EviLLM instances with capabilities comparable to existing cybercriminals and evaluate their effectiveness.

entry.title: What to Preserve in Recursive Computation: A Local Predictive Sufficiency Principle

author.name: Peilin Wang, Feng Shiyang, Hongfu Gao, Cencheng Zhao, Di Yuan, Hui Chen, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: This theoretical work addresses information loss in recursive computation, where intermediate states are repeatedly compressed. It introduces a local predictive sufficiency principle with recursive predictive closure, proving that controlling local predictive deficiencies at interfaces bounds root-level discrepancy, and derives a tractable variational training procedure from it.

entry.title: Guess My Weight: Profiled Side-Channel Recovery of Floating-Point Neural-Network Weights

author.name: Timon Lum\'ir Fillo, J\'an Mikulec, Anubhab Baksi, Jakub Breier, Xiaolu Hou

entry.summary: Presents a profiled template attack that recovers bit-exact IEEE-754 single-precision neural-network weights from power measurements, targeting the multiplication of a known input with first-layer weights. This extends side-channel attacks beyond reduced-precision settings to the full 32-bit floating-point space.

entry.title: Policy as Data: Replay-Based Policy Dual Averaging via Advantage Regression

author.name: Nianli Peng, Geoffrey J. Gordon, Kiant\'e Brantley

entry.summary: Introduces RDA2C, an actor-critic method that treats replay data as a first-class input to policy improvement: historical advantage estimates contribute directly to a dual score model fitted by regression, from which the current policy is derived via regularized dual averaging with entropy regularization.

entry.title: ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Penghui Yang, Long Xing, Xuanlang Dai, Ziyu Liu, Kai Chen, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: ResOPD improves on-policy distillation under sparse teacher interfaces by providing unbiased full-vocabulary reverse KL gradient estimation while communicating only sparse teacher signals such as top-k distributions. It resolves the trade-off between high-variance sampled-token estimators and biased top-k objectives via tail residualization.

entry.title: Task-Aware Joint Pruning and Distillation for Efficient Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Miao He, Peng Cheng, Zhongjie Ba, Qing Wen, Li Lu, Xin Yang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: The paper proposes a task-aware compression framework for SSL-based audio deepfake detectors that combines cross-domain knowledge distillation with movement-guided structured pruning to preserve forgery-discriminative features under aggressive compression. This enables deployment of deepfake detection on resource-constrained devices where 300M+ parameter SSL models are infeasible.

entry.title: Human-Like Attention? A Psychophysical Comparison of Visual Search in Humans and MLLMs

author.name: Renchi Zhang, Joost C. F. de Winter, Dimitra Dodou, Harleigh C. Seyffert, Yke Bauke Eisma

entry.summary: This study compares visual search behavior between 1,250 humans and MLLMs using identical 2D and 3D stimuli, finding that both show efficient feature search and degraded conjunction search as set size grows, with strong error-rate correlations (rho = 0.82). Divergences also emerged, suggesting MLLMs share some but not all human difficulty signatures.

entry.title: SimpleMark: Fast Multi-Bit Text Watermarking under f -Divergence Constraints

author.name: Benjamin D. Kim, Wanrong Zhang, Weitong Ruan, Lav R. Varshney, Daniel Alabi

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for multi-bit watermarking of LLM text where security is defined via f-divergence from the base model distribution, with per-key, per-message guarantees supporting TV and KL divergences. The coding-based scheme optimally biases next-token distributions under a divergence budget and characterizes the embedding-rate, decoding-reliability, and security tradeoff. Important for provenance and detection of machine-generated text with formal guarantees.

entry.title: Scalable Minimal-Change Learning for Controllable Image Editing

author.name: Shuo Chen, Fengming Huang, Yu Yao, Mingming Gong, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: The work formalizes minimal-change editing, changing only specified attributes while preserving everything else, as an optimization objective for instruction-based image editing. It uses reinforcement learning with an agentic vision-language reward model that audits candidate edits for unimplemented requested changes and unintended changes, merged via a group-level rubric. This avoids weak proxies like latent L1 regularization and scales without extra supervision.

entry.title: Adaptive Mean Flow for Responsive Closed-Loop Robot Control

author.name: Aksel Vaaler, Marco Job, Christian Holden, Olav Egeland

entry.summary: The paper introduces Adaptive Mean Flow (AMF), a framework addressing the latency of iterative denoising in diffusion and flow-based robot policies that hinders high-frequency closed-loop control. AMF enables responsive action updates using the most recent state information instead of open-loop action chunking. This targets a well-known limitation of modern imitation-learned policies.

entry.title: S$^3$N: A Spherical Spiral Scanning Network for Weather Forecasting

author.name: Fan Yan, Chen Hui, Weisi Lin, Haiqi Zhu, Feng Jiang, Sun-Yuan Kung, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a Spherical Spiral Scanning Network for machine-learning weather prediction, with a bidirectional L2Proj mapping to avoid reconstruction errors of HEALPix pointwise mappings and cross-face communication that avoids handcrafted boundary handling. Addresses polar-area distortion and inter-face information flow in global forecasting architectures. An architecture contribution to an active applied area.

entry.title: The Numerical Linear Algebra of Large Language Models

author.name: Abdelkader Baggag, Yousef Saad

entry.summary: A survey/perspective paper by numerical linear algebra authorities (including Yousef Saad) framing LLMs as the latest driver of NLA evolution, following historical waves such as QR algorithms for eigenproblems and sparse solvers. It examines the numerical linear algebra problems underlying LLM training and inference. Such a bridge between the NLA and ML communities can shape research on efficient computation for large models.

entry.title: Your Temporal Link Predictor Is Blind to Who Is Active: A Missing Factor That Transfers Across Models

author.name: Ji Zhang, Zixin Liu, Yiran Ding, Jiayi Wang, Yilu Du, Weijia Xuan

entry.summary: The authors prove that standard negative sampling in temporal link prediction cancels source node activity from the optimal score, so models are never rewarded for learning who is likely to act at all. They propose SNAM, a self-exciting point-process model of source activity fitted to decayed interaction counts, and show this factor dominates under harder historical and inductive negatives.

entry.title: Learning without Overwriting: A Theory of Self-Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning in Continual Reasoning

author.name: Shinichi Uemura, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Modeling LLM reasoning as search over a directed acyclic graph, the paper provides a unified theoretical analysis of OPSD and SFT dynamics in continual learning, with optimization guarantees. It shows OPSD with hints from correct outputs enables continual learning without forgetting via sparse yet effective gradients.

entry.title: Task Inference Beyond Least Squares in Behavioral Foundation Models

author.name: Kuan-Hsun Tu, Chien-Sheng Chiang, Hsin-Wei Chen, Ping-Chun Hsieh, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: The paper identifies that ordinary least squares task-vector inference in behavioral foundation models biases zero-shot policies away from optimality because it leaves reward ordering unconstrained. It proposes BLS, which balances reward reconstruction error against successor-measure mismatch, with a suboptimality gap upper bound.

entry.title: PACMI: Provenance-Aware Cascading Memory Invalidation for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Liu, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Yiqun Duan, Mingkai Zheng, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: Proposes PACMI, a framework for LLM agent long-term memory that tracks dependencies among memories and new evidence via a provenance graph with typed edges, assigning records to a four-state validity lattice. It supports cascading invalidation of outdated memories while preserving historically useful records, addressing a real gap in current agent memory systems.

entry.title: WaveGSSM: Graph Wave State Space Models for Propagating Spatio-Temporal Patterns

author.name: Junyou Zhu, Fenying Cai, Ping Xiong, Christian Nauck, Langzhou He, Chao Gao, J\"urgen Kurths, Frank Hellmann

entry.summary: WaveGSSM is a second-order graph state-space model that maintains two coupled latent states per node, representing both the current pattern and its temporal rate of change, with a graph-wave transition updating the motion state. This explicitly models how patterns propagate across graphs, addressing a limitation of space-then-time spatio-temporal GNN architectures. Empirical results show the same field can yield different futures depending on recent rate of change.

entry.title: Dynamic Quadtree Tokenization and Transformer for Adaptive Mesh PDE Forecasting

author.name: Yilin Zhuang, Noah Zambrano, Karthik Duraisamy

entry.summary: WAMRViT is a Vision Transformer for PDE forecasting that tokenizes inputs as balanced quadtrees using a wavelet-inspired refinement criterion, jointly encodes position and refinement level with 3D rotary embeddings, and regrids in cell space for stable long-horizon rollouts. This dynamically allocates resolution to shocks, fronts, and interfaces that occupy small evolving regions. It addresses the quadratic attention cost trade-off between resolution and rollout horizon in neural PDE surrogates.

entry.title: A KKL Observer Perspective on Reservoir Computing

author.name: Anastasia Bizyaeva, Fernando Casta\~nos, Jaime A. Moreno

entry.summary: Shows that the reservoir computing problem is mathematically an extension of the classic Kazantzis-Kravaris-Luenberger observer design problem from systems and control theory. This correspondence allows long-standing open questions in RC, such as why reservoirs learn and how to choose architectures, to draw on the mature KKL literature. A unifying theoretical reframing with cross-disciplinary payoff.

entry.title: DreamTest: World-Model Surrogates for Search-Based Testing of Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents

author.name: Qinghua Xu, Guancheng Wang, Boxi Yu, Liting Lin, Lionel Briand

entry.summary: Introduces DreamTest, a world-model surrogate for search-based testing of deep RL agents in cyber-physical systems. It adapts a recurrent state-space model to learn agent behavior and environment dynamics from training logs, then uses imagined rollouts to produce failure scores that guide test configuration search. This models how tests unfold rather than predicting pass/fail outcomes directly, reducing the cost of finding diverse failures.

entry.title: Ontology Concept Overlap as a Training Signal: Knowledge-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Aditya Tanna, Abhishek Jindal

entry.summary: The paper proposes a soft verifier for RL post-training of language models on clinical QA based on UMLS Concept Unique Identifier overlap computed via scispaCy, providing a graded, externally specified reward without a model in the loop. This is combined within GRPO with an entropy-normalized LLM judge for safety and evidence axes and a small consistency penalty. It fills a gap between preference-based RLHF and binary verifiable rewards for domains where near-correct answers differ by one entity.

entry.title: How Do People Challenge Racial Stereotypes Online? Counter-Story Detection Across Reddit Communities

author.name: Uma Sushmitha Gunturi, Jimin Mun, Maarten Sap, Maria Antoniak

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first computational framework for detecting counter-storytelling against racial stereotypes on Reddit, including a three-dimensional taxonomy grounded in narratology and Critical Race Theory plus a multi-stage detection pipeline. It opens a new area distinct from prior counterspeech research. Strong interdisciplinary social-science contribution.

entry.title: MemStrata: 95% and 90.91% Source-Aware Accuracy on LongMemEval-500 and LoCoMo-1540 with a Local Qwen 3.8 27B Q4_K_M Reader

author.name: Neeraj Yadav (Called It Inc.)

entry.summary: MemStrata is a conversational memory system that achieves 95% on LongMemEval-S and 90.91% on LoCoMo categories 1-4 using a local quantized Qwen 3.8 27B reader with a 24,000-token evidence ceiling, layering nonduplicated, dated, speaker-attributed source spans over a retrieval backbone. It also proposes source-aware grading, where the judge checks the reference against the full source history, yielding notably different scores than reference-only grading. The paper highlights how benchmark grading methodology affects reported long-term memory performance.

entry.title: DeferKV: Rethinking Eviction Timing for One-Shot KV Cache Compression

author.name: Zhe Wang, Jiakai Li, Yujia Sun, Rongzheng Wang, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: DeferKV shows that one-shot KV cache eviction should be delayed from the end of prefill to the first real decoding step, since early decode queries provide attention signals more predictive of subsequent decode attention. Quantitative analysis shows the largest single-step gain occurs at the prefill-decode boundary. This simple timing change improves long-context compression quality.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Textual World Modeling through Structured Reasoning

author.name: Fangxin Wang, Xiang Gao, Yuguang Yao, Kaiwen Dong, Nikash Walia, Kamalika Das

entry.summary: The paper tackles error compounding in long-horizon textual world modeling by introducing structured reasoning that conditions multi-step dynamics predictions on action sequences, addressing weak credit assignment from endpoint-only supervision and information loss in intermediate states. This enables agents to better compare possible futures before acting. It advances language-based world models for planning.

entry.title: DP-ES: Differentially Private Evolution Strategies for Prompt Optimization

author.name: Ziniu Liu, Aiping Li, Yue Han, Han Yu, Junjian Zhang, Dong Zhu, Changjian Li, Shiqiang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors diagnose instability in token-level differentially private prompt optimization (e.g., DP-OPT's high variance on GSM8K) as a structural flaw of greedy token-by-token construction, and propose DP-ES, which evolves a population of full prompts via LLM mutations that never touch the private data, spending privacy budget only on sampled-Gaussian evaluation. Selection is treated as post-processing.

entry.title: From Sight to Foresight: Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Feiran Wang, Xiaoqi Wang, Ziwei Li, Wenbin He, Yan Yan, Liu Ren

entry.summary: The paper introduces SpatialMind, a metric-scale vision-language model for predictive spatial reasoning that forecasts distances, motion directions, and spatial relations in future, unobserved intervals from a video prefix. A metric depth adapter anchors reasoning to real-world scale and a progressive state chain grounds future prediction in observed dynamics.

entry.title: FLASHSWIN: Unlocking Large Windows and Dense Tokens in Swin Vision Transformers with Memory Efficient Attention

author.name: Tushar Kataria, Gerald Sabin, Ponnuswamy Sadayappan, Shireen Y. Elhabian

entry.summary: FLASHSWIN replaces standard Swin windowed attention, which materializes M-squared-by-M-squared score matrices and full relative-position bias gradients, with a FlashAttention-based memory-efficient implementation. This frees Swin and SwinV2 from the small-window, coarse-token regime, enabling large windows and dense tokens for fine-grained tasks.

entry.title: GeoBridge-VLA: Geometry-Aware Residual Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hyun Song, Kangmin Kim, Loren Jinsoo Um, Minhui Han, Jaehyeok Park, Taewan Cho, Andrew Jaeyong Choi

entry.summary: GeoBridge-VLA is a two-stage method that learns geometric features from a pretrained VLA's frozen visual encoder with depth supervision, then trains a gated residual interface so these features augment existing visual tokens without a second image encoder or extra tokens. Deployment requires only RGB, robot state, and language, with no depth observations at test time. The method injects precise spatial reasoning into manipulation-focused VLA models.

entry.title: StageVLN: Spatial and Trajectory Auxiliary Guidance for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Anh Dao, Quan-Dung Pham, Le Danh Vinh, The Anh Nguyen, Nguyen Viet Tri Pham, Yiyu Chen, Pham Tuyen Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: StageVLN shapes VLM-based navigation representations during training using privileged spatial and trajectory guidance from a frozen geometry model, while keeping the original lightweight inference pathway intact. This improves scene geometry and progress awareness without deploying depth estimators or explicit maps at test time.

entry.title: Safe Image Generation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Eungyeol Han, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: Proposes an in-generation safety framework for text-to-image models that monitors the denoising trajectory, detects emerging NSFW signals from intermediate representations, and intervenes during generation rather than only filtering prompts or moderating outputs afterward. The RL-based intervention targets a broader adversarial space than pre/post-generation checks.

entry.title: Anatomy-preserving unpaired cone-beam CT refinement for image-guided radiotherapy using pseudo-label guided diffusion

author.name: Qi Lai, Yutong He

entry.summary: RefineCBCT is an unpaired diffusion-based framework that removes artifacts from cone-beam CT images while preserving patient-specific anatomy, using pseudo-label guidance and short-step sampling. It achieves best results across metrics on LUNG TCIA data, relevant for image-guided radiotherapy.

entry.title: Video Encoders Built on Image Representations

author.name: Jusheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang, Longqi Cai, Liangzhe Yuan, Yuxiao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: The paper asks whether compact video encoders can be built on frozen image representations by decoupling per-frame representation, cross-frame token allocation, and temporal interaction, using a question-aware selector to allocate frame tokens. This contrasts native video pathways that couple neighboring frames during encoding.

entry.title: Less Context, Better Geometry: Masked Geometric Encoder for Robust 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Zhimin Shao, Xijun Liu, Zhaoliang Zhang, Yutao Tang, Abhay Yadav, Rama Chellappa, Cheng Peng

entry.summary: The paper identifies weaknesses of all-to-all global attention in 3D foundation models, including quadratic complexity and unreliable cross-view evidence propagation. It proposes a Masked Geometric Encoder that strategically drops frame tokens during training and distills from a full-context teacher, yielding more robust geometric representations under incomplete cross-view context.

entry.title: ROOT: Discovering Rewards for User-Specified Embodied Behaviors

author.name: Eren Sadikoglu, Aditya Taparia, Xinyuan Liu, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: ROOT (Reward Optimization via Observable Trees) casts reward design as aligning learned policies with user-specified embodied behaviors, addressing LLM-based reward synthesis failures on subtle visual properties like gait naturalness and posture. Instead of scalar training statistics, it discovers reward functions from observable behavioral descriptions.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Visuomotor Policies through Local Recovery Supervision

author.name: Yuzhi Zhang, Xinyu Liu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a framework in which visuomotor policies recursively self-improve: each round audits the current policy to locate unresolved failures, generates corrective demonstrations at those failure states via a fixed multimodal tool-using teacher agent, and updates the policy that drives subsequent data collection. A frozen student tests whether teacher interventions support further progress, enabling iterative recovery-focused learning.

entry.title: The Unexpired Plan: A Free Monitor for Accelerated Diffusion Policies

author.name: Yi Zhao, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: This paper studies training-free acceleration of diffusion policies through reuse monitors that decide when shortcut denoising is safe, evaluating 114 accelerator configurations across four policy families priced in closed-loop success rather than feature distance. It shows monitor response design matters greatly: published re-arm gates lose twenty points even with an oracle statistic, while an absorbing response recovers performance.

entry.title: Controllable and Photorealistic Pedestrian Risky Motion Generation for End-to-End Driving Safety Evaluation

author.name: Siyuan Liu, Miao Li, Haibao Yu, Haohong Lin, Qing Zhou, Bingbing Nie, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: ControlPed combines trajectory-level conflict synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting to generate photorealistic, motion-controllable safety-critical vehicle-pedestrian scenarios for evaluating end-to-end driving systems. It is built on HazardPed, a dataset from 10,352 traffic videos with conflict trajectories, HD maps, and annotated 3D human motions, and lifts synthesized conflicts into 3D human motion before rendering. This bridges the gap between controllable trajectory generators and photorealistic video approaches.

entry.title: Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving

author.name: Aniket Didolkar, Anirudh Goyal, Nan Rosemary Ke, Siyuan Guo, Michal Valko, Timothy Lillicrap, Danilo Rezende, Yoshua Bengio, Michael Mozer, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: The paper provides evidence that strong LLMs possess metacognitive knowledge, such as the ability to name skills and procedures relevant to a given math task, using a prompt-guided procedure to elicit and cluster interpretable skill labels. It validates that these labels are meaningful to the model's reasoning, informing skills-based routing and curriculum approaches. This connects interpretability, reasoning, and self-knowledge in LLMs.

entry.title: CADForge: Agentic Single-View CAD Reconstruction with Explicit Geometry Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Lu, Zhifei Yang, Tianao Dong, Mingzhe Xing, Zhen Xiao, Yikai Wang

entry.summary: CADForge is an agentic framework that reconstructs editable parametric CAD models from single images by decomposing objects into CAD-meaningful components, inferring geometric constraints, and translating them into executable CadQuery programs with a review agent validating results. It addresses practical manufacturing needs where reconstruction must yield editable, precise geometry rather than meshes. Explicit mathematical reasoning replaces end-to-end black-box generation.

entry.title: CORE-RL: Confidence-Oriented Reliability Evaluation of Black-Box Reinforcement Learning Policies

author.name: Santhosh GS, Ananya Ravi, Devika Jay, Abhishek Sarkar, Perepu Satheesh Kumar, Saurav Prakash, Kaushik Dey, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for evaluating black-box RL policies delivered as opaque executables or remote APIs, integrating early task termination and safety constraint violations into a Unified Reliability Metric. The approach targets deployment in critical domains where policy internals are inaccessible to protect intellectual property.

entry.title: RAGStress: A controlled benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation under knowledge-base degradation

author.name: Shiqi Yang, Jiekai Ma, Gaoyuan Du

entry.summary: RAGStress is a controlled benchmark for stress-testing RAG systems under systematic knowledge-base corruption, pairing four naturalistic corruption types with three severity levels across 182,546 documents from 57 MMLU subjects and 52,500 evaluations. It reveals how clean-retrieval assumptions break down under realistic KB degradation, an important and neglected evaluation axis for deployed RAG systems.

entry.title: Runtime Authorization of Self-Generated Subgoals in Long-Horizon Tool-Using AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the authorization gap where per-tool permission checks cannot guarantee that an agent's evolving goal graph stays within the principal-approved task. It proposes a formal model with version-bound witnesses for goal-graph mutations, atomic commit boundaries for protected effects, and proofs of trace-policy and forbidden-state preservation under explicit assumptions.

entry.title: EVISKILL: Grounding Skill Evolution in Replayable Evidence

author.name: Yan Zhou, Yili Wang, Yiwei Dai, Qinggang Zhang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: EVISKILL addresses continual skill evolution for LLM agents by grounding edits to procedural knowledge in replayable evidence, preserving behavioral evidence and task contexts that support changes. It recognizes that global validation outcomes incompletely judge constituent changes, discarding locally supported corrections or deferring evidence that needs more experience.

entry.title: DREAM: Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-agent Debate

author.name: Khanh-Binh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Tien Anh Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh, Hung Le

entry.summary: DREAM improves multimodal multi-agent debate by assigning each agent and sample a dynamic visual resolution instead of a fixed input, and by countering groupthink where agents conform to confident but hallucinated peers. The two-component design targets both visual-scale variation and premature consensus.

entry.title: Grounded Joint-Attention Other-Play for Zero-Shot Coordination

author.name: Giulia Benintendi, Constantin Ruhdorfer, Fabian K\"ogel, Andreas Bulling

entry.summary: The paper introduces MATE, a multi-agent RL method inspired by human joint attention in which agents coordinate by aligning visual attention on scene-salient objects during interaction rather than relying on arbitrary partner-dependent conventions. Combined with other-play ideas, this aims at zero-shot coordination with unfamiliar partners.

entry.title: CVIF: A Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework for Geometric Diagram Understanding in MLLMs

author.name: Jiahui Kang, Bifan Wei, Lingling Zhang, Tianwen Jiang, Qiuyong Xiao, Jihong Zhang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: CVIF is a training-free, inference-time method that localizes critical layers in multimodal LLMs and applies visual interventions during the transition from evidence aggregation to semantic decoding, using a Geometry-Constrained Local Relation Reconstruction module and adaptive steering. It targets the tendency of MLLMs to rely on textual priors over visual evidence in geometric diagrams.

entry.title: Global Evaluation of AI and NWP Precipitation Forecasts During Atmospheric River Events

author.name: Marina Vicens-Miquel, Taylor Mandelbaum, Amy McGovern, Aaron J. Hill, Daniel Rothenberg

entry.summary: This paper evaluates 24-hour precipitation forecasts from GFS, GEFS, GraphCast, and AIFS over Days 1-10 globally and across three regions during atmospheric river events, using the Extreme Weather Bench framework. It provides the first sufficiently global characterization of whether AI weather models forecast AR-related extreme precipitation as well as numerical weather prediction.

entry.title: Representational Control over Self-Report & Behavior Coherence in LLM Risk-Taking

author.name: Rafal Kocielnik, Peiyang Song, Pengrui Han, Myrl G. Marmarelis, Ramit Debnath, Dean Mobbs, R. Michael Alvarez

entry.summary: This study uses activation steering to examine whether the gap between what LLMs self-report about risk-taking and how they actually behave is a prompting artifact or a property of internal representations. The authors survey nine steering-vector extraction methods across two granularities, evaluated on behavioral tasks, measuring self-report and behavior under the same internal intervention. The work connects interpretability tools with questions about model dispositions and coherence.

entry.title: Weight Decay and Neuron Condensation: A Three-Stage Analysis of Two-Layer ReLU Networks

author.name: Cheng Xu, Pengxiao Lin, Zhangchen Zhou, Zhi-Qin John Xu

entry.summary: Theoretically characterizes how weight decay shapes training dynamics in two-layer ReLU networks via three stages: rapid fitting, amplitude compression, and neuron condensation. Introduces a residual correlation field that governs neuron amplitudes and directions, explaining how kernel decay and weight decay interact to drive parameter-direction alignment.

entry.title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment

author.name: Pronoma Banerjee, Anuva Shah, Jason Wu, Md. Masudur Rahman, Sanjay Mohanty, Satya Kurada, Juan P. Wachs

entry.summary: ARISE is an agentic planning framework for few-shot medical image understanding, applied to inflammatory bowel disease assessment from capsule endoscopy and intestinal ultrasound. It frames interpretation as a sequential workflow with image-grounded self-evaluation to improve reasoning, reduce hallucination, and increase interpretability.

entry.title: A Systematic Analysis of the Predictive Power of LM Surprisal in Reading Chinese

author.name: Hongao Zhu (Department of Linguistics, University of California San Diego), Muxiaoqiao Xu (School of Foreign Languages, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yikang Liu (School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Siyuan Song (School of Foreign Languages, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Department of Linguistics, University of Texas at Austin), Yuxia Wang (School of Foreign Languages, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Byung-Doh Oh (Division of Linguistics and Multilingual Studies, Nanyang Technological University), Hai Hu (Department of Language Science and Technology/Division of AI and the Humanities, Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

entry.summary: The study proposes the Shortest Matching Sequence alignment scheme to map eye-tracking word segmentations to LM subword tokenization in Mandarin, then uses Chinese-Pythia models trained from scratch on 30B tokens to test whether surprisal predicts reading times. Contrary to prior null findings, surprisal is shown to predict Chinese eye-tracking measures across three corpora.

entry.title: Grammar-Guided Code Watermarking with Green Temperature

author.name: Hyundong Jin, Hyeseon An, Soohan Lim, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: GTCW integrates grammar-constrained decoding with probability-aware watermarking for LLM-generated code, restricting watermark token selection to continuations admitted by the current grammar state. This directly constructs the watermark over syntactically valid continuations, mitigating the quality degradation that existing entropy-based or syntax-aware code watermarking methods suffer.

entry.title: Expanding LLM Reasoning

author.name: Rian Atri, Evan Luo

entry.summary: The paper studies where within an existing reasoning chain additional inference compute should begin, defining expansion utility as correctness change from restarting at a stored step, measured across nine models on six benchmarks. A fixed always-last-restart rule is a strong baseline; the learned router beats uniform placement but shows no detected gain over the simple rule.

entry.title: CACFG: Curvature-Aware Classifier-Free Guidance and Optimal Control

author.name: Max Collins, Dasith de Silva Edirimuni, Jordan Vice, Tim French, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: Recasts classifier-free guidance for diffusion models as a continuous-time optimal control problem with curvature-aware corrections, addressing why CFG works despite violating principled sampling dynamics and extending the theory to deterministic samplers used in practice. This offers both a theoretical explanation and potentially better-behaved guidance at high strengths. Deepens the theoretical understanding of a ubiquitous technique.

entry.title: LightMTP: Lightweight Latent Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Tamara Czinczoll, Julie Kallini, Gerard de Melo, Chen Shani

entry.summary: LightMTP is a parameter-light latent multi-token prediction objective for LLM pretraining that encodes future tokens into vector representations without relying on external helper models, unlike prior latent MTP approaches. It aims to capture longer-range structure beyond next-token prediction while avoiding the large parameter overhead and limited gains of existing MTP methods. This is relevant to pretraining objective design.

entry.title: Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zexin Li, Ruili Yao, Yiming Zeng, Xiaoxue Gao

entry.summary: This work studies black-box adversarial attacks on deep RL, where perturbations crafted on a surrogate policy transfer to an unknown victim, formulated as return minimization under per-step budgets. The authors show ported image-classification attacks are no better than random noise, then propose a trajectory-level attack optimized over a receding horizon via differentiable modeling. It advances security analysis of RL systems in realistic threat models.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and the New Science of Culture

author.name: Douglas R. Guilbeault, Bhargav Srinivasa Desikan, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that cognition and culture are co-constituted and now empirically tractable, with subjectivities measurable as trajectories through a high-dimensional cultural field built from embedding methods and generative models. It claims vector geometry recovers individual conceptual structure, organizational communication, and large-scale ideologies across modalities. It sketches an ambitious research program for computational social science.

entry.title: Agentic schema-guided extraction of materials process knowledge from scientific literature

author.name: Sameer Sadruddin, Jennifer D'Souza

entry.summary: SciKGExtract combines LLM-based extraction, chemical normalization via PubChem, and agent-based refinement to populate knowledge graphs from materials-science literature, evaluated on 176 atomic-layer-deposition papers for ZnO and IGZO. The schema-guided approach with expert-annotated evaluation makes it a serious contribution to scientific information extraction.

entry.title: BRANCH-MoE: Balance-Aware Tree Routing for Large Embedding Models

author.name: Gang Fu, Adel Javanmard, MohammadHossein Bateni, Vahab Mirrokni

entry.summary: BRANCH-MoE organizes MoE experts at the leaves of a binary decision tree, with branching probabilities centered on an arrival-weighted mean estimated by exponential moving average, promoting balanced subtree utilization without auxiliary load-balancing losses. The paper provides theoretical justification for the estimator and targets large embedding models. This offers a structured alternative to flat MoE routers whose expert indices carry no topological meaning.

entry.title: On the Trade-off Between Information Loss and Generalization in Sparse Attention

author.name: Zhongqi Fan, Zheng Tan

entry.summary: The paper provides a systematic theoretical analysis of sparse attention, characterizing sparsification-induced approximation error via Jensen-Shannon divergence and connecting this information loss to the generalization gap. It addresses two open questions: how sparsification affects attention fidelity and how that loss interacts with generalization. This helps explain when sparse Transformers can safely replace dense ones.

entry.title: FoSeRL: Formal Sequential Robustness Certification for Reinforcement Learning Policies

author.name: Sara Taheri, Deep Kumar Ganguly, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y, Majid Zamani

entry.summary: FoSeRL certifies deployed reinforcement learning policies against temporally sparse, precommitted action attacks by bounding return loss with a target probability, without retraining or smoothing the policy. It requires only a resettable simulator with shared randomness, avoiding the need for analytical dynamics models.

entry.title: One Token Can Be Enough: Bridging Prompting and Activation Steering with Prefix Steering

author.name: Xudong Zhu, Zhihui Zhu

entry.summary: The paper establishes theoretical conditions under which single- or multi-token activation steering can match prompt-induced attention-head outputs, connecting prompting and steering at the attention level. It then proposes Prefix Steering, which applies steering directions only briefly at the start of generation yet guides subsequent behavior like a prompt.

entry.title: Beyond Overparameterization: Provable Learning of Input-Convex Multi-Layer Polynomial Networks with Active Queries

author.name: Jinqi Tang, Qian Chen, Shihong Ding, Cong Fang

entry.summary: The paper achieves parameter-level recovery of deep L-layer polynomial networks, moving beyond overparameterized and NTK regimes, by using active data queries. This extends feature-learning theory past shallow or single-neuron targets to genuinely deep architectures.

entry.title: VERA: Verdict-Conditioned Reliability for Adaptive LLM Judges

author.name: Qiushui Xu, Syamil Mohd Razak, Tao Yuan, Piotr Habas

entry.summary: VERA estimates the reliability of LLM judge verdicts from hidden activations, distinguishing correct from incorrect judgments within each predicted-verdict group, outperforming output-level confidence. It enables a periodic adaptation framework for LLM judges integrating reliability-ranked updates, replay, and refresh of reliability directions.

entry.title: ColdDDI: Evaluating Knowledge Utilization in Cold-Start Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction

author.name: Jiheng Liang, Chen Zhao, Di Wu, Chenyang Bu, Yunpeng Hong, Xingquan Zhu, Yi He

entry.summary: Introduces ColdDDI, a diagnostic benchmark built from DrugBank with roughly 565k drug-drug interaction pairs, testing whether models actually use molecular, textual, or knowledge-graph evidence in cold-start DDI prediction. It annotates interactions by pharmacological mechanism and evaluates pairs with zero, one, or two unseen drugs.

entry.title: The Blind Spot Paradox: When Adaptive Classifiers Defeat Drift Detectors

author.name: Rapha\"el Minato, Fabrice Popineau, Arpad Rimmel, Bich-Li\^en Doan

entry.summary: This work reveals an operational conflict between adaptive classifiers and concept-drift detectors: when a model's internal adaptation outpaces cumulative drift detectors like CUSUM or Page-Hinkley, accuracy recovers before detection thresholds are crossed. Instrumenting an Adaptive Random Forest shows surviving trees absorb 98.6 percent of the post-drift error transient, and a single background tree swap drops external detection rates by 31 percentage points. The authors derive a finite-horizon boundary and a critical magnitude floor below which drift becomes fundamentally undetectable.

entry.title: RoSA: Rotational Sparse Adaptation for Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Muhammad Azeem Lodhi, Chao Zhou, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: RoSA is a fine-tuning method complementary to PEFT that freezes lower layers and rotates a trainable block across later layers over training, progressively increasing frozen layers near the input. This reduces optimizer-state memory, backpropagation cost, and even forward cost when activations are cached. Because it is orthogonal to the trainable parameterization, it composes with LoRA-style methods and sparse optimizers.

entry.title: FairProp: Fair Node Representation Learning via Differentiable Propagation Layers

author.name: Emmanouil Kariotakis, Aritra Konar

entry.summary: FairProp studies group fairness in GNN node classification, link prediction, and node regression via differentiable propagation layers, providing demographic parity gap bounds for an arbitrary number of sensitive groups. The node classification bound improves on the closest prior result, and the paper provides the first parity bounds for deployed sigmoid-activated link prediction and for node regression. This advances theoretically grounded fairness in graph learning.

entry.title: The Birkhoff Geometry of Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections: Two Channels, Vertex Viscosity, and Sinkhorn as a Retraction

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zhizhou Sha, Chiwun Yang

entry.summary: This paper provides a geometric theory of manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC), which widen a transformer's residual stream to n parallel streams mixed by doubly stochastic matrices computed via Sinkhorn normalization. The analysis shows the mixer splits the stream into a mean channel (where mHC is exactly a residual network) and a contracting difference channel acting as fading memory with a computable horizon, and characterizes the Sinkhorn-logit map as a retraction on the Birkhoff polytope. This gives principled understanding of an emerging architecture family.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Graph Representation Learning: Embed in One Metric, Optimize with Another

author.name: Federico Larroca, Paola Bermolen, Marcelo Fiori, Bernardo Marenco

entry.summary: The authors show that numerical difficulties of hyperbolic graph embedding at large radii in Poincare ball and Lorentz models stem from a silently fixed choice of tangent parametrization, and that this choice is one endpoint of a one-parameter family of optimization preconditioners with varying curvature. They demonstrate that alternative preconditioner choices are possible and preferable for gradient-based learning.

entry.title: Shared Geometry Is Not Shared Physics: A Layerwise Test of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Astronomy

author.name: Kshitij Duraphe, Aravind Kannappan, Dun Li Chan, Okiki Famutimi, Yaswant Sai Ejjagiri, Michael J. Smith, John F. Wu

entry.summary: Analyzing representations from every layer of 36 pretrained models across matched astronomical optical images, infrared images, and spectra, the authors find significant local-neighborhood alignment in all 139 model-survey comparisons, but alignment does not increase with depth and geometry-selected stages underperform label-selected stages in every image-transfer comparison. The results complicate the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by showing geometric alignment does not imply scientific interchangeability. This is a thoughtful empirical stress test of a popular hypothesis.

entry.title: Gaussian Flow Dynamics: Simulation-Free Neural SDE Learning Beyond One-Time Marginals

author.name: Grigory Bartosh, Christian A. Naesseth

entry.summary: Introduces Gaussian flow dynamics, a construction of stochastic processes from smoothly evolving Gaussian marginals that makes marginal-preserving gauge degrees of freedom explicit and parameterizable for simulation-free neural SDE training. This admits state-dependent diffusion and richer temporal structure than standard Gaussian-marginal posteriors, which otherwise implicitly fix dynamics and bias learned models. A principled improvement to latent SDE training.

entry.title: SIFT: Robust Meta-Faithfulness Verification of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Md. Basim Al Zabir Shammo, Hasan Siddiki, Mahmudul Hasan, Md. Faisal Sheikh, Jakaria Habib

entry.summary: Formalizes meta-faithfulness of chain-of-thought faithfulness detectors as an invariance principle: a valid detector must return identical verdicts on traces differing only by transformations preserving ground-truth faithfulness. The paper proves three negative and constructive results, including that no detector using only intervention-response profiles can separate faithful from epiphenomenal mechanisms with identical signatures. This audits the auditors of reasoning models.

entry.title: Exact Fast Batch Simulation for Tabular Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haochen Zhang, Lingzhou Xue, Zhong Zheng

entry.summary: The authors develop an exact fast-simulation framework for finite-horizon tabular MDPs that represents batches via aggregate Markov flows rather than generating individual trajectories. Two modes cover cases with and without direct access to transition distributions, potentially majorly accelerating RL simulation when only aggregate statistics are needed.

entry.title: Taylor Representations for Model-Free RL in Networked MDPs

author.name: Salah Chikhi, Abdelhaq Chaoui, Asuman Ozdaglar, Saurabh Amin

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical justification for Taylor-expansion approximations of Q-functions in networked Markov decision processes with many agents. It shows that finite-speed information propagation and discounting make local Taylor coefficients decay exponentially with graph distance, enabling scalable local critic representations with bounds controlled by graph locality. This offers a principled path around the exponential blow-up of multi-agent RL.

entry.title: P3: Persistent Particle Planning for Constrained Diffusion Control

author.name: Hikmet Simsir, Mahyar Fardinfar, Ozgur S. Oguz

entry.summary: P3 is a sequential Monte Carlo framework for controlling diffusion-model trajectory priors at test time, maintaining a weighted population of candidate plans across replanning steps. It shifts and partially re-noises candidates, refines them with new observations, and applies constraint-aware resampling without retraining the diffusion model, analyzed as a Feynman-Kac particle system. This enables consistent, feasible sequential decision-making from diffusion priors.

entry.title: Steering Speech-Language Models: Training-Free Task Specialization via Contrastive Activation Addition

author.name: S\'everin Baroudi, Yanis Labrak, Pierfrancesco Melucci, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek, Herv\'e Bredin, Mirco Ravanelli, Ricard Marxer

entry.summary: The authors extend activation steering to SpeechLLMs with a training-free Contrastive Activation Addition protocol that derives steering vectors for speech tasks like transcription from a small number of labeled utterances. Adding these vectors at inference time, especially combined with prompting, improves performance on tasks such as ASR. First exploration of training-free steering in the speech domain.

entry.title: Selecting Repetition Counts Across Model Scales in Data-Constrained Pretraining

author.name: Ziyue WANG, T. Kanamori

entry.summary: This study examines how the optimal data repetition count in pretraining changes with model size when working with a finite target corpus mixed with generic data. Using Wikipedia-derived data and Proof-Pile-2, the authors show repetition-count rankings shift with scale and that a candidate-selection procedure based on smaller-model loss curves can retain the best measured count at larger scales. It provides practical guidance for multi-epoch training in data-constrained settings.

entry.title: Probabilistic Race and Ethnicity Prediction Using Group-Specific Name Lists

author.name: Kyla Chasalow, Noah Dasanaike, Kosuke Imai

entry.summary: The paper proposes list-powered BISG, extending Bayesian Improved Surname Geocoding to derive calibrated race/ethnicity probabilities from group-specific name lists, enabling disparity estimation for groups and regions lacking Census name-frequency data. This broadens valid statistical inference for equity research beyond US Census categories. Authored by established researchers including Kosuke Imai.

entry.title: VHDL-REPOBENCH: A Repository-Level Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on VHDL Design Generation

author.name: Prashanth Vijayaraghavan, Akul Malhotra, Ashutosh Jadhav, Ehsan Degan, Vandana Mukherjee

entry.summary: VHDL-RepoBench is a large-scale repository-level benchmark for LLM VHDL generation, curating about 100 open-source repositories with roughly 2.5k VHDL files and 500 self-verifying testbenches. It fills a gap left by Verilog-focused benchmarks and targets realistic, cross-file design tasks relevant to FPGA and safety-critical hardware.

entry.title: VolS-GS: Relightable Gaussian Splatting with Volumetric Subsurface Scattering

author.name: Junyeong Ahn, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: VolS-GS reconstructs relightable objects from one-light-at-a-time captures using Gaussian splatting, and models subsurface scattering by embedding a differentiable finite-volume light transport solver within the Gaussian scene representation. This lets light propagate through object interiors rather than relying on per-primitive appearance or purely local kernels.

entry.title: RPFQ-ViT: Rotated Phase-Frame Quantization for Extremely Low-Bit Weights in Vision Transformers

author.name: Mengyuan Fan, Bokai Huang, JiaMing Pan, Xiaokun Yuan, Peizhuang Cong, Zhewen Tan, Tong Yang

entry.summary: RPFQ-ViT introduces rotated phase-frame quantization that quantizes paired channels in 2D phase planes, letting low-bit codes preserve the directional geometry of Transformer projections while recovering magnitude with lightweight scaling. It serves as a drop-in QAT replacement to enable extremely low-bit ViTs without severe accuracy loss.

entry.title: Reflection-Robust 6DoF Object Tracking with Light Fields

author.name: Nikolai Goncharov, Donald G. Dansereau

entry.summary: The paper introduces a light-field-based 6DoF tracker that handles reflective surfaces by decomposing view-dependent appearance into diffuse albedo and an environment map, turning reflections from a nuisance into a pose cue. The method recovers reflection-robust depth, builds a relightable surface light field, and refines pose from a coarse initialization. This targets a known weakness of appearance-stability assumptions in robotics and autonomous driving trackers.

entry.title: Code2Games: Enabling Coding Agents for Gaming World Generation

author.name: Wei Wu, Ziyang Xu, Zeyu Zhang, Yang Zhao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Code2Games is an agentic framework that generates coherent gaming worlds from natural-language game intent by coordinating scene analysis, gameplay planning, constrained world generation, and engine customization through a shared scene-gameplay representation with persistent element correspondence. It builds on a Blender base world and verifies consistency after generation. The work extends coding agents toward maintaining consistency across assets, scenes, and executable gameplay logic.

entry.title: Hybrid-Basis Feature Forecasting for Diffusion Sampling Acceleration

author.name: Kai-Liang Cheng, Yuan-Yuan Cheng, Yu-fan Jin, Xiao-Ming Fu

entry.summary: HybridFF is a training-free, plug-and-play framework that accelerates diffusion sampling by forecasting feature evolution across multiple complementary basis families (capturing local smoothness, long-range trends, and non-monotonic variation) combined with fusion weights. Two variants trade off quality versus speed: fixed model-specific weights or adaptive weighting. This matters because sampling cost remains a central barrier to diffusion model deployment.

entry.title: Every View Counts: View-Consistent Panoptic Quality for Multi-view Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Youngmin Lee, Byungha Ko, Guhnoo Yun, Dong Hwan Kim

entry.summary: Proposes View-Consistent Panoptic Quality (VC-PQ), extending panoptic quality from a single image to unordered sets of input views, counting equally every view where an instance is visible. It shows that the commonly used scene-level PQ borrowed from per-scene optimization methods systematically underweights misses and ID changes in feed-forward 3D multi-view models.

entry.title: MoCAR: Motion-code Coordinate-aware AutoRegression for Continuous Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Yiming Xu, Hao Cheng, Monika Sester

entry.summary: MoCAR casts trajectory forecasting as next-code prediction in a continuous, coordinate-aware latent space, where learned motion codes capture both local trajectory geometry and evolving reference-frame transitions. This adapts autoregressive language-style generation to continuous, multimodal motion prediction.

entry.title: Extending Dynamic World Surface Water Mapping to Sentinel-1 with AlphaEarth Embeddings

author.name: Rohit Mukherjee, Frederick Policelli, Beth Tellman, TC Chakraborty, Jonathan Giezendanner, Jonathan A. Sullivan, Ning Sun

entry.summary: This work extends Google's Dynamic World land cover mapping to Sentinel-1 SAR imagery so surface water can be mapped regardless of cloud cover, using DW water classes as weak supervision. It combines annual AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings for spatial context with S1 backscatter for acquisition-time observation, achieving IoU comparable to S2-based baselines on globally distributed validation scenes.

entry.title: EvoMem-VLA: State-Evolution Memory for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuheng Na, Zhide Zhong, Junjie He, Junfeng Li, Haodong Yan, Jiaan Wang, Jiaguan Zhu, Yangyang Zheng, Tianyu Huang, Haoang Li

entry.summary: EvoMem-VLA addresses memory limitations of VLA models on long-horizon tasks by constructing state-evolution memory that explicitly encodes changes between historical states rather than isolated snapshots. These change representations preserve evidence of interaction outcomes so the policy can track task progress beyond what is currently visible.

entry.title: REDIRECT: A 1% Fix for Bad Robot Habits

author.name: Yu Zhang, Jiazhuo Li, Yancong Wei, Kangkang Dong, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu

entry.summary: REDIRECT repairs robot policies that acquired bad habits from small defective segments in mixed-quality teleoperation data, using only episode-level retained/problematic labels to localize the branch point and re-anchor a retained continuation. It achieves recovery using roughly 1% of the full-training sample budget across three randomized ManiSkill-style environments, without frame-level annotations or extra interaction.

entry.title: PatternDex: Learning Interaction Patterns to Guide Reinforcement Learning of Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation of Articulated Objects

author.name: David Minkwan Kim, Runfa Blark Li, Beckham Po-Ju Lee, Nikolay Atanasov, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: PatternDex learns hand-object motion correlations from human demonstrations as token sequences called interaction patterns, then estimates target-robot wrist motions and contact points to guide RL training for bimanual dexterous manipulation of articulated objects. Because guidance is fitted to the target embodiment, the method avoids the embodiment gap that plagues direct demonstration transfer.

entry.title: FreeSpeed: Training-Free Speed Control for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Shilin Shan, Qiheng Wang, Jinghan Yang, Junqiao Fan, Hao Wan, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: FreeSpeed is a training-free post-processing module that adjusts the execution speed of imitation-learned policies at test time, exploiting the observation that directional inconsistency of action chunks reflects task-phase criticality. It modifies action step lengths aggressively only where safe, avoiding out-of-distribution failures from naive time-scaling.

entry.title: Conditional Trajectory Peaks: Single-Pass Multimodal Policies over Action Chunks

author.name: Di Wu, Rongtian Shen, Ping Liu, Xuhua Chen, He Zheng, Lingfeng Zhang, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: CTP is a single-pass multimodal imitation learning framework that jointly predicts complete action-chunk candidates, their probability masses, and trajectory scales, with specialization and cross-chunk consistency mechanisms (DAPS and ETBT) that geometrically align exchangeable candidate sets across replanning cycles. This enables diverse yet temporally consistent executable futures under the same observation. Reported coverage scores suggest improved multimodal behavior coverage.

entry.title: Preference Optimization with Multi-Sample Comparisons

author.name: Chaoqi Wang, Zhuokai Zhao, Chen Zhu, Karthik Abinav Sankararaman, Michal Valko, Xuefei Cao, Zhaorun Chen, Madian Khabsa, Yuxin Chen, Hao Ma, Sinong Wang

entry.summary: The paper extends post-training for LLMs and diffusion models beyond single-sample preference comparisons by proposing multi-sample DPO (mDPO), capturing properties like generative diversity and bias that single-pair comparisons miss. The approach generalizes standard preference optimization to listwise settings. This addresses a real limitation of RLHF/DPO-style post-training pipelines.

entry.title: Training Numerical Intelligence via Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery

author.name: Peter Chen, Wotao Yin

entry.summary: This paper introduces ADSD, a framework that first diagnoses why numerical solvers perform poorly and then uses that diagnosis to discover and package reusable solver skills. It reframes solver self-improvement from trial-and-error code editing into a structured diagnosis-then-repair process for AI-generated scientific code.

entry.title: TCMClinicalReason-Bench: Can Language Models Reason from Pathogenesis to Prescription over Real-World Clinical Cases?

author.name: Jirui Dai, Chenkai Zhang, Yan Jia, Yukai Wang, Ruiyang He, Changyong Luo, Zhi Liu

entry.summary: The authors build TCMClinicalReason-Bench from 2,000 multicenter electronic health record cases to test whether LLMs can perform evidence-grounded traditional Chinese medicine reasoning, tracing from etiology and pathogenesis through syndrome diagnosis to prescription. Seven models, including general-purpose and TCM-specific systems, were evaluated zero-shot with an evidence-constrained rubric, with Qwen3.7-Plus among the evaluated models. The benchmark distinguishes case-grounded reasoning from fluent but unsupported clinical conclusions.

entry.title: Functionally Equivalent or Not? Graph-Grounded Differential Surrogate Execution for Code Equivalence

author.name: Amit Kachroo, Like Hui, Haitao Mao, Yuhao Zhang, Nguyen Vo

entry.summary: FEAgent assesses functional code equivalence by combining typed program-graph evidence with bounded differential surrogate execution, addressing cases where tests, textual similarity, and LLM judgment all fail and direct execution is impossible due to unavailable or unsafe environments. The agent aligns interfaces and behavior-relevant graph anchors before issuing bounded queries over call-flow, control-flow, and data-flow structure. It targets code modernization, patch validation, and code-generation evaluation.

entry.title: CRAFT: An Agentic Spreadsheet Form Filling System with Template Awareness

author.name: Leyao Gu, Yingjie Xiong, Zirui Tang, Jiangtao Zhou, Yeye He, Chunwei Liu, Xuanhe Zhou, Fan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces CRAFT, a template-aware agent framework for spreadsheet form filling that grounds detected errors to specific spreadsheet regions, restores corrupted template state, and performs constrained local repair rather than free-form regeneration. A Rectangle-Aware Slot Grounder proposes writable cells while protected regions and label-slot hints constrain edits.

entry.title: Label Agreement Does Not Measure Authorization

author.name: Amir Sabbaghziarani, Bradley Thomas Baker, Theodore J. LaGrow, Sergey Plis

entry.summary: The authors built an agentic LLM pipeline for label ontology and metadata harmonization on neuroimaging cohorts (COBRE, FBIRN) and audited it, finding healthy aggregate agreement scores hid failures. They show label agreement does not capture whether an agent was entitled to propose a label, whether output was complete enough to act on, or whether labels shifted with evidence, and these properties come apart empirically.

entry.title: Dynamic Routing as a New Dimension for Test-time Versatility of LLMs

author.name: Michal \v{S}tef\'anik, Marek Kadl\v{c}\'ik, Josef Kucha\v{r}, Michal Spiegel

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether dynamic routing programs that execute or iterate subsets of a model's layers can serve as a second axis of test-time adaptation beyond chain-of-thought token spending, identified from only 3-10 demonstrations via a training-free, transferable strategy. The findings clarify when program selection strategies transfer across models and tasks without gradient updates.

entry.title: BACAM: Behavior-Aware Continual Agent Merging for Multi-Turn Interaction

author.name: Shuaitong Li, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Xizhe Zheng, Yifan Xu, Jianhao Huang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: BACAM studies continual model merging, integrating incoming expert agents sequentially without retaining previously merged experts, while matching behavior on interaction trajectories rather than just parameter or feature alignment. It learns parameter-wise merging gates from candidate-generated trajectories using expert-guided behavioral supervision to avoid disrupting previously integrated behavior.

entry.title: LexiHorizon: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Deep Search

author.name: Zhiqing Nong, Liang Wen, Chao-Hsuan Liu

entry.summary: LexiHorizon tackles RL training of deep search agents when retrieval is sensitive to query formulation, requiring repeated query reformulation and long-horizon trajectories with expanding retrieved content. It proposes methods to stabilize policy training for sustained long-horizon query exploration under unstable retrieval.

entry.title: CASE: Cost-Aware Stopping for Efficient Long-Video Agents

author.name: Yiming Du, Chenghao Liu, Zhiyuan Liu, Fangxing Zheng, Zhao Wang, Junnan Nie, Songfang Huang

entry.summary: CASE is a plug-in termination framework for long-video agents that frames the question of when enough evidence has been gathered as policy-conditioned sequential stopping. It combines auxiliary evidence assessment with the host agent's execution state, learns a decision gap with a lightweight Ridge regressor trained on cost-aware targets from native trajectories, and produces stop-or-continue decisions.

entry.title: SkillGATE: Gate-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search for Skill Retrieval

author.name: Rongchen Zhao, Yu Chen, Yanming Yang, Shijia Xu, Juyuan Wang, Jin Xu, Zibin Zheng, Jingping Liu

entry.summary: SkillGATE formulates skill retrieval from large external skill libraries as an adaptive information-foraging process and solves it with a graph-guided hierarchy and Gate-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search. The approach coordinates region-level navigation with skill-level selection, resisting semantic distractors and early routing errors.

entry.title: How Should a Prompt Optimizer Spend a Tight Budget? BudgetAPO with Noise-Adaptive Evaluation

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Zhichao Wang, Huanyu Yan, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: This paper introduces BudgetAPO, a single-stage automatic prompt optimizer designed for settings where subject-model API calls are expensive and rate-limited. It uses a noise-adaptive rule to size evaluation minibatches per task and a greedy allocation policy across candidates, addressing failure modes of existing methods like GEPA and OPRO that assume hundreds to thousands of calls.

entry.title: Mining Agent Skills from Production Traces

author.name: Yue Ran Kang, Colton Mikolajczyk, Chhaya Methani, Hazel Mak, Sahil Bhatnagar, Susheel Suresh, Alejandro Gutierrez Munoz

entry.summary: This controlled study examines how trace sampling, access to success/failure labels, and skill form (ordered workflows versus alternatives) affect downstream agent performance when skills are mined from execution traces. Holding the pipeline fixed, it compares six combinations of mining evidence and skill form, including the practical setting where success labels are unavailable.

entry.title: MiniCorp: The Last Mile of the AI Agent Firm

author.name: Jingying Zeng, Zhenwei Dai, Jinning Li, Changho Shin, Dylan Zhang, Yuxuan Lu, Qi He, Dakuo Wang, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: MiniCorp is an office simulator in which multiple agents collectively run a demonstration e-commerce company, coupling an external world of customers, competitors, and market dynamics with an internal world of agents observing, discussing, and acting. It is designed to generate longitudinal enterprise data at scale to train and study self-running organizational agents where historical archives are incomplete or counterfactual-free.

entry.title: RollPlace: Improving Macro Placement via Monte Carlo Rollout Search

author.name: Qi Zhou, Guojun Liu, Guangzhi Qi, Ming Lu, Jiechu Liu, Zhongli Liu, Jianqun Yang, Xingji Li

entry.summary: RollPlace is a two-stage framework for macro placement in chip design that first generates initial layouts via ML or heuristics, then refines them by selectively adjusting specific macros using Monte Carlo rollout search. This moves beyond single-shot generation common in prior RL-based EDA work, addressing the need for post-hoc refinement.

entry.title: The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance

author.name: Stefan B\"uhler, David Exler, Markus Reischl, Mark Schutera

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open two-probe benchmark that places language models on a spectrum between always complying with instructions and always resisting them. An active probe measures exploitability (accepting a lower payoff when told to act) and a passive probe measures stoppability (giving up a higher payoff when told to wait), combining into a compliance index kappa. Applied to twelve models, including Claude, it reveals that most models justify compliance by pointing to the instruction itself.

entry.title: Reward-DAgger: Robot-Gated Interactive Imitation Learning with General-Purpose Progress-Based Reward Models

author.name: Ryan Li, Yigit Korkmaz, Erdem B{\i}y{\i}k

entry.summary: Reward-DAgger is an interactive imitation learning framework in which a general-purpose progress-based reward model gates when human intervention is needed during robot deployment. Unlike prior runtime monitoring methods that require task- and policy-specific training or tuning, the approach is architecture-agnostic and detects failures and recovery behaviors across tasks using dense progress signals. This reduces the overhead of iteratively improving generalist robot policies in unseen environments.

entry.title: Risk-Calibrated Proposal Transport for Finite-Particle Diffusion Steering

author.name: Ziseok Lee, Jaehyeon Kim, Seungwon Kim, Seunghyun Moon, Haneul Choi, Wooyeol Lee, Donghyun Koh, Minhyeong Lee, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: This theoretical and methodological paper addresses inference-time steering of diffusion models via Feynman-Kac-corrected sequential Monte Carlo, showing that variance-controlling guidance (VCG) proposals, while optimal in the population limit, can catastrophically increase residual risk with finite particle counts and accelerate particle collapse. The authors propose a risk-calibrated proposal transport method that fixes these finite-particle failure modes. The work matters because SMC-based steering is a key approach for combining pretrained diffusion experts or reward models without retraining.

entry.title: GlitchPatch: Repairing Glitch Tokens in Frozen Language Models via Local Retokenization

author.name: Kunsheng Tang, Peigui Qi, Yide Song, Peijun Huang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: GlitchPatch repairs glitch tokens, anomalous vocabulary entries causing LLM output failures, without model-internals access by optimizing input tokenization. An empirical study of BPE merge-rule deletion reveals trade-offs between fixing glitch failures and collateral damage to normal tokens sharing merge nodes, motivating a local retokenization repair approach for frozen checkpoints.

entry.title: Localization Lens for Improving Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hasan Farooq, Murtaza Taj, Mehwish Nasim, Arif Mahmood

entry.summary: Proposes a localization-aware enhancement for medical vision-language models, adding expert-validated anatomical and positional representations at the data, architecture, and alignment levels, with pixel shuffle used to refine spatial information. Targets the known weakness of Med-VLMs in understanding anatomy and spatial positioning.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Solar Image Synthesis: Adapting the Surya Foundation Model from He I 10830 {\AA} to EUV Translation and Coronal Hole Segmentation

author.name: Marco Marena, Andr\'es Mu\~noz Jaramillo, Qin Li, Haodi Jiang, Jinghao Cao, Wen He, Ziyang Zhang, Chenxi Yuan, Chao Wang, Haimin Wang, Bo Shen

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Surya solar foundation model to translate historical helium-10830 Angstrom solar observations into modern extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) images (SDO/AIA 94, 193, and 304 Angstrom) and to segment coronal holes. Using parameter-efficient techniques such as a convolutional input adapter, low-rank backbone updates, and dedicated output decoders trained on temporally paired, registered observations, the approach extends solar morphology research to the pre-EUV observational record, which matters for space weather history and long-term solar cycle studies.

entry.title: TSAE: Structured Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Time-Series Forecasting Models

author.name: Baoxi Liu, Yi Xie
