entry.summary: TSAE is a structured sparse autoencoder that decomposes hidden states of time-series forecasting models into individually inspectable features, organizing cross-variable structure via shared and variable-routed private dictionaries and separating feature detection from temporal continuity constraints. It goes beyond input attribution by exposing internal features.

entry.title: Operational Abstractions of Neural Network Concepts via Topological Representations

author.name: Mathieu Pont, Christoph Garth

entry.summary: The paper introduces Topological Concept Representations (TCR), a post-hoc abstraction that jointly characterizes concepts in a learned representation and their relationships by building an intermediate concept space from recoverability and interaction scores and encoding its organization via topology. Concept interventions are expressed as edits to this abstraction and propagated back to the underlying network. This generalizes beyond interventions specific to particular editing methods.

entry.title: AraYoungVoices: A Diverse L1/L2 Corpus of Arabic Child and Adolescent Speech

author.name: Shammur Absar Chowdhury, Zien Sheikh Ali, Houssam Eddine-Othman Lachemat, Hamdy Mubarak

entry.summary: This paper introduces AraYoungVoices, a 151.72-hour Arabic read-speech corpus with 286 speakers aged 7-18, split into AraKids and AraTeens subsets covering native (L1) speakers from four major Arabic dialect regions and second-language (L2) speakers from diverse linguistic backgrounds. The authors benchmark four pretrained ASR models under zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, including unseen-speaker evaluation protocols, to quantify performance gaps on child, adolescent, and L2 speech.

entry.title: Discrete Action Matching: Learning Stochastic Dynamics from Samples via State Graphs

author.name: Mikhail Persiianov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: Discrete Action Matching (DAM) extends Action Matching to finite-state settings using discrete Wasserstein geometry, deriving an action-minimization objective for the canonical minimum-kinetic-energy current given a marginal path. The key technical observation is that density dependence of the discrete action reduces to neighboring density ratios, which DAM estimates before learning an action potential. The learned fields also define a graph-supported Markov sampler.

entry.title: EMG-GPT: Predictive Pretraining on Residual-Quantized EMG Tokens for Hand Pose Estimation

author.name: Ettore Magni, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias, Stefanos Zafeiriou, Konstantinos Barmpas

entry.summary: EMG-GPT is a causal transformer that performs self-supervised pretraining on discrete surface electromyography tokens from a frozen residual vector quantization tokenizer, learning temporal dynamics via depth-autoregressive future-code prediction. The model achieves competitive results on hand-pose regression and tracking, showing that EMG-only pretraining yields transferable representations.

entry.title: Optimal Control with Learned Critics under Unmodeled State Dependencies

author.name: Philipp Schoch, Markus Ryll

entry.summary: The paper presents a learning-based MPC framework that augments a nominal analytical model with a residual dynamics network for unmodeled state-dependent effects such as contacts, and uses learned critics to compensate for finite-horizon myopia. This combines the structure and data efficiency of model-based planning with learned components, reducing the interaction data demands of pure model-free RL.

entry.title: Does Explainability Survive Data Drift?

author.name: Samuel Ozechi

entry.summary: This paper studies whether explanation fidelity degrades under data drift, even when the feature-target relationship remains stable, and whether pre-drift explanations remain faithful after a model is replaced. It addresses a gap in ML governance where performance is monitored routinely but explanations are not, despite being required in regulated domains like healthcare and finance.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing via Path-based Inference

author.name: Eshant English, Wei-Cheng Lai, Yanfeng Yang, Kenji Fukumizu, Taiji Suzuki, Christoph Lippert

entry.summary: Develops a statistical two-sample test that treats the generative dynamics of deep models as objects of inference, using stochastic interpolants to connect two distributions through a shared Gaussian bottleneck. The authors prove a characterization of the null hypothesis via reflection symmetry of the path's denoiser/velocity fields at a single noise level. This is theoretically deep work bridging generative modeling and hypothesis testing.

entry.title: Selecting Long-Horizon Trajectories for Reliable and Efficient Terminal-Agent Training

author.name: Cuong Dang, Hoang Anh Just, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Studies the supervision horizon (how many trajectory tokens to keep when imitating teacher trajectories) for training terminal agents, finding reliability improves then saturates: a 12K-token horizon beats 16K on Terminal-Bench while using 30% less training time. Horizon length also shapes behavior, from premature termination to over-persistence, analyzed via a bias-complexity bound. A practical training insight for agent imitation learning.

entry.title: TasteRoute: Personalized Routing for Video Generation

author.name: Zhi Rui Tam, Chao-Chung Wu, Sin-Han Yang, Peyton Ku, Brendan Kuang, Tzu-Ting Hsieh, Min-Fang Hsu, Fang-Ling Tsai, Yun-Nung Chen, Wei-Chiu Ma, Chieh-Yen Lin

entry.summary: TasteRoute is a personalized router for video generation that selects among multiple text-to-video and image-to-video models based on the request, individual user preferences, and generation budget. The key motivation is an empirical finding that human annotators agree with a consensus oracle on their favorite video only 34-55% of the time, implying routing should be preference-aware rather than quality-based. The system is competitive with strong baselines on preference routing while lowering average generation cost.

entry.title: ROT: Rotating Hidden States towards Contextual Vectors for Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs

author.name: Yijing Du, Xiangcheng Zhan, Shuo Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies object hallucination in large vision-language models and finds that hallucinated tokens show anomalous contextual deviation in intermediate layers, with lower similarity to both textual and visual contexts. Building on this, it proposes ROT, a training-free, layer-specific method that rotates hidden states toward contextual vectors to mitigate hallucination. This offers a lightweight alternative to attention-manipulation interventions.

entry.title: Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? Localizing the Origins of Silent Failures in Agentic Vulnerability Repair

author.name: Wenji Bai, Muhammad Waseem, Zeeshan Rasheed, Jaakko Peltonen, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: The paper proposes SAGE, a trace-based method that localizes the earliest point where an LLM agent repairing security vulnerabilities diverges from the task's security intent, even for silent failures that pass functional checks. It combines security-reasoning assessment with reconstructed code history, addressing a gap in existing failure attribution methods. This supports targeted safeguards for agentic coding workflows.

entry.title: SoK: Semantic Decision Engines in Network Control Loops

author.name: Delong Li, Chen Li, Xu Wang, Haochen Gong, Rui Lang, Guangsheng Yu

entry.summary: This systematization-of-knowledge paper surveys 139 families of semantic decision engines (e.g., learned/LLM-based decision systems like Jev) used in network control loops, classifying them by decision interface, execution path, and verification ownership. It finds a striking gap: while 50 families claim suitability for control loops or time budgets, only four support the claim with matched measurements, and only four report deadline attainment overall. The authors show via bounded tests that these unverified gaps can reverse admission verdicts, highlighting a real reliability problem for deploying semantic decision engines in latency-sensitive network control.

entry.title: Symmetry and AI-assisted discovery of magic-state factories

author.name: Shubham P. Jain, Adam Wills, Shraddha Singh

entry.summary: This paper develops symmetry-restricted and AI-assisted search methods for discovering magic-state distillation circuits in fault-tolerant quantum computing, using a unified binary-matrix formulation covering both triorthogonal codes and direct circuit searches. It shows that distance-at-least-three is equivalent to pairwise-distinct nonzero syndromes, making previously intractable search regimes tractable. This matters because magic-state factories dominate the resource cost of quantum computing.

entry.title: One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline

author.name: Shih-Chen Tseng, Chih-Hsuan Chen, Ryan Yang, Hsi-An Chen, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: Formulates aspect-ratio-adaptive flowchart relayout as a new task: given a raster flowchart and a target aspect ratio, produce a structurally faithful, editable layout for canvases from paper columns to social media previews. The proposed agentic pipeline avoids characteristic failures of image-to-image stretching, agentic text-to-image hallucination, and parse-then-render edge mis-routing.

entry.title: Synthesizing Physics Formulae with Transformers

author.name: Shuwei Wang, Vadim Bulitko, Michael Youngblood, Ramon Lawrence, William Yeoh, Shinichi Nakagawa, Matthew R. G. Brown, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Addresses overfitting in transformer-based symbolic regression, where generated formulae fit training data but fail to extrapolate to unseen input ranges, by shaping the distribution of training formulae. The authors show substantially improved extrapolation and further gains from fine-tuning on noise-corrupted data.

entry.title: Articulatory Entrainment and Coordination Complexity in Spontaneous Autistic and Non-autistic Dialogue

author.name: Thanushi Withanage, Carol Espy-Wilson, Elizabeth Redcay, Desi Jones, Noah Sasson

entry.summary: Introduces a speaker-independent framework using acoustic-to-articulatory inversion and coordination complexity metrics to quantify articulatory entrainment in spontaneous conversations between autistic and non-autistic adults. It finds non-autistic dyads increase coordination complexity and entrainment over time while autistic dyads show moderate effects. This matters for accessibility and speech AI research on atypical interaction patterns.

entry.title: CEENs: Causality-enforced evolutional networks for solving time-dependent partial differential equations

author.name: Jeahan Jung, Heechang Kim, Hyomin Shin, Minseok Choi

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses long-time integration failure of PINNs as a temporal causality violation, where networks satisfy governing equations at later times before learning initial conditions. It proposes causality-enforced evolutional networks that split the time domain into nonoverlapping subintervals with dedicated networks, mimicking classical time-stepping schemes. This addresses a well-known and persistent PINN weakness.

entry.title: Path Laplacian Encodings for Directed Graphs

author.name: Lydia Mezrag, Semih Cant\"urk, Michael Perlmutter, Bastian Rieck, Guy Wolf

entry.summary: PathLapPE introduces spectral positional encodings for directed graphs derived from the path Laplacian, providing node- and edge-level features that capture directional higher-order structure and plug into standard graph learning architectures. This addresses the common limitation of symmetrized representations that discard asymmetric interactions in citation networks, web graphs, and flow networks. Consistent empirical gains are shown on node- and graph-level benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Discriminative Geometry for Drifting Models

author.name: Doudou Zhang, Wenwen Hou, Yilin Chen, Qi Chen

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why drifting models (which move iterative distribution refinement from inference to training) perform poorly with pixel-space representations but well with pretrained feature spaces. The authors trace the gap to the discriminative geometry of the representation and its effect on kernel density estimation weighting, and propose persistent representation learning that continuously adapts the representation as the generator trains.

entry.title: Prompt Dominance and Asymmetric Verifier Costs: Empirical Ablations of GRPO at 1B Scale on GSM8K

author.name: Yi Hou

entry.summary: This paper provides controlled ablations of GRPO reinforcement learning at 1B scale, training OLMo-2-0425-1B on GSM8K with a from-scratch implementation. It finds that prompt choice is the first-order factor (zero-shot prompts leave the base model producing degenerate outputs with almost no gradient signal, while 3-shot prompts enable learning at 18.3%), that estimator variants like Dr. GRPO fall within seed noise at this scale, and it separately measures how degraded verifier quality affects both training rewards and test-time selection.

entry.title: Revealing After Overwriting: An Exponential POMDP OPE Lower Bound under History-Dependent Logging

author.name: Youyu Luo, Pengzhan Zhou, Zhida Qin, Jia Wang, Zuotao Fu, Yu Liu, Chao Chen

entry.summary: The paper constructs POMDPs where off-policy evaluation under history-dependent logging requires exponentially many samples even when overlap, coverage, and observation-only revealing are bounded. The constructions show logger memory makes states distinguishable while target-relevant evidence is erased, forcing exponential sample complexity for horizons H at least 3.

entry.title: Robust Ensemble Guidance for Scientific Inverse Problems

author.name: Zixiang Li, Wei Wang, Yunchao Wei, Yao Zhao, Yue Song

entry.summary: REG improves ensemble guidance for diffusion-based inverse problems by weighting observations using ensemble predictive spread and adaptively clipping standardized residuals, preventing high-spread or extreme-residual observations from dominating corrections. Both operations reuse existing particles, adding no extra denoiser or forward-model evaluations.

entry.title: Bellman-Centric Learning: Near-Optimal Regret for Linear Bandits with Memory

author.name: Jingyuan Liu, Huiwen Jia

entry.summary: Studies linear bandits with memory, where past actions induce endogenous nonstationarity, and develops RSM-LinUCB, a Bellman-centric algorithm that learns like a bandit and plans like RL. It proves a high-probability regret bound separating memory-induced error from reward estimation error, achieving near-optimality in this setting.

entry.title: Collaborative Personalized Preference Alignment for LLMs under Data Deficiency

author.name: Liyan Yang, Yige Yuan, Zhiqin Yang

entry.summary: This paper addresses personalizing LLM responses to heterogeneous user preferences when user-specific feedback is scarce. The authors identify gradient conflicts, both across users and within each user, as a key obstacle to learning shared aligner initializations for few-shot adaptation. They propose an approximate Pareto-optimality-based approach to collaboratively learn initializations that support adaptation to diverse preference profiles.

entry.title: Ultrasound Operator Guidance Using World Modeling and Retrieval Based Action Planning

author.name: Noortje I. P. Schueler, Hans van Gorp, Ruud J. G. van Sloun

entry.summary: The authors formulate ultrasound probe guidance as multi-step planning within a learned world model, using a V-JEPA 2.1 backbone to encode probe views into a latent space where anatomically related views are close together. A retrieval mechanism over a database of reference latent states then suggests actions to guide less-trained operators toward a target view.

entry.title: Lossy Compression of PDE Training Inputs: Field Reconstruction Error Does Not Order the Cost to a Trained Operator

author.name: Huy Hoang Le

entry.summary: This paper studies how lossy compression of operator-learning benchmark data affects downstream trained operator accuracy, showing theoretically and empirically that reconstruction error does not determine the degradation of the trained model. The key insight is that solution operators attenuate input perturbations, and the fraction of perturbation transmitted varies by more than two orders of magnitude across equations, consistent with their smoothing behavior. This matters for the increasingly terabyte-scale PDE benchmark ecosystem where storage costs drive compression decisions.

entry.title: Empirical Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Kaede Shiohara

entry.summary: EVA is a generative framework for continuous-valued sequences that keeps the VAE evidence lower bound but learns autoregressive latent priors empirically from training data, requiring only a single additional linear layer. Replacing the standard-Gaussian prior constraint alleviates the prior-posterior latent gap and enables high-fidelity ancestral sampling for sequential generation. Experiments on image and sound synthesis show strong results.

entry.title: Separators Make Carry Propagation Learnable:The Geometry of Latent Carry in a Multiplication Transformer

author.name: Sama Satariyan (SCAI), Raphael Cousin (SCAI), G{\'e}rard Biau (LPSM, IUF, MEGAVOLT)

entry.summary: Training small Llama-style transformers from scratch on 4x4 multiplication without chain of thought, the authors show that inserting a space token between digits raises exact-match accuracy from 1% to 89%. Interpretability analysis reveals output digits are learned in carry-chain order and the carry-in is encoded as an angle on a ring in the residual stream. This provides a mechanistic account of how tokenization formatting gates arithmetic capability in transformers.

entry.title: Improved Convergence of Large Stepsize Gradient Descent for Logistic Regression

author.name: Xiaochuan Gong, Ang Li

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that gradient descent with a large constant stepsize (eta = 1/epsilon) reaches loss epsilon on linearly separable logistic regression in polylogarithmic steps in arbitrary dimension, substantially improving prior O(1/sqrt(epsilon)) bounds that had only been tightened for 2D data. The proof hinges on better bounding the transition time from the oscillatory phase to the stable, monotonically decreasing phase of training.

entry.title: Broaden Your Views for Self-Supervised Video Learning

author.name: Adri\`a Recasens, Pauline Luc, Jean-Baptiste Alayrac, Luyu Wang, Ross Hemsley, Florian Strub, Corentin Tallec, Mateusz Malinowski, Viorica Patraucean, Florent Altch\'e, Michal Valko, Jean-Bastien Grill, A\"aron van den Oord, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: BraVe is a self-supervised video learning framework that exploits time by giving one view a narrow temporal window and the other broad access to the video, forcing generalization from the narrow view to overall content, and processing the views with different backbones of varying capacity. It was a notable advance in video self-supervision from a DeepMind/Oxford team including Andrew Zisserman and Aaron van den Oord.

entry.title: StepCAD: Mesh-to-CAD Code Generation via LLM Policy and Geometry-Guided Search

author.name: Ghadi Nehme, Faez Ahmed

entry.summary: StepCAD converts 3D meshes into executable CAD programs by combining a state-conditioned policy that predicts construction actions with IoU-guided tree search that refines programs through local edits. This addresses limitations of single-pass methods that rely mostly on sketch-extrude representations and lack error-correction opportunities. The generative optimization framing matters for engineering design workflows and CAD reconstruction more broadly.

entry.title: Latent Score-Based Bayesian Cram\'er-Rao Bound Estimation for High-Dimensional Imaging Systems

author.name: Evan Scope Crafts, Thomas Wynn, Seonyeong Park, Mark Anastasio, Umberto Villa

entry.summary: This paper introduces a data-driven method for estimating the Bayesian Cramer-Rao bound in high-dimensional imaging inverse problems where prior distributions are analytically intractable. The approach reformulates the problem in the latent space of a pre-trained variational autoencoder, using score-based estimation to compute the Bayesian Fisher information matrix at manageable dimensionality before mapping results back to the original image space. This provides a practical tool for quantifying fundamental performance limits in computational imaging tasks that were previously intractable.

entry.title: Asking the Crowd the Right Question: Bias-Cancelling Weights for Federated Learning

author.name: Ilya Kuruzov, Dmitrii Vishovan, Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: The paper treats the weighting of client risks in federated learning as a wisdom-of-crowds problem, showing that optimal weights are inversely proportional to client error energies and that excess risk scales with aggregate bias energy. It also characterizes fundamental identifiability limits of recovering the shared truth from biased clients.

entry.title: Locality Sensitive Hashing for p-Exponential Kernels with Applications to Density Estimation

author.name: Barak Gorodissky, Tal Wagner

entry.summary: The paper proves that the p-exponential kernel exp(-||x-y||_p) is LSHable for all 1 < p <= 2, extending prior knowledge beyond p = 1, via a new mosaic LSH scheme based on a Poisson hyperplane process with l1-biased p-stable vectors. This yields new efficient density estimation methods for these kernels.

entry.title: Transferable Adversarial Robustness for Speech Foundation Models via Hierarchical Stabilization

author.name: Aref Mousavi, Shahab Sherafat, Kiarash Kiani Feriz, Amirparsa Safari, Raoof Zare Moayedi, Mohammad Hossein Rohban, Mohammad Sabokrou

entry.summary: This work shows that adversarial robustness for frozen speech foundation models can be learned once, before downstream tasks are known, by stabilizing representations across hidden layers rather than performing adversarial fine-tuning per task. The method couples representation stability with decision-boundary margin analysis and preserves adaptation efficiency. It matters because it decouples robustness certification from costly per-task adversarial training.

entry.title: An evolutionary origin of collective decision making in humans and machines

author.name: Guocheng Wang, Qi Su, Joshua B. Plotkin

entry.summary: This theoretical work extends the study of evolving collective intelligence to non-linear decision tasks and multi-layer voting institutions, such as districts electing representatives, rather than simple single-layer averaging. It identifies conditions under which uninformed individuals evolve collective intelligence through social learning in these richer structures. The framework bridges evolutionary theory, collective decision making, and potential machine-learning system design.

entry.title: Combining Improvements in Uplink AI-RAN

author.name: Petteri Kela, Dani Korpi, Mikko Honkala

entry.summary: The paper evaluates multiple uplink AI features for 6G radio access networks operating together, using an integrated link-level and system-level simulator with a mirrored data pipeline to serve deep-learning MIMO receivers under realistic schedulers. Prior AI physical-layer features were mostly assessed in isolation. This provides the first system-level picture of their joint behavior in multi-cell, multi-user deployments.

entry.title: Gaussian Universality and Its Breakdown in Tensor-Network Machine Learning

author.name: Shi-Tuan Wang, Zidu Liu, Li-Wei Yu

entry.summary: Using a moment-based analytical approach, the paper identifies precise conditions for when Gaussian-process universality holds and fails in tensor-network learning models, focusing on matrix product states. In the large bond-dimension limit, models converge to Gaussian processes with explicit finite-size deviation bounds, while in the large physical-dimension limit this universality breaks down differently for local versus global observables. This clarifies the theoretical limits of Gaussian approximations for structured architectures.

entry.title: NeuroCBIR: A Fast and Accurate Image Retrieval System for Whole-Brain and Region-Specific MRI

author.name: Felix Nieto-del-Amor, Jingru Fu, J. -Sebastian Muehlboeck, Eric Westman, Daniel Ferreira, Rodrigo Moreno

entry.summary: This paper introduces NeuroCBIR, a content-based image retrieval framework for 3D T1-weighted brain MRI that supports both whole-brain and region-specific queries across 103 cortical and subcortical regions. It uses a variational autoencoder with contrastive learning to produce scan-specific embeddings, enabling fast retrieval of structurally similar scans for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. The work addresses the scalability and generalizability limitations of prior neuroimaging retrieval methods.

entry.title: Singular parameters and missing limits in neural PDE solvers

author.name: Daniel Fern\'andez

entry.summary: The paper shows that neural PDE solvers can approach an accurate solution while their parameters diverge, so the limiting solution may have no finite representation in the chosen model class. For translated-kernel models, the authors characterize the missing functions, recover them by adding kernel derivatives, and prove this completion makes the best approximation attainable.

entry.title: Can LLMs Separate Pasted Artifacts from User Speech? Absorption at Unmarked Prompt Seams

author.name: Sugam Panthi, Muhaiminul Yeamin, Rabab Abdelfattah

entry.summary: This paper introduces SEAM, a 300-example benchmark studying absorption: when an LLM treats a user comment typed after pasted text as part of the pasted content during editing tasks. It highlights an untested failure mode distinct from instruction-data separation, relevant to everyday prompt composition and indirectly to prompt-injection-adjacent robustness. A novel and practically relevant robustness study.

entry.title: Evidence and Intervention: A Coupled Active-Inference Extension of Rational Speech Act Models

author.name: Yonghyeon Gwon, Elliot Murphy, Chun Kee Chung

entry.summary: This paper extends Rational Speech Act (RSA) models of pragmatics by coupling them with active inference: the listener models the speaker's expected free energy within its own variational free energy, so each utterance functions both as evidence about the partner and as an intervention on them. This allows the model to separate distinct update targets (what the listener infers versus how the listener's beliefs are causally changed) that standard one-shot RSA collapses together. The work matters because it bridges formal pragmatics, Bayesian theories of mind, and active inference in a way that could improve computational models of dialogue.

entry.title: From Overloaded to Guaranteed: High-Throughput Multi-SLO Enforcement for LoRA-Assisted On-Premise LLM Deployment

author.name: Zeshen Zhang, Han Zhao, Weihao Cui, Quan Chen, Yu Liu, Yongjun Deng, Jing Yang, Jiuchen Shi, Chen Chen, Youmin Chen, Yu Feng, Minyi Guo

entry.summary: HALO is a scheduler for serving multiple LoRA-adapted LLM services on resource-constrained on-premise servers, introducing spatial multiplexing that overlaps base and LoRA computation plus improved batching to enforce heterogeneous SLOs. It targets privacy-sensitive deployments in hospitals and government where cloud service is undesirable. Solid systems contribution to LLM serving.

entry.title: InstMoE: Adaptive Multimodal Routing with Specialized Experts

author.name: Guimin Hu, Xiang He, Yingjian Li, Zheng Lian, Boyan Xu, Ruichu Cai

entry.summary: InstMoE proposes an adaptive mixture-of-experts routing framework for multimodal learning that dynamically routes inputs to specialized unimodal and cross-modal experts, adapting information pathways to input characteristics. To prevent routing from being misled by irrelevant modality-specific variations, it adds a Contrastive Semantic Alignment module that groups semantically similar inputs. This addresses the heterogeneity of multimodal inputs at the routing level rather than just the modality level.

entry.title: Breaking the Tie: A Cluster-Aware Routing Framework for Large Language Models

author.name: Yao Lu, Zhaiyuan Ji, Yaxin Gao, Zeyu Wang, Zhe Tang, Jiaheng Wei, Zhaowei Zhu, Shanqing Yu, Qi Xuan

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses LLM routing, the problem of dynamically assigning user queries to the best model in a pool of candidates. The authors identify a failure mode they call routing noise: when multiple models can correctly answer the same query, standard classification-style routers are misled, which can cause routing collapse. They propose a cluster-aware routing framework that accounts for overlapping model capabilities when deciding where to send queries.

entry.title: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks

author.name: Jiuheng Wan, Runze Li, Chen Chen, Tingyuan Hu, Daiyang Yu, Yimin Jing, Taolin Zhang, Richang Hong

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces MedPrune, a multi-agent collaboration framework for medical visual question answering that models the diagnostic process as a heterogeneous communication graph of specialist agents. It dynamically prunes redundant nodes and edges from the communication topology to improve reasoning quality while cutting token and computational costs. The work matters because multi-agent medical AI systems are often impractical due to excessive communication overhead, and topology pruning offers a path to deploying them efficiently.

entry.title: Beyond Token Accuracy: Prioritizing What Matters for Visual Reconstruction

author.name: Zhicheng Liu, Zhouxiang Zhao, Chenliang Wu, Zhaohui Yang, Zhaoyang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes AdapToC, an adaptive visual-token communication framework for multimodal systems that jointly considers image content, channel conditions, and communication budgets. Instead of static token-selection policies, it performs instance-wise resource allocation and optimizes directly for image reconstruction quality rather than token-level accuracy.

entry.title: Sparse-GS2Mesh: 3D Gaussian Splatting Guided by Novel Stereo Views and 2DGS for Sparse View Surface Reconstruction}

author.name: Younghyun Noh, Minje Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: This computer vision paper introduces Sparse-GS2Mesh, a stereo-aware framework for surface reconstruction from sparse-view images. It addresses a known weakness of 3D Gaussian Splatting in sparse-view regimes — incomplete geometry due to missing depth supervision — by initializing 3DGS with epipolar depth priors and leveraging novel stereo views plus 2D Gaussian Splatting for surface extraction. This matters because sparse-view reconstruction is a common practical constraint in robotics, AR/VR, and scanning, where dense multi-camera capture is unavailable.

entry.title: TAME:Topology-Aware Text-Driven Motion Editing across Heterogeneous Humanoid Skeletons

author.name: Qichen Zheng, Siyuan Yang, Chong Wang, Jun Liu, Shijian Lu, Alex Kot, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: TAME is a flow-matching transformer for text-driven motion editing that works across humanoid skeletons of differing joint counts and hierarchies, representing motion as per-joint, per-frame tokens. Skeletal attention follows each character's hierarchy, replacing fully connected attention with topology-aware interactions.

entry.title: Decouple, Purify and Unite: Semantic-Structural Prototype Learning for Federated Medical Segmentation

author.name: Xingyue Zhao, Wenke Huang, Linghao Zhuang, Yanzhou Su, Zhifeng Wang, Haoyu Zhao, Mengfan Li, Junjun He, Tao Tan, Dakai Jin, Le Lu, Mang Ye, Qiang Yang, Ming Feng

entry.summary: FedBCS+ tackles feature heterogeneity in federated learning for medical image segmentation via decoupled contextual alignment and style-purified aggregation, using frequency-domain operations and multi-level semantic-structural prototypes. It addresses incomplete contextual representation and layerwise style and aggregation biases in prototype-based federated methods.

entry.title: LightVLN: Efficient Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation with Compact Memory and History-Guided Local Aggregation

author.name: Yiming Zhao, Tianshun Li, Jingle He, Ruonan Chai, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: LightVLN is a lightweight aerial vision-and-language navigation framework pairing a compact 0.5B language backbone with efficient representations of historical and current observations, compressing each historical frame into a single token using features already computed by the policy. History- and instruction-conditioned local aggregation supports long-horizon navigation on UAVs. The design targets onboard deployment where large backbones and dense visual histories are impractical.

entry.title: Construction and Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Near-Real-Time Fire Detection from MTG FCI Imagery

author.name: Asaf Vanunu, Boaz Nadler, Arnon Karnieli

entry.summary: The study builds and evaluates ML models for near-real-time wildfire detection from the new MTG FCI geostationary satellite imagery at 1-km and 2-km resolutions, comparing against threshold-based operational algorithms using VIIRS fire references across Europe, Africa, and the Middle East. The 1-km models substantially outperform both 2-km variants and operational baselines, with F1 gains up to 0.36 and better detection of small fires. This is significant for operational wildfire monitoring and disaster response.

entry.title: ArticuTable: Generating Instance-Level Interactive Rigid-Articulated 3D Tabletop Scenes from a Single Image

author.name: Kai Lv, Yibo Yin, Lijun Guo, Heng Fan, Kaihao Zhang, Xingping Dong

entry.summary: This paper introduces ArticuTable, a framework that reconstructs 3D tabletop scenes from a single image with two key capabilities: objects are represented with executable part-level articulation rather than as monolithic rigid bodies, and the recovered scene layout stays consistent with the input viewpoint. This enables embodied agents to interact with reconstructed environments at the level of individual movable parts, going beyond whole-object manipulation.

entry.title: SteadySplats: Resampling of Low-Variance Gaussians for High-Fidelity Stochastic Rendering

author.name: Felix Windisch, Thomas K\"ohler, Lukas Radl, Chris Wyman, Georgios Kopanas, Bernhard Kerb, Markus Steinberger

entry.summary: SteadySplats makes stochastic order-independent transparency practical for 3D Gaussian Splatting by attacking visible noise at both representation and synthesis levels: history-based spatial resampling accelerates image convergence, temporal importance resampling maintains coherence under camera motion, and a color regularizer reduces per-ray variance during training. A Vulkan-based renderer demonstrates high-fidelity stochastic rendering. This matters for robust real-time rendering of radiance fields with transparency.

entry.title: Generating the Wild: Individual-Consistent Image-to-Video Generation for Wildlife

author.name: Yuzhuo Li, Di Zhao, Xinyu Zhang, Daniel Wilson, Yun Sing Koh

entry.summary: Proposes an image-to-video generation approach that preserves fine-grained identity cues of individual animals, such as fur texture and stripe boundaries, by focusing on high-frequency information that standard I2V models neglect. This enables synthesis of additional training observations for wildlife re-identification from a single reference image, addressing data scarcity in conservation applications.

entry.title: Patch-based Querying Identifies Structures of Interest in Electron Microscopy

author.name: Niels Vyncke, Nicolas Nadisic, Yvan Saeys, Aleksandra Pi\v{z}urica

entry.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised, patch-based retrieval framework for volume electron microscopy that locates self-similar cellular structures from only a few manual annotations. It addresses the bottleneck where vEM data generation has outpaced human annotation capacity, offering an interactive tool for biomedical image analysis.

entry.title: Multitask Conditional Generative Adversarial Network Enables Automatic Whole Knee Cartilage and Menisci Segmentation and Reliable T1\r{ho} and T2 Quantification Without High-Resolution Morphological Images

author.name: Ahmed Tahseen Minhaz, Richard Lartey, Zhiyuan Zhang, Jeehun Kim, Kunio Nakamura, Mingrui Yang, Jiasen Zhang, Weihong Guo, Naveen Subhas, Carl S. Winalski, Xiaojuan Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a multitask conditional GAN (MT-cGAN) that synthesizes DESS-like MRI images and simultaneously segments knee cartilage and menisci directly from quantitative MRI echo images, eliminating the need for expensive, time-consuming high-resolution 3D DESS scans. Evaluated retrospectively on 508 knee MRI volumes from 361 subjects across three cohorts, the approach supports early osteoarthritis detection via reliable T1rho and T2 quantification. This matters because it could substantially reduce cost and scan time for qMRI-based osteoarthritis screening in clinical practice.

entry.title: GS-Pool: Object-Level Change Detection in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Boaz Keren-Gil, James Gain, Patrick Marais

entry.summary: GS-Pool enables object-level change detection between two independently reconstructed 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes of the same space, handling stochastic training variance and sparse re-scans. It lifts SAM2 masks from photographs onto Gaussians, building an object pool so change decisions are made per 3D object with masks.

entry.title: From communication to computation in neurons-on-a-chip: an in silico study of neurotopomorphic computing

author.name: Michael Taynnan Barros

entry.summary: This study introduces IC-cubed, a framework integrating neuronal dynamics, functional communication, and structural support to characterize how network architecture in neurons-on-a-chip supports computation. Nine architectures were simulated as conductance-based spiking networks and evaluated on frequency decoding, temporal-order discrimination, and fading memory tasks, revealing that predominantly feedforward circuits decode best while sequential chain architectures serve other computational roles.

entry.title: Bi-manual Stabilization of the Cervical Spine for Safe Physical Human-Robot Interaction in Rolling Maneuvers

author.name: Elizabeth Peiros, Moira Bohley, Lucas Yager, Derek Chen, Rebecca Fellbaum, Chris D'Ambrosia, Ananya Rao, Xiao Liang, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: This paper presents algorithms and adaptations enabling bi-manual robots to stabilize a patient's cervical spine during rolling maneuvers, maximizing grip strength within safety bounds while controlling neck rotation. The authors report human-level performance in maintaining target rotational alignments, relevant to battlefield, disaster, and athletic injury response.

entry.title: An End-to-End Framework for Modelling Pneumatic Soft Robots Based on Differentiable Finite Element Methods

author.name: Shaohong Zhong, Yao Yao, Perla Maiolino, Ingmar Posner

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end differentiable finite element method framework for modeling pneumatic soft robots, supporting gradient-based system identification and trajectory optimization. The approach balances accuracy, computational efficiency, and speed where prior soft-robot models made trade-offs.

entry.title: End-to-End Safe Social Navigation via Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning and Probabilistic Perception

author.name: Tommaso Van Der Meer Andrea Garulli, Antonio Giannitrapani, Renato Quartullo, Alberto Vaglio, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: JESSI is a lightweight JAX-based end-to-end RL framework mapping raw LiDAR scans directly to kinematically feasible commands for social navigation, using Dirichlet-parameterized continuous action spaces and deterministic bounding for safety. An attention-based perception module extracts probabilistic human states for interpretable, socially aware behavior without assuming known human positions and velocities.

entry.title: DASH: A da Vinci Adapter for Serial-link and Humanoid Robots as an Accessible Platform for Surgical Robotics Research

author.name: Sara Wickenhiser, Junrong Zhou, Zekai Liang, Lizzie Peiros, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: DASH provides two types of adapters to mount da Vinci Classic and Xi surgical instruments on general-purpose serial-link and humanoid robots without instrument modification, enabling teleoperated laparoscopic research with native robotic actuation. The platform aims to lower cost and infrastructure barriers to surgical robotics research, particularly for lower-resourced facilities.

entry.title: Execution-Aligned Progressive Noise for Consistent Asynchronous Replanning in Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Di Wu, Ping Liu, Xuhua Chen, He Zheng, Lingfeng Zhang, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes EAPN, a method that structures stochastic noise across and within action chunks for generative robot policies, aligning a shared noise trajectory with actual execution displacement so that asynchronous replanning remains consistent instead of mode-switching. Aligned stochastic history is combined with committed action context to condition subsequent chunk generation. This addresses a practical failure mode of diffusion-style policies deployed in real-time control loops.

entry.title: Tactile Perception through Fluid-Solid Interaction

author.name: Arman Goshtasbi, Minke Berghuis, Aida Parvaresh, Saravana Prashanth Murali Babu, Robert W. Style, Ahmad Rafsanjani

entry.summary: This work develops electronics-free soft tactile sensors based on fluid-solid interaction: a fluid-filled elastomeric channel connected to only two external pressure sensors produces distinct pressure patterns when different surface regions are touched, encoding position and force. A machine learning pipeline with feature extraction and soft clustering decodes the signals. This avoids embedded electronics that are susceptible to interference and environmental degradation.

entry.title: On the Tightness and Computational Tractability of Higher-Dimensional Confidence Sequences

author.name: Fabian Denoodt, Sibylle Hess, Joaquin Vanschoren, Christian A. Naesseth

entry.summary: This new paper addresses multivariate confidence sequences for monitoring bounded vector means, where existing methods trade off statistical tightness against computational tractability. The authors propose three lifts of one-dimensional betting-based confidence sequences to higher dimensions, including a portfolio region that is much tighter but lacks closed-form boundaries, and develop tractable approximations for it. This matters for sequential monitoring of multiple metrics in production ML systems.

entry.title: Understanding Self-Predictive Learning for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Zhaohan Daniel Guo, Pierre Harvey Richemond, Bernardo \'Avila Pires, Yash Chandak, R\'emi Munos, Mark Rowland, Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Charline Le Lan, Clare Lyle, Andr\'as Gy\"orgy, Shantanu Thakoor, Will Dabney, Bilal Piot, Daniele Calandriello, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper analyzes learning dynamics of self-predictive representation learning in RL, where trivial constant representations appear to minimize prediction error. The central insight is that optimization design prevents collapse: faster optimization of the predictor and semi-gradient updates on representations are crucial. This provided the first rigorous account of why self-predictive methods like BYOL-style RL algorithms avoid collapse.

entry.title: Humans Are Not Chinchillas: Revisiting “How Quick and Big Would A Software Intelligence Explosion Be?”

author.name: James_T

entry.summary: This LessWrong post critically re-examines Davidson and Houlden's quantitative model of a software-only intelligence explosion, arguing that several of the original parameter choices were too aggressive. The author contends that Chinchilla scaling alone cannot justify 4-5 orders of magnitude of training-efficiency gains past human efficiency, and that revised evidence for the returns parameter r lowers the likely ceiling. Under the adjusted parameters, the model still finds it somewhat likely that at least 3 years of AI progress could compress into one year, but a 10-year-in-one software explosion becomes considerably less probable.

entry.title: Current AIs out-persuade professionals in lab settings but (probably) not in the world

author.name: Linch

entry.summary: A Forethought analysis of AI persuasion capabilities, arguing that lab evaluations show AI matching or exceeding professional persuaders while real-world persuasive impact is probably lower, and that persuasion benchmarking is poorly understood relative to domains like cybersecurity or math. The post frames persuasion broadly as directed social influence, including mass persuasion, preference shaping, and manipulation of common knowledge. It contributes a conceptual map and calibration of an under-measured AI risk capability.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion for Large Graph Generation via Structural Candidate Restriction

author.name: Yassin Mohamadi, Zeno Geradts, Marcel Worring

entry.summary: The paper introduces a discrete diffusion approach to large graph generation that uses structural candidate restriction to avoid the quadratic cost of standard diffusion graph generators, targeting graphs beyond the ~3k-node limit while faithfully matching degree distribution, clustering, and path lengths without memorizing training data.

entry.title: Penumbra: Sample-Efficient Adversarial Search for Regulatory Obligations

author.name: Anthony Rhodes

entry.summary: Penumbra is an adversarial search method for regulatory red-teaming of AI agents in finance, healthcare, and law, where compliance violations leave no lexical signature. It walks from a verified anchor under an expanding edit budget until a two-evaluator committee flips verdicts, emitting minimal-edit response pairs that straddle compliance, with adaptive allocation to maximize coverage under a per-probe cost of one generation and two adjudications.

entry.title: CIPO: Counterfactual Imagination Policy Optimization for Adaptive Tool Granularity Selection

author.name: Yu Li, Yunlu Wan, Zijian Zhu, Han Luo, Chao Ren, Long-Fei Li, Lei Feng

entry.summary: CIPO frames skill use in LLM agents as adaptive tool granularity selection, deciding per state whether to use atomic fine control or composite skill-level abstraction. It trains this policy with counterfactual imagination, comparing consequences of atomic versus skill choices available from the same state as the most direct training signal.

entry.title: From Papers to Mechanisms: An Evidence-Grounded Knowledge Substrate for Scientific Language Models

author.name: Qiuhui Chen, Yibo Liu, Tao Dai, Jiafan Lu, Zhenglei Zhou, Weimin Zhong

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evidence-grounded mechanism knowledge substrate organizing scientific literature into provenance-linked evidence units, role-typed entities, and directed mechanism paths, instantiated as the MS3 schema for conductive-fiber flexible sensors over 13,689 papers. MS3 retrieval outperforms closed-book generation, web search, and raw-PDF RAG across ten language models on in-domain and coverage-shift QA benchmarks.

entry.title: SYNLAT: Syntax-Aligned Text-Latent Compression for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yifeng Zhao, Hongjun Yu, Shibo Wang, Yunjiao Zhou, Zixiao Zhu, Zhipeng Ning, Kezhi Mao, Junlang Qian

entry.summary: SynLat is a text-latent chain-of-thought compression framework that aligns compression boundaries with syntactic structure via non-overlapping Syntax-Aligned Units, avoiding fragmentation of phrases and formulas. An answer-conditioned teacher constructs progressive KEEP/LATENT targets for a single compression-conditioned student that generates mixed text-latent reasoning, reducing output token costs.

entry.title: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Mingtian Tan, Palash Goyal, Mihir Parmar, Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das, Chun-Liang Li, Nanyun Peng, Thomas Hartvigsen, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: SEER is a closed-loop framework that dynamically optimizes event conditioning for time series forecasting driven by exogenous events and structural shifts. It translates prediction errors into two feedback mechanisms: a reflective retrieval memory that refines queries and filters spurious noise, and a persistent causal knowledge base reasoning about event impacts. This addresses shortcomings of standard retrieval-augmented forecasting under high noise and missing signals.

entry.title: RRM-GPT: A Framework and Vision for Radio Resource Management Foundation Models

author.name: Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Akram Bin Sediq, Koosha Pourtahmasi Roshandeh, Omar Mashaal, Ahmad M. Nagib, Jale Sadreddini, Hatem Abou-Zeid

entry.summary: RRM-GPT is an autoregressive framework treating radio resource management decisions like language generation: an encoder tokenizes heterogeneous network observations and a decoder emits decisions field-by-field conditioned on network state. Pretraining on unannotated network logs aims to make RRM models reusable across functions and deployments instead of rebuilt per setting.

entry.title: Cluster Validation Indices as Self-Supervised Objectives for Text Representation Learning

author.name: Kishor Kumar Bhaumik, Nicolas Roque dos Santos, Neil Shah, Jia Chen, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: SilK performs label-free self-supervised fine-tuning of language encoders by regressing a simplified silhouette toward a target value after clustering the corpus, using cluster validation indices as objectives. This avoids the multiview data, in-batch negatives, and auxiliary graphs required by contrastive and negative-free methods.

entry.title: MGPO: Manifold-Guided Diffusion Alignment for Task-Aware Dataset Distillation

author.name: Yunyi Chen, Chenru Wang, Xinyi Ye, Zexin Zheng, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: MGPO reformulates diffusion-based dataset distillation as a multi-objective reinforcement learning problem, combining a pixel-space discriminative reward with a latent-space geometric reward based on class-wise minimum spanning trees. This corrects the objective mismatch where likelihood-driven diffusion prioritizes density over decision boundaries and mitigates mode-collapse-style coverage loss in distilled datasets.

entry.title: Can Prosodic Style Be Inferred from Text Alone? Evidence from Unsupervised Acoustic Clusters

author.name: Abdul Rehman, Jian-Jun Zhang, Xiaosong Yang

entry.summary: This paper tests the untested assumption in expressive text-to-speech that written text carries enough information to select prosodic style, using style labels derived purely from acoustic clusters of six speakers in a 1,200-hour conversational corpus. Text embeddings are used to predict held-out utterance clusters across twelve text encoders with several controls applied.

entry.title: Physics-Informed but Not Physics-Consistent: Error Geometry and Subspace Projection for Neural AC Power Flow

author.name: Changhun Kim, Timon Conrad, Redwanul Karim, Karan Pahlajani, Julian Oelhaf, David Riebesel, Tom\'as Arias-Vergara, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: The paper shows that neural AC power-flow solvers, including emerging foundation models, achieve accurate voltage predictions whose small errors can still produce large AC power-balance residuals, revealing an accuracy-consistency gap. Using SVD bases fitted to training solutions, they find neural errors contain substantial components outside the dominant solution subspace. Calibrated solution-subspace projection is proposed to enforce physical consistency.

entry.title: Anlu: Enabling In-Context Time Series Anomaly Detection in Foundation Models via Counterfactual Supervision

author.name: Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Meng Wang, Yue Pan, Wenjun He, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies in-context learning for time-series anomaly detection with reference-conditioned detection, where a reference record indicates the operating regime. It introduces counterfactual supervision, pairing a query with two references supporting different labels, to force the model to use the reference rather than fit recognizable anomalies from the query alone. This improves regime-aware anomaly detection with frozen foundation models.

entry.title: A Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Electromigration Analysis in Multi-Segment Interconnects

author.name: Pavlos Stoikos, Anuj Pathania, George Floros

entry.summary: A physics-guided transformer encodes interconnect lines as geometry- and DC-aware segment tokens and predicts transient electromigration stress with a lightweight query decoder, trained with physics-consistent objectives. It offers a fast surrogate for computationally expensive physics solvers in chip reliability analysis.

entry.title: AdaEva: Accelerating LLM-Driven Algorithm Design with Adaptive Partial Evaluation

author.name: Tai Nguyen, Fei Liu, Phong Le, Carola Doerr, Nguyen Dang

entry.summary: Introduces AdaEva, a drop-in framework for LLM-driven automated algorithm design that progressively evaluates candidate algorithms on growing subsets of the training instance pool, eliminating clearly uncompetitive candidates early. It draws on ideas from algorithm configuration to cut the heavy evaluation cost of evolutionary LLM4AD loops.

entry.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

author.name: Yueran Ma

entry.summary: The paper studies how LoRA adapter rank relates to double descent under label noise, using a module-matched rank sweep that extends past full rank and compares each rank with dense fine-tuning of matched modules on vision backbones and a 7B language model. Findings include that on DeiT-Tiny risk is lowest at rank one and rises sharply as the adapter gains capacity to fit noise, with the second descent extending beyond the dense fine-tuning parity point. This gives practical guidance on choosing LoRA ranks.

entry.title: Billion-Scale Thumbnail Optimization for Uncurated Short-Form Videos via Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Ying Han, Ling Liu, Fabio Soldo, Vu Nguyen, Danio Wang, Liz Kidd, Yongle Cao, Theodore Rose, Su-Lin Wu, Romer Rosales

entry.summary: The paper describes a deployed real-time thumbnail optimization system at billions-of-videos scale on a major short-form video platform, using an online multi-armed bandit framework with multi-stage candidate generation to replace static default frames. The authors claim this is the first published demonstration of an online MAB framework at O(B) scale for uncurated short-form video.

entry.title: Outcome-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: ZheXu Wang, Mao-Lin Luo, Yankun Hong, Zi-Hao Zhou, Bo Ye, Jian Zhao, Xialiang Tong, Min-Ling Zhang, Tong Wei

entry.summary: The authors analyze on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) through the lens of RLVR advantage formulation, showing that vanilla OPSD under-penalizes incorrect trajectories because it applies a fixed divergence objective regardless of outcome correctness. They propose an outcome-guided variant that incorporates correctness signals to stabilize and improve training.

entry.title: Lightweight Semantic EEG Foundation Model for Frozen Cross-Disorder Transfer

author.name: Rita Huan-Ting Peng, Nhat Bui

entry.summary: USE-FM is a lightweight (1.46M parameter) EEG foundation model trained via self-supervised reconstruction on the TUEG corpus, evaluated with a frozen encoder on abnormal EEG detection and seizure recognition against much larger models like LUNA-Base and CBraMod. It demonstrates efficient cross-disorder transfer without full fine-tuning.

entry.title: When Does a Diffusion Model Decide What to Draw ?

author.name: Snigdha Chandan Khilar

entry.summary: Measures when diffusion models commit to semantic content during generation by introducing the committor: the class distribution obtained by restarting generation from a partially denoised image many times. Findings on CIFAR-10 show coarse decisions occur at roughly twice the noise level of fine decisions, and a cheaper classifier-based proxy correlates with these measurements.

entry.title: Fast Last-Iterate Convergence in Zero-Sum Markov Games with Bandit Feedback

author.name: Yuheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies last-iterate convergence in unknown two-player zero-sum discounted Markov games with bandit feedback where players learn independently along a single trajectory. The proposed Adaptive Regularized TD Learning (ARTD) achieves a t^(-1/4) duality gap bound with high probability, improving on the previous t^(-1/(9+nu)) rate of Cai et al. 2023, without requiring knowledge of the hitting time bound, horizon, or confidence level.

entry.title: Considering Context: When World Models Need Context Encoders

author.name: Oleg Smirnov, Sofiane Ennadir, John Pertoft, Bjartur Hjaltason, Sara Karimi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the assumption behind context-aware model-based RL via predictive sufficiency, quantifying what access to a latent environment context adds to next-step prediction and decomposing it into history-recoverable, context-required, and model-deficit components. It classifies context-aware algorithms by the predictive risk their conditioning targets and tests them across environments of increasing identification difficulty. This clarifies when external context encoders are actually needed.

entry.title: Mitigating Over-squashing without Rewiring: A Sheaf Effective Resistance Perspective

author.name: Andr\'e Ribeiro, Germano Barcelos, Amauri H. Souza, Diego Mesquita, Ana Luiza Ten\'orio

entry.summary: Building on cellular sheaves, the paper introduces sheaf effective resistance, generalizing the graph-topological measure of over-squashing bottlenecks to depend on the sheaf attached to the graph. The authors prove that for flat vector bundles, Jacobian-based over-squashing sensitivity is upper bounded by a sheaf effective resistance quantity, enabling mitigation by adjusting the sheaf rather than rewiring the graph. This offers a theoretically grounded alternative to graph rewiring for long-range GNN dependencies.

entry.title: Largest Rashomon sets of decision trees for robust contextual optimization

author.name: Lorenzo Bonasera, David Pisinger

entry.summary: Studies predictive multiplicity in decision trees, proposing a framework that jointly selects an operational decision and the largest Rashomon set of trees so that cost, shortage, or risk targets hold under the local empirical distributions every tree induces at a query point. It specializes to regression, showing a tree affects the decision only through observations sharing the query leaf. This provides robustness guarantees under model ambiguity.

entry.title: Variance-Aware Fine-Grained Gap-Dependent Bounds for Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haochen Zhang, Lingzhou Xue, Zhong Zheng

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open problem by establishing the first fine-grained gap-dependent regret bound for UCB-Bernstein+ in variance-aware model-free online RL for episodic tabular MDPs. It also integrates a stage-wise policy update design to control policy switching cost.

entry.title: Causal Lag Structure Discovery in Confounded Time Series via Orthogonalized Adaptive Estimation

author.name: Hong Kiat Tan, Isaac-Neil Zanoria, James Chen, Haoyang Lyu, Mihai Cucuringu

entry.summary: ORACLE-VARX is a unified pipeline for discovering causal lag structure in confounded multivariate time series, combining double/debiased machine learning for confounder removal, adaptive sequential testing for data-driven lag selection, and Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected z-tests for false-discovery-rate-controlled edge selection. The authors prove debiased estimation guarantees per rolling window. This is valuable for scientific and policy applications needing reliable time-series causal discovery.

entry.title: IGA-KAN: Isogeometric Analysis with Physics-Informed Closed-Form Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Forward and Inverse PDEs

author.name: Sima Naraghi, Kourosh Parand, Amirhossein Sadr, Dara Rahmati

entry.summary: IGA-KAN augments isogeometric analysis rather than replacing it: on each knot-vertex patch, a local Kolmogorov-Arnold ridge model is fitted in closed form via a single batched linear least-squares problem to the strong form of the PDE and the IGA solution, with models blended by IGA hat functions. This avoids non-convex optimization, learning rates, and initialization entirely while improving PDE solution accuracy on exact NURBS geometry. The method supports both forward and inverse problems with error control.

entry.title: Verb-ICL: Rethinking In-Context Learning for Structured Prediction

author.name: Fan Bai, Hengshuo Miao, Sanjit S Batra, Hamid Reza Hassanzadeh, Ardavan Saeedi, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: Verb-ICL is a selective annotation framework for in-context learning on structured prediction, combining token-level coverage-based example selection with generated error feedback that codifies task-specific annotation guidelines into demonstrations. It targets the compositional, token-level patterns that sentence-level ICL misses. Practical improvement to ICL for NER-style and other structured tasks.

entry.title: Harness-Search: Guiding Long-Horizon Search through Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Shanyong Wang, Zhenwen Ji, Lei Jin, Yining Zhao, Yicheng Qian, Chengqiang Lu, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Lizhen Cui, Yanyu Xu

entry.summary: Harness-Search is a multi-agent search harness that decouples three responsibilities, proposing retrieval actions, updating persistent state, and deciding when to stop, to prevent the failure modes of single-agent long-horizon search such as losing track of unresolved questions or terminating prematurely. The design targets evidence gathering and synthesis into well-supported answers over extended interactions. It contributes to the growing area of structured agent harnesses for deep research tasks.

entry.title: UniBRep: Learning Unified Geometry and Topology for Image-conditioned B-Rep Generation

author.name: Haiyang Ying, Allen Tu, Jiaye Wu, Tom Goldstein, Matthias Zwicker

entry.summary: UniBRep adapts a pretrained image-to-3D model to generate a feature mesh serving as a unified intermediate representation for image-conditioned CAD B-rep generation. Dual decoders produce geometry and face-separation features, and a guided construction pipeline fits parametric surfaces and assembles an explicit B-rep via a CAD kernel.

entry.title: EagleDepth: Efficient Fine-Grained Depth Estimation via Pixel Diffusion Decoder

author.name: Bowen Chai, Tianbao Zhang, Shuyu Wu, Dexin Zuo, Zhaoxin Fan, Danping Zou

entry.summary: EagleDepth is an efficient monocular depth estimation framework for high-resolution images that keeps depth-aware latent representations as guidance while generating the final depth map directly in pixel space, avoiding VAE reconstruction artifacts and latent-decoding overhead. Components are trained sequentially, fine-tuning a pretrained latent model first.

entry.title: CoDG-Net: Structure-Guided Style Diffusion and Collaborative Learning to Mitigate Catastrophic Forgetting in Medical Image Domain Generalization

author.name: Yucheng Song, Jincan Wang, Haokang Ding, Zhiqiang Tian, Kangxu Fan, Zhifang Liao

entry.summary: CoDG-Net addresses catastrophic forgetting in medical image segmentation domain generalization, where cross-domain robustness is gained at the cost of source-domain knowledge, threatening deployed clinical diagnostics. It combines structure-guided style diffusion augmentation constrained by anatomical consistency in the frequency domain with collaborative learning to preserve source knowledge. The dual focus on augmentation and forgetting is a useful pairing for medical DG.

entry.title: Spatial Supervision Without Attribution Optimization: Improving Post-Hoc Class Activation Maps via Box-Guided Evidence Routing

author.name: Wenhao Liang, Liangwei Nathan Zheng, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes BGER, which trains a lightweight gate on final feature maps under box or mask supervision and routes classification through gated features, while Grad-CAM is computed at the pre-gate representation so attribution maps never enter the training objective. This raises MaxBoxAccV2 from 0.584 to 0.715 on CUB-200-2011, improving CAM quality for free.

entry.title: Terrain-Dependent Intra-Cycle Leg Timing for Effective Locomotion on Granular Slopes

author.name: Long Zhao, Xingjue Liao, Feifei Qian

entry.summary: Using a hexapedal robot on a tiltable granular bed, the authors measure how slope-dependent shear and normal resistive forces affect legged locomotion and develop a robot-terrain interaction model predicting anchoring timing, step length, and speed as functions of terrain strength and slope. The model reveals slope-induced performance effects and informs intra-cycle leg timing strategies for granular slopes like sand dunes.

entry.title: WasserMan: Benchmark for Underwater Manipulation Policy Learning

author.name: Danil Belov, Artem Erkhov, Sergei Parsegov, Pavel Osinenko

entry.summary: WasserMan is presented as the first multi-task simulation benchmark for visuomotor learning of floating-base underwater contact manipulation, offering ten expert-solvable tasks, two vehicle-arm platforms, a bimanual configuration, and underwater dynamics. The authors benchmark ACT, diffusion policies, and behavioral cloning across tasks, finding that removing integral action can prevent task completion and action interfaces affect success rates.

entry.title: GJK-CBF: Control Barrier Functions for Convex Rigid Body Collision Avoidance on SE(3)

author.name: Yi-Hsuan Chen, Shuo Liu, Wei Xiao, Michael Otte, Calin Belta

entry.summary: Formulates control barrier functions for convex rigid body collision avoidance using the GJK algorithm to obtain witness pairs directly, avoiding the computational overhead of differentiable optimization for CBF gradients. The result is an efficient real-time safety filter for SE(3) collision avoidance among general convex bodies.

entry.title: Demonstration-Calibrated Port-Hamiltonian Retuning for Manipulation Policies

author.name: Yulong Yang, Fan Wu, Christine Allen-Blanchette, Amit Chakraborty

entry.summary: PHRetune is an offline method that derives impedance controller gains for frozen diffusion and VLA policies without evaluation rollouts or gain search, learning a port-Hamiltonian model from demonstrations to estimate effort and energy of predicted actions. Policy predictions on recorded observations are assessed against this energy model to select deployed gains.

entry.title: Robotizing Human Videos with Physically Consistent Interactions

author.name: Ching-Lam Cheng, Shengfeng He, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: This work converts human manipulation videos into robot demonstrations by replacing hands with rendered robots while enforcing physical plausibility: an interaction-aware contact reconstruction module recovers dense 3D hand-object contacts and stabilizes them into parallel-jaw grasps, and a depth-aware compositing module resolves robot-object occlusions. This tackles the embodiment gap that limits using scalable human video data for manipulation training.

entry.title: Physics Residual Dynamics and Reduced Order Whole-Body Planning for Obstacle Aware Human Robot Cloth CoTransportation

author.name: Moein Forouhar, Kosar Behnia, Anirvan Dutta, Hamid Sadeghian, Ville Kyrki, Sami Haddadin, Gokhan Alcan, Eckehard Steinbach

entry.summary: This paper presents hierarchical planning for dual-arm mobile-manipulator co-transportation of cloth with a human, using a physics-residual conditional recurrent VAE that learns corrections to a linearized cloth physics model to predict full cloth configuration over a 40-step horizon. Predicted deformation feeds an MPPI planner built on a reduced-order whole-body model, enabling obstacle-aware transport despite unactuated interior cloth. This addresses a hard deformable-object coordination problem.

entry.title: SkillScriptBench: Benchmarking Self-Evolution of Executable Agent Skill Packages Beyond Markdown

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Haoran Li, Yuhao Zhang, Jiahe Guo, Hongyu Luo, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Kawai Chung, Junle Chen, Changxuan Fan, Qing Zong, Lingyun Xie, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SkillScriptBench is a 350-task benchmark built from a survey of over 35,000 GitHub-hosted agent skill packages, separately evaluating documentation repair, script repair, and behavior preservation during skill self-evolution. Each task includes injected faults and executable checks of required behavior.

entry.title: RAGrasp: Geometry-Semantic Template Retrieval and Grasp Transfer

author.name: Shenzhe Zhu, Chengxiao He, Jan Harder

entry.summary: Presents a retrieval-augmented pipeline for planar parallel-jaw grasping that uses a small set of locally collected, grasp-annotated RGB-D templates instead of large public or synthetic training datasets, requiring no end-to-end retraining for new deployments. It combines DINOv2 features with SAM2 segmentation and a two-stage geometry-semantic matching for grasp transfer.

entry.title: $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention

author.name: Wenyin Liu (Guangdong University of Technology), Yiheng Huang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Kai Wang (Beijing Denglu Technology Ltd)

entry.summary: TRIZ^a is a general R&D automation paradigm combining TRIZ inventive theory (40 principles, contradiction matrix) with LLM-driven agent evolutionary search, using theory-guided ideation to replace random mutation. It measures functional information under a frozen reference contract combined with TRIZ Ideality and hard promotion gates, validated in cybersecurity domains including PowerDuck GOOSE and CICIoT2023.

entry.title: Not All Answers Are Contextually Persuadable: Inference Dynamics in Large Language Models under Contextual Influence

author.name: Zongye Hu, Weiqing Luo, Yanjie Fu, Yu Gan, Haofeng Zhang, Ziyi Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a theoretical framework for analyzing contextual influence on LLM predictions at the level of internal inference dynamics rather than output-level answer changes. It shows that predictive representations under repeated contextual assertions do not drift unboundedly but converge to stable, query-dependent regimes that constrain which answers are contextually persuadable.

entry.title: How corner is a corner case? Percentile control for highway scenario generation

author.name: Jiaxi Liu, Hang Zhou, Hangyu Li, Yifan Wang, Keke Long, Chengyuan Ma, Bin Ran, Xiaopeng Li

entry.summary: This AV testing paper defines the adversity of a generated driving scenario as its percentile in the conditional distribution of future risk given observed history, enabling calibrated answers to how extreme a generated corner case is. It supports fine-tuning scenario cornerness for autonomous-vehicle safety testing before deployment.

entry.title: Memory Canonicalization: A Framework and Benchmark for Cross-Model Drift in Persistent LLM Memory

author.name: Amit Vadnere, Aishwarya Lonarkar

entry.summary: This paper identifies that the same stored memory object can be interpreted differently by different LLMs retrieved under identical conditions, factually or emotionally, and proposes memory canonicalization: a write-time pipeline that rewrites raw memories into explicit, structurally disambiguated canonical form with emotional valence represented explicitly. It provides both a framework and a benchmark.

entry.title: Look Before You Leap: Thermodynamic Arbitration of Parametric and Non-Parametric Knowledge in LLM Agents via Self-Regulating Memory Architectures

author.name: Akash Das, Ishan Roy

entry.summary: This paper critiques the Retrieve-Always paradigm in agentic frameworks, arguing it forces models into pathological induced amnesia where they reflexively distrust internal knowledge. It proposes a self-regulating memory architecture that thermodynamically arbitrates between parametric and external non-parametric knowledge, deciding when external retrieval is actually warranted.

entry.title: PharmAgent: Constraint-Aware Search with Frozen Language Models for Molecular Optimization

author.name: Nihui Shao, Guanxing Chen, Jilong Shi, Zhengyang Bai, Haohuai He, Zhenchao Tang, Qiujie Lv, Yu-An Huang, Zhi-An Huang

entry.summary: PharmAgent is a molecular optimization method that uses frozen language models with a Lagrangian controller translating constraint violations into accumulated constraint pressure kept separate from current property measurements, plus structure-indexed replay of relevant evaluated transitions. This gives frozen LMs explicit constraint control and experience without tailored retraining.

entry.title: Factoriax: A GPU-Accelerated Factorio-Style Simulator for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mickey Beurskens, Tristan Tomilin, Thiago D. Sim\~ao

entry.summary: Factoriax is a JAX-based GPU-accelerated factory-building RL simulator where agents collect resources, build and arrange machines into production pipelines, benchmarked on an Easy Rocket task. A billion-step PPO run (500k episodes) completes in roughly eight minutes, enabling large-scale long-horizon RL experiments.

entry.title: RocketAgent: A Long-Horizon Engineering Agent for Multidisciplinary Design of Liquid-Rocket Thrust Chambers

author.name: Junxiang He, Runze Mao, Kun He, Teng Zhang, Liming Zheng, Ke Xiao, Zhi X. Chen

entry.summary: RocketAgent is a long-horizon engineering agent in which a plan-owning coding agent coordinates skills for performance sizing, subsystem optimization, geometry generation, and multiphysics assessment of liquid-rocket thrust chambers. It uses a provenance-aware knowledge graph for method selection and a typed Design Intermediate Representation to keep shared parameters and artifacts consistent across dependent analyses.

entry.title: GPlaceRL: An Open-Source Graph Reinforcement Learning Framework for Detailed Placement

author.name: Pavlos Stoikos, Foteini Oikonomou, Christos Poulos, Maria Pantazi-Kypriou, Athanasios Tziouvaras, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Georgios Karakonstantis, George Floros

entry.summary: GPlaceRL is an open-source graph RL framework for detailed placement refinement in chip design, representing legalized placements as graphs with a modular environment for studying graph encoders, policies, rewards, and local actions. It fills a gap, as most learning-based placement work targets floorplanning or macro/global placement.

entry.title: AEGIS: Differentiable Mars Climate Model with Neural Closures

author.name: Sameera S Kashyap, Victor Cruz, Angel Yepez, Razvan Marinescu

entry.summary: AEGIS is a differentiable general circulation model for Mars that incorporates neural closures, replacing legacy Fortran GCM implementations with a modern differentiable framework. Mars GCMs are mission-critical for entry, descent, and landing operations but face sparse observations, a thin CO2 atmosphere, and a volatile dust cycle with no terrestrial analog for validation. Differentiability enables data assimilation and learning of subgrid closures despite these challenges.

entry.title: Language Model Fingerprinting Requires Rethinking Watermark Teachers

author.name: Jeongyeon Hwang, Anshul Nasery, Sewoong Oh, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: This paper reexamines LLM fingerprinting via watermark distillation, showing that prior protocol evaluations understate text-quality degradation because they favor overly strong watermark teachers. Weakening the watermark improves quality but sacrifices detectability, so the authors argue that text watermarks designed for per-output verification are poor distillation teachers for model fingerprinting, and propose alternatives exploiting the fact that fingerprint verification aggregates over many outputs.

entry.title: FTD-GNO: Memory-Efficient Graph Neural Operators through Functional Tensor Decomposition of the Kernel

author.name: Xiaomin Zhang, Boyue Wang, Junbin Gao, Yongli Hu anbd Baocai Yin

entry.summary: FTD-GNO decouples high-dimensional integral kernels in graph neural operators into low-dimensional mode-wise functions using CP, Tensor-Train, and Tucker decomposition formats. This reduces the substantial computational and memory overhead of standard GNOs when solving PDEs at high resolutions or with large graph neighborhoods.

entry.title: Specific Algorithmic Interpretability of Neural Networks: A Case Study on Textures

author.name: Yanglin Zhang, Anneke von Seeger, Gilad Lerman, Ron Levie

entry.summary: The authors develop a framework for constructing neural networks whose trained parameters retain explicit algorithmic interpretation, addressing the gap where algorithm-inspired architectures lose interpretability after standard training. Modeling data as class-dependent stochastic processes, they initialize networks to exactly implement statistics-estimation algorithms and prove properties supporting this interpretation, with textures as a case study.

entry.title: Active-DiNTS: Active Differentiable Network Topology Search

author.name: Gean Trindade Pereira, Thierry Urruty, Muriel Visani, Andr\'e C. P. L. F. de Carvalho

entry.summary: Active-DiNTS embeds pool-based active learning into a bi-level differentiable neural architecture search for 3D medical image segmentation, jointly discovering architectures and curating labels. Unlabeled MRI volumes are ranked by uncertainty signals and only top-ranked cases are annotated, reducing annotation and compute costs.

entry.title: Hidden Risks of Jev: An Empirical Study of Security, Privacy, and Dual Use

author.name: Shang Wang, Tianqing Zhu, Huajie Chen, Jiayang Li, Meng Yang, Bo Liu

entry.summary: This is described as the first systematic security and privacy study of Jev-style typed classification APIs used as application decision layers, using both an official API and a local controllable model (NanoJev). It investigates security threats when such models route requests and select tools, private information leakable despite constrained typed outputs, and dual-use concerns. The findings are relevant as probability-scored typed classification endpoints become common integration points.

entry.title: LogSig-SSM: Time-Series Modelling with Multi-Scale Log-Signature Compression for State-Space Models

author.name: Felix Oury, Nicolas Calvo Peiro, Reiko J. Tanaka

entry.summary: LogSig-SSM compresses long, irregularly sampled multivariate time series into shorter token sequences using multi-scale windowed log-signatures, then processes the compressed sequence with selective state-space models like Mamba. This combines the rough-path theory strengths of neural CDEs/RDEs for irregular sampling with the linear scaling of SSMs for long sequences. The hybrid addresses the poor scalability of continuous-time models and the limited within-block mixing of SSMs.

entry.title: Bayesian Entropy-based Reordering for Calibrated Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zhejun Jiang, Mijung Park
