entry.summary: BayesER is a post-hoc Bayesian decoding framework for masked diffusion language models that replaces miscalibrated softmax confidence with predictive entropy from posterior-averaged predictions to prioritize reliable token commitments during denoising. It builds a lightweight approximate posterior centered at the pretrained checkpoint, similar to Laplace-LoRA but without training adapters. This targets the underexplored question of uncertainty calibration in diffusion LM decoding.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning for the Retrieval of Immunotherapy-Associated Molecular Signatures from Histopathology

author.name: Sigrid Vila-Bagaria, Mar Teixid\'o, Miquel Pi\~nol, Felip Vilardell, Robert Montal, Veronica Vilaplana

entry.summary: CCMIL is a cross-modal contrastive multiple-instance learning framework that imputes a costly 10-gene RNA signature for Inflamed/Non-Inflamed gastric adenocarcinoma subtypes directly from standard H&E histopathology slides. It aligns visual morphology with molecular phenotypes in a shared latent space, enabling interpretable search-by-case retrieval for pathologists. This could reduce dependence on expensive RNA profiling for immunotherapy response prediction.

entry.title: A Strong Baseline for Evaluating Vision Encoders in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yilin Yang, Jun-Tao Tang, Kengyi Wang, Siyuan Su, Gaoyong Luo, Mingda Chen

entry.summary: The paper revisits cross-modal evaluation of vision encoders for multimodal LLMs via large-scale experiments, identifying limitations in prior experimental designs and formulations. It introduces RAVEL, a simple training-free method based on cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval that achieves state-of-the-art correlation with downstream MLLM performance.

entry.title: Scenario-Based Compositional Statistical Model Checking for Safety Specifications

author.name: Abhinav Pomalapally, Arya Raeesi, Kevin Kai-Chun Chang, Beyazit Yalcinkaya, Sanjit A. Seshia

entry.summary: The paper introduces a compositional statistical model checking framework that decomposes composite scenarios into primitives and specifications into sub-specifications, verifying primitives independently and composing results. This avoids redundant simulation when scenarios share structure, improving efficiency of safety evaluation in domains like autonomous driving.

entry.title: Non-invasive Seizure Detection Using Wearable Wrist-worn Accelerometry and Deep Learning

author.name: Nilushika Udayangani Hewa Dehigahawattage, Kishor Nandakishor, Marimuthu Palaniswami

entry.summary: The study develops a wearable seizure detection system using a single wrist-worn accelerometer with deep learning, targeting multiple seizure types including short-duration events. It aims to replace expensive, in-hospital video-EEG monitoring and unreliable seizure diaries with long-term ambulatory monitoring. This could substantially improve epilepsy care accessibility and reliability.

entry.title: Investigating Query-Insensitive Behavior in Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Eryk Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Alberto Presta, Karol Szurkowski, Michal Byra

entry.summary: This study challenges the assumption in spatio-temporal video grounding that every query is relevant to the input video, testing state-of-the-art models under irrelevant or missing queries. Models still produce plausible spatio-temporal predictions even with unrelated or removed queries, and dataset regularities in HCSTVG-v2 and VidSTG may encourage this shortcut behavior. The findings question benchmark validity in STVG.

entry.title: Anosognosia in LLMs: Probing Self-Awareness of Quantized Computational Substrate

author.name: Yoshihiro Izawa, Gouki Minegishi, Yoko Yamakata

entry.summary: Inspired by the neurological condition anosognosia, the paper tests whether LLMs can recognize degradation in their own quantized computational substrate. Models fail to self-report quantization state from generated text, yet linear probing shows internal representations contain clear method-specific fingerprints, and training enables partial self-recognition. It is a novel probe of model self-knowledge with implications for introspection research.

entry.title: SimForcing: Distilling Simulation Motion Priors into Real-Domain Robot World Models

author.name: Xiaodong Wang, Tianle Li, Chuanxin Song, Junliang Xie, Zhanmi Zhong, Suiying Wu, Peixi Peng

entry.summary: SimForcing is a simulation-guided framework that distills motion knowledge from a simulation teacher into real-domain action-conditioned robot world models via latent-motion distillation, while using simulation as a controllable reference for prediction. This addresses the sim-to-real appearance gap and the risk of inaccurate simulation predictions misleading real-video generation. It matters for building world models that respond precisely to robot actions with realistic dynamics.

entry.title: KVE-KD: Key Visual Evidence-Guided Knowledge Distillation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jianbin Zhang, Xin Sun, Shanwen Wang, Wei Ye, Susanto Rahardja

entry.summary: Introduces a knowledge distillation framework that dynamically concentrates feature supervision on task-relevant visual tokens rather than applying uniform supervision or static token selection. It uses the final pre-generation textual token as a semantic anchor to identify the target cross-modal fusion layer and select key visual evidence.

entry.title: LD-EnFF: Latent-Dynamics Ensemble Flow Filtering for Data Assimilation with Sparse Observations

author.name: Ziyu Tian, Kaichen Shen, Wenbo Hao, Phillip Si, Peng Chen, Wei Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a sequential Bayesian filtering framework that performs forecast propagation and filtering updates in a compact latent space, combining a latent dynamics surrogate for ensemble propagation with a VAE-based state-dependent observation model. This targets the compounding challenges of expensive high-dimensional simulations and sparse noisy observations in data assimilation.

entry.title: Consideration Circuits: Depth Separation and Universality Beyond a Single Softmax

author.name: Junjie Xiao, Huiwen Jia

entry.summary: Introduces consideration circuits, multi-stage choice models built as DAGs of multinomial logit units, and proves a sharp depth-norm separation showing three-stage depth beats two on a compromise task where single-softmax RUM models have irreducible error. This extends choice modeling theory beyond single-softmax architectures. It bridges behavioral modeling and neural network depth theory.

entry.title: Adaptive Bregman Alternating Projections for Feasible Gromov-Wasserstein Learning

author.name: Aoran Zhang, C\'esar A. Uribe

entry.summary: Proposes A-KL-BAPG, an adaptive-penalty variant of Bregman alternating projected gradient for Gromov-Wasserstein problems that combines a fixed-penalty burn-in with a guarded increasing-penalty phase and a Sinkhorn-inspired safeguard, proving finite termination and feasibility. This addresses the persistent feasibility gap of fixed-penalty relaxations in the nonconvex GW problem. Relevant to structured distribution comparison without shared feature spaces.

entry.title: BARQ: Balanced Codebook Refinement for Low-Bit LLM Quantization

author.name: Chenhang Cui, Xu Xie, Linrui Xu, Xiaohao Liu, Xingyu Zhu, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: BARQ improves codebook-based low-bit quantization of LLMs by fixing imbalanced nearest-codeword assignments: it uses entropically regularized optimal transport with uniform marginals and curvature-weighted costs for soft assignments, ensuring all codewords are used. This boosts effective codebook utilization and quantization quality, addressing storage and memory-traffic bottlenecks in LLM deployment. Balanced assignment is a clean solution to a known failure mode of codebook methods.

entry.title: Variance-Optimal Control Variates for Learning with Black-box Feedback

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Shuhan Zhang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that even an exact action-value function can be far from variance-optimal as a control variate in learning with black-box feedback, because the value function minimizes noise per-action rather than accounting for shared parameters across the gradient. The authors derive an unbiased correction at no extra oracle cost and characterize the residual-based variance-optimal solution.

entry.title: How Should Teachers Be Prepared? RL on Student-Induced States for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Haoyue Liu, Zhichao Wang, Jionghao Zhu, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Prep-OPD uses reinforcement learning before on-policy distillation to train the teacher to adapt to student-generated reasoning states and correct course on errors, addressing evidence that strong independent solvers degrade when continuing student prefixes. Training optimizes teacher continuations from fixed student-induced states.

entry.title: Advectra: Asymmetric Latent Transport for Non-Stationary Physics

author.name: Nodens Koren, Thomas Hofmann, Georgios Kissas

entry.summary: Advectra is a transport-aware latent neural operator that decouples source and target coordinate systems via a regularized kinematic coordinate map, creating an approximately co-moving latent frame for advective dynamics. Combined with geometry-aware ordering for state-space models, it handles transport-dominated systems where coherent structures move relative to fixed frames.

entry.title: When Does Retrieval Help? A Study of In-Context Adaptation in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Joris K\"oster, Zizhan Zheng, Siavash Khajavi

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares four retrieval methods (image-based, state-augmented, VLA-feature-based, and others) within the RICL framework for adapting vision-language-action robot models in context without parameter updates. It establishes how retrieval quality translates into task performance for robot policies.

entry.title: ReMaD: Tuning-free Domain Adaptation for Classification and Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Elijah Bolluyt, Cristina Comaniciu

entry.summary: Proposes Reduced-rank Mahalanobis Distance, a training-free refinement that fits closed-form distribution statistics from target-domain embeddings to adapt pretrained classifiers and detect out-of-distribution samples. The method removes uninformative latent directions to align latent-space distributions across domains without finetuning or OOD data knowledge.

entry.title: MEND: RL For Flow Models via Proximal Velocity Matching

author.name: Shreshth Saini, Neil Birkbeck, Yilin Wang, Balu Adsumilli, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: MEND is a reinforcement learning method for reward post-training of flow models based on proximal velocity matching. It caps rewards within prompt groups, proposes gradient-aligned moves accepted only when capped reward gain exceeds a quadratic displacement price, and regresses onto velocity targets without KL penalties, frozen references, or advantage weights. The authors report outperforming Flow-GRPO within 100 updates.

entry.title: Lipschitz Thinking: Ten Years of Certifiable-by-Design Robust Neural Networks

author.name: Fabio Brau, Giorgio Piras, Maura Pintor, Battista Biggio

entry.summary: This survey/tutorial reviews a decade of Lipschitz-bounded neural networks, explaining the principles of Lipschitz-constrained layers, mechanisms for enforcing bounds, and how they yield robustness certificates at the cost of a single forward pass. It traces how these layers have been incorporated into increasingly expressive models, narrowing the gap between empirical robustness and formal guarantees. As a synthesis it serves as an entry point to certifiable robustness research.

entry.title: SPDAlign: Interpretable Riemannian Alignment for EEG Forward Modeling Shifts

author.name: Shanglin Li, Shiwen Chu, Okan Ko\c{c}, Chenyu Liu, Qibin Zhao, Motoaki Kawanabe, Mitsuo Kawato, Yi Ding

entry.summary: SPDAlign targets unsupervised domain adaptation for EEG brain-computer interfaces by studying distribution shifts arising from the domain-specific forward process, linked to factors like head geometry. Using a classic generative EEG model, the authors theoretically characterize these shifts and propose an interpretable Riemannian alignment on symmetric positive definite matrices, removing the need for costly labeled calibration data. This could substantially improve practical BCI utility across sessions and subjects.

entry.title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study

author.name: Ivan Don\`a, Hans H. Brunner, \'Alvaro Troyano Olivas, Chi-Hang Fred Fung, Momtchil Peev, Giovanni Iacca

entry.summary: The authors build a federated learning framework that uses physics-based information-theoretically secure key exchange for additive masking, overcoming finite key-rate and storage constraints via frozen backbones and knowledge distillation. A medical imaging case study demonstrates sustained training of models under stronger-than-computational security guarantees. It bridges cryptographic key distribution practice with privacy-preserving ML.

entry.title: Decoupling Time and Space: A Temporally Conditioned Refinement for EEG Source Imaging

author.name: Marco Morik, Jesse Palarus, Carmen Vidaurre, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stream framework for EEG source localization that decouples global temporal representation learning (a Transformer-based temporal condition encoder with factorized spatiotemporal attention) from per-time-point spatial refinement, addressing the trade-off between frame-by-frame models that lose temporal context and costly full 4D spatiotemporal networks.

entry.title: Amortized Score-Hamiltonian Policy Iteration: A Grid-Free Scheme for Relaxed Stochastic Control Problems

author.name: Qi Feng, Gu Wang

entry.summary: Develops an amortized, grid-free policy-value iteration based on continuous Langevin dynamics for entropy-regularized infinite-horizon relaxed stochastic control. It connects improvement rates to relative Fisher information and projects actor and value dynamics onto shared samplers and a parametric critic. The work bridges optimal control theory with score-based learning.

entry.title: Latent-Lagrangian Neural Networks for Reduced Order Modeling of Non-autonomous Nonlinear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Anand Kumar Agrawal, Anders Thorin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a latent Lagrangian framework for reduced-order modeling of forced nonlinear dynamical systems, learning latent coordinates alongside latent kinetic and potential energy networks while using force supervision to avoid ODE solves during training. Physical consistency is enforced via the principle of virtual work, with good generalization to unseen forces and initial conditions.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization

author.name: Qihao Zhou

entry.summary: The paper characterizes, up to logarithmic factors, the minimax expected query complexity for finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave optimization, proving a lower bound via a dual-chain construction and matching the Catalyst upper bound for large condition numbers. For the small-curvature regime it introduces recursive proximal descent-ascent (RPDA) with matching complexity.

entry.title: FORGE: Verification-Gated Behavioral Repair for Generative Language Models

author.name: Hsin-Ling Hsu, Min-Yu Chen, Nai-Chia Chen, Yan-Ru Chen, Yi-Ling Chang, Fang Yu

entry.summary: FORGE is a framework for targeted behavioral repair of generative LLMs (e.g., demographic bias, toxic generation), designed to eliminate specific defects while preserving overall functionality and ideally providing per-instance correctness guarantees, addressing limits of fine-tuning, model editing, and constraint-based repair.

entry.title: Unmentioned Checklist Findings Change How Reinforcement Learning Appears to Improve Chest Radiograph Report Checking

author.name: Ali Vosoughi, Akhil Kasturi, Chenliang Xu, Axel Wismueller

entry.summary: This study trains a vision-language model with reinforcement learning to fill a 12-finding chest radiograph checklist without seeing the sentence under test, then evaluates automated checking of radiology reports. It reveals that the training format, which encodes unmentioned findings as absent, inflates measured gains on the training checker while lowering independent checker performance, exposing evaluation artifacts. This is an important caution for AI-assisted radiology evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Polynomial neural surrogates for designing photonic quantum experiments

author.name: Rohit Chaurasiya, Xuemei Gu

entry.summary: The authors build a physics-inspired polynomial neural surrogate for PyTheus, a graph-based quantum-optics simulator, to accelerate the search for experimental configurations generating target quantum states. Polynomial activations mirror the graph perfect-matching structure underlying state amplitudes, and surrogates for four-, six-, and eight-photon systems achieve higher accuracy with fewer trainable parameters. This speeds up AI-driven quantum experiment discovery.

entry.title: The Surrogate Is Not the Reward: Post-Surrogate Primary-Outcome Acquisition in Contextual Bandits

author.name: Kyungbok Lee, Michael R. Kosorok

entry.summary: This paper studies contextual bandits where a cheap surrogate signal is observed before deciding whether to spend budget acquiring the costly primary outcome that defines regret. The proposed Audited Surrogate Bandit sets pre-surrogate acquisition from decision relevance and redistributes after seeing the surrogate using residual uncertainty, with theoretical guarantees for finite policy classes.

entry.title: Rewrite What Matters: Adaptive Multilingual Query Rewriting for Reasoning via Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rui Qi, Yufeng Chen, Yunlong Liang, Chuan Meng, Sijin Lu, Ge Shi, Jinan Xu, Fandong Meng, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: mRewriter-R1 formulates multilingual query rewriting for LLM reasoning as a multi-turn sequential decision problem trained with reinforcement learning, letting the model adaptively choose rewriting operators rather than applying one-size-fits-all translation. This targets performance disparities across languages with equivalent semantics. A competent RL application with a credible industry-affiliated author list.

entry.title: DimSteer: Steering LLM Authoring with Automatically Discovered Stylistic Controls

author.name: Ajit Mallavarapu, Ziwei Gu

entry.summary: DimSteer is an authoring interface that samples prompt-local completions, discovers high-variance activation-space axes of stylistic variation, labels them, and exposes them as sliders with pole previews and diff comparisons. A 16-participant within-subjects study shows reduced mental demand, effort, and frustration versus prompt-only revision.

entry.title: templar: agentic induction and evolution of standardized radiology reporting templates from large-scale clinical corpora

author.name: Xiaotian Hu, Mingxuan Liu, Zhonghan Wang, Xinfeng Zhang, Yiming Huang, Ziang Wang, Kasidit Anmahaepong, Yijin Li, Yifei Chen, Hongjia Yang, Zihan Li, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: TEMPLAR is an agentic framework that induces and continuously evolves standardized radiology reporting templates from large clinical corpora, overcoming context-length limits of single-LLM induction and the static, closed-corpus nature of prior corpus-scale methods. Templates are grounded externally and adapted downstream, addressing the fragility of expert-consensus templates.

entry.title: ClasSAE: Class-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders via Differentiable Feature-Class Affinity

author.name: Jakub St\k{e}pie\'n, Marcin Mazur, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: ClasSAE trains sparse autoencoders so that features are automatically assigned to classes and the encoder is guided toward class-separable representations, using a differentiable top-k operator over a trainable feature-class affinity. This contrasts with post-hoc scoring over frozen dictionaries, aiming to improve reliability of feature-based interventions like unlearning and concept editing.

entry.title: CellSplat4D: PSF-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse Robotic Live-Cell Imaging

author.name: Yingda Tao, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: CellSplat4D reconstructs gaps in sparsely sampled live-cell microscopy by fitting a PSF-aware 4D Gaussian model whose time-continuous blobs carry position, shape, and lifetime, enabling cell tracking and lineage (division) recovery from photon-limited acquisitions. The approach targets robotic microscopes where every volume acquisition costs the specimen precious photons.

entry.title: SelectOccFlow: Selective Spatiotemporal Aggregation for 3D Occupancy and Scene Flow Prediction

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Kai Luo, Yuanfan Zheng, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: SelectOccFlow addresses unreliable spatial and temporal aggregation in camera-based 3D occupancy and scene flow prediction for autonomous driving. It introduces Semantic-Guided Sampling for semantically compatible image evidence plus progressive refinement across image, temporal, and voxel domains.

entry.title: PortraitAes: Intent-Conditioned Structured Portrait Aesthetics Assessment

author.name: Junzhou Xie, Haozhong Xiong, Xunyun Tian, Kaile Du, Tianchen Yu, Qiang Li, Wei Liu, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Huang, Yang Shi, Guangcan Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces PortraitAes-Bench, an 11K-scale benchmark for portrait aesthetic assessment conditioned on photographic intent, arguing that identical visual attributes like blur or lighting can serve one intent but undermine another. Existing single-score models and general MLLMs learn context-agnostic priors and produce inconsistent judgments. The benchmark and intent-conditioned approach support data filtering and preference modeling in image-generation pipelines.

entry.title: Kinematics-Centric Continuous Sign Language Retrieval with Gloss-Guided Boundary-Aware Alignment

author.name: Chang Liu, Ke Han, Davide Talon, Elisa Ricci, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: This work reformulates sign language-text alignment in a structured kinematic space using 3D SMPL-X motion as the primary representation, reducing dependence on appearance-heavy RGB signals that entangle motion semantics with visual variation. A gloss-guided boundary-aware alignment module captures the compositional structure of signing. This improves cross-modal retrieval and sign language understanding robustness.

entry.title: End-to-End Autonomous Recursive Arborescence Deformable Flow and Non-Linear Hemodynamics for Patient-Specific Coronary Centerline Extraction

author.name: Zeyu Jia, Xin Ming

entry.summary: Formulates coronary centerline extraction as an end-to-end framework decoupling continuous geometric arborescence generation from non-linear hemodynamic modeling, avoiding severed bifurcations from voxel segmentation and non-anatomical shortcuts from Euclidean spanning trees. Includes an autonomous ostium landmark localization head and non-linear flow modeling that better captures ischemia across arterial narrowings.

entry.title: Harnessing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-Free Human-Object Interaction Detection

author.name: Zhaolin Cai, Huiyu Duan, Liu Yang, Yanjun Qin, Bo Ai, Wei Chen, Xiongkuo Min, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: This work achieves training-free human-object interaction detection by better coordinating MLLM inference, letting interaction hypotheses actively guide visual exploration rather than running loosely coupled inference stages. It reduces overlooked participants and unresolved ambiguities relative to prior training-free approaches.

entry.title: A Flexible and Generic Approach for Explainable Landscape Analysis and the pyXla Toolbox

author.name: Tony Ombaso, Anna S. Bosman, Arnaud Liefooghe, Katherine M. Malan, S\'ebastien Verel

entry.summary: The paper presents a generic, extensible framework for explainable fitness-landscape analysis, addressing the fragmentation of existing techniques and the poor interpretability of computed landscape features. It is released as the pyXla Python toolbox, enabling practitioners to apply and interpret landscape analysis across diverse problem domains.

entry.title: Return-to-Home Feasible Micro-Aerial Vehicle Exploration for 3D Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction

author.name: Prajit Krisshnakumar, Fan Yang, Koichiro Niinuma

entry.summary: This work presents a topology-first active reconstruction framework for indoor MAV exploration under strict flight-time budgets, decoupling high-fidelity 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering from a lightweight TSDF/occupancy scaffold used for collision checking. It builds a sparse 3D Voronoi skeleton roadmap to ensure return-to-home feasibility with conservative margins.

entry.title: Safe Ergodic Control for Multi-Robot Systems via Quadratic Programming

author.name: Yo Toyomoto, Mohamed Elobaid, Bryce L. Ferguson, Alberto Quattrini Li, Shinkyu Park

entry.summary: Introduces a QP-based multi-robot ergodic controller that jointly optimizes coverage (time spent proportional to a target spatial distribution) and safety, using a new Gaussian-kernel ergodic metric that is time differentiable. This differentiability allows exponential decay of the metric to be imposed as a time-varying control barrier function constraint, enabling real-time safe ergodic coverage without offline trajectory optimization.

entry.title: Learning Coordinated Visuomotor Box-Pushing from Solo Demonstrations

author.name: Ryusei Matsumoto, Mei Kinjo, Yoko Sasaki, Keisuke Okumura

entry.summary: This work investigates whether teleoperated single-robot demonstrations can train decentralized, communication-free multi-robot visuomotor policies for coordinated box-pushing, avoiding the difficulty of collecting collective demonstrations. It systematically studies dataset creation for this multi-robot imitation learning setting.

entry.title: Recon2Servo: Robotic Ultrasound Visual Servoing via Learned Image-to-Motion Inference

author.name: Yameng Zhang, Pei Liu, Dianye Huang, Yizhao Qian, Zhongyu Chen, Xiangyu Chu, K. W. Samuel Au, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: Recon2Servo learns 6-DoF ultrasound probe control directly from 2D B-mode images, using a LoRA-finetuned DINOv3 encoder and a bidirectional relation module to estimate relative probe pose for closed-loop target-view alignment. This avoids reliance on anatomical priors or handcrafted features, improving generalizability across imaging targets.

entry.title: Radar2Plan: Benchmarking 4D Radar for End-to-End Open-Loop Ego-Trajectory Planning

author.name: Ling Yao, Yichun Xiao, Jin Jin, Yihan Zhang, Fangqiang Ding

entry.summary: Radar2Plan is a modular benchmark connecting 4D radar encoders, scene representations, and planning heads through common interfaces for open-loop ego-trajectory planning, evaluated on real-world datasets (DSERT-RoLL and MAN TruckScenes). It fills a gap where existing 4D radar benchmarks target perception rather than downstream planning, especially under adverse weather and poor illumination. The benchmark enables controlled comparisons of sensor and planner configurations.

entry.title: Stochastic Shortest Path: Minimax, Parameter-Free and Towards Horizon-Free Regret

author.name: Jean Tarbouriech, Runlong Zhou, Simon S. Du, Matteo Pirotta, Michal Valko, Alessandro Lazaric

entry.summary: The paper studies reinforcement learning in the stochastic shortest path setting, where an agent minimizes expected cost to reach a goal state without a fixed horizon. It proposes EB-SSP, a model-based algorithm achieving the minimax regret rate in terms of the optimal expected cumulative cost, closing the gap with the lower bound. This is a significant theoretical advance toward horizon-free RL.

entry.title: VA-learning as a more efficient alternative to Q-learning

author.name: Yunhao Tang, R\'emi Munos, Mark Rowland, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper introduces VA-learning, which directly learns advantage and value functions via bootstrapping without explicitly learning Q-functions, retaining Q-learning-like off-policy theoretical guarantees. This improves sample efficiency in both tabular settings and deep RL agents on Atari-57, and reveals a connection to the dueling architecture. It offers a simple rethinking of canonical value-based RL.

entry.title: Bridging the EHR Divide: Asymmetric Contrastive Learning for Cross-National Medical Representation Transfer

author.name: Qingyang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose Asymmetric Supervised Contrastive Learning, a pre-training objective that clusters patients sharing a target positive outcome without pulling negative trajectories together, motivated by clinical outcome heterogeneity. They pre-train temporal Transformers on 3.98 million patients from Taiwan's NHIRD database and transfer to two U.S. EHR datasets.

entry.title: AdaSpark: Adaptive DSpark with Online Learning for Tree Verification and N-gram Fill

author.name: Liquan Liu, Yifan Zhang, Bowei Xu

entry.summary: Introduces AdaSpark, an online-learning scheduler for speculative decoding with block drafters that learns both verification-width value and per-candidate acceptance rates while serving, without prior profiling or calibration. It adaptively trades off expected accepted tokens against verification cost in tree-structured draft verification.

entry.title: Periscope: Extending Frozen Language Models Beyond Their Context Window

author.name: Mohamed Eltahir, Anas Obayd, Raed Rashid, Abdulrahman Alghamdi, Abdulrahman Mousa, Abdallah Ahmed, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: Periscope is a training-free inference method that arranges N text chunks on a K-by-K grid, queries a frozen model over K local consecutive spans and K strided spans, and reads answer log-odds at a single token to build an evidence map without extra cost. It factorizes long-text reading for finite decision tasks such as relevance or evidence selection. This offers a cheap alternative to context extension for document-level QA and retrieval decisions.

entry.title: Gradient-Free Sampling from Generative Models via Stochastic Bounded Extremum Seeking

author.name: Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: Introduces a sampling approach for energy- and score-based generative models requiring no gradient evaluations, replacing the score drift term with a high-frequency dithered cosine of the model value. The authors prove convergence of the dithered Ito SDE trajectories to those of the target Langevin or reverse-diffusion SDE via an averaging argument extending bounded extremum seeking. A control-theoretic route to score-free sampling.

entry.title: SALUS: Automated Auditing of NL-to-SQL Benchmarks through Weak Supervision of Multi-Agent Output

author.name: Shiyuan Zhou, Ashwin Gerard Colaco, Sainyam Galhotra, Sharad Mehrotra

entry.summary: SALUS automatically detects annotation errors in natural-language-to-SQL benchmarks by framing auditing as weakly supervised error detection, using SQL outputs from multiple LLM agents to drive complementary labeling functions and a generative label model. Since known benchmarks contain significant annotation errors that distort reported progress, this improves evaluation reliability. It matters for the credibility of text-to-SQL leaderboards and model comparisons.

entry.title: Organize Primitives into Semantic Parts: Reinforcement Reasoning for 3D Segmentation

author.name: Xiaoming Gong, Ruoyu Wu, Zhenhong Sun, Chunlin Chen, Daoyi Dong, Huadong Mo, Zhi Wang, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: RePart formulates organizing 3D primitives into semantic parts as a finite-horizon Markov decision process solved with trajectory-level reinforcement reasoning, building on a Composable Primitive Workspace of superquadrics. It addresses the fact that geometric decomposition alone cannot determine semantic part membership.

entry.title: Salvation Lies Within: Eliciting Inherent Style Transfer in Step-Distilled Diffusion Models

author.name: Shengyin Sun, Yiming Li, Yingzhao Lian, Xing Li, Xingzhi Zhou, Anxin Tian, Zhili Wang, Haoyang Li, Ziqiang Cui, Chen Ma

entry.summary: StyleForge is a fully automatic, training-free framework that elicits style-transfer capability already encoded in step-distilled text-to-image models, expressing reference styles as reusable rendering instructions combining overall rendering characteristics with local color information. This avoids costly post-training adaptation that alters native few-step generation behavior. It offers a complementary, language-driven route to stylization in fast generation models.

entry.title: From Transformation to Target State: Rethinking Query Representation for Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Yihe Zhao, Songhe Feng

entry.summary: Identifies a representational asymmetry in zero-shot composed image retrieval: modification text describes a transition from the reference state while candidates depict completed target states. It reformulates the task as target-state reconstruction followed by retrieval and instantiates ASAP-CIR, a training-free framework built on a frozen multimodal model.

entry.title: STC-MPM: Coupled Deformation, Progressive Damage, and Cut Formation in Soft-Tissue Cutting

author.name: Kewei Zuo, Jiahe Chen, Ziao Kuang, Junsheng Zhu, Etsuko Kobayashi

entry.summary: STC-MPM is a Material Point Method framework coupling finite-strain deformation, history-driven continuum damage, and configurable post-failure behavior to simulate soft-tissue cutting, where blade motion may deform rather than cut compliant material. Damage initiates only when tensile strain history exceeds a material threshold, linking incision formation to evolving mechanical response. Relevant applications span surgical robotics and food handling automation.

entry.title: Orchestrating Level-$K$ Policies Against Unknown Opponents in Partially-Observable Dynamic Games

author.name: Addison Kalanther, Sanika Bharvirkar, Daniel Bostwick, Chinmay Maheshwari, Shankar Sastry

entry.summary: This paper formulates deployment against opponents of unknown reasoning level as dynamic orchestration of a fixed pretrained Level-K policy library in a partially observable Markov game, showing that selecting the response of the most likely opponent level need not maximize expected return. It compares classification-based orchestrators trained offline or on-policy against reinforcement-learning-based orchestrators. This connects opponent modeling, game theory, and library-based policy selection.

entry.title: SGAnalog: An End-to-End Circuit Benchmark from Open-Source Silicon Tapeouts

author.name: Yueting Li, Weihang Ding

entry.summary: SGAnalog is a benchmark of 273 topologically distinct analog circuit designs from Tiny Tapeout open-source silicon submissions, pairing schematic images with SPICE netlists under fixed, containerized processing. It tests whether models learn transferable circuit skills and whether outputs work under defined process and test conditions.

entry.title: Auditing Pairwise Equivalence Judgments: Self-Critique Effects and Diversity Measurement in Multi-Agent Hypothesis Generation

author.name: Ji Young Byun, Anthony Hu, Jesse Rogers, Roujia Wang, Manasa Kesapragada, Falgun Shah

entry.summary: The paper studies two evaluation questions for multi-agent scientific hypothesis generation: how much self-critique changes delivered hypotheses beyond run-to-run variability, and how the pairwise equivalence rule used to group hypotheses affects measured diversity, across four proprietary instances with fixed opening hypotheses.

entry.title: VIGIL: Verifier-Informed Gated Improvement Loop for Spreadsheet Question Answering

author.name: Kang Li, Lu He, Sandarsita Guntupalli

entry.summary: VIGIL is a continual-learning framework for enterprise spreadsheet question answering that verifies and repairs SQL candidates within questions, while across episodes updating only a small calibrator and selector under gated feedback, keeping the base model and prompts frozen. This design lets enterprise agents improve from delayed feedback without letting every correction rewrite system behavior. It builds on the FiCo retrieval-and-execution backbone.

entry.title: MERCI Cards: An LLM Evaluation and Deployment Framework for High-Stakes Domains

author.name: Aparna Komarla, Annalisa Szymanski

entry.summary: Presents MERCI Cards, a mathematical framework for iterative LLM evaluation and deployment in high-stakes, resource-constrained domains, demonstrated on AI systems used in criminal justice. The framework formalizes model selection, rubric design, evaluation, and deployment as weighted multi-objective optimization and guides improvements across deployment cycles.

entry.title: Towards Credible Agent-Based Policy Simulations: Disentangling Opportunities and Preferences in a Financial Inclusion Case Study of Egypt

author.name: Alba Aguilera, Georgina Curto, Nardine Osman, Ahmed Al-Awah

entry.summary: This paper presents a general framework, aligned with the Capability Approach, for building credible agent-based policy simulations grounded in data and domain-expert knowledge, disentangling opportunities from preferences in agent behavior. It is demonstrated through a financial inclusion case study in Egypt with heterogeneous individuals and firms.

entry.title: Toward a Locally Deployable Agentic Co-Scientist: Small-Model Planning for Early-Stage Drug Discovery

author.name: Tian Liang, Jiayu Chang, Alejandro F. Frangi, Mobarak I. Hoque, Richard A. Bryce

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight, tool-augmented agentic framework in which a locally deployable compact language model plans calls to 18 modular drug-discovery tools, with a Unified Molecular Schema and LoRA fine-tuning across three compact model families on 1,263 curated query-plan pairs. Fine-tuned Llama 3.2-3B reaches near-perfect tool-selection F1 and schema-compliant plan generation on held-out queries, enabling privacy-preserving local deployment.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Time-Series Question Answering via Decoupled Perception and Reasoning

author.name: Jing Xie, Haochen Yuan, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: TSHarness is an agentic framework for cross-dataset zero-shot time-series QA that decouples numerical perception from contextual reasoning via a structured Time-Series Perception State, with a learned tool selector invoking numerical tools guided by a reusable memory of analytical knowledge. It targets generalization when input series, question contexts, and answer formats shift simultaneously.

entry.title: Why, Where, How: Taxonomy-guided Error Grounding for Code Repair in NL2SQL

author.name: Suchan Lee, Woomin Song, Hwanjo Yu, Sangwoo Mo

entry.summary: TEG turns a supplied error diagnosis into a structured correction input for NL2SQL repair, mapping error types to construct classes to reconsider and specific edit operations, including masking selected query constructs. It addresses the problem that executable-but-wrong SQL reveals neither why, where, nor how to fix the query.

entry.title: Image Synthesis as an Intermediate for Controllable Time Series Generation

author.name: Haochen Yuan, Jing Xie, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: VisualBridge uses time-series plots as a visual intermediate representation to bridge language-level temporal semantics and numerical sequence generation, exploiting multimodal LLMs' strength in image understanding. An MLLM converts plotted series into structured semantic representations with controllable trend, seasonality, and volatility, and a semantic editing policy trained with forecasting rewards generates task-beneficial sequences.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Limited Clustering Gains: A Controlled Study of Multilingual Company Entity Resolution

author.name: Yijiashun Qi, Yuxuan Li, Hanzhe Guo

entry.summary: This controlled study adapts multilingual E5 encoders for company entity resolution and finds that large retrieval improvements (direct pair recall rising from 53.74% to 76.98%) translate into minimal clustering gains because the downstream pair classifier is unchanged. The negative result clarifies that entity resolution pipelines must be co-optimized end to end.

entry.title: Data-Driven Personas for Survey Simulation: Insights into Simulation Alignment Across Data-Access Regimes

author.name: Dongryeol Lee, Weronika {\L}ajewska, Leonardo Perelli, Saab Mansour

entry.summary: This work studies demographic group-level survey simulation where personas are induced from heterogeneous anonymized public behavioral data rather than costly target-domain human data. The authors find that out-of-domain personas rarely beat simulations conditioned only on basic demographics, largely due to population mismatch, offering practical guidance on data regimes for LLM survey simulation.

entry.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design

author.name: Haosen Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: EASER is a reflective agent that bridges literature reasoning and biological sequence generation by steering a diffusion-based generator through learned low-rank property matrices, proposing intervention hypotheses such as anchors and editable positions. It targets the gap where LLMs can devise design strategies from scientific text but cannot reliably implement them for sequences.

entry.title: GraphDecide: Benchmarking System One Models on Graph Tasks

author.name: Xianliang Yang, Yapu Zhang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: GraphDecide is a model-independent benchmark for evaluating choice-based System One models (such as Jev) on graph decision tasks, using structural task profiles, matched graph-text contrasts, and heuristic-proposal controls across fourteen model configurations. Results show that accurate adjacency recognition does not guarantee broader structural correctness.

entry.title: Conditional Rank Allocation for Taxonomy-Aware Medical Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Guangyuan Dong, Ziwei Hong, Xuehao Zhou, Zidong Yu, Bingchen Liu, Kehan Liu, Chuang Liu, Rong Fu, Yuchao Hou

entry.summary: ARBOR is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for medical question answering that selects rank-one components from a shared low-rank basis per question, using a gate that combines question representations with specialty and operation tags. The paper provides an illustrative theoretical separation showing conditional selection can beat fixed low-rank updates, and demonstrates gains with Qwen3-8B across CMB, CMExam, MedQA, and MedMCQA benchmarks.

entry.title: WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration

author.name: Le Chen, Lixin Liu, Jan Schneider, Zeju Qiu, Simon Guist, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Dieter B\"uchler

entry.summary: WAMJET is an agentic harness that accelerates inference of World Action Models for robot manipulation by equipping coding agents with reusable optimization guidance plus measurement and validation tools. It follows a bottleneck-driven workflow where the agent profiles, modifies targeted code, validates, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack while preserving model behavior.

entry.title: The Score Is Not the Structure: Brain Alignment and Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Saman Rahbar

entry.summary: This methodological critique examines what brain-similarity and cross-lingual transfer scores actually measure, showing that in cross-lingual probing, the probe itself often fails: in four of seventeen languages it performs at chance, so 64 of 272 language pairs were scored with a non-functioning tool, and dropping those pairs substantially weakens the claimed shared-structure relationship. It cautions against interpreting similarity scores as evidence of shared structure between models, brains, or languages.

entry.title: Streaming Multi-Track Timeline Control for 3D Human Motion Generation

author.name: Yangsong Zhang, Anujith Muraleedharan, Rikhat Akizhanov, G\"ul Varol, Fabio Pizzati, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: TimelineControl enables interactive 3D human motion generation where new text instructions arrive during synthesis while ongoing actions continue, such as answering a phone while walking. It combines interval-aware conditioning, causal part-structured representations, and part-aware denoising to coordinate overlapping, independently timed action tracks. This is a meaningful step beyond one-shot text-to-motion generation toward real-time interactive applications.

entry.title: DUET: Co-Evolving Solver and Grader Agents

author.name: Fengyu Gao, Sourav Pal, Austin Z. Henley, Arjun Radhakrishna, Gustavo Soares

entry.summary: DUET addresses the coupled challenge of continually improving agentic workflows and evaluating them: as a solver agent evolves, its failure modes change and a fixed evaluator becomes inadequate. The framework co-evolves a solver agent and a grader agent so that evaluation improves alongside behavior, providing feedback for optimization. This tackles a fundamental problem for deployed agents in technology, finance, and enterprise settings.

entry.title: Scaling of Wireless Foundation Models via Representation Diversity and Multi-Branch Architectures

author.name: Ahmed Mohamed, Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Hatem Abou-Zeid

entry.summary: The paper proposes objective diversity as an alternative scaling axis for wireless foundation models, fusing frozen representations from independent encoders trained with reconstructive, predictive, and contrastive objectives. This preserves more signal information than pure capacity scaling when pretraining data are limited, improving downstream task performance.

entry.title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni

entry.summary: This theory paper studies p-mean social welfare maximization for allocating indivisible goods with multiplicities encoded in binary, unifying Nash welfare and egalitarian criteria. It proves NP-hardness for every fixed rational p<1 with only two item types, Nash and egalitarian hardness with three item types, and strong NP-hardness with a single agent type and unrestricted item types.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Stress Testing of Overload Monitoring for Resilient Emergency Cellular Networks Using Internet CDR Proxies

author.name: Bilal Hussain, Xiao Tang, Tan Li, Muhammad Azhar, Danista Khan, Fawad Ahmad

entry.summary: Trains a lightweight CNN to detect cellular network overload during emergencies using Call Detail Record aggregates as a privacy-friendly proxy for signaling stress, then stress-tests and adapts the detector with diffusion-synthesized surge patterns. Shows default alert thresholds fail under realistic stress-test conditions.

entry.title: Towards Automatically Pruning Logging Code with Coding Agents: How Far Are We?

author.name: He Yang Yuan, Haonan Zhang, Xin Wang, An Ran Chen, Kisub Kim, Zishuo Ding, Zhenhao Li

entry.summary: This software engineering study examines logging code removal, an underexplored counterpart to logging generation, by mining and validating real-world removal cases from Python and Java repositories. The authors derive 10 removal patterns and 11 removal reasons and introduce LogRem, a 387-case dataset for benchmarking coding agents on automatic logging pruning.

entry.title: PreAct-Nav: Agentic Reasoning Before Action for Urban Navigation

author.name: Jing Xie, Shouwei Ruan, Yubin Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Junwei Yang, Songchang Jin, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: PreAct-Nav equips frozen embodied navigation policies with anticipatory agentic reasoning for long-horizon urban navigation, anchoring local decisions in persistent predictions about action consequences and future conditions. It aims to translate distant goals into coherent local decisions where linguistic reasoning over transient observations falls short.

entry.title: Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: S K Swaminathan, Damiya Gondha, Theyanesh Eswaramoorthy Rajahkrishnan, Aritra Hazra

entry.summary: Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP) modify Contrastive Reinforcement Learning by conditioning the policy on direction and distance to selected visited-state waypoints in representation space during online training, then applying the same interface directly to the final goal at deployment without planning. Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP beats CRL on seven tasks and spends more time near the goal. It exploits the reachability geometry learned by the contrastive critic that raw-goal conditioning ignores.

entry.title: Settling the Computational Complexity of Max-Min Allocation with Ternary Valuations

author.name: Thi Ngoc Anh Vu, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni, J\"{o}rg Rothe

entry.summary: This theory paper settles complexity questions for allocating indivisible goods to maximize egalitarian welfare under ternary valuation classes. It gives a polynomial-time algorithm for additive {p,q}-valuations when p=2, constant-gap hardness for p>=3, an approximation ratio for bi-valued cases, and resolves a conjectured tractability for {-2,0,c} valuations via reduction to maximum-weight perfect matching.

entry.title: IRSTD-Agent: Agentic Infrared Small Target Detection via Zoom-Guided Interaction Learning

author.name: Jiawen Xi, Yu Zhang, Tianyi Zhao, Zhu Liu, Maoxun Yuan, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: IRSTD-Agent is an agentic framework where a multimodal LLM adaptively decides where and at what scale to inspect an image for infrared small-target detection, using five tools (PROPOSAL, ZOOM, DETECT, DROP, REFINE) to progressively gather fine-grained visual evidence. It targets maritime monitoring and aerial surveillance applications where precise localization of small targets has challenged MLLM approaches.

entry.title: BeliefGraph-JEPA: Structured Latent World Models for Action-Conditioned Time Series

author.name: Yue Li, Kangqi Ni, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: BeliefGraph-JEPA is a structured latent world model for action-conditioned time-series forecasting that factorizes driver influence into typed latent-effect states evolving over the forecast horizon. It routes influence to individual targets rather than relying on static relational graphs or implicit direct conditioning.

entry.title: Cut Binary Cross Entropy: Efficient Large-Vocabulary Loss and Gradient Kernels for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yaoyiran Li, Haowen Ning, Mohamed Hammad

entry.summary: CutBCE is an exact, hardware-accelerated BCE loss and gradient operator implemented in JAX and Pallas for large-vocabulary sequential recommendation, avoiding the O(BNV) memory blowup of dense logits materialization that causes OOM errors. It adapts chunked-loss techniques, previously developed for softmax cross-entropy in LLMs, to the unexplored multi-label BCE setting.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Time-Series Inference of Lindblad Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems

author.name: Julian Guam, Jianqing Liu

entry.summary: Applies a raw time-series Transformer to infer unknown, potentially time-dependent dissipation rates and Hamiltonian parameters of open quantum systems governed by the Lindblad master equation, removing the hand-crafted features of prior work. This is an AI-for-physics contribution showing transformers can perform system identification under decoherence where analytical inversion fails. It matters as evidence that sequence models can invert complex physical dynamics directly from trajectories.

entry.title: Relational Synthesis: Structure-Mediated Concatenative Synthesis for Foley and Retrieval-Augmented Audio Generation

author.name: Keren Shao, Ayaka Kawano, Shlomo Dubnov

entry.summary: The paper introduces relational synthesis, a variant of concatenative synthesis that replaces a target-matching cost with a relational Gromov-like structural cost, enabling generation of novel audio that stays acoustically consistent with a retrieved source without verbatim copying. This simultaneously addresses a Foley production goal and the well-known copying problem in retrieval-augmented neural audio generation. The approach offers a non-neural-network-based angle on the RAG fidelity-versus-copying tradeoff.

entry.title: On Hyperparameter Tuning on the Test Set

author.name: Matteo Fregonara, Tom Viering, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: This paper empirically quantifies how much performance inflation actually results from tuning hyperparameters on the test set, a practice usually treated as a cardinal sin in machine learning. Using MNIST-1D, CIFAR-10, and GLUE tasks, the authors systematically measure the magnitude of the effect and question how severe the dogma-violation truly is. The findings suggest the inflation is real but its size may be smaller than folklore implies.

entry.title: JLD: Perceptual Distance Through A Jacobian Lens

author.name: Shreshth Saini, Balu Adsumilli, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: Jacobian Lens Distance is a new perceptual image distance that derives its geometry from a frozen vision encoder rather than fitted human judgments, making it more robust across resolutions where label-fitted metrics degrade. It uses the encoder Jacobian to combine locality of early patch features with perceptual sensitivity of deeper representations. This targets applications in compression, restoration, and generation.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Objective Evaluation of Modern Text-to-Speech for Turkish Using Speech Quality Assessment Models

author.name: Yunus Emre Ozkose, Alperen Kahraman, Ali Haznedaroglu

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks four modern TTS systems (Chatterbox, CosyVoice, OmniVoice, VoxCPM2) in fine-tuned and zero-shot configurations for Turkish, a morphologically rich lower-resource language, comparing them against a VITS baseline and natural speech. It uses eighteen objective quality metrics spanning learned naturalness predictors and intelligibility estimators. The work matters because TTS evaluation on non-English, morphologically complex languages is under-characterized.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Calibration of Pre-Generation Success Probes for Multilingual LLM Routing

author.name: Andrea Paganelli, Stefano Civelli, Pietro Bernardelle, Gianluca Demartini

entry.summary: The paper examines whether pre-generation success probes, which estimate response correctness from hidden activations, remain reliable across languages along discrimination, calibration, and utility dimensions. Using MATH problems in 10 languages and 8 open-weight models, it compares English-trained probes against language-specific alternatives for cost-aware multilingual routing. The findings inform whether cheap probe-based routing generalizes beyond English.

entry.title: ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data

author.name: Amogh Singh, Yash Shah, Chiara D'Ercoli, Arash Mehrjou, Patrick Schwab, Timothy Jones, Pietro Li\`{o}

entry.summary: ARO learns aligned representations from multi-omics cancer data to reconstruct missing and unpaired modalities, prioritizing practical applicability in incomplete-data settings over large foundation models. It achieves low reconstruction MSE and latent embeddings that support downstream biological reasoning.

entry.title: Topology-Informed Prompt-Conditioned Universal Segmentation of Uterine Structures from Ultrasound and MRI

author.name: Yongheng Sun, Yuexi Gu, Jingwen Sun, Maureen Kohi, Mingxia Liu

entry.summary: TPUS is a unified prompt-conditioned segmentation framework for multiple uterine structures across ultrasound and MRI, using topology-informed constraints and modality prompts to handle heterogeneous appearances, resolutions, and label spaces while avoiding negative transfer. It supports screening and treatment planning for uterine diseases.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Guided Discovery of Weight-Five Bivariate Bicycle Codes

author.name: Juan Cruz-Benito

entry.summary: Building on an earlier LLM-guided program-evolution workflow, the author catalogs 1,142 weight-five bivariate bicycle code proposals, mostly attributable to LLM-generated programs, certifying several CSS realizations with strong parameters such as [[180,4,14]]. It provides exact distance evidence and verified constructions, demonstrating LLM-guided search as a tool for quantum code discovery. This extends AI-assisted discovery into quantum error-correcting code design.

entry.title: TreeWalker: Partial Evaluation for Grouped Tree-Ensemble Inference

author.name: Durmus Karatay, Richard Newman

entry.summary: Presents TreeWalker, which applies partial evaluation to grouped tree-ensemble inference where rows share feature values, walking each tree once per group and skipping constant features and empty subtrees. It works directly on standard LightGBM and XGBoost models without retraining and comes with a structural work decomposition and speedup analysis.

entry.title: Evolving LLM-Generated Features for Interpretable Classification

author.name: Jack Butler, Zainab Afolabi, Nikita Kozodoi

entry.summary: Proposes an evolutionary framework where an LLM generates candidate natural-language binary feature definitions (rubrics), evaluates samples against them, and evolves the feature set guided by classification errors, per-class activation rates, and ablation scores. The resulting features feed transparent classifiers like logistic regression, targeting regulated domains such as credit scoring and medical diagnosis.

entry.title: Ideal Paths for Approximating Logistic Gradient Descent Trajectories at Large Initialization

author.name: Junjie Xiao, Huiwen Jia

entry.summary: Constructs a unique continuous ideal path approximating full-batch logistic gradient descent trajectories under large initialization, using minimum-norm projection rules, going beyond classical implicit-bias results that characterize only the limiting direction. This gives geometric insight into how fine-tuning from pretrained models evolves. Relevant to understanding transfer learning dynamics.

entry.title: Do RUL explanations hold up? Faithfulness and stability of attributions on C-MAPSS

author.name: Manh Hien Nguyen, Ngoc Thanh Nguyen, Isabella Mendoza Cortes, Tam Khuat, Thanh Pham, Nhat Quang Tran, Ushik Shrestha Khwakhali, Loan Do

entry.summary: Trains 1D CNN, LSTM, and Transformer models for remaining-useful-life prediction on NASA C-MAPSS and rigorously audits Integrated Gradients, occlusion, and attention attributions using deletion/insertion faithfulness, noise stability, cross-seed agreement, and within-RUL consistency checks. It highlights evaluation gaps in the XAI-for-predictive-maintenance literature. A useful negative-results and rigor contribution.

entry.title: UnAct: Gradient-Free Unlearning via Targeted Activation Intervention

author.name: Saeed Abdul Muizz, Aayat Rafiq, Iqra Altaf Gillani, Janibul Bashir

entry.summary: UnAct is a machine unlearning method that removes class information from a trained image classifier using only forward passes over a few forget images: it scores late-layer units by their responses to the forget data and attenuates the most responsive connections over repeated rounds, requiring no gradients or labels. This contrasts with retrain-free baselines like SSD/LFSSD that still need backpropagation over the full dataset. It matters for privacy-sensitive deletion requests with limited forget data.

entry.title: Anticipating the Consequences of Curriculum Decisions with Large Language Models

author.name: Octavio Pappalardo, Nathan Herr, Tim Rockt\"aschel

entry.summary: The paper frames automatic curriculum learning as a sequential decision-making problem and identifies a gap between quantities that determine curriculum decision value and the local learning signals typically used to guide them. It investigates whether LLMs, given richer information about the learning problem, can better anticipate the consequences of curriculum decisions, introducing a method combining online learning-progress estimates with LLM-informed prediction. A novel direction of using LLMs as world models for training dynamics.

entry.title: Localized Operator Learning with Adaptive Partition-of-Unity Mixture-of-Expert Networks

author.name: Madison Cooley, Ramansh Sharma, Shandian Zhe, Robert M. Kirby, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: The authors introduce a partition-of-unity mixture-of-experts framework for neural operator learning, where geometry-aware gating networks create smooth spatial partitions blending local expert networks, with a hierarchical architecture called HiRefPOU for DeepONets. They also adapt the same principle to Fourier Neural Operators to add spatial adaptivity for PDEs with sharp interfaces and multiscale structure.

entry.title: Physics-Augmented Graph Transformers for Patch-Antenna Forward and Inverse Design

author.name: Avi Epstein, Snir Nehemia, Haim Suchowski, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: The authors present a physics-augmented graph transformer framework that predicts antenna radiation patterns as signal reconstruction on irregular surface meshes. An auxiliary objective predicting complex surface currents (PAIS) improves multiple GNN backbones at no inference cost, and the framework also supports inverse design.

entry.title: Private Component-by-Component Learning

author.name: Dvir Karni, Eliad Tsfadia

entry.summary: The paper studies differentially private learning of hypotheses specified by k components in the realizable setting, overcoming the problem that approximate component choices can destroy exact realizability. Using LabelBoost and alternating data reservoirs, it achieves only a root-k over epsilon privacy sample overhead relative to single-component active learning.

entry.title: Underscoring the Problem: Why Softpick Fails at Initialization

author.name: Aryan Sood, Jaikaran Singh, Ishaan Bansal

entry.summary: The paper explains why Softpick attention (which removes softmax attention sinks by rectifying scores) fails at scale, reframing the failure as a normalization problem at initialization where denominator rows cause divergent behavior. It proposes a family of operators that independently choose the positive- and negative-shifted denominators.

entry.title: Joint Estimation of Common-Slope Decay Rates and Spatial Amplitudes Using Parameterized Nonnegative Matrix Factorization

author.name: Jeremy B. Bai, Filip Elvander, Sebastian J. Schlecht

entry.summary: Formulates joint estimation of common-slope decay rates and spatial amplitudes from room impulse responses as parameterized nonnegative matrix factorization with the Itakura-Saito divergence. It derives closed-form amplitude updates and a convex decay-rate update via a SAGE algorithm, plus a contribution-weighted variant to accelerate estimation, producing detailed reverberation-time curves without backward integration.

entry.title: Square-Root Regret for Adversarial Multiplayer Bandits without Collision Information or Shared Randomness

author.name: Chenyu Gan

entry.summary: Addresses adversarial multiplayer bandits with multiple labeled players and no collision information, shared randomness, or communication channel, designing a communication and synchronization protocol with a Monte Carlo public constructor. Achieves square-root regret simultaneously for all oblivious reward sequences with high probability after preprocessing.

entry.title: Discovered, Not Designed: Population Evolution for Collaborative and Compute-Intensive Model Discovery

author.name: Bo Peng, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Yifan Wu, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: The authors introduce Population Evolution (PE), a hierarchical framework where LLM-driven searches across related training instances share experimental evidence to guide code-change proposals and promotion to larger training scales. For expensive targets, PE screens candidates on small subsets via peer and intermediate evaluations before full-scale training. They also release RMD-Bench to evaluate both transfer and compute-constrained settings on ranking and watch-time tasks.

entry.title: Joint Precision Neural Networks: Task-Aware Dependency and Predictive Learning

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Samuel Rey, Antonio G. Marques, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: The paper proposes task-aware learning of precision matrix structures, extending PCA and covariance neural networks by exploiting the inverse covariance, which encodes conditional independencies rather than raw correlations. It addresses the instability of finite-sample precision estimates by jointly learning regularized, task-dependent graph structures alongside prediction.

entry.title: Sampling Allocation of LinUCB: Optimal Design Limits in the Small-Gap Regime

author.name: Yujie Liu, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Yunbei Xu

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes the sampling allocation of LinUCB in the small-gap regime where reward gaps scale as n^{-1/2}, the hard instances underlying worst-case regret lower bounds. Using a mean-field perspective on the empirical sampling distribution, it proves LinUCB's allocation converges to D-optimal experimental designs. This connects bandit adaptivity to classical optimal design theory in the regime where LinUCB is near-optimal.

entry.title: Generative World Models Enable Predictive Control of Laser Melt Pool Dynamics

author.name: Yiyang Yan, Markus Bambach, Mohamadreza Afrasiabi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a generative world model for laser melt pool dynamics in additive manufacturing, predicting evolution from temperature and phase morphology histories under candidate laser actions. Generative latent dynamics capture unresolved melt flow effects, enabling more accurate recursive rollouts than deterministic regressors, and the differentiable learned dynamics support predictive control. This brings the world-model paradigm to manufacturing process control at timescales beyond high-fidelity simulation.

entry.title: Improving Proactive AI Assistance with Hierarchical Procedural Understanding

author.name: Jin-Seop Lee, TaeYeon Won, SeongJun Jung, JungHoon Kim, Boyang Albert Li, Jin-Young Park, Jaehong Yoon, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: The paper addresses proactive AI assistants that observe user activity and decide when and what guidance to offer, arguing that existing datasets support only fixed-granularity or detection-based proactive understanding. The authors introduce data and methods incorporating hierarchical procedural structure so guidance can adapt to fine-grained task progress and user expertise. This targets a practically important capability for next-generation assistants.

entry.title: Adapting prior-data fitted networks for tabular anomaly detection

author.name: Maximilian Bershtman, Niv Cohen

entry.summary: This work investigates how TabPFN representations can be adapted for tabular anomaly detection under the difficult constraints of no labeled anomalies at deployment and a contaminated reference set that may itself contain anomalies. The authors begin with frozen TabPFN features and study scoring approaches suited to these conditions.

entry.title: Online Control via Counterfactual Tracking

author.name: Yunzong Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies online control of known linear dynamical systems with adversarial costs, introducing counterfactual tracking, which decouples learning from control: an online learner builds a reference trajectory from benchmark policies' counterfactual trajectories and a corrective law steers the system toward it. Charging each reference change its recovery cost reduces the problem to online learning with switching costs, yielding regret guarantees against general benchmark classes.

entry.title: Same Output, Different Gold: Measuring How Reference Choice Moves a Multilingual Benchmark Score

author.name: Parth Kulshreshtha, Shivali Dalmia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: The authors exploit a rare dual-annotation record from a six-language PII benchmark to hold system outputs fixed and swap the gold reference, measuring how benchmark scores move. Score shifts of up to 4.95 F1 points (7.55 in the worst language) show reference choice is a substantial and often ignored source of benchmark variance. This is a valuable methodological caution for interpreting leaderboard differences.

entry.title: Frame-Level Temporal Alignment for Human-to-Robot Visual Adaptation

author.name: Xizhe Zhang, Jingfeng Zhang, Zirun Zhou, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Proposes Frame-Level Temporal Alignment (FLTA), a framework that adapts visual encoders pretrained on human videos to robot manipulation by learning shared task-progress representations without frame-level correspondence annotations. It handles differences in execution rate and non-key frame proportions between human and robot demonstrations using two temporal priors. This improves transfer from abundant human video data to robot learning.

entry.title: All against the machine: the Solo score for rating skill in variable environments

author.name: David Reguera, Xavier R. Hoffmann, Irene P\'erez, Pol Colomer-de-Sim\'on, Miquel Masoliver, Xavier Guardiola, Jan Wedekind, Mari\'an Bogu\~n\'a

entry.summary: Proposes the Solo score, a distribution-free metric for rating individual skill in player-versus-environment settings with heterogeneous tasks, high randomness, and no direct opponents. Each task outcome is mapped to a bounded performance score with zero population mean and variance bounded by 1/3, enabling direct cross-task comparison, with a reshuffling-based significance test. Applicable to games, education, finance, and AI agent benchmarking.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Bregman Douglas-Rachford Splitting for Discrete Optimal Transport

author.name: Yifan Xu, Shiqian Ma

entry.summary: This work develops GPU-accelerated Bregman Douglas-Rachford splitting solvers for discrete optimal transport across three input formats (cost matrix, point cloud, grid-based separable cost), with hardware-aware algorithmic designs. The implementations reportedly achieve state-of-the-art runtime against eight GPU baseline solvers in what the authors call the first cross-solver GPU study.

entry.title: Static Bootstrap Placement for Encrypted Language Model Decoding

author.name: Halil Ibrahim Kanpak, Didem Unat

entry.summary: AR-HE runs the full autoregressive decoding loop of a language model on the server under homomorphic encryption, selecting and consuming tokens without client round trips per token, including server-side bootstrap placement for the growing encrypted state. The client sends one encrypted prompt and remains offline during generation.

entry.title: A Statistical Inference Framework for PMI Estimation and SGNS Word Embeddings

author.name: Zhongqi Fan

entry.summary: This paper develops a rigorous statistical framework for Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) estimation and its connection to Skip-gram with Negative Sampling (SGNS), which implicitly factorizes a shifted PMI matrix. The authors prove consistency, asymptotic unbiasedness, and asymptotic normality of the empirical PMI estimator, derive its variance via the Delta method, and use stochastic approximation theory to obtain a variance decomposition for SGNS-based PMI estimation separating data variance from optimization variance. This addresses a long-standing gap in characterizing finite-sample uncertainty in word association measures that underpin word embeddings.

entry.title: The sublevel Flood bifiltration: towards scalable 2-parameter persistent homology

author.name: Matt\'eo Cl\'emot, Julie Digne, Julien Tierny

entry.summary: The authors introduce the sublevel Flood bifiltration, a new construction that approximates the sublevel offset bifiltration to make two-parameter persistent homology computable on large point sets. They prove stability properties and give efficient computation algorithms. This addresses a major scalability limitation in topological data analysis.

entry.title: Isotropic Gaussian Processes Improve Vanilla Bayesian Optimization in High Dimensions

author.name: Wei-Ting Tang, Madhav Muthyala, Joel A. Paulson

entry.summary: Iso-BO shows that replacing the standard automatic relevance determination Gaussian process with an isotropic one-shared-lengthscale GP improves vanilla Bayesian optimization in high-dimensional, low-observation regimes, with analysis showing the marginal log likelihood depends on ARD lengthscales only through weighted pairwise distances. This is a simple modeling change with controlled comparison against a matched BO pipeline. It challenges the default ARD choice in high-dimensional BO.

entry.title: PhaseMatcher: Autoregressive Phase-Set Identification with Spectral Decomposition

author.name: Zhonglong Peng, Qiuliang Liu, Chang Chen, Geng Zhong, Qi Li, Lihong Wang, Lan Jiang, Shifeng Jin

entry.summary: This paper introduces PhaseMatcher, an autoregressive framework for identifying complete phase sets from powder X-ray diffraction data. It addresses the problem of residual distortion by re-estimating contributions of all previously identified phases using physics-guided spectral decomposition against original observations. This matters for materials science, where accurate phase identification underpins crystallographic analysis.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence Rate of Normalized Gradient Descent under H\"older Smoothness

author.name: Yuki Takezawa, Eduard Gorbunov

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper analyzes the last-iterate convergence of normalized gradient descent for convex objectives satisfying Hölder smoothness conditions, addressing the gap between theoretical analyses (which typically bound the best or averaged iterate) and practical implementations (which return the final iterate). The authors prove an upper bound of O((log^2(T)/T)^((1+nu)/2)) for constant stepsize, showing only a logarithmic overhead compared to best-iterate guarantees, and demonstrate via numerical experiments. This matters because last-iterate guarantees are the practically relevant ones, and the paper clarifies when the known lower bound overhead for nonsmooth cases (nu = 0) can be softened.

entry.title: Inverse Cross-spectral Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series

author.name: Lorenzo Marinucci, Leonardo Di Nino, Gabriele D'Acunto, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Sergio Barbarossa

entry.summary: The paper introduces iCSNNs, graph neural networks for stationary multivariate time series whose graph shift operators are inverse cross-spectral density matrices, encoding frequency-specific conditional relationships between variables. This extends covariance-based neural networks beyond iid settings to capture joint temporal and cross-variable structure.

entry.title: WNet: Discrete Wavelets Transform for Efficient Token Mixing

author.name: Rana Aref Salama, Abdou Youssef, Mona Diab

entry.summary: WNet replaces self-attention in a Transformer encoder with token mixing based on the discrete wavelet transform, offering three attention-free mixers (linear fusion, learned gating, per-token scale selection) plus a hybrid that keeps attention only in the last layer. Receptive-field analysis shows wavelet mixers build multi-scale structure while avoiding quadratic cost. An interesting architecture-efficiency contribution, though results beyond the abstract are not visible.

entry.title: Usage-Modulated Sentiment Representations in Large Language Models

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Yanfu Zhang, Gang Zhou, Ye Gao

entry.summary: This interpretability study tests whether sentiment in LLM activation spaces is captured by more than a single linear direction, examining how usage factors like tone and audience adaptation modulate sentiment representations. Using a controlled paired dataset that holds content fixed while varying polarity and usage factors, the authors analyze Llama, Mistral, and Gemma models, identify a shared sentiment direction, and probe residual structure via erasure and generation-time tone steering. The work contributes to mechanistic understanding of how pragmatic factors are encoded.

entry.title: Adaptive Utilization of Low-Rank Adaptation via Conditioned Gating

author.name: Guang Yang, Changhao Guan, Chao Huang, Yufeng Chen, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: U-LoRA improves parameter-efficient fine-tuning by using conditioned gating to learn token-level utilization coefficients along low-rank adaptation directions, rather than applying a shared low-rank update across all tokens. Sequence-level context coordinates and constrains these coefficients. This makes better use of the limited adaptation subspace for heterogeneous tokens.

entry.title: Improving Diversity in LLM Short Story Generation

author.name: Zahra Solati Dehkordi, Vasileios Lampos

entry.summary: DivLM is a two-phase post-training framework for diverse creative short-story generation: continued pre-training on a creative-writing corpus with weight residuals to restore instruction following, followed by RL with a composite reward that maximizes diversity across genre, tone, style, and named entities while preserving quality.

entry.title: Factorized Delayed Streams Modeling for LLM-based Streaming ASR

author.name: Tatsunari Takagi, Kai Washizaki, Atsushi Kojima, Lianbo Liu, Koki Nikaido, Yui Sudo

entry.summary: The paper simplifies LLM-based streaming speech recognition by removing a padding token from Delayed Streams Modeling and proposing F-DSM, which factorizes the waiting probability from the text-token distribution. This removes ASR-specific tokens from the text softmax and lets the large-vocabulary softmax be skipped on waiting steps, improving efficiency with competitive accuracy.

entry.title: PhysMamba: Selective State Space Models as Learned Articulated Body Simulators

author.name: Haochuan Zhang, Sinisa Todorovic

entry.summary: PhysMamba is the first learned articulated body simulator based on selective state space models, predicting full-body next-frame states from position, rotation, and joint-action history without velocity inputs. With CUDA graph compilation, Mamba2 achieves about 9,300 FPS on an H100 while maintaining rollout accuracy under partial observation.

entry.title: VCURF: Virtual Camera-based Uncertainty of Radiance Fields

author.name: Liyan Chen, Nathaniel Burgdorfer, Philippos Mordohai

entry.summary: VCURF quantifies pixel-wise uncertainty for radiance fields (NeRF and Gaussian Splatting) by measuring inconsistencies among renderings from virtual cameras sampled near a target viewpoint. It treats the radiance field as a black box requiring only color and depth rendering, making it applicable to arbitrary models.

entry.title: TRIM-ReID: Duplication-Aware Token Reduction and Modality-Aligned Interaction for Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification

author.name: Wanke Xia, Ruiding Zhu, Xingguo Xu, Zhengbo Zhang, Dongxia Liu, Yuan Jin, Taojie Zhu, Yiting Zhao, Yihang Ding

entry.summary: TRIM-ReID improves multi-modal re-identification across RGB, near-infrared, and thermal modalities by unifying dense feature extraction, duplication-aware intra-modal token reduction, and aligned inter-modal interaction. It targets the problem that globally aligned encoders lose fine-grained identity cues and duplicate tokens add noisy, costly computation.
