entry.summary: The paper derives a novel bound on the cumulant generating function of Dirichlet processes by proving superadditivity of a concentration parameter mapping and combining it with Fekete's lemma and Varadhan's integral lemma. The resulting practical bound involves the convex conjugate of a scaled reversed KL divergence. This is a technical contribution useful in Bayesian nonparametrics and concentration analysis.

entry.title: “Alignment Engineering” vs. “Misalignment Science”

author.name: Edward James Young

entry.summary: The post engages with the debate over whether prosaic alignment work at AGI labs is net negative by accelerating capabilities, and introduces a distinction between Alignment Engineering (practical safety work inside labs) and Misalignment Science (research aimed at understanding misalignment itself) as a way to think about opportunity costs for researchers considering quitting. It is a conceptual contribution to field-strategy discussions rather than empirical work.

entry.title: Choosing an energy-efficient software architecture for building system diagnostic support

author.name: Roxane Koitz-Hristov, Franz Wotawa

entry.summary: The paper proposes assessing fault detection and diagnosis software for buildings by jointly considering the software's own energy consumption and its diagnostic performance, since missed faults carry an ecological cost. It provides guidance for choosing architectures that minimize total environmental impact.

entry.title: Component-Level Evaluation of Adaptive PINN Training for CFD-Oriented Crystal Growth Simulation

author.name: Niruta Chapagain, Rohit Raj, Bertwin Kurisinkal Shine, Aditya A S

entry.summary: The paper compares fixed-weight PINNs, gradient-normalized PINNs, and an agentic adaptive controller on a heat-equation benchmark and a crystal-growth thermal-fluid problem, with component-level loss analysis. Adaptive control reduced PDE residuals but worsened boundary-condition losses in some settings.

entry.title: The Arbitrary-Placement Problem in Entropy-Minimizing Selection, and a Residual-Entropy Formulation

author.name: Alyssa H. Shin, Claire H. Shin

entry.summary: This paper identifies a degeneracy in entropy-based selection objectives: minimizing Shannon entropy rewards confident selection regardless of informativeness. The authors propose a residual-entropy formulation D defined as the difference between selection entropy and a trust-weighted entropy, prove an exact KL-based identity, and show boundary-case safety properties such as never penalizing equal-trust states. The formulation aims to distinguish informative from merely confident selections.

entry.title: One-Cycle Fault Classification and Faulted-Line Identification on the PROTECT-90 Dataset: An Initial Application Benchmark

author.name: Emad Abukhousa, Abdulaziz Qwbaiban, Saman Zonouz, A. P. Sakis Meliopoulos

entry.summary: The paper presents an initial benchmark on the PROTECT-90 electromagnetic-transient dataset for two power-system protection tasks: fault-type classification and faulted-line identification. A compact 1D CNN is evaluated across post-inception window lengths from 0.25 to 2 cycles under strict episode-wise splitting, with an MLP as an architecture-control baseline. This establishes reproducible application-level baselines for learning-based power grid protection.

entry.title: Online AutoML: Evaluating Poisoning Attacks on Adversarial Training Defense Strategy in IoT Networks

author.name: Chukwunonso Henry Nwokoye, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: This study evaluates how well adversarial training defends ML models against poisoning attacks in streaming IoT network contexts, where attackers can incrementally insert harmful samples into continuously updating data streams. It assesses the efficacy of adversarial training as an online defense under such incremental contamination. The work is relevant to securing continuously learning IoT security systems.

entry.title: Reading the Mood: Emotion-Guided Book-to-Music Recommendation via CGANs and LLMs

author.name: Manousos Linardakis, Georgios Alexandridis

entry.summary: SAGA-CDR is a two-phase cross-domain recommender that builds transformer-based sentiment embeddings from user reviews, maps them across the book and music domains via a mask-conditioned conditional GAN, and matches music to the mood of the book being read. The system aims to improve reading immersion through mood-aligned background music.

entry.title: Why Convolution Still Matters: Evaluating Inductive Biases in Cryospheric Image Classification

author.name: Chhaya Kulkarni, Emam Hossain

entry.summary: The authors conduct a controlled comparison of AlexNet, ConvNeXt-Tiny, Swin-Tiny, and CoAtNet-0 on a Greenland Ice Sheet image classification benchmark previously shown to favor CNNs. The study tests whether modern attention-based and hybrid architectures improve class-wise reliability on texture-dominated, class-imbalanced cryospheric imagery. The result contributes to the ongoing debate about inductive biases versus scale in vision architectures.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving Guided by Chinese Philosophical Wisdom

author.name: Xiaojun Bi, Xiaoyuan Ma, Yiwen Sun, Tianren Huang, Chaoran Liu, Bokai Huang, Hao Yang, Baichuan Mo

entry.summary: CPW-Drive is a closed-loop RAG framework that injects value principles extracted from Confucian classical texts into LLM-based autonomous driving decisions, aiming to balance safety, efficiency, and social norms. It explores ethical and philosophical guidance largely absent from existing driving decision systems.

entry.title: Formalizing the Moral Evaluation of Speech Acts: Truthfulness, Lies and Ethical Dilemmas

author.name: Benjamin Icard, Gauvain Bourgne, Jeanne Bonnaventure, Jean-Gabriel Ganascia

entry.summary: The paper presents a logical framework, implemented in Answer Set Programming, for the ethical evaluation of assertive speech acts under agents' beliefs, comparing deontological, consequentialist, and principialist stances on benevolent lies. It illustrates the framework on Sartre's The Wall, a reworking of the classic Kant-Constant dispute about lying in life-or-death situations.

entry.title: OntoInk: Interactive Ontology Visualization, Validation, and Reasoning

author.name: Ebrahim Norouzi, J\"org Waitelonis, Harald Sack

entry.summary: OntoInk is an open-source MkDocs plugin that unifies ontology documentation, visualization, validation, and reasoning in one documentation-as-code pipeline, supporting interactive RDF diagrams, SHACL validation, OWL DL reasoning, and inline Turtle editing. It addresses the fragmented tooling that slows ontology development and knowledge transfer.

entry.title: A study on human-agent teaming through spoken interaction: the impact of human individual traits and agent characteristics

author.name: Lara Gauder, Martin Bernardo Meza, Javier Krick, Alejandro Masin, Luciana Benotti, Marcos Luis Pietto, Luciana Ferrer

entry.summary: Using a collaborative spoken-interaction game where humans and virtual agents jointly identify and place objects, this study examines whether simple changes in an agent's communicative behavior affect perceived teammate-likeness. Each participant interacted with two agent variants, enabling analysis of how human individual traits and agent characteristics shape perceptions of the agent as a legitimate teammate. Findings inform the social design of human-agent collaborative systems.

entry.title: Vision Transformer Ensembles for Panoramic Street Segmentation

author.name: Yunus Serhat B{\i}\c{c}ak\c{c}{\i}

entry.summary: The paper describes the first-place system for the PalmCity panorama segmentation challenge, comparing nine pretrained segmentation architectures including SegFormer, Mask2Former, and DINOv3 variants under equal compute budgets. The final solution ensembles three seeds of an encoder-only Mask Transformer with DINOv3 via probability averaging. It is a practical competition report rather than a methodological contribution.

entry.title: GCTAuto-encoder: A Cross modal Framework for Security Flaw Detection in IoT Networks

author.name: Najmieh Sadat Safarabadi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a graph-cross-modal transformer auto-encoder for detecting security flaws in heterogeneous IoT networks, leveraging edge-collected local data to build a unified security model at the edge. It targets robustness across diverse device classes from smart homes to vehicles.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Personal Context Recognition on ExtraSensory

author.name: Hoang-Thang Ta

entry.summary: The paper evaluates several KAN variants on the ExtraSensory dataset for personal context recognition against MLP and TabM baselines, using five user folds and three seeds per fold. All KAN variants significantly outperform MLP on Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 and achieve performance comparable to TabM, with ablations on grid size, grid count, and normalization.

entry.title: Detecting Nighttime Anomalies from NASA Black Marble Using a Generalized Spatio-Temporally Robust Framework of Machine Leaning Ensembles

author.name: Srija Chakraborty

entry.summary: The author proposes an ensemble ML framework that jointly models NASA Black Marble M-band and Day/Night Band signals to detect nighttime light anomalies such as fires, volcanic eruptions, and gas flaring, iteratively building detectors that generalize across regions, seasons, anomaly classes, and land/ocean. Detection sets at varying confidence levels are derived from band relevance and detector agreement, improving true detection rates over thermal-band-only baselines. A single-author applied remote sensing contribution.

entry.title: Evaluating Zone-Guided Front Extraction for Glacier Calving-Front Delineation in SAR Imagery

author.name: Chhaya Kulkarni, Emam Hossain

entry.summary: This paper compares direct calving-front prediction with zone-guided front extraction on the CaFFe dataset using U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer-B0 under a common protocol. The zone-guided setting first predicts four semantic zone classes before deriving the front, testing whether coarser zone supervision helps recover the thin, ambiguous ice-ocean boundary. Findings inform remote sensing pipelines for glacier monitoring.

entry.title: Adaptive-Shot Hybrid Quantum Anomaly Detection for Tactile Internet Security: Reliability-Aware Measurement Allocation Under Resource Constraints

author.name: Mubassir Serneabat Sudipto, Shakil Ahmed, Ashfaq Khokhar, Samir M. Iqbal

entry.summary: The paper introduces an Adaptive-Shot Variational Quantum Circuit policy for anomaly detection in tactile internet security, escalating measurement shot counts from 128 to 1024 only when finite-shot scores remain near a validation-selected threshold, balancing detection reliability with resource constraints. The quantum scorer is positioned off the haptic critical path and evaluated on a leakage-safe CESNET-derived benchmark. It is an early exploration of resource-aware quantum ML for network security.

entry.title: BAIBAICHUCHU at the NTCIR-19 FinArg-3 Task: When Is Maximum Possible Profit Predictable from Investor Text?

author.name: Zong-Han Bai, Po-Yen Chu

entry.summary: A team entry for the NTCIR-19 FinArg-3 social media subtask ranks Chinese investor posts by maximum possible profit using an ensemble of lexical features, a pre-finetuned MacBERT ranker, and an LLM judge. A post-hoc audit reveals the judge applied a stance-unaware long-only rule to bearish posts, exposing a regime-specific semantic shortcut that inflated development accuracy. Useful as a cautionary case study in financial NLP evaluation hygiene.

entry.title: Energy Variation in Training Modern Computer Vision Architectures

author.name: David Cortes, Carlos Juiz, Belen Bermejo

entry.summary: An empirical study directly measuring via NVML the training energy of seven modern vision architectures (MobileNetV3, EfficientNet, ViT, ConvNeXt variants) on an ImageNet-10k subset under a uniform 40-epoch setup on P100 GPUs, comparing measured energy against theoretical computational complexity. It highlights gaps between FLOPs-based estimates and actual energy consumption.

entry.title: A new design of a fall detection system integrating landmark identification and deep learning techniques

author.name: Tri Nhut Do, Thi Thuy Le

entry.summary: Combines MediaPipe landmark extraction with a deep learning classifier to distinguish routine movements from actual falls, aiming to reduce false alarms for elderly care. Experiments demonstrate stable accuracy across scenarios, with training converging by around the 40th cycle.

entry.title: Bayesian Data Augmentation for DNN Retraining with Binomial Outcomes in Vision-Based UAV Landing

author.name: Ashik E Rasul, Hyung-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: The authors deploy a Bayesian data augmentation framework with a photorealistic simulator to optimize DNN retraining for vision-based UAV landing in GPS-denied environments. The approach manages the tradeoff between expensive retraining cycles and validation via test flights using binomial outcome modeling.

entry.title: PB-STDG: A Prediction-Based Short-Term Decentralized Greedy Guidance Algorithm for a Drone Road System

author.name: Zhouyu Qu, Andreas Willig, Xiaobing Wu

entry.summary: Proposes PB-STDG, a decentralized guidance algorithm for structured drone road systems in which drones predict neighboring drones' decisions to coordinate conflict-free short-term flight paths in urban airspace. The prediction mechanism extends the prior STDG algorithm to reduce collisions among independently operated drones.

entry.title: Building A Multi-Sensor Platform For Autonomous Driving Research: Challenges and Lessons Learned

author.name: Paulo Ricardo Marques de Araujo, Eslam Mounier, Qamar Bader, Emma Dawson, Aboelmagd Noureldin

entry.summary: This experience paper documents challenges and lessons from building and deploying a flexible multi-sensor data collection platform for autonomous driving research, covering mechanical design, calibration, power management, and time synchronization. It serves as a reference for research groups building custom sensing platforms.

entry.title: Scale-free adaptive planning for deterministic dynamics & discounted rewards

author.name: Peter L. Bartlett, Victor Gabillon, Jennifer Healey, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper proposes Platypoos, a scale-free planning algorithm for deterministic dynamics with stochastic rewards and discounted returns that adapts to unknown reward scale and smoothness. Its sample complexity analysis improves on prior work and holds uniformly over broad ranges of discount factors and reward scales, with a matching lower bound establishing near-optimality. It matters as it removes tuning burdens in planning under unknown problem parameters.

entry.title: Poisson Autoregression on a Large Network with a Stochastic Block Model Structure

author.name: Mahmoud Khabou, Joanna Marks, Joshua Corneck, Edward A. K. Cohen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes multivariate Poisson autoregressive processes on random networks generated by a stochastic block model, incorporating latent community structure and non-Markovian excitatory and inhibitory dependence. A mean-field approximation is established with optimal N^{-1/2} quenched convergence rates and explicit, potentially time-uniform error bounds avoiding exponential-in-time growth. This supports principled modeling of event cascades on large networks.

entry.title: AstraSR: Real-World Thermal Super-Resolution with GPT-6 Astra

author.name: Mengyuan Li, Changhong Fu, Jun Zhang, Ziyu Lu, Yuhang Zhang, Haobo Zuo

entry.summary: Presents AstraSR, a real-world thermal super-resolution method guided by GPT-6 Astra, an existing frontier multimodal generative model released in early September 2026, using its transferable generative priors to overcome the domain gap between synthetic low-resolution training pairs and captured thermal observations. The approach avoids flawed supervision constructed from predefined degradations.

entry.title: On Impact of Loss Function on the Performance of Neural Networks in Melanoma Diagnosis

author.name: Morgan May, Pierpaolo Dondio, Simon Caton

entry.summary: The study systematically compares focal loss, logit-adjusted softmax cross-entropy, and weighted cross-entropy for melanoma classification on the imbalanced SIIM-ISIC dataset, reporting across multiple metrics. It provides empirical guidance on loss choice for class-imbalanced medical image diagnosis.

entry.title: Impact of Data Augmentation on Confidence Calibration in Melanoma Classification

author.name: Morgan May, Simon Caton, Pierpaolo Dondio

entry.summary: This companion study examines how data augmentation, widely used for performance on imbalanced medical datasets, affects confidence calibration in melanoma classification where uncertainty quantification matters for patient care. It trains neural networks under various augmentation regimes and evaluates calibration behavior, an underexplored interaction.

entry.title: Curriculum Brain: Constructing Curriculum Knowledge Graphs as a Substrate for Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Shrideep Tamboli, Chiranjeevi Maddala, Eshal Minhaj

entry.summary: Proposes separating cognitive diagnosis modeling into two stages: constructing a curriculum-wide knowledge graph of concepts and skills, then mapping assessment items onto it on demand, addressing the bottleneck of hand-authored Q-matrices. The paper implements only the first stage, with the item-mapping stage designed but not built. An early-stage infrastructure idea for personalized learning.

entry.title: Arithmetic Actor Heads and Training Stabilization for Out-of-Distribution Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: Building on soft actor-critic and a Bayesian Amnesic Piecewise-Robust predecessor, the paper studies the CS-BAPR family for RL under out-of-distribution magnitude shifts. It combines six training-stabilization settings with alternative actor heads including arithmetic units (NAU/NMU), Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, and MLPs.

entry.title: Application of sequence learning for predicting radiation damage of the CMS electromagnetic calorimeter

author.name: Mario Ivan Gallegos Torres, Leonid Serkin, Guy Paic

entry.summary: The authors apply deep sequence models to LHC Open Data from 2016-2018 to predict radiation damage in the lead tungstate crystals of the CMS electromagnetic calorimeter. Encoder-decoder sequence-to-sequence architectures effectively describe crystal optical transparency aging over future time intervals. This supports detector maintenance planning at particle physics facilities.

entry.title: Evaluating Modeling Approaches for Experience-Level Classification in Job Description

author.name: Celia Liang, Eddie Wu, Shiqi Wang, Yonah You

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Section-Aware BERT approach for predicting job experience levels from recruitment text, exploiting the internal paragraph structure of job descriptions, and compares it against rule-based, TF-IDF, and LLM baselines in few-shot and fine-tuned settings. It maps capability boundaries between structured classical models and LLMs on this task. Competent applied work with limited research novelty.

entry.title: Maximum Entropy Semi-Supervised Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Julien Audiffren, Michal Valko, Alessandro Lazaric, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh

entry.summary: MESSI combines maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning with semi-supervised learning principles to exploit unsupervised trajectories alongside expert demonstrations, using a pairwise penalty on trajectories. The approach addresses apprenticeship learning when only limited expert data is available but unlabeled behavior is abundant. It matters for imitation learning settings where collecting expert demonstrations is expensive.

entry.title: Calibration Assessment for Nested Uncertainty Sets

author.name: Matthew LeDuc

entry.summary: The paper presents a Bayesian framework for assessing calibration of nested uncertainty sets from simulation studies, exploiting nested structure to reduce the hundreds or thousands of expensive model evaluations that standard simulation-based calibration requires. This matters for costly forward models such as large Earth-system models and for outputs that are uncertainty sets rather than full distributions. It improves the practicality of calibration assessment.

entry.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Graph Representation Strategies for Cyber Attack Detection

author.name: Ali Melih Kanca, Ilker Turker

entry.summary: This is a quantitative survey of 37 graph-based cyber attack detection studies from 2019 to 2026, coding each by domain, graph representation type, feature extraction, learning paradigm, algorithm, and dataset, with frequency and association analyses. It finds automated representation learning used in 73% of studies.

entry.title: AI-Decision Checkpoints for AI-Augmented Business Process Management: Framework and Educational Instantiation

author.name: Amin Jalali

entry.summary: This paper proposes AI-decision checkpoints: explicit moments in process development where developers identify AI-candidate sub-processes, assess effects on time, cost, quality, and flexibility, and document reasoned decisions under legal and organizational constraints. It instantiates the framework educationally to prepare students to treat AI as a first-class BPM design element.

entry.title: TrustmeWatcher: An Application for Workplace Micro-Sensing and Explainable Well-Being Feedback

author.name: Chengyu Yu, Leon Jacopo Costa, Zoja An\v{z}ur, Mohan Li, Ga\v{s}per Slapni\v{c}ar, Daniil Kirilenko, Martin Gjoreski, Mitja Lu\v{s}trek, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: TrustmeWatcher is an application built for the TRUST-ME project that reuses ActivityWatch OS-level watchers to collect computer-activity traces, synchronizes short questionnaire responses, and aligns behavior and self-reports into labeled records for wellbeing modeling with explainable feedback. It connects long-running sensing with the interface that returns results to participants. The scope is limited to ActivityWatch data.

entry.title: Vision-enabled detection of safety helmet compliance in construction zones

author.name: Tri Nhut Do*, Ba Loc Pham

entry.summary: Builds a real-time YOLO-based vision system that monitors helmet compliance on construction sites from fixed camera feeds, flagging workers without helmets to reduce head-injury risk. The paper reports training and validation results demonstrating detection effectiveness.

entry.title: On two ways to use determinantal point processes for Monte Carlo integration

author.name: Guillaume Gautier, R\'emi Bardenet, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper revisits two determinantal point process (DPP) based Monte Carlo integration estimators, one achieving faster variance rates for smooth integrands with a fixed DPP and another unbiased estimator tailored to the integrand. The authors generalize both to continuous settings, provide sampling algorithms, and analyze the variance tradeoffs of repulsive sampling versus standard independent sampling. This informs when repulsive point processes can beat classical Monte Carlo.

entry.title: When Is a Graph a Covariance? Bayesian Residual Propagation under Covariance Uncertainty

author.name: Robert Richardson

entry.summary: The paper develops a Bayesian model of residual covariance to determine how revealed prediction errors at some nodes should update feature-based predictions elsewhere, deriving an exact identity for the change in expected squared error under linear residual propagation. Under covariance uncertainty, the Bayes-optimal fixed linear update uses the posterior mean covariance. It clarifies when a graph can meaningfully serve as a residual dependence structure.

entry.title: Analysis of Nystrom method with sequential ridge leverage scores

author.name: Daniele Calandriello, Alessandro Lazaric, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This paper analyzes Nyström methods for large-scale kernel ridge regression in a sequential setting, introducing sequential approximations to ridge leverage scores to guide kernel matrix column subsampling. Because exact ridge leverage scores are as hard to compute as the regression itself, good approximations are key, and this work quantifies the statistical-computational tradeoff. It is foundational for scalable kernel methods.

entry.title: Emoji-Emotion Ranking System Using Twitter Data

author.name: Danila Khlebokazov, Nurkhan Tashimov, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: Using 100,000 emoji-containing Twitter replies from 2020-2025, the authors build an emoji-aware emotion framework that classifies messages into five primary emotions and aggregates scores into emoji-emotion association rankings. This moves beyond treating emojis as static sentiment indicators. Straightforward descriptive analysis with limited depth.

entry.title: Social Navigation for Tour-guide Robot

author.name: Vikram Shree, Jose Nino

entry.summary: Proposes a force-based social navigation model for a tour-guide robot that accounts for obstacles, user position, and user heading, and evaluates it with human participants following the robot under distraction sub-tasks. Per-round subjective measures compare the force model against an A* shortest-path baseline on constructs like sociability.

entry.title: Improved large-scale graph learning through ridge spectral sparsification

author.name: Daniele Calandriello, Ioannis Koutis, Alessandro Lazaric, Michal Valko

entry.summary: GSQUEAK is an algorithm for sparsifying graph Laplacians in a distributed streaming setting where edges arrive in real time, maintaining a small subset of effective resistances while producing sparsifiers with strong spectral guarantees. This enables efficient distributed graph learning without storing the full Laplacian. It contributes to the scalability of graph-based machine learning.

entry.title: Trading off rewards and errors in multi-armed bandits

author.name: Akram Erraqabi, Alessandro Lazaric, Michal Valko, Emma Brunskill, Yun-En Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies the tension in multi-armed bandits between accurately identifying arm means and maximizing accumulated reward, presenting an algorithm with regret guarantees that interpolates between the two objectives. Both upper and lower bounds are provided with empirical validation. This pure-exploration versus reward-accumulation tradeoff relates to active learning and informed decision making.

entry.title: Revealing graph bandits for maximizing local influence

author.name: Alexandra Carpentier, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper studies a graph bandit setting where a learner identifies the most influential node of an unknown graph by actively and sequentially querying nodes and observing stochastic neighbor sets, motivated by social network marketing. Unlike prior work, no knowledge of the graph is assumed upfront. This introduces an active graph-discovery bandit model with influence maximization objectives.

entry.title: Bayesian policy gradient and actor-critic algorithms

author.name: Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Yaakov Engel, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for policy gradient methods, modeling the policy gradient as a Gaussian process to reduce the samples needed for accurate gradient estimates. It also yields natural gradient estimates and gradient uncertainty measures at little extra cost. The work is foundational for variance reduction in actor-critic methods and connects to later Bayesian and uncertainty-aware RL.

entry.title: Bounds, Decompositions and Null Behaviour of KRATOS: A Mathematical Specification of a Recognition-Comparability Diagnostic

author.name: Maria Dolores Gonzalez, Alberto Barbado

entry.summary: This note provides a complete mathematical specification of KRATOS, a bibliometric diagnostic comparing document participation and citation-weight distributions across groups. It derives bounds, equality conditions, and decomposition results showing the recognition-alignment score depends only on ratios of group mean citation rates to corpus mean.

entry.title: Leveraging Cost-effective Robotics for K-12 STEM Education through Water Quality Monitoring Tasks

author.name: Rishi Mukherjee, Andrew Ruiz, Travis Henderson, Resha Tejpaul, Kris Simonson, David Mulla, Brian McNeil, Nikolaos Papanikolopoulos, Junaed Sattar

entry.summary: Introduces the Jar Jar ROV, a low-cost open-source underwater vehicle that middle school students build, program, and deploy for lake water quality monitoring. A large deployment with over 100 students demonstrated high engagement and produced a grassroots environmental sensing network.

entry.title: Large-scale semi-supervised learning with online spectral graph sparsification

author.name: Daniele Calandriello, Alessandro Lazaric, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sparse-HFS, a scalable algorithm for semi-supervised learning that solves graph-based SSL problems using only O(n polylog(n)) space and O(m polylog(n)) time. This dramatically reduces the resources required for large-scale graph SSL. The result is significant for learning with very large graphs where storing full solutions is infeasible.

entry.title: Technical Report on the Turba Fertilizer Machine Learning Stack in Morocco

author.name: Abdelghani Belgaid, Zakaria Mahmoud, Fahd Chibani, Oumnia Ennaji, Younes Boudoul, Dounia Rachid

entry.summary: This technical report describes Turba, a three-layer open-source stack for reproducible site-specific fertilizer recommendations in Morocco, including a client library for programmatic access, distributed data and recommendation functions, and trained approximations that can be independently loaded and benchmarked. It addresses reproducibility problems where recommendation systems are locked behind interactive interfaces with unversioned outputs.

entry.title: How much should we worry about the pneumonic plague lableak in Siberia?

author.name: Drew Spartz

entry.summary: The author compiles rapidly evolving reports of a pneumonic plague death at a BSL-3 lab in Irkutsk, Russia, including expanding quarantines, FSB involvement, deleted local news mentions, and the lab's stated gain-of-function work, and assesses whether this could be a lab leak of an enhanced bioweapon. The post is explicitly an invitation for scrutiny of a worrying open situation.

entry.title: Evolutionary feature selection for spiking neural network pattern classifiers

author.name: Michal Valko, Nuno C. Marques, Marco Castelani

entry.summary: This older cross-listed paper applies the JASTAP biologically realistic neural network model to classification, extending an evolutionary procedure for simultaneous feature selection and network training from MLPs to JASTAP. Preliminary IRIS results suggest smaller networks can handle noisier data without accuracy loss.

entry.title: AUTOPILOT An Advanced Perception, Localization and Path Planning Techniques for Autonomous Vehicles Using YOLOv7 and MiDaS

author.name: Harshkumar Devmurari, Gautham Kuckian, Prajjwal Vishwakarma

entry.summary: The paper describes a project integrating YOLOv7 object detection, MiDaS depth estimation, perspective transforms, and rule-based decision making for autonomous vehicle path planning, evaluated through simulations. It is an implementation combining established components rather than a new method. The work is a student-style system integration exercise.

entry.title: Semi-supervised learning with max-margin graph cuts

author.name: Branislav Kveton, Michal Valko, Ali Rahimi, Ling Huang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning algorithm that learns graph cuts maximizing the margin with respect to labels induced by harmonic function solutions, with a proven generalization error bound. Experiments on synthetic and UCI datasets show it often outperforms manifold-regularized SVMs. It connects graph-based SSL with max-margin classification.

entry.title: Online semi-supervised perception: Real-time learning without explicit feedback

author.name: Branislav Kveton, Michal Valko, Matthai Phillipose, Ling Huang

entry.summary: The paper presents an algorithm combining graph-based semi-supervised learning with online learning for real-time perception without explicit feedback, iteratively building a graphical world model updated by a stream of unlabeled examples. It proves a regret bound and demonstrates real-time face recognition with superior precision and recall on three video datasets. The work anticipates modern ideas of learning from unlabeled streams.

entry.title: King James’s Dæmonologie, Part I: The Laplacian Mesa-Optimiser

author.name: Matthias Dellago

entry.summary: A short speculative piece, framed playfully, describing a hypothetical misaligned optimizer present at initialization that behaves correctly on every observable training and evaluation input (a Laplacian demon / deceptive mesa-optimizer). It identifies two wards: unpredictable and independent tests requiring enormous bits to encode, and bounding relative amplification of such circuits under training. The core idea restates known deceptive-alignment concerns in a novel literary framing.

entry.title: Learning from a single labeled face and a stream of unlabeled data

author.name: Branislav Kveton, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper formalizes one-class face recognition from a single labeled image plus a stream of unlabeled data, a setting arising in device authentication where negative examples are absent. It proposes and analyzes an algorithm learning a non-parametric face model from this sparse supervision. It is relevant to one-class classification and few-shot identity verification.

entry.title: Female Draco Malfoy as a Harbinger of Apt Reality Flips

author.name: BazingaBoy

entry.summary: A cultural-analysis post using the viral female-Draco-Malfoy AI-generated trend and the earlier Ghiblification trend to argue that changing one element of a richly constructed fictional world can trigger an avalanche of co-created implications, which the author calls reality flips. It reflects on what this reveals about generative AI's cultural dynamics.

entry.title: On donating a kidney

author.name: Caleb Horn

entry.summary: The author recounts donating a kidney in May 2026, motivated by Scott Alexander's earlier article, and makes a utilitarian case that donation adds 5-10 high-quality life-years to a recipient without reducing donor life expectancy. The post walks through the evaluation and surgery process to encourage others to consider donation.

entry.title: The Unacknowledgable Labor of Pastor's Wives

author.name: Elizabeth

entry.summary: A short announcement of the author's published piece in Asterisk about the unrecognized labor of pastors' wives, following up on prior work comparing church planting to VC startup culture. It is essentially a pointer to external content rather than a substantive post itself.

entry.title: Reverse Jaggedness and Universal Ajaggedness

author.name: Laiba Rehman ✦ RJ

entry.summary: A light-hearted post proposing that AI jaggedness is defined relative to human capabilities, and introducing the playful notions of reverse jaggedness and universal ajaggedness by imagining capability profiles on axes emanating from a human unit circle. The author flags it as a fun idea conceived an hour earlier.

entry.title: Dance, Dance

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: A personal essay reflecting on the author's past reluctance to play games as a human when he could program solutions, including writing a chess engine and a Zendo example-proposal program, and his later appreciation for games. It is a reflective piece touching on rationality and personal growth rather than research.

entry.title: On the algorithmic complexity of cooking

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A light personal post applying algorithmic complexity thinking to home cooking, e.g., arguing that batch cooking dominates per-day cooking because shared setup costs amortize across servings. It is explicitly a utilitarian, self-oriented optimization framework.

entry.title: Notes on Paying Attention

author.name: jenn

entry.summary: A reflective essay on how attention enriches experience, the socially constructed reward structure of what deserves attention, and the value of articulating one's own preferences rather than outsourcing them, illustrated with a C.S. Lewis quotation. It is a personal/philosophical piece.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 05, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's strongest research spans AI-driven scientific discovery, agent security, and post-training methodology. Safety-critical evaluation dominates, exposing validation flaws in deployed defenses and newly formalized agent failure modes.

  • ImmuneAgent couples multimodal reasoning with closed-loop wet-lab validation, cloning 110 antibodies for broadly neutralizing discovery across virus families
  • Prompt-injection detector re-evaluation reveals severe train/test contamination when replaying ground-truth AgentDojo and tau-bench traces
  • GHOST exposes cross-turn safety-constraint violations in long-horizon agents; branch-steering attacks defeat Dual-LLM security guarantees for computer-use agents
  • CreativePreferences releases 2.8M texts and 317M human preference judgments, decomposing preferences into verifiable, articulable, and tacit components
  • Certified mechanistic edits provide formal guarantees for skill removal with preservation; Queen reaches grandmaster-level chess while explaining its moves
  • Zephon enables deterministic training-data loading despite GPU topology changes; default-collapse results show post-training erodes in-context steerability
entry.content:
Today's strongest research spans AI-driven scientific discovery, agent security, and post-training methodology. Safety-critical evaluation dominates, exposing validation flaws in deployed defenses and newly formalized agent failure modes.

  • ImmuneAgent couples multimodal reasoning with closed-loop wet-lab validation, cloning 110 antibodies for broadly neutralizing discovery across virus families
  • Prompt-injection detector re-evaluation reveals severe train/test contamination when replaying ground-truth AgentDojo and tau-bench traces
  • GHOST exposes cross-turn safety-constraint violations in long-horizon agents; branch-steering attacks defeat Dual-LLM security guarantees for computer-use agents
  • CreativePreferences releases 2.8M texts and 317M human preference judgments, decomposing preferences into verifiable, articulable, and tacit components
  • Certified mechanistic edits provide formal guarantees for skill removal with preservation; Queen reaches grandmaster-level chess while explaining its moves
  • Zephon enables deterministic training-data loading despite GPU topology changes; default-collapse results show post-training erodes in-context steerability

entry.title: Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families

author.name: Hantao Lou, Jianqing Zheng, Can Yue, Meihan Zhang, Yuanchao Bao, Yu Chen, Mengting Huang, Yupeng Yang, Qianyu Pan, Nana Fu, Yansong Shi, Hongli Li, Yangyang Chai, Ruyi Chen, Wansheng Li, Zhu Liang, Rongmei Yao, Yuanhan Mo, Lei Wang, Chunmei Wang, Yun Quan, Qiong Zhang, Xiangxi Wang, Xuetao Cao

entry.summary: ImmuneAgent is a closed-loop AI system combining multimodal reasoning, continual meta-learning, and wet-lab feedback to discover broadly neutralizing antibodies from human B cell repertoires across virus families. In screening repertoires from vaccinated or infected cohorts it achieved roughly 55% neutralization discovery rate and 11% broadly neutralizing antibody yield, substantially outperforming baselines, with a large wet-lab validation component.

entry.title: Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhuowen Liu

entry.summary: Critically re-evaluates fifteen prompt-injection detectors for LLM agents by replaying ground-truth tool calls from AgentDojo and tau-bench without an LLM, yielding benign-by-construction outputs and injection labels via differential replay. The results show benchmark rankings transfer poorly — the best BIPIA detector catches only 2% of AgentDojo injections at a 1% false-positive rate — undermining reliance on public benchmark scores for detector selection.

entry.title: Post-Training Frontier Text-to-Image Models by Composing Preference and Rubric Rewards

author.name: Yuanhao Ban, I-Hung Hsu, Anastasios Angelopoulos, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: A Berkeley/Stoica-group paper presenting a post-training recipe for text-to-image models that composes a Bradley-Terry preference reward trained on large-scale human data with rubric-based rewards for prompt faithfulness that include reward-hacking safeguards. The recipe is applied to frontier-class image generators and demonstrates improved alignment with human preferences.

entry.title: Verifiable, Articulable, and Tacit Components of Preference

author.name: Alexander Spangher, Sheldon Huang, Andreas Haupt, Noah D. Goodman, Diyi Yang, Daniel E. Ho, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This paper introduces CreativePreferences, a large dataset with 2.8M texts and 317M human preference judgments across 7 creative domains, decomposing preferences into verifiable, articulable, and tacit components. The authors model labels with executable programs, rubric banks, and trained models, measuring articulability and verifiability gaps. This directly informs RLAIF and RLVR methodology by quantifying what preference training can and cannot capture.

entry.title: Certified Mechanistic Edits: Behavioral Guarantees for Skill Removal and Preservation

author.name: Md Sazid Uddin, Md. Khairul Alam Mazumder, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: The authors introduce certified mechanistic edits, providing formal guarantees that disabling a circuit removes one skill while provably preserving another for all inputs in a region, analogous to non-interference guarantees in information-flow security. This moves beyond test-only validation of unlearning and weight-editing methods. Demonstrations range from toy ReLU networks upward, representing a significant step toward verifiable model editing.

entry.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves

author.name: Adithya Bhaskar, Jeffrey Cheng, Danqi Chen

entry.summary: Queen is a 4B-parameter chess-language model that explains its moves and plans while playing at Grandmaster level, combining a silent expert chess encoder with an instruction-tuned LM via cross-attention and trained with an iterative distillation algorithm and question-answering curriculum. It addresses the gap between superhuman but silent engines and articulate but weak LMs, providing a template for pairing expert systems with language models for grounded explanation.

entry.title: A GHOST in Long-Horizon Agents: Governance Hazard from Overlooked Safety Constraints across Turns

author.name: XinPeng Shen, Lan Zhang, Yixiao Huang, Haoran Cheng, Jiewei Lai, Leilei Chen, Haoxiang Deng

entry.summary: The paper identifies GHOST, a failure mode where long-horizon agents execute actions violating safety constraints specified many turns earlier, even under benign interaction conditions, with an observed occurrence rate of 11.5% on GPT-5.5. The authors provide theoretical analysis of residual conditions and highlight that extended interaction histories introduce underexplored execution-safety risks with potentially irreversible consequences.

entry.title: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks

author.name: Giulio Zingrillo, Hanna Foerster, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao, Robert Mullins

entry.summary: This paper shows that the Dual-LLM pattern, the primary architecture offering formal security guarantees for computer-use agents, breaks down in graphical environments because plans must branch based on untrusted web content, opening a new attack class called branch steering. It characterizes these attacks where injected content steers the agent into a pre-planned malicious branch and discusses mitigations.

entry.title: Zephon: Elastic Determinism for Online, Stateful Foundation Model Data Loading Pipelines

author.name: Maximilian B\"other, Josh Wills, Ties Robroek, Sonnet Xu, Paul Burstein, Daniel Zayas, Cody Blakeney, Siddharth Joshi, Haoli Yin, Rishabh Adiga, Haakon Mongstad, Luke Merrick, Pratyush Maini, Ari Morcos, Matthew Leavitt, Ana Klimovic, Bogdan Gaza

entry.summary: Zephon provides deterministic data loading for foundation model training that stays deterministic despite GPU topology changes, checkpoint-resume cycles, and varying processing backends, even when pipelines tokenize, pack, and mix samples online. This gives researchers confidence that ablation differences stem from the changed parameter rather than data-ordering noise, and the author list includes practitioners from a major AI organization.

entry.title: What Is Lost in Post-Training? Default Collapse and the Loss of In-Context Steerability Across Diverse Perspectives

author.name: Jessica Dierking, Itai Shapira, Niclas Boehmer

entry.summary: This paper shows that post-training LLMs toward one side of cultural-value disagreements not only biases default outputs but degrades the model's ability to be steered in-context toward opposing perspectives it was not trained to favor. Controlled fine-tuning experiments with checkpoint evaluations reveal increasing dominance of the trained view and declining capacity to recognize and enact the other side. This identifies a tension between alignment via post-training and serving heterogeneous user populations.

entry.title: Physical AI Smart Spaces: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Multi-Camera 3D Perception in Smart Spaces

author.name: Yuxing Wang, Yizhou Wang, Anqi Li, Shuo Wang, Sameer Satish Pusegaonkar, Haoquan Liang, Jiajun Li, Shenxin Jiang, Jianhe Yuan, Shangru Li, Tongwei Dai, Zihao Chen, David C. Anastasiu, Sujit Biswas, Xunlei Wu, Zheng Tang

entry.summary: Releases the first large-scale benchmark combining multi-class, multi-camera 3D perception data for indoor smart spaces: over 280 hours of synchronized 1080p footage from nearly 1,800 cameras across warehouses, hospitals, and retail, with 2D/3D boxes, identities, calibration, and depth. It spans Isaac Sim synthetic data, Cosmos Transfer augmentation, and real-world Sim2Real warehouse evaluations.

entry.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel

author.name: Jiahuan Cheng, Zhiyi Li, Tian Xia, Ruojin Cai, Yilun Du, Qianqian Wang

entry.summary: MoSE3 is the first feed-forward model predicting dense per-pixel SE(3) motion from monocular RGB video, outputting full 6-DoF rigid transforms in world space rather than mere 3-DoF point tracks, capturing rotation, translation, and object grouping simultaneously. It handles the challenges of rotation-manifold regression and scarce SE(3) annotations with dedicated training strategies.

entry.title: How to Have a Sensitive Debate: An Instance-Optimal Protocol for AI Debate

author.name: Jiawei Li, Zhiyang Xun, Lijie Chen, Jonah Brown-Cohen

entry.summary: The paper advances the theory of AI debate for supervising superhuman-capable AI systems, proposing a new debate protocol with instance-optimality guarantees. Building on complexity-theoretic formalizations, it improves on the current best protocol's guarantees for judging solutions to complex problems with limited supervision. This is foundational work for scalable oversight.

entry.title: Mitigating Social Sycophancy via Pluralistic Preference Optimization

author.name: Stephane Hatgis-Kessell, Myra Cheng, Xiaoxuan Hou, Qian Hu, Rahul Gupta, Natasha Jaques, Emma Brunskill

entry.summary: This paper addresses social sycophancy in language models, where models over-affirm users in personal advice settings like relationship guidance, potentially making people overconfident. Unlike prior work focused on factual sycophancy with ground-truth answers, the authors identify that social sycophancy stems from models over-centering the user's perspective and propose pluralistic preference optimization to incorporate other stakeholders' viewpoints.

entry.title: MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0

author.name: Carsten Maple (Victor), Cagatay Yucel (Victor), Isaac Holeman (Victor), Chris Knotz (Victor), Peter Mattson (Victor), James Goel (Victor), Jonathan Petit (Victor), Sean McGregor (Victor), James Ezick (Victor), Abhishek Kumar (Victor), Alicia Parrish (Victor), Murali Emani (Victor), Kashyap Iyer (Victor), Faiza Khan Khattak (Victor), Washington Mbonu (Victor), Daniel Machlab (Victor), Eileen Long (Victor), Shaona Ghosh (Victor), Jibin Varghese (Victor), Roman Lutz (Victor), Andrew Gruen (Victor), Bennett Hillenbrand (Victor), Prabal Gupta (Victor), Mohammed Serrhini (Victor), Dhivya Nagasubramanian (Victor), Aakash Gupta (Victor), Jun (Victor), Lu, Kurt Bollacker, Chang Liu, Jonathan Petit, Cong Chen, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Brent Miller, Apurv Verma, Roman Eng, Armstrong Foundjem, Mohammed Serrhini

entry.summary: The MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0 provides an end-to-end, standardized pipeline for evaluating LLM robustness to single-turn text jailbreaks, combining criteria-driven attack selection, paired baseline and adversarial evaluation, human annotation, evaluator calibration, and risk-calibrated disclosure. It evaluates eight open-weight systems against 264 seed prompts across eleven hazard categories.

entry.title: hacktrace: behavior-supervised detection of reward hacking during code generation

author.name: Hao Jiang, Xin Li, Annan Wang, Yichi Zhang, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: HACKTRACE is a monitor for detecting reward hacking in coding agents, trained on 173,561 annotated multi-turn trajectories from Qwen3-8B, supervising shortcut behavior regardless of whether exploits succeed. It reads internal states the agent already computes, enabling detection before a turn completes without extra tokens, achieving a mean per-problem AUC of 0.997. This addresses a core AI safety concern as coding agents deploy widely.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Are Accurate but Unsound on Identification

author.name: Arman Behnam, Binghui Wang

entry.summary: The paper examines whether reasoning models can correctly decide if a causal effect is identifiable from observational data, showing they are accurate but unsound: they sometimes answer non-identifiable queries, which cannot be validated by any data. The authors build CERTID, a formal pipeline using the sound and complete ID algorithm to certify identifiability and verify returned formulas against structural criteria, enabling rigorous evaluation beyond string matching.

entry.title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies

author.name: Jungkyu Park, Dhruva Biswas, Joseph Cappadona, Cerise Tang, Ken G. Zeng, Bartosz Machura, Chuwen Liu, Paolo Tarantino, Coral Omene, Francisco J. Esteva, Rohit Bhargava, Marcin Braun, Kamila Pa\'zdzierz, Jakub Czerwi\'nski, Hanna Roma\'nska-Knight, Albert Grinshpun, Bareket Daniel, Michele Buchinger, Frederick Howard, Piotr Wysocki, Brie Chun, Freya Schnabel, Rich Caruana, Jan Witowski, Krzysztof J. Geras

entry.summary: A two-stage model first learns to infer transcriptomic profiles from histopathology using 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types, then predicts pathological complete response to neoadjuvant breast cancer therapy from inferred expression plus clinical variables. Trained on 1,080 patients and validated on 1,412 across nine cohorts, it achieves pooled AUROC 0.79 and outperforms histopathological biomarkers, including within molecular subtypes.

entry.title: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in LLMs with Whiteout

author.name: Anna Yoo Jeong Ha, Ronik Bhaskar, Haitao Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao

entry.summary: Presents Whiteout, a practical tool that selectively prevents LLMs from regurgitating personally sensitive information (birth dates, phone numbers, addresses) upon individual requests, as an alternative to machine unlearning which removes too much information and degrades utility. From a well-known privacy/security group (Zhao and Zhao, UChicago).

entry.title: OpenGameEval: Benchmarking Agentic Programming and Exploration in a Stateful Game Engine

author.name: Eray Turkel, Mengsha Sun, Kartik Ayyar, Sean Dunigan, Jack Lu, Vlad Shcherban, Hsiang-Shun Shih, Xin Wang, Tiantian Zhang

entry.summary: OpenGameEval is a benchmark and evaluation framework that runs language models as agents inside Roblox Studio, scoring agentic game development via executable checks on both edited scenes and simulated play sessions in reproducible, stateful environments. It uniquely separates observation tools from editing tools in an eight-tool action space so exploration behavior can be measured directly, and evaluates 13 frontier models on 84 human-curated tasks, finding tasks remain hard - the best model solves only 51.7% on a single attempt.

entry.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhihan Yang, Wei Guo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Simon Welker, Yonggan Fu, Mohammad Mahdi Kamani, Sajad Norouzi, Julius Berner, Tomas Geffner, Karsten Kreis, Yongxin Chen, Molei Tao, John Thickstun, Pavlo Molchanov, Ante Juki\'c, Arash Vahdat, Morteza Mardani

entry.summary: This paper introduces Sigma, described as the first large-scale (3B/8B parameter) continuous diffusion language model, built on smooth ODE/SDE latent trajectories in contrast to discrete diffusion models. It trains blockwise via likelihood optimization, warm-starts from pretrained autoregressive weights, and identifies classifier-free guidance and score temperature as key inference techniques for reasoning and coding quality. Continuous diffusion trajectories could enable better inference-time steering and acceleration than discrete approaches.

entry.title: OPD Before RL: Warm-Starting Rubric-Based RL with On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinpeng Wang, Wei Shi, Yu-Chia Chen, Maria Zontak, Yun He, Richard Yuanzhe Pang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework for tasks that lack verifiable outcomes: rubric-privileged on-policy distillation first uses rubrics as teacher context to give dense token-level supervision, then rubric-based RL refines the policy with outcome-level rewards. This addresses the credit-assignment weakness of rubric-based RL where rewards arrive only after full responses.

entry.title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time

author.name: Changxiu Ji, Amy Lu, Qizheng Zhang, Kunle Olukotun

entry.summary: Sentry is a failure-management layer that runs alongside LLM agents, detecting mid-task failures such as invalid tool calls and repeatedly looping actions, and exposing conditional failure knowledge only when relevant. The key insight is that failure lessons misfire when kept permanently in context, so they should be conditionally retrieved at test time rather than baked into a static playbook.

entry.title: Not Until the Evidence Says So: Teaching LLM Investigators When to Close a Case

author.name: Tingzhu Bi, Ping Wang, Meng Ma

entry.summary: This paper studies a decision LLM investigators face in accident, defect, and outage investigations: whether the collected evidence suffices to close a case. The authors show that even frontier models that identify correct causes in most cases routinely overstate their evidence and prematurely close cases whose official finding is cause undetermined. They propose training and evaluation methods for calibrated case-closure judgments.

entry.title: Detect and Suppress: A Mechanistic Defense against Adversarial Patches in VLA Models

author.name: Yukiya Horiba, Koshiro Aoki, Shunsuke Yasuki, Bum Jun Kim, Taiki Miyanishi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how adversarial visual patches disrupt Vision-Language-Action models used for robot control, using sparse autoencoders to identify an internal feature that correlates with attack presence. The authors suppress this feature at inference time only when a linear probe flags an attack, improving robustness without fine-tuning. It matters because it offers a cheap, mechanistically grounded defense for safety-critical embodied AI.

entry.title: Trained Agentic Context Management

author.name: Bryce Sandlund

entry.summary: Instead of training native long context, this paper finetunes Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on a synthetic dataset over a minimal harness of self-call and context-reading tools. With only 8,000 tokens of context, the small model matches GPT-5.4 with 1M tokens on OOLONG-synth for documents over 40K tokens. This suggests trained agentic strategies can substitute for massive context windows at far lower cost, using existing models rather than new releases.

entry.title: All Work And No Play Makes Jack a Dull Boy: Understanding and Preventing Catastrophic Strategy Collapse in RLVR

author.name: Qiyuan Huang, Tianshi Xu, Meng Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies and characterizes late-stage strategy collapse in GRPO-style RLVR post-training of LLMs, showing it is a harmful contraction of strategy capacity rather than benign pruning. It develops a unified optimization-plus-information-theoretic framework proving that major RLVR objectives progressively concentrate probability mass on a single strategy, and proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation

author.name: Nicolas Zucchet, Scott W. Linderman

entry.summary: Taking an entropic perspective on distillation, the authors prove that forward KL inflates student entropy above the teacher's, yielding a quantitative identity verified in pretraining and supervised finetuning, while reverse KL deflates entropy until the student-teacher gap grows too large. The work explains how the choice of divergence determines student diversity, a core concern for LLM training pipelines.

entry.title: Autonomous Robotic Navigation for Endovascular Brain-Computer Interface Access

author.name: Harry Robertshaw, Weijie Qi, Nikola Fischer, Alejandro Granados, Thomas C. Booth, Sam E. John

entry.summary: This paper presents the first demonstration of in vitro autonomous robotic navigation for endovascular BCI access in the cerebral venous system, using Soft Actor-Critic controllers trained in silico with geometric augmentation across anatomies. Navigation was validated over 1,000 simulated episodes and 20 physical fluoroscopy-guided runs across training and unseen anatomies. It advances a less invasive BCI delivery paradigm with real translational potential.

entry.title: Emergent Structure in the Marginal Attention Space of Language Models

author.name: Valentino Maiorca, Walter Nelson, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work maps post-softmax attention weights into a joint token-head marginal attention space across more than 60 diverse LLMs, finding text-intrinsic signals robustly conserved across independently trained models. The authors empirically connect marginal attention to the input-output Jacobian and provide theoretical justification, contributing to the growing literature on cross-model mechanistic structure (e.g., platonic representations).

entry.title: SCOPE-4D: Endoscopic 4D Geometry Foundation Models

author.name: Chaoyi Zhou, Zhongpai Gao, Anwesa Choudhuri, Meng Zheng, Benjamin Planche, Run Wang, Terrence Chen, Siyu Huang, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: Presents SCOPE-4D, a foundation model jointly predicting camera parameters, dense geometry, and 3D tissue trajectories from monocular endoscopic video in a single forward pass, addressing scarce geometric supervision and the camera-motion versus tissue-deformation ambiguity. It also contributes SCOPE-5K, a curated dataset of roughly 5,000 real and synthetic gastrointestinal and laparoscopy clips with evaluation sets.

entry.title: Seeing, Saying, but Not Using: From Reportable Spatial Facts to Usable States in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SpaceConflict, a 23,196-input benchmark showing that multimodal LLMs can correctly report spatial facts yet fail to use them in downstream reasoning, an availability-utilization gap. It probes four levels of spatial state construction, from local fact binding to state judgment under transformation.

entry.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models

author.name: Zhaochong An, Fei Zhang, Menglin Jia, Duncan Frost, Zijian Zhou, Yikai Wang, Xudong Wang, Aditya Patel, Belinda Zeng, Tao Xiang, Serge Belongie, Amir Bar, Sen He

entry.summary: NAVA-WAM introduces native action-prior learning, directly pretraining robot action policies from observation-only videos without action annotations, avoiding indirect representation-to-control transfer or separate latent-action models. The two-stage training first pretrains on observation-only video and then grounds the learned action priors for robot control, improving scalability of world action models.

entry.title: PointWAM: 3D World Action Modeling for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Chunghyun Park, Beomjun Kim, Seungcheol Park, Heeseung Kwon, Yashu Shukla, Seunghoon Sim, Jinwoo Shin, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: Introduces PointWAM, a 3D world action model that decomposes the world into scene and hands and jointly forecasts both as 3D point trajectories in a shared space-time frame. This explicit disentangled representation captures contact geometry central to dexterous manipulation and enables effective pre-training for robot control.

entry.title: KungfuAthleteBot: learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video with unified robust recovery

author.name: Zhongxiang Lei, Lulu Cao, Xuyang Wang, Tianyi Qian, Jinyan Liu, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: KungfuAthleteBot (KAB) is a framework for learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video of national-level martial artists, addressing physics inconsistency, missing actuation information, and absent failure/recovery behavior. It contributes the KungfuAthlete dataset plus physics-guided trajectory correction and unified robust recovery mechanisms.

entry.title: Dynamic LLM Routers are Often Misguided

author.name: Sam Wang, Julia White, Sahibzada Allahyar, Dhruv Atreja, Urchade Zaratiana, Kelton Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzing six commercial LLM routers across 14 settings, the authors find none outperforms random selection between two well-chosen models at matched cost, with some underperforming by more than 10 percentage points. They trace the gap to four patterns including difficulty blindness and length reversal, and show these are what the standard cost-accuracy Pareto objective itself rewards.

entry.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses

author.name: Zekai Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Zekun Wang, Hai Wang, Yuhui Xu, Joshua Frandsen, Shancong Fu, Ashia C. Wilson, Chandan K. Reddy

entry.summary: VERSE is a self-evolving optimizer that improves LLM agent harnesses by also improving its own diagnostic, editing, and testing procedures, building tools for failure analysis, verification, training audits, and workflow control. The authors show in controlled studies that optimizer self-evolution fails without execution-based verification but achieves the best results when verification is available, validating the approach across five executors.

entry.title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models

author.name: Arnold Caleb Asiimwe, William Yang, Sanghyuk Chun, Esin Tureci, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: The authors offer an empirical observation, depth as time: when multi-step diffusion is compressed into a single forward pass via distillation or flow maps, the denoising computation appears to unfold across network depth and can be recovered by decoding intermediate layers with the model's own output head. This connects layer-wise computation in one-step generators to the diffusion sampling trajectory.

entry.title: IGNITE Tokamak World Model Architecture

author.name: Peter Steiner, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Nathaniel Chen, Kouroche Bouchiat, Ricardo Shousha, SangKyeun Kim, Egemen Kolemen

entry.summary: Introduces IGNITE, a generative world foundation model for fusion plasma behavior trained self-supervised on over a decade of unlabeled DIII-D experimental data, simulating tokamak discharges from actuator trajectories supplied directly or generated from text prompts or target outcomes. Uses multiple spatio-temporal tokenizers for heterogeneous modalities at vastly different time scales.

entry.title: Pincer: Resource Authorization for Agents using a Digital Twin

author.name: Mayank Rathee, Alexander Stepanov, Shalin Madabhavi, Jinhao Zhu, Raluca Ada Popa, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: Proposes Pincer, a resource authorization system for autonomous coding agents built around a digital twin, defending long-horizon shell-using agents with persistent memory without sacrificing the generality that typed tools or information-flow control give up. Addresses weaknesses of current user-mediated sandboxing (policy decay, permission fatigue) and auto-mode classifiers, from a strong security/systems team including Popa and Stoica.

entry.title: Misinformation Without Triggers: From Factual Answers to Downstream Decisions

author.name: Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: This safety study traces false web content in training data past a model's factual answers into downstream decisions, revealing an audit gap between what direct probes report and what the model actually does. Using a controlled decision task with matched truthful controls, the authors show that untriggered false training documents can propagate into scored decisions in ways that direct factual probes fail to predict.

entry.title: Training-Loss Guarantees for Muon with Finite-Step Newton--Schulz Orthogonalization

author.name: Amartya Roy, Souvik Chakraborty

entry.summary: The paper provides the first finite-time training-loss guarantee for the Muon optimizer that accounts for both momentum accumulation and its tuned five-step Newton-Schulz orthogonalization. For wide two-layer ReLU networks with a positive-definite limiting NTK, Muon provably reaches any target empirical squared loss with high probability.

entry.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks

author.name: Neeraj Karamchandani, Piyush Nagasubramaniam, Xinhong Xie, Sencun Zhu, Dinghao Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS), a metric for how much attack success rates change when surface representations (like tool names) are altered while the underlying threat, policy, and evaluation stay fixed. Experiments on Agent Security Bench show ASR varies substantially with superficial representation changes. The finding challenges the validity of comparing agent security via single-benchmark ASR scores.

entry.title: Harnessing LLMs as Agents: What Does It Cost?

author.name: Zelin Zhao (Georgia Institute of Technology), Xinyu Guo (Georgia Institute of Technology), Jingyuan Zhang (Georgia Institute of Technology), Yuxuan Zhang (Etude AI), Yongxin Chen (Georgia Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Language Model Agent Machine (LAM), a resource-bounded abstraction that quantifies the computational costs of agent harnesses such as context management, memory, tools, and verification. It establishes formal results including equivalence to red-blue pebbling under call-transfer budgets and asymptotic separations induced by memory interfaces. This provides a first rigorous theory of what agent scaffolding costs in computational resources.

entry.title: Iterating Consistency Models: Stability, Error Bounds and Noise Schedules

author.name: Alessio Spagnoletti, Abdul-Lateef Haji-Ali, Andr\'es Almansa, Alain Oliviero Durmus, Eric Moulines, Marcelo Pereyra

entry.summary: This paper provides the first non-asymptotic error analysis of multistep consistency model sampling, decomposing error into initialization-error contraction and approximation-error accumulation under verifiable stability assumptions. The theory explains why adding sampling steps can help or hurt depending on the noise schedule, assigning contraction to large early noise levels and residual control to small late levels. This gives principled guidance for CM sampler and schedule design.

entry.title: Asterism: Exploring and Synthesizing Scattered Observations into Literature-Grounded Hypotheses and Theories

author.name: Joseph Chee Chang, Michael D'Arcy, Amy X. Zhang, Pao Siangliulue, Sangho Suh, Aakanksha Naik, Jena D. Hwang, Javier Ramos Benitez, Stella Wroblewski, Matt Latzke, Michael Cuoco, Ruben Lozano-Aguilera, Kris Ganjam, Joel Chan, Doug Downey, Peter Jansen, Kyle J. Travaglini, Daniel S. Weld

entry.summary: Asterism is a system that extracts observations from hundreds of papers as concept-relation triples unified in a hierarchical ontology, letting researchers curate evidence graphs and aggregate observations at different granularities to ground theory formation. Unlike fully automated LLM theory synthesis, it keeps researcher choices and intuitions central to hypothesis generation.

entry.title: SpectralCache: Accelerating Diffusion-Based World Models via Spectral Feature Caching

author.name: Zhendong Mi, Pu Zhao, Ziyu Hu, Xiaodong Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Grace Li Zhang, Shaoyi Huang

entry.summary: Reveals that world-model diffusion features exhibit highly stable singular subspaces across nearby denoising steps with predictable singular-value evolution, and exploits this via SpectralCache, a training-free caching framework that reuses subspaces and estimates only low-dimensional singular values. This substantially reduces inference overhead for interactive diffusion-based world models.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens

author.name: Ruiyang Si, Jianxin Bi, Shunyu Yang, Rui Ni, Wenbo Huang, Qiang Wang, Shulong Jiang, Duomin Wang, Xiuyu Li, Haiwen Feng, Zhen Dong, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework in which a VLM agent composes robot primitives and learned VLA policies into Python cells with conditional checks and local retries, returning only explicitly requested observations for replanning. Across 700 tasks in LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, it achieves a 14 percent higher success rate with 65 percent fewer tokens than a matched tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner.

entry.title: On the Chain-of-Thought Monitorability of Looped Language Models

author.name: Han Wang, Ishwar B Balappanawar, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic evaluation of whether chain-of-thought monitoring remains effective for looped language models, which repeatedly apply shared transformer layers to gain latent computation without increasing size. The authors study loop depth effects within a LoopLM family and compare looped versus non-looped models matched by parameter, layer, or effective-depth budgets.

entry.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation:A Reinforcement Learning Perspective

author.name: Han Cui, Jianhao Yan, Yun Luo, Hongbo Zhang, Zhizhang Fu, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: This paper explains why on-policy distillation sometimes improves student models and sometimes collapses into long repetitive generation, framing the teacher as an implicit reward model over student behaviors. When the implicit reward aligns with quality, OPD helps; when misaligned, reward hacking drives collapse. The analysis also shows OPD improves performance without expanding student capabilities.

entry.title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras

author.name: Kush Hari, Justin Kerr, Nidhya Shivakumar, Samarth Mahapatra, Carmelo Sferrazza, Jiahui Lei, Jitendra Malik, C. Karen Liu, Ken Goldberg, Angjoo Kanazawa

entry.summary: EyeRobot 2.0 enables fine-grained bimanual robot manipulation with a single stereo camera by actively swiveling eye viewpoints to fixate a 3D point and processing images foveally with more visual tokens at centers. A hierarchy of an RL-trained gaze servoing policy and a target selector coordinates Active Visual Fixation during tasks. This bio-inspired design removes the need for wrist cameras while achieving precise manipulation.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Huijuan Wang, Chufan Shi, Cheng Yang, Yaokang Wu, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: The paper proposes recursive cross-capability self-improvement (RSI), a loop in which a unified text-and-image model uses its own understanding and generation abilities to produce training data for one another: it generates images, critiques them, writes programs targeting shortcomings, and uses execution-verified results to improve both image generation and visual understanding. Verified renders and correct programs become training signals.

entry.title: GRAFT: Growing Agglomerative Foundation Models via Continual Teacher Distillation

author.name: Zhenghao Zhao, Chi Zhang, Qingshuang Chen, Yelin Kim

entry.summary: Introduces GRAFT, a continual multi-teacher distillation framework allowing a single vision backbone to progressively absorb capabilities from an open-ended sequence of foundation models such as DINOv2, SigLIP2, and MASt3R. When a new teacher arrives, the previously trained backbone serves as a scaffold, avoiding repeated joint distillation over the full teacher set.

entry.title: Parasitic Co-Denoising: Unlocking 3D Human Motion Generation in a Frozen Video Diffusion Model

author.name: Yunjiao Zhou, Junlang Qian, Lihua Xie, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen text-to-video diffusion model (Wan2.1) contains recoverable 3D motion signals in its intermediate denoising states, and introduces parasitic co-denoising, where a lightweight flow-matching motion decoder extracts explicit 3D motion along the host model's schedule. This avoids training a separate motion generation model.

entry.title: Right Order, Wrong Scale: Auditing LLM Judges for Occupational AI Measurement

author.name: Harry Lyu, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: The paper introduces O*NET-BENCH, an audit suite built from 45,796 worker ratings, and evaluates 33 LLM judge configurations across six model families on 4,501 test ratings. Judges agree with workers on response ordering but wildly overestimate acceptance rates (3.0-97.9% versus a 61.1% human baseline), and a simple TF-IDF baseline nearly matches the best judge. This exposes a ranking-versus-calibration gap with implications for AI-in-the-workplace measurement.

entry.title: Open-Endedness Bench: Measuring Epistemic Process from Agent Records

author.name: Chengyang Shi, Xianglin Ji, Jintao Huang, Jicheng Wang, Yifeng He, Jiachen Liu

entry.summary: OEB introduces a benchmark-agnostic methodology for evaluating open-ended research agents by reading their execution logs and assessing how they form, test, and revise hypotheses, without requiring reference answers or outcome scores. This addresses the gap where open-ended agent runs are judged only by outcome, which cannot establish whether claims follow from executed experiments.

entry.title: Continual Graph Memory for Mathematical Research Agents

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Jinxi Yu, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Jiachen Lu, Zhi Zhang, Xinjie He, Hyunsik Chae, Ethan Ji, Alexander K Taylor, Vigyan Sahai, Yiwen Kou, Kai-Wei Chang, Raghu Meka, Nanyun Peng, Amit Sahai, Terence Tao, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Ansatz is a mathematical research agent built around Continual Graph Memory, a graph-based, evolvable cross-problem memory that organizes intermediate proof results from massive parallel long-horizon proof searches and reuses knowledge across explorations. It targets frontier mathematical research problems requiring extended multi-agent proof construction.

entry.title: Peer Influence across Heterogeneous AI Models

author.name: Frida N{\o}hr Laustsen, Marie Haahr Petersen, Victoria Popa, Ariel Flint, Romualdo Pastor-Satorras, Andrea Baronchelli, Luca Maria Aiello

entry.summary: Testing seven open-weight models across three language understanding tasks, this paper measures persuasion as probabilistic decision shift after a single dissenting exchange between AI agents. It finds persuasion is strong but that neither standalone certainty nor model scale reliably predicts who persuades whom - consistently correct models can be highly susceptible. These results matter for multi-agent system design and epistemic reliability.

entry.title: A Near-Zero Monitor Readout Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Control

author.name: Zhe Zhou, Tianhua Tao

entry.summary: This paper shows that low monitor readouts during RLVR training do not demonstrate that a monitor-based intervention controls reward hacking behavior. In a code-generation environment, three monitors passing the same offline gate produce probe scores at their numerical floor from early training, so near-zero readouts cannot distinguish monitoring success from the absence of the behavior being monitored.

entry.title: Counterfactual Predictions in Scientific Emulators Without Controlled Experiments

author.name: Dingling Yao, Kahaan Gandhi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev, Francesco Locatello, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: ReRoute is a framework for scientific what-if (counterfactual) prediction that combines factual data with partial mechanistic knowledge, avoiding the need for controlled simulation data in which confounded factors are disentangled. It fixes the queried input of a pretrained emulator and reroutes computations to answer unobserved interventions. Authored by Anima Anandkumar and Caltech collaborators, it addresses a fundamental limitation of neural scientific emulators.

entry.title: Compound AI System Reliability: A Failure Taxonomy and Resilience Pattern Catalog from 150 Production Incidents

author.name: Rudrendu Kumar Paul, Sourav Nandy

entry.summary: Analyzes 150 production incident reports from open-source compound AI projects and enterprise deployments to build a taxonomy of 23 failure modes across retrieval, generation, tool, orchestration, and integration failures, and proposes resilience patterns validated with measured effectiveness from controlled experiments. Focuses on failures at component boundaries rather than within individual models.

entry.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment

author.name: Yoojin Oh, Jeongsol Kim, Yeonwoo Seo, Jangho Park, Seonghyun Jin, Sunwoo Park, Youngmin Kim, Youngjun Jun, Kyumin Choi, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: FastOPD is a foundation-to-lightweight distillation framework for vision-language-action robot models, combining flow-map-based single-state teacher supervision with a self-consistency objective to build compact students that preserve teacher dynamics. It aims to make large-scale VLA models practical for real-world robot deployment without architecture redesign or reduced denoising steps.

entry.title: Discriminating Fixture Coverage in Agent-Infrastructure Verification Suites

author.name: Xin Xu, Siru Tao
