IntentCoding addresses this by masking the intent and applying multi-strength contrastive decoding to amplify its influence at generation time, improving adherence to fine-grained multi-constraint instructions.

entry.title: Latent-MOPD: Latent Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhengyu Fang, Seoyeon Hong, Jie Yang, Muyang Li, Koyoshi Shindo, Brandon Joseph Lwowski, Jing Li

entry.summary: Latent-MOPD is the first representation-level multi-teacher on-policy distillation method for LLMs, integrating specialists through both output predictions and hidden states without additional teacher training. It coordinates representation supervision via late-layer target selection, shared projections for unequal hidden widths, and domain-grouped updates, with supervision gradually shifting from hidden states to token predictions. This extends on-policy distillation beyond output-distribution matching.

entry.title: Conditional Capacity and Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Particle Transformers

author.name: Kaushik Pendiyala, Haris Zia, Trevin Lee, Timothy Legge, Alejandro J. De Leon, Zihan Zhao, Aaron Wang, Abhijith Gandrakota, Jennifer Ngadiuba, Richard Cavanaugh, Javier Duarte

entry.summary: The paper studies dense versus MoE particle transformers on the 188-class JetClass-II benchmark, varying expert count, routing capacity, top-K, and auxiliary losses. Findings include that top-1 MoE improves over dense at nearly unchanged compute when token dropping is avoided, more stored experts yield little gain, and expert assignments grow more strongly associated with physics classes over training. This grounds MoE design choices in a real scientific domain.

entry.title: Peer Effects in Signed Networks: Separating Influence Through Positive and Negative Ties

author.name: Xiaojing Du, Jiuyong Li, Lin Liu, Debo Cheng, Jixue Liu, Thuc Duy Le

entry.summary: The paper defines causal peer effects through positive and negative ties in signed social networks, including sign-composition effects of reallocating treatment between tie types, and provides identification formulas. It proposes SiDE, a signed-exposure doubly robust estimator, proving double robustness and showing that sign-blind analysis mixes opposing influences.

entry.title: Coverage You Can Steer: Online Conformal Calibration for RL-Driven Hardware-Aware NAS

author.name: Pedro Brandimarte, Nerea Aranjuelo, Marcos Nieto, Oihana Otaegui

entry.summary: The paper addresses the failure of distribution-free conformal guarantees in RL-driven neural architecture search, where the improving policy and layer-by-layer construction violate exchangeability. It replaces one-shot quantile estimation with online adaptive conformal inference to prune candidates while retaining coverage guarantees throughout the search.

entry.title: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Lu\'is Marques, Rong Fang, Disha Kamale, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: The authors propose SLLCP, a post-hoc conformal calibration layer over frozen vision-language models that converts unreliable VLM collision-likelihood estimates into distribution-free safety bounds for trajectory monitoring in autonomous driving. This addresses the gap between VLM reasoning ability and the guarantees required for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Depth Hypothesis Guided Iterative Refinement for Event-Image Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Daikun Liu, Teng Wang, Changyin Sun

entry.summary: HypoDepth reframes event-image monocular depth estimation from direct full-depth regression into a constrained depth search using a discrete Depth Hypothesis Volume, with a 3D cost volume and multi-scale correlation search guiding residual refinement. The lightweight cost-volume design enables efficient iterative refinement suited to event cameras' dynamic properties.

entry.title: FlashSinkhorn 2: Block-Sparse Entropic Optimal Transport

author.name: Felix X. -F. Ye, Yu Chin Fabian Lim, Naigang Wang, Davis Wertheimer

entry.summary: FlashSinkhorn 2 is a GPU solver for entropic optimal transport with squared-Euclidean cost that couples a coarse centroid-based stage with a block-sparse fine stage, avoiding evaluation of all pairwise point interactions per Sinkhorn iteration. It solves large discrete OT problems to a prescribed marginal residual on a single GPU. Morton-ordered blocks enable screening and fused kernel execution.

entry.title: Hypothesis-guided discovery of cognitive algorithms via program refinement

author.name: Huiwen Alex Yang, Mark K. Ho, Bill D. Thompson

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid approach to cognitive modeling that treats discovery of cognitive algorithms as program refinement: human-created cognitive models expressed as probabilistic programs are handed to LLM agents tasked with refining them against behavioral data. This combines the interpretability and human expertise of traditional cognitive modeling with the scalability of LLM-based model generation. It targets harder tasks like algorithm recovery than prior LLM-based approaches.

entry.title: Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks Need Scenario-Grounded Stress Testing

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Lian Xu, Hao Xue

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that time series forecasting evaluation is too narrow, rewarding low held-out error and treating robustness as Gaussian noise or bounded perturbations. The authors contend that real input-side anomalies reflect structured events causing regime shifts and broken cross-variable dependencies, and advocate scenario-grounded stress testing to capture semantic, causal, and system-level failures.

entry.title: Modeling Shared and Individual Structure for Cross-Subject Continuous Affect Regression from EEG-fNIRS

author.name: Xuan Wang, Bing Wang, Shuai Chang, Hao Yuan, Xinbo Qi, Xinyue Zhang

entry.summary: The paper tackles zero-shot cross-subject continuous valence-arousal estimation from synchronized EEG-fNIRS recordings, decomposing affect trajectories into stimulus-shared structure and individual structure estimated from a label-free EEG marker. It predicts raw-scale trajectories for test subjects whose labels are never observed, a harder setting than typical subject-dependent affect modeling.

entry.title: AMBER: Multi-View Adaptive Budget Allocation for Listwise Vision-Language Reranking

author.name: Wenteng Chen, Jiachen Zhu, Rong Shan, Tianyi Xu, Yuxiang Chen, Congmin Zheng, Teng Wang, Junjie Wu, Weiwen Liu, Changwang Zhang, Weinan Zhang, Jun Wang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: AMBER is an online, budgeted framework for multimodal listwise reranking that treats fragmented VLM outputs as local tournaments maintained via continuous Elo updates, then allocates VLM calls adaptively across candidate views. It replaces fixed call schedules with dynamic global resource allocation to reduce expensive inference costs.

entry.title: Relevant Evidence Decoding for Audio-Visual Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Hyunjae Ra, Aecheon Jung, Jungin Park, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: This paper identifies a cross-modal interference problem in audio-visual LLMs where joint inference can weaken correct single-modality predictions, such as losing confidence in a heard violin when a guitar appears visually. Its Relevant Evidence Decoding method extends contrastive decoding to select the perceptual evidence a given question actually requires.

entry.title: Lightweight, Rubric-Guided Trajectory Evaluation for Production AI Agents

author.name: Linh-An Phan, MingXue Wang, Guangyu Wu, Feng Pan, Zhaoyu Pang, Yanbin Zhang

entry.summary: LiteTrajEval is a budget-bounded architecture for evaluating LLM agent trajectories: it derives domain rule profiles offline, preprocesses trajectories with heuristic failure signals, serializes under a fixed token budget, and invokes a single rubric-guided LLM judge. Evaluated on Magentic-One-style and tau-bench-style trajectories, it targets the cost problem of repeated production evaluation. The output is structured diagnostic reports.

entry.title: CVE2AP: Automated Generation of PDDL-Encoded Attack Paths via Large Language Models

author.name: Lin Cui, Vincenzo Scotti, Raffaela Mirandola

entry.summary: CVE2AP uses LLMs to automatically convert CVE threat intelligence into formally machine-verifiable attack paths encoded in PDDL, replacing expert-driven manual modeling. This improves scalability of cybersecurity analysis for vulnerability exploitation and attack progression reasoning.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System

author.name: Rub\'en Manrique, Michelle Castellanos, Jorge Morales, Juan David Guti\'errez, Antonio Barreto Rozo, Joaqu\'in V\'elez Navarro

entry.summary: This paper introduces an expert-validated 1,042-item benchmark of Colombian law across ten legal areas and three question formats, built with a human-in-the-loop multi-stage expert review pipeline. Evaluating 15 proprietary and open-weight models shows wide accuracy ranges on closed questions (0.577 to 0.905 for Gemini 3.1 Pro, an established model since early 2026) and significant factual reliability gaps in free-text legal answers.

entry.title: Causal discovery identifies pathways linking physical activity to dementia risk in the UK BioBank

author.name: Wasif Khan, Panayiotis V. Benos, Joshua K. Wong, Ruogu Fang

entry.summary: This study combines LLM-guided causal discovery with mediation analysis on 42,293 UK Biobank participants to identify pathways through which moderate-to-vigorous physical activity lowers dementia risk, including depression, functional capacity, smoking, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease. It demonstrates how LLMs can guide causal structure learning in large-scale epidemiological data. The work matters for both AI methodology and clinical science around dementia prevention.

entry.title: Network-in-the-Loop at Scale: GPU-Batched 5G Simulation for Massively Parallel Robot Learning

author.name: Zifan Zhang, Mingzhe Han, Kannan Athreya, Yuchen Liu

entry.summary: Isaac-Net is a GPU-batched 5G New Radio simulation module that advances uplink scheduling of thousands of environments in lockstep with Isaac Lab physics, enabling network-in-the-loop training for multi-robot fleets on private 5G networks. It bridges the gap between GPU robot simulators that oversimplify networking and packet-level simulators that cannot keep pace. This matters for realistic training of networked multi-robot policies.

entry.title: FinDialogLens: Event Extraction over Multi-Party Dialogue for Missed-Trade Identification in Financial Chatrooms

author.name: Chin-Lun Fu, Hong Ni, Behrouz Madahian

entry.summary: Presents FinDialogLens, a hybrid LLM pipeline for event extraction over multi-party financial chatroom dialogue to recover missed trades, using compact fine-tuned classifiers as scaffolds to detect RFQ triggers and outcomes, segment per-event windows, and fill argument roles. Achieves 92.1% and 94.3% on key metrics with GPT-4o on a challenging industrial task.

entry.title: From Fragments to Global Maps: Learning Vectorized Map Aggregation with Large Language Models

author.name: Ziwei Li, Yi-Tang Chen, Xiaoqi Wang, Wenbin He, Han-Wei Shen, Liu Ren

entry.summary: Proposes MapMergeLLM, a data-driven framework that formulates aggregation of noisy, fragmented, overlapping local map predictions into global HD maps for autonomous driving as conditional sequence generation with LLMs, replacing hand-crafted association thresholds. Aims to handle road-structure variation and detector-specific errors without manual tuning.

entry.title: TPBench: A Turning-Point Benchmark for Dialogue Compression

author.name: Minji Park, Seunghyun Yoon, Hyuk Lim

entry.summary: TPBench is a benchmark for dialogue compression that targets turning-point eviction — the failure where a compressor preserves facts but drops the turn that changed the conversation state, such as a user correction or revised constraint. It evaluates three information targets (initial goal, current revised slot value, and both) at fixed retention budgets, grounding answers in human dialogue-state annotations from MultiWOZ and SGD. This exposes failure modes hidden by single aggregate retention scores.

entry.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback

author.name: Khang Luong, Dinh Thai Son, Hoang Ta, Hung The Tran, Tuan Quang Dam

entry.summary: The paper studies best-arm identification in bandits when only one bit of feedback per round is available, via threshold queries over a query set of arms. It develops a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive and embeds it into fixed-clipping and phased-elimination algorithms with near-optimal (epsilon, delta)-PAC guarantees.

entry.title: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites

author.name: Jiangang Han

entry.summary: WebFovea is a vision-based web agent that placed second in the WebRetriever Challenge 2026, and the paper analyzes why a correct model decision can still fail in execution: parsing of the reply, action application, result reporting, and verification must each succeed. It emphasizes harness engineering and round-trip verification for reliable operation on live websites.

entry.title: SyntaxBench: A Statistical Diagnostic Framework for Character-Level Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Mohsen Larni (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Sobhan Ebrahimi Azar (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Pouyan Nahed (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Kazem Taghva (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas)

entry.summary: SyntaxBench is a benchmark with five core character-level reasoning tasks (counting, containment, palindromes, edit distance, longest-string selection) plus a harder substring-extraction stress test, using matched English and random-string inputs with multiple shot settings. It evaluates whether current LLMs handle small syntactic errors that matter in real deployments.

entry.title: The Price of Greenwashing: Algorithmic Verification and Market Discipline using Conformal Machine Learning

author.name: Sourav Bose, Taoufik Bouraoui

entry.summary: The authors fuse SEC financial fundamentals with facility-level EPA greenhouse gas registries to build a statistically guaranteed baseline of physical corporate emissions, using gradient boosting with Mondrian Conformal Prediction. They quantify the gap between self-reported and algorithmically estimated emissions via a Conformal-Weighted Coefficient, offering an objective greenwashing measure for financial markets. The work targets a real econometric gap beyond subjective ESG ratings.

entry.title: Co-design Gym: A Unified Benchmark for Embodiment-Policy Co-optimization

author.name: Aviraj Newatia, Yordan Tsvetkov, Leonard Pleiss, Andrew Spielberg, Rika Antonova

entry.summary: This benchmark addresses the joint optimization of an agent's embodiment and its control policy, a problem class where optimizing each separately is suboptimal. Co-design Gym provides a unified suite spanning robotics-style tasks so the community can study co-optimization explicitly, moving beyond the fixed-embodiment assumption in most RL benchmarks. Co-designed by a credible academic team including Andrew Spielberg and Rika Antonova.

entry.title: VisAudit: Evaluating Multimodal Agents for Visual Diagnosis and Repair

author.name: Shicheng Liu, Adam Kahirov, Qi Zhang, Zhimin Hu, Song Wang, Junhong Lin, Julian Shun, Yada Zhu

entry.summary: VisAudit is a benchmark for evaluating whether multimodal agents can autonomously review visualizations: recognizing when a chart is wrong, deciding what to change, repairing it without breaking correct content, and verifying success. It goes beyond existing benchmarks that test chart generation or defect detection in isolation, providing configurable auxiliary evidence such as source tables and code. This fills a gap in agentic evaluation for data visualization workflows.

entry.title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction

author.name: Vansh Ramani, Har Ashish Arora, Dhairya Kuchhal, Sayan Ranu, Tarak Karmakar

entry.summary: DISSOLVR is a transparent framework for molecular solubility prediction that couples molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior, challenging the trend of opaque deep-learning architectures in chemistry. The authors perform a comprehensive literature review and benchmarking, showing the interpretable approach approaches or matches state-of-the-art performance across aqueous and organic solubility. This matters for pharmaceutical development and environmental modeling.

entry.title: Structural-Functional Brain Connectivity Generation via Multimodal Hypergraph-based Flow Matching

author.name: Chyong Yi Poh, Hwa Hui Tew, Junn Yong Loo, Rapha\"{e}l C. -W. Phan, Fuad Noman, Pew-Thian Yap, Chee-Ming Ting

entry.summary: The paper proposes MHG-FM, a multimodal hypergraph flow matching framework for jointly generating and translating between structural and functional brain connectivity networks. By using hypergraphs instead of pairwise graphs, it captures higher-order interactions and preserves cross-modal structure-function relationships that independent generation methods miss.

entry.title: On Unlearning for Time-series Forecasting

author.name: Zeyu Shi, Yanhui Luo, Ziming Hong, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Shanshan Ye, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: The paper tackles machine unlearning for time-series forecasting, where deleted observations participate in multiple causally connected windows, making gradient-based unlearning unstable. It proposes methods tailored to these dependencies to honor deletion requests without costly retraining in sensitive longitudinal-data domains.

entry.title: Dirac-Interconnected Neural Elements: Discovering Modularity in Physical Systems Without Reduction

author.name: Reiho Li, Razmik Arman Khosrovian, Takaharu Yaguchi, Hiroaki Yoshimura, Takashi Matsubara

entry.summary: DINEs are a neural architecture that represents physical systems as interconnections of components using Dirac structures, discovering modularity without requiring it to be known a priori or reducing the system to an ODE that discards algebraic constraints. This preserves the physical structure of interconnected dynamical systems during data-driven modeling.

entry.title: Learn Feasibility Once, Optimize All Objectives: Derivative-Free Diffusion Models for Chance-Constrained Programming

author.name: Ziwen Liu, Yan Liu, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Yao Yan, Weichen Zhao

entry.summary: D3Opt disentangles constraint modeling from objective optimization in chance-constrained programs by training a risk-conditioned diffusion model on constraint-filtered decisions once, then freezing it as a reusable prior for post-specified objectives. This enables derivative-free optimization of non-convex, non-smooth objectives under fixed chance constraints.

entry.title: 16-bit Precision of Convolutional Neural Networks on Microcontroller Units for 8-bit Costs

author.name: Rui Liu, Benjamin Paa{\ss}en

entry.summary: The W16A16 quantization scheme achieves 16-bit precision inference on Armv7E-M microcontrollers at the speed and energy cost typically associated with 8-bit approaches. The paper analyzes the architecture to explain the performance advantage, reporting roughly 10 times lower quantization error along with measured time and energy savings.

entry.title: On the Convergence of Success Conditioning for Policy Optimization

author.name: Matthew Brun, Xu Andy Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides formal convergence guarantees for success conditioning, a widely used strategy that reinforces actions leading to successful outcomes in stochastic environments. The authors prove convergence to optimal policies on a broad class of MDPs and derive rates, including O(1/eps^p) iteration bounds for discounted MDPs and results for single-period settings. This puts a common heuristic in RL practice on firmer theoretical footing.

entry.title: RINS: Residual-Image Neural Subspace Solvers for Large Sparse Linear Systems

author.name: Zhongyan Ouyang, Weixin Liao, Mingquan Feng, Yehui Tang, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Gate-RINS is a neural subspace solver for large sparse linear systems from PDE discretizations that generates polynomial correction bases from cached residual probes, modulated by a lightweight pointwise gate. The projected least-squares update is unchanged, so the neural component only picks expansion directions while numerical closure tests them. Experiments across six PDE-derived benchmarks plus a hybrid controller schedule show improved solver behavior.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Asymptotics and Dataset Selection for Private Transfer Learning

author.name: Filip Kova\v{c}evi\'c, Edwige Cyffers, Stefano Sarao Mannelli, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: The paper models when acquiring external, potentially sensitive data justifies its cost for transfer learning, using high-dimensional regression with heterogeneous sources and weighted ridge estimation. It accounts for negative transfer and the noise injected by differential privacy, providing theoretical guidance for data purchasing and collaborative learning decisions.

entry.title: Clinical Concept Centers in LLMs

author.name: Aishik Nagar, Abhishek Vaidyanathan, Arun-Kumar Kaliya-Perumal, Elijah Tzen Hsuen Boey, Stefan Winkler

entry.summary: This work extends mechanistic interpretability into clinical decision support, asking whether clinical concepts are linearly encoded in LLM latent spaces. Building on findings that internal representations encode more than verbalized output, it probes whether latent-space evaluation can reveal clinically relevant structure that stated reasoning omits.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes

author.name: Alexander Ardaiz, Varun Budati, Ali Habibnia

entry.summary: This paper evaluates DDQL and K-means-partitioned mixture-of-DDQL-experts against parameter-matched dense networks on BTC/USDT limit order book data, finding no learned configuration significantly improves mean implementation shortfall over vanilla DDQL, and all underperform simple baselines like TWAP. It highlights training-seed variance as a source of spurious architectural gains and analyzes tail risk and failure modes. A valuable cautionary result about RL in financial execution.

entry.title: Amortized Structured Stochastic Variational Inference for Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models

author.name: Maksym Tretiakov, Sarah Lucie Filipp, Vincent Fortuin, Ruth Misener, Ruby Sedgwick, James Odgers

entry.summary: The paper improves uncertainty estimation in Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models by replacing the standard mean-field variational approximation with amortized structured stochastic variational inference, allowing the latent-space posterior to be conditionally dependent on GP inducing points. This captures epistemic uncertainty of the learned manifold more faithfully. Results demonstrate improved behavior over the mean-field baseline.

entry.title: EpiWorld: Grounding LLM Policy Agents in Epidemiological World Models

author.name: Zeeshan Memon, Yiqi Su, Kai Shu, Naren Ramakrishnan, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: EpiWorld is a closed-loop framework that grounds an LLM policy agent in a learned action-conditioned epidemiological world model plus a tiered skill library of public-health protocols and surveillance tools. It aims to let LLMs reason about epidemic interventions with realistic dynamics, quantitative signals, and institutional constraints.

entry.title: Adaptive Mutual Distillation for Balanced Multi-Task Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Baohang Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Yichong Huang, Chengpeng Fu, Wenshuai Huo, Zekun Zhou, Zekun Yuan, Tingjia Zhang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: AMD is a post-training framework in which two LLMs trained with different task-balancing strategies distill from each other, using short shared training probes to adaptively weight cross-model supervision across tasks, transfer directions, and training stages. It aims to combine complementary task strengths in multi-task post-training.

entry.title: Investigating the Role of Reasoning-Language Alignment in Monolingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Oliver Hauck, Mario Sanz-Guerrero, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: This study examines whether forcing models to reason in a non-English language degrades RAG accuracy, extending prior short-prompt findings to settings where the model must integrate large amounts of retrieved German evidence. It builds a fully monolingual German RAG testbed over The Dark Eye tabletop RPG world, a niche but richly documented German domain.

entry.title: Writerslogic at PAN 2026: Process over Content for Robust Detection under Domain Shift

author.name: David L. Condrey

entry.summary: This paper describes systems for three PAN 2026 shared tasks unified by a shared analytical framework: feature robustness under distribution shift is governed by support overlap between training and test distributions, yielding a taxonomy of domain-anchored, domain-portable, and domain-invariant features. It explains why generator-specific features fail under domain shift while vocabulary fingerprints, compression measures, and character n-grams survive.

entry.title: Confidence-Controlled XAI Auditing for Pedestrian Detection under Domain Shift

author.name: Ruben Dario Florez-Zela

entry.summary: Audits post-hoc explanation faithfulness for a YOLOv8s pedestrian detector across the PIE and JAAD driving datasets using ROI-based D-Deletion, confidence stratification, and statistical corrections. Findings show deletion-based faithfulness is strongly coupled to detection strength at explanation time, and after controlling for it, D-RISE faithfulness remains domain-dependent in central confidence bins.

entry.title: Capturing Dynamics: The 4D Facial Expression Intensity Dataset

author.name: Zesheng Wang, Alexandre Bruckert, Pierre Lebreton, Patrick Le Callet, Yante Li, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces 4DFEID, a dataset of 2,869 mesh sequences generated with parametric face models under controlled geometric variations, enabling study of facial expression intensity in genuinely 3D and temporally continuous form rather than frame-level 2D representations. The dataset supports perception and analysis tasks relevant to affective computing and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: CrowdOcc: Monocular Semantic Scene Completion for Quadruped Robots in Crowded Indoor Environments

author.name: Feiyang Chen, Jincheng Hu, Yiduo Chen, Jihao Li, Yue Liang, Bingzhao Gao, Yanjun Huang, Yuanjian Zhang

entry.summary: CrowdOcc contributes an RGB-D dataset of 25.1K frames from 11 crowded indoor scenes plus a monocular semantic scene completion framework for quadruped robots. It combines normal-guided geometry fusion for occlusion robustness with human-centric sparse interaction modeling to improve human occupancy prediction.

entry.title: Geometry-Aligned Semantic Matching for Cross-Modal Planar Image Registration

author.name: Zhiwei Wang, Defeng He, Yuxing Li, Meilu Zhu, Edmund Y. Lam

entry.summary: CDPM addresses cross-modal image matching by progressively adapting DINOv3 to produce geometrically consistent semantic representations, then preserving their dominance during fine-grained correspondence estimation. The method bridges the gap between semantically consistent but geometrically loose features and accurate local CNN details.

entry.title: Interpretable Deepfake Detection in Videos via Explicit Forensic Features and Temporal Modeling

author.name: Chahira Benhama, Mohand Sa\"id Allili, Assia Hamadene

entry.summary: This work proposes an interpretable deepfake video detection framework that explicitly encodes physically grounded forensic cues over temporal windows of identity-consistent facial trajectories, using 68 structured descriptors per frame. The explicit representation enables transparent analysis and improved generalization across datasets compared to end-to-end black-box detectors.

entry.title: From Language Priors to Field Adaptation: Preference Learning for Traversability Estimation

author.name: Simon Schwaiger, David Seyser, Alessandro Scherl, Zlatan Ajanovi\'c, Wilfried W\"ober, Gerald Steinbauer-Wagner

entry.summary: Proposes sample-efficient preference learning for image-based traversability estimation, using von Mises-Fisher mixture prototypes in a frozen vision-language feature space. Natural-language relative rules provide a commonsense prior while sparse relative image annotations adapt the prototypes to a target domain, matching fully supervised WayFAST accuracy with far fewer labels.

entry.title: RUL-Aware RRT*: Degradation-Balanced Motion Planning for Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Haibo Li, Zhiguo Zeng, Xu Li

entry.summary: This work extends RRT* motion planning for robotic manipulators by incorporating joint remaining-useful-life (RUL) information, adaptively shifting joint usage away from the most degraded actuators. Evaluated across full-health, heterogeneous-degradation, and other scenarios, it aims to prevent premature failure of the weakest joint and reduce unplanned downtime. This connects prognostics and health management with motion planning.

entry.title: Cross-Fitting Under Nonregularity: Normality and Inference via Locality

author.name: Bruno Fava

entry.summary: This statistics paper studies confidence intervals for cross-fitted estimators when standard asymptotics fail due to nonregularity, as in model-comparison via cross-validation, heterogeneous treatment effect testing, and optimal treatment regime estimation. Using a new locality condition, the author proves a central limit theorem still holds but with an asymptotic variance corrected for cross-fold correlation. This yields valid inference in settings where naive cross-fit intervals undercover.

entry.title: Label-Efficient Time Series Classification at Scale: A Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM with Counterfactual Attribution

author.name: Nguyen Ho, Bach Tung Tran, Trung Ky Nguyen, Zhenchang Xia, Bolong Zheng, Long Van Ho

entry.summary: The paper studies few-shot time series classification in a fixed-label regime with only K labeled examples per class, proposing Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM, an episodic metric-learning framework pairing an Omni-Scale CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration and counterfactual attribution. It targets label-scarce industrial, wearable, and clinical monitoring settings.

entry.title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Yushuo Zhao, Dewei Liu, Junfeng Fang, Bimei Wang, Tiantian Rao, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: DNAlign is a lightweight safety alignment framework that treats the LLM as a dynamic system and applies control-theoretic perturbations restricted via null-space projection to the harm-related subspace, aiming to steer generation toward safe behavior without degrading general capabilities. It targets the persistent safety-utility trade-off in alignment.

entry.title: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency

author.name: Yulong Ming, Jie Xu, Zihan Wu, Xiaohua Jia

entry.summary: PACE is a system that decides when compiling repeatedly executed GUI procedures into programs is worthwhile, with a measurement protocol recording successful and failed compilation costs and an online algorithm weighing uncertain payback against unknown future reuse and GUI drift. It compares agent and program execution costs on matched inputs to estimate per-use savings.

entry.title: MRVQ: One Resident Index for Dimension- and Rate-Elastic Vector Search

author.name: Sean Culatana, Shang-En Huang, Kang Li

entry.summary: MRVQ (Matryoshka Residual Vector Quantization) is a post-hoc quantizer for frozen embeddings whose single maximum-rate code can be truncated both by dropping residual stages (lowering rate) and dropping coordinates (lowering dimension), so one artifact serves every dimension-rate pair. Across two datasets, four embedding families, and multiple code sizes, it achieves the lowest RAM of evaluated designs with strong quality.

entry.title: EviDent-CBCT: Evidence-Bottlenecked Report Generation from Dental CBCT under Non-Exhaustive Report Supervision

author.name: Ruiyang Hao, Zhi Qin Tan, Yulan He, Owen Addison, Yunpeng Li

entry.summary: EviDent-CBCT generates dento-maxillofacial CBCT reports from 3D scans under incomplete supervision, where non-mention of a finding may reflect absence or non-reporting. An anatomy-aware network produces a discrete evidence record, a dental-logic consistency projection reconciles incompatible findings, and an image-blind local language model renders the report from that record. The evidence-bottleneck design addresses both reliability and the messy realities of clinical documentation.

entry.title: Approximation Property of Dropout Neural Networks: Sobolev Rates and Confidence Bounds

author.name: Jia-He Yao

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes finite-sample, high-probability uniform approximation rates for ReLU networks with independently dropped edges, constructing constant-depth networks of size on the order of p^-9 times Sobolev-unit-ball error terms with confidence bounds. It also derives matching Sobolev lower bounds. The work quantifies how dropout randomness affects approximation, bridging universal approximation and probabilistic guarantees.

entry.title: Bandits via Additive Quantized Representations

author.name: Ami Tavory, Noam Touitou, Tal Sarig, Frank Cheng, Ido Guy

entry.summary: The paper uses offline-trained residual quantization codebooks as a representation layer for contextual bandits, mapping continuous contexts into discrete multi-level centroid assignments with bounded O(1)-style memory. This yields additive bandit algorithms with nonlinear expressivity without retraining or large replay buffers, beating non-RQ counterparts across 13 datasets. Likely from an industrial team addressing online efficiency.

entry.title: Efficient Memory Crystallization for Graph Learning under Non-Stationary Distribution Shifts

author.name: Yue Hou, Ruomei Liu, Yingke Su, Junran Wu, Ke Xu

entry.summary: EMC is a training-free test-time framework that distills each incoming graph domain into a compact memory via a closed-form solution to a memory-oriented objective, avoiding costly auxiliary generative modules used for cross-domain graph adaptation. This targets non-stationary graph distribution shifts more efficiently than generative memory synthesis.

entry.title: Adaptive Second-Order Solvers for Fast Stochastic Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Ella Kemperman, Luca Ambrogioni

entry.summary: The authors adapt proportional-integral step-size control to diffusion model sampling using a diffusion noise-normalized error estimator, incorporating previous errors for smoother step adaptation. They also show per-sample trajectories share structure that can be aggregated into a fixed schedule, retaining speed benefits without runtime adaptation.

entry.title: Dual-Context Analog Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jung Min Choi, Ngoc Son Le, Ibram Abdelmalak, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: DuoTS improves long-term time-series forecasting by retrieving past states analogous to the present and progressively integrating their observed continuations as evidence, rather than relying on a single nearest match. It combines a parallel patch encoder base forecast with retrieval-augmented refinement to avoid unreliable single analogs and redundant patch candidates.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Deep Sequence Models

author.name: Junghwan Lee, Jonghyeok Lee, Yao Xie

entry.summary: This paper surveys how deep sequence models, including RNNs and Transformers, can be integrated into conformal prediction frameworks for time series, where exchangeability-based coverage guarantees fail. It systematizes the design space and studies how deep model properties interact with conformal calibration for reliable uncertainty quantification in forecasting. This serves as a structured reference for a fast-moving area.

entry.title: Explainable Molecular Structure Inference from GC--MS with Diffusion Models and LLM Reranking

author.name: Changlin Liu, Tianyu Yi, Chengchun Liu, Boxuan Zhao, Fanyang Mo

entry.summary: DiffGCMS is a spectrum-conditioned discrete graph diffusion model for de novo molecular structure elucidation from GC-EI-MS data, addressing the limitation of reference-library matching for unknown compounds. A two-stage framework adds LLM-based reasoning and reranking over candidate structures generated from spectra.

entry.title: Automatic Evaluation of Mental Health Stigma in Online Communication

author.name: Naomi Baes, Jemima Kang, Nick Haslam, Chris Groot, Alsa Wu, Luc Raszewski, Yulia Otmakhova

entry.summary: This work introduces a theory-grounded benchmark for detecting mental health stigma in naturally occurring news and social media text, with a fine-grained taxonomy covering stigma mode, domain, and specific components across multiple conditions. It enables automatic evaluation of both explicit and subtle stigma such as blame, pity, and social distancing.

entry.title: FUSEye: Training-Light Fisheye Detection with Overlapping Views and Zero-Initialized Adapters

author.name: Wenya Su, Kai Luo, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Kunyu Peng, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: Presents FUSEye, a parameter-efficient framework converting a frozen COCO-pretrained YOLO26-x detector into a fisheye camera detector by adding roughly 227k parameters via zero-initialized adapters, overlapping grid views, and other targeted modifications addressing radial distortion and boundary object shrinkage. It avoids the label and compute costs of full fine-tuning.

entry.title: ChromaGS: Text-Driven Semantic Editing of 4D Gaussian Avatars

author.name: Antonio Canela, Jordi S\`anchez-Riera

entry.summary: ChromaGS enables real-time, language-guided color editing of animatable 3D Gaussian head avatars by augmenting each Gaussian with learned soft assignments to semantic regions and decomposing colors into region-level base colors and Gaussian-level residuals. Edits are applied at render time with no retraining, propagating coherently across all associated Gaussians while preserving fine details.

entry.title: Traversing the Satisfaction-Diversity Frontier in Text-to-Image Diffusion

author.name: Kevin Zhai, Siva Rajesh Kasa, Soumya Roy, Sumit Negi, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: The paper reframes multi-sample text-to-image generation as a satisficing problem where each image must clear a reward floor and the batch must meet a diversity cutoff, rather than mixing reward and diversity into one aggregate score. Varying the reward floor traces a frontier between worst-candidate reward and batch diversity. This prevents high diversity from compensating for low-quality samples.

entry.title: Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Agent Safety False Alarm Auditing

author.name: Xichen Yan, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Guangyi Zhang, Jiaqi Wu, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: This paper casts false-alarm auditing for LLM agent safety monitors as a positive-unlabeled ranking problem, exploiting small sets of verified-safe non-alarmed trajectories while alarms remain unlabeled. It addresses the monitor-induced selection bias where observed safe references pass the monitor while hidden safe alarms do not.

entry.title: When Numbers Start Talking: Numerical Signalling and Strategic Behaviour Among LLMs

author.name: Alessio Buscemi, Daniele Proverbio, Alessandro Di Stefano, The Anh Han, German Castignani, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: The study examines how different message types (natural language, numerical signals, random sequences) affect cooperation among LLM agents playing four strategic games with different cooperation equilibria. Results show structured messages alter payoffs but without a predictable pattern, challenging assumptions about AI agent communication. The work also probes effects of assigned agent personalities.

entry.title: EditHero: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Part-Level 3D Editing and Vibe Modeling

author.name: Ruihan Yu, Yu-Ju Tsai, Muyao Niu, Runyi Li, Lian Fu, Hanqing Liu, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yonghao Yu, Sho Kuno, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: EditHero is the first benchmark for long-horizon, part-level 3D editing, evaluating natural-language edit sequences for both geometry and texture with hand-reviewed targets produced by a deterministic assembly engine. It contrasts non-agentic methods that regenerate objects top-down against LLM/VLM agents that edit bottom-up. This addresses the realistic setting where assets evolve through many sequential revisions rather than single edits.

entry.title: Student-Guided Teacher Distillation for Efficient LLM Task Routing: Positioning Against Jev-Style System-1 Classifiers

author.name: Haifeng Wu, Srinivasan Manoharan, Jian Wan, Fangbo Tu, Junhua Zhao, Xin Chen

entry.summary: Studies a student-guided distillation pipeline for routing requests to 60 LLM task categories: a compact ModernBERT student produces a full distribution in one pass to retrieve top-k candidates, which a larger DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot NLI teacher reranks, with iterative label improvement. Avoids linear cost scaling with taxonomy size.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Speculative Sampling for Diffusion Draft Trees

author.name: Marcello Bullo, Yanxiao Liu, \"Oyk\"u S{\i}la G\"uner, Arpan Mukherjee, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: RASS improves speculative sampling for diffusion generation by exploiting the free ranking of draft candidates along proposal-target mean displacement, ordering verification to accept better candidates sooner within tree-based draft schemes like D-GRS. The rule is based on rank-aware list coupling and preserves the target distribution exactly. It increases throughput without extra target-model evaluations.

entry.title: A Generative Model of Complex Networks Using Graphons and Neural Inverse Operators

author.name: Wooseong Choi, Italo'Ivo Lima Dias Pinto, Chen Sun, Gaurav Gupta, Dong Song, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: This paper bridges mechanistic and deep generative graph models by formulating both generation and parameter recovery in function space, using a multifractal step graphon with recursive construction and neural inverse operators for amortized inference. This retains interpretability while generalizing beyond training graph sizes. It targets scientific applications needing both simulation fidelity and parameter recovery.

entry.title: Light Entropic Optimal Transport on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Xavier Aramayo-Carrasco, Petr Mokrov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: ManifoldLightOT learns kernel-induced entropic optimal transport couplings directly on common manifolds such as spheres, tori, SO(3), and SE(3) by constructing geometry-specific Gibbs kernels with compatible potential parameterizations. This avoids the costly iterative methods, simulated dynamics, or geometry-oblivious generic neural models of prior manifold EOT solvers.

entry.title: Electronic Density versus Geometry for Machine-Learned Molecular Absorption Spectra

author.name: Siddharth Dhanpal, Peter Elliott, Paolo Emilio Trevisanutto, Alin M. Elena, Gilberto Teobaldi

entry.summary: The paper compares ground-state electron density versus molecular geometry as input representations for machine-learning surrogates that predict molecular optical absorption spectra, avoiding expensive first-principles excited-state calculations. The choice of representation strongly affects surrogate performance, informing future design of ML models for spectroscopy. Relevant to computational chemistry and materials discovery workflows.

entry.title: Evaluating VQA in Vision Language Models using Cooperative Principles

author.name: Monika Shah, Sudarshan Balaji, Somdeb Sarkhel, Sanorita Dey, Deepak Venugopal

entry.summary: This paper evaluates VQA performance of major VLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llava) when questions violate Grice's conversational maxims, using generated modifiers that add ambiguous or false information. Violations degrade VLM performance, and human-VLM differences in pragmatic reasoning are quantified, including lower human cognitive effort for resolving VLM-induced versus human-induced violations.

entry.title: To Jev or Not? Evaluating the Accuracy and Efficiency of Structured Decision Models for Hate-Speech Moderation

author.name: Demetris Paschalides, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: HATEDECIDE evaluates six structured decision-model configurations that accept natural-language criteria for hate-speech moderation across four datasets, benchmarking against specialized, zero-shot, commercial, and supervised baselines. It asks whether these models can accommodate varying hate-speech definitions without task-specific training while remaining efficient enough for large-scale moderation.

entry.title: An AI-Based Multi-Stage Approach for Androgenetic Alopecia Assessment from Low-Magnification Scalp Images

author.name: Mahmoud Raslan, Nada Omar, Omar Khaled, Tarek Waleed, Mohamed Hazem, Rania Mounir, Solwan Elsamanoudy, Ahmed Mourad, Noura Adel, Muhammad Rushdi

entry.summary: Builds a multi-stage clinical decision-support pipeline for androgenetic alopecia that combines follicular unit localization, ordinal shaft counting, calibrated shaft-width estimation, and an interpretable rule layer, evaluated on 243 patients and roughly 158,000 expert-annotated follicular units. Under patient-disjoint testing, YOLOv8m and EfficientNet-B5 variants achieve strong detection and classification performance.

entry.title: A Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based Pipeline for End-to-End Procedural Modeling of Field-Grown Maize from Point Clouds

author.name: Mozhgan Hadadi, Talukder Z. Jubery, Adarsh Krishnamurthy, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian

entry.summary: This paper presents an automated pipeline that reconstructs editable procedural 3D maize models from raw point clouds using a multimodal VLM to annotate leaf midlines in rendered views, with deterministic geometry back-projecting annotations to fit organ-level parameters. It removes the need for manual tuning or species-specific segmentation training data, supporting high-throughput phenotyping and in silico breeding.

entry.title: Aggregate accuracy conceals concentrated temporal vulnerability in a spiking speech classifier

author.name: \.Ismail Can Dikmen

entry.summary: Shows that aggregate accuracy hides locally vulnerable utterances by exhaustively analyzing 725,070 adjacent-bin single-count input changes around 100 validation utterances of a frozen spiking speech classifier. It finds adverse perturbations are highly concentrated in a few sources, and that a post hoc gradient prefix search finds all vulnerable cases at a fraction of the census cost, outperforming margin-guided and surrogate-gradient searches.

entry.title: A Passive AI System for Verifying Physical State on Automated Liquid Handlers

author.name: Junqiong Joanne Qiu, Zeckria Kamrany, Ananya Anand, Emma Vidal, Yunjia Johanna Bai, Nathan S Chen, Sean Son, Varada Abhyankar, Taryn Jakub, Eleazar Eskin

entry.summary: The Labware Setup Checker is a passive vision system that verifies deck preparation on an Opentrons Flex liquid handler using an external consumer webcam and a browser application, without modifying hardware or firmware. It segments the deck, corrects slot assignments via known geometry, classifies labware, and flags missing, misplaced, or unexpected items against a reference protocol library. It was validated during SwabSeq sequencing runs.

entry.title: The AI Risk Observatory: What Can We Learn from AI Disclosures in Annual Reports About Societal Resilience?

author.name: Bart Jaworski

entry.summary: The study applies an LLM-based two-stage classification pipeline to 9,821 annual reports from 1,362 UK listed companies to track AI risk and adoption disclosures from 2020 to 2025. AI risk mentions rose from 2.8% to 41.2% of reports, and adoption disclosures rose from 13.8% to 45.2%, validated against human annotations. This provides a scalable signal for societal resilience research and corporate AI governance monitoring.

entry.title: MEA: A Reward-Driven Multi-Agent System for Faithful Model Explanations

author.name: Yuyang Cheng, Raghav Kaushik Ravi, Srivarshinee Sridhar, Sriparna Saha, Akash Ghosh, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: MEA is a multi-agent framework that lowers the expertise barrier for post-hoc ML explanations: a Proposer agent selects and configures explanation tools while an Actor agent, optimized end-to-end against faithfulness rewards, synthesizes tool outputs into explanations. It targets domain experts in high-stakes settings who cannot navigate explanation method outputs themselves. The work connects explainability with agentic orchestration.

entry.title: Designing the Future of User Feedback for Generative AI

author.name: Alisa Frik, Julia Bernd, Amitis Karami, Mohammad Tahaei

entry.summary: A multi-phase academic-industry collaboration with eBay studying how to design post-deployment user feedback mechanisms for generative AI that are usable for consumers and actionable for product teams. The benchmark evaluation of current industry approaches identified issues like poor discoverability and unclear terminology, leading to design guidance motivated by regulations calling for post-deployment user engagement.

entry.title: ROUTEAUDIT: Interaction-Aware Identification for Budgeted Multi-Verifier Routing

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Tianshu Fu, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: ROUTEAUDIT formulates verifier routing for LLMs as a contract-conditioned identification problem, introducing a contract lattice and policy-independent response tape to attribute quality-cost differences to specific system components. It enables fairer comparisons between adaptive multi-verifier systems when catalogs, accounting, or scoring change.

entry.title: Interpreting at Write Time: A Policy Ablation for Multi-Goal Agent Memory

author.name: Albert Sadowski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: This paper studies what long-running agent memory should summarize for when serving multiple standing user goals, comparing three policies: goal-agnostic summarization, a single all-goal summary, and per-goal summaries read jointly. It frames summarization as a lossy, purpose-laden act whose omissions become permanent once history is unreadable.

entry.title: Safeguarding Mutual Correction in Source-Free Domain Adaptation via Cut Statistics

author.name: Seongjun Lee, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: This paper addresses source-free domain adaptation by enabling bidirectional correction between a source-pretrained model and a vision-language model, exploiting their distinct failure modes instead of one-way supervision. It uses cut statistics to safeguard the mutual correction process. The work targets confirmation bias that plagues self-refinement approaches.

entry.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation

author.name: Geonwoo Bang, Dongho Kim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: EVOL tackles sparse-reward reinforcement learning for learning path recommendation by using a knowledge-tracing simulator to synthesize per-learner expert demonstrations via evolutionary search, then training a deployment-free policy. This imports a simulator-based demonstration learning recipe from robotics into education. It sidesteps the absence of true expert paths in student log data.

entry.title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation

author.name: Ruiqi Zhang, Jiahao Wang, Mingxuan Li, Haichen Luo, Chaoting Wang, Guoyu Mou, Keyu Lai, Hanchao Lv, Jiaxu Wang, Yibo Zheng, Aijun Yang, Xiaohua Wang

entry.summary: SimuVerity is a benchmark of 101 text-to-executable Simulink model-generation tasks across ten engineering domains, with a hierarchical evaluator that checks deliverability, executability, and engineering qualification before scoring accuracy, fidelity, control integrity, and robustness. Existing Simulink benchmarks only test compilation or similarity to references, not whether models satisfy engineering requirements. It is a notable step toward agentic AI in industrial engineering workflows.

entry.title: Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Preservation

author.name: Xiaofei Yin, Tong Chu, Jiyuan Fu, Jun Lan, Shuheng Zhou, Huijia Zhu

entry.summary: SF-MOPD mitigates capability interference in multi-teacher on-policy distillation by coupling a fast model updated directly by each teacher with a slow reference model, preserving general capabilities while acquiring domain expertise. This addresses the drift problem where distillation displaces the student from its initialization and degrades broad capabilities. It is relevant to the increasingly common practice of specializing foundation multimodal models.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Typed Decisions: Calibrated System One Models from Biomedical Sentence Encoders

author.name: Pritam Deka

entry.summary: Presents SBERT2S1, converting biomedical sentence encoders into schema-constrained typed decision models with cross-head and prior-fused residual variants, plus the BIODECIDE evaluation suite and MEDLINE-S1, a 243k-decision training set derived from NLM indexing. Finds retrieval pretraining improves zero-shot matching but its fine-tuning benefit depends on head architecture.

entry.title: Improving the Energy-Efficiency of the Code Generated by LLMs through Effective Prompting

author.name: Ritika Rekhi, Bing Zhang, Md Arman Islam, Jaya Krishna Pasham, Yeswanth Chitturi, Akshay Paramesha, Isha Valiveti, Asif Imran, Bekir Turkkan, Tevfik Kosar

entry.summary: Evaluates 21 prompting strategies for energy-efficient LLM code generation, identifying 8 strategies tested across 10 open-weight and proprietary LLMs for Python and C++, measuring execution energy beyond functional correctness. Motivated by the growing environmental footprint of AI-generated software.

entry.title: Distributed Learning with Selective State Space Models: Architecture-Aware Convergence Analysis

author.name: Adam Piaseczny, Md Kamran Chowdhury Shisher, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: Derives architecture-aware convergence guarantees for federated learning (FedAvg and FedProx) when applied to selective state space models like Mamba2, characterizing how recurrent stability, input-dependent discretization, and state projection affect training. This fills a gap where standard federated methods are architecture-agnostic despite SSMs' distinct dynamics.

entry.title: Revisiting Visual Representation Enhancement of VLMs via Kernel Canonical Correlation Analysis

author.name: Peilin Yang, Xiaoyu Liu, Jian Sun, Qinghua Tao

entry.summary: This work revisits KUEA, a recent method that fine-tunes CLIP image encoders by aligning their kernel matrices with vision-centric DINOv2 to improve fine-grained visual perception. The authors show that reducing the weight of the DINOv2 alignment loss does not necessarily hurt fine-grained performance, suggesting kernel-matrix element-wise discrepancy is an insufficient formulation, and propose an improved approach based on kernel canonical correlation analysis. The result refines understanding of how to transfer strong visual representations into vision-language models.

entry.title: ConvoDrift: A Multi-Turn Conversational Dataset for Modeling Stylistic Tone Evolution

author.name: Vihindi Kotalawala, Pamoda Dilranga, Gayani Thoradeniya, Prasan Yapa

entry.summary: ConvoDrift is a dataset for modeling progressive stylistic tone drift in multi-turn conversations under fixed semantic intent, built on 15,727 shared conversational structures with six annotated prompt-response pairs per conversation covering style drift and direction labels. It supports adaptation and persona-conditioned alignment research and includes a derived pairwise variant.

entry.title: Evolving Hybrid Quantum-Classical Architectures for Image Classification

author.name: Devroop Kar, Daniel Krutz, Travis Desell

entry.summary: The paper automates the design of parameterized quantum circuits within hybrid quantum-classical neural networks for image classification, replacing hand-designed circuit ansatze with evolutionary search over circuit structure, gates, and qubit connectivity. This yields task-adapted compact quantum circuits paired with classical feature extractors.

entry.title: Consecutive Posterior Fusion for Diffusive Recovery of Unobservable Image Structures

author.name: Elena Morotti, Davide Evangelista, Elena Loli Piccolomini

entry.summary: The paper introduces CPF-DDNM, an inference-time method for diffusion-based inverse problems in imaging that fuses consecutive measurement-aware posterior estimates along the reverse process, rather than relying only on instantaneous estimates. This improves recovery of image structures that are unobservable or weakly constrained by measurements in severely ill-posed problems. The approach is notable because it requires no retraining, operating purely at inference time.

entry.title: ForestQuery: Boundary-Aware and Spatially Anchored Query Learning for Unified Forest Point Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Zhihao Zhan, Le Tao, Yifei Tian, Xin Liu, Jie Yuan

entry.summary: ForestQuery is a query-learning framework for unified semantic and instance segmentation of forest point clouds, explicitly modeling boundary uncertainty and using spatial anchoring to exploit forest-specific structure. It addresses irregular tree geometry, occlusion, and ambiguous instance boundaries in fine-grained 3D forest scene understanding.

entry.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game

author.name: Siu Tung Wong (Institute of Finance and Technology, University College London), Carlo Campajola (Institute of Finance and Technology, University College London, UZH Blockchain Center)

entry.summary: The authors place a PPO agent in a continuous-time broker-trader game with a known analytical solution, using the closed-form optimal control to verify the discrete reward implementation and diagnose learning behavior. The study shows that even with a correct reward, PPO dynamics can mislead, and analytic results can guide training. It provides a rare ground-truth testbed for RL in financial optimal control.

entry.title: TRACE: A Reproducible Benchmark for Electricity Price Forecasting with Official Operational Text

author.name: Xinyi Yi, Moy Yuan, Ioannis Lestas

entry.summary: TRACE is a reproducible benchmark of 7,300 zone-day instances pairing electricity prices from five US market zones with official operational text available at forecast time, carefully reconstructed at each cutoff to prevent leakage. Evaluations show the text carries real forecasting signal for central movement and tail risks. The benchmark fills a gap in multimodal (numerical plus textural) electricity price forecasting.

entry.title: CRISP: A Framework for Clause-Reconstructed Interpretable NeuroSymbolic Propositions

author.name: Alex Chan, Shafi Muhtasim Chowdhury, Ekin Can Erku\c{s}, Ole-Christoffer Granmo, Alex Yakovlev, Rishad Shafik

entry.summary: CRISP reconstructs the last-layer activation vector of binary neural teachers as Tsetlin Machine clauses, assigning one individual TM per neuron and representing each hidden bit as propositional clauses over Booleanized inputs. This yields a direct symbolic trace from named input thresholds to named teacher neurons, evaluated on MNIST-family datasets. It addresses auditability of neural decisions through neurosymbolic methods.

entry.title: Post-Training Quantization of Autoregressive Weather Models

author.name: Ananyo Bhattacharya, Swastik Bhattacharya, Christiane Jablonowski

entry.summary: This work applies post-training quantization to deep-learning weather forecasting emulators that perform autoregressive inference via GPU matrix multiplication. The goal is to reduce compute and memory so high-resolution numerical weather prediction can scale further using out-of-the-box hardware optimizations. Quantization quality is evaluated against the forecast skill of full-precision emulators.

entry.title: RAOA: Alternating-Operator Neural Computation with Programmable Radio Propagation

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino

entry.summary: RAOA explores whether programmable radio propagation can serve as computational depth rather than mere communication, proposing a recurrent architecture that alternates an energy-derived problem update with a mixing update over a persistent latent state. Recomputing the problem field after each mix makes repeated passes compositional, improving discrete optimization solution quality without increasing learned-control counts. This is a novel intersection of wireless physics and neural computation.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Cascade for Near-Real-Time Forest Anomaly Detection from Sentinel-1 SAR Time Series

author.name: Pann Thinzar Seint, Subas Chhatkuli, Bryan Atwood

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage statistics-plus-encoder cascade for near-real-time detection of tropical forest loss using Sentinel-1 SAR time series, overcoming cloud-cover limits of optical monitoring and seasonal backscatter confounds. The system targets operational use cases including illegal logging response and carbon market verification.

entry.title: Understanding Trajectory Heterogeneity in Federated World Model Learning

author.name: Yipan Wei, Zhaokun Yan, Ziming Hong, Jiaqi Wu, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks federated learning of world models under cross-time ownership constraints, using hourly action-conditioned clinical prediction across eight MIMIC-IV disease cohorts with over 40 million transitions. It evaluates ten federated algorithms across 32 partition configurations and identifies findings about how trajectory heterogeneity affects federated world-model training.

entry.title: Page-EntroKV: Hardware-Aligned, Entropy-Weighted KV-Cache Eviction under Grouped-Query Attention

author.name: Inbasekaran S

entry.summary: Page-EntroKV formalizes KV-cache eviction at the physical-buffer granularity that grouped-query attention actually allocates, pooling heads within each group using sink-aware entropy-derived weights. This avoids the cache inflation caused by divergent per-head eviction choices and the dilution of specialized retrieval heads from naive mean pooling.

entry.title: Cross-cohort TB classification using clinical data gathered in Uganda and South Africa

author.name: Joshua M. Jansen van V\"uren, Devendra S. Parihar, Daphne Naidoo, Marisa Klopper, Frank Cobelens, Lutz Kolbe, Kimsey Zajac, Willy Ssengooba, Moses Joloba, Grant Theron, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: First cross-country evaluation of machine learning on clinical and demographic data for tuberculosis screening, using the CAGE-TB dataset from South Africa and Uganda. The authors compare logistic regression, MLPs, and CNNs with greedy feature selection to identify patients who would benefit from expensive molecular testing.

entry.title: Deep Bayesian REFoCUS

author.name: Simon Penninga, Ruud van Sloun

entry.summary: The paper formulates ultrasound multistatic recovery from arbitrary transmit sequences as Bayesian inference, training a deep generative prior to handle rank-deficient regimes where classical linear REFoCUS decoders fail. The method provides uncertainty estimates in the acquisition null space and shows strong generalization despite simulation-to-in-vivo distribution shift.

entry.title: Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jung Min Choi, Ngoc Son Le, Ibram Abdelmalak, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: MARO processes the look-back window from the most recent patch to the oldest, anchoring the latent state on recent evidence so that older patches are folded into a recency-centered representation. This architectural change expresses the unequal contribution of recent versus distant context that uniform processing stacks leave implicit.

entry.title: Broken scale symmetries in undercomplete linear autoencoders

author.name: Farhad Pashakhanloo, Jacob A. Zavatone-Veth

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how finite-stepsize SGD breaks exact scale symmetries in neural network loss landscapes, focusing on undercomplete linear autoencoders. The authors show analytically that SGD selects a preferred sign for scale drift on the PCA solution manifold, favoring large decoder weights, with dynamics admitting an analytical description. This refines prior accounts of noise-balancing symmetry breaking in homogeneous networks.

entry.title: Expected Utility Regret Rule: Minimax and Bayes Optimal Portfolio Choice

author.name: Masahiro Kato

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes the Expected Utility Regret (EUR) rule for portfolio choice, which jointly selects a portfolio class and estimates weights to minimize expected utility regret against an oracle investor. In a regular parametric return model, a single EUR rule simultaneously attains minimax and Bayes lower bounds, including leading constants, without using the Bayes prior. The framework recovers mean-variance and related rules as special cases.

entry.title: Evaluating and Improving the Robustness of Large Language Models to Input Sequence Variations

author.name: Narek Maloyan

entry.summary: This thesis develops metrics and methods for LLM robustness against prompt injections, backdoors, and quality-metric manipulation. Contributions include a generative robustness metric based on Jensen-Shannon divergence, theoretical bounds relating localized attack success to classifier stability, and an adaptive evolutionary attack (ASA) targeting LLM-as-a-Judge systems.

entry.title: Hold-Out Scoring for Efficient Gaussian DAG Learning

author.name: Donguk Shin, Byeongguk Kang, Inseol Lee, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: HOST is an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional Gaussian DAG learning that replaces expensive subset search with nodewise hold-out scoring and convex regression, without requiring a supplied indegree bound. The key insight is that correct ordering recovery only requires one-sided control of score errors, improving the statistical-computational tradeoff.

entry.title: Landscape-Dependent Performance of Photonic Quantum Solvers in QUBO Feature Selection for Financial Risk Detection

author.name: Nirvik Sahoo, Paul Robert Griffin

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks photonic entropy computing (QCI Dirac-3) and simulated boson sampling against classical branch-and-bound (Gurobi) across thirteen QUBO-based feature selection methods on credit card fraud and consumer default datasets. Results show photonic solvers can match full-feature model performance with far fewer features on some problem landscapes, with performance dependent on the QUBO landscape. It offers a rare empirical head-to-head of photonic quantum-inspired hardware for an ML task.

entry.title: HakemBench: A Turkish Benchmark of Typed Decisions

author.name: Sait Furkan Teke (ufak AI)

entry.summary: HakemBench is a fully open Turkish benchmark of 2,346 items with 4,275 decision questions across seven practical tracks such as fact-checking, moderation, and legal routing, requiring models to output option probabilities. A unified harness measures decision quality, calibration, and selective automation with bootstrap intervals, plus robustness probes for option order and translation.

entry.title: StanceEval 2026: The Second Stance Detection Shared Task

author.name: Rasha Albalawi, Nuha Albadi, Hamzah Luqman, Asma Yamani, Maram Kurdi, Saad Ezzini, Ahmed Ashraf, Maged Al-Shaibani, Nora Alturayeif

entry.summary: This paper describes the second StanceEval shared task on Arabic social media stance detection, featuring cross-target generalization tracks that test thematic transfer (Women Driving) and fully unseen targets (E-Cars, Trimester System). With 80 registered teams from 12 countries, it provides a community benchmark resource for low-resource stance detection.

entry.title: Single-Pass Uncertainty Heads for Claim-Level Hallucination Detection in Persian Medical Language Models

author.name: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Pedram Rostami, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Sadra Hakim, Audrina Ebrahimi

entry.summary: The authors adapt the LLM Uncertainty Head framework to Aya-Expanse-8B-based Persian medical models (Gaokerena-V and Gaokerena-R), constructing two new Persian claim-level hallucination datasets with 1,600 paired responses each. The single-pass approach avoids the cost of repeated-sampling uncertainty estimation and extends hallucination detection resources to a new language and medical domain.

entry.title: Benchmarking Literature Retrieval for a Model Organism: A Dictyostelium Case Study

author.name: Yun Wang, Gad Shaulsky, Toma\v{z} Curk, Bla\v{z} Zupan

entry.summary: Presents a curator-generated retrieval benchmark from dictyBase for the model organism Dictyostelium, addressing the gap between broad biomedical retrieval evaluations and narrow, organism-specific knowledge-base settings. The study examines cross-encoder reranking, gene-aware query expansion, and abstract-only versus full-text retrieval in this sparse-literature domain.

entry.title: The Shape of Speech: A Geometric Measure of Coarticulation for Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation

author.name: Danzel Serrano, Przemyslaw Musialski

entry.summary: Introduces a geometric measure of coarticulation in speech-driven 3D facial animation: lip-path length compared against a consonant-aware shortest route through vowel and consonant positions. The measure requires only forced alignment so it applies without ground truth, and is demonstrated on four state-of-the-art methods across architectural families.

entry.title: Autonomous mobile robot operations logistics: a dataset of jobs, dispatch events and robot states

author.name: Jan-Felix Klein, Yongkuk Jeong

entry.summary: MoRoOp is a dataset of autonomous mobile robot (AMR) material-transport operations recorded over nine eight-hour shifts in a laboratory kit-supply scenario. It links 1,382 job specifications, 4,815 operations, 19,352 dispatch events, and per-wheel robot-state observations including position, velocity, and state of charge. It enables research on job generation, dispatching, and fleet-level robot control.

entry.title: A Residual Tree Gaussian Process Modeling Framework for High-Dimensional Data

author.name: Pulong Ma, Li Ma

entry.summary: The paper introduces ResTGP, a Bayesian residual tree Gaussian process framework for large spatial datasets with heterogeneous structure over high-dimensional domains. The method decomposes a Gaussian process across a dyadic tree of resolutions via iterated predictive and residual processes, making each node amenable to modeling. It addresses a real computational inadequacy of standard GPs for modern multi-dimensional spatial data.

entry.title: Reasoning with Evidence, Not Merely Rationales: Verifiable Preference Proofs for LLM-Based Recommendation

author.name: Yu Hou, Nathaniel Kang, Pengkai Wang, Hua Li

entry.summary: PROVE-REC addresses the grounding-influence gap in LLM recommendation, where generated preference rationales may be weakly supported by evidence or have no effect on rankings. Its two-pass design converts interaction history into verifiable preference proofs with linked evidence, then predicts the next item using only the proof and its evidence.

entry.title: Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Doseok Jang, Jon Ander Campos, Youran Qi

entry.summary: LMOPD is a multi-teacher on-policy distillation method that enforces an explicit lexicographic priority order over rewards, selecting reward-specialist teachers per rollout only when a deficiency gate detects a failure on a higher-priority objective. This prevents asymmetric trade-offs, such as conciseness improving at the cost of correctness, which scalarized reward mixing suffers from. It targets RLVR-style post-training where protecting correctness is paramount.

entry.title: A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling

author.name: Yixing Li, Jiahang Zhou, Zhiyu Zeng, Xin Ai

entry.summary: DAIST decomposes full-package 2.5D/3D-IC thermal simulations into block-level subdomain problems solved by neural operators, coupled through iterative exchanges of interfacial temperature and heat flux. This local-to-global architecture eliminates the topology lock-in that forces monolithic AI surrogates to retrain when die count or layout changes, versus hours-long FEM runs. Companion work to the data center capacity planning paper by an overlapping team.

entry.title: Neuron merging via inverse-activation regression for post-training compression of sigmoid neural networks

author.name: Ao Kuniya, Jun Ohkubo

entry.summary: The paper studies cluster-based neuron merging for compressing trained sigmoid-activation networks, treating compression as coarse-graining that should decide which information to retain when consolidating neuronal degrees of freedom. Beyond data-free contribution-weighted averaging, it proposes mapping neuron responses back to pre-activation space via inverse-activation regression before merging. This retains useful information that structured pruning would simply discard.

entry.title: Differentiable Koopman Operator for Contrastive Learning on Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Md Abrar Jahin, Taufikur Rahman Fuad, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: KAIROS embeds a differentiable Koopman operator within a dynamic-graph contrastive learning framework to linearize temporal evolution of node representations, pairing raw features with a graph-diffused structural view under multi-granularity objectives. The goal is robustness to distribution shifts on evolving interaction networks.

entry.title: LS-AR: Future-Predictive Latent Steering in Autoregressive LLMs

author.name: Anubha Gupta, Eduardo Pignatelli

entry.summary: LS-AR is a dual-channel autoregressive architecture that decouples continuous goal steering from discrete token decoding via FiLM conditioning, combining a static goal encoder for macro-objective retention with a dynamic recurrent state tracker. It reports strong results on long-horizon retrieval tasks extending past context limits.

entry.title: AIBL: Augmented Instance-Based Learning with Structured Memory and Neural Embeddings

author.name: Radha Poovendran, Andrea Stocco, Linda Bushnell

entry.summary: AIBL modernizes Instance-Based Learning Theory by formulating case-based sequential decision making in a learned vector space, using neural embeddings for partial matching, activation, and blending over stored situation-decision-utility instances. This enables IBLT to handle high-dimensional sequential data such as text, images, and user histories.

entry.title: Turnover-Orthogonal Credit Assignment for Open-Team Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Amit Thakur, Mukesh Singhal

entry.summary: TOCA introduces a value decomposition for open-team multi-agent RL that separates credit for actions from credit for exogenous agent turnover events, so surviving agents are not rewarded or penalized for population changes outside their control. It derives a centered decomposition of event-conditioned value into action, turnover, and interaction components.

entry.title: Contrastive Neural Embeddings Reveal Individual Traits Beyond Conversational Role

author.name: Hubert Huang, Michelle McCleod, Brendan Ames, Evie Malaia

entry.summary: The authors apply CEBRA contrastive embeddings to EEG from conversing dyads and show that labels such as the difference in partners' autism-quotient scores decode well above chance, while permutation controls reveal subtleties in how to validate such embeddings. The work examines embedding geometry rather than just decoding accuracy as the validation criterion. It touches on both representation-learning methodology and cognitive neuroscience.

entry.title: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Generalization of Large Language Models in Temporal Extraction Tasks

author.name: Fahmid Shahriar Iqbal, Ritam Dutt, Soumitra Das, Arnav Verma, Sagnik Ray Choudhury

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how prompted LLMs generalize in time and event expression extraction across four dimensions of distribution shift, comparing model families, architectures, scales, and prompting strategies. It finds that strong in-domain base performance generally predicts, but does not guarantee, reliable behavior under distribution shifts.

entry.title: A Manifold-Aware Topic Modeling Approach via Rank-Based Prototypes

author.name: Thiago C\'esar Castilho Almeida, Daniel Carlos Guimar\~aes Pedronette

entry.summary: MARETopic is a training-free topic modeling framework that casts topic discovery as rank-based prototype selection: embeddings are projected onto a low-dimensional manifold, ranked neighborhood lists are built, and a greedy algorithm selects K exemplar real documents whose neighborhoods cover the corpus. This avoids hubness and anisotropy problems of absolute distances and grounds topics in actual corpus texts.

entry.title: From Expression to Reaction: Role-aware Visual Transfer and Stimulus-guided Reasoning for Interlocutor Emotion Recognition

author.name: Wei Wang, Zhaowu Li, Jianjie Luo, Fu Lee Wang, Lap-Kei Lee, Zhenguo Yang

entry.summary: Proposes RASG for recognizing listener emotions from listener-only video and speaker-only audio, with modules for role-aware visual transfer using reliable pseudo-labels and stimulus-guided boundary reasoning for ambiguous reactions. It tackles supervision mismatch from lacking labeled listener data and context-dependent interpretation of listener expressions.

entry.title: LOCUS: Landmark-Oriented Container Discrimination Using Spatial Graphs

author.name: Taylor Bergeron, Shibani Senthilbabu, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: LOCUS trains a graph neural network to update CLIP embeddings with spatial information, enabling robots to disambiguate which container plausibly contains a hidden target object. It jointly reasons about spatial and semantic relationships where cosine similarity with CLIP alone fails. The work targets robust object search in unstructured real-world environments.

entry.title: RIPPLE in Still Water: Zero-Shot Clustering in Federated Learning with Wavelet Scattering Transform

author.name: Alessandro Licciardi

entry.summary: RIPPLE performs clustered federated learning by assigning clients to clusters entirely offline from spectral characterizations of their local data, using variance-weighted PCA prototypes embedded via wavelet scattering transforms. This avoids the communication overhead, gradient-exposure privacy risks, and missing-client problems of in-training clustering methods.
